translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of the blessing and mercy of Allah, the Most High, and serves as a reminder to the believer that all actions and endeavors should be done in the name of Allah, seeking His guidance and blessings. It is a recognition of Allah's attributes of mercy and compassion, and an acknowledgement that He is the only one worthy of worship and devotion.
orig: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the special status and responsibility that comes with being human, and serves as a reminder of the obligation to live up to the expectations of God and to fulfill the purpose for which we were created.
orig: الرحمن الرحيم

translation: And the Day of Judgment will come, and the wrongdoers will be told, 'Surely what you used to mock at is coming.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when the wicked will be confronted with their misdeeds and mocked for their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the fate of those who have done wrong. It serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the accountability they will face on that day.
orig: مالك يوم الدين

translation: You alone we worship, and Your aid we seek.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of monotheism and dependence on God. The first part, 'You alone we worship,' emphasizes the exclusivity of worshiping God and rejects the idea of worshiping anyone or anything else. The second part, 'and Your aid we seek,' highlights humanity's need for God's guidance and support in all aspects of life. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's sovereignty and seeking His help in all aspects of life.
orig: إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

translation: And guide us to the straight path
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God to guide us to the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and obedience to God. The phrase 'al-sirāt al-mustaqīm' is often translated as 'the straight path', but it also means 'the path that leads to the peak or the goal'. The verse is asking God to guide us to the path that leads to the ultimate goal of human existence, which is to live a righteous life and to worship God in the best possible way. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from God and relying on Him to show us the way, rather than relying on our own limited knowledge and understanding.
orig: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

translation: And the path of those whom You have blessed, not of those who have been cursed, nor of those who have gone astray.
interpretation: This verse describes the path of the righteous, which is separate from those who have been cursed and those who have gone astray. The verse emphasizes the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, and serves as a reminder that God's blessings are reserved for those who follow His commandments and live a righteous life. The verse also highlights the importance of staying on the path of righteousness and avoiding the pitfalls of sin and disobedience.
orig: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: That is the Book, there is no doubt in it, a guidance for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an, describing it as a book that contains no doubt or uncertainty. The verse also highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to serve as a guidance for those who are righteous and seek to live according to God's will. The verse underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and direction for believers, and serves as a reminder of the central role that the Qur'an plays in Islamic faith and practice.
orig: ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه هدى للمتقين

translation: And they believe in the unseen [i.e., the Hereafter] and establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the belief in the Hereafter and the importance of establishing prayer and giving charity as a means of purifying one's soul and expressing gratitude to God for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. It emphasizes the idea that true faith is not just about belief in God, but also about putting that belief into practice through good deeds and righteous actions.
orig: الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and they are certain of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the belief in the Qur'an and previous scriptures, and the belief in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of having certainty in the Hereafter, which is a central tenet of Islam. The verse also highlights the connection between belief in the Qur'an and belief in previous scriptures, indicating that belief in one is not possible without belief in the other. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their belief and to be mindful of their ultimate goal, which is to attain a successful outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك وبالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: And those who are guided by their Lord, they are the ones who are successful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of guidance from God and its impact on an individual's life. The phrase 'على هدى من ربهم' (alaa hijabin min rabbihim) means 'guided by their Lord' and implies that those who are guided by God are the ones who are truly successful. The word 'مفلحون' (muflihoon) means 'successful' and refers to those who have achieved success in both this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that true success is not limited to material gains or worldly achievements, but rather it is the result of being guided by God and living according to His will. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek guidance from God and to live their lives in accordance with His commandments, in order to achieve true success and happiness.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and children will not benefit them anything [in the Hereafter].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that wealth and children, which are often seen as sources of pride and security in this life, will be of no use to those who disbelieve in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that true success and prosperity come from living a righteous life and following God's commandments, rather than relying on material possessions or worldly achievements.
orig: إن الذين كفروا سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And God has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing and upon their eyes is a covering, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have rejected God's message and have turned away from His guidance. Their hearts are sealed, meaning they are no longer receptive to the truth, their ears are closed to hearing the message, and their eyes are covered from seeing the signs of God. They are condemned to a great punishment in the hereafter as a result of their rejection and disbelief.
orig: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: And among the people are those who say, 'We believe in Allah and in the Last Day,' but they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about people who claim to believe in God and the Hereafter, but their actions do not reflect their belief. They are not true believers, as their belief is not reflected in their actions. This verse highlights the importance of not just professing belief, but also living according to that belief. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not just about what we say, but about how we live our lives and the actions we take.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

translation: They mocked at God and those who believed, but they will soon know. Or do they not know that God's punishment is severe?
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who mock and ridicule God and the believers. The verse warns them that they will soon come to know the severity of God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and disbelieving, reminding them that God's punishment is not to be taken lightly and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: يخادعون الله والذين آمنوا وما يخدعون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And in their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease, and they will have a painful punishment because they used to lie.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people in question have a spiritual disease in their hearts, which has caused them to be deceitful and lie. As a result, God has increased their disease, and they will face a painful punishment. The verse highlights the consequences of dishonesty and the importance of being truthful in one's actions and words. It serves as a warning to those who engage in deception and reminds them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they continue to live a life of dishonesty.
orig: في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضا ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they said, 'We are but reformers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were warned not to cause corruption on earth, but they replied that they were reformers, suggesting that their actions were justified and intended to improve society. The verse highlights the irony of their claim, as their actions were, in fact, harmful and contrary to the common good. It serves as a reminder that those who seek to justify their harmful actions under the guise of reform or progress must be held accountable for their actions and that true reform must be done with the intention of pleasing God, not for personal gain or selfish motives.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم لا تفسدوا في الأرض قالوا إنما نحن مصلحون

translation: And indeed, they were, in their intoxication, nearer to disbelief than faith, and they say, 'Are we to be left to our own devices?',
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who are steeped in their own desires and heedless of the consequences of their actions. They are so consumed by their own desires that they are blind to the truth and are on the brink of disbelief. They are unwilling to accept the idea that they will be held accountable for their actions and are in denial about the possibility of punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their spiritual responsibilities and are absorbed in their worldly desires, reminding them of the importance of living a life of faith and obedience to God.
orig: ألا إنهم هم المفسدون ولكن لا يشعرون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Believe as the people believe,' they said, 'Shall we believe as the foolish believe?' Indeed, they are the foolish ones, but they do not know.
interpretation: The verse addresses a situation where a group of people were invited to believe in God's message, but they refused, comparing themselves to the common people who had already believed. They implied that they were wiser and more knowledgeable than the masses, and therefore, they did not need to believe. The verse responds by pointing out their foolishness, indicating that they are indeed the foolish ones, but they lack understanding and are unaware of their own ignorance.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا كما آمن الناس قالوا أنؤمن كما آمن السفهاء ألا إنهم هم السفهاء ولكن لا يعلمون

translation: And when they met those who believed, they said: 'We believe' but when they were alone with their Shaitans, they said: 'Surely we are with you, indeed we were but mocking.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the behavior of some people who outwardly claim to believe in God and His message, but in reality, they are not sincere in their belief. They are actually mocking the believers and are in league with the forces of evil, represented by the 'Shaitans' (devils) in the verse. The verse highlights the danger of hypocrisy and the importance of being truthful in one's beliefs and actions.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم قالوا إنا معكم إنما نحن مستهزئون

translation: And God will mock at them and let them drown in their own confusion.
interpretation: The verse describes God's punishment of those who have disobeyed Him. The phrase 'yastahzi'oon' (يستهزئ) implies that God will mock them, making fun of their foolishness and lack of faith. The word 'tughyaan' (طغيان) means 'confusion' or 'perplexity', indicating that they will be left in a state of disarray and uncertainty. The verse suggests that those who disobey God will be punished and left in a state of confusion, with no escape or respite.
orig: الله يستهزئ بهم ويمدهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And those who have earned evil will be punished by the evil they have earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of reaping what one sows. Those who have engaged in evil deeds and oppressed others will face the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that the punishment they receive will be proportionate to the evil they have committed, and they will not be treated unjustly. It serves as a warning to those who engage in oppressive behavior, reminding them that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town like this one while its people were unjust, so We gave them a punishment in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم وتركهم في ظلمات لا يبصرون

translation: And they (the disbelievers) schemed, and We schemed, but they did not perceive (the outcome).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the plots and schemes of the disbelievers against the believers, and how God outsmarted them. The verse indicates that the disbelievers thought they had the upper hand, but in reality, they were unaware of the ultimate outcome, which was their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always in control, and that the plans of the disbelievers will ultimately fail, while the believers will triumph.
orig: صم بكم عمي فهم لا يرجعون

translation: Or [consider] the one who has been given the knowledge that has not been given to him, so he has been given a great sin and a false pride. Indeed, Allah will not have him turn back to the correct way.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who have been given knowledge and yet they use it for sinful purposes, becoming arrogant and proud of their knowledge. Their actions are a rejection of God's guidance, and as a result, they are unable to turn back to the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning to those who have been given knowledge and are using it for negative purposes, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of humility and righteousness.
orig: أو كصيب من السماء فيه ظلمات ورعد وبرق يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم من الصواعق حذر الموت والله محيط بالكافرين

translation: And the thunder proclaims His praise, and the angels [also] praise Him, and He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about Allah, and He is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and majesty of God, who controls even the elements, such as thunder and lightning. The thunder is described as proclaiming God's praise, indicating that all of creation, including natural phenomena, glorifies and honors God. The verse also mentions the angels, who are also commanded to praise God. The verse then describes God's power to send thunderbolts and strike those who reject and dispute the existence and authority of God. The verse ends by emphasizing God's severity in punishment, indicating that those who reject God will face severe consequences.
orig: يكاد البرق يخطف أبصارهم كلما أضاء لهم مشوا فيه وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا ولو شاء الله لذهب بسمعهم وأبصارهم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only one God, the creator of all humanity, as a means of becoming righteous. It highlights the connection between worship and righteousness, indicating that true worship leads to a life of virtue and morality. The verse also emphasizes the continuity of God's message and the responsibility of each generation to follow and adhere to it. The use of the phrase 'those before you' serves as a reminder of the long line of prophets and believers who have come before and sets the stage for the rest of the Qur'an's message.
orig: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: It is He who has made the earth a bed for you, and the sky a canopy, and has sent down water from the sky and brought forth with it gardens of various types, as a source of sustenance for you. Therefore, do not set up rivals to Allah when you know [the truth].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and provision for humanity. He has created the earth as a comfortable place for us, and the sky as a protective canopy. He has also sent down water from the sky, which has resulted in the growth of various types of gardens, providing us with sustenance. The verse serves as a reminder of God's blessings and our responsibility to recognize and acknowledge His greatness. It warns us against setting up rivals to God, indicating that we should not associate any partners with Him, and that we should recognize and worship only one God.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض فراشا والسماء بناء وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And indeed, you are in doubt about the Qur'an that We have sent down to Our servant. So come with a surah the like of it and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' skepticism towards the Qur'an and challenges them to produce a chapter similar to it. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which is beyond human capability to produce, and highlights the futility of the disbelievers' attempts to discredit it. The verse also warns the disbelievers that they will be held accountable for their rejection of the Qur'an and their denial of God's signs.
orig: وإن كنتم في ريب مما نزلنا على عبدنا فأتوا بسورة من مثله وادعوا شهداءكم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: So indeed, those who reject the message of God will face the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message, which is the eternal punishment in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment by describing the fuel of the Fire as both men and stones, indicating that nothing can extinguish it, and that it is prepared exclusively for the disbelievers. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of their fate in the Hereafter.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا فاتقوا النار التي وقودها الناس والحجارة أعدت للكافرين

translation: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds, that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. It is a promise of Allah, truthful and faithful [in His promise].
interpretation: The verse promises a reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds, describing a paradise where they will reside forever, surrounded by gardens and rivers. The verse highlights the beauty and tranquility of this reward, emphasizing that it is a promise from Allah, who is truthful and faithful in His promises. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to live a righteous life and to strive for good deeds, with the assurance that their efforts will be rewarded in the afterlife.
orig: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أن لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار كلما رزقوا منها من ثمرة رزقا قالوا هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل وأتوا به متشابها ولهم فيها أزواج مطهرة وهم فيها خالدون

translation: Indeed, Allah will not embarrass you with a parable, but the ones who disbelieved will say, 'What has turned your Lord away from us?' Say, 'Until they are given over to their Lord, either in the morning or at noon.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority, stating that He will not be embarrassed or held accountable for His actions. The verse also highlights the disbelief of those who reject God's message, questioning why God has abandoned them. The response to their question is that they will be given over to their Lord, either in the morning or at noon, indicating that they will be held accountable for their actions and that God's punishment will come suddenly and unexpectedly.
orig: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها فأما الذين آمنوا فيعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين

translation: Those who break the covenant of Allah after it has been ratified, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land, it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who break God's covenant and go against His commands, causing corruption and destruction in the land. The verse emphasizes the severity of their actions and the consequences they will face. The phrase 'break the covenant of Allah' refers to the breaking of the covenant between God and His servants, which is a grave offense. The phrase 'sever what Allah has commanded to be joined' refers to the breaking of relationships and the causing of division among people, which is also a grave sin. The phrase 'spread corruption in the land' refers to the spreading of evil and injustice, causing harm to others and destroying the peace and harmony of society. The verse warns of the severe punishment that those who commit such acts will face, and serves as a reminder of the importance of following God's commands and living a righteous life.
orig: الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, and then He directed Himself to the heaven, and made them seven heavens, and He is with everything aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and control over the universe. The verse states that God created everything on earth and then turned His attention to the heavens, creating seven heavens, indicating His immense power and ability to create and sustain multiple realms. The phrase 'and He is with everything aware' suggests that God is all-knowing and aware of everything in His creation, emphasizing His omniscience and ability to watch over and guide His creation.
orig: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن سبع سماوات وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.' They said, 'Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?' We said, 'We will make you a successive authority.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is speaking to the angels and announcing His plan to create a successor on earth. The angels express their concern that the human being who will be created will cause corruption and shed blood. God reassures them that He will make them a successive authority, indicating that He will guide and support them in their role as guardians of the earth. The verse highlights the responsibility that comes with being a guardian of the earth and the importance of fulfilling that responsibility in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

translation: And Adam learned the names of all things, then he presented them to the angels and said, 'Inform me of the names of these, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene in which Adam, the first human, is given the task of learning and identifying the names of all things. He is then asked to present these names to the angels, who are believed to possess knowledge and wisdom. The verse highlights Adam's eagerness to learn and his desire to verify the accuracy of his knowledge. It also underscores the importance of knowledge and understanding in Islam, as well as the belief in the angels' knowledge and their role in guiding and teaching humans.
orig: وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They said, 'Glory to You, our Lord! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: In this verse, the believers are expressing their submission to God's will and acknowledging that their knowledge is limited to what God has taught them. They are recognizing God's infinite wisdom and understanding, and acknowledging that they are but mere servants, dependent on God's guidance and mercy. The verse highlights the importance of humility and the recognition of one's limitations, as well as the belief in God's omniscience and wisdom.
orig: قالوا سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

translation: And (mention, O Muhammad), when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad and instructing him to remind the angels of God's plan to establish a successive authority on earth. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's authority and dominion extend beyond the heavens and the earth, and that He has the power to appoint whom He wills as His successive authority on earth. The verse also underscores the idea that the Prophet Muhammad is a part of this plan and has a critical role to play in establishing God's authority on earth.
orig: قال يا آدم أنبئهم بأسمائهم فلما أنبأهم بأسمائهم قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they all prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene in which God commands the angels to prostrate before Adam, the first human, as a sign of respect and obedience. All the angels comply, except for Iblis (Satan), who refuses to submit and is characterized as arrogant and disbelieving. This verse highlights the pride and disobedience of Iblis, who would later become a constant opponent of humanity and a source of temptation and evil in the world.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى واستكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: And We said: O Adam! Dwell you and your wife in the Garden, and eat from it a plentiful (of fruits) as you wish, and do not approach this tree, for you will become of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing Prophet Adam and his wife, instructing them to live in the Garden of Eden and enjoy its abundance. However, they are warned not to approach a particular tree, lest they become sinners. The tree in question is often interpreted as the Tree of Knowledge, and the prohibition against approaching it serves as a test of Adam and Eve's obedience to God's command. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة وكلا منها رغدا حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town and village, and We have sent Our punishment upon them in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of many towns and villages that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأزلهما الشيطان عنها فأخرجهما مما كانا فيه وقلنا اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين

translation: Adam received words from his Lord, and He relented towards him. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Adam, the first human, realized his mistake and sought forgiveness from God. The verse highlights God's mercy and willingness to accept repentance, as He relented towards Adam and forgave his sin. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is always ready to accept repentance and forgive those who turn to Him in sincerity.
orig: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of the word 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular nation or community, but is universal and applicable to all people. The verse underscores the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message and serves as a reminder that his teachings are meant to bring people closer to God and to promote peace, love, and harmony among all people.
orig: قلنا اهبطوا منها جميعا فإما يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the truth. They will be the inhabitants of Hell, doomed to suffer eternally. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment and serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's revelations, reminding them of the dire consequences of their disbelief.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you, and fulfill your covenant with Me, I will fulfill My covenant with you, and fear none but Me.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the children of Israel and reminding them of the favors He has bestowed upon them. God is asking them to remember His blessings and to fulfill their part of the covenant, which is to obey His commandments and worship Him alone. The verse also emphasizes the mutual nature of the covenant, where God will fulfill His part in return for the Israelites' obedience. The verse concludes by reminding them to fear none but God, indicating that He is the only one worthy of fear and obedience.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم وإياي فارهبون

translation: And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and do not be the first to deny it, and do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear Me alone.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in the revelations sent down by God, which include the Qur'an and the scriptures that came before it. The verse warns against rejecting or denying God's revelations, and encourages believers to hold fast to their faith, even in the face of adversity or temptation. The verse also cautions against trying to compromise or cheapen God's signs or revelations by exchanging them for worldly gain or material possessions. Instead, believers are encouraged to fear God alone and to hold Him in the highest esteem.
orig: وآمنوا بما أنزلت مصدقا لما معكم ولا تكونوا أول كافر به ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا وإياي فاتقون

translation: And do not obscure the truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity. It prohibits the concealment of truth and the spreading of falsehood. The verse addresses those who are aware of the truth but choose to hide it, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to always speak the truth, even if it is difficult, and to never compromise one's integrity for personal gain or to avoid conflict.
orig: ولا تلبسوا الحق بالباطل وتكتموا الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and bow down with those who bow down.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing a strong connection with God through prayer and giving charity (zakah) and also encourages believers to humble themselves and show humility by bowing down in prayer with others who are also seeking guidance and forgiveness from God. It highlights the importance of community and unity among believers, and serves as a reminder that true worship involves not only personal devotion but also a commitment to the greater good of the community.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واركعوا مع الراكعين

translation: And certainly We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the value and worth of every human life, and serves as a reminder that humans are special creations of God, deserving of respect, dignity, and honor. The verse also underscores the responsibility that comes with this honor, as humans are expected to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life, which is to worship and serve God.
orig: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون

translation: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is a heavy burden except for the humble ones.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and prayer in times of hardship. The phrase 'And seek help through patience and prayer' suggests that patience and prayer are means of seeking help and support from God. The phrase 'it is a heavy burden except for the humble ones' indicates that the burden of trials and hardships is made lighter for those who are humble and submissive to God's will. The verse highlights the value of humility and submission in times of difficulty and encourages believers to turn to God in prayer and seek His help.
orig: واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة وإنها لكبيرة إلا على الخاشعين

translation: And those who think that they will be punished in this world, so they await their Lord's punishment, and they are sure that they will return to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who believe in the afterlife and the accountability of their actions before God. They recognize that their ultimate destination is with God and that they will be held accountable for their deeds in this life. The verse highlights their certainty in God's punishment and their belief in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to those who are skeptical or dismissive of the idea of accountability and the Hereafter, emphasizing the importance of living a virtuous life and being mindful of one's actions.
orig: الذين يظنون أنهم ملاقو ربهم وأنهم إليه راجعون

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you, and that I have preferred you over the nations.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the children of Israel, reminding them of the special favor and blessings that He has bestowed upon them. The verse emphasizes God's grace and mercy towards the Israelites, who were chosen by God to be His chosen people. The phrase 'over the nations' suggests that the Israelites were elevated to a position of prominence and superiority over other nations, indicating their unique status and relationship with God. The verse serves as a reminder to the Israelites of God's goodness and generosity towards them, and encourages them to live up to their responsibilities as God's chosen people.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another, and no compensation will be accepted from it, nor will intercession be of benefit, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of individual accountability on Judgment Day. No one will be able to help or intercede for another person, and no amount of wealth or status will be of any use. Each person will be responsible for their own actions and will face the consequences of their choices. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on one's own spiritual growth and development, rather than relying on others or material possessions for salvation.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها شفاعة ولا يؤخذ منها عدل ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, so is there any lesson in this?
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers, reminding them of God's punishment on previous communities who disobeyed and were destroyed. The verse emphasizes that the destruction was not just limited to the individuals but also their offspring and families. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, asking them to reflect on the lessons from the past and to take heed of God's punishment. The verse also highlights the severity of God's punishment, indicating that it is not limited to this life but extends to the Hereafter, where the punishment will be much greater.
orig: وإذ نجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And when We divided the sea for you and saved you and drowned the followers of Pharaoh, and you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous event of Moses and the Israelites crossing the Red Sea, which was divided by God's command, allowing them to safely reach the other side. Meanwhile, Pharaoh and his followers, who were in pursuit of the Israelites, were drowned in the sea. The verse highlights God's power and mercy in saving the believers and punishing the oppressors. It serves as a reminder to the believers of God's ability to protect and guide them, and to the disbelievers, a warning of the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: وإذ فرقنا بكم البحر فأنجيناكم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And We gave Moses forty nights, then you took the calf after him, and you were unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to the incident of the golden calf, where the Israelites, led by Aaron, created an idol in the form of a calf and worshiped it, thereby disobeying God's commandments. The verse emphasizes the betrayal and injustice of the Israelites, who turned away from God's guidance and instead chose to worship an idol. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of disobedience and the importance of staying true to God's commands.
orig: وإذ واعدنا موسى أربعين ليلة ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: Then We forgave you after that so that you might give thanks.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's mercy and forgiveness towards His servants. Despite the people's disobedience and ingratitude, God chose to forgive them and give them another chance to turn back to Him. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and recognizing God's blessings in our lives, as the forgiveness was given so that people might be grateful for God's mercy and acknowledge His favors upon them.
orig: ثم عفونا عنكم من بعد ذلك لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And indeed, We have given Moses the Book and the criterion that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Book (the Torah) given to Prophet Moses and the criterion ( Furqan) that serves as a guidance for the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Book and the criterion as a means of guidance for those who seek to live a righteous life and to distinguish right from wrong. The verse also underscores the idea that the revelation given to Moses was not only a source of guidance but also a criteria to differentiate between truth and falsehood.
orig: وإذ آتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And Moses said to his people, 'O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. Turn to your Creator and kill yourselves [i.e., your evil inclinations], that He may forgive you.' Then He accepted your repentance, indeed He is the Acceptor of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing his people, who have committed a grave sin by worshipping the golden calf instead of Allah. Moses tells them that they have wronged themselves and that they must turn to Allah and repent by killing their evil inclinations. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and the mercy of Allah, who accepts the repentance of those who turn to Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of turning to Allah and seeking His forgiveness, and the assurance that He is ever-merciful and accepting of those who repent.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم إنكم ظلمتم أنفسكم باتخاذكم العجل فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم عند بارئكم فتاب عليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. Therefore, turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves [the calf], that is better for you in the sight of your Creator.' He said, 'Indeed, I am, out of fear, of what you have done, that Allah may forgive you.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing his people who have committed a grave sin by worshiping a golden calf instead of Allah. Moses tells them that they have wronged themselves and must turn to Allah in repentance and kill the calf they have been worshiping. Moses is afraid of Allah's punishment for their sin, but he is also hopeful that Allah may forgive them if they repent. The verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in repentance and the possibility of forgiveness for those who seek it.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نؤمن لك حتى نرى الله جهرة فأخذتكم الصاعقة وأنتم تنظرون

translation: Then We sent forth among you (O Muslims) after them, to convey Our Message unto you, for We have sent forth among you (O Muslims) those who were chosen and selected to convey Our Message unto you.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the prophets and messengers who were sent by God to guide humanity after the death of the previous prophets. The verse emphasizes that the messengers were chosen and selected by God to convey His message to the people. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is a continuation of the messages of previous prophets and that it is a mercy from God to humanity. It also highlights the importance of following the guidance of the prophets and messengers, as they are the chosen ones who have been entrusted with the responsibility of conveying God's message to humanity.
orig: ثم بعثناكم من بعد موتكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We have put a barrier between you and those who are being punished, and an obstacle between you and the disbelievers, and We have covered them with a veil, so they cannot see.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the barrier or obstacle that God has placed between the believers and those who are being punished, as well as between the believers and the disbelievers. The verse suggests that this barrier is a means of protection for the believers, preventing them from being influenced by the disbelievers and their harmful beliefs and actions. Additionally, the verse implies that the disbelievers are spiritually blinded, unable to see the truth and guidance that is present in front of them.
orig: وظللنا عليكم الغمام وأنزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And indeed, We have said to you, 'Enter this town and eat from it freely wherever you wish, and enter the gate prostrating and say, 'Relieve us of our sins, and we will be forgiven.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Israelites' disobedience and their refusal to enter the promised land. Despite God's command to enter the land and take possession of it, the Israelites were afraid and refused to do so. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Israelites were supposed to enter the land with humility, symbolized by the act of prostration, and to seek forgiveness for their sins. The verse serves as a reminder that disobedience and lack of faith can lead to missed opportunities and negative consequences.
orig: وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم وسنزيد المحسنين

translation: And We have not sent down the Book to you, [O Muhammad], except that you may clarify to them that which they have differed over, and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to provide clarity and guidance to those who have differed in their beliefs and to serve as a source of mercy for those who believe in it. The verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a means of resolving disputes and providing guidance for those who seek to live righteously.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأنزلنا على الذين ظلموا رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when Moses asked for water for his people, We said, 'Strike the rock with your staff.' And there gushed forth from it twelve springs, and all the people knew that the water was from God, and they drank from it, and they were not oppressors in the earth, nor did they cause corruption.
interpretation: The verse describes the miracle of the gushing forth of twelve springs from the rock when Moses struck it with his staff, as commanded by God. The verse emphasizes that the water was a blessing from God, and all the people knew it, and they drank from it. The verse also highlights the righteousness of the people, stating that they were not oppressors and did not cause corruption on earth. The verse serves as a reminder of God's provision and blessings, and the importance of being grateful and righteous.
orig: وإذ استسقى موسى لقومه فقلنا اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانفجرت منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم كلوا واشربوا من رزق الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And when Moses said to his people: 'Indeed, we have been oppressed. Let us strike with our wealth and our children and our women and our offspring, and let us cry out to our Lord for help.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is speaking to his people, who have been oppressed and persecuted by their enemies. He suggests that they should unite and fight back against their oppressors, using their wealth, children, women, and offspring as a means of defense. The verse highlights the desperation and hopelessness of the people, who feel that they have no other choice but to cry out to God for help. It also emphasizes the idea that the people have been wronged and are seeking justice and relief from their oppressors.
orig: وإذ قلتم يا موسى لن نصبر على طعام واحد فادع لنا ربك يخرج لنا مما تنبت الأرض من بقلها وقثائها وفومها وعدسها وبصلها قال أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير اهبطوا مصرا فإن لكم ما سألتم وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير الحق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, those who have Judaized, the Sabians, and the Christians will be judged on the Day of Resurrection, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity of faith and the idea that all believers, regardless of their specific religion, will be judged by God on the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes that there will be no fear or sadness for those who have lived righteously, indicating that they will be rewarded for their good deeds. The verse also underscores the idea that true faith is not limited to one particular religion, but rather encompasses all those who believe in God and live according to His commandments.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى والصابئين من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And recall when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you, 'Take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it, that it may benefit you.'
interpretation: The verse reminds the Prophet Moses and the Children of Israel of the covenant they made with God and the miraculous event when the mountain was raised above them. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and adhering to the teachings and commands given by God, which are for their own benefit and guidance. The verse also highlights the idea that the covenant and the revelation were not just a one-time event, but a continuous reminder and guidance for the believers.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: Then, after that, your hearts became hardened, so that they were like rocks, or even harder.
interpretation: The verse describes how the people's hearts became hardened and callous, likening them to rocks, indicating a state of spiritual hardship and resistance to God's guidance. The verse suggests that this hardening of the heart is a consequence of their disobedience and rejection of God's signs and messengers, leading them further astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: ثم توليتم من بعد ذلك فلولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لكنتم من الخاسرين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you are not aware of it. Indeed, the wicked will be questioned about their sins on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of communities in the past that were wiped out by God's punishment. The verse highlights the ignorance of the current generation about these past events and serves as a warning that the wicked will be held accountable for their actions on Judgment Day. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the punishment of the wicked is not limited to this life, but will continue in the afterlife, where they will be questioned about their sins and held accountable for their actions.
orig: ولقد علمتم الذين اعتدوا منكم في السبت فقلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And We have made it a punishment for those who were warned, that they were warned and did not turn back.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the destruction of the town was not only a punishment for their sins but also a warning for those who were aware of the warning signs and still chose not to repent. The use of the phrase 'And We have made it a punishment' suggests that the punishment was not just a natural consequence of their actions, but a deliberate act of God's judgment. The phrase 'for those who were warned' suggests that the people had been warned of the consequences of their actions, but chose to ignore the warning. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of human choice and action.
orig: فجعلناها نكالا لما بين يديها وما خلفها وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And when Moses said to his people, 'Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow.' They said, 'Are you taking us in ridicule?' He said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is instructed by God to command his people to slaughter a cow, but they react with disbelief and mockery, thinking that Moses is joking or trying to deceive them. Moses responds by seeking refuge in God from being among the ignorant, indicating that he is not trying to deceive them but rather convey the message of God. The verse highlights the importance of following the commands of God, even when they may seem strange or difficult to understand, and the danger of mocking or disobeying God's commands.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه إن الله يأمركم أن تذبحوا بقرة قالوا أتتخذنا هزوا قال أعوذ بالله أن أكون من الجاهلين

translation: And they say, 'Call upon your Lord for us that He may make clear to us what has been revealed to you. Indeed, God knows that which has been revealed to you.' Say, 'All revealed knowledge is with God, and I am only a warner.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a request made by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask God to clarify what has been revealed to him. The Prophet responds by saying that all revealed knowledge belongs to God and that he is only a warner, indicating that he is not the source of the revelation but merely a messenger tasked with conveying the message. The verse highlights the limit of the Prophet's role and emphasizes God's sovereignty over all knowledge and revelation. It also underscores the idea that the Prophet's mission is not to provide new information or guidance but to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to remind them of God's presence and authority.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا فارض ولا بكر عوان بين ذلك فافعلوا ما تؤمرون

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord for us that He may make clear to us what has befallen us.' He said, 'Indeed, it is a cow, yellow and of a certain age, which has been decreed for you. So, when they saw it, they were stunned.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the people of Prophet Moses were afflicted with a deadly disease and were desperate for a solution. They asked Moses to ask God for guidance, and God revealed to Moses that the cure for their disease was a yellow cow of a certain age. When the people saw the cow, they were amazed and humbled by the power and wisdom of God. The verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in God's guidance, even in the face of seemingly impossible challenges.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما لونها قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة صفراء فاقع لونها تسر الناظرين

translation: They said, 'Call upon your Lord to make clear to us what the cow should be. Indeed, we will be guided aright if Allah wills.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the Israelites' request to Moses to seek guidance from God regarding the sacrifice of a cow, which they believed would absolve them of their sins. The verse emphasizes their recognition of God's power and authority, acknowledging that they will be guided aright only if God wills. The verse also underscores the idea that guidance and enlightenment come from God alone, and that human beings must seek His guidance and surrender to His will in order to find the right path.
orig: قالوا ادع لنا ربك يبين لنا ما هي إن البقر تشابه علينا وإنا إن شاء الله لمهتدون

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I will slaughter it (the camel) and bring it to them, and they will eat it, and their hearts will be comforted.' But then they did not do it, so he (Salih) said, 'Bring me a fat calf and they will eat it, and they will be fed.'
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Salih and the people of Thamud who were punished by God for their disobedience. The verse highlights the mercy and compassion of Prophet Salih, who wanted to help his people by sacrificing a camel to feed them. However, the people of Thamud refused to listen and instead, they killed the camel, which led to their destruction. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of listening to God's messengers and following their guidance, lest one suffers the same fate as the people of Thamud.
orig: قال إنه يقول إنها بقرة لا ذلول تثير الأرض ولا تسقي الحرث مسلمة لا شية فيها قالوا الآن جئت بالحق فذبحوها وما كادوا يفعلون

translation: And when you killed a soul, you were jealous of it, and Allah is the one who brings it out, and you concealed what was in your breasts, and Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the crime of murder and its gravity in the eyes of God. The verse specifically highlights the jealousy and envy that can motivate such a heinous act, and how it is a violation of the sanctity of human life, which is a gift from God. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge of the secrets of the heart and the fact that He will bring to light what is hidden in the breasts of people. The verse serves as a warning against violence and a reminder of the accountability of human beings before God.
orig: وإذ قتلتم نفسا فادارأتم فيها والله مخرج ما كنتم تكتمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فقلنا اضربوه ببعضها كذلك يحيي الله الموتى ويريكم آياته لعلكم تعقلون

translation: Then He turned to you from after that, that He may test you, and forgive you. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse explains how God turned to the people after they had been hardened and became like stone, indicating that they had become spiritually lifeless and unresponsive to God's guidance. The purpose of God's turning to them was to test them and forgive them, signifying that God is forgiving and merciful, and that He gives people the opportunity to repent and turn back to Him. The verse highlights God's mercy and willingness to forgive those who are willing to repent and change their ways.
orig: ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And they await eagerly that the angels should come to them [in punishment], but they will not come except in the form of a great storm, and they will not receive any warning before it.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of those who reject God's message and await the punishment of the angels. Instead of receiving the punishment they desire, they will be met with a great storm that will bring destruction and no warning will be given to them beforehand. The verse highlights the severity of God's punishment and the certainty of its arrival, as well as the foolishness of those who reject God's message and choose to await the punishment instead of turning to Him in repentance.
orig: أفتطمعون أن يؤمنوا لكم وقد كان فريق منهم يسمعون كلام الله ثم يحرفونه من بعد ما عقلوه وهم يعلمون

translation: And when they (the believers) met those who believed not, they said: 'We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us, and in what was sent down to Ibrahim and Ismail and Ishaq and Ya'qub and the Tribes, and in the Book given to Musa and in the Book given to 'Isa, son of Maryam, and in the Revelation given to the Prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him (Allah) we submit.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the believers when they encountered those who did not believe in God. The believers declared their faith in God and in the revelations sent to the prophets, including Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, as well as the books given to Moses and Jesus, and the revelations given to the prophets. The verse emphasizes the unity of the believers and their submission to God, rejecting any distinction between the prophets and their messages. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not limited to a particular prophet or revelation, but encompasses the belief in one God and the recognition of all His messengers.
orig: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا قالوا آمنا وإذا خلا بعضهم إلى بعض قالوا أتحدثونهم بما فتح الله عليكم ليحاجوكم به عند ربكم أفلا تعقلون

translation: And they know not that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ignorance of those who think they can hide their thoughts and actions from God. It emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all things, including what people conceal and reveal. It serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and that nothing is hidden from Him. It also implies that those who think they can hide their wrongdoing from God are mistaken and will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: أولا يعلمون أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, but they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who are illiterate and do not have a deep understanding of the Scripture. They rely on hearsay and assumptions rather than actual knowledge. The verse suggests that they are not familiar with the contents of the Scripture and are only speculating about its meaning. It serves as a warning against those who claim to have knowledge of the Scripture without actually understanding it, highlighting the importance of seeking knowledge through authentic sources and not relying on assumptions or hearsay.
orig: ومنهم أميون لا يعلمون الكتاب إلا أماني وإن هم إلا يظنون

translation: Woe to those who write the Book with their own hands and then claim that it is from God, that they may exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they have earned.
interpretation: The verse condemns those who falsely attribute their own writings to God, seeking to profit from them. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their offense, using the word 'woe' twice to express the severity of their punishment. The first 'woe' is for their actions, writing the Book with their own hands and claiming it is from God, while the second 'woe' is for the consequences of their actions, the price they will have to pay for their deception. The verse serves as a warning against fraudulent claims of divine inspiration and the dangers of using religion for personal gain.
orig: فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم ثم يقولون هذا من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا فويل لهم مما كتبت أيديهم وويل لهم مما يكسبون

translation: And they say, 'We will not be punished except according to a fixed decree.' But their belief in a fixed decree will not save them from the punishment. Or do they say, 'We will not be punished except according to a fixed decree'? But their belief in a fixed decree will not save them from the punishment. Or do they say, 'We will not be punished except according to a fixed decree'? But their belief in a fixed decree will not save them from the punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' misconception that they will not be held accountable for their actions and that they will not be punished except according to a fixed decree. The verse refutes this idea by stating that their belief in a fixed decree will not save them from the punishment. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is certain and that it will come regardless of their beliefs or excuses. The verse also highlights the futility of their argument that they will not be punished except according to a fixed decree, as if they are trying to shift the blame from themselves to God. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and self-deluded, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their beliefs will not save them from the punishment.
orig: وقالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودة قل أتخذتم عند الله عهدا فلن يخلف الله عهده أم تقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And they have earned a bad deed, and their affair is in the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have earned a bad deed and their ultimate destination in the Hereafter. Their actions have led them to be the companions of the Fire, indicating that they will reside in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment and serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بلى من كسب سيئة وأحاطت به خطيئته فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, they are the dwellers of Paradise, they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward for those who believed in God and did good deeds. The phrase 'الجنة' (Paradise) refers to a place of eternal bliss and happiness, where believers will reside after death. The use of 'خالدون' (abide) emphasizes that their stay in Paradise will be forever, indicating that it is not a temporary reward. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their faith and actions will lead them to a beautiful outcome in the afterlife.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And remember when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel: 'Worship none but Allah and be good to parents, the near relatives, the orphans, the poor, and the traveler.' And you said: 'We agree.' Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you are witnesses.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Children of Israel and reminds them of the covenant they made with God, which includes worshipping only Allah and treating their parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers with kindness. The verse highlights the importance of fulfilling this covenant and warns against turning away from it, as only a few of them did. The verse serves as a reminder to the Muslim community to adhere to their covenant with God and to be mindful of their responsibilities towards the vulnerable members of society.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله وبالوالدين إحسانا وذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وقولوا للناس حسنا وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة ثم توليتم إلا قليلا منكم وأنتم معرضون

translation: And recall when We took your covenant, not to shed each other's blood or drive each other out of your homes. Then you ratified it, and you are witnesses.
interpretation: This verse refers to the covenant made between the Muslim community and the Meccan tribes, known as the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. The verse highlights the importance of the covenant and the obligation of both parties to refrain from violence and aggression against each other. The verse also emphasizes the significance of the Muslim community's commitment to the covenant and their responsibility to uphold it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of keeping promises and fulfilling obligations, and it highlights the significance of peaceful coexistence and the avoidance of conflict.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم ولا تخرجون أنفسكم من دياركم ثم أقررتم وأنتم تشهدون

translation: Then you killed yourselves and expelled a group of you from their homes, and you supported one another against them with sin and aggression. And if they come to you, they will dispute with you, and if they prevail over you, they will be tyrants over you. Do they not think about the near punishment? Indeed, Allah will not fail in His promise. Indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the believers' behavior, who have turned against each other and fought among themselves. The verse describes how they have killed each other and expelled some of their own people from their homes. The verse warns them that their actions will lead to severe punishment from God, who will not fail in His promise. The verse also highlights the irony of their behavior, as they claim to be believers but act against each other with sin and aggression. The verse serves as a reminder of the near punishment that awaits them if they do not change their ways and turn back to God.
orig: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم وتخرجون فريقا منكم من ديارهم تظاهرون عليهم بالإثم والعدوان وإن يأتوكم أسارى تفادوهم وهو محرم عليكم إخراجهم أفتؤمنون ببعض الكتاب وتكفرون ببعض فما جزاء من يفعل ذلك منكم إلا خزي في الحياة الدنيا ويوم القيامة يردون إلى أشد العذاب وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Those who exchange the life of this world for the Hereafter will not escape punishment. And they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who prioritize the life of this world over the Hereafter will face punishment in the afterlife. The phrase 'exchange the life of this world' implies a trade-off between the temporal pleasures of this life and the eternal reward of the Hereafter. The verse warns that those who make this trade-off will not be able to avoid punishment, and that they will not have any supporters or helpers on Judgment Day.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة فلا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Book and We sent after him messengers, and We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and We supported him with the Holy Spirit. But whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant and became rebellious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the succession of prophets sent by God, including Moses and Jesus, who were given clear signs and proofs of their prophethood. The verse also emphasizes the reaction of the people to these prophets, who were often met with arrogance and rebellion instead of submission to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and submission to God's commandments, and the consequences of rejecting His messengers and signs.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وقفينا من بعده بالرسل وآتينا عيسى ابن مريم البينات وأيدناه بروح القدس أفكلما جاءكم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسكم استكبرتم ففريقا كذبتم وفريقا تقتلون

translation: And they say, 'Our hearts are wrapped up, so they will not be reminded, and in their ears is deafness, and they will not be believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they are reminded of God's signs and admonitions. They respond by claiming that their hearts are wrapped up and they cannot be reminded of the truth. They also claim to have deafness in their ears, indicating that they are not willing to listen to the message. The verse suggests that their refusal to listen and believe is a result of their own choice, rather than any external factor. The verse serves as a warning to those who are resistant to the message of Islam, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their choices.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا غلف بل لعنهم الله بكفرهم فقليلا ما يؤمنون

translation: And when a book came to them from Allah, confirming what was with them, they turned against those who disbelieved, so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse refers to a situation where a group of people were given a book or a revelation from God that confirmed and reinforced their existing beliefs. However, instead of embracing the truth and righteousness, they rejected it and turned against those who believed in it. The verse warns that the curse of God is upon those who reject faith and choose to disbelieve, and that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به فلعنة الله على الكافرين

translation: And they say, 'We have believed in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey.' But then they turn away, and soon they are rebellious again.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who claim to believe in God and the Messenger, but their actions do not match their words. They quickly turn away from their faith and return to their disobedient ways. This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but do not follow through with their beliefs in their actions. It serves as a warning to those who are insincere in their faith and a reminder that true belief is reflected in one's actions, not just in words.
orig: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله على من يشاء من عباده فباءوا بغضب على غضب وللكافرين عذاب مهين

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has revealed,' they said, 'We believe in what has been revealed to us,' and they disbelieve in what is beyond that, while it is the truth confirming what is with them.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to believe in the revelations of Allah. They claim to believe in what has been revealed to them, but they reject what is beyond that, which is the truth that confirms their own scriptures. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of the disbelievers, who claim to be believers but reject the truth that is presented to them. It serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of the Prophet Muhammad's message and reminds them that the truth is consistent across all revelations, and that rejecting it will only lead to their own destruction.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم آمنوا بما أنزل الله قالوا نؤمن بما أنزل علينا ويكفرون بما وراءه وهو الحق مصدقا لما معهم قل فلم تقتلون أنبياء الله من قبل إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, the example of Moses had come to you, and then you took the calf [in worship] after him, and you were unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to the incident of the golden calf, where the Israelites, shortly after being freed from slavery in Egypt, created an idol in the form of a calf and worshiped it, thereby disobeying the commands of Moses and God. The verse highlights the ingratitude and injustice of the Israelites, who quickly forgot the blessings and miracles that God had bestowed upon them through Moses and instead turned to idolatry. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of loyalty and obedience to God and His prophets, and warns against the dangers of disobedience and ingratitude.
orig: ولقد جاءكم موسى بالبينات ثم اتخذتم العجل من بعده وأنتم ظالمون

translation: And when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you, 'Take what We have given you with strength and listen to Our words.' They said, 'We hear and disobey.' Their hearts were filled with disbelief and rebellion. Say, 'How wretched is that which your faith enjoins upon you! How evil is what they have been enjoined!'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Israelites, who were given the Torah and the covenant of God, but they rejected it and instead chose to disobey and rebel. The verse highlights the irony of their disobedience, as they claimed to be believers but their actions proved otherwise. The verse also emphasizes the severity of their disbelief and the consequences they will face for their rejection of God's commandments. The verse serves as a warning to all who claim to be believers, reminding them of the importance of living according to their faith and not just claiming to believe.
orig: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واسمعوا قالوا سمعنا وعصينا وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل بكفرهم قل بئسما يأمركم به إيمانكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the Last Home with Allah is for you, if you are righteous. Indeed, they will not be harmed by the punishment, and if they were to be punished, they would not be harmed by the punishment, and if they were to be punished, they would not be harmed by the punishment.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the assurance of a blessed life in the Hereafter for those who are righteous and faithful. The verse emphasizes that the righteous will not be harmed by the punishment of God, indicating that their faith and good deeds will protect them from His wrath. The verse also implies that the punishment is not necessarily a physical one, but rather a spiritual and moral purification for those who have strayed from the right path. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in sin and injustice, encouraging them to repent and turn to God for forgiveness and guidance.
orig: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And indeed, We will not delay the punishment for the wicked. It shall come to them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and justice, stating that He will not delay punishment for those who have earned it. The punishment will come suddenly, catching the wicked off guard and unaware, indicating that they will not have the opportunity to repent or make amends for their actions.
