The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the need to repent and turn to righteousness.
orig: ولن يتمنوه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And they will be surprised when they are gathered to Hell, and it will be said to them: 'Surely, you were My servants who used to glorify Me, but you used to love to be praised for what you were not doing. So, now, your punishment will be doubled, and you will not be helped.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene on Judgment Day when the wicked will be gathered to Hell and confronted with their misdeeds. They will be surprised and regretful, realizing too late that their earthly pursuit of praise and recognition was meaningless and led them astray. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, which will be doubled due to their arrogance and lack of sincerity. The verse serves as a warning to those who prioritize worldly recognition and fame over their relationship with God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of living a life of righteousness.
orig: ولتجدنهم أحرص الناس على حياة ومن الذين أشركوا يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة وما هو بمزحزحه من العذاب أن يعمر والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Say, 'Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision?' Say, 'They are for those who believe in the unseen, in the name of Allah they are given.'
interpretation: This verse is a response to those who reject the idea of Prophethood and the revelation of God. The verse argues that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been given the Qur'an, which is a mercy and a guidance from God, and that it is a proof of his prophethood. The verse also emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a collection of words, but it is a revelation from God, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the angel Gabriel. The verse also emphasizes the importance of faith in the unseen, which is a fundamental aspect of Islam. The verse also highlights the idea that the Qur'an is a guidance and a mercy for the believers, and that it is a proof of God's favor and blessing upon them.
orig: قل من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك بإذن الله مصدقا لما بين يديه وهدى وبشرى للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town that was unjust, and We had given them a chance to repent, but they refused. And for the disbelievers, their Lord is indeed angry.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's message and refusing to repent from sinful ways. The use of the phrase 'many a town' emphasizes the repetition of this cycle throughout history, where communities have been given the opportunity to turn to God but have chosen to reject His message. The phrase 'their Lord is indeed angry' underscores the gravity of their actions and the certainty of their punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's wrath.
orig: من كان عدوا لله وملائكته ورسله وجبريل وميكال فإن الله عدو للكافرين

translation: And indeed, We have sent you clear signs and examples, and none deny them except the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and abundance of the signs and examples that God has sent to humanity through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the fact that these signs and examples are so clear and convincing that no one can deny them except those who are stubbornly rebellious and disobedient. The verse serves as a warning to those who refuse to believe, reminding them that their denial is not due to a lack of evidence or clarity, but rather due to their own stubbornness and refusal to submit to the truth.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليك آيات بينات وما يكفر بها إلا الفاسقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أوكلما عاهدوا عهدا نبذه فريق منهم بل أكثرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when a messenger from God came to them, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs, as if they knew nothing.
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of some people who were given the Scripture (i.e., the Jews and Christians) when a messenger from God came to them, confirming the truth of their scriptures. Instead of accepting the message, they rejected it and threw the Book of God behind their backs, indicating their disregard for God's message and their unwillingness to submit to His will. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who claim to have knowledge of the Scripture but reject the truth when it is presented to them.
orig: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم كأنهم لا يعلمون

translation: Follow what the devils said to the angels of God concerning Solomon's kingdom, and Solomon disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching the people magic and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut, and what they taught to the king's people, without knowledge, so they became sorcerers, and what they knew was only a test, and they knew that whoever bought it would not benefit them, and they knew that they would not cause harm to anyone except by God's leave, and they knew that they would not be able to harm anyone, for they had already known the consequences of their actions, and they had already known the evil that they had earned.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the devils who taught magic to the people of Solomon's kingdom, and how Solomon disbelieved and became a sorcerer. The verse highlights the negative consequences of their actions, as they became sorcerers and caused harm to themselves and others. The verse also emphasizes the idea that their actions were a test from God, and that they would not be able to harm anyone except by God's leave. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in magic and other forms of disbelief, reminding them of the negative consequences of their actions and the powerlessness of their actions against God's will.
orig: واتبعوا ما تتلو الشياطين على ملك سليمان وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس السحر وما أنزل على الملكين ببابل هاروت وماروت وما يعلمان من أحد حتى يقولا إنما نحن فتنة فلا تكفر فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله ويتعلمون ما يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق ولبئس ما شروا به أنفسهم لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And if only they had believed and been righteous, they would have had a reward from Allah, a good reward, if only they had known.
interpretation: The verse highlights the regret that the disbelievers will have on the Day of Judgment, realizing that they could have had a good reward from God if they had believed and lived righteously. The verse emphasizes the idea that faith and righteousness are the keys to earning God's reward, and that those who reject faith will miss out on this reward. The phrase 'if only they had known' suggests that the disbelievers were ignorant of the truth and failed to recognize the opportunity they had to earn God's favor. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to encourage others to do the same, as it is the only way to earn God's reward and avoid regret on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not say 'ra'ina' but say 'unzurna' and listen and obey the disbelievers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers not to use the term 'ra'ina' (which means 'our shepherd') when addressing their leaders or guides, but instead to use the term 'unzurna' (which means 'our guardian' or 'our protector'). The verse also emphasizes the importance of listening and obeying the leaders, as disobedience will result in a painful punishment for the disbelievers. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to authority and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا وللكافرين عذاب أليم

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not an angel been sent down to him? Indeed, We send down (revelation) only by the command of your Lord. Indeed, Allah is of His servants (only) a Warner.
interpretation: The disbelievers in this verse are questioning the authenticity of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) prophethood, asking why an angel has not been sent down to him. The response from God is that revelation comes only by the command of the Lord, and that God chooses whom He wills to send His message. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not just a prophet, but a Warner, whose role is to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the right path. The verse also highlights the idea that God's sovereignty and power are not limited to the physical realm, but also extend to the spiritual realm, and that He chooses whom He wills to guide and whom He wills to leave astray.
orig: ما يود الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب ولا المشركين أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم والله يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And whatever calamity befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the calamities that befall individuals or communities are a result of their own actions and choices. It suggests that the suffering is a consequence of their sins and injustices, and that God is merciful and forgiving, willing to pardon those who repent and make amends. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of our actions are not random or arbitrary, but rather a reflection of our own choices and the natural order of the universe. It also highlights the importance of taking responsibility for our actions and seeking forgiveness when we have wronged.
orig: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And do you not know that Allah has sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and that there is no protector or helper for you besides Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over all of creation, including the heavens and the earth. It is a reminder that God is the only one who can provide protection and help, and that believers should turn to Him alone for assistance. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and authority, and encourages believers to rely on Him in times of need.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And how many a prophet has been deceived by the deceiver when he was deceived, and the deceiver has gone astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the phenomenon of false prophets who deceive their followers and lead them astray. The verse emphasizes the idea that these false prophets are themselves deceived by Satan, who is the ultimate deceiver. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be cautious of those who claim to be prophets but are actually leading them astray, and to only follow those who are truly guided by God.
orig: أم تريدون أن تسألوا رسولكم كما سئل موسى من قبل ومن يتبدل الكفر بالإيمان فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفارا حسدا من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق فاعفوا واصفحوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And establish prayer and give zakat, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah of what you do, sees.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer and giving zakat (charity) as a means of purifying one's soul and seeking Allah's blessings. The verse also reminds believers that their actions are being observed by Allah, and that they will be rewarded for their good deeds. The phrase 'whatever good you put forward for yourselves' suggests that even small acts of kindness and generosity will be recognized and rewarded by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a virtuous life and to strive for good deeds, as they will be held accountable for their actions on Judgment Day.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله إن الله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And they say, 'Never will we be believers until we see the Garden of Eden with our own eyes.' But how will they know the reality of the Garden of Eden when they have been blind to the signs of God in this life?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who demand to see the Garden of Eden before they believe. The verse suggests that their demand is misguided, as they have failed to recognize and acknowledge the signs of God in their lives. The verse implies that the disbelievers are spiritually blind and, therefore, unable to recognize the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and instead rely on their senses to guide them. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and submitting to the signs of God in this life, rather than waiting for a miraculous experience.
orig: وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة إلا من كان هودا أو نصارى تلك أمانيهم قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And indeed, Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. Indeed, He will be questioned about his people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Abraham and how he was tested by God with certain commands, which he fulfilled. The verse highlights Abraham's obedience and faith in God, and how he will be questioned about his people on Judgment Day. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow in Abraham's footsteps and be obedient to God's commands, and to be prepared for the Day of Judgment.
orig: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: The Jews say, 'The Christians have nothing to do with this. nor do the Christians have anything to do with this. They read the Book as such, and those who do not know say, 'If only God would judge between us and them on the Day of Resurrection, surely God will judge between them.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the conflict between the Jews and the Christians, each claiming that the other has nothing to do with the truth. The verse highlights their ignorance and lack of understanding of the true teachings of their respective religions. They rely on their own interpretations of the scriptures, rather than seeking guidance from God. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God will be the ultimate judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, and that He will distinguish between truth and falsehood.
orig: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء وهم يتلون الكتاب كذلك قال الذين لا يعلمون مثل قولهم فالله يحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who prohibits the mention of Allah's name in His mosques and strives to destroy them? It was not for them to enter them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who prohibit the mention of Allah's name in mosques and strive to destroy them. These individuals are described as unjust and will face consequences in both this life and the Hereafter. In this world, they will experience disgrace, and in the Hereafter, they will face a great punishment. The verse highlights the gravity of their actions and serves as a warning to those who seek to prevent the worship of Allah and destroy His places of worship.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه وسعى في خرابها أولئك ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the east and the west. Whichever way you turn, there is the face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is all-encompassing and knowledgeable.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipresence and knowledge. It suggests that no matter which direction one turns, they will always be facing Allah, indicating that He is present everywhere and aware of all things. The verse also highlights Allah's vast knowledge, implying that He is aware of all things, including the actions and thoughts of His creation. It serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is always watching and aware of their actions, and that they should strive to live a righteous life in accordance with His will.
orig: ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله إن الله واسع عليم

translation: And they say, 'God has taken a son.' Glory be to Him! No, indeed, whatever is in the heavens and earth is His. All is obedient to Him.
interpretation: The verse addresses the misconception that God has taken a son, which is denied by the speaker. The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, stating that everything in the heavens and earth is His and is obedient to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and authority, and that He is the only one worthy of worship and obedience.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه بل له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And the heavens and the earth and everything in them were created, and when He (God) decreed a matter, He only said to it, 'Be,' and it was.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of the universe and everything in it by God's command. The verse emphasizes the power of God's word, whereby He simply speaks and His will is done. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the significance of His command in shaping the world and all that exists.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض وإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who do not know say, 'Had God willed, we would not have worshiped idols, or had He not willed, we would not have been polytheists.' Those before them did the same, their hearts resemble each other. We have detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: The verse addresses the excuses made by those who reject God's message, claiming that they would not have worshiped idols or been polytheists if God had not willed it. The verse refutes this argument by pointing out that such excuses are similar to those made by previous generations who also rejected God's message. The verse emphasizes that the signs and evidence of God's oneness are clear and available for those who are willing to understand and accept the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who are resistant to God's message, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their choices.
orig: وقال الذين لا يعلمون لولا يكلمنا الله أو تأتينا آية كذلك قال الذين من قبلهم مثل قولهم تشابهت قلوبهم قد بينا الآيات لقوم يوقنون

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a messenger of God, sent to convey the message of Islam and warn people of the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'bringer of good news' refers to the Prophet's task of announcing the good news of God's mercy and forgiveness to those who believe and follow His commandments, while the phrase 'warner' highlights his responsibility to warn people of the punishment they will face if they reject God's message. The verse underscores the importance of the Prophet's mission and the gravity of the message he conveyed.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion. Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance.' And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would have from Allah no protector or helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Jews and Christians will never be satisfied with Muslims until they abandon their own religion and adopt theirs. The verse warns Muslims against conforming to the desires of others, especially when it goes against the guidance of Allah. It reminds them that Allah's guidance is the only true guidance and that following any other path will leave them without protection or support from Allah. The verse encourages Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by external pressures or influences.
orig: ولن ترضى عنك اليهود ولا النصارى حتى تتبع ملتهم قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعد الذي جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital. They [are the ones who] believe in it and who disbelieve in it, they are the losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an, the holy book of Islam, and its role in guiding people to the right path. The verse indicates that those who have been given the book, meaning the Muslims, recite it with its true recital, indicating that they understand and follow its teachings. The verse also warns those who reject the book, describing them as losers. The verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an in the lives of Muslims and serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يتلونه حق تلاوته أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you, and that I have preferred you over the nations.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the children of Israel and reminding them of the special favor and blessings that He has bestowed upon them. The verse emphasizes the idea that God has chosen the children of Israel to be His chosen people, and that He has given them a special status and privilege above other nations. The verse serves as a reminder to the children of Israel to be grateful for God's blessings and to live up to the responsibilities that come with being God's chosen people.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين

translation: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another, and no compensation will be accepted from it, nor will intercession be of benefit, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of individual responsibility and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. On that day, no one will be able to help another, nor will material possessions or social status be of any use. The verse warns against relying on intercession or compensation to save oneself from God's punishment. Instead, each person must turn to God and seek His mercy and forgiveness in order to be saved.
orig: واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس شيئا ولا يقبل منها عدل ولا تنفعها شفاعة ولا هم ينصرون

translation: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make me an imam for the people,' he replied, 'I will make you an imam for the people.' And when he said, 'And from my offspring?' He said, 'My covenant will not be granted to the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham asks God to make him an imam (leader) for the people, and God agrees. However, when Abraham asks that his offspring also be made imams, God rejects this request, stating that His covenant (of leadership) will not be granted to the wrongdoers. This verse highlights the importance of leadership and the responsibility that comes with it. It also emphasizes that leadership is not a birthright, but rather a trust that must be earned through righteousness and justice. The verse serves as a reminder to leaders that they must rule with fairness and integrity, and that their leadership is not a guarantee of salvation for their people.
orig: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن قال إني جاعلك للناس إماما قال ومن ذريتي قال لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We have made the House a place of return for the people and a sanctuary. And take the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer. And We entrusted to Abraham and Ishmael that they purify My House for those who circumambulate the House, and those who stand and those who bow and those who prostrate.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance of the Kaaba as a sacred place of worship and a symbol of unity for the Muslim community. The verse also highlights the importance of prayer and the role of Abraham and Ishmael in purifying the House of God. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to maintain the purity of their faith and their devotion to God, as well as their responsibility to protect and preserve the sacred places of worship.
orig: وإذ جعلنا البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى وعهدنا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل أن طهرا بيتي للطائفين والعاكفين والركع السجود

translation: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city a secure and peaceful place, and provide for its people from the fruits of the earth, and from the blessings of the Hereafter.' And whoever rejects, I will give him a little enjoyment, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire, and that is a wretched destination.
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is praying to God to make Mecca a peaceful and secure place, and to provide for its people from the fruits of the earth and the blessings of the Hereafter. The verse then warns those who reject God's blessings and choose to disbelieve, that they will be given a short period of enjoyment, but ultimately, they will be compelled to the punishment of the Fire, which is a wretched destination. The verse highlights the importance of gratitude and faith in God's blessings, and serves as a warning to those who reject God's message.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا بلدا آمنا وارزق أهله من الثمرات من آمن منهم بالله واليوم الآخر قال ومن كفر فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره إلى عذاب النار وبئس المصير

translation: And indeed, Abraham raised the foundations of the House and Ishmael, our Lord, accept our sacrifice. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes the story of Prophet Abraham and his son Ishmael, who were instructed by God to build the Kaaba in Mecca. The verse highlights the significance of the Kaaba as a sacred place of worship and the importance of following God's commands. The phrase 'our Lord, accept our sacrifice' indicates that the act of building the Kaaba was a form of worship and an expression of submission to God. The final phrase, 'Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing', emphasizes God's attribute of being all-hearing and all-knowing, signifying that He is aware of all our actions and thoughts, and that we should always be mindful of His presence.
orig: وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت وإسماعيل ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: Our Lord, make us Muslims, Your religion, and make our descendants a Muslim community, and grant us a noble reputation in this world and forgive us, for You are the Acceptor of Repentance, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God to make the speaker and their descendants Muslims, and to grant them a good reputation in this world. The verse also asks for forgiveness, acknowledging that God is the Acceptor of Repentance and the Most Merciful. The verse highlights the importance of faith and reputation in Islam, and serves as a reminder to believers to live a righteous life and seek forgiveness for their sins.
orig: ربنا واجعلنا مسلمين لك ومن ذريتنا أمة مسلمة لك وأرنا مناسكنا وتب علينا إنك أنت التواب الرحيم

translation: Our Lord, send among them a messenger from themselves, who will recite Your verses to them and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them, for You are the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to God to send a messenger to guide the people and teach them the ways of God. The messenger is asked to recite the verses of God to the people, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and purification, and highlights God's power and wisdom. It is a call for spiritual guidance and a reminder that God is the ultimate source of knowledge and wisdom.
orig: ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And who is more astray than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them, and he forgets the meeting of his Lord? Indeed, We have given him a great authority over his own self, but he does not prevent the evil of his soul.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who are reminded of God's signs and verses but choose to ignore them and turn away. They are so caught up in their own desires and worldly pursuits that they forget the ultimate purpose of their creation and the meeting with their Lord. The verse highlights the irony of how such individuals have been given free will and the ability to choose between right and wrong, yet they still choose to ignore the truth and follow their own desires. This verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of God's signs and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن يرغب عن ملة إبراهيم إلا من سفه نفسه ولقد اصطفيناه في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And when his Lord said to him, 'Submit!' He said, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when God commanded Abraham to sacrifice his son Ismail as a test of his faith. Abraham's response, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,' shows his complete surrender to God's will and his willingness to obey His command, even if it meant sacrificing his own son. The verse highlights Abraham's faith and trust in God, as well as his willingness to put God's commands above all else, including his own desires and emotions. It serves as an example for believers to follow, reminding them of the importance of submitting to God's will and trusting in His wisdom.
orig: إذ قال له ربه أسلم قال أسلمت لرب العالمين

translation: And Abraham left his legacy to his sons, and Jacob said, 'O my sons! Indeed, God has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of religious inheritance and the significance of leaving a righteous legacy for future generations. Abraham, a great prophet and leader, passed on his faith and values to his sons, emphasizing the importance of submission to God's will and living a life in accordance with His commandments. The verse also underscores the idea that Islam is a religion that values peace and harmony, as the word 'Muslims' in the verse implies a sense of surrender or submission to God's will, rather than a sense of conflict or violence.
orig: ووصى بها إبراهيم بنيه ويعقوب يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And (remember) when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'What do you worship?' They said, 'We worship your Lord and the Lord of your fathers, Ibrahim, Ismail, and Ishaaq, one God, and to Him we submit (as Muslims).
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is asking his father and people about their beliefs and they respond by stating that they worship one God, the same God worshiped by Abraham's ancestors, Ibrahim, Ismail, and Ishaaq. The verse highlights the unity of God and the continuity of the message of monotheism throughout the generations. It also emphasizes the submission of Abraham and his descendants to the will of God, signifying their commitment to follow God's commandments and live according to His will.
orig: أم كنتم شهداء إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه ما تعبدون من بعدي قالوا نعبد إلهك وإله آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق إلها واحدا ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they say, 'Be Jews or Christians, you will be guided.' Say, 'Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth.' And he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse addresses the situation where some people are trying to persuade others to adopt their religion, either Judaism or Christianity. The response given by the believers is that they follow the religion of Abraham, which is a monotheistic religion that inclines towards truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of Abraham, who is considered a patriarch of the three major monotheistic religions, and rejects the idea of polytheism.
orig: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا قل بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are submitters [to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the message of all prophets and the belief in one God. It emphasizes that all prophets had a common message, that of submission to the will of God, and that there is no distinction between them. It also emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of all prophets, including Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jesus, and the Descendants. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not exclusive to the prophet Muhammad, but rather it is a continuation of the message of all prophets before him. It also emphasizes the importance of submitting to God's will and following His commandments.
orig: قولوا آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى وما أوتي النبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And indeed, those who believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, and those who are fearful of their Lord - they are the ones who are [truly] guided by their Lord, and they will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, they are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of belief in the revelations of God, both past and present, and the fear of God. It emphasizes that those who believe and have fear of God will be guided by Him and will have their reward with Him. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance and success come from following God's teachings and living a life of obedience to Him.
orig: فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق فسيكفيكهم الله وهو السميع العليم

translation: And Allah's is the most beautiful names, so let the names of the servants of Allah be Abdullah (slave of Allah).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of Allah, the creator of the universe, by mentioning some of His most beautiful names. The verse encourages believers to use names that reflect their servitude to Allah, such as Abdullah, which means 'slave of Allah'. It highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging Allah's power, wisdom, and authority, and serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives in accordance with Allah's will.
orig: صبغة الله ومن أحسن من الله صبغة ونحن له عابدون

translation: Say, 'We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are submitters to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith and the belief in one God, and the belief in all the prophets and messengers sent by God. It stresses that all prophets were sent by the same God and that their message was the same, that is, to worship only God and submit to His will. It also emphasizes the importance of not distinguishing between the prophets and their messages, and that all of them are equally important and valid. The verse also highlights the importance of submission to God and His commandments, and that it is the key to true faith and salvation.
orig: قل أتحاجوننا في الله وهو ربنا وربكم ولنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم ونحن له مخلصون

translation: And (mention, O Muhammad), when Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob were, as We took them as (Our) servants, and (We did not send them as) witnesses to Us, and We did not send them as guardians (of the message), and Allah is, over what they used to do, Witness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special relationship between God and the prophets Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob. God took them as His servants and did not send them as witnesses or guardians of the message. Instead, God Himself is the Witness over their actions. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and His knowledge of all that they did. It serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of our actions, and that we will be held accountable for our deeds.
orig: أم تقولون إن إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط كانوا هودا أو نصارى قل أأنتم أعلم أم الله ومن أظلم ممن كتم شهادة عنده من الله وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك أمة قد خلت لها ما كسبت ولكم ما كسبتم ولا تسألون عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the foolish among the people will say, 'What has turned them away from their qibla, which they used to face in prayer?' Say, 'To Allah belongs the east and the west. He guides not the disobedient people.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of the change of the qibla, the direction of prayer, from Jerusalem to Mecca. The foolish people are puzzled by this change and wonder why the Muslims are no longer facing Jerusalem. The answer is that Allah is the Lord of the east and the west, and He guides those who are obedient to Him. The verse emphasizes the idea that the change of the qibla is a sign of God's authority and power, and that those who question it are rebellious and disobedient.
orig: سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And thus We have made you a medium nation, that you may be witnesses to the people, and the Messenger a witness to you, and We did not make the Qibla which you used to face, except that We might know who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels. And indeed, it was not except that perhaps your Lord may test you, which of you is the most righteous. And Allah will not waste the faith of the believers. Indeed, Allah is Gentle with the people, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse explains the role of the Muslim community as a witness to the world and the Prophet Muhammad as a witness to the believers. The change of the Qibla from Jerusalem to Mecca is mentioned as a test for the believers, to distinguish those who truly follow the Prophet from those who are insincere. The verse also emphasizes that God will not waste the faith of the believers and that He is Gentle and Merciful towards them.
orig: وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيدا وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه وإن كانت لكبيرة إلا على الذين هدى الله وما كان الله ليضيع إيمانكم إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: And indeed, We have seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you toward a direction that will satisfy you. Indeed, We have seen the vision of the crescent moon, and the believers will rejoice at the sight of their Lord's bounty. Indeed, We have seen the turning of their faces toward the direction of the sacred mosque, and indeed, their faces will be turned toward the direction of their Lord's mercy. Indeed, those who have been given knowledge see that the truth is from your Lord, and that which they used to reject will be made clear to them.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) ascension to heaven, where he was given the responsibility of leading the prayers for all the prophets and believers. The verse also alludes to the miraculous night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and the ascension to heaven, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) was given the honor of leading the prayers in the Masjid al-Aqsa. The verse emphasizes the Prophet's (peace be upon him) role as a leader and guide for all believers, and how he was chosen by God to convey the message of Islam. The verse also highlights the importance of the sacred mosque and the direction of prayer, and how it is a symbol of unity and guidance for believers. The verse ends by emphasizing the role of knowledge and understanding in recognizing the truth and the importance of accepting and following God's guidance.
orig: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم وما الله بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And if you were to follow their desires, after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers against following the desires of those who have received the Scripture (Jews and Christians) after the knowledge of the truth has come to them. The verse implies that those who follow their desires and inclinations, rather than the teachings of the Qur'an, will be considered among the wrongdoers and sinners.
orig: ولئن أتيت الذين أوتوا الكتاب بكل آية ما تبعوا قبلتك وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم وما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم من بعد ما جاءك من العلم إنك إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: Those who have been given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons, and indeed, there is a party of them who conceal the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a revelation from God and its recognition by the People of the Book, who are the Jews and Christians. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is as familiar to them as their own children, indicating its authenticity and their innate knowledge of its truth. However, the verse also acknowledges that there are those among the People of the Book who deliberately conceal the truth and reject the Qur'an's message, despite their knowledge of its authenticity.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم وإن فريقا منهم ليكتمون الحق وهم يعلمون

translation: And the truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the truth and not doubting the words of God. It implies that the truth comes from God and is not open to interpretation or debate. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical or hesitant to accept the teachings of God, reminding them that denying the truth will only lead to their own detriment.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And for every matter, there is a time, and everything is recorded in a book, indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that everything in the universe, including human actions and events, is subject to a predetermined plan and timeline set by God. The verse suggests that every matter has its own appointed time, and that everything is recorded in a book, indicating that God has complete knowledge and control over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of God's sovereignty and the importance of trusting in His plan, even when we may not understand the timing or outcome of events.
orig: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أين ما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And from where you come out (for dawn prayer) and cut off a portion of the masjid (al-Haram) and indeed it is (a place of) transgression (for you) that your Lord may destroy it (the masjid al-Haram) because of what you have done, and indeed Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of the sacred mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram) in Mecca, which was a place of great significance for the Muslim community. The verse suggests that the destruction was a punishment from God for the wrongdoings of the people, who had turned away from His commandments and became corrupt. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their religious obligations and who take their blessings for granted. It reminds them that God is aware of their actions and will hold them accountable for their deeds.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وإنه للحق من ربك وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And from where you come out, turn your face towards the sacred mosque, and indeed, the believers were commanded to do so, that they may be distinguished from the disbelievers. Do not fear them, fear Me, and that I may complete My favor upon you, and that you may be guided.
interpretation: In this verse, Muslims are commanded to face the sacred mosque in Mecca during prayer, which serves as a symbol of their faith and devotion to God. The verse also emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between believers and disbelievers, indicating that those who are faithful to God will be guided and receive His favor. The verse also reminds believers not to fear people, but to fear God instead, indicating that God's approval and guidance should be their ultimate concern.
orig: ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة إلا الذين ظلموا منهم فلا تخشوهم واخشوني ولأتم نعمتي عليكم ولعلكم تهتدون

translation: And We have sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves, who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom, and teaches you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a teacher and guide, sent by God to the people. He is described as a messenger who recites God's verses, purifies the people, and teaches them the Book (the Qur'an) and wisdom. The verse highlights the Prophet's ability to teach the people what they did not know, indicating that he was not only a conveyor of divine revelation but also a teacher who could help his followers understand and apply the teachings in their lives. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role in guiding humanity towards a righteous and just life.
orig: كما أرسلنا فيكم رسولا منكم يتلو عليكم آياتنا ويزكيكم ويعلمكم الكتاب والحكمة ويعلمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون

translation: And remember Me, and do not forget Me, and be grateful to Me, and do not deny Me.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful to God, and warns against forgetting and denying Him. The verse highlights the reciprocal relationship between God and His creation, where God remembers and blesses those who remember and worship Him, and forgets those who forget and deny Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay mindful of God's blessings and to cultivate a spirit of gratitude, humility, and obedience.
orig: فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا تكفرون

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and prayer for believers, reminding them that Allah is with those who are patient and that seeking help through these means will bring them closer to Allah. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah in times of hardship and to trust in His plan, rather than resorting to other means or seeking help from other sources. It serves as a reminder that true strength and support come from Allah, and that patience and prayer are key to receiving His help and guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not say that those who are killed in the way of Allah are dead. Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive it.
interpretation: This verse addresses the common misconception that martyrs are dead. The Qur'an corrects this misconception by clarifying that martyrs are not dead, but rather they are alive and receiving sustenance from Allah. The verse emphasizes that the perceived separation between life and death is a veil that prevents us from seeing the reality of the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that the sacrifice of martyrs is not in vain and that their reward is with Allah.
orig: ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات بل أحياء ولكن لا تشعرون

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a decrease in wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, poverty, and loss of lives and crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience during these trials, as it is a quality that is highly valued in Islam. The phrase 'give good tidings to the patient ones' suggests that those who are patient during these trials will receive good news, indicating that their patience will be rewarded in the hereafter.
orig: ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين

translation: And when a calamity befalls them, they say, 'Indeed we belong to God, and to Him we will return.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the response of the believers when faced with adversity. It emphasizes their trust and faith in God, acknowledging that they belong to Him and will eventually return to Him. The phrase 'Indeed we belong to God' signifies their recognition of God's sovereignty and their submission to His will. The phrase 'and to Him we will return' underscores the belief in the afterlife and the eventual return to God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith during difficult times and to find solace in the knowledge that they will ultimately return to God.
orig: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

translation: And upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and it is they who are the guided ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who have been guided by God and are recipients of His blessings and mercy. The verse emphasizes the idea that the believers are not only guided but also blessed and recipients of God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that they are not only guided but also loved and cared for by God, and that they should continue to live according to His will in order to receive His blessings and mercy.
orig: أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be amidst gardens and rivers of paradise. If you see them, you will recognize them by their marks, and you will know them by their distinguishing features. And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward of the righteous in paradise, who will be surrounded by gardens and rivers. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment, which can come at any time, either in the morning or at noon. The verse emphasizes the recognition and distinction of the righteous, indicating that their good deeds and faith will be evident and acknowledged by God. The destruction of unjust towns serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن يطوف بهما ومن تطوع خيرا فإن الله شاكر عليم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear to the people in the Scripture, they will be cursed by God and cursed by those who curse.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the consequences of concealing or distorting the message of God as revealed in the Qur'an. Those who deliberately hide or distort the truth will be cursed by God and by those who curse. The verse emphasizes the importance of spreading the message of God and not hiding it from others. It also serves as a warning to those who might try to distort the message for their own purposes, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they do so.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى من بعد ما بيناه للناس في الكتاب أولئك يلعنهم الله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

translation: Except those who repent, believe, and do good deeds, for them Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the possibility of redemption for those who have committed wrongdoing. It emphasizes that those who repent, believe, and do good deeds will have their past wrongs transformed into good deeds, indicating a complete transformation and a fresh start. The verse underscores the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, who is willing to pardon and transform the lives of those who turn to Him in repentance and righteousness.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا وبينوا فأولئك أتوب عليهم وأنا التواب الرحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them will be the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of disbelief and the rejection of God's message. The 'curse of Allah' refers to the wrath and punishment that awaits those who reject faith, and the 'angels' and 'all the people' indicate that this punishment is not only from God but also from the entirety of creation, signifying the gravity of the offense. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of the truth of Islam, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار أولئك عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And your god is one God, there is no god except Him, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. It stresses that there is only one God who is worthy of worship, and that all other deities or objects of worship are false and futile. The verse also highlights the attributes of God, describing Him as 'the Beneficent' and 'the Merciful', indicating that He is a loving and compassionate God who desires the well-being of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus their devotion solely on God and to reject all other objects of worship, trusting in His mercy and grace.
orig: وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail through the sea with that which profits men, and the water which Allah has sent down from the sky, thereby reviving the earth after its death and dispersing therein all kinds of beasts, and the winds which scatter clouds and the clouds which are driven between the sky and the earth, are indeed signs for people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world. The creation of the heavens and the earth, the cycle of day and night, the movement of ships on the sea, the rain that revives the earth, and the winds that scatter clouds are all evidence of God's existence and authority. The verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of these natural phenomena and their role in sustaining life on earth. The verse also suggests that people who reflect on these signs will come to understand and appreciate the beauty and complexity of God's creation.
orig: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار والفلك التي تجري في البحر بما ينفع الناس وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among the people are those who take other than Allah as their object of desire, loving them with a love that is due to Allah alone. And those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. And if those who did wrong could see, when they behold the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the difference between those who worship and love Allah alone and those who worship and love other things, such as wealth, power, or status, alongside Allah. The verse emphasizes that the love and obedience due to Allah is not shared with anyone or anything else. The verse also warns those who commit injustices and wrongdoing that they will face severe punishment from Allah, and that Allah has all power and authority over all things. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to strengthen their love and devotion to Allah and to avoid associating partners with Him.
orig: ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله والذين آمنوا أشد حبا لله ولو يرى الذين ظلموا إذ يرون العذاب أن القوة لله جميعا وأن الله شديد العذاب

translation: And when the punishment came to them, those who were oppressed were saying: 'The believers were saying: 'Where is this from? Is this from God?'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the oppressed people when they were afflicted with punishment. They questioned the source of the punishment, wondering if it was from God. The verse highlights the tendency of people to question God's justice and wisdom when faced with adversity, and how they often fail to recognize the consequences of their own actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is a consequence of people's own actions, and that they should turn to God in repentance rather than questioning His justice.
orig: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب وتقطعت بهم الأسباب

translation: And those who followed said, 'If only we had a chance to punish them as they punished us, we would have taken revenge on them.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of those who were persecuted and oppressed for their beliefs. They express their desire for revenge against their oppressors, wishing they had the power to punish them as they were punished. The verse highlights the natural human desire for justice and retribution in the face of oppression. However, it also suggests that seeking revenge is not the best approach, as it can lead to an endless cycle of violence and retaliation. Instead, the verse implies that the oppressed should rely on God's justice and wait for His assistance, as He is the ultimate judge and avenger.
orig: وقال الذين اتبعوا لو أن لنا كرة فنتبرأ منهم كما تبرءوا منا كذلك يريهم الله أعمالهم حسرات عليهم وما هم بخارجين من النار

translation: O mankind, eat from what is lawful and good on the earth, and do not follow the footsteps of the devil. For he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life and avoiding the temptations of Satan. The verse encourages people to only consume what is halal, or permissible, and to avoid engaging in any actions that are forbidden by God. The verse also warns people against following in the footsteps of Satan, who is described as a clear enemy of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to always strive to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالا طيبا ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger to convey to you Our verses and purify you and teach you the Book and wisdom and to warn those who believe in Our verses about the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophethood and the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights three aspects of the Prophet's mission: purification, teaching, and warning. The Prophet was sent to purify the people from their sins and misguidance, to teach them the Qur'an and wisdom, and to warn them of the punishment of the Hereafter. The verse also underscores the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and wisdom, and the importance of believing in its message.
orig: إنما يأمركم بالسوء والفحشاء وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they said, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing, even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of the disbelievers who refused to accept the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Despite being told to follow the revelations sent by Allah, they insisted on following their ancestors' ways, even though their ancestors were not guided and lacked understanding. The verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance rather than blindly adhering to tradition and the ways of the ancestors. It also underscores the fact that guidance and understanding come from Allah alone, and that true guidance cannot be found through human effort or tradition.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما ألفينا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعقلون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: And they are like those who have disbelieved, who are deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not understand.
interpretation: The verse likens those who have disbelieved to those who are deaf, dumb, and blind. This metaphor highlights their inability to understand or respond to the message of Islam. Just as a deaf person cannot hear, a dumb person cannot speak, and a blind person cannot see, those who have disbelieved are unable to comprehend or respond to the truth of Islam. This verse emphasizes the spiritual blindness and deafness of those who reject God's message.
orig: ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق بما لا يسمع إلا دعاء ونداء صم بكم عمي فهم لا يعقلون

translation: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided you and be grateful to Allah, if you are believers indeed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and appreciation for the blessings and provision that God has bestowed upon believers. The use of the phrase 'good things' highlights the idea that the provision is not only sufficient but also beneficial and pure. The verse also serves as a reminder that gratitude is a fundamental aspect of faith and that believers should be mindful of the source of their blessings and express their gratitude to God. The phrase 'if you are believers indeed' underscores the idea that gratitude is a hallmark of true faith and that those who are truly grateful are the ones who are truly believers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم واشكروا لله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: Forbidden to you are the dead and the blood and the flesh of the pig and that which is slaughtered to other than Allah, and that which is killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a headlong fall or by the goring of horns, and that which is partly eaten by a wild animal, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death], and that which is sacrificed on stone altars, and [profanity] devoted to other than Allah. Whoever should come to his Lord as a disbeliever, his recompense will be with his Lord, and the angels will take him, and the righteous will be in gardens, questioning concerning the guilty.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the consumption of certain animals, including the dead, blood, pigs, and animals that have been sacrificed to idols or killed in a specific way. It also warns those who reject God's message and instead follow false deities, that their punishment will be severe, and they will be questioned by the righteous in paradise about their actions.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل به لغير الله فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and purchase a small gain - those consume not into their bellies except the Fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. For them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against concealing or distorting the teachings of the Qur'an for personal gain. Those who do so will face a painful punishment on Judgment Day, as they have ignored the true message of Islam and instead sought to exploit it for their own benefit. The verse emphasizes that neither God's words nor their own souls will be purified on the Day of Resurrection; instead, they will be consumed by the Fire of Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who would distort or hide the truth of Islam for personal gain, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزل الله من الكتاب ويشترون به ثمنا قليلا أولئك ما يأكلون في بطونهم إلا النار ولا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Those who have earned the punishment by exchanging the guidance of Allah for a price, and their torment will be multiplied on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have deliberately chosen to reject the guidance of Allah and instead followed their own desires and worldly gains. They have traded the eternal reward of the Hereafter for temporary earthly benefits. Their punishment will be multiplied on the Day of Resurrection, indicating that their rejection of Allah's guidance has led them to a path of destruction and they will face the consequences of their choices.
orig: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى والعذاب بالمغفرة فما أصبرهم على النار

translation: It is because Allah has revealed the Book with the truth; indeed, those who differed in the Book are in a great dissension.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, indicating that it is the word of God as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also highlights the division and disagreement among those who have differed in their understanding and interpretation of the Book, indicating that their divergence is a result of their own personal biases and misinterpretations, rather than any fault in the Book itself.
orig: ذلك بأن الله نزل الكتاب بالحق وإن الذين اختلفوا في الكتاب لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: By no means (should it be so) that the verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions and deeds, as the punishment can come at any time, without warning. It also emphasizes the importance of faith in God, the Hereafter, and the Day of Judgment, as well as the importance of being kind and charitable to others, especially the poor and needy. Additionally, the verse emphasizes the importance of prayer, giving charity, and patience during times of hardship and difficulty.
orig: ليس البر أن تولوا وجوهكم قبل المشرق والمغرب ولكن البر من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر والملائكة والكتاب والنبيين وآتى المال على حبه ذوي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل والسائلين وفي الرقاب وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء وحين البأس أولئك الذين صدقوا وأولئك هم المتقون

translation: O you who have believed, it is decreed upon you to kill the murderer, the free man for the free man, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. Whoever finds relief in his brother's crime, let him pay the diyah with goodwill and follow up with good treatment. That is a relief from your Lord and a mercy. Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse establishes the principle of retaliation or qisas in cases of murder, where the punishment should fit the crime. The verse emphasizes the importance of equal retaliation, regardless of the social status of the victim or the perpetrator. The verse also encourages the forgiveness and pardon of the victim's family, and offers a way out of the cycle of violence through the payment of diyah (blood money) and good treatment. The verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of taking a life and the importance of justice and mercy in Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم القصاص في القتلى الحر بالحر والعبد بالعبد والأنثى بالأنثى فمن عفي له من أخيه شيء فاتباع بالمعروف وأداء إليه بإحسان ذلك تخفيف من ربكم ورحمة فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers in the Battle of Mecca. The verse describes the victory as a clear and manifest triumph, indicating that it was a decisive and conclusive victory, and that the triumph was evident to all. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and that He is always with them in their struggles against evil and injustice.
orig: ولكم في القصاص حياة يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تتقون

translation: And leave in the will for the believers who will inherit from you, a good legacy, that they may enjoy it perpetually; and restrain not the poor and the needy from it.
interpretation: The verse instructs believers to leave behind a good legacy for their inheritors, specifically mentioning the poor and the needy. The verse emphasizes the importance of not withholding the inheritance from these groups, suggesting that it is a moral obligation to ensure that they have access to the resources they need. The verse highlights the importance of social responsibility and the need to care for those who are less fortunate, ensuring that they have a chance to enjoy the blessings that have been bestowed upon them.
orig: كتب عليكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت إن ترك خيرا الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بالمعروف حقا على المتقين

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of his Lord's verses but turns away from them? Indeed, We will take vengeance on the wicked.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of ignoring or rejecting God's signs and verses. The person who is described in this verse is one who has heard the message of God but chooses to turn away from it. The verse emphasizes that such a person is unjust and that their actions will incur God's wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that God is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
orig: فمن بدله بعدما سمعه فإنما إثمه على الذين يبدلونه إن الله سميع عليم

translation: And whoever fears Allah and removes himself from wrongdoing and mischief, then surely Allah will grant him a way out. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fearing Allah and avoiding wrongdoing and mischief. The verse promises that those who do so will be granted a way out of their difficulties and hardships. The phrase 'a way out' can be interpreted both literally, as in a physical escape from a difficult situation, and figuratively, as in finding a solution to a problem. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: فمن خاف من موص جنفا أو إثما فأصلح بينهم فلا إثم عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fasting is decreed upon you as it was decreed upon those before you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fasting as a means of attaining righteousness and spiritual growth. The use of the phrase 'those before you' highlights the continuity of the divine message and the fact that fasting has been a common practice among God's servants throughout history. The verse also underscores the idea that fasting is not just a physical act, but a means of spiritual purification and self-refinement. The phrase 'that you may become righteous' suggests that fasting has a transformative effect on the individual, helping them to develop self-control, empathy, and a stronger connection to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أياما معدودات فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين فمن تطوع خيرا فهو خير له وأن تصوموا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed as guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and the Criterion. So, whoever witnesses the month should fast it, and whoever is ill or on a journey, then a number of other days. Allah desires ease for you, and does not desire hardship for you, and that you may complete the period, and that you may exalt Allah for what He has guided you, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the month of Ramadan and the revelation of the Qur'an during this month. It emphasizes that fasting during Ramadan is not only a duty, but also a means of ease and guidance for believers. The verse also highlights Allah's desire for believers to complete the period of fasting and to exalt Allah for His guidance. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of gratitude and recognizing the blessings of Allah in one's life.
orig: شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه ومن كان مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر ولتكملوا العدة ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And when My servants ask you about Me, then surely I am near, answering the caller when he calls upon Me. Therefore, they should respond to Me and believe in Me, so that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's closeness to His servants and His readiness to answer their prayers. The verse encourages the believers to have faith in God's ability to hear and respond to their prayers, and to respond to His call by obeying His commandments and following His guidance. The verse also highlights the importance of belief in God as a means of guidance and spiritual growth.
orig: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي لعلهم يرشدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم فتاب عليكم وعفا عنكم فالآن باشروهن وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل ولا تباشروهن وأنتم عاكفون في المساجد تلك حدود الله فلا تقربوها كذلك يبين الله آياته للناس لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not devour one another's wealth unjustly, nor bribe the officials with it, that you may knowingly devour a portion of the wealth of the people wrongfully, while you know.
