interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the responsibility of guiding others lies not with the believers, but with Allah. The verse warns against taking upon oneself the burden of guiding others, as it is ultimately up to God to guide those who have gone astray. The verse also serves as a reminder that the believers' role is to convey the message of Islam and invite others to the right path, but it is God who ultimately guides those who are willing to listen and follow. The verse encourages the believers to focus on their own deeds and seek God's guidance, rather than relying on their own abilities to guide others.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think that they will escape. Indeed, they will not cause failure [to Allah's plan].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who disbelieve in God and reject His message will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions. They may think they can outsmart God or avoid His punishment, but ultimately, they will not be able to thwart His plan. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that their disbelief will not save them from the consequences of their actions. It also highlights the power and authority of God, who is in control of all things and will not be defeated by those who reject Him.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly, their reward is with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of charity and generosity, particularly when it is done discreetly and without fanfare. The phrase 'by night and by day' suggests that the act of giving should be a continuous and consistent part of one's life, regardless of the time or circumstances. The phrase 'secretly and openly' emphasizes the importance of humility in giving, suggesting that one should not seek to draw attention to their charitable deeds. The verse also reassures the givers that their reward will be with God, and that they will not be afraid or saddened by their acts of generosity.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who consume usury will not stand except as stands one whom the devil has prostrated by his touch. That is because they say, 'Trade is like usury,' but God has permitted trade and forbidden usury. Those who are admonished by their Lord and desist will be rewarded with their past deeds, but the punishment will be doubled for those who return [to usury].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the prohibition of usury and warns those who engage in it. The verse likens those who consume usury to those who have been possessed by the devil, indicating the negative impact it has on their spiritual and moral state. The verse also highlights the difference between trade and usury, emphasizing that while trade is permitted, usury is strictly forbidden. The verse offers a chance for those who have engaged in usury to repent and desist, promising them a reward for their past deeds, but warns that those who return to usury will face double the punishment.
orig: الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس ذلك بأنهم قالوا إنما البيع مثل الربا وأحل الله البيع وحرم الربا فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه فانتهى فله ما سلف وأمره إلى الله ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And God obliterates the signs of the disbelievers and renders their deeds vain.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and authority over the disbelievers. The phrase 'يمحق الله' means 'God obliterates' and signifies that God has the power to erase or cancel out the signs of disbelief, rendering the deeds of the disbelievers vain and useless. The verse emphasizes that God does not approve of the actions of the disbelievers and will ultimately bring their deeds to nothing. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the ultimate authority of God.
orig: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات والله لا يحب كل كفار أثيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and maintained the prayer and given the zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and rewards that await the believers who have lived a righteous life, performed good deeds, maintained their prayers, and given zakah (charity). The verse emphasizes that these believers will have no fear of punishment or retribution, and they will not grieve on the Day of Judgment. Instead, they will receive their reward from Allah, indicating that their good deeds have been accepted and recognized by God. The verse serves as a motivation and encouragement for believers to continue living a virtuous life and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and leave what remains of the unlawful income, indeed, you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and avoiding any remaining unlawful income. The verse addresses the believers, reminding them that their belief in Allah and their faith in Him should be reflected in their actions and their relationship with wealth. The verse encourages them to leave any unlawful income, indicating that it is not worth risking their spiritual well-being and relationship with Allah for the sake of material gain. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is reflected in one's actions and that believers should strive to live a life that is pleasing to Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: So, if you do not do so (i.e., follow the Messenger's instructions), then fear the fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers, whose flames will not be extinguished (in this world or the Hereafter) and they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and choose to disobey God's commands. It describes the punishment they will face in the Hereafter, which is described as a fierce fire that will not be extinguished. The verse also emphasizes that the disbelievers will not receive any help or support, either in this life or the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and encourage others to do the same, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they continue on their current path.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تظلمون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims over their enemies in the Battle of Mecca. The verse describes the victory as a clear and manifest triumph, indicating that it was a decisive and conclusive victory, and a sign of God's favor and support for the believers. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to remain grateful for God's blessings and to continue to strive in His cause.
orig: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing the Day of Judgment, when every soul will be returned to Allah and held accountable for its actions. The verse underscores the idea that each person will receive exactly what they have earned, and that they will not be wronged in any way. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives in accordance with God's will and to be mindful of their actions, as they will ultimately be held accountable for them.
orig: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, when you are told to give charity, then give what is purified and do not withhold the best of it. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah of what you spend will see it.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving charity and the expectation that believers will give their best and not withhold it. The verse also reminds believers that God is aware of their actions and will see what they spend in charity. The verse encourages believers to be generous and give their best in charity, as it will be seen by God and will be a means of purification for them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله ذلكم أقسط عند الله وأقوم للشهادة وأدنى ألا ترتابوا إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And indeed, you are upon a plain method of religion, but those who are opposed to faith are in deviation and dissension. Do they think that their opposing your religion will invalidate it? Indeed, they are the ones who will be invalidated. Do they think that they can delude God? Indeed, God is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of Islam as a religion, in contrast to those who oppose it and are in a state of confusion and disagreement. The verse suggests that those who reject Islam are misguided and their attempts to undermine the religion will ultimately fail. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom, implying that He is aware of the actions and intentions of all individuals and will ultimately judge them based on their deeds.
orig: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وليتق الله ربه ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and authority over all things. It reminds believers that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to God and that they will be held accountable for their actions and thoughts, whether they are hidden or revealed. The verse also highlights God's power to forgive or punish as He sees fit, underscoring His justice and mercy. It serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives with a sense of accountability and to seek God's forgiveness and guidance.
orig: لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and so have the believers. Each one believes in God, His angels, His scripture, and His messengers. They say, 'We hear and we obey. Forgive us, our Lord. To You is the destiny.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith among believers and their commitment to following God's commands. The verse highlights the belief of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad peace be upon him) and the believers in the revelations sent by God. It also stresses the belief in God, His angels, scripture, and messengers. The verse concludes with the believers' acknowledgment of their submission to God and their request for forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God and the consequences of not following His commands.
orig: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير

translation: God does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear. He gets what he deserves, and so does she. Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not burden us as You did those before us. Our Lord, do not impose on us what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and mercy. It acknowledges that God does not expect more from a person than they are capable of, and that He will not hold us accountable for things that are beyond our control. The verse also highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and pardon from God, and implores Him to help believers against those who reject faith. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the protector of the believers and that He will help them in times of need.
orig: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: There is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsistent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. The phrase 'the Living' signifies that God is eternal and ever-present, while 'the Self-Subsistent' indicates that He is self-sufficient and does not need anything else to exist. The verse is a declaration of God's uniqueness and a reminder that all existence depends on Him. It is a call to monotheism and a rejection of any other deity or entity that may be considered divine.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه وأنزل التوراة والإنجيل

translation: And indeed, We have sent forth to the nations (prophets) to warn them, and We have brought down upon them (their) destruction (at the hands of the Israelites).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the sending of prophets to various nations to warn them of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards righteousness. The verse also mentions the destruction that befell those nations who rejected the prophets and refused to heed their warnings. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the certainty of His punishment for those who disobey Him.
orig: من قبل هدى للناس وأنزل الفرقان إن الذين كفروا بآيات الله لهم عذاب شديد والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Indeed, Allah does not conceal anything from the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power, stating that nothing in the earth or heavens is hidden from Him. This verse is a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that nothing can escape His observation. It serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives in accordance with God's commandments, as they are always under His watchful eye.
orig: إن الله لا يخفى عليه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: It is He who has created death and life, that He may test you, which of you is the best in deed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over life and death. By creating death, God has established a means of testing humanity, to see who among them is the most righteous and worthy of His reward. The verse highlights the idea that life and death are not random events, but rather tools that God uses to evaluate and judge human behavior. The verse also underscores the idea that the ultimate goal of human existence is to live a righteous life and to be judged as such by God.
orig: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هو الذي أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ فيتبعون ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة وابتغاء تأويله وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself, indeed You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, asking Him not to let the believers' hearts deviate from the path of guidance after He has guided them. The verse also asks for God's mercy, acknowledging that He is the source of all mercy and the One who can grant it. The verse highlights the importance of God's guidance and the need for His mercy in order to stay on the right path. It also emphasizes the dependence of believers on God and their recognition of His power and grace.
orig: ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: Our Lord, indeed You will gather the people on the Day of Judgment, there will be no doubt about it. Indeed, Allah will not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and authority as the creator and sustainer of the universe. The verse also highlights the certainty of the Day of Judgment, when all humanity will be gathered before God for judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human actions and the promise of God to reward or punish accordingly. It also underscores the idea that God is faithful to His promises and will not fail to fulfill His word.
orig: ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will not benefit from their wealth or their children from Allah anything, and they are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that wealth and children will not save the disbelievers from God's punishment. In fact, they will be the fuel for the Fire of Hell, indicating that their material possessions and offspring will not protect them from the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that their earthly possessions and families will not save them from the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك هم وقود النار

translation: And the people of Pharaoh and those before them had denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people of Pharaoh and previous nations who denied the signs of God, and how they were punished as a result. The verse emphasizes that it was not just Pharaoh, but many nations before him, who had rejected God's signs and were thus subject to His punishment. The phrase 'seized them for their sins' implies that God's punishment was a direct result of their disobedience and rejection of His signs. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآياتنا فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم والله شديد العقاب

translation: Say to those who have disbelieved that they will be defeated and gathered to Hell, and what a terrible destination!
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to inform the disbelievers of their fate. They will be defeated and gathered to Hell, a place of eternal punishment. The verse emphasizes the horror of Hell as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and choose to live in disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of one's actions in this life and the consequences of rejecting the truth.
orig: قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون وتحشرون إلى جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: And indeed, there was a sign for you in the two groups that met in combat, one group fighting in the cause of Allah and the other disbelieving. They advanced upon each other, [the believers] having superior numbers. Allah supported the believers with His victory. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslim army, led by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), fought against the pagan Meccans. The verse highlights the disparity in numbers between the two groups, with the Muslims being outnumbered. Despite this, Allah granted the Muslims victory, demonstrating His power and might. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's support for the believers and His ability to grant them victory, even in the face of adversity.
orig: قد كان لكم آية في فئتين التقتا فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة يرونهم مثليهم رأي العين والله يؤيد بنصره من يشاء إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: And indeed We have destroyed the likes of you, so how was the punishment of the deniers?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers, reminding them that they are not the first to reject God's message. The verse mentions the destruction of previous communities who also rejected God's messengers and were punished as a result. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, emphasizing that they will meet the same fate as those who came before them if they continue to reject God's message. The verse also highlights the temporary nature of worldly possessions and material wealth, which are ultimately insignificant in the face of God's judgment.
orig: زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا والله عنده حسن المآب

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.',
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by Allah to inform the people that he is only a warner, a person who gives warning, and that there is no God but Allah, the One and Only, who is the ultimate authority and power. This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the prophethood of Muhammad, and serves as a reminder to the people to turn to Allah and follow His commandments in order to avoid His punishment.
orig: قل أؤنبئكم بخير من ذلكم للذين اتقوا عند ربهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وأزواج مطهرة ورضوان من الله والله بصير بالعباد

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse describes the prayer of the believers who seek forgiveness and protection from God. They acknowledge their sins and ask for God's mercy, recognizing that they are worthy of punishment. The verse highlights the importance of faith and repentance, as well as the hope for God's forgiveness and protection from the punishment of Hell. The believers' request for protection from the Fire indicates their fear of God's punishment and their desire to avoid it. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them in the afterlife.
orig: الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار

translation: And the patient ones, and the truthful ones, and the obedient ones, and the devout ones, and the charitable ones are rewarded with their Lord's forgiveness and pleasure.
interpretation: The verse highlights the virtues of five different types of people who will be rewarded by God for their good deeds. The first group, 'al-sabirin' (the patient ones), refers to those who endure hardships and trials with patience and faith. The second group, 'al-sadiqin' (the truthful ones), are those who are truthful in their words and actions. The third group, 'al-qanitin' (the obedient ones), are those who are obedient to God and follow His commandments. The fourth group, 'al-munfiqin' (the devout ones), are those who are devoted to God and are mindful of their duties towards Him. The fifth group, 'al-musrifin' (the charitable ones), are those who give generously to others and are charitable with their wealth. The verse emphasizes that these virtues are not only praiseworthy but also rewarded by God with His forgiveness and pleasure.
orig: الصابرين والصادقين والقانتين والمنفقين والمستغفرين بالأسحار

translation: And God is witness that there is no god but He, and the angels, and the possessors of knowledge, upholding the justice. There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the fact that He is the only one worthy of worship. The verse also highlights the importance of knowledge and the role of the angels and the righteous in upholding justice. The phrase 'there is no god but He' is repeated twice for emphasis, underscoring the exclusivity of God's divinity and the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with God). The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to reject all forms of polytheism and idolatry.
orig: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the religion is Islam, and those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah - indeed, Allah is swift in [taking] account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of religion and the fact that all prophets and scriptures prior to the Qur'an were sent by God to guide humanity. However, the verse also acknowledges that disagreements and differences among people arose after the knowledge of God's message had been revealed, due to jealousy and rivalry. The verse warns those who reject God's signs and verses that they will be held accountable for their disbelief and will face swift punishment.
orig: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ومن يكفر بآيات الله فإن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And indeed, We have sent you (O Muhammad) as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner. And (We have sent) the Qur'an down to you, so that you may clarify to the people what has been revealed to them, and so that they may reflect.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminding him of his role as a messenger of God. God is emphasizing the importance of the Qur'an, which was revealed to the Prophet as a guidance and a mercy to humanity. The verse highlights the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam to the people and to clarify the truth that has been revealed to them. The verse also encourages the people to reflect on the message of the Qur'an and to recognize the truth in it.
orig: فإن حاجوك فقل أسلمت وجهي لله ومن اتبعن وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم فإن أسلموا فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who order justice from among the people - promise them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject God's signs and prophets and oppress and kill the righteous people who call for justice, that they will face a painful punishment. It emphasizes that denying God's revelations and persecuting the prophets and the righteous is a serious offense that will not go unpunished. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of such actions and encourages people to follow the path of justice and righteousness.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير حق ويقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life and the Hereafter, and they have no supporters.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have squandered their opportunities in this life and have not prepared for the Hereafter. They have no supporters or helpers, and their efforts have been in vain. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglecting their spiritual responsibilities and focusing solely on worldly pursuits. It reminds them that their efforts will be in vain and they will have no one to turn to for help in the Hereafter.
orig: أولئك الذين حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They were invited to the Book of Allah that they might arbitrate between them, then a party of them turned away, and they were averse.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and asks him if he has considered the people who were given a portion of the Scripture, referring to the Jews and Christians who had access to the Bible. They were invited to the Book of Allah, the Qur'an, to arbitrate between them and settle their disputes. However, a party of them turned away and refused to accept the Qur'an, showing aversion to its teachings. The verse highlights the rejection of the Jews and Christians to the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an, despite having the Scripture and knowing the truth.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يدعون إلى كتاب الله ليحكم بينهم ثم يتولى فريق منهم وهم معرضون

translation: And they said, 'We will not be punished except according to our deeds, and the punishment will not befall us except after a number of years.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's misconception that they will not be held accountable for their actions and that they will not be punished until after a long period of time. The verse emphasizes their wrong belief that they can escape God's punishment and their lack of understanding of God's power and justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who think they can evade God's punishment and encourages them to reflect on their actions and turn to righteousness.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودات وغرهم في دينهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Then how [will it be] when We gather them together for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be gathered together and rewarded or punished according to their deeds. The verse emphasizes the certainty of this day and the fact that each person will receive exactly what they deserve, without any injustice or wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of every individual and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the Hereafter.
orig: فكيف إذا جمعناهم ليوم لا ريب فيه ووفيت كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say: O Allah, Owner of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and take the kingdom away from whom You will, You exalt whom You will and abase whom You will, in Your hand is the good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, the owner of the kingdom, acknowledging His sovereignty and power over all things. The verse emphasizes God's ability to give and take away kingdoms, to exalt and abase whom He wills. The phrase 'in Your hand is the good' signifies that God has the power to grant prosperity and success to whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of God's authority and control over all aspects of life, and encourages the believer to trust in God's wisdom and justice.
orig: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء بيدك الخير إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: By the night as it conceals (the light of the sun), and by the day as it manifests (the light of the sun), and by the life that emerges from the dead, and by the death that emerges from the living, and by the alternation of the two, (the night and the day), and by the will (of God) that is not subject to account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the cycles of life and death, and the power of God's will that governs them. The first part of the verse describes the alternation of night and day, which symbolizes the cycles of life and death. The second part of the verse mentions the emergence of life from death and death from life, highlighting the cyclical nature of existence. The verse concludes by emphasizing that God's will is not subject to account or questioning, indicating that His power and wisdom are beyond human comprehension.
orig: تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل وتخرج الحي من الميت وتخرج الميت من الحي وترزق من تشاء بغير حساب

translation: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that, then he will not have any relationship with Allah, except that you fear them [the disbelievers]. And Allah cautions you against His punishment, and to Allah is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and allegiance among believers, and warns against forming alliances with non-believers. The verse prohibits believers from taking disbelievers as allies, emphasizing that doing so would be a betrayal of their faith and would lead to divine punishment. The verse also implies that fear of the disbelievers is not a valid reason for forming such alliances, and that true loyalty and fear should be reserved for Allah alone. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of standing by one's faith and principles, even in the face of adversity or fear.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, 'Indeed, what you conceal in your breasts or declare, Allah knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and His knowledge of all things, whether hidden or manifest. It reminds believers that God is aware of their thoughts, intentions, and actions, and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also highlights God's power and control over all things, indicating that He is capable of managing and governing all affairs, both in this life and in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives with integrity and righteousness, as they will be held accountable for their actions, and to trust in God's justice and wisdom in all matters.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: Every soul will find what it has done of good present on that day, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and between that (evil) was a great distance. And your Lord is full of grace towards His servants, but My punishment is severe.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when each person's soul will be confronted with their past actions, both good and evil. The good deeds will be presented as a manifestation of God's grace, while the evil deeds will be a source of regret and remorse. The verse emphasizes the idea that the consequences of one's actions will be severe, and that God's punishment is not to be taken lightly. The verse also highlights God's mercy and grace towards His servants, indicating that those who have lived righteously will be rewarded and protected from harm.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, 'If you love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a means of expressing love for Allah. By following the Prophet's teachings, one can earn Allah's love and forgiveness, and ultimately attain a state of spiritual purity and closeness to Allah. The verse also highlights Allah's attribute of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that even those who have committed sins can still seek forgiveness and find solace in Allah's mercy.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Obey Allah and the Messenger, for if you turn away, then indeed Allah does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger. The verse addresses the believers, reminding them that disobedience to God and His Messenger is a sign of disbelief. The verse warns the believers that if they turn away from the teachings of God and His Messenger, they risk earning God's displeasure. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God and His Messenger, and to be mindful of the consequences of disobedience.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah has chosen Adam and Noah and the descendants of Abraham and the descendants of Imran above the nations.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special status and distinction given by God to certain individuals and communities. Adam, the first human, is chosen as the father of humanity, and Noah, the prophet who saved his family and two of every kind of animal from the flood, is chosen for his righteousness. The descendants of Abraham, including Ishmael and Isaac, are chosen for their faith and obedience, and the descendants of Imran, including Mary, the mother of Jesus, are chosen for their piety and devotion. The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and the idea that He chooses whom He wills for His purposes, and that His choices are not limited by human expectations or criteria.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, said: 'O my Lord, indeed I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicating it to Your service. Accept it from me, for You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: Mary, the mother of Jesus, made a vow to God to dedicate her son to His service. She recognized God's greatness and acknowledged that her son was a gift from God, and she wanted to give him back to God as a sign of her gratitude. This verse highlights Mary's faith and devotion to God, as well as her willingness to submit to His plan. It also emphasizes God's attribute of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, indicating that He is aware of all things and is always ready to listen to those who call upon Him.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her through Our angel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was one of the devout ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her exceptional faith and devotion to God. The verse emphasizes Mary's purity and chastity, which was guarded by her father Imran. The verse also highlights the miraculous conception of Jesus, where God blew His spirit into Mary through the angel Gabriel. Mary's belief in God's words and scriptures, as well as her devotion to God, serves as an example for all believers. The verse also underscores the importance of faith and obedience to God, and how it can lead to righteousness and spiritual purity.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her garment through Our angel Gabriel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was one of the devout ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the annunciation of the birth of Jesus to Mary, the daughter of Imran. The verse emphasizes Mary's piety and her belief in God's message delivered by the angel Gabriel. The verse also highlights the miraculous nature of Jesus' conception, which was a result of God's divine intervention. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and grace, and the importance of faith and obedience to His will.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: And indeed, Zakariya prayed to his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
interpretation: The verse describes the prayer of Prophet Zakariya, who appealed to God for a righteous descendant. Zakariya's prayer was prompted by his desire for a child who would carry on his prophetic legacy and spread God's message. The verse highlights Zakariya's faith in God's ability to grant his request, as well as his trust in God's power to hear and respond to his supplications. The verse serves as an example of the importance of prayer and faith in God, and how they can lead to the fulfillment of one's hopes and desires.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: And the angels called out to him, 'Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah and honorable and a noble prophet.'
interpretation: The verse describes the angel's announcement to Zechariah of the birth of John the Baptist, who was a prophet and a messenger of God. The verse highlights the honor and nobility of John, who was chosen by God to play a significant role in preparing the way for Jesus. The verse also emphasizes the idea that John's birth was a miraculous event, as his mother was barren and his father was old. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and mercy in granting children to those who are faithful to Him.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: And my Lord said: 'Verily, We shall destroy the wrongdoers, and We shall leave none of them (alive) in the land, except a few who will be spared (as a warning) to the rest, in order that they may return (to the right path).'
interpretation: This verse describes God's plan to destroy the wicked people and spare only a few of them as a warning to the rest. The verse emphasizes God's power and authority to punish those who disobey Him and His prophets. The verse also suggests that the destruction will be total and complete, leaving none of the wrongdoers alive in the land, except for a few who will be spared to serve as a warning to others. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: And your Lord said, 'Make a sign for me, and I will make a sign for you. Indeed, I will not speak to the people for three days except by revelation, or your Lord's decree. Indeed, We are, in the remembrance of your Lord, frequently remembering.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask for a sign from Him, and in return, God will also give a sign to the Prophet. The sign requested by the Prophet is not specified in the verse, but the sign given by God is revealed in the next verse, which is the miraculous night journey of the Prophet from Mecca to Jerusalem and his ascension to heaven. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembrance of God and the Prophet's commitment to follow God's commands and remember Him frequently.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the world.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the angels appeared to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and delivered a message from God. The verse emphasizes the special status that God has given to Mary, choosing her above all other women in the world. The verse highlights God's grace and favor upon Mary, and serves as a reminder of the important role that she plays in the history of prophets and messengers. The verse also underscores the idea that God's choice and purification of Mary was not based on her own merits or actions, but rather on God's sovereign will and grace.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the world.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of Mary, the mother of Jesus, in Islam. Allah has chosen her, purified her, and given her a unique position among all women. This verse is often interpreted as a sign of Mary's virtues and her role as a symbol of purity and righteousness for Muslims.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: And indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], by the revelation of the Qur'an, and We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad, and highlights his role as a mercy to all nations. The verse underscores the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam, and his mission to spread God's mercy and guidance to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse also underscores the importance of the Qur'an as the literal speech of God, revealed to guide humanity to the right path.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: And the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him. His name is Jesus, the son of Mary, and he will be held in honor in this world and the Hereafter, and he will be of those who are near to God.'
interpretation: The verse is an announcement by the angels to the Virgin Mary that she will give birth to a son, Jesus, who will be a prophet and a messenger of God. The verse emphasizes the honor and respect that Jesus will receive both in this life and in the afterlife. The phrase 'son of Mary' signifies that Jesus was born of a virgin birth, and 'near to God' indicates that Jesus will have a special relationship with God and will be a vessel for God's message. The verse serves as a prophecy of Jesus' role as a prophet and messenger, and highlights his importance in the history of religion.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: And the people of the city came to the prophet in the morning and in the evening, crying and weeping, seeking the forgiveness of God.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's reaction to the prophet's message, as they came to him in large numbers, seeking forgiveness and repenting for their sins. The fact that they came to the prophet both in the morning and in the evening suggests that they were persistent in their quest for forgiveness and that they recognized the gravity of their mistakes. The verse highlights the power of the prophet's message and the people's recognition of their need for spiritual guidance and forgiveness.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: And He created death and life, that He may test you, which of you is the best in deed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of God's creation of death and life. The verse explains that the creation of death and life is a means of testing humanity, to determine who among them is the best in deed. The verse emphasizes the idea that the ultimate goal of human existence is to live a righteous life and to be tested in faith, obedience, and good deeds. The verse also underscores the idea that death is not an end in itself, but rather a means to an end, a tool for God to assess the faith and actions of humanity.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And He has taught you the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse highlights the revelation of divine scriptures, specifically mentioning the Qur'an, the Torah, and the Gospel. It emphasizes God's role as the source of knowledge and wisdom, underscoring the importance of religious education and guidance. The verse also suggests a connection between the Qur'an and previous scriptures, acknowledging their shared divine origin and complementary nature. The phrase 'and wisdom' may indicate that the Qur'an contains not only revelation but also sound counsel and guidance for believers.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And We sent to the Children of Israel: 'I will send to them a Messenger from among themselves, rehearsing to them My Signs and Sacred Laws.' I revealed to them how to create birds out of clay, and I healed the blind and the leper by God's leave. And I brought the dead to life by God's leave. And I informed you of what you ate and what you stored in your houses. Surely, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the miracles and signs that God sent to the Children of Israel through His messenger. The verse highlights God's power and authority in creating life and healing the sick, as well as His knowledge of all things, including what people eat and store in their homes. The verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel to believe in God and follow His commandments, and it also serves as a warning to those who deny God's signs and miracles. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience to God, and it encourages people to reflect on the signs and miracles that God has revealed to them.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And remember when Moses said to his people: 'O my people! Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you from there some information or a burning firebrand, so that you may warn your people and be mindful of your Lord.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is reminding his people of the miraculous event when he encountered a fire on Mount Sinai, which was a sign of God's presence and a manifestation of His power. Moses was instructed by God to bring a burning firebrand from the fire and use it as a warning to his people, reminding them of God's authority and their need to be mindful of His commands. The verse highlights Moses' leadership and his role as a prophet, as well as the importance of heeding God's messages and being mindful of His power and authority.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, my Lord and your Lord is Allah, so worship Him, this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the fact that He is the Lord of all creation, including the speaker and the audience. The verse encourages the audience to worship God and follow a straight path, indicating that the path of righteousness is clear and straightforward, and that those who follow it will be guided to the truth and avoid error.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And when they (the disbelievers) plotted against Jesus, son of Mary, We supported him, and We sent to him angels who fought along with him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the conspiracy of the disbelievers against Jesus, son of Mary, and how God supported him by sending angels to fight alongside him. The verse highlights God's protection and support for Jesus, and how He thwarted the plans of the disbelievers. The verse also emphasizes the belief in God and the oneness of God, as the angels who fought alongside Jesus were believers in God and acknowledged His power and authority.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and followed the Messenger, so write us down among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse expresses the believers' faith in the revelation sent by God and their commitment to follow the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the importance of being a witness to the truth and a faithful follower of the Prophet, which is a fundamental aspect of Islam. The verse also highlights the idea of being accountable for one's actions and being willing to testify to one's beliefs, as well as the importance of being part of a community of believers who share the same values and principles.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And they plotted and planned, and God planned, and God is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the contrast between the plans and schemes of human beings and the ultimate plan of God. The verse suggests that human beings may have their own plans and schemes, but ultimately, God's plan will prevail. The phrase 'khair al-makirin' (the best of planners) emphasizes God's ability to outsmart and outplan human beings. The verse serves as a reminder that human beings should not become too confident in their own plans and abilities, but rather, they should acknowledge and submit to the will of God.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: And indeed, Allah will say, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?"'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is addressing Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) and asking him if he had told the people to take him and his mother, Mary, as deities besides Allah. This verse is a reminder that Prophet Jesus, like all other prophets, was a human being and a servant of Allah, and that he was not divine or worthy of worship. The verse also emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the belief in the oneness of Allah, and serves as a warning against the dangers of polytheism and the association of partners with Allah.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And as for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and the severity of God's punishment for those who reject faith. The verse indicates that the punishment will be both in this world and the Hereafter, signifying that the consequences of disbelief are not limited to the present life but will also extend into the afterlife. The verse also emphasizes that the disbelievers will have no helpers or allies to protect them from God's punishment, indicating that they will be left alone to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their reward will be with their Lord, and Allah will not wrong them at all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who have faith and do good deeds will be rewarded by God. The use of the phrase 'their reward will be with their Lord' suggests that the reward is not only temporal but also spiritual, and that it will be given to them by God Himself. The second part of the verse, 'and Allah will not wrong them at all', serves as a reassurance that God will not oppress or wrong those who have believed and done good deeds. This verse serves as a motivation for believers to live a righteous life and to have faith in God's justice and mercy.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear verses and examples from the past, and lessons for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the Qur'anic message, which is full of examples and lessons for those who fear God. The verse highlights the significance of learning from the past and the importance of fearing God in order to live a righteous life. The phrase 'clear verses' refers to the clarity and simplicity of the Qur'anic language, making it easy for believers to understand and follow. The phrase 'examples from the past' refers to the stories of previous prophets and nations mentioned in the Qur'an, which serve as lessons for believers. The verse encourages believers to reflect on these stories and learn from their experiences, in order to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus with God is like the example of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was.
interpretation: This verse draws a parallel between the creation of Jesus and the creation of Adam. Just as God created Adam from dust, He created Jesus through a miraculous conception. The verse emphasizes the power of God in creating life and the similarity between the two prophets in terms of their divine origin. The use of the word 'Be' (kun) in both cases highlights the idea that God's command is sufficient to bring about creation, and that both Jesus and Adam were brought into existence through God's will and power.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: And the truth is from your Lord, so do not be of the doubters.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of accepting the truth and not doubting the words of God. The phrase 'min rabbik' (from your Lord) signifies the divine origin of the truth and underscores its authority and certainty. The verse encourages believers to have faith and confidence in God's words, rather than questioning or doubting them. It serves as a reminder that God's truth is absolute and unchanging, and that it is the responsibility of believers to accept and follow it without hesitation or skepticism.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then he turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have set veils over their hearts, lest they understand this Qur'an, and in their ears, deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for them whether you invite them or do not invite them, they will not follow you. Indeed, the wrongdoers will be companions in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who reject the message of the Qur'an and turn away from its teachings. They are described as unjust and their hearts are veiled, preventing them from understanding the Qur'an and its message. The verse warns that even if they are invited to guidance, they will not follow it and will instead remain in their state of disbelief and sin. The verse ends by stating that these wrongdoers will be punished in the Fire.
orig: فمن حاجك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنت الله على الكاذبين

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an is the true narrative, and there is no deity except Allah, and indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an, confirming its status as the word of God. It also underscores the unity of God and rejects the idea of polytheism, affirming that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship. The description of Allah as 'Al-Aziz' (the Exalted in Might) and 'Al-Hakim' (the Wise) highlights God's power and wisdom in revealing the Qur'an and guiding humanity towards righteousness.
orig: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: So, indeed, those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, they are forgiven, theirs is Paradise as a reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance, faith, and good deeds. It emphasizes that those who turn to God in repentance and commit to living a righteous life will be forgiven and rewarded with Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder that the path to salvation is through faith and good works, and that God is merciful and forgiving to those who seek redemption.
orig: فإن تولوا فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين

translation: Say, O people of the Book, come to a word common between us and you that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him, and none of us takes others as lords besides Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and agreement among people, specifically between Muslims and People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It encourages them to come to a common understanding and a shared belief in the oneness of God, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry. The verse also highlights the importance of not associating partners with God, whether it be other deities or human beings, and emphasizes the belief in the exclusive worship of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of the central tenet of Islam, the belief in the oneness of God, and the importance of unity and agreement among believers.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

translation: O people of the Book, do not be excessively eager in your religion, and do not say about God except the truth. The Torah and the Gospel were only revealed after him, but do you not reason?
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, that is, the Jews and Christians, and cautions them against being overzealous in their religion. They are warned not to attribute things to God that are not true, and are reminded that the Torah and the Gospel were revealed after the time of the Prophet Abraham. The verse encourages them to use reason and reflect on the signs of God's existence and message, rather than blindly following their own desires and misinterpreting God's word.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تحاجون في إبراهيم وما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل إلا من بعده أفلا تعقلون

translation: Here are the interpreters, they have interpreted for you what you have been given, though they are not aware of its interpretation, and God knows and you do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the irony of people who claim to be interpreters of religious texts, yet they themselves do not fully understand the true meaning behind the words. It highlights the limitations of human knowledge and the importance of humility in seeking guidance from God. The verse warns against relying solely on human interpretation and emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from God, who is the ultimate source of knowledge and wisdom.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء حاججتم فيما لكم به علم فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And Abraham was not a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a monotheist, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the belief in one God, and that Abraham, the father of the prophets, was a monotheist, a Muslim, and not a polytheist. The verse rejects the idea that Abraham was a Jew or a Christian, as these religions came later, and instead, emphasizes his belief in one God, which is the core of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder that the belief in one God is not limited to any particular religion or tribe, but is a universal truth that transcends all boundaries.
orig: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the first house [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah [Mecca], blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Kaaba in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam, and its significance as the first house of worship established for humanity. The verse emphasizes the blessings and guidance that the Kaaba represents for Muslims and the world at large. It also highlights the importance of the Kaaba as a symbol of unity and direction for believers, and serves as a reminder of the spiritual connection between Muslims and their Creator.
orig: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين

translation: And a group of the people of the Scripture said [to each other], 'Believe in that which has been revealed to the believers at the time of the Prophet, and do not follow the desires of those who do not follow the truth.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a situation where a group of people from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) were urged to have faith in the revelations received by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and not to follow the desires of those who reject the truth. The verse highlights the importance of adhering to the teachings of the Prophet and not being swayed by personal desires or the influence of those who reject the truth. It emphasizes the significance of following the guidance of God's messenger and the consequences of not doing so.
orig: ودت طائفة من أهل الكتاب لو يضلونكم وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: O people of the Book, do not be excessive in your religion, and do not say about God except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of God, and His word that He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in God and His messengers, and do not say, 'Three.' Refrain; better is it for you. God is only one God. Glory be to Him, that He should have a son. To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. God is sufficient for a witness.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, that is, the Jews and Christians, and warns them against exaggerating their religion and not to attribute false things to God. The verse specifically refers to the belief in the Trinity, which is rejected in Islam. The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and that He is sufficient as a witness. The verse also reminds the People of the Book that Jesus, whom they consider the Messiah, was only a prophet and a messenger of God, and that he was born of the Virgin Mary through the miraculous intervention of God's spirit. The verse ends by emphasizing the importance of belief in God and His messengers.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله وأنتم تشهدون

translation: O people of the Book, do not obscure the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, who are accused of distorting the truth and hiding it from others. The verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and transparency, and warns against spreading falsehood and deception. It serves as a reminder that truth is a fundamental value in any religious or moral system, and that hiding or distorting it is a violation of that value. The verse is a call to action, encouraging the People of the Book to refrain from such behavior and instead uphold the truth.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل وتكتمون الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And a party of the people of the Scripture said: 'Believe in the morning and disbelieve in the afternoon; and they were commanded to disbelieve in the afternoon, and they were returned to disbelief.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were given the Scripture (i.e., the Jews and Christians) who were commanded to believe in God and His Messenger in the morning, but they rejected faith in the afternoon. They were commanded to disbelieve in the afternoon, and as a result, they were returned to a state of disbelief. The verse highlights the hypocrisy and inconsistency of those who claim to be believers but fail to act accordingly. It serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not act according to their beliefs, reminding them that true faith requires consistent action and commitment.
orig: وقالت طائفة من أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالذي أنزل على الذين آمنوا وجه النهار واكفروا آخره لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And do not obey one whose religion is different from yours, until they follow your religion. Say, 'Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah. One to whom Allah gives guidance - he is guided to his Lord. And one whom He misguides - you will not find for him any guardian to guide him onto a straight path.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of Allah and not following anyone whose religion is different from yours. The verse warns against taking as a leader or guide someone who does not follow the religion of Allah, as they will not be able to guide others to the straight path. The verse also highlights the power of Allah in guiding and misguiding, indicating that those who are guided by Allah will be guided to their Lord, while those who are misguided will not have any guardian to guide them onto a straight path.
orig: ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم قل إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: And He it is Who sends His blessings upon whom He wills among His servants, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty and grace, as He bestows His blessings upon whomever He chooses among His servants. The verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, indicating that He is not limited by human expectations or deservingness. Rather, God's blessings are a manifestation of His grace and generosity, and He can bestow them upon anyone He wills, regardless of their past actions or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and forgiveness are not limited by human constraints, and that He is always ready to shower His blessings upon those who turn to Him in faith and obedience.
orig: يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And among the People of the Scripture are those who, if you entrust them with a large amount [of wealth], will return it to you with blessings, and among them are those who, if you entrust them with a single silver coin, will not return it to you unless you keep after them for it. That is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us concerning the unbelievers.' And they tell a lie concerning Allah while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the difference between two types of people among the People of the Scripture. The first group consists of those who are trustworthy and honest, and will return a large amount of wealth that has been entrusted to them, with blessings. The second group, on the other hand, is dishonest and will not return even a single silver coin unless constantly reminded. The verse suggests that this dishonesty is a result of their belief that they are not accountable for their actions towards non-believers. They also lie about Allah, knowing full well that their actions are against His teachings.
orig: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك ومنهم من إن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤده إليك إلا ما دمت عليه قائما ذلك بأنهم قالوا ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God tests people through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and fruits. However, the verse also emphasizes the importance of patience and resilience in the face of such challenges. The phrase 'give good tidings to the patient ones' suggests that those who are patient and persevering in the face of adversity will be rewarded and blessed by God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that trials and tribulations are a part of life, but that they should not lose hope or faith in God's mercy and justice.
orig: بلى من أوفى بعهده واتقى فإن الله يحب المتقين

translation: Indeed, those who barter away the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them. They will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the gravity of breaking the covenant with God and compromising one's faith for worldly gain. Those who do so will face severe consequences in the afterlife, including the loss of any spiritual reward and God's disfavor. The verse warns against prioritizing temporary, earthly benefits over one's relationship with God and the promise of the Hereafter. The punishment mentioned is not limited to the Hereafter but also extends to the present life, where such individuals will be deprived of God's guidance, mercy, and protection.
orig: إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا أولئك لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة ولا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, there is a group among them who distort the Scripture with their tongues, so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. And they say, 'This is from Allah,' but it is not from Allah. They say about Allah what is not true.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who manipulate and distort the words of the Qur'an, claiming that it is from God, but in reality, it is not. They use their own interpretations and twist the words of the Qur'an to suit their own agendas and beliefs, attributing their own ideas to God. The verse warns against such people and their false claims, emphasizing that their actions are not from God, but rather from their own imagination and desire to deceive.
orig: وإن منهم لفريقا يلوون ألسنتهم بالكتاب لتحسبوه من الكتاب وما هو من الكتاب ويقولون هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون

translation: And do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping only one God, Allah, and avoiding the worship of any other being or creature, including celestial bodies like the sun and the moon. Prostration is a sign of submission and worship, and it is only appropriate to direct it towards the Creator, Allah, who is worthy of all praise and worship. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to maintain their devotion to Allah and avoid any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: ولا يأمركم أن تتخذوا الملائكة والنبيين أربابا أيأمركم بالكفر بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون

translation: And when Allah made the Prophets' covenant, 'I will give you a Scripture and Wisdom, then comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, believing in him and supporting him.' He said, 'Do you agree and take this upon yourselves?' They said, 'We agree.' He said, 'Then bear witness and I am with you among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse describes the covenant that Allah made with the Prophets, where He promised to give them a Scripture and Wisdom, and then send a Messenger who would confirm and support their message. The verse highlights the importance of belief and support for the Messenger, and the responsibility of the Prophets to convey the message and bear witness to it. The verse also emphasizes the idea of accountability, as the Prophets are reminded that they will be witnesses for or against their communities on the Day of Judgment.
