orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة ثم جاءكم رسول مصدق لما معكم لتؤمنن به ولتنصرنه قال أأقررتم وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري قالوا أقررنا قال فاشهدوا وأنا معكم من الشاهدين

translation: And whoever does that (i.e., follows the messenger) after that (i.e., after the messenger's death), then those are the ones who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) after his death. The verse states that those who reject the message are transgressors, indicating that they have gone astray and are deserving of punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the consequences of rejecting his message.
orig: فمن تولى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And they belied the meeting of Allah, and His messengers, and they shall come out of the graves with their faces covered with shame and remorse.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who denied the meeting with Allah and His messengers. They will be resurrected from their graves on the Day of Judgment with their faces covered in shame and remorse for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting God's message and the certainty of the Hereafter.
orig: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون

translation: Say, 'We believe in God and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We do not differentiate between any of them. And we are submissive to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of all prophets and the belief in one God. It stresses that all prophets received revelations from the same God, and that there is no distinction between them. It also underscores the importance of submission to God's will, as expressed in the phrase 'we are submissive to Him.' The verse serves as a reminder that all prophets were sent by God to guide humanity, and that their messages were not contradictory but rather complementary, all coming from the same divine source.
orig: قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا وما أنزل على إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى والنبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him, and he will be of the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Islam as the only accepted religion by God. It warns those who seek to follow any other religion or belief system that it will not be accepted by God and they will be considered losers in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of embracing Islam as the only true religion and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كيف يهدي الله قوما كفروا بعد إيمانهم وشهدوا أن الرسول حق وجاءهم البينات والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those are the ones who have been cursed by Allah and angels and all the people, altogether.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the severe punishment that awaits those who have earned the wrath of Allah and the curses of the angels and all of humanity. The verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the curse, indicating that it is not limited to one group or individual, but rather it is a universal condemnation. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in opposition to Allah's commandments, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the certainty of their punishment.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم أن عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: Except those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the possibility of forgiveness and redemption for those who have committed wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes that even after committing injustices, one can still repent and make amends, and Allah will forgive and show mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's grace and mercy, encouraging individuals to turn towards righteousness and seek forgiveness.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief, their repentance will not be accepted, and they are the ones who are astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of apostasy, where individuals who have consciously rejected their faith and continue to commit acts of disbelief will not be forgiven. Their refusal to repent and return to the right path has led them astray, and they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who have turned away from their faith, encouraging them to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness before it's too late.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بعد إيمانهم ثم ازدادوا كفرا لن تقبل توبتهم وأولئك هم الضالون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, and theirs will be a punishment of Hell, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief and the certainty of punishment in Hell for those who die in a state of disbelief. The verse also highlights the idea that no one can intercede or help those who are in Hell, indicating that the punishment is absolute and cannot be mitigated by any means.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به أولئك لهم عذاب أليم وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And they will not attain piety until they spend from what they love and what they spend is not accepted, for indeed Allah, of what they spend, is Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that true piety is not achieved by simply giving away wealth, but rather by giving away what one loves and values the most. The phrase 'what they spend is not accepted' suggests that the act of giving should be done with a sincere intention and not for show or to gain recognition. The verse highlights the importance of giving with a pure heart and the fact that God is aware of all that we give and the intentions behind it.
orig: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون وما تنفقوا من شيء فإن الله به عليم

translation: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to itself before the Tawrah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Tawrah and recite it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the Children of Israel were allowed to eat all foods except for those that they had forbidden to themselves through their own religious practices before the revelation of the Tawrah. The verse challenges the Children of Israel to bring the Tawrah and recite it, suggesting that they are not truthful in their claims and that they have deviated from the true teachings of their religion. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to the true teachings of one's religion and not inventing new prohibitions or restrictions that are not based on divine revelation.
orig: كل الطعام كان حلا لبني إسرائيل إلا ما حرم إسرائيل على نفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of attributing lies to God, which is considered the utmost form of injustice. It suggests that those who deliberately fabricate such lies are the worst kind of wrongdoers, as they are not only disobeying God but also misleading others and leading them astray. The verse serves as a warning against spreading falsehoods and the importance of being truthful in one's beliefs and actions.
orig: فمن افترى على الله الكذب من بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And say, 'Truth is from Allah and falsehood is from Satan.' And say, 'Indeed, I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Most High.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of distinguishing between truth and falsehood and recognizing the source of each. The phrase 'Truth is from Allah' signifies that truth is a divine attribute and that it is only revealed through the prophets and messengers of God. On the other hand, 'falsehood is from Satan' indicates that falsehood and deception are the work of Satan, the enemy of God. The second part of the verse is a declaration of the oneness of God, emphasizing that there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Most High, and that the speaker is only a warner, a prophet or messenger, and not the source of the message itself.
orig: قل صدق الله فاتبعوا ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the first house established for the people was that of Bakka, blessed and guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the establishment of the first house of worship, specifically the Kaaba in Mecca, which was built by the Prophet Abraham and his son Ishmael. The verse emphasizes the significance of this event, describing the Kaaba as a source of blessing and guidance for all people. The verse also highlights the importance of the Kaaba as a symbol of unity and a focal point for the Muslim community, representing the connection between the believers and their Lord.
orig: إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة مباركا وهدى للعالمين

translation: And indeed, Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the story of Prophet Abraham, who was tested by God with certain commands and fulfilled them, demonstrating his obedience and righteousness. God rewarded him for his good deeds and recognized him as one of the righteous. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's commands and living a virtuous life, as it leads to divine reward and recognition. It also underscores the idea that God is aware of the actions of humanity and rewards those who do good.
orig: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ومن كفر فإن الله غني عن العالمين

translation: Say, O people of the Scripture, do not obscure the signs of Allah and do not deny them, for Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, specifically the Jews and Christians, and instructs them not to distort or conceal the signs of God, which include the miracles, prophecies, and revelations that were sent to them. The verse also warns them against denying or rejecting these signs, as God is fully aware of their actions and will hold them accountable. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with being the guardians of the Scripture and the importance of adhering to the truth and the commandments of God.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله والله شهيد على ما تعملون

translation: Say, 'O people of the Book, do not obscure the way of Allah with your opinions and do not seek to make it seem crooked while you know (the truth).'
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book, who are accused of distorting the message of God and spreading misinformation. The verse implies that they are intentionally trying to mislead people and lead them astray from the true path of God. The use of the word 'opinions' suggests that their actions are based on personal biases and interpretations rather than on the true teachings of God. The verse serves as a warning to those who twist the message of God to suit their own purposes and reminds them that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن تبغونها عوجا وأنتم شهداء وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Indeed, most hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, questioning their integrity and sincerity. It highlights the hypocrisy of claiming to be a believer while not acting accordingly. The verse emphasizes that actions speak louder than words and that true faith is reflected in one's actions, not just mere words. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to align their actions with their beliefs and to be mindful of their behavior, as it is the actions that will ultimately be judged by God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا فريقا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب يردوكم بعد إيمانكم كافرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكيف تكفرون وأنتم تتلى عليكم آيات الله وفيكم رسوله ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of living a life of obedience to Allah and dying as a Muslim. The phrase 'fear Allah as He should be feared' means to have a deep reverence and respect for Allah, and to live according to His commands. The verse serves as a reminder that life is short and that one should always be mindful of one's relationship with Allah, striving to live a life that is pleasing to Him. The verse also highlights the importance of dying as a Muslim, indicating that one's faith should be a central part of one's identity until the very end of one's life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided, and remember the favor of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so you became, by His grace, brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of fire, and He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses that you may be guided.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among believers, and how it is a blessing from God that they were able to overcome their differences and come together in faith. The verse also highlights God's favor upon them, in that they were once enemies, but He brought their hearts together and made them brothers. Additionally, the verse mentions a specific instance where God saved them from a dangerous situation, pulling them back from the brink of a pit of fire. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of God's guidance and protection, and encourages them to hold firmly to their faith and unity.
orig: واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And among you, there are some who propagate good and order what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of promoting good values and ordering what is right, while forbidding what is wrong. It emphasizes the positive impact of such actions on the individual and society, and describes those who do so as 'successful' or 'winners' in life. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility of every individual to stand up for what is right and to speak out against injustice, and assures them of a positive outcome for their efforts.
orig: ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And do not be like those who divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. And for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse warns against division and differing among the believers, especially after the truth has become clear to them. The verse implies that such division and differing is a result of disobedience and disregard for the truth, and that it will incur a severe punishment from God. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain united and steadfast in their faith, and to avoid allowing petty differences to cause division and strife among them.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم البينات وأولئك لهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On a Day when their faces will be whitened and their faces will be blackened. As for those who have been wicked, their faces will be blackened: Are you now rewarded for what you used to do?
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people's faces will be either whitened (symbolizing purity and innocence) or blackened (symbolizing sin and guilt). The verse addresses those who have lived a life of sin and injustice, suggesting that their faces will be blackened on that day as a consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that our actions have consequences and that we will ultimately be held accountable for them. The phrase "Are you now rewarded for what you used to do?" emphasizes the idea that our actions have consequences and that we will reap what we sow.
orig: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم بعد إيمانكم فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: And those who have been granted wisdom will know it by their Lord's grace, and they will be of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the people who have been granted wisdom by God's grace. They are the ones who recognize and acknowledge the truth and live according to it. They are the righteous ones who have been guided by God and are on the path of righteousness. The verse emphasizes the idea that wisdom is a blessing from God, and those who have been given this blessing will use it to live a virtuous life and be among the righteous.
orig: وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون

translation: These are the verses of God that We recite to you in truth, and God does not desire injustice for the knowledgeable ones.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, indicating that it is a revelation from God, and that its teachings are meant for those who seek knowledge and guidance. The verse also highlights the idea that God does not desire injustice or oppression for those who possess knowledge and understanding, indicating that those who seek to live righteously and justly will be protected and guided by God's teachings.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وما الله يريد ظلما للعالمين

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and to Allah will all matters be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all things, both in the heavens and on earth. It reinforces the idea that everything in existence belongs to Allah and will ultimately return to Him. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and control over all things and encourages believers to submit to His will and live according to His commandments.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: You were the best nation that was brought out for mankind, commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong, believing in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Some of them are believers, but most of them are rebellious.
interpretation: The verse praises the Muslim community for their righteousness and their commitment to commanding good and forbidding evil. The verse also addresses the People of the Scripture, who are criticized for their lack of belief in Allah and their rebellion against His commandments. The verse highlights the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands as the key to a righteous and just society.
orig: كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وتؤمنون بالله ولو آمن أهل الكتاب لكان خيرا لهم منهم المؤمنون وأكثرهم الفاسقون

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various trials, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and failure of crops. However, the verse also assures that those who are patient and persevering during these trials will receive good news and ultimately triumph over their challenges. The verse highlights the importance of patience and resilience in the face of adversity and encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and trust in God's plan.
orig: لن يضروكم إلا أذى وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس وباءوا بغضب من الله وضربت عليهم المسكنة ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون الأنبياء بغير حق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: And there are some among the People of the Book who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you, and what was revealed to the prophets before you, and they bow in humility before Allah.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the unity of faith among the People of the Book, specifically the Jews and Christians, who believe in Allah and the revelations sent to the prophets, including the Qur'an. The verse highlights their humility and submission to God, as they bow down in prayer, demonstrating their devotion to their faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the commonality of belief among the People of the Book and the importance of humility in faith.
orig: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten to good deeds and are foremost in them.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous people who believe in Allah and the Hereafter. They are those who practice what they preach and enjoin good deeds while forbidding evil. They are quick to perform acts of kindness and are at the forefront of doing good deeds. They are the ones who will be rewarded in the Hereafter for their good deeds.
orig: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين

translation: And they will not cease to fight you, [O Muhammad], until they turn you back from your religion, if they can. And whosoever of you turns back from his religion, then he will die in disbelief, and their deeds will be vain in this life and in the Hereafter. They desire that you should disbelieve as they have disbelieved, so that you may be alike. Therefore, take not from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and take not from among them any companion or supporter.
interpretation: This verse warns Muslims against befriending or allying with those who have rejected Islam and turned against the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes that those who turn away from their faith and ally with disbelievers will be considered disbelievers themselves and will face severe consequences in this life and the hereafter. The verse also commands Muslims to seize and kill those who reject Islam and not to take them as allies or supporters.
orig: وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will not benefit from their wealth or their children from Allah anything, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that wealth and children will not save those who disbelieve from the punishment of God. The verse uses the metaphor of fire to describe the punishment, indicating its intensity and eternal nature. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that their wealth and children will not protect them from the consequences of their disbelief. The verse highlights the idea that the punishment of God is not limited to this life, but will continue in the afterlife, where those who disbelieve will abide in the fire forever.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they are like the parable of the wind that blows over the harvest of the wicked, and it brings them no good. Allah has caused their deeds to be lost, and they have been destroyed, and they are not saved.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a wind that blows over a harvest to describe the fate of those who live in injustice and oppression. Just as the wind blows away the chaff, leaving behind only the useful grains, so too will God's judgment separate the righteous from the wicked. The wicked will be destroyed, and their deeds will be of no avail, while the righteous will be saved. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر أصابت حرث قوم ظلموا أنفسهم فأهلكته وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Indeed, the disbelievers will not fail to cause you harm, wishing you harm and hatred in their hearts, and their tongues will not cease to speak ill of you, wishing you evil. And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against befriending disbelievers, emphasizing that the disbelievers will only bring harm and speak ill of the believers. The verse also highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust, emphasizing the certainty of God's punishment. The use of the phrase 'wishing you harm and hatred in their hearts' suggests that the disbelievers' enmity towards the believers is not just a temporary or superficial feeling, but a deep-seated hatred that is rooted in their hearts. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be cautious in their relationships and to prioritize their faith and values over any personal connections they may have with disbelievers.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا بطانة من دونكم لا يألونكم خبالا ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر قد بينا لكم الآيات إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: And indeed, you are those who love them, but they do not love you, and you believe in the Scripture, all of it, while they are disbelievers in the Hereafter. And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe.' But when they are alone, they bite their fingers at you in rage. Say, 'Die in your rage.' Indeed, Allah knows what is in their hearts.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrites who pretend to be friends with the believers but actually hate them and disbelieve in the Hereafter. The verse highlights their two-faced nature, as they appear friendly and Muslim on the outside but are actually filled with anger and disbelief on the inside. The verse commands the believers to reject their false claims of faith and to tell them to die in their rage, indicating that their hypocrisy will not be tolerated. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is aware of their inner thoughts and feelings, and their attempts to hide their true beliefs will not be successful.
orig: ها أنتم أولاء تحبونهم ولا يحبونكم وتؤمنون بالكتاب كله وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Indeed, the believers who have believed in Our verses - when they are reminded of them, they fall upon their faces and weep, and they are humbled by their Lord's remembrance. Indeed, they will have a reward close to their Lord. Indeed, they will be given hiring in exchange for their patience, a gardens and silk. Indeed, they will be satisfied with their Lord's remembrance. They will be rewarded according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of believers when they are reminded of God's verses. They are moved to tears and humbled by the remembrance of their Lord, and they will receive a reward in the afterlife for their faith and patience. The verse emphasizes the idea that the believers' reward will be proportional to their good deeds and that they will be content with their Lord's remembrance.
orig: إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها وإن تصبروا وتتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا إن الله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the annunciation of the birth of Jesus to the Virgin Mary by the angels. The verse emphasizes the purification and selection of Mary by God, highlighting her unique status among women. The verse also underscores the divine intervention in the birth of Jesus, which is seen as a miraculous event. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and grace, and the importance of faith and obedience to God's will.
orig: وإذ غدوت من أهلك تبوئ المؤمنين مقاعد للقتال والله سميع عليم

translation: And indeed, they had plotted to cause sedition and confusion among you [the believers] and to turn you away from the truth, and Allah would have succumbed to their plot had it not been for the grace of Allah and His mercy upon you, and Allah is the Guide of the believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the plot of the hypocrites to cause confusion and sedition among the believers, and how Allah's grace and mercy prevented them from succeeding. The verse highlights the role of Allah as the Guide of the believers, indicating that He is the only one who can guide and protect them from harm. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to put their trust in Allah and to be mindful of the plots of those who seek to mislead them.
orig: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed, Allah has favored you in the Battle of Badr, and you were weak, so have gratitude to Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: In this verse, Allah reminds the believers of His favor upon them in the Battle of Badr, where they were vastly outnumbered and outmatched, yet they emerged victorious due to Allah's assistance. The verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah for His blessings and favors, and encourages the believers to recognize and appreciate the divine intervention in their lives. The verse also serves as a reminder that success and victory come from Allah alone, and that gratitude and humility are essential for continued success and guidance.
orig: ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة فاتقوا الله لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers, who mock you for your faith, and support you with three thousand angels, distinct and not hidden.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's promise to support the believers who are mocked and ridiculed for their faith. The verse indicates that God will provide three thousand angels as a means of support and protection for the believers. The phrase 'distinct and not hidden' suggests that these angels will be visible and recognizable, and their presence will serve as a sign of God's favor and protection. The verse serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for believers who face persecution and ridicule for their faith, reminding them that they are not alone and that God is always with them.
orig: إذ تقول للمؤمنين ألن يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم بثلاثة آلاف من الملائكة منزلين

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that believers may face in their lives, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and loved ones. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges, and reassures believers that they will be rewarded for their steadfastness. The phrase 'give good tidings' suggests that the reward for patience will be joyous and plentiful, and serves as a source of encouragement for believers to endure the hardships they face with faith and hope.
orig: بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى لكم ولتطمئن قلوبكم به وما النصر إلا من عند الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve or deny Our signs will be in the punishment of Hell, they will have a painful retribution.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject God's message and deny the truth of the Qur'an that they will face a painful punishment in Hell. The verse emphasizes that their disbelief and rejection of God's signs will lead to their suffering in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical or resistant to the message of the Qur'an, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to reconsider their stance.
orig: ليقطع طرفا من الذين كفروا أو يكبتهم فينقلبوا خائبين

translation: And nothing prevented their hands from it, for they were not able to revenge except that they were destroyed, or deterred from their punishment.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people of the town were unable to defend themselves against the punishment of God, and their attempts to revenge or resist it were futile. The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of those who oppose God's will and the inevitability of their punishment. The verse also serves as a warning to those who might be tempted to challenge God's authority and justice, reminding them that they will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all creation, stating that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him. The verse also highlights Allah's power to forgive or punish as He sees fit, demonstrating His justice and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is the ultimate authority and that they should seek His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume the orphan's wealth except in a way of improving it until he reaches maturity. And fulfill the covenant. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating the wealth of orphans with care and not misusing it for personal gain. It also stresses the importance of fulfilling covenants and agreements, as they will be questioned about on Judgment Day. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to act with integrity and honesty in all their dealings, including those involving the wealth of vulnerable individuals like orphans.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse urges the believers to fear the punishment of Hellfire, which has been prepared for those who reject the message of Islam and live in disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with God's commandments.
orig: واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger, Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse promises that those who obey God and His Messenger will receive mercy, indicating that obedience to God is a means of receiving His mercy and blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow the teachings of Islam and the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in order to live a righteous life and earn God's mercy.
orig: وأطيعوا الله والرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And they hastened to seek forgiveness from their Lord, and a garden, the doors of heaven were opened for them, and they were made to enter Gardens of perpetuity, an abode of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the righteous individuals who were warned of the impending punishment. They immediately sought forgiveness from God and were rewarded with a beautiful garden, symbolizing paradise. The verse emphasizes the mercy and grace of God, who opens the doors of heaven for those who repent and live a righteous life. The phrase 'an abode of the righteous' signifies that the garden is a place where the pious people will reside in peace and happiness, indicating the reward for their good deeds.
orig: وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين

translation: And those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and do not follow up what they spend with reminders (of their generosity) or (their) boasting, their reward is with their Lord, and there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of humility and selflessness in those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah. It emphasizes that true charity is not about seeking recognition or praise from others, but rather about sincerely desiring to please God and help those in need. The verse also assures such individuals that their reward will be with God, and they will not be afraid or saddened by their generosity, as their focus is on pleasing God rather than seeking human praise.
orig: الذين ينفقون في السراء والضراء والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين

translation: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and do not persist in what they have done, while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness from God. It emphasizes that only God can forgive sins and that those who seek forgiveness must not continue to engage in the behavior that led to their sin. The verse also underscores the importance of self-reflection and self-awareness, as those who seek forgiveness must recognize the wrong they have done and make a conscious effort to change their behavior.
orig: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and guidance in Islam. The phrase 'those who have been given knowledge' refers to those who have been blessed with the ability to discern the truth and understand the Qur'an. The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a source of guidance for those who seek to live a righteous life and achieve spiritual growth. The phrase 'the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy' refers to the path of God, which is the ultimate goal for believers. The verse serves as a reminder that knowledge and guidance are essential for living a life that is pleasing to God and achieving spiritual success.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed generations before you, and We will observe how you will fare, and We will see.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, reminding them that God has destroyed previous generations that disobeyed Him. The verse warns the current generation that they too will face destruction if they continue to disobey God. The phrase 'We will observe how you will fare' implies that God is watching and waiting to see how humanity will respond to His message. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and encourages the believers to stay on the righteous path.
orig: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, and We have shown them no warning.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, reminding them that God has destroyed many towns in the past that were unjust and did not heed the warnings. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to stay on the right path and not to fall into the same mistakes as those who came before them. The use of the word 'around' in the translation emphasizes that the destroyed towns were nearby, making the warning more immediate and personal for the audience.
orig: هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And do not be weak, and do not grieve, for you will be superior, if you are believers, indeed.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers not to lose hope or be sad, as they will ultimately be victorious if they remain true to their faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in overcoming adversity and achieving success. The use of the phrase 'you will be superior' suggests that believers will attain a higher status and rank in the eyes of God and in society, as long as they remain steadfast in their beliefs.
orig: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Indeed, the Qur'an is a noble Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. It is a revelation from the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the noble nature of the Qur'an, indicating that it is a book that cannot be compared to any other book. The verse also highlights the Qur'an's protection from any falsehood or alteration, both in its revelation and in its transmission. The phrase 'from before it or from behind it' signifies that the Qur'an is safeguarded from any attempt to alter or manipulate its content, whether it be from the past or in the future. The verse also underscores the Qur'an's divine origin, emphasizing that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the All-Knowing God.
orig: إن يمسسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس وليعلم الله الذين آمنوا ويتخذ منكم شهداء والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And God will suffice the believers against the disbelievers, and He will surely punish the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's support and protection for the believers, and His punishment for the disbelievers. The verse implies that the believers have been oppressed and marginalized by the disbelievers, and that God will come to their aid and defend them. The verse also serves as a warning to the disbelievers, warning them of the consequences of their disbelief and the punishment that awaits them.
orig: وليمحص الله الذين آمنوا ويمحق الكافرين

translation: And if you were to see those who were given the Scripture, how they would envy you, for they would say, 'Would that we were given what has been given to them, so that we might be guided.'
interpretation: The verse describes the jealousy and envy of the People of the Book towards the Muslims, who have been given the guidance of Islam. The verse suggests that the People of the Book wish they had been given the same guidance and blessings as the Muslims, and they recognize the superiority of Islam over their own religion. The verse highlights the beauty and perfection of Islam and the desire of others to have the same guidance and blessings.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين

translation: And indeed, you were wishing for death before you meet it, so that you might be saved from the punishment of a painful day.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers were longing for death to avoid the punishment that they knew was coming. They were afraid of the Day of Judgment and the retribution that they would face for their sins. The verse highlights the irony of their situation, as they were wishing for death, which is typically seen as a negative and fearful event, in order to avoid the punishment that they knew was coming. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of God's punishment and the fear that it inspires in those who reject faith.
orig: ولقد كنتم تمنون الموت من قبل أن تلقوه فقد رأيتموه وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed away before him. Then, if he was killed or caused to die, would you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is just one in a line of prophets who have come before him, and that his message is not unique or exclusive. The verse also warns the believers against turning back on their faith if something were to happen to the Prophet (peace be upon him), reminding them that the Prophet's death or departure would not affect the truth of the message he brought. The verse also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the reward that awaits those who are grateful to Allah.
orig: وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم ومن ينقلب على عقبيه فلن يضر الله شيئا وسيجزي الله الشاكرين

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so let them not dispute the signs of Allah, for every arrogant one will be humiliated.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans are limited in their understanding and knowledge, and therefore should not dispute or question the signs and revelations of God. The verse also warns against arrogance and pride, as those who are haughty and refuse to submit to God's will shall be humiliated.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تموت إلا بإذن الله كتابا مؤجلا ومن يرد ثواب الدنيا نؤته منها ومن يرد ثواب الآخرة نؤته منها وسنجزي الشاكرين

translation: And indeed, many prophets were killed with their Lord's permission, fighting for the cause of Allah. They did not weaken or abandon their effort because they were not hastening to receive their reward in this world. And Allah loves the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sacrifices made by prophets in the cause of Allah. They were willing to give up their lives, and their reward was not in this world, but in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes their steadfastness and dedication to their mission, and how they did not weaken or abandon their effort, even in the face of adversity. The verse also underscores Allah's love for those who are steadfast in their faith and actions.
orig: وكأين من نبي قاتل معه ربيون كثير فما وهنوا لما أصابهم في سبيل الله وما ضعفوا وما استكانوا والله يحب الصابرين

translation: And their statement was no other than that they said, 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins and excesses in our affair and make firm our foothold and give us victory over the disbelieving people.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the prayer of the believers, seeking forgiveness for their sins and excesses, and asking for guidance and victory over those who reject the message of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and the need for spiritual purification, as well as the desire for a firm foothold in one's faith and the desire for victory over those who oppose the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness and to strive for righteousness, while also serving as a warning to those who reject the message of God, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وما كان قولهم إلا أن قالوا ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: And God has given them (the unbelievers) a reward in this world, and certainly the reward of the Hereafter is much better for those who believe and are pious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony that those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief are only rewarded with temporary and finite pleasures in this world, while those who believe and live righteously will receive a much greater and eternal reward in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to not be swayed by the temporary temptations of this world, and to instead focus on earning the ultimate reward in the Hereafter.
orig: فآتاهم الله ثواب الدنيا وحسن ثواب الآخرة والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the disbelievers will surely be overcome and lost, so do not be swayed by their prosperity and glory. Indeed, they will be like a firewood that has been consumed. And do not be afraid, for Allah is with you, and He will support you with a mighty victory.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers and tells them that despite the apparent prosperity and power of the disbelievers, they will ultimately be defeated and destroyed. The verse uses the metaphor of firewood to describe their fate, implying that they will be consumed and reduced to nothing. The verse also reassures the believers that God is on their side and will support them with a mighty victory, giving them hope and confidence in the face of adversity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا الذين كفروا يردوكم على أعقابكم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: And God is your Lord and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and His role as the ultimate helper and supporter of believers. The verse stresses that God is not only the Lord of the universe, but also the one who assist and helps those who turn to Him in times of need. The phrase 'khair al-nasirin' (the best of helpers) highlights God's unique ability to provide aid and support to those who seek it, and serves as a reminder that true help and support come from God alone.
orig: بل الله مولاكم وهو خير الناصرين

translation: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment, in requital for their disbelief in the message of their Lord. Indeed, they have not been humbled by the punishment, and they have not returned to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who refused to accept the message of their Lord and were punished as a result. The verse indicates that the punishment was not enough to make them realize their mistake and turn back to God. Instead, they continued to disbelieve and were subjected to further punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: سنلقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب بما أشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا ومأواهم النار وبئس مثوى الظالمين

translation: And indeed, Allah has truthfully fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them (the enemy) by His permission, until you became numerous and prevailed and were desired to take revenge, and He (Allah) held back your hands from them and their hands from you, that it may be a lesson for the believers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about a specific situation where the believers were given permission by God to fight their enemies and were successful in their conquests. However, when they became numerous and powerful, they began to desire worldly gains and forgot about their spiritual goals. God then intervened and stopped them from taking revenge, teaching them a lesson in humility and reminding them of their true purpose as believers.
orig: ولقد صدقكم الله وعده إذ تحسونهم بإذنه حتى إذا فشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر وعصيتم من بعد ما أراكم ما تحبون منكم من يريد الدنيا ومنكم من يريد الآخرة ثم صرفكم عنهم ليبتليكم ولقد عفا عنكم والله ذو فضل على المؤمنين

translation: When you were climbing up the high ground and were not paying attention to anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind. He (the Messenger) was grieving over your state, as you were not suffering (from a great calamity) except for what you had done, and (you were not) fearing (the punishment) as much as you should have feared (it). And Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Muslim community, specifically those who were present during the Battle of Uhud. The verse describes how the community was climbing up a high ground, implying that they were in a state of pride and arrogance, and were not paying attention to the Messenger's call. The Messenger was grieving over their state, as they were not suffering from a great calamity, indicating that they were not facing any significant challenges or hardships, yet they were not fearing God's punishment as much as they should have. The verse serves as a reminder to the community to fear God and to be mindful of their actions, as God is well-acquainted with what they do.
orig: إذ تصعدون ولا تلوون على أحد والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم فأثابكم غما بغم لكيلا تحزنوا على ما فاتكم ولا ما أصابكم والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Then He sent down upon you, after the affliction, a feeling of security, a slumber that overtook a group of you, and another group was worried about themselves, thinking that they had no hand in the decision. They said, 'Have we any say in this matter? The matter is entirely up to God.' Indeed, they are concealing within themselves what they do not reveal. Had they but been in your position, they would have fought, but they were overpowered by the fear of death. Say, 'If you had been in my position, you would have done no better. Indeed, God is Knowing of what is within the breasts.'
interpretation: The verse describes how a group of people were affected by a feeling of security and complacency after a period of hardship, and how another group was worried about their own fate. The verse suggests that the latter group was fearful of death and did not have the courage to fight for their rights. The verse also implies that the people were not honest with themselves and were hiding their true feelings and intentions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of what is in people's hearts and that He will ultimately judge them based on their actions and intentions.
orig: ثم أنزل عليكم من بعد الغم أمنة نعاسا يغشى طائفة منكم وطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم يظنون بالله غير الحق ظن الجاهلية يقولون هل لنا من الأمر من شيء قل إن الأمر كله لله يخفون في أنفسهم ما لا يبدون لك يقولون لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء ما قتلنا هاهنا قل لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل إلى مضاجعهم وليبتلي الله ما في صدوركم وليمحص ما في قلوبكم والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Indeed, those who have been carried away by their desire for immediate gratification and have been led astray by the devil, for them the punishment will be doubled. They have forgotten that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of being swayed by one's desires and the influence of Satan. Those who prioritize worldly pleasures over their spiritual well-being will face double the punishment in the afterlife. The verse also emphasizes Allah's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that even those who have strayed can still seek forgiveness and turn back to Allah.
orig: إن الذين تولوا منكم يوم التقى الجمعان إنما استزلهم الشيطان ببعض ما كسبوا ولقد عفا الله عنهم إن الله غفور حليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers, 'If they had been with us, they would not have been killed.' Consider how Allah has made their deeds fruitless in this world, and indeed, they will be killed while they are disobedient.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, urging them not to be like the disbelievers who rationalized their killing of their own brethren by saying that if they had been with them, they would not have been killed. The verse emphasizes the futility of their actions and the fact that they will ultimately be killed while they are disobedient to God. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to avoid such behavior and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين كفروا وقالوا لإخوانهم إذا ضربوا في الأرض أو كانوا غزى لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم والله يحيي ويميت والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And if you had killed in the way of Allah or to seek the forgiveness of Allah, indeed, the reward from Allah is far better and more lasting.
interpretation: The verse highlights the idea that the reward for fighting in the cause of Allah or seeking forgiveness from Allah is far better and more lasting than any worldly reward. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their ultimate goal should be to please Allah and seek His forgiveness, rather than seeking worldly gains or recognition. The phrase 'in the way of Allah' refers to fighting in a just cause, such as defending the faith or liberating oppressed people, and 'seeking the forgiveness of Allah' refers to the act of repenting and seeking forgiveness for one's sins. The verse emphasizes the idea that the reward for these actions is not limited to this life, but will be rewarded in the afterlife as well.
orig: ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متم لمغفرة من الله ورحمة خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from Allah's way. They follow nothing but assumptions and they are only conjecturing.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following the majority or popular opinion, especially when it goes against God's teachings. It emphasizes that the majority of people can be misguided and that true guidance comes from following God's way, not from conforming to societal norms or expectations. The verse encourages critical thinking and questioning of assumptions, rather than blindly following the crowd.
orig: ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

translation: By the grace of Allah, you were gentle towards them, had you been harsh and stern of heart, they would have dispersed from around you; so pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of gentle and compassionate leadership. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was commanded by God to adopt a gentle approach towards his companions, even when they were guilty of mistakes or wrongdoing. This approach encourages unity and cooperation, rather than driving people away through harshness and severity. The verse also emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and consulting others in decision-making. Finally, the verse reminds us that true reliance is on Allah, and that those who rely on Him are beloved to Him.
orig: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك فاعف عنهم واستغفر لهم وشاورهم في الأمر فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله إن الله يحب المتوكلين

translation: Indeed, Allah will aid you with a victory, and none can overcome it. Indeed, Allah will bring disgrace upon those who disbelieve, and Allah's aid is not to be prevented.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and the certainty of His aid for the believers. The verse assures the believers that Allah will grant them victory, and no one can overcome it. The verse also warns the disbelievers of the consequences of their disbelief, as Allah will bring disgrace upon them. The verse concludes by emphasizing that Allah's aid is not to be prevented, indicating that His help is certain and inevitable for those who have faith in Him.
orig: إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And no prophet could (ever) be false to his trust. And if he had fabricated against Us some of the sayings, We would certainly have seized him by the right hand, Then We would certainly have cut off his aorta. And not one of you could have held Us off from (punishing) him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the integrity and honesty of the prophets, stating that they cannot be false to their trust and cannot fabricate anything against God. The verse also serves as a warning to those who might try to distort or manipulate the message of the prophets, as they will be held accountable by God. The image of God seizing the person by the right hand and cutting off their aorta is a powerful metaphor for the consequences of such actions, emphasizing the certainty and severity of God's punishment.
orig: وما كان لنبي أن يغل ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن باء بسخط من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while they were wrongdoers, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were characterized by injustice and wrongdoing. The use of the word 'indeed' emphasizes the certainty and reality of the punishment that was inflicted upon them. The phrase 'while they were wrongdoers' underscores the idea that the punishment was not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of their own actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هم درجات عند الله والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Allah has indeed blessed the believers when He raised among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been in clear error before.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessing of God upon the believers, where He sent a Messenger from among themselves to guide them and purify them. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Messenger's role in teaching the believers the Book and wisdom, indicating that they were previously in a state of error and misguidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of the Prophet's mission and the impact it had on the believers, as well as the responsibility of the believers to follow the teachings of the Prophet and adhere to the guidance provided in the Book.
orig: لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you are unaware.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that God has destroyed nations in the past for their sins and injustices, but the current generation may not be aware of it. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them that God's punishment is always present and that they should learn from the mistakes of the past to avoid suffering the same fate.
orig: أولما أصابتكم مصيبة قد أصبتم مثليها قلتم أنى هذا قل هو من عند أنفسكم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And what struck you on the day the two armies met? By the will of Allah, and to know the believers.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslim army was defeated and many lives were lost. The verse suggests that the defeat was a test from God to distinguish the true believers from the hypocrites. The phrase 'by the will of Allah' emphasizes that the outcome of the battle was predestined and that God's will must be accepted. The second part of the verse, 'and to know the believers,' implies that the battle served as a means to identify those who were truly committed to their faith and those who were not. The verse highlights the importance of steadfastness and loyalty in the face of adversity and serves as a reminder that true faith is tested during difficult times.
orig: وما أصابكم يوم التقى الجمعان فبإذن الله وليعلم المؤمنين

translation: And let those who oppose know that they will be defeated and say, 'Are we to return to our families after being defeated while they are still in disbelief?' They have brought their doom upon themselves, and that is a far greater calamity than being killed in battle. Say, 'The fire of Hell is more severe and will burn for longer.' Surely, this is a warning to those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who oppose the believers and threaten them with defeat. The verse tells them that they will indeed be defeated and their disbelief will only bring them closer to their doom. The verse also warns them of the severity of the punishment they will face in Hell, which is far worse than any earthly punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وليعلم الذين نافقوا وقيل لهم تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله أو ادفعوا قالوا لو نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان يقولون بأفواههم ما ليس في قلوبهم والله أعلم بما يكتمون

translation: And they say, 'If we had listened or reasoning, we would not have been killed.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the excuses made by the disbelievers who were killed in battle. They claim that if they had listened to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or used their reason, they would not have been killed. However, their argument is flawed, as they were given the opportunity to accept Islam and refused. Their refusal to listen and submit to God's commandments led to their destruction. The verse highlights the importance of listening to the truth and using one's reason to recognize and accept it.
orig: الذين قالوا لإخوانهم وقعدوا لو أطاعونا ما قتلوا قل فادرءوا عن أنفسكم الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And do not think those who have been killed in the way of Allah are dead. Indeed, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that martyrs who have died in the cause of Allah are not to be considered dead, but are instead alive and receiving sustenance from their Lord. This verse serves to comfort the families and loved ones of those who have made the ultimate sacrifice in the name of Allah, and to remind them that their loved ones are not gone, but are instead living in the presence of Allah, blessed and content.
orig: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

translation: And they are joyful in what Allah has bestowed upon them from His bounty and in the believers who have not been granted any share in it, saying, 'Surely, Allah's favor is not but a means of pride for us over them.' How wrong are their judgments!
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of the disbelievers who are happy with the blessings they have received from Allah and look down upon those who have not received the same blessings. They think that their possessions are a sign of their superiority over the believers, and they take pride in their wealth, forgetting that true happiness and success come from faith and righteous deeds. The verse warns against such pride and misconception, reminding the believers that true happiness comes from faith and righteous deeds, not from material possessions.
orig: فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ألا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: They will be rewarded with blessings from God and grace. Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the promise of God's blessings and grace for the believers. The phrase 'يستبشرون' (they will be rewarded) emphasizes that the believers will receive a reward that is proportionate to their good deeds. The phrase 'بنعمة من الله' (from God's grace) underscores the divine origin of this reward, and 'وفضل' (and grace) emphasizes the abundance of God's favor. The final phrase, 'لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين' (Indeed, God does not waste the reward of the believers), serves as a reassurance that God will not let the good deeds of the believers go to waste, but will certainly reward them in this life or the hereafter.
orig: يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين

translation: And those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after they had been afflicted with hardship, those who did good among them will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of resilience and perseverance in the face of adversity. It emphasizes that those who responded to Allah and the Messenger even after experiencing hardship, and continued to do good deeds, will be rewarded generously. The verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and continue to do good deeds, even during difficult times, with the promise of a great reward in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the believers who have recognized the truth of Islam and have submitted themselves to God. They are seeking forgiveness for their past sins and asking for protection from the punishment of the Fire (Hell). The verse highlights the importance of faith and seeking forgiveness, as well as the belief in the Hereafter and the accountability of one's actions. It also emphasizes the idea that true belief is not just a verbal declaration, but also entails action and obedience to God's commands.
orig: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

translation: And they were followers of the Lord of Mercy, and they did not invite evil upon themselves. And they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the owner of great bounty.
interpretation: The verse describes the righteous people who were blessed with the grace of God and did not bring harm to themselves. They followed the will of God and were guided by His pleasure, which is a reference to their obedience to God's commands. The verse highlights the idea that those who follow God's will and live a righteous life will be rewarded with His bounty and mercy.
orig: فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم

translation: Verily, Satan is afraid of you, so be not afraid of them, and fear Me, if you are believers indeed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fear that Satan has of the believers, and the importance of not fearing Satan or his followers. Instead, believers should fear God alone, indicating a complete submission to His will and a recognition of His power and authority. The verse serves as a reminder that Satan is a formidable enemy, but ultimately, his power is limited and believers have nothing to fear from him if they remain true to their faith.
orig: إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه فلا تخافوهم وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would not cease to be in doubt about the Hour. And [they] will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' skepticism regarding the Day of Judgment. They will continue to doubt and question the Hour until it suddenly comes upon them, catching them off guard. The verse highlights the certainty of the Hour and the fact that it will come unexpectedly, emphasizing the importance of being prepared for it. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are skeptical about the Day of Judgment, reminding them that their disbelief will not change the reality of the Hour and its inevitability.
orig: ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا يريد الله ألا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief [in exchange] for faith will not harm Allah at all, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who have chosen to disbelieve in God and instead follow false deities or ideologies will not harm God in any way, but will only bring punishment upon themselves. The phrase 'purchased disbelief' highlights the idea that disbelief is a choice, and that those who choose it are exchanging their faith for something that will ultimately lead to their downfall. The verse serves as a warning to those who are considering turning away from God, reminding them that their actions will have severe consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And those who disbelieve think that they are being clever and successful, but in reality, they are only increasing their sin and punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of the disbelievers' attitude towards their disbelief. They think they are being clever and successful in rejecting God's message, but in reality, they are only accumulating more sin and punishment for themselves. The verse emphasizes the idea that disbelief is not a sign of intelligence or success, but rather a sign of ignorance and misguidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's message, reminding them that their disbelief will only lead to more harm and suffering.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما ولهم عذاب مهين

translation: And Allah would not have caused the believers to be destroyed along with the wicked people, until He separates the wicked from the good, and Allah is not to inform you of the Unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers and if you believe and fear Him, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy in separating the believers from the wicked, indicating that Allah will not destroy the righteous along with the wicked. The verse also highlights the importance of faith in Allah and His messengers, and the reward that comes with it. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to fear Allah, as the reward for their belief and righteous deeds will be great.
orig: ما كان الله ليذر المؤمنين على ما أنتم عليه حتى يميز الخبيث من الطيب وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب ولكن الله يجتبي من رسله من يشاء فآمنوا بالله ورسله وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا فلكم أجر عظيم

translation: And those who hoard the gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day of Resurrection, their wealth will be heated in the fire of Hell and used to burn their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs. They will be told, 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so now taste what you have hoarded.'
interpretation: The verse warns those who hoard wealth and do not use it in the way of Allah, that they will face a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Their wealth will be turned into a source of suffering, as it will be heated in the fire of Hell and used to burn their bodies. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a result of their own actions and that they will be forced to experience the consequences of their greed. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to use their wealth in a responsible and charitable manner, in order to avoid such a fate.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: And indeed, We have heard the whispers of those who said, 'Allah is poor and we are rich.' We will record what they said and kill them, and say to them, 'Taste the punishment of burning!',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who mocked God's revelation and boasted about their wealth, implying that God was poor and unable to punish them. The verse threatens them with a painful punishment, describing it as a burning fire that they will be subjected to.
