translation: And what is wrong with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and for the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this town whose people are oppressors! Make for us from Yourself a protector and make for us from Yourself a helper!'
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers' lack of action in standing up for the oppressed and fighting for justice. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for those who are oppressed and in need, and calls upon the believers to seek God's help and support in their quest for justice. The verse also highlights the idea that the oppressed people are not just victims, but also have agency and are capable of seeking help and support from God. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that they have a responsibility to stand up for justice and to support those who are in need, and that they should seek God's help in doing so.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the devil. Fight, therefore, against the allies of the devil. Indeed, the strategy of the devil is weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dichotomy between the believers who fight for Allah's cause and the disbelievers who fight for the devil's cause. The verse emphasizes that the believers' fight is righteous and just, while the disbelievers' fight is driven by the devil's influence and is therefore misguided and weak. The verse encourages the believers to fight against the devil's allies, indicating that the struggle against evil is an ongoing one and that the believers must be vigilant in their fight against the forces of darkness. The verse also suggests that the devil's strategy is ultimately weak and will be defeated by the righteousness of the believers.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told: 'Restrain your hands [from fighting] and establish prayer and give zakah?' But then when fighting was ordained for them, behold, a group of them fear people as they fear Allah or with a greater fear. They said: 'Our Lord, why have you ordained fighting for us? We will not fight unless for a near term gain.' Say: 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah. And injustice will not be done to you, [even] as much as a thread [in a date seed].
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrites who were told to restrain themselves from fighting and instead focus on their prayers and charity. However, when fighting was ordained for them, they showed fear and reluctance, preferring the temporal gains of this world over the spiritual rewards of the Hereafter. The verse rebukes them for their lack of faith and reminds them that the enjoyment of this world is fleeting and insignificant compared to the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. The verse also emphasizes that God will not wrong them, not even by the smallest amount, and that their fear of fighting is misplaced.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: And where they are killed, they will be put to death, whether they are in towers raised high or in a pit fallen deep.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The verse states that regardless of their fortifications or defenses, whether they are in high towers or deep pits, they will still face death and punishment from God. The verse serves as a warning to those who refuse to believe and obey God's commandments, reminding them that their attempts to avoid punishment are futile and that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever calamity befalls you, it is from Allah, and whatever good fortune befalls you, it is from Allah. And We have sent you (Muhammad) to the people as a messenger, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that both good and bad fortune come from God, and that believers should not attribute their successes or failures to their own efforts or luck. Instead, they should recognize that everything comes from God, and that He is the ultimate source of all blessings and afflictions. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of God, sent to guide the people and convey His message. The verse ends by emphasizing that God is sufficient as a witness, indicating that He is the ultimate authority and that His testimony is enough to establish the truth of the Prophet's message.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: And whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah, and whoever turns away - We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the consequences of disobeying him. It highlights the fact that the Prophet is not responsible for the guidance of those who choose to disobey, and that his role is only to convey the message of Islam. The verse also underscores the idea that obeying the Prophet is equivalent to obeying Allah, and that disobedience to the Prophet is a sign of disobedience to Allah. This verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to follow the teachings of the Prophet and to recognize the authority of the Prophet in matters of faith and practice.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: And they say, 'Follow our leader, and we will guide you to the right way.' Say, 'Surely, I cannot be a guardian over you, for I do not follow anything except what has been revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day.'
interpretation: The verse addresses a situation where some people are asking the Prophet to follow their leader, implying that they have a better understanding of the right path. The Prophet responds by saying that he cannot be a guardian over them, as he only follows what has been revealed to him through divine revelation. He also expresses his fear of God's punishment if he were to disobey His commands. The verse highlights the importance of following divine guidance and the Prophet's role as a mere conveyor of God's message, rather than a leader or guardian over his people.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: And when a community was afflicted with a calamity, they would cry out to their messenger, and they would turn away from him in aversion. And if they had only been patient and pondered, they would have seen that the Messenger was truly from Allah. But now they have denied him, and soon they will come to know the truth of what they denied.
interpretation: This verse speaks about a community that was afflicted with a calamity and how they reacted by turning away from their messenger. The verse highlights the importance of patience and contemplation, suggesting that if they had only been patient and reflected on the situation, they would have realized that the messenger was truly from God. Instead, they denied the messenger and will soon come to know the truth of what they denied.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed. Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: The verse commands Muslims to fight in self-defense against those who fight them, but warns them against transgressing the limits set by God. The verse emphasizes that God does not like those who transgress or commit aggression, and that believers should always strive to act with justice and compassion, even in times of conflict. The verse serves as a reminder that violence is only justified in self-defense and that Muslims must always strive to act with morality and ethics, even in the face of aggression.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever brings a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it, and whoever brings an evil deed, he will have the like of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of reciprocity in the spiritual realm. The verse teaches that every good deed that a person performs will be rewarded with ten times its like, while every evil deed will be punished with a similar retribution. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences in the afterlife, and that God is aware of all that we do, and will reward or punish us accordingly. The verse also highlights the importance of striving for good deeds and avoiding evil actions, as they will have a direct impact on our spiritual well-being and our ultimate fate in the afterlife.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: And when you were born, you were adorned with the finest ornaments. Then you grew up and became proud, and you were reprimanded. Indeed, Allah is watchful over all things.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the arrogance and pride of humans. The verse describes how humans are born with the finest ornaments, referring to the beauty and purity of a newborn child. However, as they grow up, they become proud and arrogant, forgetting their humble beginnings and the blessings bestowed upon them by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is watchful over all things, and that He sees and knows all, including the actions and intentions of human beings. It warns humans to be mindful of their behavior and to avoid becoming too proud or arrogant, lest they face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: And Allah is the only deity worthy of worship, and He will gather you all on the Day of Resurrection, there is no doubt in it. And who is more truthful than Allah in what He says?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the certainty of the Day of Judgment. The verse stresses that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship, and that He will gather all people on the Day of Resurrection, a day when all will be judged based on their deeds. The verse also highlights the truthfulness of Allah's words, indicating that His promises and warnings are always fulfilled and should be taken seriously. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as well as the certainty of being held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: And what is with you, oh double-standard ones, that you fear the disbelievers and Allah is more worthy that you should fear Him, if you are believers indeed?
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrites who were afraid of the disbelievers, while they should have feared Allah more. The verse highlights the double standards of those who claim to be believers but are more concerned with the opinions of disbelievers than with pleasing Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that true believers should fear Allah more than anyone or anything else and that their fear of Allah should be greater than their fear of the disbelievers.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: And had they believed in Allah and the Prophet (Muhammad SAW) and had they not hidden their faith, they would not have been punished. So, (on the contrary), they disbelieved him and We caused them to perish as they had disbelieved the Messengers before them (and thus they became) examples (of Our punishment).
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith in Allah and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse states that those who hide their faith and disbelieve in the Prophet will be punished. The verse also warns that the punishment will be severe, using the example of previous nations who disbelieved in the Messengers and were subsequently destroyed. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be mindful of the consequences of disbelief.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except those who reach a people between whom and you there is a covenant, or who come to you with their breasts restrained from fighting you or fighting their own people. Had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. And if they had been allowed to go out to you, they would have not been prevented from fighting you. And indeed, the believers will be tried and tested in their wealth and lives. And Allah will make evident those who are true. And it is He who will cause the hypocrites to be slain (in the Hereafter),
interpretation: This verse speaks about the exception to the rule of fighting against those who are in a covenant with the Muslims or those who have come to the Muslims with peaceful intentions. The verse emphasizes that even though they may have the ability to fight against the Muslims, they choose not to do so and instead seek peace. The verse also highlights the importance of testing the faith of believers through trials and tribulations, and how Allah will make evident those who are true believers. Additionally, the verse warns the hypocrites that they will be punished in the afterlife for their insincerity.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that believers may face in life, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges, and encourages believers to remain steadfast and faithful to God. The verse also serves as a reminder that these trials are a means of testing and purifying the faith of believers, and that those who are patient and steadfast will be rewarded with God's blessings and mercy.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: And there is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment to the victim's family, unless they give charity as a ransom. But if the victim's family forgives, then the compensation payment is to be paid to them, and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then he will be punished with a punishment similar to the punishment of the victim's family. Indeed, the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment to the victim's family is a ransom from the punishment of Allah. And whoever does not find the means to free a believing slave, then fasting for two consecutive months, seeking forgiveness from Allah. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of accidental killing between believers and provides guidelines for the consequences of such an act. The verse emphasizes that the killing of a believer, even by mistake, is a grave matter and requires a punishment that is similar to the punishment of the victim's family. The verse also emphasizes the importance of freeing a believing slave and paying a compensation to the victim's family as a way of seeking forgiveness from Allah. The verse also provides an alternative punishment for those who cannot afford to free a believing slave, which is fasting for two consecutive months and seeking forgiveness from Allah. The verse highlights Allah's knowledge and wisdom in dealing with such matters.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his reward will be Hell, where he will abide eternally, and God will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of killing a believer, which is considered a grave sin and a violation of the sacredness of human life. The punishment for such an act is specified as eternal residence in Hell, accompanied by God's anger, curse, and severe punishment. The verse serves as a strong warning against harming or killing believers, and underscores the importance of respecting the sanctity of human life and the severe consequences of violating it.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, do not say to one who has been given good tidings, 'You are not a believer.' You desire the fleeting life, while Allah desires the Hereafter. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, reminding them not to judge others based on their outward appearance or to assume that someone is not a believer simply because they have been given good tidings. The verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly life and the fact that Allah desires the Hereafter for His servants. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their spiritual growth and not to be distracted by the fleeting pleasures of this life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: The believers who sit at home, other than those who are disabled, are not equal to those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has given those who strive with their wealth and their lives a higher rank than those who sit at home. Allah has promised a great reward to those who strive in His cause.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the difference between those who are actively participating in the cause of Allah, using their wealth and lives to support the faith, and those who are not actively participating, but are instead sitting at home. The verse indicates that those who are actively participating have a higher rank in the eyes of Allah and will receive a greater reward. The verse encourages believers to be proactive in their faith and to strive for Allah's cause, promising them a great reward for their efforts.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear victory and manifest triumph. And We have forgiven you, and We have been Merciful to you, and We have aided you with a manifest victory.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the victory and forgiveness that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's forgiveness and mercy are a manifestation of His grace and mercy towards humanity. The phrase 'manifest triumph' refers to the clear and decisive victory that God has given to the believers, and the phrase 'We have aided you with a manifest victory' suggests that God's assistance and guidance were instrumental in achieving this victory. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and grace, and encourages believers to be grateful for His blessings and to strive to live according to His will.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those who have denied the meeting of the Hereafter are the ones who have denied their Lord. So they have no fear of the Day they will be returned to Him. Their punishment is the Fire, and they will be forgotten, forgotten in the world. They will not be remembered except for their shame, they will be crying out for destruction, 'Our Lord, we have seen the punishment, and we have been the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who deny the existence of the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment. They will be punished in Hell and forgotten in this world. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment and their regret and shame on the Day of Judgment, when they will realize the error of their ways and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical or reject the idea of the Hereafter, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for the feeble old men and women and the children, they cannot drive away the Path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the vulnerability of certain members of society who are unable to defend themselves against the forces of evil. The feeble old men and women, as well as the children, are unable to drive away the path of evil and are in need of protection. The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting and caring for these vulnerable members of society, and serves as a reminder of the responsibility of the stronger members of society to safeguard them from harm.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: And perhaps your Lord will forgive them, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse expresses the possibility of God's forgiveness for those who have committed wrongdoing. The use of the word 'perhaps' suggests that forgiveness is not guaranteed, but it is a possibility that God may grant to those who truly repent and turn to Him. The description of God as 'the Forgiving, the Merciful' emphasizes His attribute of forgiveness and mercy, and serves as a reminder to those who have wronged themselves and others that God's mercy is always available to them, should they seek it.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever migrates for the cause of Allah will find many refuge and abundance in the earth, and whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has fallen upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward for those who migrate for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that those who leave their homes and migrate to a new land will find plenty of opportunities and resources, indicating that their migration will lead to a better life. The verse also assures that if such a person dies on their journey, their reward will be given to them by Allah, indicating that their sacrifice will not go unrewarded. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's forgiveness and mercy towards those who migrate for His cause.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you (Muhammad) strike in the land, there is no blame upon you for (not observing) the prayer at its time, if you fear that those who disbelieve will give you trouble. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever your clear enemies.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and permits him to neglect the prayer at its designated time when he is engaged in a military campaign or defending against an enemy attack. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers are the clear enemies of the believers and that the Prophet and his followers must be vigilant and prepared to defend themselves against their enemies, even if it means temporarily setting aside certain religious obligations. The verse highlights the importance of self-defense and the protection of one's community in the face of aggression and persecution.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: And when I (Muhammad) said to them: 'Verily, I am a warner to you, just as Noah and the prophets after him warned their people', then I invited them to the obedience of Allah and feared that a painful punishment would afflict them if they disobeyed. So, I took my share of admonition and they took their share of punishment. Then, a group of them turned to Allah and followed me, and a group of them did not. So, I am not responsible for their punishment. Indeed, Allah is the One Who punishes the disbelievers, if they had only known.
interpretation: The verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a warner to his people, just like the previous prophets, including Noah. The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warning and admonition given by the Prophet, and the consequences of not doing so. The verse also underscores the idea that the Prophet is not responsible for the punishment of those who reject the message, as it is Allah Who punishes the disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder to those who reject the message to fear Allah and turn to Him, lest they face the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: When you have finished the prayer, remember Allah, standing, sitting, and on your sides. Indeed, the prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specific times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah at all times, whether standing, sitting, or lying down. It serves as a reminder to believers that prayer is not just a ritual to be performed at specific times, but a way of life that should be practiced consistently. The verse also highlights the significance of the prayer as an obligatory act for believers, and stresses the importance of adhering to its prescribed times.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not hasten in seeking the punishment, for indeed, they will be punished, just as they will be punished, and they will not be benefited by their punishment when it comes. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: The verse advises against rushing to seek revenge or punishment against those who have wronged us, as it is ultimately up to God to deliver justice. The verse emphasizes that the punishment will come in God's due time, and it will be just as severe as the harm that was inflicted. The verse also highlights that the punishment will not benefit the wicked when it comes, as they will not be able to escape or avoid it. The verse ends by emphasizing God's knowledge and wisdom in His judgments.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with truth, so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has revealed, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a criterion for judgment. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to use the Qur'an as a criterion to judge between people, and not to be an advocate for those who are treacherous or unjust. The verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a source of truth and a guide for those who seek justice and righteousness. It also underscores the Prophet's role as a judge and arbitrator, and his responsibility to uphold justice and fairness in all his interactions.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah, highlighting Allah's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful. It encourages believers to turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness, acknowledging their mistakes and sins. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is ever-merciful and willing to forgive those who seek His pardon. The verse also underscores the idea that seeking forgiveness is a sign of faith and a means of purifying one's soul.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue with those who are unjust, indeed Allah does not love the one who is a persistent sinner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of not engaging in arguments or debates with those who are unjust and wicked. It suggests that such individuals are not worthy of being argued with, as they are unwilling to listen to reason or accept truth. Instead, the believer should focus on their own spiritual growth and development, rather than wasting time and energy on those who are not receptive to guidance. The verse also highlights the fact that God does not love those who are persistent in their sinful ways, and that such individuals will face consequences for their actions.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: And they (the disbelievers) plotted and planned, but their plotting and planning was against themselves, and they were not aware of it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who plotted and planned against the believers, but their efforts were ultimately futile and ended up being against themselves. The verse highlights the idea that the disbelievers were unaware of the ultimate failure of their plans and the consequences of their actions, which were against God's will. The verse serves as a reminder that God's plan is supreme and that those who oppose it will ultimately be defeated.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: And you were always plunged in doubt and uncertainty, and you were always disputing and opposing [the truth].
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and their skepticism towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an. The verse implies that they were constantly arguing and disputing the truth, and they were uncertain about the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that on Judgment Day, it will be too late to argue or dispute, and those who opposed the truth will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does an evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from God when one has committed a wrong or harmful act. It highlights the mercy and forgiveness of God, who is ever-ready to pardon those who seek His forgiveness. The verse also underscores the idea that forgiveness is not just about being pardoned, but also about learning from one's mistakes and making amends. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who seek it, and that seeking forgiveness is a sign of spiritual growth and development.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever earns an evil deed, indeed earns it against himself, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. It emphasizes that when an individual commits a sin or wrongdoing, they are ultimately harming themselves, rather than anyone else. The verse also underscores God's omniscience and wisdom in allowing individuals to make their own choices and face the consequences of those choices. It serves as a reminder to individuals to be mindful of their actions and to take responsibility for their own spiritual well-being.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever earns a sin or a crime, and then blames it on an innocent person, has indeed burdened himself with a falsehood and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave injustice of accusing an innocent person of a sin or crime that they did not commit. It emphasizes the double wrongdoing of the accuser, who not only committed the original sin or crime but then has the audacity to shift the blame onto an innocent party. The verse serves as a warning against false accusations and the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions, as well as the importance of standing up for justice and defending the rights of the innocent.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if it were not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have desired to mislead you. But they do not harm except themselves, and they will not harm you except for a little while. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you what you did not know. And the grace of Allah upon you is great.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the grace and mercy of Allah upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The verse warns against the evil intentions of some people who seek to mislead the Prophet and the believers, but reassures them that their harm is limited and temporary. The verse also highlights the revelation of the Qur'an and the wisdom it contains, and how it has taught the Prophet and the believers things they did not know before. The verse ends by emphasizing the greatness of Allah's grace upon the Prophet and the believers.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in much of their secret talks, except for him who enjoins charity, or kindness, or reconciliation between people. Whoever does so seeking the pleasure of God, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere intentions and actions, emphasizing that good deeds and kindness towards others are the only valuable aspects of human interaction. Secret talks and conspiracies are deemed useless and unbeneficial, unless they are motivated by a desire to help others or promote peace and reconciliation. The verse also underscores the idea that actions done seeking God's pleasure are the most valuable and will be rewarded accordingly.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then he turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have set veils over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears, deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for them whether you invite them or you are silent. Indeed, the judgment of ignominy is upon them and theirs is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject the message of the Prophet and turn away from the guidance of Allah. The verse emphasizes that even if the Prophet tries to guide them, they will not follow, and their hearts and ears are veiled from understanding the truth. The punishment that awaits them is described as one of ignominy and pain. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet and choose to live in disbelief, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and its distinction from other sins. While God may forgive other sins, He will not forgive shirk, indicating its severity and the grave offense it represents against God's oneness and uniqueness. The verse also highlights the misguided nature of those who commit shirk, suggesting that they have strayed far from the path of righteousness and are in need of guidance and forgiveness.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: And they will not be reprimanded except by a clear verse, and they will not be reminded except by a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that people will not be held accountable for their actions unless they have been clearly warned and reminded of the consequences of their actions. The verse suggests that the responsibility for guiding people lies with the prophets and messengers who have been sent by God to guide humanity. The verse also implies that people have a tendency to ignore or reject the message of the prophets, and that they will only be reminded of the truth through a clear and direct message.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, and We have shown (their destruction) as a lesson.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder of the destruction of the towns that were destroyed before, and serves as a lesson for those who are living in sin and injustice. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of these towns was not just a random event, but a deliberate act of God's punishment, meant to teach a lesson to those who are alive and to come. The verse warns that God's punishment is not limited to the past, but is still relevant and applicable to those who are living in disobedience.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a mercy, highlighting his responsibility to convey the message of Islam and guide humanity towards the right path. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of the significance of the Prophet's mission and the impact it has had on human history.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed them, and theirs has been the devil's share.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of communities that were consumed by their desires and followed the devil's way. Their destruction was a consequence of their own actions, and the devil's influence over them only increased their deviation from the righteous path. The verse highlights the idea that the devil's influence is a temptation that can lead people astray and ultimately result in their downfall.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Those who have earned evil will be flung into the Fire. They will not die there, nor will they be alive. They will be exposed to its heat and their skin will be burned, and they will be punished with a lasting punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who have earned evil deeds and will be punished in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment, describing it as a burning fire that will not consume them, but will cause them eternal suffering. The verse also highlights the duration of the punishment, indicating that it will be everlasting and not temporary. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as a reward from Allah, and that which is with Allah is best for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who believed in God and did righteous deeds. The phrase 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' is a metaphor for Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and happiness. The phrase 'abiding eternally therein' emphasizes that this reward is not temporary, but rather eternal. The verse also highlights that this reward is a gift from Allah, and that it is the ultimate goal for the righteous. The phrase 'and that which is with Allah is best for the righteous' suggests that the reward in the afterlife is not limited to the physical pleasures of Paradise, but also includes the spiritual joy of being close to God.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: And indeed, We will suffice you against the scoffers, who possess a manifest sin.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and assures him that God will suffice him against the scoffers who ridicule and reject his message. The phrase 'manifest sin' refers to the obvious evil deeds and injustices committed by these scoffers, which are a result of their disbelief and rejection of the truth. The verse implies that their mockery and disbelief will not go unpunished, and that God will take revenge on them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and a reminder that God is aware of their deeds and will hold them accountable.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] a speck on a date stone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of good deeds and faith in Islam. It assures believers that those who do righteous deeds, regardless of their gender, will be rewarded with entry into Paradise, where they will not be wronged or suffer any injustice, not even to the extent of a tiny speck on a date stone. The verse highlights the idea that faith and good deeds are interconnected and that they are the key to a blissful life in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah and he is a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of submitting oneself to Allah and following the teachings of the Prophet Abraham, who was known for his righteousness and truthfulness. The phrase 'submits his face' signifies the utmost obedience and humility before Allah, and 'doer of good' refers to those who act upon their beliefs. The verse also emphasizes the special relationship between Allah and Abraham, who was chosen by Allah as his intimate friend, indicating the high status and respect that Abraham held in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and control over all of creation, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'And to Allah belongs' signifies that everything in existence belongs to God and is under His dominion. The second part of the verse, 'And Allah is sufficient as a Witness', highlights God's omniscience and ability to testify to the actions and deeds of all creation. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is aware of all that they do and that they will be held accountable for their actions on Judgment Day.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: And they ask you to breathe life into the females upon whom you have pronounced divorce, and they ask you to return what has been written for them, and they are eager that you should marry them, and they conceal within themselves what Allah has revealed of the truth, and they are content with the worldly life, and they neglect the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrites who ask the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to compromise the teachings of Islam and allow them to keep their wives despite having pronounced divorce. They also ask him to return the dowry that was given to their wives, indicating their greed and attachment to worldly possessions. The verse highlights the contrast between those who are content with the fleeting pleasures of this life and those who prioritize the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the desires of this world.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And indeed, a woman who had been accused of adultery was brought to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) while she was pregnant. But the Prophet (peace be upon him) did not punish her until she gave birth to her child. Then, when she had given birth, he commanded that she should be stoned to death. The people asked him, 'O Prophet of Allah! Why did you not command her to be stoned to death until she gave birth to her child?' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'I did not want her to suffer the punishment of Allah twice, both in her pregnant state and after giving birth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) compassion and mercy towards the woman who had been accused of adultery. Despite the gravity of her sin, he did not punish her until she had given birth to her child, showing concern for her well-being and the well-being of her unborn child. This verse also underscores the importance of treating sinners with compassion and not punishing them twice for the same sin, as well as the importance of protecting the rights and dignity of all individuals, including those who have made mistakes.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And certainly We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience during these trials, promising good tidings for those who are patient and faithful. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith, and that those who persevere will be rewarded.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And indeed, We will suffice [for the disbelievers] in their absence, and indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge, suggesting that even in the absence of the disbelievers, God is sufficient to carry out His will and plan. The phrase 'and indeed' is repeated twice for emphasis, underscoring the idea that God's sufficiency is not limited by the presence or absence of others. The description of God as 'Wise and Knowing' highlights His infinite wisdom and understanding, implying that His actions are always guided by His infinite wisdom and knowledge.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and indeed We have given those who were given the Scripture before you a clear warning. And indeed, those who disbelieve will be losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over all creation, stating that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him. The verse also warns those who were given the Scripture before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), specifically the Jews and Christians, that they will be held accountable for their actions and will be losers if they disbelieve and reject God's message. The verse serves as a reminder to all people, regardless of their religious affiliation, to recognize and submit to God's authority and to live according to His commandments.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'And to Allah belongs' signifies that everything in the universe, including all creation and all that happens, is under Allah's control and ownership. The second part of the verse, 'And Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs', highlights Allah's ability to manage and govern His creation. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is in control of all things and that they should trust in His plan and wisdom.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the tests and trials that people will face in life, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and resilience in the face of these challenges, and reminds believers that these tests are a means of purification and a way to earn reward in the afterlife. The verse also serves as a reminder that God is All-Powerful and has control over all things, and that believers should put their trust in Him and have faith in His plan.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: And whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who seek the rewards of this world and the Hereafter will find them with Allah. The verse suggests that the rewards of this world are not limited to material gain, but also include spiritual and moral growth. The phrase 'And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing' underscores the idea that God is aware of all human actions and intentions, and that He will reward or punish accordingly. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their actions have consequences in this life and the next, and that they should strive to live a virtuous life to receive God's blessings.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing up for justice, witnesses for Allah, even as against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or decline [to give it], then indeed Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for justice, even if it means testifying against oneself, one's parents, or one's relatives. It reminds believers that Allah is more worthy of them than their personal interests or family ties. The verse warns against following personal inclination or distorting testimony, as Allah is fully aware of their actions and will hold them accountable. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize justice and righteousness over personal interests and to uphold the truth, even if it is difficult or unpopular.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that has been revealed to His Messenger, and the Scripture that was revealed before. Whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His Scripture, and His Messenger has certainly gone astray into clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah, His Messenger, and the revealed Scripture. It warns against disbelief in Allah, His angels, His Scripture, and His Messenger, which is equated with going astray into clear error. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is not just a matter of belief in Allah but also involves belief in His Messenger and the Scripture that has been revealed to him. It highlights the gravity of disbelief and serves as a warning to those who reject faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse describes a group of people who have oscillated between belief and disbelief, and have ultimately increased in their disbelief. The verse states that God will not forgive them, nor guide them to a path. This verse serves as a warning to those who are wavering in their faith, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that God is aware of their actions and will not guide those who consistently reject faith.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Woe to the hypocrites, they will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the hypocrites, warning them of a severe punishment from God. The word 'بشر' (bashr) means 'woe' or 'alas', expressing a sense of regret and sorrow. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the punishment that awaits the hypocrites, who pretend to be believers but are insincere in their faith. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to be Muslims but lack sincerity in their beliefs and actions, reminding them of the consequences of their hypocrisy.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And those who disbelieve take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that, then indeed they will not harm Allah at all. Indeed, Allah will give the believers victory over the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mistake of those who reject faith in Allah and instead choose to ally themselves with others who share their disbelief. The verse emphasizes that this choice will not harm Allah in any way, and that ultimately, Allah will grant victory to the believers over the disbelievers.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And indeed, We have sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah, they deny them and mock at them, so do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of distinguishing oneself from those who reject and mock the teachings of Allah. Believers are commanded not to engage in conversation with such individuals, indicating that their actions and beliefs are incompatible with the teachings of Islam. The verse also serves as a warning to hypocrites and disbelievers, as they will be gathered together in Hell, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: And those who hoard up gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day when it will be heated in the Fire of Hell and their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs will be branded with it. This is the treasure that they hoarded for the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The verse warns those who hoard wealth and do not use it in the way of God, that they will face a painful punishment on the Day of Judgment. The verse describes the punishment as being branded on their foreheads, flanks, and backs with the very wealth they hoarded, indicating that their greed and attachment to material possessions will be the cause of their suffering. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to use their wealth in the way of God and to not let it become a source of distraction from their faith.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and do not remember God except rarely.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but whose actions and intentions are far from it. They try to deceive God and their fellow humans by pretending to be pious, but in reality, they are far from it. They are more concerned with appearances and showing off their supposed piety to others rather than truly remembering and worshiping God. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but whose actions do not reflect their claims.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: And between them and between the believers there will be a barrier, and on that Day the wrongdoers will say, 'If only we had a return [to the world], we would be among the believers!',
interpretation: The verse describes the situation on the Day of Judgment, where there will be a barrier between the believers and the disbelievers. The disbelievers will regret their actions and wish they had another chance to be among the believers, but it will be too late. The verse emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life and having faith in God, as it will determine one's fate in the afterlife.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you want to give Allah against yourselves a clear authority?
interpretation: This verse warns Muslims against befriending or allying themselves with non-believers, emphasizing that such an action would be a clear betrayal of their faith and would give Allah a reason to punish them. The verse highlights the importance of loyalty and allegiance to the Muslim community and the potential consequences of betraying that loyalty.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them any helper.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits the hypocrites in the Hereafter. They will be placed in the lowest depths of Hell, a place of intense suffering and torment. The verse also highlights the fact that there will be no helper or savior for them on the Day of Judgment, and they will be left to face the consequences of their actions alone. This verse serves as a warning to those who pretend to be believers but do not truly follow the teachings of Islam, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they do not change their ways.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except those who repent, amend, and hold fast to God, and purify their religion for God alone, then they will be with the believers, and God will give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance, self-improvement, and devotion to God. It emphasizes that those who turn to God and reform their ways will be counted among the believers and will receive a great reward in the Hereafter. The verse also underscores the idea that true faith is not just a matter of belief, but also involves purifying one's religion and devoting oneself fully to God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for righteousness, assuring them of a great reward in the Hereafter.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: And what Allah has revealed to you of blessings until you become grateful and believe, and indeed Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the blessings and favors that Allah has bestowed upon humanity are a means of testing their gratitude and faith. The verse implies that the ultimate goal of these blessings is to inspire gratitude and belief in the hearts of those who receive them, and that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His distribution of these blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of the sources of their blessings and to recognize the wisdom and knowledge of Allah in their lives.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the evil to be uttered in speech, except when one has been wronged. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking truthfully and avoiding evil speech. The exception to this rule is when one has been wronged, in which case it is permissible to speak out against the injustice. The verse highlights the importance of justice and the need to stand up against oppression. The phrase 'Allah is Hearing and Knowing' serves as a reminder that God is aware of all that we say and do, and that He will hold us accountable for our actions.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you do good, you will do good for your own souls, and if you do evil, it will be against them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that when individuals do good deeds, they are ultimately benefiting themselves, while evil deeds will only harm them in the end. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom in His judgment of human actions, reminding believers that their deeds will be held accountable by a wise and all-knowing God.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and desire to separate between Allah and His messengers, and say, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in some,' and desire to take a path in between.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who pretend to believe in God and His messengers, but in reality, they do not truly believe. They try to find a middle ground between belief and disbelief, thinking that they can deceive God and His messengers. The verse emphasizes that this kind of hypocrisy is unacceptable and that true faith requires a complete submission to God and His messengers, without any compromise or manipulation.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse identifies the disbelievers and emphasizes that they will face a humiliating punishment. The use of the word 'truly' suggests that their disbelief is a certainty, and that they will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'We have prepared' implies that the punishment is already set and ready to be executed, emphasizing the inevitability of the consequences of disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they continue to disbelieve.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believed in Allah and His messengers and did not distinguish between any of them, they will receive their reward and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and His messengers, and the unity of all prophets. It teaches that those who believe in Allah and His messengers, without differentiating between them, will receive their reward and Allah's mercy. The verse highlights the idea that all prophets are from the same source, and that belief in one prophet is belief in all prophets. It also underscores Allah's attribute of being Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, indicating that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: They ask you to bring down a book from the sky, but they asked Moses for something even greater than that, and they were struck by the thunderbolt for their wickedness. Then they took the calf [as their god] after the clear signs had come to them, and We forgave you [Moses] that day. And We gave you a clear authority.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the request of the people who asked the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to bring down a book from the sky, similar to how Moses was asked by his people to bring down a book from God. However, the verse highlights the fact that the people of Moses asked for something even greater than a book, they asked for a divine sign, and they were punished for their wickedness. The verse then goes on to describe how the people of Moses took the golden calf as their god, despite the clear signs that were given to them, and how God forgave Moses on that day and gave him a clear authority. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of following the prophets and their teachings.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised the mountain above them like a canopy, and We said to them, 'Enter the gate prostrate' and We said to them, 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath', and We took from them a firm covenant.
interpretation: The verse describes the miraculous event when Moses and the Israelites were given the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai. The mountain was raised like a canopy over their heads, symbolizing God's power and authority. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God's will, as the Israelites were commanded to enter the gate of the mountain prostrate, in a state of humility and submission. The verse also highlights the significance of the Sabbath, a day of rest and worship, which was instituted as a covenant between God and the Israelites. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to adhere to God's commands and to remember the covenant they have made with Him.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And because they broke their covenant, We cursed them and hardened their hearts, blocking off their ears and their hearts. They rejected the verses of Allah and killed the prophets unjustly. Their hearts are filled with pride, and their ears are closed to the truth. They will not believe, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the consequences of breaking the covenant with God. The people in question were given the responsibility of protecting and following God's commandments, but they failed to do so. As a result, God cursed them and hardened their hearts, causing them to become deaf to the truth and blind to the signs of God's existence. They rejected the revelations of God and even went so far as to kill the prophets who were sent to guide them. Their arrogance and pride have made them deaf to the message of God, and their hearts are closed off to the truth. Only a few will be able to break free from this cycle of disbelief and find the path to righteousness.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And because of their disbelief and their words against Mary, We gave them a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelief and blasphemy of a group of people who rejected the miraculous birth of Jesus through the Virgin Mary. Their disbelief and words against Mary led to a severe punishment from God. The verse highlights the gravity of disbelief and blasphemy, and serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And because of their saying: We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of Allah. But they did not kill him, nor did they cause his death. It was made to seem so to them.
interpretation: The verse addresses the claim made by some Jews that they killed Jesus, son of Mary, who was a prophet and messenger of God. The verse clarifies that they did not actually kill Jesus, but it only seemed that way to them. This verse is a correction of the false belief that Jesus was killed, and it emphasizes that the idea of Jesus' death was a misunderstanding. The verse also highlights the difference between the beliefs of Muslims and Jews, as Muslims believe that Jesus was not killed, but rather raised up to God.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And indeed, there were those who were entrusted with the Scripture before you, [they were] entrusted with the Book of God, and they were witnesses to it, and they did not become disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Jewish community who were entrusted with the Scripture, specifically the Torah, and were witnesses to its authenticity. The verse emphasizes that despite being entrusted with the Scripture, they did not become disbelievers. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with being entrusted with the Word of God, and the importance of remaining faithful to it.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: And indeed, those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of those who have been given knowledge, that is, the scholars and the learned, upon reading the Qur'an. They recognize that the teachings revealed in the Qur'an are the ultimate truth and lead to the path of Allah, the Most High and the Most Praised. This verse serves as a testimony to the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an, as well as a reminder to those who possess knowledge to use it to guide others towards the righteous path.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And We have destroyed them, and theirs was the punishment of the Hereafter, and the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of those who were unjust and denied the truth. Their punishment was not only in this life but also in the Hereafter, where it will be far more severe. The verse warns those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that their actions have consequences that will not be avoided or mitigated by worldly means.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But the steadfast ones in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of 'steadfastness' in knowledge, indicating that true faith is not just a passing belief, but a deep-rooted conviction that endures through trials and tribulations. The verse also emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Qur'an and the previous scriptures, and the practice of prayer and charity as a means of purifying one's soul and demonstrating devotion to God. The verse assures that those who possess these qualities will be rewarded generously in the Hereafter.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent forth to you just as We sent to Noah and the prophets after him, and We sent to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book of Psalms.
interpretation: This verse lists a series of prophets who were sent by God to guide humanity. It emphasizes the continuity of God's message and the unity of the prophets' mission. The list includes prophets from different periods and backgrounds, showing that God's message is universal and timeless. The verse also highlights the significance of the book of Psalms, which was given to David, indicating its importance in the history of divine revelation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and guidance, and encourages believers to reflect on the teachings of the prophets and follow their example in submitting to God's will.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you (O Muhammad) revelations before this, and We have destroyed many a sinful town.
interpretation: This verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God has sent him many revelations before this one, and that those revelations were a mercy and guidance for the believers. The verse also mentions that God has destroyed many sinful towns in the past, emphasizing His power and justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that they will face the same fate as those who were destroyed before them if they continue to disobey and reject God's commands.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messenger (Muhammad SAW) are but sentinels. For what reason then have (the disbelievers) Allah's wrath be upon them?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and other messengers are merely warning signs for humanity, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and guiding them towards righteousness. The verse questions why the disbelievers would incur Allah's wrath, knowing that the messengers have been sent to guide them towards the right path.
