It highlights the importance of heeding the message of the messengers and the consequences of rejecting their message.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness to it. Sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an. Allah is the first witness to the truth of the revelation He has sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The use of the word 'bears witness' (shahida) in the verse emphasizes the idea that Allah is a reliable and trustworthy witness, and His testimony is sufficient to establish the truth of the Qur'an. The verse also mentions that the angels too bear witness to the truth of the Qur'an, indicating that the message of the Qur'an is not limited to human beings but is also acknowledged by the spiritual beings in the heavens. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as a Witness' underscores the idea that Allah's testimony is enough to establish the authenticity of the Qur'an, and no further evidence is needed.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have gone astray, [and have been] misguided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual loss and misguidance of those who reject faith and actively turn others away from the path of God. It highlights the seriousness of their actions, as they are not only harming themselves but also leading others astray. The verse serves as a warning to those who are on the path of disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to the right path.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and act unjustly, theirs will not be forgiven, nor will they be guided to a path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and injustice. The verse states that those who reject faith and instead choose to live in disobedience to God's commands, will not be forgiven and will not be guided to the right path. Their actions have sealed their fate, and they will have to face the consequences of their choices. This verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief and injustice, reminding them of the gravity of their actions and the need to turn back to God and seek forgiveness.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: And indeed, the road to Hell is paved with good intentions, and it is easy for the disbelievers to follow it.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the path to Hell is not necessarily marked by evil intentions, but rather by good intentions that have been misguided. The disbelievers, who reject the truth and refuse to follow God's guidance, find it easy to follow this path because it aligns with their own desires and interests. The verse serves as a warning to believers, reminding them to be mindful of their intentions and actions, and to seek guidance from God to avoid falling into the same trap.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O people, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe in him; it is better for you. And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message he brought from Allah. It encourages the people to accept the truth and warns them of the consequences of rejecting it. The verse also highlights Allah's sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, signifying that everything in the universe belongs to Him and that He is the ultimate authority. The verse ends by emphasizing Allah's knowledge and wisdom, indicating that His decisions are always just and wise.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O people of the Book, do not exceed limits in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth. Indeed, the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is a messenger of Allah and His word that He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. Believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, 'Three'! Refrain from it, for it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is the only one God, the Most High, the Most Great. To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, who are warned not to exceed limits in their religion and not to attribute false statements to Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of believing in Allah and His messengers, including Jesus, who is described as a messenger of Allah and His word conveyed to Mary. The verse also warns against the use of the phrase 'Three' to refer to the Trinity, emphasizing that Allah is one God, the Most High, the Most Great, who is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs. The verse serves as a reminder to the People of the Book to adhere to the true teachings of their religion and to avoid polytheism.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: And the Messiah will not refrain from being a slave to Allah, nor will the angels near [to Him]. And whoever refrains from worshiping Allah will suffer the consequences, and they will be brought before Him, all of them, in humiliation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and uniqueness of God, and the fact that even the Messiah and the angels, who are considered to be closest to God, are still His slaves and subject to His will. The verse also warns those who refuse to worship God and instead choose to worship other deities or reject the idea of worship altogether, that they will face consequences for their actions. The verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, all people will be brought before God, regardless of their beliefs or actions, and they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them to His mercy. Indeed, He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. Indeed, Allah had promised them forgiveness and a great reward. And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, their refuge will be the Fire. They will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fate of believers and disbelievers. The former will be admitted to God's mercy and rewarded with gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will abide forever. The latter, on the other hand, will be punished in the Fire, a painful and severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and righteous deeds in attaining God's forgiveness and reward, while also serving as a warning to those who reject God's signs and deny His existence.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, a clear proof has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse addresses all humanity, emphasizing that a clear and conclusive proof of God's existence and message has been sent to them through the Qur'an. The 'clear light' refers to the guidance and wisdom contained in the Qur'an, which illuminates the path for those who seek truth and righteousness. The verse underscores the responsibility of human beings to recognize and accept this proof, and to live according to its teachings.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them to mercy and grace from Himself and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and guidance that await those who have faith in Allah and hold fast to Him. The phrase 'الذين آمنوا بالله' (those who believe in Allah) refers to those who have submitted themselves completely to Allah, accepting His Oneness and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The phrase 'واعتصموا به' (and hold fast to Him) means that they have firmly grasped onto Allah's rope, that is, they have accepted and followed His commandments and prohibitions. The reward for such believers is 'فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه' (He will admit them to mercy and grace from Himself), indicating that they will be recipients of Allah's mercy and grace in this life and the hereafter. Additionally, Allah will 'يهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما' (guide them to Himself on a straight path), meaning that He will guide them towards righteousness and keep them on the right path, leading them to ultimate success and happiness.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts. Indeed, the livestock has been made lawful for you, except what is being slaughtered, or blood, or the meat of pigs, or what is sacrificed to other than Allah, or that which has been killed by strangling, or killed by a blow to the head, or killed by a fall, or killed by being gored, or from that which has been partially eaten by a wild animal, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death]. And indeed, Allah judges what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling contracts and treaties, and specifically addresses the consumption of meat. The verse prohibits the consumption of animals that have not been properly slaughtered, such as those killed by strangling, blow to the head, fall, or being gored. Additionally, it prohibits the consumption of animals that have been partially eaten by a wild animal. The verse also emphasizes that Allah is aware of all actions and judges accordingly.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, do not profane the symbols of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial animals, nor the garlands, nor the crescent moons, and do not profane the sacred things, that you may seek the bounty of your Lord and His good pleasure. And when you have completed the pilgrimage, then you may hunt, and do not let the hatred of a people who prevent you from the Sacred Mosque incite you to transgress. And cooperate with one another in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and honoring the sacred symbols and institutions of Islam, such as the sacred month and the sacrificial animals. It also prohibits the believers from engaging in sinful behavior, such as profaning the sacred things, and encourages them to cooperate with one another in righteousness and piety. The verse also warns against hatred and aggression towards others, and reminds the believers to fear Allah and His severe punishment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And He has forbidden you dead animals, and blood, and the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and the animal which has died of natural causes or has been killed by another beast or by a human being, and that which has been sacrificed to idols. And He has forbidden you to seek knowledge of the future. Indeed, He has perfected for you your religion, and has completed His favor upon you, and has approved for you Islam as a religion. But whoever is compelled by extreme necessity, not desiring it nor transgressing, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the dietary restrictions placed upon Muslims, specifically prohibiting the consumption of dead animals, blood, pork, animals dedicated to other than Allah, and animals that have died of natural causes or been killed by another animal or human. Additionally, the verse prohibits seeking knowledge of the future. The verse emphasizes that these restrictions are part of a larger plan to perfect and complete Allah's favor upon Muslims, and that Islam is the approved religion. However, in cases of extreme necessity, where an individual is not desiring to transgress and is not acting out of malice, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you what is lawful for them, say, 'Lawful for you are good things, and what you have taught the beasts and animals, training them to remember the name of Allah, as has been taught to you, and fear Allah, indeed Allah is swift in accounting.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of what is lawful for the believers, and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) responds by saying that good things are lawful for them. The verse then highlights the importance of teaching animals and beasts the remembrance of Allah, as a means of purifying their souls and drawing closer to God. The verse concludes by emphasizing the need to fear Allah and remember that He is swift in accounting, indicating that He is aware of all our actions and will hold us accountable for them.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: Today, the righteous are forgiven their food and the believers are forgiven their food. And the believers who were given the Scripture before you were forgiven their food, when you give it to them, not taking it from the disbelievers, nor from the polytheists, and whoever disbelieves in the Hereafter, his work has failed, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the forgiveness of food for the righteous and believers. It emphasizes that the believers who were given the Scripture before, meaning the Jews and Christians, were also forgiven their food. The verse also warns against taking food from disbelievers or polytheists, indicating that the forgiveness of food is only for those who believe in one God and follow His commandments. The verse ends by stating that those who disbelieve in the Hereafter will be losers, indicating that belief in the Hereafter is crucial for a person's faith and ultimate success.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your hands to the elbows; and wipe your heads [with water] and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janaba, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have touched women and cannot find water, then perform tayammum with clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Allah does not desire to make difficulty for you, but He desires to purify you and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purification and cleanliness in religious practices, particularly during prayer. It instructs believers to wash their faces, hands, and feet before prayer, and to perform tayammum (a form of dry ablution) if water is not available. The verse also highlights the importance of spiritual purification and gratefulness to God for His blessings. The use of the phrase "Allah does not desire to make difficulty for you" suggests that God's purpose in commanding these practices is not to burden believers, but to purify and bless them. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of maintaining spiritual and physical cleanliness in daily life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant which He has bound you with, when you said, 'We hear and we obey.' And indeed, Allah knows the secrets of the breasts.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers to remember the blessings and favors of Allah upon them, and the covenant that they have made with Him. The verse specifically refers to the moment when the believers responded to the call of Islam and accepted the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and highlights the fact that Allah is aware of the secrets of the hearts and minds of human beings. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain committed to their faith and to be mindful of their actions, as Allah is always watching and aware of their thoughts and deeds.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing up for Allah as witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for justice and righteousness, even if it means going against the interests of a particular group or individual. It encourages believers to be impartial and fair, and not to let personal biases or prejudices influence their judgment. The verse also reminds believers to fear Allah and to be mindful of their actions, as Allah is aware of everything they do.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And Allah has promised those who have believed and done righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse promises forgiveness and a great reward to those who have believed and done righteous deeds. The verse highlights the importance of faith and good deeds as the criteria for receiving God's forgiveness and reward. The verse also emphasizes the idea that belief and action go hand in hand, and that true faith is reflected in good deeds. The reward mentioned in the verse is not limited to the hereafter but also includes the blessings and peace that one can experience in this life.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the truth. They will be the companions of the Fire, indicating that they will suffer in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief. It serves as a warning to those who are skeptical or resistant to the idea of faith, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the importance of submitting to God's will.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people came to you and We sent against them a group of soldiers, so they were confined to their hands and were about to be conquered, and they were certain that they would be defeated. And they were sure that they would be defeated.
interpretation: The verse reminds the believers of the favor of Allah upon them, specifically the time when they were in a vulnerable position and a group of soldiers was sent against them. The verse emphasizes the hopelessness of the situation, with the enemy confined to their hands and the believers on the brink of defeat. However, Allah intervened and saved them from their predicament, demonstrating His power and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to put their trust in Allah and to remember His favor, especially in times of hardship and uncertainty.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed, We have taken a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent from them twelve leaders, and Allah said, 'I will be with you, if you establish the prayer and give the zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and lend Allah a goodly loan. Indeed, I will remit your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that, he has indeed strayed from the straight path.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the covenant between God and the Children of Israel, where God appointed twelve leaders from among them. The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer, giving zakah (charity), believing in God's messengers, and supporting them. In return, God promises to be with them, forgive their sins, and grant them entrance to paradise. The verse also warns those who reject this covenant and disbelieve in God, describing them as having strayed from the straight path.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And among those who say, 'We are Christians,' We have taken their covenant, but they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of, so We stirred up enmity and hatred between them until the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrites who claim to be Christians but have forgotten the true teachings of their religion. They have forgotten the covenant they made with God and have instead stirred up enmity and hatred among themselves. The verse warns that on the Day of Resurrection, God will remind them of their actions and hold them accountable for their deeds.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O people of the Book, Our messenger has come to you making clear to you much of what you used to hide from the Book and forgiving much. Indeed, a light and a clear Book has come to you from Allah.
interpretation: The verse addresses the people of the Book, meaning the Jews and Christians, and reminds them that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been sent to clarify and reveal the truth that was hidden or distorted in their scriptures. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet has been sent to forgive and overlook many of their past mistakes and sins, and that the Qur'an is a light and clear book that has come from Allah, providing guidance and clarity to those who seek it.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: And Allah guides not the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not guide those who disobey and reject His commands. The verse implies that those who choose to disobey Allah are left to their own devices and are not under His guidance or protection. This serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's teachings, reminding them that they will not have His guidance or support in their lives. It also highlights the importance of obeying Allah's commands and living a righteous life in order to receive His guidance and blessings.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, those who say: 'Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary' have disbelieved. Say: 'Who then has the least power against Allah if He had willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother, and whoever is in the earth altogether?' And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills.
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim that Jesus, son of Mary, is God, which is a belief held by some Christians. The verse states that those who make this claim have disbelieved and are reminded that God has power over all things. The verse asks rhetorically, who can oppose God's will if He had wanted to destroy Jesus and his mother, and emphasizes that everything in the heavens and earth, including Jesus and his mother, is under God's control and creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's authority and power over all things and refutes the belief that Jesus is God or equal to God.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones.' Say, 'Why then does He punish you for your sins? Indeed, you are human beings, just like those who were created before you. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the return.
interpretation: The verse addresses the claim of the Jews and Christians that they are the children of God and His beloved ones, and therefore, they are immune to punishment. The verse refutes this claim by pointing out that they are human beings, just like others who were created before them, and that they are not exempt from God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that God's punishment is not based on lineage or ancestry, but rather on the individual's actions and deeds. The verse also highlights God's sovereignty over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, and that ultimately, all will return to Him for judgment.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O people of the Book, Our messenger has come to you, making things clear to you, upon a period of time, from the messengers, that you may be able to say: 'We have not been given a clear sign'; indeed, a clear sign has come to you, and Allah is Powerful over all things.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, reminding them that a messenger has been sent to them, who has made things clear to them over a period of time, just like the messengers before him. The verse emphasizes that the messenger has brought a clear sign from God, and that they have no excuse to deny it. The verse also highlights God's power and authority over all things, indicating that His punishment is certain and inescapable for those who reject His message.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you, when He made prophets among you and made you kings and gave you what He had not given to anyone else in the world.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is reminding his people of the blessings that God has bestowed upon them. He highlights the fact that God has sent prophets among them, which is a sign of His favor and mercy. Additionally, God has made them kings, which symbolizes their authority and power. The verse also mentions that God has given them what He has not given to anyone else in the world, indicating their unique status and privilege. Moses' message serves as a reminder to the people of their responsibility to live up to God's expectations and to be grateful for the blessings they have received.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O people, enter the holy land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back on your heels, for you will turn back as losers.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to enter the holy land, which is a metaphor for living a righteous life and following God's commandments. The verse warns against turning back or retreating from one's faith, as it leads to spiritual loss and defeat. The verse encourages the believers to persevere and remain steadfast in their faith, promising them success and victory in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed there is a people of tyrannical men in it who have rejected us. We will not enter it until they leave it, for indeed, we are unable to enter it as long as they are there.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the Israelites when Moses invited them to enter the promised land. They expressed their fear of the giants who lived there, saying that they would not be able to enter the land as long as those giants were still there. The verse highlights the Israelites' lack of faith and trust in God's promise, as well as their unwillingness to confront the challenges and obstacles that lay ahead. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and courage in the face of adversity, and the need to trust in God's plan and provision.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: And indeed, those who fear Allah - He will give them a way out. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings and relief that come with fearing Allah and living a righteous life. The phrase 'He will give them a way out' implies that God will provide a means of escape or relief for those who are pious and fear Him. The second part of the verse emphasizes that God is with those who do good deeds, suggesting that He is always present and supportive of those who strive to live a virtuous life. The verse encourages believers to have faith and trust in God, and to live according to His will in order to receive His guidance and blessings.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, we will never enter it, as long as they are in it, for we will not enter it until they leave it. Go ahead, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are staying right here.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the Israelites when Moses invited them to enter the Promised Land. They refused to enter the land as long as the previous inhabitants were still living there, expressing their unwillingness to fight and conquer the land. The verse highlights the Israelites' lack of faith and trust in God's promise and their reluctance to engage in battle. It also shows their disobedience to Moses' leadership and their unwillingness to take risks and face challenges.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: My Lord, I have no power except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the wicked people.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is imploring God to distinguish between himself and his brother Aaron, and the wicked people who reject God's message. Moses recognizes that he has no authority or control over anyone else, but he asks God to separate him and his brother from those who oppose God's will. This verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's limitations and seeking God's guidance and intervention in the face of adversity.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed them, and theirs is a lesson to the people of understanding.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the previous nations who were wicked and ignored the signs of God. Their destruction serves as a lesson to those who come after them, a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the certainty of God's justice. The phrase 'people of understanding' suggests that the lesson is not just for the masses, but for those who have the ability to reflect and comprehend the signs of God.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he cast them away, so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who were destroyed.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the prophet Sulaiman and the queen of Sheba. The verse warns against the dangers of pride and arrogance, as the queen of Sheba was punished for her refusal to accept the prophet's message and her attempt to kill him. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment can come suddenly and unexpectedly, and that those who reject God's signs will face consequences. The verse also highlights the role of Satan in leading people astray and the importance of being mindful of one's actions and beliefs.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: And indeed, I will divert your hands and your feet and your skins from you and leave you in your beds as a witness to My punishment.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the disbelievers who have been warned of His punishment but refuse to believe. God says that He will make their hands, feet, and skins, which were once used for sin and disobedience, to be the cause of their destruction. The phrase 'leave you in your beds' implies that they will be struck down in their own homes, where they feel most secure, and will be unable to escape God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires, reminding them that God's punishment is near and inevitable.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I want to recompense those who commit sin and aggression with the punishment of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's intention to punish those who commit sin and aggression. The use of the word 'Indeed' at the beginning of the verse suggests a strong affirmation of this intention. The phrase 'those who commit sin and aggression' refers to those who have violated God's laws and committed injustices. The punishment mentioned in the verse is specifically the Fire, which is a metaphor for the suffering and torment that awaits those who have committed wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: And he killed his soul, his brother, so he became one of the losers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about Cain's murder of his brother Abel, which is seen as a symbol of the destructive nature of jealousy and envy. Cain's actions were motivated by a desire to eliminate his brother's success and goodness, but ultimately, he brought destruction upon himself, becoming one of the 'losers' in the eyes of God. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of envy and the importance of controlling one's negative emotions.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: And God sent a crow to search for water in the land, that he might show his brother how to obtain water, saying, 'Woe to me! I cannot be like this crow and find water for my brother.' So he became of the regretful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a crow that was sent by God to search for water in a land where the people were suffering from drought. The crow's search for water is a metaphor for the search for guidance and righteousness. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from God and following the right path. The phrase 'Woe to me!' expresses the regret and remorse that one feels when they realize they have strayed from the right path. The verse serves as a reminder to turn to God in times of hardship and to seek guidance from Him.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: And We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inheritance of the earth by the righteous servants of God. The phrase 'after the Reminder' refers to the fact that the message of the Qur'an is a reminder to the people of the earth, a reminder of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment. The verse emphasizes that the earth will be inherited by those who are righteous and just, indicating that the reward for their good deeds will be the inheritance of the earth. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are wicked and unjust, reminding them that they will not inherit the earth, but rather will face punishment for their actions.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: Indeed, those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth [with] corruption, their recompense is that they will be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet will be cut off from opposite sides or they will be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences for those who fight against God and His Messenger and engage in corruption on earth. The punishment for such individuals is severe, including death, crucifixion, amputation of limbs, or exile from the land. This punishment serves as a deterrent to those who would consider such actions and serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of going against God's will. The verse emphasizes the shame and disgrace that those who engage in such actions will face in this life and the severe punishment they will face in the Hereafter.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except those who repent before you overcome them, and know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness before it's too late. The verse emphasizes that those who repent and turn to God before they are overtaken by punishment will be spared, indicating that repentance can avert the consequences of sin. The verse also underscores God's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful, signifying that He is always ready to accept those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him and strive in His cause, that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and seeking a close relationship with Him through acts of worship and obedience. The phrase 'means of approach' refers to the various ways in which one can draw closer to Allah, such as prayer, fasting, charity, and pilgrimage. The verse also encourages believers to strive in Allah's cause, which includes spreading Islam, fighting injustice, and struggling against one's own desires. The ultimate goal of these efforts is success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve would like to have all the good things in the world and the like of it with them, and they will be given a punishment that will be timely.
interpretation: The verse describes the mentality of those who reject faith in God and the Hereafter. They desire to accumulate all the wealth and luxuries of this world, but they will ultimately face a punishment that is proportionate to their disbelief and greed. The phrase 'and the like of it with them' suggests that they want to take their material possessions with them to the Hereafter, but they will be disappointed to find that their wealth will not save them from God's punishment. The phrase 'and they will be given a punishment that will be timely' implies that the punishment will be swift and certain, and will not be delayed.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They wish to extinguish the fire, but it will not be extinguished until they are consumed by it, and they will be tormented in their own Fire, and they will be punished because they were not far-sighted.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who seek to avoid the punishment of God by trying to extinguish the fire of hell. However, the fire will not be extinguished until it has consumed them, indicating that their attempts to avoid punishment will be unsuccessful. The verse also highlights the fact that they will be punished in their own fire, indicating that they will be punished in accordance with their own deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who seek to avoid the consequences of their actions, reminding them that they will ultimately face the punishment they deserve.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: The thief, the male and the female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, and as a punishment from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse discusses the punishment for theft, specifically the cutting off of the thief's hand. The verse emphasizes that this punishment is a recompense for their actions and a punishment from Allah. The use of the phrase "Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise" serves to highlight God's power and wisdom in enforcing this punishment. The verse serves as a deterrent to those who might consider theft, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions, and also emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and law in society.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And whoever repents after his injustice and reforms, indeed, Allah will relent on him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of repentance and the mercy of God. It emphasizes that even if one has committed injustices in the past, if they repent and reform, God will forgive them and show mercy. The verse encourages individuals to turn towards God and seek forgiveness, promising that God will relent and show compassion. The verse also underscores the idea that repentance is not just a one-time event, but a continuous process of self-reflection, improvement, and growth.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, Allah has knowledge of the heavens and the earth, and He punishes whom He wills, and forgives whom He wills. And Allah is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and His ability to punish or forgive anyone He chooses. The verse highlights God's knowledge of all things, both in the heavens and on earth, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also underscores God's power and authority, reminding believers that He is capable of doing anything He desires. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in God's justice and mercy, and to trust in His wisdom and knowledge.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger, do not be grieved by those who hasten to disbelieve, such as those who say, 'We believe' with their tongues, but their hearts do not believe, and those who support the disbelievers. They have not harmonized their hearing and their hearts. And those who seek to distort the words after their places, saying, 'We have heard,' but they did not observe. And if they are given what they are told, they will not be reminded. And if they are not given, they will be warned. And those who turn away from the reminder will have no share in the Hereafter. They are the ones whose hearts Allah will not purify for them in this world, and they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, urging him not to be saddened by those who reject the message of Islam. The verse describes two types of people who reject the message: those who claim to believe with their tongues but their hearts are not sincere, and those who openly support the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes that these people have not truly listened to the message and have not allowed it to touch their hearts. The verse also warns those who distort the message or reject it altogether, stating that they will not have a share in the Hereafter. The verse ends by stating that Allah will not purify the hearts of those who reject the message in this world, and they will face a great punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: And if they (the unbelievers) had believed in Allah and the Prophet (Muhammad SAW) and what has been sent down to him, surely, they would have received provisions and safety from Allah. But they denied, so a seal has been placed upon their hearts and they have been deaf and blinded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and the rejection of God's message. The verse indicates that those who reject God and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will be denied provision and protection from God. Their hearts are sealed, and they become deaf and blind to the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to turn to God and His Prophet for guidance and protection.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We have sent down the Torah, in which there is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted [to God] judged those who were entrusted with the Scripture, and the rabbis and the scholars, because they were entrusted with the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people, but fear Me, and do not buy the verses of God for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then they are the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Torah, which contains guidance and light for those who follow it. The prophets and scholars who submitted to God judged others according to the teachings of the Torah, and were witnesses to its truth. The verse warns against fearing people instead of God and against buying the verses of God for a small price, indicating that the value of God's revelations cannot be measured by material wealth. The verse also emphasizes the importance of following God's revelations and not judging by anything else, as those who do not follow God's revelations are considered disbelievers.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We have destroyed them, and theirs are the houses, and the keys are in their places, and the disasters are in their seasons, and the pain is in their ears, and the punishment is in their sin, and whoever believes in Him, he will be a loser, and whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of communities that have been unjust and rejected God's signs. The verse emphasizes that the destruction is not only physical but also spiritual, as the people's houses are left empty and their keys are still in their places, indicating that they were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse also warns that those who reject God's revelations and do not follow His commandments will face punishment and be considered wrongdoers.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We have followed their footsteps, the footsteps of the prophets, and We sent them the Book, a guidance and a light, and a confirmation of what was between their hands, a guidance and a mercy for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse explains how God has continued to guide humanity through the ages by sending prophets who have followed in the footsteps of previous prophets. The prophets were given the scripture, which served as a guidance and a light, and a confirmation of what was revealed to them. The scripture was a guidance for the righteous and a mercy for those who believed. The verse highlights the continuity of God's message and the importance of following the teachings of the prophets.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then they are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Qur'an and the consequences of not doing so. The phrase 'People of the Gospel' refers to the Christians, who are being addressed here. The verse is instructing them to follow the teachings of the Qur'an, which is the final revelation from God, and to judge by its teachings. The verse warns that those who do not follow the teachings of the Qur'an are considered defiantly disobedient and will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, confirming what is between your hands of the Book, and the judgment of Allah to which you are commanded to follow it, and do not follow their desires, diverging from the truth that has come to you. For each We have made a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation, but to test you through what has come to you. So, strive for the good deeds, to Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an as a revelation from God, confirming the truth in the Scriptures that came before it. It warns the believers not to follow their own desires and deviate from the truth, but to adhere to the law and way of life that God has prescribed for them. The verse also highlights the purpose of diversity in religious practices and beliefs, which is to test humanity's obedience and faith in God. The ultimate goal is for all people to strive for good deeds and return to God, who will judge their actions and inform them of their fate.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And indeed, We have sent down to you clear verses and examples from the past, and warnings for those who fear Allah and are mindful of their Lord. And the punishment will surely befall those who disobey Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warning signs and examples from the past, as mentioned in the Qur'an, in order to avoid the punishment that awaits those who disobey Allah. The verse also highlights the fear of Allah and mindfulness of one's Lord as key characteristics of those who are righteous and will be spared from punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that disobedience will not go unpunished.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse prohibits Muslims from taking Jews and Christians as allies or friends, as they are allies of one another and will not support the Muslim community. The verse emphasizes that those who ally themselves with Jews and Christians are essentially one of them and are not guided by Allah. This verse highlights the importance of Muslim unity and the need to be cautious of external influences that may compromise the faith and values of the Muslim community.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reaction of those who have been given knowledge, that is, the believers who have been guided by God's revelation. They see the truth in the Qur'an and recognize its divine origin. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a guidance from God, leading to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy, that is, the path that leads to God's pleasure and mercy. The verse highlights the importance of knowledge and understanding in recognizing the truth of God's revelation and following His guidance.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe will say, 'How unjust were those who disbelieved in their Lord? Their works have failed them, so they are losers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the believers when they see the punishment of those who disbelieved in God. The believers recognize that the disbelievers' actions were in vain and that their disbelief has led to their downfall. The verse highlights the contrast between the success of the believers and the failure of the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith in God and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should turn back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him, humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is All-Embracing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers and warns them against turning back from their religion. The verse describes the characteristics of those who are faithful and obedient to God, saying that they are humble towards the believers and mighty against the disbelievers. The verse also emphasizes that those who strive in the cause of God will be given grace and success, and that God's grace is a gift that He gives to whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for the cause of God, and it also highlights the reward of those who are faithful and obedient.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Indeed, Allah and His Messenger and the believers who maintain the prayer and give the zakat are the ones who are true to their promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prayer and charity as fundamental aspects of a believer's life. The phrase 'ورسوله' (and His Messenger) is significant as it emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a leader and guide for the Muslim community. The phrase 'يقيمون الصلاة' (they establish prayer) indicates the importance of regular prayer and its role in maintaining a strong spiritual foundation. 'يؤتون الزكاة' (and give the zakat) highlights the importance of charity and giving back to the community. The phrase 'هم راكعون' (they bow down [in prayer]) emphasizes the humility and submission required in prayer. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay true to their faith and maintain a strong spiritual practice.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and those who have believed, indeed the party of Allah - they will be the predominant ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger, and the belief in the latter's message. It emphasizes that those who follow God's commandments and believe in the Prophet's teachings will be the ultimate victors. The verse is a reminder that the righteous will ultimately triumph over the wicked, and serves as an encouragement to believers to remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of adversity.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and play, and the disbelievers as allies. Indeed, they are allies of one another. And fear Allah, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against befriending those who mock and ridicule their religion, and those who disbelieve in God. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God and being mindful of one's faith, and not to align oneself with those who oppose it. The verse also highlights the unity and alliance between believers and disbelievers, indicating that those who reject God's message are on the same side, while believers must stand together in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in mockery and play, and that is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers when the believers call to prayer. Instead of taking the call to prayer seriously, they mock and make fun of it, indicating their lack of understanding and ignorance of the significance of prayer. The verse highlights the contrast between the believers, who take prayer seriously and understand its importance, and the disbelievers, who do not comprehend the value of prayer and instead mock it. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the mockery and disbelief of others.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, O people of the Book, do you resent us except that we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before? And indeed, most of you are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, asking them if their resentment towards the believers is based on their belief in Allah and the revelations that have been sent to them. The verse implies that the People of the Book have a history of disobedience and rebellion against God's teachings, and that their resentment towards the believers is rooted in their own disbelief and arrogance. The verse serves as a reminder that true belief in God requires submission to His will and obedience to His commandments, and that those who reject God's revelations will face the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, 'Have you seen the one who has been cursed by Allah and with whom He has been angry, and whom He has made monkeys and pigs, and servants of the tyrant? They are worse in position and further astray from the path.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have been cursed by God and are under His anger. They have been compared to monkeys and pigs, which are considered impure and filthy animals in Islam. Additionally, they are described as servants of a tyrant, indicating that they are under the control of an oppressive ruler. The verse emphasizes their wretched state and how far they have strayed from the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they came to you, they said, 'We have believed,' while they were disbelievers,
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who outwardly claimed to have faith in Islam, but in reality, they were not sincere in their beliefs. They were pretending to be Muslims, but their actions and hearts were not in line with the teachings of Islam. The verse highlights the danger of hypocrisy and the importance of being truthful and sincere in one's beliefs. It serves as a warning to those who claim to be Muslims but do not truly follow the teachings of Islam, and it emphasizes the importance of being genuine and sincere in one's faith.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them rushing into sin and aggression and their consumption of illicit gain. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the widespread nature of sin and injustice among the people, who are eagerly engaging in various forms of wrongdoing, such as aggression and the pursuit of illicit gain. The verse emphasizes the negative nature of their actions, describing them as 'evil', and suggesting that their behavior is not only harmful to others but also morally reprehensible. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the need to repent and turn towards a righteous path.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And if the Rabbaniun and the Ahbar had not been prohibited from saying their evil sayings and consuming the unlawful, surely they would have been punished in a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the religious leaders and scholars who have been corrupted by their own desires and have abandoned the true teachings of their faith. They are condemned for their evil words and actions, and are warned of a painful punishment if they do not repent and change their ways. The verse highlights the importance of religious leaders being mindful of their own behavior and setting a good example for their followers, lest they face the consequences of their misdeeds.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is tied up.' Tied up are their hands, and they are cursed for what they said. Nay, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills. Indeed, their evil deeds have been adorned for them, and Allah has sent them astray. They are forgetful, so He will cause them to forget their revelations, or He will make them forget their revelations, and they will not be remembered.
interpretation: The verse addresses the statement made by the Jews, who claimed that God's hand is tied up and unable to punish them. The verse refutes this claim, stating that God's hands are outstretched and He spends as He wills. The verse implies that the Jews' statement was a result of their arrogance and disbelief, and that they have been misguided by their own evil deeds. The verse also suggests that God will cause them to forget their revelations, indicating that they will not be able to remember or follow His teachings.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if the people of the Scripture had believed and been righteous, We would have removed from them their evil deeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the People of the Book, who were given the Scripture (the Jews and Christians) and how they would have been spared from their evil deeds and admitted to Paradise if they had believed and lived righteously. The verse highlights the idea that faith and righteousness are the criteria for salvation, and that those who meet these criteria will be rewarded with eternal bliss in Paradise.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if they had believed in Me and in My signs, and had not rejected the Prophets, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet would have been a nation guided and a people who fear [Allah].
interpretation: The verse indicates that the people were given the opportunity to believe in God and His signs, but they rejected the Prophets and refused to follow God's guidance. As a result, they missed out on the blessings and guidance that come from following God's commands. The verse also suggests that had they believed, they would have been a nation guided and a people who fear Allah, indicating that belief in God and His signs is the key to guidance and righteousness.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. If you do not, you will not have conveyed His message. Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) conveying the message of Islam to the people. The verse warns the Prophet that if he does not convey the message, he will not have fulfilled his duty as a messenger of God. The verse also assures the Prophet that God will protect him from the people, indicating that the Prophet will face opposition and hostility from those who reject the message. The verse ends by emphasizing that God does not guide the disobedient people, indicating that those who reject the message will not be guided to the truth.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, O people of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the inclinations of those who have gone astray, and do not yield to those who have no fear of God and His punishment, lest you be seized by a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, that is, the Jews and Christians, and admonishes them not to go beyond the limits of their religion and follow the inclinations of those who have gone astray. It warns them not to yield to those who have no fear of God and His punishment, lest they be seized by a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying within the boundaries of one's religion and not being influenced by those who have strayed from the right path. It also serves as a warning against the consequences of disobedience and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, those who have migrated and striven in the cause of Allah, and those who have believed and have not emigrated - for those who have believed in Allah and the Last Day, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the blessings and rewards that await the believers who have migrated and struggled in the cause of Allah. It emphasizes that those who have believed in Allah and the Last Day will have no fear of punishment or sadness, indicating that they will be protected and rewarded in the afterlife. The verse also highlights the importance of migration and striving in the cause of Allah as a means of attaining salvation and achieving a state of ultimate peace and happiness.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And We took the covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire, they denied some and killed some.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the covenant that God made with the Children of Israel and how He sent prophets to guide them. However, instead of following the prophets' teachings, the Israelites often rejected and even killed them. The verse highlights the disobedience and rebelliousness of the Israelites, who were unwilling to listen to God's message and instead chose to follow their own desires. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of following God's commandments.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they had thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah's punishment, but the punishment came to them from where they did not expect, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who thought that their fortresses and strongholds would protect them from God's punishment. However, the punishment came to them unexpectedly, indicating that no amount of human effort or fortification can protect one from God's wrath. The verse highlights the all-knowing and wise nature of God, who is aware of all human actions and can punish at any moment. The verse serves as a warning to those who rely on material possessions and fortifications for protection, reminding them that only God's mercy and forgiveness can truly protect them.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: And indeed, those who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary' have disbelieved. Say, 'And who could oppose God if He had willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth?' And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. Indeed, God is capable of all things.
interpretation: The verse addresses the claim made by some people that Jesus, the son of Mary, is God. The verse refutes this claim by asking a rhetorical question, suggesting that if God had wanted to destroy Jesus and his mother, who could have stopped Him? The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power over all things, indicating that He is capable of anything. The verse serves as a reminder to those who reject God's oneness and associate partners with Him, that He is the only one worthy of worship and that those who oppose Him will face His punishment.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Those who disbelieve say: Allah is the third of three; there is no god but One God, and if they refrain not from what they say, those who disbelieve of them will be punished.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelief of those who claim that God is three entities, suggesting a polytheistic belief. The verse emphasizes that there is only one God, and those who reject this belief and insist on their polytheistic views will face punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the oneness of God and encourage others to do the same, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of adhering to the belief in one God.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: And they do not implore Allah except while they are in a state of fear. Then once they are saved, they forget their prayer and become defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to only turn to God in times of crisis, when they are afraid or in need. However, once they are saved or their problems are solved, they quickly forget their prayers and return to their disobedient ways. The verse suggests that true faith is not just about seeking help in times of need, but also about maintaining a consistent relationship with God and living a righteous life.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: And Jesus, son of Mary, was not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They used to eat food. Look how We make clear the signs to them, then look how they are averse to the truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Jesus, son of Mary, was a prophet like other prophets before him, and his mother, Mary, was a righteous woman who supported the truth. The verse also highlights the fact that prophets are human beings who need to eat and drink like everyone else. The verse then questions the disbelievers, asking them why they refuse to believe in the signs and miracles that God has sent to them through His prophets. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of the prophets is one of truth and guidance, and that rejecting it will only lead to destruction.
