orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Serve Allah or serve the Taghut. Whatever you worship besides Him will not harm or benefit you. Verily, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah and avoiding the worship of any other being or entity. The verse warns that worshiping anything else besides Allah will not bring any benefit or harm, indicating that it is futile to worship anything else. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, emphasizing that He is fully aware of all that we do and that our actions are not hidden from Him. The verse serves as a reminder to focus our worship solely on Allah and to avoid idolatry, as it is the only way to attain true guidance and success.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, 'O people of the Book, do not exceed limits in your religion, and do not follow the inclinations of those who went astray before, and they misled many, and they strayed from the right path.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, who are the Jews and Christians, and warns them against going beyond the limits of their religion and following the misguided inclinations of their predecessors. The verse implies that those who went astray before them were misled by their own desires and led many others astray, causing them to stray from the right path. The verse serves as a reminder to stick to the true teachings of their religion and not to be swayed by personal desires or the influence of others.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Woe to those who disbelieve from the children of Israel, on account of their rebelliousness, and their false utterances, against David and Jesus, the son of Mary, because they were disobedient and used to exceed the limits.
interpretation: The verse condemns the disbelief of the children of Israel, specifically their rebellion against God and their false statements against the prophets, including David and Jesus, son of Mary. The verse emphasizes their disobedience and tendency to exceed the limits set by God. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and prophets, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: And they were not forbidden from doing evil, so they committed what was evil.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people in question were not restrained from doing evil and, as a result, they engaged in wicked deeds. The verse implies that the lack of restraint or accountability can lead individuals and societies to commit heinous acts, emphasizing the importance of self-reflection and accountability in preventing such acts.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And indeed, many of them We destroyed, [including] nations and cities. So their deities, which they used to worship, availed them not when the command of your Lord came to them. And they were not ones who could avert [the punishment].
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who denied the messengers and the consequences of their disbelief. The use of the phrase 'many of them' emphasizes that this is a recurring pattern throughout history, where nations and cities have been destroyed due to their disobedience. The verse also emphasizes that the idols and deities they worshipped were of no avail when God's punishment came upon them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them that they will not be able to escape the punishment of God.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would have been better guided than those who were given authority and wealth, but many of them were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse highlights the connection between faith and guidance. It suggests that those who believe in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him (the Qur'an) would be better guided than those who were given authority and wealth. The verse implies that material wealth and authority do not necessarily lead to guidance, and that true guidance comes from faith and submission to Allah. The verse also warns against the dangers of disobedience and rebellion against Allah's commandments, which can lead to a person's downfall.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: And indeed, the most affectionate of the people towards the believers are those who said, 'We are Christians.' They are the ones who are priests and monks, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: The verse highlights the affection and respect that the believers receive from the Christians, specifically those who are priests and monks. These individuals are not only religious leaders but also humble and unassuming, not boastful or arrogant. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate and value the positive relationships between people of different faiths, and to recognize the importance of humility and modesty in religious leaders.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth, saying, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so write us down among the witnesses'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the believers when they hear the revelations given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are moved to tears by the truth they have recognized, and they implore God to include them among the witnesses of the faith. The verse highlights the joy and conviction of the believers in their faith and their desire to be counted among those who bear witness to the truth of Islam.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: And God will punish them for their sayings, [by] gardens and rivers, they will abide therein forever. That is the recompense of the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who have done good deeds and lived a righteous life. The phrase 'gardens and rivers' is used to describe a place of eternal bliss and happiness, where the righteous will reside forever. The verse emphasizes that this reward is a recompense for their good deeds and is a manifestation of God's justice, where those who have lived a virtuous life will be rewarded with a life of eternal joy and peace.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the truth. They will be the companions of the Fire, indicating that they will suffer eternal punishment in Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful to you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, reminding them that God has made certain things lawful for them and that they should not prohibit or forbid them. The verse also warns against transgressing or exceeding the limits set by God, as He does not like those who transgress or commit injustice. The verse emphasizes the importance of living within the boundaries set by God and not overstepping them, as this can lead to harm and injustice.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And spend what We have provided you with, good and lawful, and fear Allah, Whom you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spending what Allah has provided us with in a lawful and good manner, and to fear Allah, the One whom we worship. It suggests that our provisions are a blessing from Allah and should be used in a way that is pleasing to Him. The verse also highlights the relationship between our actions and our worship, reminding us that true worship is not limited to religious rituals, but also encompasses how we live our lives and use the resources we have been given.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: And let not the hatred of a people that disbelieved in the first place cease from you, so that you become oppressors. And fear the punishment, for indeed, Allah will punish the disobedient.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against oppressing others, especially those who have disbelieved in the first place. It emphasizes the importance of fearing God's punishment and avoiding oppressive behavior, as it can lead to severe consequences. The verse also highlights the importance of keeping promises and being mindful of one's actions, as they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed wine, gambling, [sacrificing to] stones, and divination are impurity from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding activities that are considered impure and sinful, such as wine, gambling, and divination. These activities are described as being from the work of Satan, indicating that they are harmful and lead individuals away from the righteous path. The verse encourages believers to avoid these activities in order to achieve success in both this life and the hereafter. The use of the word "impurity" highlights the negative impact that these activities have on an individual's spiritual and moral purity, and serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual foundation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, Satan only wants to provoke enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling and to distract you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So, will you be deterred?
interpretation: This verse highlights the Satan's strategy to use intoxicants and gambling as tools to create enmity and hatred among people, and to distract them from the remembrance of Allah and their obligations towards Him. The verse serves as a warning to believers, reminding them of the dangers of these vices and the importance of staying vigilant in their faith and spiritual practices.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. Indeed, if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger has been entrusted with a clear message.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger. The phrase 'obeys Allah and obey the Messenger' signifies that obedience to God and His Messenger is inseparable. The verse warns the believers to be mindful of their actions and their responsibility to follow the teachings of Islam. The phrase 'be aware' serves as a reminder that the Prophet has been entrusted with a clear message, and those who reject it will be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights the gravity of the Prophet's message and the need for the believers to take it seriously.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Not upon those who believed and did righteous deeds shall be any fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and rewards that believers will receive in the afterlife. It assures them that they will not experience fear or grief, as they have lived a life of faith and righteousness. The verse also highlights the importance of both belief and good deeds, as both are necessary for a person to attain salvation. The verse serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for believers, reminding them that their faith and actions will be rewarded in the hereafter.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be patient; indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and faith in God's plan, reminding believers that they will not be tested beyond their limits. The verse encourages them to fear God and have patience in the face of adversity, as they will be judged based on their deeds in life. The verse also highlights the idea that everyone will be given only what they can handle, and that God is aware of their capabilities and limitations.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill the game while you are in a state of sacred inviolability or hunting it in the sacred precincts, just as you would kill one another. Indeed, God has given you judgment and wisdom. How can you disobey God's commandment and violate the sanctity of the sacred precincts?
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers and prohibits them from hunting game while they are in a state of sacred inviolability or within the sacred precincts. The verse emphasizes that God has given humans judgment and wisdom, and therefore they should not engage in acts that go against His commandments. The verse also highlights the importance of respecting the sanctity of the sacred precincts, which are places of great spiritual significance. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to always act in accordance with God's will and to avoid actions that may harm others or violate the sacred.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: And He has subjected to you, as from Him, all that is in the heavens and on earth: behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God, who has control over all things in the heavens and on earth. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's creation and to recognize His authority and dominion over all things. The verse also serves as a reminder that everything in the universe is subject to God's will and that humans should submit to His commandments and live according to His guidance.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And Allah has made the Ka'bah, the sacred House, a place of resort for people and the sacred month and the animals of sacrifice and the garlands. That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Ka'bah, the sacred House in Mecca, as a place of pilgrimage for believers. The verse also highlights the importance of the sacred month, during which the pilgrimage takes place, and the animals of sacrifice, which are offered to God as a symbol of submission and devotion. The verse further emphasizes God's knowledge and power, indicating that He is aware of all things, both in the heavens and on earth. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of God's greatness and His presence in all aspects of life.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the dual nature of God's attribute of punishment. On one hand, God is severe in punishment, indicating that those who commit evil deeds will face severe consequences. On the other hand, God is also Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that those who repent and turn to God will receive mercy and forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and to seek God's forgiveness, while also serving as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in sin.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And the Messenger has not been given except the conveyance of the message, and God knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of the Prophet's role to only convey the message of God, and that he has no control over the response of the people. The verse also highlights God's knowledge of all that is hidden and revealed, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and the believers that their role is to convey the message and leave the outcome to God, who is the ultimate judge of all actions and intentions.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, 'The evil and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of the evil may please you.' So fear Allah, O you of great intellect, that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the difference between good and evil, and the danger of being swayed by the appearance of abundance or quantity. The phrase 'even though the abundance of the evil may please you' suggests that the wicked may seem powerful and successful, but this is an illusion. The true measure of success is not wealth or status, but rather the fear of Allah and adherence to His commandments. The verse encourages the reader to cultivate a deep sense of self-awareness and moral discernment, in order to distinguish between right and wrong and to choose the path of righteousness.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things that, if they are shown to you, will bring you distress. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. God has pardoned you, and God is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers and advises them not to ask about certain things that, if revealed, would cause them distress. The verse implies that such questions may be a sign of weakness in faith or lack of trust in God's plan. Instead, the believers are encouraged to focus on the revelations given in the Qur'an, which will provide clarity and guidance. The verse also emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, reminding believers that He is ever-forgiving and patient.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: And God has not created the heavens and the earth and everything between them except with truth, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God's creation is based on truth and justice, and that the heavens and the earth and everything in between were created with a purpose. The verse also highlights the ignorance of most people who deny or reject this truth and instead choose to believe in falsehood. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's power and wisdom in creation, and the consequences of rejecting this truth.
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' they said, 'Enough for us is what we found our fathers upon.' Their fathers were not knowledgeable nor were they guided.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of some people when they were invited to follow the teachings of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They refused, saying that they were content with the beliefs and practices of their ancestors. The verse highlights the ignorance and misguidance of these people, who were unwilling to listen to the message of Islam and instead chose to follow the traditions of their ancestors, even though they were not based on knowledge or guidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who blindly follow their ancestors' beliefs and practices without questioning or seeking guidance from God's revelation.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول قالوا حسبنا ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعلمون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from the Fire, whose fuel is men and stones, over which are angels, stern and powerful, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting oneself and one's family from the Fire of Hell, which is fueled by men and stones. The verse also highlights the role of angels as guardians over the Fire, who are obedient to God's commands and carry out His will. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a righteous life and avoid actions that may lead them to Hell.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, testify between yourselves when death approaches one of you at the time of bequeathing, two just men from among you, or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death overtakes you, you should detain them after the prayer. Then if you are in doubt, they should swear by Allah, 'Indeed, we will not exchange our testimony for a price, even if it should be a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah, for then we would be among the sinful.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of truthful testimony, especially in matters related to inheritance and death. It encourages believers to be honest and impartial in their testimonies, even if it means going against their personal interests or those of their relatives. The verse also highlights the gravity of concealing or distorting the truth, likening it to a sinful act. The use of the phrase 'we will not exchange our testimony for a price' underscores the importance of integrity and the value of truth in Islam. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to always act with honesty and integrity, even in the most difficult of circumstances.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا شهادة بينكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين الوصية اثنان ذوا عدل منكم أو آخران من غيركم إن أنتم ضربتم في الأرض فأصابتكم مصيبة الموت تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله إن ارتبتم لا نشتري به ثمنا ولو كان ذا قربى ولا نكتم شهادة الله إنا إذا لمن الآثمين

translation: So, indeed, We have punished them. And they have received their punishment in the morning and at noon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the punishment of God is certain and will come suddenly, without warning, just as it did for the towns that were destroyed in the past. The verse also highlights the idea that the punishment will be severe and will not be limited to a specific time of day, indicating that the people will be punished at all times, whether in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فإن عثر على أنهما استحقا إثما فآخران يقومان مقامهما من الذين استحق عليهم الأوليان فيقسمان بالله لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما وما اعتدينا إنا إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة على وجهها أو يخافوا أن ترد أيمان بعد أيمانهم واتقوا الله واسمعوا والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say, 'What was your response to the people?' They will say, 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment when Allah will gather all the Messengers and ask them about their response to the people they were sent to guide. The Messengers will reply that they have no knowledge of the unseen, and that only Allah has knowledge of the unseen. The verse highlights the limitation of the Messengers' knowledge and the vastness of Allah's knowledge, emphasizing that only Allah has the ability to know and see all things. The verse also serves as a reminder that the Messengers were not all-knowing and that their role was to convey the message of Allah, not to have knowledge of the unseen.
orig: يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: And remember when Allah said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in old age, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel, and when you created from clay the form of a bird with My permission, and you breathed into it and it became a bird with My permission, and when you healed those born blind and the lepers with My permission, and when you brought forth the dead with My permission, and when I protected you from the children of Israel when they came to you with clear signs and said, 'This is nothing but evident magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the various miracles and blessings that Jesus, son of Mary, received from Allah. The verse emphasizes how Jesus was supported by the Holy Spirit and was able to speak in the cradle and in old age, indicating his prophethood and divine connection. Additionally, Jesus was taught the Book, wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel, signifying his knowledge and understanding of the divine scriptures. The verse also mentions Jesus' ability to create a bird from clay and bring forth the dead, both of which are considered great miracles. The verse concludes by mentioning how Jesus was protected from the children of Israel, indicating that he was divinely protected and his message was not a form of magic or sorcery, as some people claimed.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم اذكر نعمتي عليك وعلى والدتك إذ أيدتك بروح القدس تكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا وإذ علمتك الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل وإذ تخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير بإذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني وتبرئ الأكمه والأبرص بإذني وإذ تخرج الموتى بإذني وإذ كففت بني إسرائيل عنك إذ جئتهم بالبينات فقال الذين كفروا منهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And when I (the Prophet Muhammad) told the disciples (of Jesus) to believe in me and my messengers, they said, 'We believe and bear witness that we are submitters (to God).'
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity of faith between the Prophet Muhammad and the disciples of Jesus, peace be upon them. It emphasizes the belief in the Oneness of God and the acceptance of the Prophets as messengers of God. The use of the word 'submitters' (Muslimoon) in the verse emphasizes the idea of submission to God's will and the recognition of God's authority over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of the commonalities between Islam and Christianity, and the importance of respecting and honoring all prophets and messengers of God.
orig: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين أن آمنوا بي وبرسولي قالوا آمنا واشهد بأننا مسلمون

translation: And when the disciples said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from the sky?', Jesus said, 'Fear God, if you are believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between Jesus and his disciples, where they ask him if God can send down a table from the sky. Jesus responds by telling them to fear God, implying that they should have faith and trust in God's power and provision. The verse highlights the importance of faith and obedience to God, and serves as a reminder that God is capable of providing for his followers in miraculous ways.
orig: إذ قال الحواريون يا عيسى ابن مريم هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء قال اتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'We want to eat from it and feel reassured by it and understand that you have spoken the truth to us and that we may be witnesses to it.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to taste the fruit of the tree. They wanted to eat from it to satisfy their hunger and also to be reassured that the fruit was indeed edible. They also wanted to understand that the speaker was telling the truth and that they would be witnesses to it. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the people and their reluctance to accept the truth without concrete evidence. It also underscores the importance of witnessing and testimony in Islam, as the people wanted to be witnesses to the truth of the speaker's statement.
orig: قالوا نريد أن نأكل منها وتطمئن قلوبنا ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا ونكون عليها من الشاهدين

translation: And Jesus, son of Mary, said: 'O God, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from heaven, that it may be a feast for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus, son of Mary, is praying to God, asking for a miraculous provision of food from heaven. The verse emphasizes the idea of unity among believers, referring to them as 'the first of us and the last of us', indicating that the provision is not only for the present generation but also for future generations. The verse also highlights the idea of God's provision and His role as the ultimate provider. The phrase 'and a sign from You' suggests that the provision is not only a means of sustenance but also a miraculous sign from God, a manifestation of His power and grace. The verse serves as a reminder of God's ability to provide for His servants and the importance of faith and trust in Him.
orig: قال عيسى ابن مريم اللهم ربنا أنزل علينا مائدة من السماء تكون لنا عيدا لأولنا وآخرنا وآية منك وارزقنا وأنت خير الرازقين

translation: And indeed, We have sent it (the Qur'an) down to you (O Muhammad SAW) in truth, and surely, Allah will guide not the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which is a revelation from God to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse warns those who deny or disobey the message of the Qur'an, stating that God will not guide such individuals, and they will face severe consequences for their disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human beings and the importance of following God's guidance as revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: قال الله إني منزلها عليكم فمن يكفر بعد منكم فإني أعذبه عذابا لا أعذبه أحدا من العالمين

translation: And remember when Allah said: 'O Jesus, son of Mary! Did you say to the people: "Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?"' He said: 'Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in myself, but I do not know what is in Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: In this verse, Allah is addressing Prophet Jesus, asking him if he had told the people to take him and his mother as deities besides Allah. Jesus responds by saying that he did not say such a thing, and that if he had, Allah would have known it. He also acknowledges that Allah is the Knower of the unseen, indicating that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse highlights the importance of not ascribing partners to Allah and emphasizes the oneness of God. It also underscores the idea that Prophets are human beings who have limitations in their knowledge and are not all-knowing like God.
orig: وإذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: I have only obeyed the commands of my Lord and your Lord, and I have been a witness over them as long as I lived among them. And when You took me, You were the Watcher over them, and You are a witness over all things.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the prophet's role as a witness over his people and his obedience to God's commands. The use of 'my Lord and your Lord' emphasizes the unity of God and the prophet's submission to Him. The verse also highlights the prophet's responsibility to watch over his people and guide them towards righteousness. The phrase 'You were the Watcher over them' suggests that God was watching over the people even after the prophet's death, indicating that God's watchfulness and care for His creation is eternal. The final phrase, 'and You are a witness over all things', reinforces the idea that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that everything is under His witness and care.
orig: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم وأنت على كل شيء شهيد

translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You, only You, are the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between God and His servants. It emphasizes that God has the power to punish or forgive, and that His servants are entirely dependent on His mercy and grace. The verse also underscores God's wisdom and might in His dealings with humanity. The phrase 'If You punish them' suggests that God's punishment is a form of correction and guidance, rather than a form of revenge or retribution. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their relationship with God is one of servitude and dependence, and that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال الله هذا يوم ينفع الصادقين صدقهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is within them, and He is capable of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over the entire universe, including all that is within it. The verse underscores Allah's power and control over all things, indicating that He is the sole authority and source of strength. It serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's greatness and their own dependence on Him, encouraging them to submit to His will and seek His guidance in all aspects of their lives.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the One who made the darkness and the light. Yet those who disbelieve in their Lord deny (the truth).
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for His creation of the universe and the contrast between light and darkness. The verse also highlights the disbelief of those who reject their Lord and refuse to acknowledge the truth.
orig: الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

translation: It is He who created you from clay, then decreed a stated term, and a specified term is with Him, yet you doubt.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority as the creator of humanity, highlighting the fact that He is the one who has brought us into existence from clay. The verse also mentions the limited nature of human existence, as our lives are bound by a 'stated term' and a 'specified term' that is determined by God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in God's plan and not to doubt His wisdom or question His decisions.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من طين ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ثم أنتم تمترون

translation: And Allah is in the heavens and on the earth, He knows your secret and your open (deeds), and He knows what you earn (good or bad).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all things, both in the heavens and on earth. He is aware of the hidden and the manifest, the good and the bad deeds of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of human actions and thoughts, and that ultimately, everyone will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم وجهركم ويعلم ما تكسبون

translation: And how many a sign has come to them from their Lord, but they have been resistant to it.
interpretation: The verse refers to the numerous signs and miracles that God has sent to the disbelievers, yet they have chosen to reject and resist them. The verse suggests that the disbelievers have been obstinate and unwilling to accept the truth, despite the overwhelming evidence and signs that have been presented to them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are stubborn and resistant to the message of God, reminding them that their denial will not change the reality of the truth and the inevitability of God's judgment.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And they have denied the truth when it came to them, so they will have news of what they used to mock.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and denied the truth that was presented to them. The verse indicates that they will be surprised and regretful on the Day of Judgment when they see the reality of what they had mocked and ridiculed. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and instead choose to follow their own desires and false beliefs, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of accepting the truth.
orig: فقد كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how We destroyed the former generations who were before them, as We had made them inhabit the earth, and We sent the sky pouring down upon them? Yet We destroyed them for their sins and created after them other generations.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetitive nature of human history, where each generation is tested with prosperity and adversity, and those who reject God's signs and continue in sin are eventually destroyed, making way for a new generation. The verse serves as a reminder to the current generation that they too will face the consequences of their actions and that they should learn from the past and turn to God.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا وجعلنا الأنهار تجري من تحتهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And if We had sent down to thee a book on parchment, and they had touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said, 'This is naught but manifest magic.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' skepticism and doubt in the authenticity of the Qur'an. The verse suggests that even if a book had been sent down on parchment, the disbelievers would have still rejected it, claiming it was nothing but magic. The verse highlights the theme of revelation and the disbelievers' refusal to accept it, emphasizing that their disbelief stems from their unwillingness to submit to God's authority.
orig: ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم لقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And they say, 'If only a king would come to us, we would follow him.' But if We had sent a king, they would have been oppressed, and they would not have been patient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's desire for a king to lead them, but they are warned that if a king were sent, they would be oppressed and would not be patient. The verse highlights the people's lack of faith and their unwillingness to submit to God's will. It emphasizes that true guidance and leadership come from God, and that human leaders are not capable of providing the guidance that people seek. The verse serves as a reminder to trust in God's plan and to seek guidance from Him alone.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك ولو أنزلنا ملكا لقضي الأمر ثم لا ينظرون

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have made them (the disbelievers) follow him (as a Prophet).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' refusal to follow the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their demand for a sign or a miracle. God responds by saying that even if He had made the Prophet an angel, the disbelievers would still have found a reason to reject him. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of the disbelievers, who refused to accept the truth and instead demanded a sign that they could understand and believe in. The verse also emphasizes the Prophet's humanity and the fact that he is a messenger of God, sent to guide people to the right path.
orig: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you [O Muhammad] from your Lord a clear sign. For We have sent death among them, and they have been returned to their Lord in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous sign sent by God to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a proof of his prophethood. The sign is described as 'clear' and 'manifest', indicating its clarity and obviousness. The verse also mentions the fate of those who rejected the sign and refused to believe in the Prophet, stating that they were destroyed by death, which was sent among them suddenly and unexpectedly, either in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Tell them to travel through the earth and see how the punishment of the disbelievers was!
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the disbelievers to travel through the earth and see the consequences of the disbelievers who were punished before them. The verse is emphasizing the importance of learning from history and the consequences of rejecting God's message. The verse also serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that they will face the same fate as those who rejected God's message in the past, if they continue to reject it.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "What thing is greatest in weight in the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah knows that and I know not." Indeed, they will be brought to account for their sins on the Day of Resurrection. They will not [then] believe in falsehood, but the disbelievers will say, "Our Lord, these are they who led us astray. Now we have no intercessors, nor do they have any proof."
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's power and knowledge, as well as the accountability of individuals for their actions in this life. The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to ask what is the greatest thing in weight in the heavens and the earth, and the answer is that Allah knows, signifying His infinite knowledge. The verse warns of the consequences of disbelief and the certainty of judgment on the Day of Resurrection, where the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions and will not be able to blame others for their misguidance.
orig: قل لمن ما في السماوات والأرض قل لله كتب على نفسه الرحمة ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم

translation: Say, O Allah, owner of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and take it away from whom You will. You exalt whom You will and humiliate whom You will. Say, Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit. And not to be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to God, the owner of the kingdom, acknowledging His power and authority over all things. The speaker is asking God to grant them the ability to be the first of those who submit to His will and not to be among those who associate others with Allah. The verse emphasizes the idea that God has the power to give and take away kingdoms and to exalt or humiliate whom He wills. The speaker is seeking guidance and submission to God's will, recognizing that only He has the power to grant such guidance and protection.
orig: قل أغير الله أتخذ وليا فاطر السماوات والأرض وهو يطعم ولا يطعم قل إني أمرت أن أكون أول من أسلم ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear that a punishment from my Lord will come upon you, a Day of Judgment, if I disobey Him.'
interpretation: The verse is a warning from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to his people, expressing his fear of God's punishment on the Day of Judgment if they continue to disobey Him. The verse emphasizes the personal responsibility of the Prophet and his accountability to God for conveying the message of Islam. It also underscores the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a righteous life and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: And whoever is granted wisdom has been granted a great good. Indeed, he will have succeeded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of wisdom and its significance as a blessing from God. The phrase 'granted wisdom' implies that wisdom is a divine gift, bestowed upon those who are worthy and deserving. The second part of the verse, 'Indeed, he will have succeeded', highlights the idea that wisdom leads to success in both this life and the hereafter. It suggests that the individual who possesses wisdom will be able to navigate life's challenges effectively and achieve ultimate success. The verse encourages readers to seek wisdom and to recognize its value as a vital component of a successful and fulfilling life.
orig: من يصرف عنه يومئذ فقد رحمه وذلك الفوز المبين

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God will support and aid those who support and aid His cause, indicating that those who strive for justice and righteousness will have God's backing and assistance. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might' underscores God's ability and authority to aid those who are on the side of justice and righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder that those who stand up for what is right and just will have God's support and protection, and that ultimately, justice will prevail.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God will support and aid those who support and aid His cause, indicating a direct correlation between human action and divine intervention. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might' serves to underscore God's authority and dominance, highlighting His ability to enforce His will and defend those who align themselves with His purposes.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: Say, 'What thing is greatest in testimony is that God is witness between me and you, and this Qur'an has been inspired to me that I may warn you thereby and whomsoever it reaches. Indeed, God is One, there is no deity except Him, and I am free from that which you associate [with Him].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a testimony from God, witnessed by both the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the recipients of the message. The verse also underscores the oneness of God and the Prophet's innocence from the idols and deities that people associate with God. The verse serves as a call to monotheism and a reminder of the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to guide them towards the right path.
orig: قل أي شيء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بيني وبينكم وأوحي إلي هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ أئنكم لتشهدون أن مع الله آلهة أخرى قل لا أشهد قل إنما هو إله واحد وإنني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Those who were given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own sons, yet they destroy their own souls, and they do not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who were given the Scripture, which refers to the Jews and Christians, who recognize the Qur'an as the word of God, yet they reject it and do not believe in it. The verse emphasizes that they are like a person who recognizes their own child, but still chooses to reject and disown them. The verse is a warning to those who reject the message of the Qur'an, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their rejection of the truth will not save them from God's punishment.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who forges a lie against Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of attributing lies to God or denying His signs and verses. The verse describes such actions as the ultimate injustice, indicating that those who engage in them will not prosper or succeed in the long run. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and false beliefs, reminding them that their actions will not go unpunished.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And on a Day when He will gather them all together, then He will say to those who associated others with Allah in worship: 'Where are My partners, those whom you claimed (as partners)?'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where God will gather all the people who associated others with Him in worship and ask them where their partners are. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who committed shirk (associating partners with God) will be questioned about their beliefs and will not have any excuse or justification for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in a state of shirk, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of being held accountable on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا أين شركاؤكم الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Then they were not able to obscure the fact that they had been polytheists, for they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where people are trying to deny their past beliefs and actions, specifically their polytheism. They are trying to cover up their past mistakes and pretend that they were not polytheists. The verse suggests that it is difficult to hide the truth and that people's actions and beliefs have consequences. It also highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and being honest about one's beliefs.
orig: ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

translation: And see how they lied against themselves, and that which they used to fabricate has been lost from them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of lying and fabricating, where the perpetrators ultimately suffer from their own deceit. The phrase 'against themselves' indicates that the lies they told had a detrimental impact on their own lives, causing them to lose what they had fabricated. This verse serves as a warning against dishonesty and encourages truthfulness, as it leads to loss and destruction.
orig: انظر كيف كذبوا على أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And indeed, there are those who listen to you and We have placed over their hearts coverings that they may not understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. Indeed, they have denied the truth before, while they are in disagreement.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who refuse to listen to the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and are unable to understand the truth due to the veil that God has placed over their hearts and ears. Despite witnessing many miraculous signs, they remain in disbelief and deny the truth. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who refuse to accept the message of Islam, and serves as a warning to those who are unwilling to listen to the truth.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها حتى إذا جاءوك يجادلونك يقول الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they (the disbelievers) schemed, and We (Allah) schemed, but they did not realize that God was plotting against them. Indeed, their plots were their own destruction, and they were encircled by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who plotted against the believers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). However, their plots were actually part of God's plan to destroy them. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers were unaware of God's plan and were deceived by their own arrogance and disbelief. The verse also highlights the irony that the very things they ridiculed, such as the Prophet's message and the belief in God, were the things that ultimately led to their downfall. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and plots.
orig: وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وإن يهلكون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And if they had seen thee, [O Muhammad], when they beheld the fire, they would have said: 'This is naught else than a spell of utter destruction.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where the disbelievers saw the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the fire that was revealed to him. They were so amazed and frightened by the sight that they thought it was a spell of utter destruction. The verse highlights the miraculous nature of the revelation and the awe-inspiring effect it had on those who witnessed it. It also underscores the idea that the Prophet's mission was not to perform magic or trickery, but to convey the message of God's oneness and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار فقالوا يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: And indeed, they were about to deceive thee from that which We have revealed to thee, [O Muhammad], so that you would invent something else against Us, and they would have accepted it from you gladly.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers were trying to deceive the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by asking him to invent a revelation that would contradict the Qur'an, which they would have gladly accepted. This verse highlights the cunning nature of the disbelievers and their desire to undermine the Prophet's message. It also underscores the importance of adhering to the truth and not compromising one's beliefs to appease others.
orig: بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they say, 'This is not but our life in this world. We live and die, and nothing but our deeds will be counted.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' misunderstanding of the purpose of life. They believe that life is limited to the physical world and that their actions have no consequences beyond death. They do not recognize the concept of accountability to God or the existence of an afterlife. The verse highlights the misguided nature of their beliefs and the importance of recognizing the true purpose of life, which is to worship God and live according to His commands.
orig: وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And if they had seen when they were told, 'Behold, your Lord is indeed Allah,' they would have said, 'Are we to abandon our gods and turn to Allah?',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' refusal to accept the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their reluctance to give up their false deities. The verse suggests that even when they were confronted with the truth of Allah's oneness, they were unwilling to surrender their false beliefs and turn to Allah. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers and serves as a warning to those who refuse to accept the message of Islam.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم قال أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: And indeed, those who have earned [their] punishment will be encircled by what they used to mock at.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have earned their punishment and will be surrounded by what they used to mock at. The verse suggests that the punishment will be fitting for their crimes, and they will be encircled by their own wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And the life of this world is not but play and amusement. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly life and its ultimate insignificance in the grand scheme of things. The phrase 'play and amusement' suggests that worldly pursuits are temporary and frivolous, and that true happiness and fulfillment can only be found in the spiritual realm. The second part of the verse highlights the contrast between the temporal nature of worldly life and the eternal nature of the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of living a virtuous life in order to attain a better reward in the hereafter.
orig: وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, but they did not believe in the signs of Allah, and they (the destroyers) were asking for the proof of what they had been warned against.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetitive nature of human history, wherein communities are destroyed by God's punishment due to their disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes that the people of these communities were warned through clear signs and proofs, but they refused to believe and were therefore destroyed. The verse serves as a warning to the current and future generations, reminding them of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding God's signs and warnings.
orig: قد نعلم إنه ليحزنك الذي يقولون فإنهم لا يكذبونك ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: And indeed, We have sent messengers before you, and We have destroyed them with [the punishment of] extinction. So are you afraid of being destroyed by the punishment of extinction?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has sent messengers before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and how they were rejected and ultimately destroyed by God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the certainty of His punishment. The use of the word 'extinction' emphasizes the complete and total nature of the destruction that awaits those who reject God's message.
orig: ولقد كذبت رسل من قبلك فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have sent down to you signs, evident and proofs, and We have surely sent apostles to warn and give good news. That He may bring you forth from darkness into the light, and indeed, He pardons you, and indeed, He is merciful to you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and guidance that God has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community. The 'clear victory' refers to the triumph of Islam over paganism and the establishment of a righteous society. The 'manifest triumph' signifies the evident and clear nature of the signs and proofs that God has sent down to guide humanity. The verse also emphasizes the role of the prophets and messengers in conveying God's message and warning people of the consequences of their actions. The ultimate goal of these efforts is to bring people out of darkness and into the light of faith and righteousness, and to receive God's pardon and mercy.
orig: وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى فلا تكونن من الجاهلين

translation: It is only the dead who are raised, and only the deaf who are gathered. And the blind are led, and those who are far astray are guided.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when the dead will be resurrected and the living will be gathered. The verse emphasizes that only the deaf and the blind will be gathered, indicating that those who are spiritually dead and unable to hear or see the truth will be raised and brought to judgment. The verse also mentions that those who are far astray will be guided, indicating that even those who have strayed far from God's path will be brought back and given the opportunity to repent and seek guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the coming judgment and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for that day.
orig: إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله ثم إليه يرجعون

translation: And they say, 'If only a sign could be sent down to him from his Lord!' But say, 'Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to prove his prophethood. The verse emphasizes that Allah is certainly capable of sending down a sign, but the majority of the disbelievers are unaware of the true nature of prophethood and the purpose of miracles. The verse highlights the irony that while the disbelievers demand a sign, they are ignorant of the fact that the Qur'an itself is a miracle and a sign of the Prophet's prophethood. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance and knowledge come from Allah, and that miracles are not the ultimate proof of prophethood, but rather a means to strengthen the faith of the believers.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And there is not a creature on earth or a bird that flies with its wings, except [that they are] communities like you [i.e., human beings]. We have not neglected anything in the Book, then to their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and interconnectedness of all living beings, pointing out that both animals and birds live in communities, just like humans. The verse also highlights the fact that everything in the universe has a purpose and a role to play, and that nothing has been neglected or overlooked by God. The verse serves as a reminder that humans are not superior to other creatures, but rather, they are all part of a larger ecosystem that is interconnected and interdependent. The verse also underscores the idea that everything in the universe will eventually return to God, highlighting the importance of living a virtuous life and being accountable for one's actions.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: And those who deny Our signs, they are the ones who are blind and deaf in the darkness of their ignorance. Whomever Allah wills to guide, He misguides him, and whomever He wills to misguide, He places him on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who reject God's signs and are therefore spiritually blind and deaf. They are unable to see or hear the truth and are lost in their own ignorance. The verse emphasizes God's power to guide or misguide whom He wills, and that those who are misguided by God are on a path that leads away from righteousness and towards destruction. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and a reminder of God's power and control over all things.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Tell me, if Allah's punishment came to you or the Hour has come upon you, would you still worship other than Allah?
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded to ask the polytheists a rhetorical question. The question is meant to make them reflect on their beliefs and actions. The verse suggests that even if Allah's punishment or the Hour (the Day of Judgment) were to come, the polytheists would still insist on worshiping other than Allah. The verse serves as a warning to those who are associating partners with Allah, reminding them that even in the face of certain punishment or judgment, they will not abandon their false deities. The verse highlights the futility of their beliefs and the certainty of Allah's judgment.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And indeed, We have sent to nations before you and afflicted them with hardship and calamity, that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the pattern of God's dealings with nations before the Prophet Muhammad's time. God sent prophets to them, but they refused to listen and continued to live in disobedience. As a result, God afflicted them with hardships and calamities, not to punish them, but to humble them and guide them towards repentance. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers that they too will face similar trials and tribulations, but they must remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God, and not succumb to the temptations of this world.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before this, they would have said: Our Lord, why did You destroy us before we had a chance to repent and correct our ways?
interpretation: This verse highlights the rebellious nature of the disbelievers. Despite the warning signs and messages from God, they refused to repent and continue to live in disobedience. The verse suggests that even if God were to destroy them, they would still try to justify their actions and blame God for their own downfall. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of humanity's own actions.
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: And We have destroyed many a generation after Noah, and sufficient is your Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse mentions the destruction of communities after Prophet Noah's time. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and wisdom in His decision to destroy these communities, implying that their destruction was not a random act but a deliberate and just punishment for their wrongdoing. The phrase 'sufficient is your Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise' underscores God's sovereignty and wisdom in His dealings with humanity, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah were to impose upon you the angel of death and take your souls, or if He were to punish you with a painful punishment, would you then be destroyed?'
interpretation: This verse is a call to reflection and introspection. The speaker is invited to consider the consequences of their actions and the potential punishment that could befall them if they continue to reject God's message. The verse emphasizes the power of God and the certainty of punishment for those who reject His message. The use of the angel of death and the mention of a painful punishment serve to emphasize the severity of the consequences. The verse serves as a reminder to reflect on one's actions and to turn to God before it's too late.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أخذ الله سمعكم وأبصاركم وختم على قلوبكم من إله غير الله يأتيكم به انظر كيف نصرف الآيات ثم هم يصدفون

translation: Tell me, O my dear people, have you seen the punishment of Allah coming to you suddenly while you are unaware?
interpretation: The verse is a warning from God to the Prophet's people, asking them to reflect on the sudden and unexpected nature of God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment will come suddenly, without warning, and that it will be a terrible and destructive force. The use of the word 'بغتة' (suddenly) and 'جهرة' (unaware) emphasizes the element of surprise and the idea that the people will be caught off guard. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to turn away from their sinful ways and to be mindful of God's justice and power.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله بغتة أو جهرة هل يهلك إلا القوم الظالمون

translation: And We have not sent the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the prophets and messengers sent by God. They are tasked with delivering good news to the believers and warning the disobedient of the consequences of their actions. The verse alleviates any fear or sadness that the believers may have, as they are reminded that the messengers are there to guide and support them. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject the message, as they will face the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين فمن آمن وأصلح فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will seize them for their lies.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of denying God's signs and revelations. The phrase 'yalmaseehim' (their lies) refers to the fact that they denied the truth and rejected God's signs, leading them to a path of destruction. The word 'fasesq' (seize) implies a sudden and intense punishment that will overcome those who rejected God's signs. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا يمسهم العذاب بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah or that I have knowledge of the unseen, nor do I say to you that I am an angel. Indeed, I only follow what is revealed to me.' Say, 'Are the blind and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to tell the people that he does not possess the treasures of God, nor does he have knowledge of the unseen. He is only a messenger who follows what is revealed to him by God. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the difference between the blind and the seeing, indicating that those who are spiritually blind cannot equal those who have been given the gift of sight by God. The verse encourages the people to reflect on their own spiritual state and to recognize the greatness of God's power and knowledge.
orig: قل لا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول لكم إني ملك إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أفلا تتفكرون

translation: And warn those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, they have none besides Him as a guardian or intercessor, and that they may fear the punishment of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of warning those who fear God and reminding them of the consequences of their actions. The verse suggests that those who fear God should be aware that they will be gathered to their Lord and that they have no one else to rely on or intercede on their behalf. The verse serves as a reminder to those who fear God to live a righteous life and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for their deeds on Judgment Day.
orig: وأنذر به الذين يخافون أن يحشروا إلى ربهم ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع لعلهم يتقون

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face. You are not accountable for their account, nor are they accountable for your account. And if you drive them away, you will be one of the unjust.
interpretation: The verse prohibits driving away those who pray to their Lord, seeking His guidance and forgiveness. The verse emphasizes that one is not responsible for others' spiritual state, and that driving them away will only make one an oppressor. It highlights the importance of tolerance and acceptance of others' beliefs and practices, and serves as a reminder that everyone is accountable to God, and that we should not judge or condemn others for their beliefs.
orig: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين

translation: And thus We have tried some of them through others, that they might say: 'Are these the ones whom God has favored?' Does not God know best the thankful ones?
