interpretation: The verse speaks about the jealousy and envy that arises in the hearts of those who reject the message of God's prophets. The verse suggests that God allows some people to be tested through others, so that they might realize the true nature of their own hearts and the depth of their ingratitude. The verse questions whether those who reject the message are truly grateful to God, or if they are merely pretending to be so. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of the thankful ones and that He will reward them accordingly.
orig: وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض ليقولوا أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you. Your Lord has written upon Himself mercy, that whoever of you does evil in ignorance, then turns after that and makes correction, then indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the encounter between the believers and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). When the believers come to the Prophet, they are greeted with the words of peace. The verse then emphasizes the quality of mercy that is inherent in God's nature, indicating that even if a person has committed evil deeds in ignorance, they can still turn back to God and seek forgiveness. The verse highlights God's forgiving and merciful nature, encouraging believers to seek redemption and guidance from Him.
orig: وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة أنه من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فأنه غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, We have divided the verses and made them clear in several ways, that the criminals may be distinguished.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the Qur'anic verses, which are designed to guide and distinguish the righteous from the wicked. The use of the word 'criminals' (مجرمين) specifically highlights the idea that the Qur'an is a guide for those who seek to live a virtuous life, and a warning for those who choose to engage in evil deeds.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been forbidden from worshipping those who you call upon besides Allah . Say, 'I do not follow your desires, for I would have gone astray if I had not been guided by Allah .
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism. The speaker is commanded to declare that they do not worship any deity other than Allah, and that they do not follow the desires of those who worship others besides Allah. The verse highlights the idea that following one's desires and the desires of others can lead to misguidance and astrayness, while only Allah's guidance can bring about true guidance and righteousness.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله قل لا أتبع أهواءكم قد ضللت إذا وما أنا من المهتدين

translation: Say, indeed I am on clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it. What you are hastening towards is not except that Allah's judgment has come, and His command is not except for the truth.
interpretation: The verse is a statement made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in response to the disbelievers' denial of his message. The verse asserts that the Prophet has been given clear evidence and signs from God to support his message, but the disbelievers have rejected it. The verse warns that the disbelievers' rejection of the truth will not stop God's judgment from coming, and that His command is always for the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's message is not just a human opinion, but it is backed by divine authority and will ultimately be fulfilled.
orig: قل إني على بينة من ربي وكذبتم به ما عندي ما تستعجلون به إن الحكم إلا لله يقص الحق وهو خير الفاصلين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I fear that you will be punished with a punishment from God and that you will be destroyed, just like the nations that were destroyed before you.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to warn the disbelievers of the punishment that awaits them if they continue to reject God's message. The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's punishment and the destruction that will befall those who disobey Him. The Prophet is told to say that he fears for the disbelievers' fate, as they will be punished just like the nations that were destroyed before them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to turn to God before it's too late.
orig: قل لو أن عندي ما تستعجلون به لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم والله أعلم بالظالمين

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is in the land and the sea, and not a leaf falls except that He knows it, and not a grain in the darkness of the earth, and not a thing wet or dry but is in a clear book.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and control over all aspects of creation. The phrase 'keys of the unseen' refers to God's knowledge of all things hidden from human comprehension. The verse then lists various examples of God's knowledge and power, including His knowledge of every leaf that falls and every grain in the earth, indicating His awareness of even the smallest details. The phrase 'clear book' suggests that all of creation is recorded in a book that is clear and accessible to God, signifying His complete knowledge and control over all things.
orig: وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو ويعلم ما في البر والبحر وما تسقط من ورقة إلا يعلمها ولا حبة في ظلمات الأرض ولا رطب ولا يابس إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees what you do, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His knowledge of all human actions. It reminds believers that God is always with them, watching and witnessing their deeds, and that He will hold them accountable for their actions on Judgment Day. The verse also serves as a warning to those who may be engaged in sinful behavior, reminding them that God sees everything they do and will bring it to light on the Day of Reckoning.
orig: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل ويعلم ما جرحتم بالنهار ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضى أجل مسمى ثم إليه مرجعكم ثم ينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and He sees everything you do, and He will reward you for your deeds, and no soul will be given except what it can bear, and Our messengers come to you to take your souls, and they will not be neglected.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over all things, including the actions and deeds of human beings. God is always present and aware of everything that is happening, and He will reward each person according to their deeds. The verse also highlights the idea that no soul will be given more than it can bear, indicating that God's justice is perfect and that each person will be held accountable for their actions. The final part of the verse mentions the role of God's messengers, who will come to take the souls of the deceased and will not neglect them, indicating that the process of death and judgment is a part of God's plan and should be accepted with faith and submission.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده ويرسل عليكم حفظة حتى إذا جاء أحدكم الموت توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون

translation: Then they returned to Allah, their Lord, humbled, and [they] did not perpetuate [their anger], for they had already been given a clear conquest.
interpretation: In this verse, the people who were previously described as 'unjust' and faced destruction, have now turned back to God and submitted to Him, acknowledging His power and authority. The phrase 'they did not perpetuate [their anger]' suggests that they have let go of their anger and resentment, and have chosen to submit to God's will. The phrase 'for they had already been given a clear conquest' indicates that they have been given a clear victory, which serves as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, God's help is always near and available to those who turn to Him in sincerity.
orig: ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق ألا له الحكم وهو أسرع الحاسبين

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from the darkness of the land and the sea? You call upon Him humbly and secretly, saying, 'If we are saved from this, we will be of the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of human beings in the face of natural disasters and the importance of seeking God's protection and guidance. The verse describes a situation where people are faced with the threat of darkness, both on land and at sea, and they have no one to turn to but God. They call upon Him in a state of humility and secrecy, acknowledging their dependence on Him and expressing their gratitude for any deliverance they may receive. The verse serves as a reminder of the fragility of human life and the need for faith in God, who is the only one capable of protecting and guiding us through life's challenges.
orig: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية لئن أنجانا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: Say, 'God will bring you out of it and [then] you will be returned to it, and you will be brought out of it again.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers' ultimate victory over their enemies, as God will bring them out of their difficulties and return them to a state of prosperity. The verse also serves as a reminder that the believers will face trials and tribulations, but they will ultimately be victorious and return to a state of grace. The verse emphasizes the power and control of God, who has the ability to bring people out of difficult situations and restore them to a state of prosperity.
orig: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب ثم أنتم تشركون

translation: Say, 'He is the One Who is able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confound you with dissension and make you taste the violence of one another.' Behold, how variously We explain the signs that they may understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power to punish those who reject His signs and continue to live in disobedience. The verse mentions three possible ways in which God's punishment could come: from above, from beneath their feet, or through internal strife and violence among themselves. The verse also highlights the diversity of God's signs and the various ways in which they are presented to humanity, with the intention of guiding them towards understanding and repentance.
orig: قل هو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذابا من فوقكم أو من تحت أرجلكم أو يلبسكم شيعا ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض انظر كيف نصرف الآيات لعلهم يفقهون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكذب به قومك وهو الحق قل لست عليكم بوكيل

translation: For every nation there is a messenger. When their messenger comes, they will be judged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of every nation for their actions. Each nation has been sent a messenger by God, who has guided them towards righteousness and warned them of the consequences of their wrongdoing. On the Day of Judgment, each nation will be judged based on their response to their messenger and the message they brought. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding the message of the messenger and living a life in accordance with God's will.
orig: لكل نبإ مستقر وسوف تعلمون

translation: And when I saw those who were neglecting Our verses, I turned away from them, that they may engage in discussion other than this. And indeed, the devil is a forgetfulness to the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) reaction to seeing people neglecting the verses of God. He turned away from them, indicating his disassociation with their actions and his disappointment in their neglect of God's message. The verse also highlights the devil's role in distracting people from remembering God and leading them astray. The phrase 'and indeed, the devil is a forgetfulness to the ignorant' suggests that the devil's influence over people is a form of forgetfulness, causing them to forget the remembrance of God and leading them towards ignorance.
orig: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين

translation: And nothing is on those who are taken to task for their error, except their recompense, but a reminder to those who fear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who are taken to task for their error will only receive their recompense, implying that they will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions. The verse also serves as a reminder to those who fear God, reminding them of the importance of living a righteous life and avoiding sin, lest they too face the same fate as those who are being punished.
orig: وما على الذين يتقون من حسابهم من شيء ولكن ذكرى لعلهم يتقون

translation: And those who took their religion as an amusement and a diversion, and the life of this world deceived them, so today We will forget them as they forgot their meeting of this Day, and as they used to deny Our verses. And We have brought them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who took their religion lightly and were distracted by the pleasures of this world. They forgot about the meeting with God on the Day of Judgment and denied the verses of the Qur'an. In response, God will forget them on that Day and they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse also mentions the revelation of the Qur'an, which is a guidance and mercy for those who believe.
orig: وذر الذين اتخذوا دينهم لعبا ولهوا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وذكر به أن تبسل نفس بما كسبت ليس لها من دون الله ولي ولا شفيع وإن تعدل كل عدل لا يؤخذ منها أولئك الذين أبسلوا بما كسبوا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: Say, 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Verily, he has no power over those who believe and rely on their Lord. His power is only over those who obey him and follow him. And when they commit an evil deed, they will have brought upon themselves their own destruction and that of their brethren. But those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, therein to abide forever. Verily, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in Allah from the evil whispers of Satan, who has no power over those who believe and rely on their Lord. It also warns those who obey and follow Satan that they will bring destruction upon themselves and their brethren. On the other hand, those who believe and do righteous deeds will be rewarded with gardens in Paradise, where they will abide forever. The verse underscores the power of Allah and His ability to do as He wills.
orig: قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا ونرد على أعقابنا بعد إذ هدانا الله كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران له أصحاب يدعونه إلى الهدى ائتنا قل إن هدى الله هو الهدى وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين

translation: And establish prayer and fear Me, and to Me is the destination.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer and fearing God. The phrase 'wa-taqwa' (and fear Me) is a command to have a deep sense of reverence and awe of God, and to live a life that is pleasing to Him. The verse also emphasizes the ultimate destination of all creation, which is to return to God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay focused on their spiritual journey and their ultimate goal of meeting God, and to live their lives in accordance with His will.
orig: وأن أقيموا الصلاة واتقوه وهو الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: And He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth with truth, and on the Day of Resurrection, He will say, 'Be, and it will be.' And His word is the truth, and to Him belongs the dominion of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes God's power and authority over the universe and emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Resurrection. The phrase 'And He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth with truth' underscores the idea that God's creation is based on justice and truth. The verse also highlights God's ability to bring things into existence with a mere command, as expressed in the phrase 'and on the Day of Resurrection, He will say, 'Be, and it will be.' The phrase 'And His word is the truth' emphasizes the authority and reliability of God's word. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom as expressed in the phrase 'and to Him belongs the dominion of the unseen and the witnessed.' Finally, the verse ends by emphasizing God's wisdom and knowledge as expressed in the phrase 'and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.'
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق ويوم يقول كن فيكون قوله الحق وله الملك يوم ينفخ في الصور عالم الغيب والشهادة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is addressing his father Azar and pointing out that the idols he worship are not truly deities. Abraham recognizes that his father and his people are misguided and lost in their beliefs. He is emphasizing the idea that idol worship is a form of ignorance and that it is not a valid way to connect with the divine. This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and rejecting false beliefs and seeking guidance from the one true God.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه آزر أتتخذ أصناما آلهة إني أراك وقومك في ضلال مبين

translation: And indeed, We have given Ibrahim (Abraham) the kingship of the heavens and the earth, and he was among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the status and honor bestowed upon Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) by God. He was chosen by God to be the leader of the heavens and the earth, and he lived a righteous life, setting an example for future generations. The verse emphasizes the significance of Ibrahim's role as a prophet and leader, and serves as a reminder of the rewards that come with living a virtuous life.
orig: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين

orig: فلما رأى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لأكونن من القوم الضالين

translation: And when the sun covered the sun, he said, 'This is my Lord; this is the greatest.' But when it set, he said, 'O my people, I am free from what you associate with Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who initially believed that the sun was his lord, but when it set, he realized that it was not worthy of worship and denied any association with it. The verse highlights the mistake of attributing divinity to anything other than Allah, and serves as a warning against polytheism and the dangers of giving up one's faith in Allah.
orig: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي هذا أكبر فلما أفلت قال يا قوم إني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who has created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward Him, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: The verse expresses the Prophet Abraham's declaration of faith, in which he affirms his belief in the Oneness of God and his rejection of polytheism. The phrase 'I have turned my face' signifies a spiritual turning towards God, indicating a deep devotion and commitment to Him. The phrase 'inclining toward Him' suggests a continuous effort to draw closer to God and to live according to His will. The final phrase, 'and I am not of those who associate others with Allah', serves as a rejection of idolatry and a declaration of monotheism, emphasizing the belief that God is unique and indivisible.
orig: إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض حنيفا وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And they say, 'We will not believe you until you bring us a sign from God.' But has not a clear sign come to them with the knowledge of the Scripture? And We have not destroyed any town except while its people were unjust.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a condition for their belief. The verse points out that the Qur'an itself is a clear sign from God, containing guidance and wisdom. The verse also warns the disbelievers that they will not be spared from God's punishment, just like the towns that were destroyed in the past because of their injustice and disobedience. The verse emphasizes that God's knowledge encompasses everything, and nothing can escape His knowledge and wrath.
orig: وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا وسع ربي كل شيء علما أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكيف أخاف ما أشركتم ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله ما لم ينزل به عليكم سلطانا فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And those who believed and did not taint their faith with injustice, those will have security and they are guided.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of faith that is free from injustice. It emphasizes that true believers are those who do not let their faith be corrupted by injustice, and that they will be rewarded with security and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and ensure that their faith is not tainted by injustice, so that they may receive God's guidance and protection.
orig: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم أولئك لهم الأمن وهم مهتدون

translation: And We gave Abraham his argument (against his people) and raised him in degrees. Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Abraham and how God gave him the ability to argue effectively against his people. The verse also mentions how God raised Abraham's status, indicating that he was elevated to a position of leadership and respect. The verse emphasizes God's wisdom and knowledge, suggesting that He is all-knowing and all-wise in His decisions and actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of using reason and argumentation to spread God's message and to stand up for what is right.
orig: وتلك حجتنا آتيناها إبراهيم على قومه نرفع درجات من نشاء إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as a mercy, and We made them leaders, guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them, 'Follow the religion of Abraham, the upright one.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the prophets Isaac and Jacob, whom God had chosen as leaders and guided by His command. The verse highlights God's mercy in choosing them and their role in guiding people towards righteousness. The phrase 'Follow the religion of Abraham, the upright one' emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of Abraham, who is considered an exemplary model of faith and righteousness in Islam. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to adhere to the teachings of the prophets and to follow their footsteps in living a virtuous life.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل ومن ذريته داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And Zakariya and John and Elias and all the righteous, each one of them was of the elect.
interpretation: This verse mentions four prophets, Zakariya, John, Elias, and Isa (Jesus), and describes them as being among the righteous and chosen by God. The verse emphasizes their special status and highlights their role as messengers of God, sent to guide humanity towards righteousness and the straight path. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following in their footsteps and striving to live a virtuous life, as well as the promise of God's favor and blessings for those who do so.
orig: وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى وإلياس كل من الصالحين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form indicates that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to guide people towards the right path and to bring them closer to God. It also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and mercy for all people, and serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with being a member of the Muslim community.
orig: وإسماعيل واليسع ويونس ولوطا وكلا فضلنا على العالمين

translation: And We have destroyed many generations before them, and We have established them in their place, and We have sent them the Warner.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of previous generations and the sending of prophets to warn the people of their impending doom. The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over all things, and serves as a reminder to the reader of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: ومن آبائهم وذرياتهم وإخوانهم واجتبيناهم وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And that is the guidance of Allah, He guides thereby whom He wills of His servants, and if they had been associated with others, surely they would have been spoiled, and they would have been, in that case, in a state of confusion and doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the uniqueness of God's guidance and how it sets apart those who follow it from those who do not. The verse implies that those who follow God's guidance are protected from being misguided by other sources, and that they are able to avoid the confusion and doubt that comes with following multiple sources. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God's guidance is a blessing and a sign of His favor upon His servants, and that it is only by His will that they are guided.
orig: ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء من عباده ولو أشركوا لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have given them the Scripture and wisdom and the Prophethood, but if they deny them, then We have destroyed the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon the Children of Israel, who were given the Scripture (the Torah), wisdom, and the Prophethood. However, if they reject these blessings and instead choose to live in disobedience, then they will face destruction. The verse serves as a reminder that the blessings of God are not to be taken for granted and that disobedience will have consequences. The use of the word 'wrongdoers' emphasizes that their destruction is a result of their own actions, rather than God's cruelty.
orig: أولئك الذين آتيناهم الكتاب والحكم والنبوة فإن يكفر بها هؤلاء فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

translation: And those who have been guided by Allah, He will increase them in guidance. And none can guide whom Allah leaves astray. Is not He the One Who is Aware of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them? Indeed, they will be returned to Him for account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that those who have been guided by Allah will continue to receive increased guidance, while those who are misguided will remain so, as Allah is the only one who can guide them. The verse also emphasizes Allah's omniscience and power, as He is aware of all things in the heavens and the earth, and everything will ultimately return to Him for judgment. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in Allah's guidance, while also serving as a warning to those who reject faith, reminding them of their eventual return to Allah and the consequences of their actions.
orig: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن هو إلا ذكرى للعالمين

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with the true appraisal when they said: 'Allah has not sent down anything to any human being.' Say: 'Who then sent down the Book that Moses brought, a light and guidance for the people? You made it into pages, disclosing them and hiding much. You were taught things you did not know, neither you nor your fathers.' Then leave them in their forgetfulness, playing.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who denied the revelation of the Qur'an, claiming that God had not sent anything to any human being. The verse responds by pointing out their ignorance and lack of knowledge, highlighting the fact that they were not aware of the true nature of the Book that Moses brought, which was a light and guidance for the people. The verse suggests that they had distorted and hidden parts of the Book, revealing only what they wanted to reveal, and keeping the rest hidden. The verse concludes by telling the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to leave them in their state of forgetfulness and playfulness, indicating that they were not willing to listen to the truth and were instead, caught up in their own delusions and games.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شيء قل من أنزل الكتاب الذي جاء به موسى نورا وهدى للناس تجعلونه قراطيس تبدونها وتخفون كثيرا وعلمتم ما لم تعلموا أنتم ولا آباؤكم قل الله ثم ذرهم في خوضهم يلعبون

translation: And this Qur'an is a blessed Book which We have sent down, blessed and authentic, which has been sent down to warn the mother of towns and those around it, and those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are careful of their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance and authenticity of the Qur'an, describing it as a blessed Book sent down by God. The verse highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to serve as a warning to the people of the mother of towns, which refers to Mecca, and those surrounding it. Additionally, the verse notes that those who believe in the Hereafter also believe in the Qur'an and are mindful of their prayers, indicating a strong connection between faith in God's revelation and the practice of prayer.
orig: وهذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك مصدق الذي بين يديه ولتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها والذين يؤمنون بالآخرة يؤمنون به وهم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah or says, 'I have received revelation,' though nothing has been revealed to him, or who says, 'I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed'? If you could but see the wrongdoers in the throes of death, the angels extending their hands, saying, 'Get out your souls! Today you will be rewarded with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth, and because you were arrogant toward His verses.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the severity of attributing lies to God or claiming to have received revelation without actually receiving it. The verse emphasizes the gravity of such actions, describing those who commit them as 'wrongdoers' who will face punishment in the afterlife. The verse also highlights the arrogance of those who claim to receive revelation similar to what God has revealed, implying that they are pretending to have a special connection with God or trying to elevate themselves above others. The verse serves as a warning to those who might be tempted to make such claims, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they continue to lie and boast about their supposed divine connection.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو قال أوحي إلي ولم يوح إليه شيء ومن قال سأنزل مثل ما أنزل الله ولو ترى إذ الظالمون في غمرات الموت والملائكة باسطو أيديهم أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون على الله غير الحق وكنتم عن آياته تستكبرون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human hearts, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of human actions and thoughts, and that He is nearer to humans than they are to themselves. This verse emphasizes the idea of God's omniscience and His intimate relationship with humanity.
orig: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة وتركتم ما خولناكم وراء ظهوركم وما نرى معكم شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء لقد تقطع بينكم وضل عنكم ما كنتم تزعمون

translation: Indeed, Allah will say to the angels, 'I am the Most Merciful, so take the souls of the wicked away from Me, and cast them into the Fire of Hell.'
interpretation: This verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment when Allah will command the angels to take the souls of the wicked and cast them into Hell. The use of the phrase 'Indeed, Allah' emphasizes the certainty and finality of this event. The verse highlights the justice and mercy of Allah, as He is the Most Merciful, yet He will still punish those who have earned His wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of their punishment.
orig: إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ذلكم الله فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His knowledge of all human actions. The verse suggests that God is always with believers, regardless of their location or situation, and that He is aware of everything they do. This verse serves as a reminder of God's constant presence and the responsibility that comes with it, encouraging believers to always act with integrity and righteousness.
orig: فالق الإصباح وجعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And He is the One who has made the stars for you, that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and wisdom in creating the stars as a means of guidance for humanity. The verse specifically mentions the stars' role in guiding people through the darkness of the land and sea, indicating their importance for navigation and travel. Additionally, the verse can be seen as a metaphor for the role of faith and guidance in helping people navigate the challenges and darkness of life. Just as the stars provide a constant and reliable source of guidance for sailors and travelers, faith in God and His guidance can provide a similar source of comfort and direction for believers.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And He is the One who has created you from a single soul, and has made from it a mate to dwell with her; and when he covers her, she carries a light burden and goes about with it easily. And when she grows heavy, they both pray to God, their Lord: 'If You give us a good child, we will indeed be grateful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and wisdom in creating human beings from a single soul and making them into pairs. The verse emphasizes the unity and complementarity of men and women, and how they are meant to support each other and work together. The verse also highlights the struggle and hardship that comes with pregnancy and childbirth, and how it is a test of faith and patience for both parents. The verse ends with the hope that the child will be a source of joy and gratitude for the parents, and serves as a reminder of God's blessings and provision.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأكم من نفس واحدة فمستقر ومستودع قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يفقهون

translation: And He is the One who has sent down water from the sky, and We have brought forth with it all kinds of plants, and from them, greenery has come out, and from the palm trees, dates are hanging in clusters, and gardens of grapes, and olives, and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Look at their fruits when they yield and their ripeness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and provision, emphasizing how He has brought forth all kinds of plants and greenery through the water He has sent down from the sky. The verse specifically mentions the variety of fruits that come from different trees, such as dates from palm trees, grapes from vineyards, and olives and pomegranates from their respective trees. The verse invites people to observe and appreciate the beauty and diversity of these fruits, and to recognize the signs of God's creation and provision in them. The verse encourages people to believe in God and appreciate His blessings, and serves as a reminder of the accountability that comes with being a recipient of such blessings.
orig: وهو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء فأخرجنا منه خضرا نخرج منه حبا متراكبا ومن النخل من طلعها قنوان دانية وجنات من أعناب والزيتون والرمان مشتبها وغير متشابه انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And they have taken besides Him gods which can do them no harm, and they have taken for themselves gods from the jinn, and they have made for them sons and daughters without knowledge, glory be to Allah, Exalted is He above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's tendency to associate others with Allah and worship them besides Him. They have taken gods from the jinn, which are believed to have supernatural powers, and have made for themselves sons and daughters, which refers to the idols they have created. The verse emphasizes that these idols are powerless and cannot harm or benefit anyone. The phrase 'glory be to Allah, Exalted is He above what they describe' highlights the greatness and majesty of Allah, and how He is above all that they attribute to Him. The verse serves as a reminder that only Allah deserves to be worshipped and that associating partners with Him is a grave injustice.
orig: وجعلوا لله شركاء الجن وخلقهم وخرقوا له بنين وبنات بغير علم سبحانه وتعالى عما يصفون

translation: And the heavens and the earth and everything in them are His, and there is no partner with Him in their creation. He is the One who created everything, and He has knowledge of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sole ownership and control over the universe and everything in it. The use of the phrase 'and everything in them' underscores the idea that nothing is excluded from God's dominion, including the heavens, the earth, and all that exists within them. The verse also highlights God's role as the sole creator of everything, and His all-encompassing knowledge of all things. It is a reminder that God is the ultimate authority and source of all knowledge, and that everything else is subordinate to Him.
orig: بديع السماوات والأرض أنى يكون له ولد ولم تكن له صاحبة وخلق كل شيء وهو بكل شيء عليم

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things. Worship Him, and He is the Disposer of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the fact that He is the sole creator and sustainer of all things. It stresses the importance of worshiping only God and recognizing His authority over all aspects of life. The verse also highlights God's role as the Disposer of all things, signifying His control and dominion over the universe. It serves as a reminder to believers to submit to God's will and to recognize His sovereignty over all aspects of life.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم لا إله إلا هو خالق كل شيء فاعبدوه وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لا تدركه الأبصار وهو يدرك الأبصار وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: And indeed, a sign has come to you from your Lord, and a punishment will come to you from your Lord
interpretation: N
orig: قد جاءكم بصائر من ربكم فمن أبصر فلنفسه ومن عمي فعليها وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: And thus We have sent forth the verses and made them clear, in order that they may be mindful and be warned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'anic verses being clear and understandable to the people, in order to serve as a reminder and warning to those who are aware of their surroundings. The verse highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to guide people towards righteousness and to warn them of the consequences of their actions. It also underscores the responsibility of the believers to reflect on the Qur'an and its teachings, in order to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: وكذلك نصرف الآيات وليقولوا درست ولنبينه لقوم يعلمون

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, for there is no god but He, and ignore the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the revelations sent by God, and rejecting the beliefs and practices of polytheists who associate other deities with God. It highlights the exclusivity of God's divinity and the need to adhere only to His teachings, without compromising or syncretizing them with other beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of idolatry and the importance of staying true to God's message.
orig: اتبع ما أوحي إليك من ربك لا إله إلا هو وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated. And We have not appointed you over them as a guardian, nor are you their advocate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and the fact that He could have prevented the people from associating partners with Him if He had willed. The verse also highlights the Prophet's role as a messenger and warner, rather than a guardian or advocate for the people. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's responsibility is to convey the message, and it is up to God to guide or punish the people as He sees fit.
orig: ولو شاء الله ما أشركوا وما جعلناك عليهم حفيظا وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And do not cursed those who call upon other than Allah, lest they curse Allah out of ignorance. Likewise, We have adorned for every nation their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against cursing those who worship others besides Allah, as it may lead them to curse Allah himself out of ignorance. The verse also highlights the fact that every nation has been adorned with their own deeds, which will be presented to their Lord on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of one's actions and the importance of recognizing the Oneness of God.
orig: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم كذلك زينا لكل أمة عملهم ثم إلى ربهم مرجعهم فينبئهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would believe in it. Say, 'The signs are with Allah.' And what will make you perceive that they will not believe in it, even if it comes?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who refuse to believe in the signs and miracles sent by God. Despite their strongest oaths, they will not believe in the signs even when they come. The verse highlights the idea that the signs are in God's hands, and it is not up to human beings to dictate when and how they will come. The verse also suggests that even when the signs do come, the disbelievers will not be convinced, indicating their deep-seated disbelief and unwillingness to submit to God's will.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءتهم آية ليؤمنن بها قل إنما الآيات عند الله وما يشعركم أنها إذا جاءت لا يؤمنون

translation: And We have turned their hearts and their eyes away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We left them in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: The verse describes how God has caused the hearts and eyes of those who reject His signs to be turned away from the truth, just as they had refused to believe in it the first time it was presented to them. As a result, they are left in their transgression, wandering blindly and unable to find the right path. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's signs and the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth when it is presented.
orig: ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And if We had sent angels to them, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered all things in front of them, they would not have believed, except that Allah wills, but most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that even if God had sent angels and the dead had spoken to the disbelievers, and all things were gathered in front of them, they still would not have believed, except for the will of God. The verse highlights the idea that faith is not something that can be forced upon someone, but rather it is a gift from God. The verse also suggests that most people are ignorant of the truth and are unwilling to listen to the message of the prophets.
orig: ولو أننا نزلنا إليهم الملائكة وكلمهم الموتى وحشرنا عليهم كل شيء قبلا ما كانوا ليؤمنوا إلا أن يشاء الله ولكن أكثرهم يجهلون

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy, devils from humans and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech, deceptions of the mind, and if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that every prophet has had to face opposition and resistance from both humans and jinn. The verse suggests that these opponents are inspired by their own desires and misguided beliefs, and that they use eloquent speech and deception to mislead others. The verse also emphasizes that if God had willed, these opponents would not have been able to do what they do, and that it is ultimately God's will that prevails. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be cautious of the deceptions of their opponents and to trust in God's ultimate authority and control.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض زخرف القول غرورا ولو شاء ربك ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And indeed, We will test those who believe not in the Hereafter with a painful punishment, so they will be the ones who will be losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. They will be tested with a painful punishment, which they will not be able to escape. The verse emphasizes that those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be the ultimate losers, as they will not only suffer in this life but also in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical about the existence of the Hereafter, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: ولتصغى إليه أفئدة الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وليرضوه وليقترفوا ما هم مقترفون

translation: Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say: We believe, and will not be tested?
interpretation: The verse raises a question about the nature of faith and the relationship between belief and action. It suggests that simply claiming to believe in God and His revelation is not enough, and that true faith is demonstrated through action and obedience to God's commands. The verse implies that those who truly believe will be tested and tried, and that their faith will be refined and purified through these trials. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is not just a matter of intellectual assent, but requires action and commitment.
orig: أفغير الله أبتغي حكما وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعلمون أنه منزل من ربك بالحق فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice. None can change His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authority and finality of God's word, which is truth and justice itself. The phrase 'fulfilled in truth and in justice' underscores the idea that God's word is not only true but also just, indicating that it is morally right and in accordance with what is fair and equitable. The second part of the verse emphasizes that God's word is unchangeable and cannot be altered or modified by anyone. The phrase 'None can change His words' reinforces the idea of God's sovereignty and the impossibility of altering His decrees. Finally, the verse ends by highlighting God's all-hearing and all-knowing nature, emphasizing that He is aware of all things and has knowledge of all that exists.
orig: وتمت كلمت ربك صدقا وعدلا لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم

translation: And indeed, most of the people in the earth have strayed from the way of Allah, while they follow their own desires and conjecture.
interpretation: The verse highlights the widespread nature of spiritual straying and the tendency of people to follow their own desires and conjecture instead of seeking guidance from Allah. The phrase 'most of the people in the earth' emphasizes the prevalence of this phenomenon, suggesting that it is the norm rather than the exception. The use of the word 'strayed' implies a departure from the right path and a loss of spiritual direction. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance can only be found in following the teachings of Allah, and that relying on one's own desires and conjecture can lead to misguidance and destruction.
orig: وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل الله إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Knowing of who strays from His way, and He is Knowing of the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all human beings, including those who stray from His path and those who are guided. The verse suggests that God is fully aware of the actions and intentions of all individuals, and that He is aware of who is following His guidance and who is not. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of human actions, and that He will hold individuals accountable for their actions in the afterlife.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم من يضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So eat of what Allah has provided for you [as lawful] and be grateful for His favor if you are believers indeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful for the blessings and provision of Allah. The use of the phrase 'as lawful' highlights the importance of only consuming what is halal and permissible by Allah. The verse also serves as a reminder that true believers are those who are grateful for the favors of Allah and acknowledge the source of their provision. It is a call to action, encouraging believers to reflect on their actions and ensure that they are living a life that is pleasing to Allah.
orig: فكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه إن كنتم بآياته مؤمنين

translation: And what is wrong with you that you do not eat that on which Allah's name has been mentioned while He has explained in detail what is forbidden to you, except what you are forced to do? Indeed, many mislead others with their own desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord - He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of why people refuse to eat certain foods that have been prohibited by God, despite the fact that He has made it clear what is allowed and what is not. The verse suggests that people are often misled by their own desires and the desires of others, rather than relying on God's guidance. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and wise, and that His prohibitions are in place for a reason, even if they may not always make sense to humans.
orig: وما لكم ألا تأكلوا مما ذكر اسم الله عليه وقد فصل لكم ما حرم عليكم إلا ما اضطررتم إليه وإن كثيرا ليضلون بأهوائهم بغير علم إن ربك هو أعلم بالمعتدين

translation: And they indulged in the manifest sin and concealed the evil within. Indeed, those who earn sin will be rewarded with what they used to commit.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of indulging in open sin and hiding one's evil deeds. The verse warns that those who engage in such behavior will ultimately be punished for their actions, receiving a reward in accordance with their deeds.
orig: وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه إن الذين يكسبون الإثم سيجزون بما كانوا يقترفون

translation: And do not eat of that which does not mention the name of Allah, for indeed, it is an abomination. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed, you will be polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mentioning the name of Allah when slaughtering animals for food. Failure to do so is considered an abomination and is associated with the influence of devils who seek to mislead humans into polytheism. The verse warns against following the footsteps of the devils and their allies, and instead encourages obedience to Allah and His Messenger. It highlights the significance of acknowledging and praising Allah for the blessings of food and life.
orig: ولا تأكلوا مما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه وإنه لفسق وإن الشياطين ليوحون إلى أوليائهم ليجادلوكم وإن أطعتموهم إنكم لمشركون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به في الناس كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها كذلك زين للكافرين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have made in every town great leaders, who commit sin and wrongdoing in it, and they do not fear the punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has placed great leaders in every town, but these leaders have failed in their duties and have become corrupt, committing sins and wrongdoing. They do not fear the punishment of God, indicating a lack of faith and a sense of accountability. The verse suggests that the leaders have become complacent in their power and have forgotten their responsibility to lead their people justly and righteously.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها وما يمكرون إلا بأنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah are given.' Allah knows best where to place His message. They will be overcome by the curse of Allah and a severe punishment for their disbelief.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign to prove the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are warned that their demand is misguided and that they will be punished for their disbelief. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and sovereignty in choosing where to place His message, indicating that the Qur'an is a guidance for those who fear Allah and a warning for those who reject faith. The verse also highlights the severe punishment that awaits those who disbelieve in Allah and His messenger.
orig: وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته سيصيب الذين أجرموا صغار عند الله وعذاب شديد بما كانوا يمكرون

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of supporting and aiding the cause of Allah, and assures believers that Allah will aid those who do so. The phrase 'Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might' highlights God's ability to help and support those who strive in His way. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate victory and success come from God, and that believers should put their trust in Him and work towards promoting justice and righteousness in the world.
orig: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام ومن يرد أن يضله يجعل صدره ضيقا حرجا كأنما يصعد في السماء كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون

translation: And this is the path of your Lord, a straight path. Indeed, We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the clarity and straightforwardness of God's path, indicating that it is easy to understand and follow for those who are willing to remember and heed God's signs. The verse also suggests that the Qur'an contains detailed guidance for those who are willing to reflect and remember God's teachings. The use of the word 'qawm' (people) in the phrase 'qawm yadhakkarun' (a people who remember) suggests that the verse is addressing a specific community or group of people who are committed to remembering and following God's teachings.
orig: وهذا صراط ربك مستقيما قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يذكرون

translation: For them is a reward of Paradise, where they will be received with open arms, and they will be greeted with 'Peace!' from their Lord, and they will be granted their desire of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of the righteous in Paradise. The use of the phrase 'For them is a reward of Paradise' emphasizes that the reward is a gift from God, and the description of the reception with open arms and the greeting of 'Peace!' from God highlights the warmth and joy of the welcome. The phrase 'and they will be granted their desire of what they used to do' suggests that the righteous will be able to enjoy the fruits of their labor and the fulfillment of their desires in Paradise.
orig: لهم دار السلام عند ربهم وهو وليهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: On a day when He will gather them all together, (and) say: 'O My slaves, you have wronged yourselves, (and) you have no right to say anything against Me. My favors surrounded you, but you denied them.' And Allah's anger will be severe.',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where God will gather all humanity and address them, pointing out their wrongdoing and ingratitude. The verse emphasizes God's favor and grace towards humanity, which was met with rejection and disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's blessings and warnings, and the certainty of His punishment for those who disobey Him.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا يا معشر الجن قد استكثرتم من الإنس وقال أولياؤهم من الإنس ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض وبلغنا أجلنا الذي أجلت لنا قال النار مثواكم خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء الله إن ربك حكيم عليم

translation: And indeed, We will enable you to recite the Qur'an, and you will not forget except what Allah wills. Indeed, We will ease you toward the path of victory.
interpretation: These verses emphasize the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a means of achieving success. The first verse states that God will enable the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to recite the Qur'an, indicating that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that is beyond human capability to produce. The second verse highlights the fact that the Prophet will not forget any part of the Qur'an, except what God wills, implying that God has the power to control human memory and forgetfulness. The third verse promises that God will ease the Prophet's path to victory, suggesting that the Qur'an contains guidance that will lead to success in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: O inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, have you not seen that the messengers from among you have come to you, relating My signs to you and warning you of the meeting of your Lord? They said, 'We have testified against ourselves, for we have been wicked.'
interpretation: The verse addresses all inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, asking them if they have not seen the messengers sent by God to guide them. The messengers have come to relate God's signs and warn them of the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes that the messengers are from among the people themselves, indicating that they have a personal responsibility to listen to and follow the message. The verse also highlights the idea that people have a tendency to be wicked and reject the message, as they have testified against themselves. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of listening to God's message and living a righteous life.
orig: يا معشر الجن والإنس ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يقصون عليكم آياتي وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا شهدنا على أنفسنا وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا وشهدوا على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا كافرين

translation: And if your Lord had not been merciful to their ancestors, they would have destroyed their settlements, and how many a town did We destroy while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy upon the ancestors of the disbelievers, despite their wicked deeds. The verse suggests that if God had not been merciful, their towns would have been destroyed, just like the many towns that were destroyed in the past due to their injustice. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and judgment, and that His mercy is not something to be taken for granted. It also warns the disbelievers that they should not assume they will be spared from punishment just because they are descended from those who were spared in the past.
orig: ذلك أن لم يكن ربك مهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها غافلون

translation: And for every degree [of sin] that they were guilty of, they will have a punishment [in the Hereafter] in proportion to their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of retribution in Islam, where every individual will be held accountable for their actions in this life and will face consequences in the afterlife. The severity of the punishment will be directly proportional to the severity of their sins. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ولكل درجات مما عملوا وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون

translation: And your Lord is the Free of Need, the owner of Mercy. If He wills, He can remove you and replace you with whatever He wills, just as He created you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and authority over His creation. He is the One who can create and destroy, and He is not in need of anyone or anything. The verse warns the believers that they should not become too attached to this world or feel a sense of security, for God can replace them with another people if He wills. The verse also highlights the idea that everything in this world is a mere trial and a test, and that true success and happiness come from living according to God's commands and being mindful of the Hereafter.
orig: وربك الغني ذو الرحمة إن يشأ يذهبكم ويستخلف من بعدكم ما يشاء كما أنشأكم من ذرية قوم آخرين

translation: Indeed, what you are promised will come to pass, and you are not ones who can escape.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of the promised punishment for those who are unjust and wicked. The phrase 'what you are promised' refers to the warning that has been given to them through the prophets and scriptures, and the phrase 'and you are not ones who can escape' underscores the idea that they will not be able to avoid or evade the punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that God's justice will ultimately prevail, and that those who reject His commands will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: إن ما توعدون لآت وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position, indeed I am working, soon you will know who will have the home of the Hereafter, indeed the wrongdoers will not be successful.
interpretation: The verse is a warning to the Prophet's people, encouraging them to work righteously and strive for the Hereafter, rather than being consumed by worldly pursuits. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate success will be for those who do good deeds and that the wrongdoers will not be successful in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the Prophet is a witness over his people and will be a witness against them on the Day of Judgment, indicating the responsibility of the Prophet in guiding his people and the accountability of his people in front of God.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون من تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And they assigned to Allah from the crops and the livestock a portion, and they said, 'This is for Allah,' by their claim, and this is for our partners. But what was assigned to their partners did not reach Allah, and what was assigned to Allah reached their partners. Evil is what they judged.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's practice of assigning a portion of their crops and livestock to Allah and their idols. They claimed that what they assigned to Allah was for Him, but in reality, it did not reach Him. Instead, it was their idols who benefited from their offerings. The verse highlights the people's misunderstanding of the concept of tithing and their misguided belief that their idols had a share in what was meant for Allah. The verse warns against such practices and emphasizes the importance of dedicating all acts of worship solely to Allah, without associating partners with Him.
orig: وجعلوا لله مما ذرأ من الحرث والأنعام نصيبا فقالوا هذا لله بزعمهم وهذا لشركائنا فما كان لشركائهم فلا يصل إلى الله وما كان لله فهو يصل إلى شركائهم ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And likewise, We have destroyed many a town that was unjust, and We have punished them with destruction, making them an example for their fellows, and a warning to those who would come after them, that they might take heed and fear Allah.
interpretation: N
orig: وكذلك زين لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم شركاؤهم ليردوهم وليلبسوا عليهم دينهم ولو شاء الله ما فعلوه فذرهم وما يفترون

translation: And they say, 'These are cattle and crops, let us not be burdened by them.' They say that without knowledge, and they attribute their neglect of God's blessings to Him, saying, 'These cattle and crops are not worth mentioning in the remembrance of God.' They have forgotten that it is He who created them and provided for them, and they will soon be returned to Him.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of those who are ungrateful for God's blessings and deny the significance of His favors. They view the cattle and crops as mere possessions and do not recognize their true value as blessings from God. They wrongly assume that these blessings are not worth mentioning in the remembrance of God, and they forget that it is God who created and provided for them. The verse serves as a reminder that everything we have is a blessing from God and that we should be grateful for His favors and remember Him in our daily lives.
orig: وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر لا يطعمها إلا من نشاء بزعمهم وأنعام حرمت ظهورها وأنعام لا يذكرون اسم الله عليها افتراء عليه سيجزيهم بما كانوا يفترون

translation: And they say, 'What is in the bellies of these animals is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our females.' Indeed, if it is killed, then they will be punished.
interpretation: The verse addresses a common misconception among the pagan Arabs, who believed that the meat of certain animals was only permissible for men and not for women. The verse refutes this idea, stating that the meat of animals is not inherently gendered and that both men and women are equal in the eyes of God. The verse also warns the pagan Arabs that if they continue to hold onto such misconceptions and disobey God's commands, they will face punishment.
orig: وقالوا ما في بطون هذه الأنعام خالصة لذكورنا ومحرم على أزواجنا وإن يكن ميتة فهم فيه شركاء سيجزيهم وصفهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And they have killed their prophets unjustly, so their reward will be with their Lord, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse refers to the killing of prophets by the disbelievers, which is considered a grave injustice. The verse states that these prophets were killed unjustly, and their reward will be with God. The verse also emphasizes that the killers will not be able to justify their actions, and they will not be wronged in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who oppose God's messengers and reminds them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: قد خسر الذين قتلوا أولادهم سفها بغير علم وحرموا ما رزقهم الله افتراء على الله قد ضلوا وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And He is the One who has made gardens of date-palms and grapes, and the trees which are laden with fruit, and the olives and the pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of their fruit when they bear fruit and give their due on the day of their harvest, and do not act extravagantly, indeed He does not love the extravagant.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the variety of fruits that God has created, including date-palms, grapes, olives, and pomegranates. It encourages people to eat of their fruit when it is ripe and to give God's due on the day of harvest. The verse also warns against extravagance and excess, as God does not love those who are wasteful and do not appreciate the blessings He has given them.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ جنات معروشات وغير معروشات والنخل والزرع مختلفا أكله والزيتون والرمان متشابها وغير متشابه كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر وآتوا حقه يوم حصاده ولا تسرفوا إنه لا يحب المسرفين

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein. And when the angels take their souls at death, they say: 'In what state were you?' They say: 'We have been in a state of oppression and injustice.' They will say: 'Then what kept you back from crying out when the angel of death came to you?' They will say: 'It was the Mercy of our Lord.' Indeed, they will question one another.
interpretation: This verse highlights the close relationship between God and humanity, emphasizing that God is nearer to us than our own jugular vein. The verse also touches upon the theme of accountability, as the angels will question the souls of the deceased about their state in life and why they did not cry out for help when death approached. The verse ends with a hint of divine mercy, suggesting that God's mercy may be a factor in the judgment of souls.
orig: ومن الأنعام حمولة وفرشا كلوا مما رزقكم الله ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: Thamanani azwaj min alddunia athnayn wamin almithali athnayn qal alddikriin haram am alanthiyyin ama ishtamaltu alayhi arham alanthiyyin nabaoonani bialAAilmi in kuntum sadiqeena
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prohibition of marrying two sisters at the same time. The verse emphasizes the gravity of this sin, describing it as a prohibition that is 'haram' (forbidden) and 'al-anthiyyin' (a severe prohibition). The verse also warns against the consequences of such an action, threatening those who engage in it with punishment in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of treating women with respect and dignity, and the severe consequences of violating this principle.
orig: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين نبئوني بعلم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And of the cattle, two, and of the sheep, two. Say, 'Is it the two males that He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse is a question posed by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in response to the pagan Meccans' objection to the prohibition of certain animals for sacrifice. The verse is asking the Meccans to consider whether it is the two male animals or the two female animals that are forbidden, or is it the offspring of the females that are forbidden? The verse is highlighting the inconsistency in the Meccans' argument and their lack of understanding of the true nature of God's commandments. The verse serves as a reminder that God's laws are not based on arbitrary reasons, but are rather based on wisdom and justice, and that those who reject God's commandments are the ones who are truly misguided.
orig: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين قل آلذكرين حرم أم الأنثيين أما اشتملت عليه أرحام الأنثيين أم كنتم شهداء إذ وصاكم الله بهذا فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا ليضل الناس بغير علم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to a soul except that it be dead or blood or the flesh of a pig or that which is impure, or profane, or the flesh of an animal which has been slaughtered in a name other than the name of Allah . But if one is forced by necessity, neither craving nor transgressing, then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse is a response to the question of what is lawful and unlawful in the context of food and slaughter. The verse explains that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has not been prohibited from anything except what is impure, dead, or the flesh of a pig. Additionally, the verse emphasizes that the meat of an animal slaughtered in the name of anyone other than Allah is also forbidden. However, the verse also provides an exception for cases of necessity, where an individual is forced to consume such meat to avoid starvation or harm. In such cases, the individual is not considered to be transgressing and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: قل لا أجد في ما أوحي إلي محرما على طاعم يطعمه إلا أن يكون ميتة أو دما مسفوحا أو لحم خنزير فإنه رجس أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن ربك غفور رحيم

translation: And We have destroyed the towns which were unjust, and We have punished them with a punishment which was exemplary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust and the punishment that was inflicted upon them. The use of the word 'وعلى' (wa-ʿalá) suggests a sense of continuity, indicating that the punishment was not just a one-time event, but rather an ongoing process. The phrase 'كل ذي ظفر' (kulli dhī ẓafir) means 'every owner of a pair' (of oxen or camels), emphasizing the idea that no one was spared from the punishment, regardless of their social status or wealth. The verse also mentions the specific punishment of 'شحومهما' (shiḥāmhumā), which refers to a severe and painful punishment. The phrase 'إلا ما حملت ظهورهما' (illā mā ḥamaltu ẓahūrhumā) suggests that the punishment was so severe that it left a lasting impact on the people, making them an example for others. The final phrase, 'وإنا لصادقون' (wa-inā l-ṣādiqūn), emphasizes the truthfulness and reliability of the punishment, indicating that it was not a random act, but rather a just and deserved consequence of their actions.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا كل ذي ظفر ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما إلا ما حملت ظهورهما أو الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم وإنا لصادقون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Forgiving and the Merciful, but His punishment will certainly reach the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness, but also serves as a warning to those who commit crimes and injustices. The verse indicates that God's punishment is certain and will reach those who commit evil deeds, serving as a deterrent to those who would otherwise choose to live a life of sin and injustice.
orig: فإن كذبوك فقل ربكم ذو رحمة واسعة ولا يرد بأسه عن القوم المجرمين

translation: And they say, 'Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped the idols, neither our fathers nor we would have prohibited anything.' Those before them did the same, until they tasted Our punishment. Say, 'Have you considered what you worship? And can you perceive what you have been worshipping?',
interpretation: The verse addresses the excuses made by the polytheists who claim that they were forced to worship idols by their ancestors and that they had no choice in the matter. The verse refutes this argument by pointing out that the people before them also made the same excuses, yet they still faced the consequences of their actions. The verse then challenges the polytheists to reflect on the nature of their worship and what they are actually worshiping, implying that their idols are powerless and cannot bring them any benefit.
orig: سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من شيء كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم حتى ذاقوا بأسنا قل هل عندكم من علم فتخرجوه لنا إن تتبعون إلا الظن وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون
