orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: And We saved him and his family, except his wife, who was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Lot and his family, who were saved by God from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse highlights the fact that Lot's wife was not among those who were saved, as she was one of those who remained behind and did not believe in God's warning. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God, and the consequences of disobedience and disbelief.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We sent upon them a flood of punishment, so observe how was the end of the sinners!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of Noah, who were warned by Prophet Noah but refused to believe and continued to live in sin. The 'flood of punishment' refers to the great flood that God sent upon them, which destroyed them all. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The phrase 'observe how was the end of the sinners' emphasizes the idea that the punishment was not only severe but also final, leaving no chance for repentance or escape.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And indeed, We have sent to [the people of] Madinah a group of angels, saying, 'Worship none but Allah. Indeed, the promise of your Lord has come to you. The recompense of your Lord will be fulfilled.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the message that the angels brought to the people of Madinah, calling them to worship only Allah and warning them of the consequences of not heeding this message. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the promise of God's recompense, indicating that the reward or punishment for one's actions is inevitable. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in disobedience to God, encouraging them to turn back to Him and worship Him alone.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not incline towards those who are unjust, lest the Fire touches you, and you have no protectors other than Allah, and you will not be supported.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against inclining towards those who are unjust and advises them to avoid their company. The verse emphasizes the consequences of befriending the wicked, which is the risk of being touched by the Fire (Hell). The verse also reminds believers that they should not rely on anyone else but Allah for protection, and that they will not have any supporters on Judgment Day if they engage in unjust behavior.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And indeed, there was a group of you who believed in what I sent forth, and another group did not believe. So wait until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division among the people regarding the message sent by the Prophet. Some believed in the message, while others rejected it. The verse tells the believers to be patient and wait for Allah's judgment, which will be the ultimate and fairest judgment. The verse emphasizes Allah's role as the best judge, indicating that His judgment is the final and most just verdict. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to have faith in Allah's justice and to trust in His ability to distinguish between right and wrong.
orig: وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا فاصبروا حتى يحكم الله بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: The arrogant leaders of his people said to those who believed among them, 'We will expel you from our town, you evil-doers!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the arrogant leaders of a town towards the believers who lived among them. The leaders, who were proud of their power and status, saw the believers as a threat to their authority and sought to expel them from their town. The verse highlights the contrast between the arrogance of the leaders and the humility of the believers, who were willing to endure persecution for their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is not deterred by worldly power or status, and that those who are faithful to God will ultimately triumph over those who seek to oppress them.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا قال أولو كنا كارهين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest triumph. And We have aided them not, but it was Allah who aided them. Indeed, He is the One who will aid them, for He is the Powerful, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the victory and triumph given by God to the believers. The verse emphasizes the idea that the victory was given by God and not by the believers' own strength or power. The verse also highlights the idea that God is the One who aids and supports the believers, and that He is the source of all power and wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to put their trust in God and to recognize that their success is a result of God's grace and mercy.
orig: قد افترينا على الله كذبا إن عدنا في ملتكم بعد إذ نجانا الله منها وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله ربنا وسع ربنا كل شيء علما على الله توكلنا ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين

translation: And the disbelieving men and women said, 'If you follow Shu'ayb, you will indeed be losers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelieving men and women when they were invited by Prophet Shu'ayb to follow him and believe in God. They mocked and ridiculed the idea of following a prophet from their own tribe, implying that they were too proud to submit to a leader from a different tribe. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject faith and refuse to submit to God's will, even when faced with clear evidence and guidance. It serves as a reminder that true faith requires humility and submission to God, regardless of one's social status or background.
orig: وقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: The liars are those who denied the Day of Reckoning, and they were the ones who were lost.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who denied the Day of Reckoning, the day when all humanity will be judged by God based on their deeds in this life. The verse emphasizes that these deniers are lost and misguided, and their denial of the Day of Reckoning is a sign of their spiritual blindness and ignorance. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the idea of accountability and judgment after death, reminding them that their denial will not change the reality of the Day of Reckoning and its consequences for their souls.
orig: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كأن لم يغنوا فيها الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, but how can I sorrow over a people who disbelieve?'
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet Lot's frustration and sadness at his people's refusal to believe in his message. Despite his efforts to convey God's message and advise them, they continued to reject his message and refused to believe in God. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassion and concern for his people, as well as his sense of helplessness in the face of their disbelief. It serves as a reminder that the Prophets were not just messengers of God, but also human beings who felt deeply the pain of rejection and disbelief.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي ونصحت لكم فكيف آسى على قوم كافرين

translation: And We have not sent any prophet to any town except that We seized its people with adversity and hardship that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of prophets being sent to guide people towards righteousness. The verse indicates that God sends prophets to towns to test their faith and obedience. The adversity and hardship that the people face serve as a reminder of their accountability to God and the consequences of their actions. The ultimate goal is that people humble themselves and turn towards God, recognizing their dependence on Him and their need for guidance. The verse warns against complacency and encourages a constant reflection on one's actions and beliefs.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نبي إلا أخذنا أهلها بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يضرعون

translation: Then We replaced the evil with good, until they forgot that which had been given to them, and they took to themselves gods instead of Allah, thanking Him not for what We had given them. And they denied Us, so We punished them. And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.
interpretation: The verse describes how God replaced the evil that the people were experiencing with good, but instead of being grateful, they turned to worship other gods instead of Allah and denied His blessings. The verse highlights the ingratitude of the people and how they forgot the favors that God had bestowed upon them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are ungrateful and take God's blessings for granted, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of being thankful for what they have been given.
orig: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء فأخذناهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And if the people of the towns had believed and been righteous, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequence of disbelief and wickedness, which is the withholding of God's blessings. The verse emphasizes that if the people of the towns had believed and been righteous, they would have received blessings from both heaven and earth. The verse serves as a reminder that faith and righteousness are essential for receiving God's favors and blessings, and that disbelief and wickedness lead to deprivation and punishment.
orig: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض ولكن كذبوا فأخذناهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أوأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى وهم يلعبون

translation: And indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder to the children of Adam.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a reminder to the descendants of Adam, stressing the importance of heeding its message and adhering to its teachings. The use of 'reminder' (dhikra) suggests that the Qur'an serves as a reminder of the truth and of God's promises and warnings, and that it is a means of guidance for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون

translation: And had not God been gracious to the inhabitants of the earth, He would have destroyed them. Indeed, the punishment is coming to them because of their sins, and it will not be averted from them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and grace towards humanity, despite their sinful nature. The verse suggests that if it were not for God's grace, humanity would have been destroyed due to their sins. The verse also implies that the punishment for their sins is inevitable and cannot be averted. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of sin and the need for repentance and obedience to God.
orig: أولم يهد للذين يرثون الأرض من بعد أهلها أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنوبهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين

translation: And We have not found in most of them (the towns) any loyalty to their covenant. Indeed, We found most of them to be rebellious (disobedient to God).
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that most towns and communities that were destroyed by God's punishment had broken their covenant with Him. They had been disobedient and disloyal to God's commands, and their punishment was a consequence of their disobedience. The verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and obedience to God's commands and serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد وإن وجدنا أكثرهم لفاسقين

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs to Pharaoh and his nobles, but they wronged them, so see how the end of the corruptors was.
interpretation: The verse describes how God sent Moses and his brother Aaron to Pharaoh and his nobles with divine signs and messages. Despite this, the Pharaoh and his people wronged them and rejected their message. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the punishment that awaits those who oppose His will. It also highlights the importance of listening to and following God's messengers, and the rewards that come with it.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فظلموا بها فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt, and declaring himself to be a messenger sent by the Lord of the worlds. This declaration is significant because it emphasizes Moses' divine authorization and the universality of God's sovereignty. By using the phrase 'Lord of the worlds', Moses is emphasizing that God's authority extends beyond just the Israelites, but to all people and all creation. This verse serves as a reminder that God's message is not limited to a particular group or nation, but is universal and applicable to all humanity.
orig: وقال موسى يا فرعون إني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you a clear sign from your Lord
interpretation: N
orig: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق قد جئتكم ببينة من ربكم فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل

translation: And indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Me and obey Me.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) is speaking to his people, informing them that he has been sent by God with a sign, a miracle, to prove his prophethood. He urges them to fear God and obey Him, indicating that the sign is a manifestation of God's power and a reminder of the consequences of disobedience. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and respecting the authority of God's messengers and the consequences of rejecting their message.
orig: قال إن كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And He released him, [from the belly of the fish], while he was sick.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the prophet Jonah, who had been swallowed by a large fish, was released from the fish's belly. The verse emphasizes Jonah's weakened state, describing him as 'sick', indicating that his time inside the fish had taken a toll on his health. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power to save and deliver, even in the most desperate of situations.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And He stretched out His hand, and thus it was evident to the watchers.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when God stretched out His hand to create the heavens and the earth, and how it was a manifestation of His power and wisdom. The phrase 'and thus it was evident to the watchers' suggests that the creation was not only a physical act, but also a manifestation of God's divine attributes, which were witnessed by the angels and other divine beings. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the role of the divine in shaping the universe.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: The people of Pharaoh's household said: This man is a tyrant, or a sorcerer.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of Pharaoh's household towards Moses, whom they perceived as a threat to their power and status. They accused Moses of being a tyrant or a sorcerer, implying that they saw him as a charismatic leader who was using his powers for personal gain. The verse highlights the contrast between Moses' righteousness and the corruption of Pharaoh's court, and serves as a reminder of the importance of standing up against oppression and injustice.
orig: قال الملأ من قوم فرعون إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: And indeed, We will bring forth [from the earth] those who were hidden from you and will make them taste the severe punishment [because] of what they used to conspire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all people will be brought forth from their graves and judged according to their deeds. The verse specifically mentions those who were hidden from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, indicating that even those who were not visible or apparent to the believers will be brought forth and judged. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that these individuals will face due to their conspiracies and evil deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the Day of Reckoning and the consequences of their actions.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not, and have not mercy on us, we shall certainly be lost.
interpretation: In this verse, the people are acknowledging their sinfulness and recognizing that they have wronged themselves. They are seeking forgiveness and mercy from God, acknowledging that if they do not receive it, they will be lost. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness, and serves as a reminder of the mercy and forgiveness that God offers to those who seek it.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وأرسل في المدائن حاشرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يأتوك بكل ساحر عليم

translation: And the sorcerers of Pharaoh's court came and said, 'Indeed, we have a rewarding job, for we are the predominant ones.'
interpretation: The verse describes the arrogance and boasting of Pharaoh's sorcerers, who believed they were superior and had a rewarding job because of their magical abilities. Their attitude reflects their ignorance and lack of humility, as they failed to recognize the power of God and instead attributed their success to their own abilities. The verse serves as a warning against pride and arrogance, reminding believers to remain humble and recognize the true source of their strength and success.
orig: وجاء السحرة فرعون قالوا إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: And indeed, you are of those brought near [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and acknowledges his status as a chosen servant of Allah, who has been brought near to Him. The phrase 'min al-muqarrabin' (of those brought near) implies a special relationship between the Prophet and Allah, signifying the Prophet's elevated spiritual status and his role as a leader and guide for humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's responsibility and the greatness of the task assigned to him by Allah.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم لمن المقربين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the ones to stone you',
interpretation: In this verse, the people of Israel are threatening to stone Moses if he does not comply with their demand to throw down the tablets containing the Ten Commandments. The verse highlights the rebellious nature of the Israelites and their lack of faith in Moses' leadership. It also underscores the gravity of the situation, as the people were willing to resort to violence in order to get what they wanted. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of leadership and the need for obedience to divine authority.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون نحن الملقين

translation: And they have said: 'What! when we are bones and fragments shall we really be raised up, also our forefathers of old?',
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' mocking response to the idea of resurrection. They find it impossible to believe that they will be raised from the dead, along with their ancient ancestors. The verse highlights their skepticism and lack of faith in the afterlife, as well as their failure to understand the power of God. It serves as a reminder that resurrection is a divine intervention that goes beyond human comprehension, and that God's power is not limited by human imagination.
orig: قال ألقوا فلما ألقوا سحروا أعين الناس واسترهبوهم وجاءوا بسحر عظيم

translation: And We inspired to Moses, 'Throw your staff,' and behold, it devoured what they were falsifying.
interpretation: The verse describes the miracle of Moses' staff, which was transformed into a serpent and consumed the false objects of worship that the people of Pharaoh were using to deceive themselves and others. The verse highlights God's power and authority, as well as Moses' faith and obedience to God's command. The verse also serves as a reminder that false idols and deities are nothing but mere objects and have no power compared to the might and majesty of the one true God.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: And the truth has come, and the falsehood has vanished. Indeed, the falsehood was bound to vanish.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. The phrase 'fawaq al-haq' (فوق الحق) means 'the truth has come' and signifies the revelation of the Qur'an, which is the ultimate truth that has come to guide humanity. The second part of the verse, 'batil mā kānā yamli'ūn' (بطل ما كانوا يعملون), means 'and the falsehood has vanished' indicating that all the falsehoods and lies that were present before the revelation of the Qur'an have been vanquished. The verse emphasizes the idea that truth will ultimately prevail over falsehood, and that those who follow the truth will be victorious in the end.
orig: فوقع الحق وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they were defeated, and they turned their backs in flight.
interpretation: The verse describes the defeat of the disbelievers and their cowardly retreat. The phrase 'they turned their backs in flight' emphasizes their hasty retreat and lack of courage in the face of the believers' army. The verse highlights the contrast between the believers' bravery and the disbelievers' cowardice, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of opposing God's will.
orig: فغلبوا هنالك وانقلبوا صاغرين

translation: And the magicians fell down prostrate.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the magicians who were present during the confrontation between Moses and Pharaoh. When Moses' staff transformed into a serpent and swallowed the serpents produced by the magicians, they were amazed and fell down prostrate in submission. This indicates that they recognized the power of God and acknowledged the superiority of Moses' miracle over their own magic tricks. The verse highlights the impact of the miracle on the magicians and emphasizes their humility and recognition of the truth.
orig: وألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and we have obeyed His messenger.,
interpretation: In this verse, the believers declare their faith in the one true God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and their obedience to His prophet. This declaration of faith serves as a testimony to their belief in the oneness of God and their commitment to following His commandments as revealed through His prophet. It also highlights the importance of obedience to God and His messenger as a fundamental aspect of faith.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people! Surely your enemy is only yourself.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing his people, who are suffering from the oppression of the Pharaoh. Moses is telling them that their real enemy is not the Pharaoh, but their own selves. This is because they have forgotten their connection to God and have become disconnected from their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that the true enemy is not external, but internal. It is the self that must be overcome in order to achieve spiritual freedom and liberation.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: Pharaoh said, 'You have believed in him before I give you permission. This is a plot that you have plotted in the city to drive out its people, but you will come to know',
interpretation: Pharaoh is accusing the believers of plotting against him and trying to drive him and his people out of the city. He is suggesting that their belief in Moses and their desire to follow him is a threat to his authority and rule. Pharaoh is trying to turn the people against the believers and make them doubt their faith. The verse highlights the struggle between Pharaoh and Moses and the conflict between their two opposing worldviews. It also shows how Pharaoh is trying to maintain his power and control over the people, even if it means oppressing and harming them.
orig: قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم إن هذا لمكر مكرتموه في المدينة لتخرجوا منها أهلها فسوف تعلمون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the scope of his prophethood, indicating that he was sent to bring guidance and mercy to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form suggests that the Prophet's message is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims of their responsibility to spread peace, love, and compassion to all people, just as the Prophet did.
orig: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, 'We are tired of our Lord's command. We will not obey.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have become tired of their Lord's command and have decided not to obey it. This verse highlights the element of disobedience and rebellion against God's command. The phrase 'min qalbin' (من قلبي) means 'from our heart' or 'from our soul', indicating that the people have made a conscious decision not to follow God's command, and their disobedience is not due to any external factors. The verse serves as a warning to those who are rebellious and disobedient, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of submitting to God's will.
orig: قالوا إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

translation: And the people of Pharaoh said: 'We will kill Moses and his people, and let their Lord send a successor. We will kill the sons and spare the women, for indeed, we are dominant over them.'
interpretation: The verse describes the arrogance and tyranny of the Pharaoh and his people, who were determined to oppress and kill Moses and his followers. They believed that by doing so, they could prevent the spread of Moses' message and maintain their power and control over the people. The verse highlights the cruelty and injustice of the Pharaoh's regime, which was characterized by oppression, violence, and disregard for human life. It also underscores the theme of resistance and defiance in the face of oppression, as Moses and his people continued to fight for their rights and their faith despite the odds against them.
orig: وقال الملأ من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا في الأرض ويذرك وآلهتك قال سنقتل أبناءهم ونستحيي نساءهم وإنا فوقهم قاهرون

translation: And Moses said to his people, 'Seek help from Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah. He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the end is for the righteous.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is advising his people to seek help from Allah and be patient in the face of adversity. He reminds them that the earth and all its resources belong to Allah, and that He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. The verse emphasizes the idea that the ultimate reward for the righteous is not in this life, but in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their spiritual growth and not to become too attached to the material possessions of this world, as they are only a means to an end, and the true reward is in the hereafter.
orig: قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If thou do not punish us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's recognition of their own sinfulness and their appeal to God for mercy. They acknowledge that they have wronged themselves and ask God not to punish them, suggesting that they are aware of their own accountability for their actions. The verse highlights the importance of self-reflection and recognition of one's own mistakes, as well as the hope for divine mercy and forgiveness.
orig: قالوا أوذينا من قبل أن تأتينا ومن بعد ما جئتنا قال عسى ربكم أن يهلك عدوكم ويستخلفكم في الأرض فينظر كيف تعملون

translation: And indeed, We have taken away the likes of Pharaoh's people with the years and the scarcity of fruits, so that they may remember.
interpretation: The verse mentions the destruction of Pharaoh's people and the scarcity of fruits that they faced as a punishment from God. The verse highlights the purpose of the punishment, which was to make them remember and reflect on their actions and turn back to God. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in arrogance and disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of remembering and turning back to God.
orig: ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And when a favorable wind came to them, they said, 'This is ours, and if a similar calamity should afflict us, we will remain patient.' But then, when they were afflicted by a storm, they turned their faces away and said, 'We have been punished; no one is able to avert the punishment of Allah.' Indeed, they had forgotten about the blessings that had been bestowed upon them, so they became blind to the truth. And most of them do not have knowledge.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of a group of people who were blessed with good fortune, but when a calamity struck, they failed to recognize the blessing and instead attributed their misfortune to God's punishment. The verse highlights the ingratitude and lack of faith of these people, who quickly forgot the favors they had received from God and instead blamed Him for their misfortunes. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and to recognize that both good times and bad times are a test of one's faith and patience. The verse also emphasizes the importance of recognizing the truth and not becoming blind to it, as the people in the verse did.
orig: فإذا جاءتهم الحسنة قالوا لنا هذه وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى ومن معه ألا إنما طائرهم عند الله ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'What sort of a sign do you bring to us that we should follow you?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convince them to follow him. The verse highlights their skepticism and unwillingness to believe in the Prophet's message without concrete evidence. The verse also implies that the disbelievers were not genuinely seeking guidance but were instead trying to test the Prophet's credibility. The verse serves as a reminder that faith cannot be forced upon people and that guidance is only possible through God's will.
orig: وقالوا مهما تأتنا به من آية لتسحرنا بها فما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood, distinct signs, but they were arrogant and became a criminal people.
interpretation: The verse describes the various punishments that were sent upon the people who lived in sin and injustice. The 'flood' refers to a devastating flood that destroyed their homes and crops, the 'locusts' ate their crops, the 'lice' infested their bodies, and the 'frogs' invaded their homes. The 'blood' refers to the blood of the innocent people they killed. The verse emphasizes that these punishments were 'distinct signs' from God, but the people remained arrogant and continued to commit crimes. The verse warns the reader of the consequences of arrogance and the importance of recognizing and heeding God's signs.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم آيات مفصلات فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the anger fell upon them, they said, 'Moses, call upon your Lord to make the punishment lessen for us.' They had said, 'We will believe in you and send with you the Children of Israel.'
interpretation: The verse describes the situation where the Israelites were faced with the wrath of God due to their disobedience. In their desperation, they turn to Moses and ask him to intercede on their behalf, asking God to lessen the punishment. They also express their willingness to believe in Moses and follow him, along with the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the theme of repentance and the importance of seeking God's mercy and forgiveness in times of hardship.
orig: ولما وقع عليهم الرجز قالوا يا موسى ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك ولنرسلن معك بني إسرائيل

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم الرجز إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون

translation: So We took revenge from them and drowned them in the sea, for they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a community that rejected God's signs and was therefore punished. The punishment is described as a drowning in the sea, which symbolizes the complete destruction of the community. The verse emphasizes that the community was warned through God's signs, but they chose to ignore them and were therefore held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and ignore His warnings, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's justice.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم في اليم بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And We have made the people who were oppressed inheritors of the eastern and western lands which We have blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the children of Israel, because they endured patiently. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made, and what they had built.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fulfillment of God's promise to the children of Israel, who were oppressed and patiently endured their suffering. God rewarded them by making them the inheritors of the eastern and western lands, which were blessed by God. The verse also mentions the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, who were punished for their oppression and injustice. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of patience and faith in God's promises, and the consequences of oppression and disobedience.
orig: وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها التي باركنا فيها وتمت كلمت ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا ودمرنا ما كان يصنع فرعون وقومه وما كانوا يعرشون

translation: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols. They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.' He said, 'You are a people who are ignorant. Indeed, those whom they invoke besides Allah will not create a fly, if they were to create a fly, it would not be except a feeble fly, and they will not be able to escape from us.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Children of Israel's journey through the sea and their encounter with a people who were idolaters. The verse highlights the ignorance of the people who were asking Moses to create a god for them, just like the other nations had gods. Moses responds by pointing out the futility of their request, saying that the gods they worship are powerless and cannot even create a fly. The verse emphasizes the uniqueness of Allah and the futility of idolatry, reminding the believers to put their trust only in Allah.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتوا على قوم يعكفون على أصنام لهم قالوا يا موسى اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة قال إنكم قوم تجهلون

translation: Indeed, they have been defeated in their affair, and their deeds have been nullified.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have rejected God's message and have chosen to live in disobedience to His commands. Their defeat is not only in their ultimate failure in the Hereafter, but also in the fact that their deeds have been rendered worthless and void. The verse emphasizes that their actions have not only been unproductive but have also been counterproductive, leading them further away from the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: إن هؤلاء متبر ما هم فيه وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered your partner-gods, those to whom you pray instead of Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth; or have they any share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book before the Qur'an so they are holding onto it?',
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by Allah to challenge the polytheists who worship other deities besides Allah. The verse asks the polytheists to show what their gods have created, either on earth or in the heavens, and whether they have a book revealed to them before the Qur'an. The verse is a challenge to the polytheists to prove the existence and power of their gods, and to show why they should be worshipped instead of Allah. The verse emphasizes the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped and highlights the futility of worshipping other deities.
orig: قال أغير الله أبغيكم إلها وهو فضلكم على العالمين

translation: And indeed, We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, killing your sons and keeping your women alive. That was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Israelites' deliverance from the oppression of the Pharaoh and his people. The verse highlights the severity of their suffering, describing how the Pharaoh's people were killing their sons and keeping their women alive. The verse also emphasizes that this trial was a test from God, demonstrating His power and control over all circumstances. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that God is always watching and testing them, and that He will deliver them from adversity if they have faith and persevere.
orig: وإذ أنجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يقتلون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And We gave Moses a term of thirty nights and completed it with ten more, and he said to his brother Aaron: 'Take my place among my people, and act righteously and do not follow the way of the mischief-makers.'
interpretation: Moses was given a time frame of 30 nights by God to complete his mission, and he was instructed to appoint his brother Aaron as his successor. Moses reminded Aaron to act righteously and not to follow the ways of those who cause corruption and destruction. This verse highlights the importance of leadership and the responsibility that comes with it. It emphasizes the need for leaders to act with justice and righteousness, and to avoid the path of those who seek to cause harm and destruction.
orig: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة وقال موسى لأخيه هارون اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين

translation: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look at You.' He said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.' And when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble and Moses fell down, exhausted. And when he recovered, he said, 'Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance and I am the first of the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the encounter between Moses and God on Mount Sinai. Moses, having been chosen by God to lead the Israelites out of Egypt, requests to see God's manifestation. God agrees, but warns Moses that he will not be able to see Him directly, instead, he will see the effect of God's presence on the mountain. When God reveals Himself to the mountain, it crumbles, symbolizing the power and majesty of God. Moses, overwhelmed by the experience, falls down and later repents, acknowledging God's greatness and his own humility. The verse highlights the importance of humility and submission to God's will, and serves as a reminder of the immense power and majesty of God.
orig: ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا وكلمه ربه قال رب أرني أنظر إليك قال لن تراني ولكن انظر إلى الجبل فإن استقر مكانه فسوف تراني فلما تجلى ربه للجبل جعله دكا وخر موسى صعقا فلما أفاق قال سبحانك تبت إليك وأنا أول المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said: 'O my people! I have been chosen by God to convey His message to you. Take what I have brought you and be grateful.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing his people, the Israelites, and informing them that he has been chosen by God to convey His message to them. Moses is emphasizing the importance of his mission and the significance of the message he has been entrusted with. He is urging his people to accept the message and be grateful for it. The verse highlights the responsibility of prophethood and the importance of being receptive to divine guidance.
orig: قال يا موسى إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but is universal and applicable to all people. The verse highlights the Prophet's role as a mercy, which is not limited to spiritual guidance but also encompasses the well-being and betterment of humanity in all aspects of life. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their faith should be reflected in their actions and that they should strive to spread love, compassion, and mercy to all people, just as the Prophet did.
orig: وكتبنا له في الألواح من كل شيء موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها سأريكم دار الفاسقين

translation: And they reject Our signs, the ones that are clear, and the path of the truth, they do not believe in it, and the path of error, they take it. That is because they gave lie to Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who reject the clear signs of God and choose to follow the path of error instead. The verse suggests that these people are not only rejecting the signs, but also lying about their true nature and ignoring the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in denial of God's signs and serves as a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها وإن يروا سبيل الرشد لا يتخذوه سبيلا وإن يروا سبيل الغي يتخذوه سبيلا ذلك بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have been ruined, so they will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting God's signs and denying the existence of the afterlife. Those who do so will have their deeds rendered worthless and will not be rewarded for their actions. Instead, they will only receive what they have earned in this life, and their ultimate punishment will be in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and worldly pursuits.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة حبطت أعمالهم هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his army followed them in tyranny and enmity until the truth came to them and drowned them while they were still wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of the Israelites' exodus from Egypt and their crossing of the Red Sea. The verse highlights the tyranny and enmity of Pharaoh and his army towards the Israelites, who were led by Moses. The verse also mentions how God's truth and justice prevailed, resulting in the drowning of Pharaoh and his army while they were still engaged in wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and justice, and how He will always stand up for the oppressed and punish the oppressors.
orig: واتخذ قوم موسى من بعده من حليهم عجلا جسدا له خوار ألم يروا أنه لا يكلمهم ولا يهديهم سبيلا اتخذوه وكانوا ظالمين

translation: And when they had provoked their Lord, and killed their prophets, and became certain that they were destroyed, they cried out for mercy, saying, 'If only our Lord show us mercy and forgive us, we will be among the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the people have been warned by their prophets to change their ways and avoid the wrath of God, but they refused to listen and continued to commit injustices. Eventually, they faced the consequences of their actions and realized their mistake, but it was too late. They cried out for mercy, but it was too late, and they were destroyed. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولما سقط في أيديهم ورأوا أنهم قد ضلوا قالوا لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا ويغفر لنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'How wickedly you have acted after my departure! Could you hasten on the order of your Lord?' And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said, 'Son of my mother, indeed the people overpowered me and almost killed me, so do not make me equal to the wicked.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses expresses his anger and sadness upon returning to his people and finding them worshipping a golden calf instead of Allah. He feels betrayed and hurt by their actions, and he throws down the tablets containing the Ten Commandments, symbolizing his frustration and disappointment. He also grabs his brother Aaron by the head and drags him toward him, indicating his anger and disappointment towards Aaron for not stopping the people from worshipping the golden calf. Moses' words to Aaron, 'Son of my mother, indeed the people overpowered me and almost killed me, so do not make me equal to the wicked,' suggest that he feels let down by his own people and feels that they have wronged him. This verse highlights the importance of loyalty and obedience to God's commands, and serves as a reminder that those who disobey God's commands will face consequences.
orig: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us to Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Allah, seeking forgiveness for himself and his brother (Prophet Abraham) and asking Allah to admit them into His mercy. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the belief in the mercy of Allah. It also emphasizes the special relationship between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his brother Prophet Abraham, who were both chosen by Allah for their righteousness and prophethood. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness and to have faith in Allah's mercy, which is a central theme in Islam.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا في رحمتك وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: Indeed, those who have taken their desires as their deity will be punished with humiliation in this world and the Hereafter. Thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood].
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of following one's desires and passions without regard for God's commands. Those who make their desires their god will face humiliation in this life and the hereafter. The verse also implies that those who invent falsehood and follow their own desires will face punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain mindful of God's commands and not to let their desires control their actions.
orig: إن الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا وكذلك نجزي المفترين

translation: And those who have earned evil deeds will be punished for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of accountability and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that those who have committed evil deeds will face punishment, but also emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness. The use of the word 'raghur' (wronged) in the phrase 'and they will not be wronged' implies that the punishment they receive will be just and deserved, rather than an injustice or oppression. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and the consequences of choosing to do evil.
orig: والذين عملوا السيئات ثم تابوا من بعدها وآمنوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Scripture, and We destroyed the former generations, and We gave him an example in their destruction, and how many a generation We have destroyed since Noah's flood.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Scripture given to Moses, which serves as a guidance and a warning for those who are willing to listen. The verse also emphasizes the destructive nature of God's punishment, as seen in the destruction of previous generations, such as the flood of Noah. The use of the word 'example' suggests that the destruction of these generations serves as a lesson for those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب أخذ الألواح وفي نسختها هدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون

translation: And Moses chose seventy men from his people to attend our meeting. When the tremor seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if you had willed, you could have destroyed them before and myself as well. Will you destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? It is but Your test that has brought this upon us. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? Indeed, it is but Your test that has brought this upon us.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is imploring God's mercy and forgiveness for his people, who have been stricken with a tremor as a punishment for their sins. Moses acknowledges that the punishment is a result of their own foolish deeds, but he also recognizes that God's ultimate goal is to test and purify His servants through such trials. Moses' plea for forgiveness and mercy serves as a reminder that even in the face of divine punishment, God's ultimate goal is to guide and forgive those who turn back to Him in repentance and faith.
orig: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقاتنا فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال رب لو شئت أهلكتهم من قبل وإياي أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

translation: And write for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter, indeed, we have turned to You in repentance. O our Lord, have mercy upon us, and have mercy upon our brothers who preceded us in faith and leave not in our hearts rancour towards those who have believed. Indeed, the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, asking for His mercy and guidance in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness, as well as the importance of having a positive relationship with one's brothers and sisters in faith. The verse also mentions the severity of God's punishment for those who reject faith and do not follow His commandments.
orig: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك قال عذابي أصيب به من أشاء ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة والذين هم بآياتنا يؤمنون

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins them to do good and forbids them from evil, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burdens and the shackles which were upon them. Those who believe in him and support him and help him, and follow the light which has been sent down with him, it is they who will be the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the rewards for those who follow him. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is unlettered, indicating that he is not a scholar or a man of knowledge, but rather a man chosen by God to convey His message. The verse also highlights the Prophet's role in guiding people to do good and forbidding them from evil, and how he relieves them of their burdens and shackles. The verse also mentions the reward for those who believe in and support the Prophet, and follow the light that has been sent down with him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of following the Prophet and his teachings, and the rewards that come with it.
orig: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحل لهم الطيبات ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم فالذين آمنوا به وعزروه ونصروه واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [the One] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, there is no deity except Him, He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse is a call to all humanity to believe in the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to accept Allah as the only God. The verse emphasizes the authority and power of Allah, who has dominion over the heavens and the earth, and who gives life and causes death. The verse also emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who is described as 'unlettered' indicating that he was not educated in the classical sense but was chosen by Allah to convey His message. The verse promises guidance for those who believe and follow the Prophet's teachings.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت فآمنوا بالله ورسوله النبي الأمي الذي يؤمن بالله وكلماته واتبعوه لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And from the descendants of Moses' people, a nation was led astray, guiding others with the truth and righteousness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Israelites, who were led astray and deviated from the right path. Despite being the chosen people of God, they failed to uphold the teachings of Moses and instead, became a nation that misguided others. The verse highlights the importance of staying true to one's faith and not letting worldly desires and temptations lead one astray. It also emphasizes the responsibility of religious leaders to guide their followers towards righteousness and truth.
orig: ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And We destroyed the people of the villages, and We sent upon them a fierce wind, and We made the stones of the (destroyed) houses fall upon them, and We drowned them in the sea, for they were unjust. And why did those who were warned not turn away?
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of the people of the villages who were warned by God but refused to turn away from their sins. The verse emphasizes the severity of God's punishment, using vivid imagery to describe the destruction, including a fierce wind, falling stones, and drowning in the sea. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment if they do not turn away from their sins.
orig: وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما وأوحينا إلى موسى إذ استسقاه قومه أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانبجست منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم وظللنا عليهم الغمام وأنزلنا عليهم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And indeed, We have given them a plain commandment, but they have ignored it. They will certainly be questioned about their disobedience.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disobedience of the people who have been given a clear commandment by God but have chosen to ignore it. The verse suggests that they will be held accountable for their disobedience and will be questioned about it on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that God's commandments are not to be taken lightly and that disobedience will have consequences.
orig: وإذ قيل لهم اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها حيث شئتم وقولوا حطة وادخلوا الباب سجدا نغفر لكم خطيئاتكم سنزيد المحسنين

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah. And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you, [the messenger], and asked for forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked for forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's messengers and the consequences of disobedience. The verse also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of God, who is willing to forgive those who repent and seek forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow the teachings of the messengers and to seek forgiveness when they have wronged themselves. It also serves as a warning to those who refuse to obey the messengers and continue to live in sin, that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا منهم قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأرسلنا عليهم رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يظلمون

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they would exceed the limits in the Sabbath, and their punishment came to them on a day of their Sabbath, and they were not warned except that they might return.,
interpretation: The verse refers to a town that was located by the sea and its people were known for their transgression and disobedience, especially on the Sabbath day. They would exceed the limits of what was allowed on the Sabbath and were warned by God to stop their sinful ways, but they refused to listen. As a result, their punishment came to them on a day of their Sabbath, catching them by surprise and serving as a reminder that God's justice will always prevail.
orig: واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر إذ يعدون في السبت إذ تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم كذلك نبلوهم بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when a community among them said, 'Our Lord, we have disobeyed our Lord and have been unjust. If only we had a chance to do good deeds, we would certainly be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about a community that realizes their wrongdoing and seeks forgiveness from God. They acknowledge their disobedience and injustice, and express a desire to do good deeds and be among the righteous. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness, as well as the desire to change one's ways and strive for righteousness.
orig: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of the heavens and the earth, and We showered them with wealth and children, and We made their hearts to grow large and forget My remembrance, and they became a people who were ignoble.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of forgetting God's remembrance and the blessings that come with it. When people forget the message of God, they become disconnected from the divine and lose their way. As a result, they are left open to the temptations of the material world and become consumed by their desires. This leads to a life of ignorance and spiritual poverty, where they forget the true purpose of their existence. The verse serves as a warning to those who have forgotten God's message and are living in ignorance, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: فلما عتوا عن ما نهوا عنه قلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And indeed, your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank, and the hellfire will be brought forth [that day]. Then, your Lord will separate them [into groups] and will acquit them [of their sins] with His knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when God will come with the angels, arrayed in rows, and bring forth hellfire. The verse emphasizes God's power and knowledge, as He will separate the people into groups, judging them with His perfect knowledge. The verse also highlights God's justice and mercy, as He will punish the wicked, but also forgive those who deserve forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human beings and the certainty of the Day of Judgment, encouraging believers to live a righteous life and warning sinners of the consequences of their actions.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربك ليبعثن عليهم إلى يوم القيامة من يسومهم سوء العذاب إن ربك لسريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: And We have destroyed them in the earth, and We have raised up others in their place.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of past nations and the rise of new ones. The verse suggests that the destroyed nations were wicked and that their destruction was a punishment from God. The verse also implies that the new nations that rose up in their place were better and more righteous. The verse serves as a reminder that God has the power to destroy and create nations as He sees fit, and that He will always replace wickedness with goodness.
orig: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, why have you destroyed us before our time?' Say, 'I am not but a warner, and there is no god except Me. I have brought you the truth, but you are not being punished except for what you used to do.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people who were destroyed are asking why they were punished before their time. The prophet responds by saying that he is only a warner and that there is no god except Allah. The prophet is telling them that they were punished because of their own actions and that they should have listened to the message of the prophet. The verse highlights the importance of listening to the message of the prophet and the consequences of not heeding the warning.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And those who are entrusted with the Scripture and the establishment of prayer, indeed, We will not waste the reward of the righteous ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an and prayer in the lives of believers. The phrase 'those who are entrusted with the Scripture' refers to the religious leaders and scholars who are responsible for interpreting and teaching the Qur'an. The phrase 'the establishment of prayer' refers to the obligatory daily prayers that Muslims perform. The verse emphasizes that those who fulfill their religious obligations and live righteously will not have their reward wasted. The verse serves as a reminder to religious leaders and believers to remain committed to their faith and continue to strive for righteousness.
orig: والذين يمسكون بالكتاب وأقاموا الصلاة إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed the like of this town, so it is up to them to acknowledge.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of the town of Sodom and Gomorrah, which was annihilated by God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that the people of the town were warned and had the opportunity to repent, but they refused to do so. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة وظنوا أنه واقع بهم خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, (saying): 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we testify.' (This was) lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: 'Verily, we were unaware of this,'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when God will ask the children of Adam about their relationship with Him. God took a covenant from their ancestors, making them testify that He is their Lord. This covenant was taken to avoid any excuses on the Day of Judgment, where humans might claim they were unaware of God's existence or their responsibility towards Him. The verse highlights the importance of acknowledging God's authority and the consequences of denying it.
orig: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين

translation: Or they say, 'We have been worshiping our Lord from before, and we have been sprung from our forefathers, and we will not be punished.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the response of the disbelievers who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and claim that they have been worshiping their Lord and have a long lineage of ancestors who were also believers. They argue that they will not be punished for their actions because they have been following the traditions of their ancestors. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth and instead rely on their ancestral beliefs and practices. It serves as a warning to them that their lineage and ancestral beliefs will not save them from the punishment of God if they continue to reject the truth.
orig: أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

translation: And indeed, We have divided the verses and sent them down in parts, gradually, in order that they may be reminded and fear Allah, or it may cause their hearts to turn (to Him).
interpretation: The verse explains that the Qur'an has been revealed in parts, over a period of time, to emphasize its importance and to encourage people to reflect and turn to God. The gradual revelation also serves as a reminder to those who have forgotten God and are living in ignorance, to fear Him and change their ways. The verse highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to guide people towards righteousness and to serve as a reminder of the consequences of their actions, ultimately leading them to turn to God and live a life of obedience to Him.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولعلهم يرجعون

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make things clear to them; then God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that all prophets were sent to their respective peoples, speaking their language and cultural context, in order to communicate God's message effectively. The verse also highlights God's sovereignty in guiding and misguiding whom He wills, indicating that the fate of individuals is ultimately in God's hands. The phrase 'the Hearing, the Knowing' reinforces God's omniscience and omnipotence, underscoring the idea that God is fully aware of all things and has complete control over all affairs.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ الذي آتيناه آياتنا فانسلخ منها فأتبعه الشيطان فكان من الغاوين

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience in dealing with sinners. Despite their disobedience, God could have punished them in this life, but instead, He gives them respite, allowing them time to repent and turn back to Him. The verse serves as a warning, reminding sinners that the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe than any punishment in this life. It encourages them to reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness before it's too late.
orig: ولو شئنا لرفعناه بها ولكنه أخلد إلى الأرض واتبع هواه فمثله كمثل الكلب إن تحمل عليه يلهث أو تتركه يلهث ذلك مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فاقصص القصص لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ساء مثلا القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا وأنفسهم كانوا يظلمون

translation: And certainly, [O Muhammad], We have guided you to the truth, and truly, [O Muhammad], We will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a guide and a source of guidance for humanity. The verse highlights the fact that God has guided the Prophet to the truth and will continue to guide him to a straight path, indicating that the Prophet is on a righteous path and is worthy of being followed. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow the teachings of the Prophet and to trust in his guidance, as he is divinely appointed to lead humanity to the truth and to the straight path.
orig: من يهد الله فهو المهتدي ومن يضلل فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many towns and villages, while their people were unaware and heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of ignoring God's signs and being heedless of the warnings. The use of 'jaahil' (ignorant) to describe the people of the destroyed towns emphasizes their lack of understanding and unwillingness to listen to God's message. The phrase 'kala al-an'am' (like cattle) suggests that they were living in ignorance, following their desires without any concern for the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in a state of heedlessness, encouraging them to reflect on their actions and turn back to God before it's too late.
orig: ولقد ذرأنا لجهنم كثيرا من الجن والإنس لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها ولهم آذان لا يسمعون بها أولئك كالأنعام بل هم أضل أولئك هم الغافلون

translation: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave the company of those who practice deviation concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of using the best names of Allah in invocations and prayers, and warns against associating with those who misuse or distort the names of Allah. The verse also implies that the consequences of such actions will be severe, and those who engage in them will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And from among our creation, We have created a community that guides with truth and establishes justice therewith.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the existence of a community that has been created by God to guide humanity towards righteousness and justice. The word 'ummah' in Arabic refers to a community or a nation, and in this context, it refers to the Muslim community. The verse emphasizes the role of this community in guiding others towards the truth and establishing justice in society. The word 'haqq' means truth and 'adl' means justice.
