The verse highlights the importance of the Muslim community's role in upholding justice and righteousness, and serving as a beacon of guidance for humanity.
orig: وممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And those who have lied about Our verses will be brought to account, for their lies, on a Day when their tongues and their hands and their feet will bear witness against them, and they will say, 'This Day, We have no advantage, indeed we are lost',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of denying and lying about God's revelations. On Judgment Day, those who have rejected God's signs will be held accountable and their lies will be exposed. Their tongues, hands, and feet will testify against them, revealing their guilt. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's truth and warns of the certainty of their loss on Judgment Day.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have given them a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the believers. The use of the word 'manifest' emphasizes the clear and obvious nature of the victory, indicating that it was a tangible and undeniable sign of God's favor and support for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their successes are not due to their own strength or efforts, but are a result of God's blessings and mercy.
orig: وأملي لهم إن كيدي متين

translation: And indeed, they had been warned not to worship the sun and the moon, but they became arrogant and were led astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who were warned not to worship the sun and the moon, but they became arrogant and were led astray. The verse highlights the idea that the people were warned against worshiping celestial bodies, but they refused to listen and instead chose to follow their own desires. The verse serves as a reminder that God's warnings should not be ignored, and that arrogance and disobedience can lead to spiritual astrayal.
orig: أولم يتفكروا ما بصاحبهم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير مبين

translation: And have they not looked at the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what Allah has created? Surely, their term is near, so let them have faith.
interpretation: The verse urges people to reflect on the vastness and complexity of the universe and the intricate balance that exists within it. It suggests that the mere observation of the natural world should be enough to convince people of the existence of a higher power and the nearness of their own death. The verse serves as a reminder to people to have faith in God and to live their lives in accordance with His will, as their time on earth is limited and their ultimate fate is fast approaching.
orig: أولم ينظروا في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وما خلق الله من شيء وأن عسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون

translation: And indeed, Allah will not guide the disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God will not guide those who disobey and reject His commands. The word 'disobedient' refers to those who oppose God's will and refuse to follow His guidance. The verse suggests that those who turn away from God's guidance will be left to their own devices and will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's guidance and a reminder that God's punishment is certain for those who disobey.
orig: من يضلل الله فلا هادي له ويذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: They ask you about the Hour: when will it come? Say: 'Knowledge of it is with my Lord, none can reveal its time but He. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth; it will not come to you but suddenly.' They ask you as if you are responsible for it. Say: 'Knowledge of it is with Allah, but most people do not know.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of the Hour of Judgment and the curiosity of people regarding its timing. The Prophet is instructed to respond by saying that the knowledge of the Hour is with God alone and that it will come suddenly, without warning. The verse emphasizes the weight and gravity of the Hour, using the metaphor of its heaviness in the heavens and the earth. The Prophet is also instructed to distance himself from having any knowledge or control over the Hour, emphasizing that the knowledge of it is exclusively with God. The verse highlights the ignorance of the people regarding the Hour and serves as a reminder of the importance of being prepared for the Day of Judgment.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها قل إنما علمها عند ربي لا يجليها لوقتها إلا هو ثقلت في السماوات والأرض لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة يسألونك كأنك حفي عنها قل إنما علمها عند الله ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "I do not possess benefit or harm for myself except what Allah has willed. And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me. Indeed, I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by Allah to inform the people that he does not possess any power to bring benefit or harm to himself, and that he is only a warner and a bringer of good tidings for those who believe. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Prophet's role is not to bring harm or benefit to himself, but rather to convey the message of Allah to the people. The verse also highlights the idea that the Prophet does not possess knowledge of the unseen, and that he is only a human being who is striving to fulfill his duty as a messenger of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to believe in the message of Allah and to follow the guidance brought by the Prophet.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا إلا ما شاء الله ولو كنت أعلم الغيب لاستكثرت من الخير وما مسني السوء إن أنا إلا نذير وبشير لقوم يؤمنون

translation: It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate, and He created from them eight pairs of cattle. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord, to whom belongs the dominion. There is no deity except Him. How then are you turned away?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and majesty of Allah as the sole creator of the universe and all that exists within it. It highlights the miraculous nature of His creation, particularly in the formation of human beings, who are created from a single soul and its mate. The verse also underscores the darkness and helplessness of human beings in their mother's womb, emphasizing their dependence on Allah for their very existence. The verse concludes by emphasizing the unity and uniqueness of Allah, and the futility of worshiping any other deity besides Him.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وجعل منها زوجها ليسكن إليها فلما تغشاها حملت حملا خفيفا فمرت به فلما أثقلت دعوا الله ربهما لئن آتيتنا صالحا لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما آتاهما صالحا جعلا له شركاء فيما آتاهما فتعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with the true appraisal, for they have not created anything, and they are themselves created.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ingratitude of those who refuse to acknowledge and appreciate Allah's power and majesty. Despite being created by Allah, they fail to recognize and give due credit to their Creator. Instead, they attribute their existence and the creation of the universe to other factors or beings, thereby showing a lack of appreciation and gratitude towards Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that everything in existence is a creation of Allah, and that He alone deserves to be praised and worshipped.
orig: أيشركون ما لا يخلق شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: And they cannot escape from Us, for We have surrounded them from all sides, and their ears will not be able to hear any sound, and their eyes will not be able to see any way out.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the complete and total control of God over the sinners, who are unable to escape His punishment. The use of the phrase 'from all sides' suggests a sense of being surrounded and trapped, with no way out. The image of the sinners' ears being unable to hear any sound and their eyes being unable to see any way out adds to the sense of helplessness and despair. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and control over all things, and the inevitability of His justice being carried out.
orig: ولا يستطيعون لهم نصرا ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. Indeed, they will follow their own desires, and whoever follows his desire does not obey you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of trying to guide those who are not willing to listen. Despite the best efforts of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to guide his people, they refused to listen and instead followed their own desires. The verse emphasizes the importance of not forcing one's beliefs on others, as people have the freedom to choose their own path. It also serves as a reminder to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers to focus on their own actions and not be deterred by the disbelief of others.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يتبعوكم سواء عليكم أدعوتموهم أم أنتم صامتون

translation: Indeed, those who call upon other than Allah are servants, just like you. So, call upon them and let them answer you, for you are truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that those who worship other deities besides Allah are still His servants, just like the believers. However, they are misguided and have not yet recognized the truth. The verse encourages the believers to call upon them and invite them to the right path, with the hope that they will respond and accept the truth. The phrase 'you are truthful ones' underscores the importance of sincerity and honesty in the call to faith, and serves as a reminder that the believers should always strive to be truthful in their words and actions.
orig: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألهم أرجل يمشون بها أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها أم لهم أعين يبصرون بها أم لهم آذان يسمعون بها قل ادعوا شركاءكم ثم كيدون فلا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, my Lord is Allah, who revealed the Book, and He takes care of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the close relationship between God and the righteous. The use of the personal pronoun 'my Lord' suggests a strong connection between the speaker and God, indicating a deep level of faith and trust. The phrase 'who revealed the Book' highlights God's role as the source of guidance and wisdom. The verse also underscores God's protection and care for the righteous, indicating that those who live a virtuous life can expect God's support and blessings.
orig: إن وليي الله الذي نزل الكتاب وهو يتولى الصالحين

translation: And those who call upon others besides Allah cannot help them, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of seeking help from anyone or anything other than Allah. It highlights the fact that those who seek help from others than Allah are unable to help themselves, and that true help and support come only from Allah. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to put their trust in Allah and to seek help only from Him, for He is the only one who can provide true assistance and guidance.
orig: والذين تدعون من دونه لا يستطيعون نصركم ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to fabricate something other than the truth. But had they succeeded, they would have taken you as a friend, and they would have been led astray, distant [from the right path].
interpretation: The verse highlights the attempts of the disbelievers to mislead the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and lead him astray from the truth revealed to him by Allah. They tried to tempt him into fabricating a different message, one that would be more appealing to their own desires and beliefs. The verse emphasizes the danger of yielding to such temptations and the importance of staying true to the divine message, as deviation from it would result in spiritual loss and misguidance.
orig: وإن تدعوهم إلى الهدى لا يسمعوا وتراهم ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

translation: And indeed, Satan will whisper to them, so encouraging them to forgetfulness.
interpretation: The verse mentions how Satan whispers to people, trying to distract them from the remembrance of God and lead them astray. The verse serves as a warning to believers, reminding them to be mindful of Satan's tricks and to seek refuge in God, who is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه سميع عليم

translation: Indeed, those who fear Allah - when a thought of evil from Satan assails them, they remember [their Lord] and at once they have insight.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of the righteous, who, when faced with temptation or evil thoughts, immediately remember Allah and turn to Him for guidance. The phrase 'thought of evil from Satan' refers to the whisperings of Satan, which can take many forms, including temptations, doubts, and evil suggestions. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah in such moments and seeking His guidance, leading to a deeper spiritual insight and protection from the evil of Satan.
orig: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون

translation: And We have destroyed many a generation before them, who surpassed them in riches and in glory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who were more prosperous and glorious than the current generation. The verse serves as a reminder that material wealth and worldly success are not a guarantee of salvation or protection from God's punishment. It also highlights the idea that every generation will face its own unique challenges and trials, and that the destruction of previous generations should serve as a lesson for the current generation to turn back to God and live righteously.
orig: وإخوانهم يمدونهم في الغي ثم لا يقصرون

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, 'We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of God are given.' God knows best where to place His message. Humiliation will befall them in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe. They will be told, 'Taste the punishment of burning!',
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who demand to receive the same signs and miracles that were given to the messengers of God. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of where to place His message and that the disbelievers will be humiliated in this life and will face a severe punishment in the Hereafter. The verse warns the disbelievers of the consequences of their disbelief and encourages them to accept the message of God's prophets.
orig: وإذا لم تأتهم بآية قالوا لولا اجتبيتها قل إنما أتبع ما يوحى إلي من ربي هذا بصائر من ربكم وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And when We read the Qur'an, listen to it and pay attention, lest you receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of listening to the Qur'an with attention and reverence, and not just hearing it casually or superficially. The verse indicates that listening to the Qur'an can bring mercy and blessings to the listener, and that it is a means of receiving guidance and wisdom from God. The verse encourages the believers to approach the Qur'an with humility, openness, and a willingness to learn and be transformed by its message.
orig: وإذا قرئ القرآن فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, and be humble and submissive, and whisper a prayer, and do not be of the neglectful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying God in all aspects of life. It encourages the believers to have a strong connection with God by being humble, submissive, and mindful of their prayers. The verse also warns against neglecting one's relationship with God and encourages a consistent and sincere practice of faith. The phrase 'do not be of the neglectful' serves as a reminder that neglecting one's spiritual duties can lead to spiritual decay and punishment.
orig: واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال ولا تكن من الغافلين

translation: Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not become arrogant because of His worship, and they declare His greatness and prostrate to Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the humility and humbleness of those who are close to God. They do not feel proud or arrogant because of their worship, instead, they glorify and praise God, acknowledging His greatness and submitting themselves to Him. The verse highlights the importance of humility in worship and the relationship between the creature and the Creator, emphasizing that true worship requires a deep sense of humility and submission.
orig: إن الذين عند ربك لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه وله يسجدون

translation: They ask you about the spoils of war. Say, 'The spoils of war belong to God and the Messenger.' Fear God and set things right among yourselves. Obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of spoils of war and provides clear guidance on their distribution. The verse states that the spoils belong to God and the Messenger, indicating that they should be used for the common good and not be appropriated by individuals. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing God and setting things right among the community, indicating that justice and fairness should be upheld in the distribution of the spoils. Additionally, the verse reminds the believers to obey God and His Messenger, emphasizing the importance of submitting to God's will and following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: يسألونك عن الأنفال قل الأنفال لله والرسول فاتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم وأطيعوا الله ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Indeed, the believers who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, their faith increases, and they rely upon their Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristic of true believers. When they hear the name of Allah, their hearts tremble with fear and reverence, and when they listen to the verses of the Qur'an, their faith is strengthened. They put their trust in Allah and rely on Him, demonstrating their belief in His power and providence. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong faith and a close relationship with Allah, which is the foundation of a believer's spiritual growth and development.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who establish the prayer and give the zakat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of establishing the daily prayers and giving zakat (charity) as a means of purifying one's soul and demonstrating obedience to God. The verse emphasizes that those who prioritize their spiritual growth through prayer and charity will be rewarded with a direct connection to God, as indicated by the phrase 'ينفقون' (they will be given). The verse serves as a reminder that spiritual growth and closeness to God are not achieved through material wealth or worldly success, but rather through consistent effort in prayer and charity.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: Those are the believers who have truly believed in their Lord and have received ranks near to Him, and forgiveness, and a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse highlights the characteristics of true believers, who have genuinely submitted to God and have earned a high rank in His sight. They have received forgiveness for their sins and have been blessed with a generous provision in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and its rewards, encouraging believers to strive for a closer relationship with God and to live a righteous life.
orig: أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم درجات عند ربهم ومغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And your Lord inspired to the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. Indeed, I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved. Therefore, strike upon their necks and strike from them every fingertip.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers were facing opposition from the disbelievers, and God commanded the angels to support the believers and strike fear into the hearts of the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the power of faith and the importance of standing up for what is right, even in the face of adversity. The phrase 'strike upon their necks' is a metaphor for the defeat of the disbelievers and the supremacy of the believers. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always with those who believe in Him and that He will support them in their struggles.
orig: كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق وإن فريقا من المؤمنين لكارهون

translation: They dispute with you in the truth after it has become clear, as if they are being driven to death while they are looking on.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where people are arguing with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) despite the clear evidence of the truth of his message. The verse suggests that they are resisting the truth and are unwilling to accept it, even though it is plainly obvious. The image of being driven to death while watching suggests a sense of inevitability and a lack of control, emphasizing the idea that resistance to the truth is futile.
orig: يجادلونك في الحق بعدما تبين كأنما يساقون إلى الموت وهم ينظرون

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid you with a mighty victory. And many a prophet has desired the victory that you desired, but it was not given to them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the promise of God's aid and victory for the believers. The verse emphasizes that God's help is not limited to any particular prophet or group of people, but is available to all who seek it. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and wisdom in granting victory to whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is always with them and will help them in their struggles, and that they should have faith in His plan and timeline.
orig: وإذ يعدكم الله إحدى الطائفتين أنها لكم وتودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم ويريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته ويقطع دابر الكافرين

translation: And the truth is confirmed, and the falsehood is vanquished. Indeed, the criminals will be brought to despair.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood and the punishment that awaits those who engage in criminal behavior. The phrase 'the truth is confirmed' suggests that what is right and just will ultimately prevail, while 'the falsehood is vanquished' indicates that anything opposed to the truth will be defeated. The final phrase, 'the criminals will be brought to despair', serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing, reminding them that their actions will lead to sorrow and regret.
orig: ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل ولو كره المجرمون

translation: When you sought help from your Lord, He responded to you, 'I will support you with a thousand angels in succession.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the support and assistance that God provides to those who seek His help. The verse emphasizes the magnitude of God's power and the extent of His support, using the imagery of a thousand angels marching in succession. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always ready to help those who turn to Him in faith and that His support is limitless and all-encompassing.
orig: إذ تستغيثون ربكم فاستجاب لكم أني ممدكم بألف من الملائكة مردفين

translation: And Allah would not have made it but as a mercy to you and to reassure your hearts, and the victory is not but from Allah, indeed Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the blessings and victories that believers receive are not because of their own strength or power, but rather because of Allah's mercy and grace. The phrase 'And Allah would not have made it but as a mercy to you' suggests that Allah's primary intention in bestowing these blessings is to bring comfort and reassurance to the believers' hearts. The phrase 'and the victory is not but from Allah' serves as a reminder that ultimate success and victory come from Allah alone, and that believers should not attribute their successes to their own efforts or abilities. The verse ends with 'indeed Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise', emphasizing Allah's greatness and wisdom in all His actions.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى ولتطمئن به قلوبكم وما النصر إلا من عند الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: When the punishment descends upon them, they will be overwhelmed by it, and they will not be able to escape it. The heavens will be closed off to them, and the earth will be tightened around them, and their coverings will be tied up over their hearts, and they will be unable to hear anything.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The punishment referred to in the verse is not limited to physical punishment but also spiritual and psychological. The heavens being closed off means that they will be cut off from God's mercy and grace, and the earth being tightened around them signifies that they will be trapped in their own sins and unable to escape the consequences. The covering tied up over their hearts symbolizes the hardening of their hearts and their inability to hear or understand the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face.
orig: إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام

translation: And when your Lord revealed to the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved. Therefore, strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip.
interpretation: The verse describes a revelation from God to the angels, in which God announces His support for the believers and His plan to cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers. The verse then commands the believers to strike the disbelievers above the necks and cut off their fingertips. This verse is often interpreted as a call to arms against the enemies of God and a reminder that God is always with the believers, supporting and protecting them.
orig: إذ يوحي ربك إلى الملائكة أني معكم فثبتوا الذين آمنوا سألقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب فاضربوا فوق الأعناق واضربوا منهم كل بنان

translation: Those who have been excessive in their dispute with Allah and His Messenger will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who have been excessive in their dispute with Allah and His Messenger, indicating that they have gone too far in their disobedience and rebellion against God's commandments. The verse implies that such individuals will face a painful punishment, emphasizing the severity of their actions and the certainty of God's retribution. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in defiance of God's commands, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of submitting to God's will.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاقق الله ورسوله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Therefore, taste [the punishment] and (know) that the disbelievers will have the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty and severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message. The use of the word 'taste' suggests a tangible and personal experience of the punishment, implying that it will be a direct consequence of their disbelief. The phrase 'the disbelievers will have the punishment of the Fire' underscores the idea that the punishment is not only a consequence of their actions, but also a manifestation of God's justice and judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to turn towards God before it is too late.
orig: ذلكم فذوقوه وأن للكافرين عذاب النار

translation: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve, marching in rows, do not turn to them the backs of your hands [in flight].
interpretation: In this verse, believers are commanded not to turn their backs in flight when they encounter disbelievers in battle. This verse emphasizes the importance of standing firm and maintaining one's ground in the face of adversity. It also highlights the importance of faith and courage in the face of opposition, and serves as a reminder that true believers should not be deterred by the strength or numbers of their enemies.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم الذين كفروا زحفا فلا تولوهم الأدبار

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: The verse warns those who turn away from God's remembrance, that they will have a depressed life and will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection blind. The verse implies that those who ignore God's message and do not live according to His commands will face a difficult life and will be punished in the afterlife. The phrase 'depressed life' suggests a life of hardship and struggle, while 'gathered on the Day of Resurrection blind' implies that they will be unable to see the truth and will be blind to the reality of their situation. The verse serves as a warning to those who ignore God's message and encourages them to turn back to Him and live according to His will.
orig: ومن يولهم يومئذ دبره إلا متحرفا لقتال أو متحيزا إلى فئة فقد باء بغضب من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: And they did not kill him, but Allah killed him. And if they had killed him, it would have been a blessing for them, but Allah raised him up to Himself. And indeed, Allah is listening and knowledgeable.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the Israelites and their prophet, whom they tried to kill, but God intervened and saved him. The verse emphasizes that the prophet's death would have been a blessing for the Israelites, but God had other plans and raised him up to Himself. The verse highlights God's power and knowledge, reminding believers that God is always listening and aware of all things.
orig: فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى وليبلي المؤمنين منه بلاء حسنا إن الله سميع عليم

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of supporting God's cause and striving for justice and righteousness. The phrase 'Allah will aid those who aid His cause' suggests that those who work towards promoting justice and righteousness will receive divine assistance and support. The description of God as 'Powerful and Exalted in Might' underscores God's ability to help and support those who strive for His cause, and serves as a reminder of God's power and authority.
orig: ذلكم وأن الله موهن كيد الكافرين

translation: Indeed, We have opened for you the gates of victory, and if you disobey, it is better for you. And obedience is better for you, and indeed, Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and advantages that come with following God's commands and being obedient to Him. The verse emphasizes that disobedience leads to negative consequences, while obedience brings blessings and God's favor. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is with the believers' serves as a reminder that God is always on the side of those who believe and follow His teachings, and that they can rely on His support and guidance in times of need.
orig: إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح وإن تنتهوا فهو خير لكم وإن تعودوا نعد ولن تغني عنكم فئتكم شيئا ولو كثرت وأن الله مع المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not oppose him, and listen (to the Prophet).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger. The use of the word 'taqwa' (piety) suggests that this obedience is not just outward, but also involves a deep sense of fear and reverence for God. The verse also emphasizes the importance of listening to the Prophet, indicating that hearing and heeding his words is a fundamental aspect of faith. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain mindful of their relationship with God and to follow the guidance of the Prophet in all aspects of their lives.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه وأنتم تسمعون

translation: And do not be like those who said, 'We have heard,' but they did not listen.
interpretation: The verse warns against mere lip service, where people claim to have heard God's message, but their actions do not reflect their words. It emphasizes the importance of not just hearing, but also listening and acting upon God's commands. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and to live according to God's teachings, rather than just giving lip service to their faith.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين قالوا سمعنا وهم لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of being deaf and dumb, not only in the physical sense but also in the spiritual and intellectual sense. It implies that those who are spiritually and intellectually inactive, and fail to use their reasoning faculties to comprehend and reflect on the signs of God, are considered the worst of living creatures in the eyes of God. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate a deep sense of spirituality and intellect, and to use their faculties of reason to recognize and appreciate the beauty and wisdom of God's creation.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الصم البكم الذين لا يعقلون

translation: And if God were to impose blame on angels, the heavens and the earth and those in them would be destroyed. Indeed, We have sent you [O Muhammad] as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner, that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor Him and respect Him [as He deserves to be respected] and glorify Him [with praise] morning and afternoon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority, indicating that even the angels, who are considered pure and righteous, are not immune to God's punishment if they were to disobey or rebel. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness, bearer of good news, and warner, reminding the believers to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, honor and respect Him, and glorify Him morning and afternoon, indicating the importance of constant remembrance and praise of Allah.
orig: ولو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم ولو أسمعهم لتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of responding to God's call and the Messenger's invitation to righteousness. The phrase 'that which gives you life' refers to the guidance and wisdom that comes from following God's commandments. The verse also highlights God's power and control over all things, including the ability to intervene between a person's thoughts and feelings, and the ultimate accountability to Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and to stay on the path of righteousness, as they will ultimately be answerable to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه وأنه إليه تحشرون

translation: And fear a trial which will not afflict the unjust among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to fear a trial that will not spare the unjust among them. The verse implies that the punishment will be severe and will not discriminate between the guilty and the innocent. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid injustice, as Allah's punishment is severe and certain.
orig: واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة واعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And remember when you were few in number, oppressed in the land, fearing that the people would snatch you away, and Allah gave you victory and relief.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of their past state of weakness and oppression, when they were a small minority and feared persecution from their enemies. However, God intervened and gave them victory and relief, demonstrating His power and care for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and protection, and encourages the believers to be grateful for His blessings and to trust in His plan.
orig: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض تخافون أن يتخطفكم الناس فآواكم وأيدكم بنصره ورزقكم من الطيبات لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [the consequence].
interpretation: This verse admonishes believers not to betray God and His Messenger, and not to betray the trusts that have been given to them. The verse emphasizes the importance of being truthful and faithful, and warns against the consequences of betrayal, which can lead to spiritual and moral decay. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay true to their faith and values, and to always act with integrity and honesty.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم وأنتم تعلمون

translation: Know that your wealth and your children are a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse reminds believers that wealth and children are a test from God, and that they should not be consumed by them. Instead, they should focus on pleasing God and seeking His reward, which is far greater than any material possessions or worldly success. The verse encourages believers to keep their priorities straight and not to let material possessions distract them from their ultimate goal of attaining God's pleasure and reward in the Hereafter.
orig: واعلموا أنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة وأن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and let the promise of Allah be a lesson for you. Indeed, the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, encouraging them to fear Allah and to take the promise of Allah as a lesson. The verse highlights the severity of Allah's punishment, indicating that those who disobey Allah will face severe consequences. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain mindful of their actions and to live in accordance with Allah's commandments, in order to avoid His punishment.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا ويكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويغفر لكم والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve conspire against you to restrain you or kill you or evict you. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the conspiracy of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. The disbelievers sought to restrain, kill or expel the Muslims. However, the verse reminds us that Allah is the best of planners and that His plan will ultimately prevail. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that they should not fear the plots of their enemies, but rather, they should trust in Allah's plan and His ability to protect and guide them.
orig: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ليثبتوك أو يقتلوك أو يخرجوك ويمكرون ويمكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we willed, we could have spoken like this. This is not but ancient fables.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they are reminded of God's signs and verses. They respond by saying that they have heard the verses before and that they could have easily come up with similar stories themselves. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who refuse to accept the truth and instead choose to dismiss it as old fables or myths. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and false beliefs.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا قالوا قد سمعنا لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And when they said, 'Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring upon us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the truth of the Prophet Muhammad's message. They challenged God to either rain down stones from the sky or bring a painful punishment upon them if the message was indeed from Him. The verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of the disbelievers, who refused to accept the truth and instead chose to mock and challenge God's power. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the certainty of His punishment for those who refuse to believe.
orig: وإذ قالوا اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء أو ائتنا بعذاب أليم

translation: And had Allah not been angry with them, He would have punished them in this world, and their punishment in the Hereafter will be greater. Indeed, they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the punishment that the wicked will face in the afterlife will be far worse than any punishment they might have faced in this life. The fact that God did not destroy them in this life was not out of mercy, but rather a sign of His anger and a warning to them to change their ways. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that the consequences of their actions will be far more severe in the afterlife.
orig: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون

translation: And they had no excuse not to fear Allah and to defend the sacred mosque, and they were not its guardians. Indeed, the guardians of the mosque are only the righteous, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the failure of the people to defend the sacred mosque and their lack of fear of Allah's punishment. The verse emphasizes that the guardians of the mosque are only the righteous, indicating that those who are not righteous have no right to protect the mosque. The verse also suggests that the people's ignorance of their responsibilities and their lack of fear of Allah's punishment are the reasons for their failure to defend the mosque. The verse serves as a warning to those who are not righteous, reminding them of their accountability to God and the consequences of their actions.
orig: وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله وهم يصدون عن المسجد الحرام وما كانوا أولياءه إن أولياؤه إلا المتقون ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And their prayer at the House of Allah was nothing but whistling and hand-clapping, so taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: The verse describes the hypocrites' insincere prayer at the Kaaba, which was devoid of any real faith or devotion. Instead of being a sincere act of worship, their prayer was nothing more than a performative act, characterized by whistling and hand-clapping. The verse warns that those who mock God's signs and reject faith will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it, then it will be to their own loss, then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of disbelievers' attempts to hinder the spread of Islam and their eventual fate. They spend their wealth to mislead others and resist the truth, but ultimately, their efforts will be in vain, and they will face destruction. The verse emphasizes that their wealth and efforts will be of no use, and they will be gathered in Hell, where they will suffer eternal punishment.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينفقون أموالهم ليصدوا عن سبيل الله فسينفقونها ثم تكون عليهم حسرة ثم يغلبون والذين كفروا إلى جهنم يحشرون

translation: Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah will surely grant them enjoyment and be pleased with them, and they with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for believers who lead a righteous life. The phrase 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' refers to a state of utmost happiness and joy in the afterlife. The phrase 'Allah will surely grant them enjoyment and be pleased with them, and they with Him' indicates a state of mutual love and satisfaction between God and the believers. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing God and living a life according to His commandments in order to attain this reward.
orig: ليميز الله الخبيث من الطيب ويجعل الخبيث بعضه على بعض فيركمه جميعا فيجعله في جهنم أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say to those who have disbelieved, that if they cease, what has past will be forgiven, and if they return, then what has passed has passed.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers, urging them to stop their disbelief and embrace Islam. The verse promises that if they cease their disbelief, their past sins will be forgiven, and if they return to their previous state of disbelief, they will be punished for their past actions. The verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and encourages the disbelievers to repent and turn to God. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the past cannot be changed, and that the only way to escape punishment is to embrace Islam and live a righteous life.
orig: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنت الأولين

translation: And fight them until there is no fitna and the religion is entirely for Allah.
interpretation: The verse commands Muslims to fight against non-believers until there is no fitna (disbelief, polytheism, or oppression) and the religion (way of life) is entirely for Allah. This means that Muslims must strive to establish a society where God's sovereignty is acknowledged and His commandments are followed. The verse emphasizes the importance of fighting against forces that seek to undermine the dominance of Allah's religion, and ensuring that Allah's laws are upheld in every aspect of life. The verse serves as a reminder that the ultimate goal of a Muslim's life is to live according to Allah's will and to establish a society that reflects His commandments.
orig: وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة ويكون الدين كله لله فإن انتهوا فإن الله بما يعملون بصير

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the special status and responsibility that comes with being a human being, and serves as a reminder that humans are accountable to God for their actions. The verse also underscores the idea that humans are not like other creatures, but are unique in their ability to choose between right and wrong and to strive for righteousness.
orig: وإن تولوا فاعلموا أن الله مولاكم نعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: And know that whatever you have been given is but a provision for this life, and that Allah will reward you for what you used to do, and that He will requite you for the good you did, and the evil you did, and that Allah is over all things Capable.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the temporary nature of the wealth and possessions that people have in this life, and that they will be rewarded or punished based on their actions in the afterlife. The verse also highlights the idea that God is all-capable and has control over all things, and that He will ultimately judge and reward or punish people based on their deeds.
orig: واعلموا أنما غنمتم من شيء فأن لله خمسه وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل إن كنتم آمنتم بالله وما أنزلنا على عبدنا يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, you are in an open conflict with the disbelievers, and they are ever plotting against you [O Muhammad], and they say, 'When will he [the punishment] be?', but I will inform you not to fear them. Indeed, Allah will finish the matter entirely, and indeed, Allah will not break His promise. Indeed, a group of My servants He has created will inherit the earth, and indeed, I will give them enjoyment [in this life] and will surely let them enjoy My provision. And indeed, I will protect them from the evil of the enemy. And indeed, I will bring them out from the darkness into the light, and indeed, they will be Mine, and indeed, I will be theirs. And indeed, My chosen servants will be victorious, and indeed, they will be honored in this world and in the Hereafter, and indeed, they will be safe from the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the conflict between the believers and the disbelievers, with the latter plotting against the former. The verse reassures the believers that they should not fear the disbelievers, as Allah will ultimately punish them. The verse also mentions that a group of Allah's servants will inherit the earth and enjoy His provision. Allah will protect them from the evil of their enemies and bring them out of darkness and into the light. The verse also mentions that the believers will be victorious and honored in this world and the Hereafter, and will be safe from the punishment of the Fire.
orig: إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى والركب أسفل منكم ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا ليهلك من هلك عن بينة ويحيى من حي عن بينة وإن الله لسميع عليم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your examples of the past, so how (will you be reminded) if at all you are to be reminded?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers, reminding them that God has destroyed many nations before them as a punishment for their sins. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of these nations serves as an example for those who are living in sin, and that they should take heed of the warning and repent before it is too late. The verse also highlights the arrogance of the disbelievers, who despite seeing the destruction of others, still refuse to believe and continue to argue against the prophets. The verse ends by emphasizing that God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of all things, and that He will indeed punish those who reject His message.
orig: إذ يريكهم الله في منامك قليلا ولو أراكهم كثيرا لفشلتم ولتنازعتم في الأمر ولكن الله سلم إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you did not pass by the destruction, so that you might reflect.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) opponents, who were skeptical of his message and denied the idea of resurrection. The verse reminds them that God has destroyed entire nations in the past, but their destruction was not a lesson for them. They did not reflect on their own destruction, nor did they learn from it. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that God's punishment is certain and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإذ يريكموهم إذ التقيتم في أعينكم قليلا ويقللكم في أعينهم ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who have believed, when you encounter a band of disbelievers, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, encouraging them to remain steadfast and remember Allah frequently when facing adversity, specifically when encountering disbelievers. The remembrance of Allah is emphasized as a means of attaining success and achieving victory over one's enemies. The verse highlights the importance of faith and the reliance on Allah in times of hardship, promoting resilience and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا لقيتم فئة فاثبتوا واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart, and be patient, indeed Allah is with the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and the Prophet (peace be upon him). It warns against disputing and arguing among believers, as it can lead to a loss of strength and courage. Instead, believers are encouraged to be patient and persevering, as God is with those who are patient and will reward them for their steadfastness.
orig: وأطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تنازعوا فتفشلوا وتذهب ريحكم واصبروا إن الله مع الصابرين

translation: And do not be like those who forgot God, so He caused them to forget themselves. They are the ones who are destroying their own souls, and they do not even realize it.
interpretation: The verse warns against forgetting God and neglecting one's spiritual well-being. When individuals forget God, they become disconnected from their spiritual selves and may engage in harmful behaviors that ultimately lead to their own downfall. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and remembering God in all aspects of life, as it is the key to spiritual health and well-being. The verse also highlights the severity of the consequences of neglecting one's spirituality, as it can lead to self-destruction and the loss of one's soul.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين خرجوا من ديارهم بطرا ورئاء الناس ويصدون عن سبيل الله والله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And indeed, Satan made their deeds appealing to them and said, 'No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector.' But when the two armies saw each other, he turned on his heels and said, 'Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the battle between the believers and the disbelievers, where Satan, who had been supporting the disbelievers, suddenly abandons them and flees, realizing that his efforts are futile. The verse emphasizes the idea that Satan's support is unreliable and that true protection comes only from God. The phrase 'I fear Allah' suggests that Satan has come to recognize the power and authority of God and is afraid of His punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to put their trust in God alone and not to rely on temporal powers or alliances.
orig: وإذ زين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم وقال لا غالب لكم اليوم من الناس وإني جار لكم فلما تراءت الفئتان نكص على عقبيه وقال إني بريء منكم إني أرى ما لا ترون إني أخاف الله والله شديد العقاب

translation: And the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is sickness said, 'These people, their religion has deceived them.' But whoever puts their trust in Allah will find that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the criticism of the hypocrites and those with sickness in their hearts towards the believers, who have put their trust in Allah. The critics claim that the believers have been deceived by their religion. However, the verse assures that those who put their trust in Allah will find that Allah is All-Powerful and All-Wise, and that their faith will be rewarded.
orig: إذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض غر هؤلاء دينهم ومن يتوكل على الله فإن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And if you could see when the angels take the souls of the disbelievers, striking their faces and their backs, saying, 'Taste the punishment of the burning fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the angels taking the souls of the disbelievers and infidels, and how they will be punished in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the physical and emotional suffering that the disbelievers will endure in hell, where they will be burned by fire and experience unbearable pain. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face in the afterlife.
orig: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And the people of Pharaoh and those before them had denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's signs and messengers. The people of Pharaoh, who were known for their arrogance and disbelief, denied the signs of God and refused to believe in Moses' message. As a result, God punished them severely, drowning them in the Red Sea. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions. It also emphasizes God's power and authority, demonstrating that He will not tolerate disobedience and will punish those who reject His signs.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كفروا بآيات الله فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم إن الله قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change their own condition, and indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God will not change the fate of a people until they change their own ways. The verse suggests that the people have the power to change their own condition by turning to God and living righteously. The verse also emphasizes God's attribute of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, indicating that He is aware of all that humans do and that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that humans have the agency to change their own lives and that God is always watching and aware of their actions.
orig: ذلك بأن الله لم يك مغيرا نعمة أنعمها على قوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وأن الله سميع عليم

translation: And the people of Pharaoh and those before them had denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and drowned the people of Pharaoh, for they were unjust.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the people of Pharaoh and those who came before them, who denied the signs of their Lord. The verse emphasizes that their denial of God's signs led to their destruction, and that they were punished for their sins. The verse also highlights the severity of their punishment, as they were not only destroyed but also drowned, emphasizing the power and wrath of God. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny God's signs and reject His message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآيات ربهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأغرقنا آل فرعون وكل كانوا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of disbelief and the gravity of rejecting faith in Allah. The 'worst of living creatures' refers to those who are deaf and dumb, not in a physical sense, but in their inability to hear and respond to Allah's message. Their lack of faith renders them spiritually lifeless and unresponsive to the truth. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: إن شر الدواب عند الله الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And those who have made a covenant with Him, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear the consequences.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have made a covenant with God, promising to follow His commandments and live according to His will. However, they repeatedly break their covenant, disobeying God's commands and showing no fear of the consequences. This verse highlights the gravity of breaking one's covenant with God and the importance of living up to one's promises and commitments.
orig: الذين عاهدت منهم ثم ينقضون عهدهم في كل مرة وهم لا يتقون

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks until, when you have subdued them, you may bind them as prisoners, and thereafter either set them free as a favor or by taking ransom, until the war lays down its burdens.
interpretation: The verse is speaking about the treatment of prisoners of war. The verse commands the believers to strike the necks of the disbelievers until they are subdued, and then to bind them as prisoners. The verse then gives two options: either to set them free as a favor or to take ransom from them. The verse emphasizes the idea of subduing the enemy and gaining control over them, rather than killing them. It also highlights the importance of treating prisoners of war with compassion and respect, and giving them the option to be set free or to pay ransom. The verse serves as a reminder that war should not be about killing or oppressing others, but about establishing justice and peace.
orig: فإما تثقفنهم في الحرب فشرد بهم من خلفهم لعلهم يذكرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سواء إن الله لا يحب الخائنين

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think that they will escape. Indeed, they will not cause failure [to God's plan].
interpretation: The verse addresses those who reject God's message and plan, reassuring them that their disbelief and actions will not hinder God's will. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things, reminding the disbelievers that their attempts to resist or escape God's plan are futile. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the certainty of God's victory over those who oppose Him.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون

translation: And prepare against them whatever you can of power and of tying up horses and foot soldiers and others from them, that you may frighten the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know, whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to prepare and mobilize their resources, including military power and manpower, to defend themselves against their enemies, who are also the enemies of Allah. The verse emphasizes that the preparation should be done in the cause of Allah, and that whatever is spent in this cause will be repaid, and the believers will not be wronged. The verse also highlights the importance of being prepared and vigilant against unknown enemies, indicating that Allah is aware of their plans and will support the believers in their struggle.
orig: وأعدوا لهم ما استطعتم من قوة ومن رباط الخيل ترهبون به عدو الله وعدوكم وآخرين من دونهم لا تعلمونهم الله يعلمهم وما تنفقوا من شيء في سبيل الله يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to fabricate something other than the truth. But had they succeeded, they would have taken you as a friend, and certainly, they would have been destroyed, as well as their people, as a punishment from Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of the disbelievers to tempt the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to alter the message of Islam and make changes to the Qur'an. The verse warns against the dangers of compromising the truth and yielding to the pressures of those who reject faith. The verse also highlights the severe consequences that those who try to distort the message of God will face, not only in this life but also in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in one's beliefs and to trust in God's plan, rather than relying on one's own limited understanding.
orig: وإن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها وتوكل على الله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And indeed, they were about to deceive you from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], so that you would invent something else against Us, but they are the ones who will be deceived.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers were trying to deceive the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by tempting him to alter the revelation he received from God. They wanted him to add or modify certain parts of the Qur'an to suit their own interests. However, the verse assures the Prophet that God's help and support are sufficient, and that those who seek to deceive him will ultimately be deceived themselves.
orig: وإن يريدوا أن يخدعوك فإن حسبك الله هو الذي أيدك بنصره وبالمؤمنين

translation: And He has united their hearts. If He had willed, He could have made them a single community, but He admits whom He wills to His mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power to unite the hearts of His creation. Despite their differences, God has the power to bring people together and make them a single community. However, He chooses to admit whom He wills to His mercy, indicating that His mercy is not obligatory, but rather a gift to those who deserve it. The verse highlights God's wisdom and might in His creation and His ability to control all affairs.
orig: وألف بين قلوبهم لو أنفقت ما في الأرض جميعا ما ألفت بين قلوبهم ولكن الله ألف بينهم إنه عزيز حكيم

translation: O Prophet! Allah has suffices you and those who follow you from the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers who follow him have been sufficiently supported and blessed by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet and his followers are not in need of anyone else's support or validation, as they have already been chosen and blessed by Allah. This verse also highlights the special relationship between the Prophet and his followers, and serves as a reminder of the importance of loyalty and obedience to the Prophet and his teachings.
orig: يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ومن اتبعك من المؤمنين

translation: O Prophet! Rouse the believers to battle. If there are twenty of you who are patient, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, for they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of mobilizing the believers to fight against the disbelievers, despite being outnumbered. The verse suggests that even a small number of believers, such as twenty, can overcome a much larger number of disbelievers, such as two hundred, and that a hundred believers can overcome a thousand disbelievers. The verse highlights the bravery and strength of the believers and emphasizes that they are fighting against a people who are ignorant of the truth and are therefore unable to understand the power of faith.
orig: يا أيها النبي حرض المؤمنين على القتال إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم مائة يغلبوا ألفا من الذين كفروا بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: Allah will test you with a year of famine and scarcity of money, and they will be exhausted, and your Lord will give you an opening and a victory, and your Lord is with the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a time of hardship and scarcity that the believers will face, where they will be tested with a year of famine and financial difficulties. However, God will provide an opening and a victory for those who are patient and trust in Him. The verse highlights the importance of patience and faith in God's plan, and assures believers that God is with them and will support them through difficult times.
orig: الآن خفف الله عنكم وعلم أن فيكم ضعفا فإن يكن منكم مائة صابرة يغلبوا مائتين وإن يكن منكم ألف يغلبوا ألفين بإذن الله والله مع الصابرين

translation: And We did not send any prophet except that he should be obeyed by Allah's permission. And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you, [their] Lord would have given them what they ask for and would have made them [even] more rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's prophets and the consequences of disobedience. The verse states that God sent prophets to guide people, and their obedience is a condition for receiving God's blessings and guidance. The verse also highlights the mercy of God, who, despite people's wrongdoing, is still willing to forgive and guide them if they turn to Him in repentance. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow God's commandments and prophets, and to seek His forgiveness and guidance in times of need.
orig: ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى حتى يثخن في الأرض تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And if it were not for a book from Allah, which had preceded, we would have punished them. [But] in their neglect, they would have been punished in this life.
interpretation: The verse implies that the punishment that the wicked people deserved was not immediate, but rather delayed by the mercy of God. The phrase 'book from Allah' refers to the Qur'an or a decree from God. The verse warns that if the punishment had not been written in the Qur'an, it would have been inflicted in this life. The verse highlights the idea that God's mercy and patience with sinners is not an indication of His weakness but rather a sign of His power and justice.
orig: لولا كتاب من الله سبق لمسكم فيما أخذتم عذاب عظيم

translation: And spend what We have provided you with, good and pure, and fear Allah, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of spending what God has provided, whether it be wealth, resources, or blessings, in a good and pure manner. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and their impact on others, and to always strive to act with integrity and compassion. Additionally, the verse reminds believers to fear Allah, recognizing His power and authority, and to seek His forgiveness and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a life of gratitude and obedience to God, and to always strive to do good in the world.
orig: فكلوا مما غنمتم حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O Prophet! Tell the captives in your hands that indeed Allah knows what is in your hearts, and He will give you what is better than what has been taken from you, and He will forgive you, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to reassure the captives in his hands that God is aware of their situation and will reward them with something better than what they have lost. The verse highlights God's knowledge of the human heart and His ability to forgive and show mercy to those who have been wronged. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God's forgiveness is not limited to the believers, but extends to all people, regardless of their faith or lack thereof. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who seek it, and that He is ever-ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لمن في أيديكم من الأسرى إن يعلم الله في قلوبكم خيرا يؤتكم خيرا مما أخذ منكم ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, they were about to deceive you from Allah's verses after Allah had given you victory over them. But Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse refers to a situation where some people were trying to deceive the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by distorting the words of God. The verse indicates that these people had previously been deceived by Satan and had turned away from God's guidance. The verse serves as a warning to those who try to distort God's words and deceive others, reminding them that God is all-knowing and wise, and that their actions will not go unpunished.
orig: وإن يريدوا خيانتك فقد خانوا الله من قبل فأمكن منهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and emigrated and fought with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah and those who have given shelter and aided - they are the allies of one another. And those who have believed but did not emigrate - for you there is no guardianship of them until they emigrate. And if they seek help from you in the name of religion, it is your duty to help, except against a people between whom and you there is a covenant. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of brotherhood and unity among believers, emphasizing that those who have believed, migrated, and fought for the cause of God are allies of one another. It also emphasizes the responsibility of believers towards one another, particularly in times of need, and the importance of helping one another in the name of religion. However, the verse also sets boundaries by stating that this responsibility does not extend to those who have not migrated and are not part of a covenant. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of loyalty and support among believers, while also emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's responsibilities and limitations.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض والذين آمنوا ولم يهاجروا ما لكم من ولايتهم من شيء حتى يهاجروا وإن استنصروكم في الدين فعليكم النصر إلا على قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another, [and] if you do [it] not, indeed there will be factional strife in the land and great corruption.
interpretation: The verse highlights the unity and solidarity among those who disbelieve in God and His message. They are allies in their disbelief and work together to spread their corrupt beliefs and practices. The verse warns that if the believers do not stand up against them, the disbelievers will cause great corruption and strife in the land. The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and cooperation among believers in the face of disbelief and corruption.
orig: والذين كفروا بعضهم أولياء بعض إلا تفعلوه تكن فتنة في الأرض وفساد كبير

translation: And those who believed, migrated, and striven in the way of Allah, and those who gave shelter and aid, they are the believers truly. For them is forgiveness and honorable provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of true believers, who not only have faith but also take action to fulfill their religious obligations. They migrate to a new land, strive in the way of God, and provide shelter and aid to others. In return, they are granted forgiveness and provision, signifying the blessings and rewards they will receive in this life and the hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله والذين آووا ونصروا أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who believed after them, and emigrated and struggled along with you, they are of you, and the brothers in religion are more entitled to inherit from one another than the orphans. And those who were born from them, some of them are more righteous than others. Surely Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of unity and brotherhood among believers. It emphasizes that those who believed in God and migrated to join the Muslim community, and those who struggled alongside them, are considered part of the same community and are equal in the eyes of God. The verse also emphasizes the importance of inheritance and the responsibility of taking care of one's fellow believers, especially those who are orphans.
