The verse ends by reminding the reader that God is all-knowing and aware of the actions and deeds of all people.
orig: والذين آمنوا من بعد وهاجروا وجاهدوا معكم فأولئك منكم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: God's curse and the curse of those who were sent by Him are upon the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse invokes God's curse and the curse of His prophets upon those who practice polytheism. The verse serves as a warning to those who associate partners with God, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions. The use of the phrase 'those who were sent by Him' refers to the prophets who were sent by God to guide humanity and convey His message. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin of polytheism and the certainty of God's punishment for those who persist in this practice.
orig: براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين

translation: And they will roam in the land for four months, and you will know that you are not able to escape from Allah, and that Allah humiliates the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to disbelieve. They will be allowed to roam freely on earth for a period of four months, but this freedom will not last forever. Eventually, they will come to realize that they are not able to escape God's punishment, and that God will humiliate them for their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the powerlessness of their disbelief in the face of God's wrath.
orig: فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله مخزي الكافرين

translation: And when the disbelievers had set up a united front against the Prophet, Allah's Messenger said to them: 'Allah is free from what you associate (with Him in worship) and I am free from what you ascribe (to me). Your forefathers were not aware of this (Qur'anic) knowledge, nor did they have any share in it.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the confrontation between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the disbelievers who were united against him. The Prophet made it clear to them that Allah is free from any association with partners or idols, and that he (the Prophet) is also free from any attribution of divinity or partnership with Allah. The verse emphasizes that the knowledge of the Qur'an and the message of Islam was not known to their forefathers, and that they had no share in it. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that they should not follow in the footsteps of their ancestors who rejected the message of Islam, and that they should instead accept the truth and submit to Allah.
orig: وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس يوم الحج الأكبر أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله فإن تبتم فهو خير لكم وإن توليتم فاعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وبشر الذين كفروا بعذاب أليم

translation: Except those who have a treaty with you from among the polytheists, then they did not fail you in anything, nor did they support anyone against you, so fulfill their treaty to them until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous [people].
interpretation: This verse refers to the treaty between the Muslims and the polytheists, specifically those who had a covenant with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse instructs the Muslims to fulfill their treaty obligations with the polytheists, as long as they did not fail them in anything and did not support anyone against them. The verse highlights the importance of honoring treaties and agreements, even with those who may have different beliefs or practices. It also emphasizes the value of righteousness and the love of Allah for those who are righteous.
orig: إلا الذين عاهدتم من المشركين ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحدا فأتموا إليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: And when the sacred months are passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them in every ambush. But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then leave their way free. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is discussing the treatment of polytheists during the sacred months. The verse commands the believers to kill or subdue the polytheists wherever they find them, and to besiege them and lie in wait for them in every ambush. However, if the polytheists repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then the believers should leave their way free and not harm them. The verse highlights the importance of forgiveness and mercy, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, and encourages the believers to act with compassion and mercy towards those who repent and turn to Allah.
orig: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وخذوهم واحصروهم واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, one of the pagans sought to harm the Prophet, but he was granted protection until he heard the words of Allah, then he believed, and he was granted security.
interpretation: The verse speaks about an incident where a pagan tried to harm the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but was prevented from doing so by the protection of Allah. The verse highlights the power of Allah's words and how they can bring about belief and protection for those who seek refuge in Him. The verse also emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in Allah and recourse to Him for protection, especially in times of danger and adversity.
orig: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

translation: And they were sold for a low price - they themselves did wrong - so they were debarred from the way. Indeed, they were a people who were criminals.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were punished for their wrongdoing. They were sold for a low price, indicating their worthlessness and insignificance in the eyes of God. The verse suggests that they brought this punishment upon themselves through their own actions, and that they were debarred from the way of righteousness. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in criminal behavior, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of following the path of righteousness.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not fear the tyrant, but they fear the believer who is humble. And their punishment will be increased by God.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the fear that tyrants inspire in the hearts of believers and the fear that believers have of God. The verse suggests that while tyrants may inspire fear through their power and oppression, it is ultimately the fear of God that should be the greatest concern for believers. The verse also implies that the punishment of tyrants will be increased by God, indicating that their oppression will not go unpunished.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: So if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of repentance, prayer, and charity as essential components of a believer's life. It emphasizes that those who repent from their sins, establish a strong connection with God through prayer, and give charity to those in need, are considered true believers and are part of the Ummah, the Muslim community. The verse underscores the idea that faith is not just a personal matter, but also a collective one, where believers are united in their commitment to God and their support for one another.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed their tokens of faith after they had witnessed them, and We have punished them for their sins.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of communities that have rejected God's signs and blessings, and instead, they turned to disbelief and sin. Their rejection of faith and disobedience to God led to their downfall and punishment. The verse emphasizes that the punishment was a result of their own actions and disbelief, and not because of any injustice on God's part. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in disbelief, warning them of the consequences of their actions and encouraging them to turn back to God and live according to His commandments.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Will you not fight a people who have violated their oaths and intended to expel the Messenger, while they did with you in the first place? They fear you not, nor do they fear Allah. Allah is more worthy that you should fear Him, if you are believers.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Muslim community, urging them to fight against a group of people who have broken their covenant and attempted to expel the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that these people have no fear of God or of the consequences of their actions, and that the believers should fear God more than they fear these people. The verse serves as a call to action, encouraging the Muslims to stand up for their rights and defend their faith, rather than allowing themselves to be intimidated or oppressed by those who seek to harm them.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And fight them until there is no fitna (disbelief) and the religion (all and only) is for Allah.
interpretation: The verse commands Muslims to fight against disbelievers until they are no longer able to oppose the will of Allah, and until the religion (i.e. Islam) is the only one practiced. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the purity of the faith and not allowing any other beliefs or ideologies to coexist with Islam. It also highlights the importance of fighting against oppression and injustice, and establishing a society where the teachings of Islam are upheld and followed.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: And He causes the night to enter the day, and He knows what is in the breasts (of people).
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and knowledge. The first part of the verse describes how God causes the night to enter the day, indicating His control over the natural world. The second part of the verse states that God knows what is in the breasts (of people), indicating His knowledge of human thoughts, intentions, and secrets. This verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-powerful, and that nothing is hidden from Him.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And the polytheists are not able to maintain the mosques of Allah, witnessing against themselves that they are disbelievers. Those are the ones whose deeds have been lost, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and the destruction of the places of worship built by the polytheists. The verse indicates that those who commit shirk are unable to maintain the mosques of Allah, and their actions are witness against themselves that they are disbelievers. The verse also warns that their deeds will be lost and they will abide eternally in the Fire, signifying the severity of the punishment for those who reject the oneness of Allah.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: Indeed, the mosques of Allah are the places of security and tranquility for the believers who perform the prayer and give zakat and do not fear except Allah. Perhaps they will be among the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of mosques as places of worship and spiritual refuge for believers. The verse emphasizes that true believers are those who perform their prayers and give zakat (charity) regularly, indicating their devotion to God and their commitment to the community. The phrase 'do not fear except Allah' suggests that true believers have complete trust in God and are not afraid of anything except God's punishment. The verse concludes by suggesting that those who follow these principles will be among the guided ones, implying that they will be rewarded in the afterlife for their righteousness.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who believed and migrated and struggled in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives are higher in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is they who will attain victory.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith, migration, and striving in the cause of Allah as the key factors that determine a person's rank in the sight of Allah. The verse emphasizes that those who have believed, migrated, and struggled in the cause of Allah, using their wealth and their lives, are considered higher in rank and will attain victory in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith requires action and sacrifice, and that the ultimate success and victory come from dedicating oneself to the cause of Allah.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And their Lord gave them good tidings of mercy and approval, and gardens for them in Paradise, remaining therein forever.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward that believers will receive in the afterlife. The phrase 'good tidings of mercy and approval' suggests that God's mercy and approval are not just rewards, but also a source of joy and happiness for believers. The image of 'gardens in Paradise' is a metaphor for the beauty and tranquility that awaits believers in the afterlife. The phrase 'remaining therein forever' emphasizes the eternal nature of this reward, indicating that believers will enjoy God's mercy and approval forever.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before you, who were stronger than you in power and more abundant in wealth and children. And We exhausted them not, but they denied Our signs, so We destroyed them, and their hearts were hardened.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations that were stronger and wealthier than the current generation. Despite their strength and wealth, they were destroyed because they denied God's signs and were ungrateful for the blessings they had been given. The verse serves as a reminder to the current generation, encouraging them to be mindful of God's power and to avoid the mistakes of the past. The verse also emphasizes the idea that material wealth and power are not a guarantee of protection from God's punishment, and that true success comes from following God's commandments and being grateful for His blessings.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they have preferred disbelief over faith. And whoever of you takes them as allies, then those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's faith over family ties. It prohibits believers from allying themselves with their families if they have chosen to reject faith and instead, encourages them to distance themselves from such individuals. The verse highlights the gravity of the sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and warns believers against being influenced by their family members who have chosen to disbelieve. It serves as a reminder that true faith requires a willingness to stand up for what is right, even if it means going against one's family and loved ones.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your relatives, your wealth which you have obtained, the commerce you fear to decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah comes with His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's faith and commitment to God and His Messenger over worldly attachments and material possessions. It warns against allowing earthly desires to take precedence over one's relationship with God, and encourages believers to focus on their spiritual growth and contribution to the cause of God, even if it means sacrificing material comforts and worldly attachments. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and happiness come from following God's commandments and striving in His cause, rather than pursuing worldly gains and pleasures.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear conquest and manifest victory. And We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest victory. And We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest victory.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The repetition of the phrase "clear conquest" and "manifest victory" emphasizes the magnitude and significance of the victory. The verse highlights the idea that the victory is not just a military or political one, but a spiritual one, as it is a manifestation of God's favor and support for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is not due to their own strength or power, but rather due to the grace and mercy of God.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down troops which you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse describes the victory of the believers and the defeat of the disbelievers. The phrase 'tranquility' refers to the peace and calm that comes from knowing that one is on the right path and that God is on their side. The 'troops' mentioned are the angels and other divine forces that were sent to assist the believers. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers were punished for their disbelief and that this punishment is a consequence of their own actions. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that they must remain faithful and obedient to God in order to receive His support and protection.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah will forgive whom He wills and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness. The phrase 'Then Allah will forgive whom He wills' indicates that God's forgiveness is not limited to those who have earned it through good deeds, but is also extended to those whom God chooses to forgive out of His mercy and grace. The phrase 'And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful' reinforces this idea and serves as a reminder that God's forgiveness is not limited to specific individuals or groups, but is available to all who seek it.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year. And if you fear poverty, We will enrich you from the bounty of Allah if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and warns them against the impurity of the polytheists. The verse prohibits the polytheists from approaching the Sacred Mosque, indicating that the place of worship is sacred and should not be defiled by those who do not believe in the oneness of God. The verse also addresses the fear of poverty among the believers, assuring them that God will enrich them from His bounty if He wills. The verse highlights the knowledge and wisdom of God in His commandments and promises.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth, until they pay the jizyah with willing submission and feel themselves subdued.
interpretation: This verse commands Muslims to fight against those who reject the belief in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and who do not follow the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the importance of fighting against those who do not follow the religion of truth, which is Islam, and who do not submit to the authority of Allah and His Messenger. The verse also highlights the importance of paying the jizyah, which is a tax paid by non-Muslims living in a Muslim state, as a sign of their submission and recognition of the authority of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of establishing justice and righteousness in society and the need to fight against those who reject the truth and oppose the will of Allah.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: And the Jews say, 'Uzair is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their statement with their mouths, imitating the saying of those who disbelieved before. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: The verse addresses the claim made by the Jews and Christians that Uzair (Ezra) and Jesus, respectively, are the sons of God. The verse dismisses this claim as a mere imitation of the disbelievers who came before them, and invites God's curse upon them for their misguided beliefs. The verse highlights the ignorance and delusion of those who attribute a son to God, the Most High, and serves as a warning to those who seek to attribute partners to Him.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And they have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god except Him. Glory be to Him, He is above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have taken their religious leaders and monks as lords instead of Allah, and have also elevated the Messiah, the son of Mary, to a status of divinity. The verse emphasizes that the Messiah and the religious leaders are not gods, but rather, they were commanded to worship only one God, who is Allah. The verse warns against the dangers of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and emphasizes the oneness of Allah, glorifying Him as the only deity worthy of worship.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except that His light should be perfected, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempt of the disbelievers to suppress the truth and light of Allah. They try to extinguish it with their words and actions, but Allah's light will always prevail and be perfected. The verse emphasizes the futility of their efforts and the ultimate victory of Allah's truth. It serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be discouraged by the attempts of those who oppose the truth.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and the universality of Islam. The phrase 'with guidance and the religion of truth' refers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) being sent by God to guide humanity to the right path. The phrase 'to manifest it over all religion' indicates that Islam is the only accepted religion by God and will eventually prevail over all other religions. The verse also highlights the opposition and dislike of the polytheists towards Islam, but their dislike does not matter as the truth and superiority of Islam will ultimately triumph.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and monks devour the wealth of the people unjustly and prevent them from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the issue of religious leaders and scholars who exploit the wealth of the people and prevent them from following the path of God. The verse also mentions those who hoard wealth and do not use it for the cause of God, warning them of a painful punishment. The verse highlights the responsibility of religious leaders to guide people towards righteousness and the consequences of misusing their position for personal gain.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: On a Day when their faces will be turned upside down in the Fire of Hell: They will say: 'Woe to us! Would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where the wicked will be punished in Hell. The verse emphasizes the regret and remorse that the sinners will feel on that day, wishing they had listened to God's commands and the Prophet's teachings. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of following God's guidance.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months in the Book of God, on the day He created the heavens and the earth; four of them are sacred. This is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein, and fight against the disbelievers all together, just as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the twelve months in the Islamic calendar, which are considered sacred in the eyes of God. The verse also highlights the significance of the four sacred months, which are considered especially sacred and are a time of increased spiritual reflection and devotion. The verse also encourages believers to unite against their common enemies, the disbelievers, and reminds them that God is on the side of the righteous.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: Indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe than the punishment of this life, and the disbelievers will say, 'Our Lord, give us a respite, and we will answer Your call and follow Your messengers.' How can they take heed on a Day when they are tried, on a Day when their wealth and children will avail them nothing, and they will not be given any respite?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment in the Hereafter compared to the punishment in this life. The disbelievers will realize their mistake and beg for a respite, but it will be too late. They will be judged based on their deeds, and their wealth and children will not be of any avail to them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of their accountability on Judgment Day.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when it is said to you, 'March forth in the cause of Allah,' you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you content with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? The provision of this world is little compared to the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers who are reluctant to sacrifice their worldly lives for the cause of Allah. The verse suggests that they are too attached to the temporal pleasures of this life and are not willing to risk their lives for the greater reward of the Hereafter. The verse contrasts the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and pleasures with the eternal nature of the Hereafter, implying that the believers should prioritize their spiritual well-being over their material comforts.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: Except that your Lord's punishment will befall you, a painful punishment, and replace you with a people other than yourselves, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse warns the disbelievers that they will face a painful punishment from Allah, which will replace them with another people. The verse emphasizes that Allah is capable of everything and that the disbelievers' actions will not harm Him in the least. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and live in disobedience to Allah's commandments, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the powerlessness of their efforts against Allah's will.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of supporting God's cause and the rewards that come with it. The phrase 'Allah will aid those who aid His cause' suggests that those who work towards promoting justice and righteousness will receive divine assistance and victory. The description of Allah as 'Powerful and Exalted in Might' underscores His ability to grant victory to those who align themselves with His will and emphasizes the magnitude of His power and wisdom.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction, and do good. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of spending in the way of Allah, which includes charitable acts, helping others, and striving in the cause of Allah. The verse warns against reckless and destructive behavior, and encourages believers to do good deeds. The verse also highlights the fact that Allah loves those who do good deeds, indicating that doing good is a way to earn Allah's pleasure and approval.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And if We had made it a near term (i.e., an easy and quick punishment), they would have said: 'Our Lord, why did you not give us a delay for a short time so that we could have followed your messengers?' But We did not destroy them except because they were unjust, and their false gods whom they invoked instead of Allah were not able to save them from Our punishment. And (mention, O Muhammad), when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers' argument that if God had given them a near term (a quick and easy punishment), they would have believed and followed the messengers. However, God refutes this claim by stating that the reason for their destruction was their injustice and their reliance on false gods instead of Allah. The verse also mentions the promise of God to make a successive authority on earth, indicating that God's plan for humanity is to establish a just and righteous society, and that those who reject His message will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Allah's forgiveness is sought. They did not appreciate the signs of Allah until it became clear to them that the liars are distinguishable from the believers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and recognizing the signs of Allah. The verse suggests that the people being addressed did not appreciate or recognize the signs of Allah until it was too late and the truth became clear. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate and recognize the signs of Allah and to seek His forgiveness before it's too late.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: And those who believe in Allah and the Last Day will not seek exemption from striving with their wealth and their lives, and Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of jihad, or striving, in the path of God. It highlights the willingness of believers to sacrifice their wealth and lives for the cause of God, and their certainty in the promise of the Hereafter. The verse also underscores the idea that God is aware of the righteous and their efforts, and that their sacrifices will not go unrewarded.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and the Hereafter - their hearts are disapproving, and they are in a state of confusion, and they are in a state of doubt, wavering between belief and disbelief, and their hearts are turned upside down.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of disbelievers who reject the existence of God and the Hereafter. Their hearts are described as disapproving, meaning they are void of faith and guidance. They are in a state of confusion, unable to distinguish right from wrong, and they are in a state of doubt, constantly wavering between belief and disbelief. Their hearts are turned upside down, indicating a state of spiritual confusion and instability. The verse highlights the inner turmoil and uncertainty that arises from rejecting the truth and guidance of God.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had wished to go out, they would have been prepared for it, but Allah restrained them, and He did not consent to their departure, and He said, 'Sit with the sedentary ones.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about a group of people who were prevented by God from leaving their homes to go out and fight in a battle. Despite their desire to leave, God restrained them and forced them to stay behind. The verse suggests that God had a reason for keeping them back, perhaps to protect them from harm or to test their faith. The phrase 'Sit with the sedentary ones' implies that they were to remain in a state of inactivity, waiting for further instructions or guidance from God. The verse highlights the power of God's will and His ability to control the actions of human beings, reminding us that our plans and desires are subject to His ultimate authority.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: And if they had gone out among you, they would have added to you nothing but confusion, and they would have stirred among you rancor and hatred, and Allah knows the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the presence of the unbelievers among the believers would have caused strife, conflict, and hatred. The unbelievers would have tried to spread their false beliefs and create discord among the believers. Allah is aware of the intentions of the wrongdoers and will not allow them to succeed in their evil plans. The verse serves as a warning to the believers to be cautious of the influence of the unbelievers and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: And indeed, they had sought to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might invent something else against Us; and then they would have taken you as a friend. And if We had not made you steadfast, you would have almost inclined to them a little. Then [We would have made you taste] the double of [punishment] in this life and the Hereafter, and you would have found none to aid you. And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might invent something else against Us; and then they would have taken you as a friend. And if We had not made you steadfast, you would have almost inclined to them a little. Then [We would have made you taste] the double of [punishment] in this life and the Hereafter, and you would have found none to aid you.
interpretation: The verse describes the attempts of the disbelievers to tempt the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to alter the revelation he received from Allah. They wanted him to compromise his message and make changes to suit their desires. The verse suggests that the Prophet was steadfast in his faith and did not give in to their pressure. If he had, he would have faced a double punishment in this life and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not to compromise their beliefs under pressure from others.
orig: لقد ابتغوا الفتنة من قبل وقلبوا لك الأمور حتى جاء الحق وظهر أمر الله وهم كارهون

translation: And among them are those who say, 'Permit me, and do not tempt me.' Surely, Hell has become an ambush for the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attitude of some people who ask for permission to engage in sinful behavior, indicating that they are aware of the wrong they are doing but choose to do it anyway. The verse warns that Hell is waiting for those who reject God's guidance and choose to disbelieve, and that it is a trap that will ensnare them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ائذن لي ولا تفتني ألا في الفتنة سقطوا وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: Indeed, We will suffice you with goodness and indeed, We will suffice them with evil.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the idea that God is sufficient for the believers, providing them with goodness and guidance, while the wicked will be sufficient for their own destruction, as they will be consumed by their own evil deeds. The verse emphasizes the idea of divine justice, where God's help and guidance are available to those who seek it, while those who choose to reject God's message will be left to their own devices and face the consequences of their actions.
orig: إن تصبك حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبك مصيبة يقولوا قد أخذنا أمرنا من قبل ويتولوا وهم فرحون

translation: Say, 'Nothing will happen to us except what Allah has written for us; He is our Protector.' And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the belief in the will of God and the reliance on Him as the protector. It encourages the believers to have faith that whatever happens to them is part of God's plan and decree, and that He will protect them and guide them through difficulties. The verse also highlights the importance of trust and reliance on God, reminding the believers that they should put their trust in God alone and not in any other being or thing.
orig: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: what if your Lord were to bring the punishment upon you, or the Hour should come upon you, would you then believe?',
interpretation: The verse is a question posed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the disbelievers, asking them to consider the possibility of God's punishment befalling them, either in the form of a sudden calamity or the ultimate punishment on Judgment Day. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder to those who reject the message of Islam, encouraging them to reflect on the consequences of their disbelief and to consider the reality of God's power and judgment.
orig: قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده أو بأيدينا فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون

translation: Say, 'Forgive us our sins, or punish us with a penalty, for we are a people who are sinners.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is asking for forgiveness from God for their sins, but also acknowledging that they deserve punishment for their wrongdoing. The use of the word 'forgive' (انفقوا) implies a recognition of the gravity of their sins and a desire to be pardoned. The alternative phrase 'or punish us with a penalty' (أو كرها) serves as a reminder that the consequences of sin are not to be taken lightly, and that punishment is a possibility if forgiveness is not granted. The phrase 'we are a people who are sinners' (كنتم قوما فاسقين) reinforces the idea that the speaker and their community are aware of their sinful nature and are seeking redemption.
orig: قل أنفقوا طوعا أو كرها لن يتقبل منكم إنكم كنتم قوما فاسقين

translation: And nothing prevents their expiations from being accepted from them, but that they disbelieve in Allah and in the Messenger and they do not come to prayer except lazily and they do not spend except reluctantly.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the reason why the disbelievers' acts of worship, such as charity and prayer, are not accepted by God is because they are devoid of faith in God and His Messenger. Their lack of belief is evident in their lack of enthusiasm and reluctance to perform these acts, indicating that their hearts are not truly devoted to God. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is not just about outward actions, but also about the intentions and sincerity behind them.
orig: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم إلا أنهم كفروا بالله وبرسوله ولا يأتون الصلاة إلا وهم كسالى ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

translation: And do not be surprised at their wealth and their children. Indeed, Allah only wants to punish them in this life and that their souls may depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the punishment of the disbelievers will not be limited to the afterlife, but will also manifest in this life. Their wealth and children, which they often use as a measure of their success and prosperity, will not protect them from Allah's punishment. Instead, their wealth and children will be used as a means of punishment, as they will be taken away from them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are proud of their wealth and children, reminding them that these blessings can be taken away at any moment, and that true success lies in living a righteous life and submitting to Allah's will.
orig: فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: They swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, but they are not of you; however, they are a people who are afraid to disagree with you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who pretend to be part of the Muslim community, but in reality, they are not. They swear by Allah to deceive and appear as if they are part of the community, but they are actually afraid to express their true beliefs and disagree with the Muslims. The verse highlights the hypocrisy and deception of these individuals and serves as a warning to the Muslim community to be cautious of such people.
orig: ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم ولكنهم قوم يفرقون

translation: And if they had found a refuge or a cave or a place to hide, they would have turned to it with a swift turning.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even if the people who were destroyed had found a place to hide or a refuge, they would have still been unable to escape God's punishment. The use of the phrase 'swift turning' emphasizes the sudden and inevitable nature of the punishment, indicating that there was no way for them to avoid it. The verse serves as a reminder that God's justice is inescapable and that those who reject His commands will face the consequences.
orig: لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات أو مدخلا لولوا إليه وهم يجمحون

translation: And among them are those who accuse you (Prophet Muhammad) of lying about the distribution of alms. If they are given something from it, they are content, but if they are not given anything, they become angry.
interpretation: This verse refers to the hypocrites who criticized the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for the way he distributed the charity. They were pleased when they received something from it, but became angry when they didn't receive anything. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of these individuals who were not truly concerned with the welfare of the community, but rather with their own personal gain. It serves as a reminder to those in positions of authority to be mindful of their responsibility to distribute resources fairly and to not let personal interests cloud their judgment.
orig: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات فإن أعطوا منها رضوا وإن لم يعطوا منها إذا هم يسخطون

translation: And if they had only been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them, and had said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger; indeed, we are for Allah',
interpretation: The verse highlights the ingratitude of the people who were not content with the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah and His Messenger. Instead of being grateful, they sought more and desired to have what was not given to them. The verse emphasizes that true believers should be content with what Allah has given them and trust in His bounty and the guidance of His Messenger. The phrase 'Sufficient for us is Allah' signifies that true believers should have faith in Allah's provision and guidance, and not seek anything beyond what He has given them.
orig: ولو أنهم رضوا ما آتاهم الله ورسوله وقالوا حسبنا الله سيؤتينا الله من فضله ورسوله إنا إلى الله راغبون

translation: Indeed, the believers, men and women, are Auliya' (helpers, supporters, friends, etc.) of one another (in Faith); they enjoin good and forbid evil, and they establish worship and give Zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. On them will be Allah's Mercy; surely Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity and support that exists among believers, both men and women. They are described as Auliya', which means friends or helpers, indicating a close and supportive relationship. The verse emphasizes their shared beliefs and practices, such as enjoining good and forbidding evil, establishing worship and giving Zakat (charity), and obeying Allah and His Messenger. The verse also mentions that Allah's mercy will be upon them, indicating His favor and blessings upon the believers. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of unity and cooperation among believers, and the rewards that come with living a righteous life.
orig: إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين والعاملين عليها والمؤلفة قلوبهم وفي الرقاب والغارمين وفي سبيل الله وابن السبيل فريضة من الله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among them are those who abuse the Prophet and say, 'He is a madman.' But he is not mad; it is they who are blind. They do not believe in God and the believers, and they are not merciful to the believers. Their punishment will be severe.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who ridicule and disrespect the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reject his message. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet is not mad or hallucinating, but rather, those who reject his message are the ones who are spiritually blind and lack faith in God and the believers. They are also devoid of compassion and mercy towards the believers. The verse warns them of severe punishment for their disbelief and mistreatment of the Prophet and the believers.
orig: ومنهم الذين يؤذون النبي ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين ورحمة للذين آمنوا منكم والذين يؤذون رسول الله لهم عذاب أليم

translation: They swear by Allah that they are indeed of you, while they are not of you. Indeed, they are a people who are afraid that the punishment of Allah will come to them, so they pretend to be believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who pretend to be believers and swear by Allah in order to deceive others and avoid the punishment of Allah. They are not true believers, but are afraid of the consequences of their actions and try to appear pious in order to avoid the wrath of God. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of these individuals and serves as a warning to those who pretend to be something they are not in order to avoid the consequences of their actions.
orig: يحلفون بالله لكم ليرضوكم والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه إن كانوا مؤمنين

translation: And they did not know that Allah had already decided to destroy them, and that they would not escape the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance of the disbelievers who were unaware of Allah's plan to destroy them. The verse implies that the punishment they will face in the Hereafter is inescapable and that they will not be able to avoid it. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and live in disobedience to Allah's commandments.
orig: ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله فأن له نار جهنم خالدا فيها ذلك الخزي العظيم

translation: And warn the hypocrites that a painful punishment is coming to them, and those who are disbelievers will say, 'Is this not enough for them that they are being warned? Indeed, they will be destroyed by what they used to ridicule.'
interpretation: The verse warns the hypocrites of a painful punishment that is coming their way, while the disbelievers will mock the warning and reject it. The verse suggests that the punishment will be so severe that even those who ridiculed the warning will be destroyed by it. The verse highlights the consequences of hypocrisy and disbelief, and serves as a warning to those who are living in denial of God's message.
orig: يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم قل استهزئوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only jesting and playing.'
interpretation: The verse suggests that those who are questioned about their behavior and their mocking of God's signs and messengers will try to downplay their actions and claim that they were just joking or playing. However, the verse implies that this excuse will not be accepted and that the consequences of their actions will still befall them.
orig: ولئن سألتهم ليقولن إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب قل أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم تستهزئون

translation: And do not apologize for your disbelief after your belief. Indeed, Allah will not forgive you, ever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and its consequences. The verse warns believers against denying their faith, as it is a grave offense that cannot be forgiven by God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in one's belief and not turning back on one's faith, lest one faces the wrath of God.
orig: لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة بأنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: The hypocrites, men and women, are from one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right, and they close their hands. They have forgotten God, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of hypocrites, who are described as being both men and women. They are described as enjoining what is wrong and forbidding what is right, indicating that they are actively promoting evil and suppressing good. The verse also mentions that they close their hands, which suggests that they are unwilling to give or help others, and have forgotten God, indicating that they are not mindful of their accountability to God. The verse concludes by stating that the hypocrites are transgressors, indicating that their actions are not in line with God's commands and that they will face consequences for their actions.
orig: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف ويقبضون أيديهم نسوا الله فنسيهم إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

translation: And Allah has prepared for the hypocrites, both men and women, and the disbelievers, the fire of Hell, they will abide therein forever. It is sufficient for them, and Allah is angry with them, and for them is a punishment enduring.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of hypocrites and disbelievers, who will be punished with eternal suffering in Hell. The phrase 'both men and women' emphasizes that neither gender is exempt from this punishment. The phrase 'It is sufficient for them' implies that the punishment is enough for their crimes, and that there is no need for further punishment. The phrase 'and Allah is angry with them' underscores the gravity of their offense and the righteousness of the punishment. The phrase 'and for them is a punishment enduring' emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment, indicating that it will not end or decrease over time.
orig: وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم ولعنهم الله ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: And those before them had been stronger than you in power, and had more wealth and children. So enjoy yourselves, just as those before you enjoyed themselves. Indeed, you have exhausted your enjoyment, just as they exhausted their enjoyment. And you have indulged in your wealth and your children, just as they indulged in their wealth and children. Indeed, you have been punished, just as they were punished. And those who have gone before them had also been punished, because their deeds were in vain, both in this life and the Hereafter. And they are the losers.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers, reminding them that even the powerful and wealthy nations before them were eventually punished by God. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers' enjoyment of their wealth and children is fleeting and will ultimately lead to their downfall, just as it did for those who came before them. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that their worldly possessions and offspring will not protect them from God's punishment. The verse also highlights the futility of their deeds, both in this life and the Hereafter, and that they will ultimately be losers in the end.
orig: كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة وأكثر أموالا وأولادا فاستمتعوا بخلاقهم فاستمتعتم بخلاقكم كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم وخضتم كالذي خاضوا أولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And how many a prophet did We send from among those who were before them, when they were unjust. We sent Noah, Abraham, and Moses, and We sent messengers after them, and they were denied. God was not to wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse highlights the history of prophets sent by God to guide people, specifically mentioning Noah, Abraham, Moses, and other messengers. Despite their efforts, the people denied and rejected them, leading to their own downfall. The verse emphasizes that God's sending of prophets was not to wrong the people, but rather to guide them. However, the people's rejection of the prophets led to their own destruction. This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and the importance of heeding the messages of His prophets.
orig: ألم يأتهم نبأ الذين من قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وأصحاب مدين والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those will be granted mercy by Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of unity and cooperation among believers, both men and women. It emphasizes their role as allies in promoting righteousness and preventing evil. The verse also emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer and giving zakah, which are two of the Five Pillars of Islam. Additionally, the verse emphasizes obedience to Allah and His Messenger as a means of receiving Allah's mercy. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's greatness and wisdom.
orig: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويطيعون الله ورسوله أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And Allah has promised the believers, men and women, Gardens under which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, and good dwellings in Gardens of perpetual residence. And Allah's promise is great indeed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to the believers, both men and women, of gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will dwell forever, and beautiful homes in gardens of eternal residence. The verse emphasizes the greatness of God's promise and the reward that awaits the believers in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings that come with faith and obedience to God, and encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their belief and actions.
orig: وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh upon them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to struggle against the disbelievers and hypocrites. The verse emphasizes the importance of being stern and unyielding in this struggle, indicating that the fate of those who reject God's message is Hell, and their ultimate destination is wretchedness and suffering. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of standing firm in their faith and being vigilant against the influence of disbelief and hypocrisy.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but indeed they have uttered blasphemy, and they disbelieved after their Islam, and they had plotted what they did not attain, and they were not wronged except that Allah and His Messenger have bestowed favor upon them. If they repent, it will be better for them, but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and there will be none for them on earth as a guardian or a helper.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have rejected the message of Islam and have turned away from their faith. They have sworn by Allah that they have not said anything against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims, but in reality, they have uttered blasphemy and disbelief. They have plotted against the Muslims but have not been able to achieve their goals. The verse warns them that if they do not repent and turn back to Allah, they will face a painful punishment in this life and the Hereafter. The verse also emphasizes that there will be no one to protect or help them on earth if they continue to reject Allah and His Messenger.
orig: يحلفون بالله ما قالوا ولقد قالوا كلمة الكفر وكفروا بعد إسلامهم وهموا بما لم ينالوا وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله فإن يتوبوا يك خيرا لهم وإن يتولوا يعذبهم الله عذابا أليما في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم في الأرض من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], 'If He gives us from His bounty, we will give charity and become among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse refers to those who made a covenant with God, promising to give charity and become righteous if they received His bounty. The verse highlights the selfish nature of their request, as they only want to receive God's blessings without any intention of actually becoming righteous. It serves as a warning against those who seek to exploit God's generosity without genuinely seeking to live a virtuous life.
orig: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the clear and decisive nature of the victory, while 'manifest triumph' emphasizes the obvious and public nature of the triumph. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of God's favor and support, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: Then, after that, your hearts were hardened and became as rocks, or even worse in hardness, because of the evil which you had committed.
interpretation: The verse describes how the people's hearts became hardened and callous as a result of their own actions and disobedience. The comparison to rocks suggests a severe hardening, indicating a state of spiritual numbness and insensitivity to spiritual truths. The phrase 'or even worse in hardness' suggests a gradual progression in hardness, implying that the people had reached a point of no return, leaving them with no choice but to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون

translation: And they did not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private conversations, and that Allah is Knowing of the unseen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ignorance of the disbelievers who were unaware of Allah's knowledge of their hidden thoughts and conversations. The verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of being All-Aware, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him, including the secrets of the hearts and the private conversations of individuals. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their thoughts and actions, as they are always under the watchful eye of Allah, who is aware of all things, seen and unseen.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم وأن الله علام الغيوب

translation: And those who hoard the gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who hoard wealth and do not use it in the way of God. They are warned of a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that wealth is a means to be used for good and not to be hoarded. Those who do not use their wealth in the way of God are considered to be in disobedience and will face punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to use their wealth in a responsible and charitable manner, and to not let wealth become an idol that replaces their devotion to God.
orig: الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم فيسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And whether you ask for their forgiveness or not, indeed, Allah will not forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God's forgiveness is not sought for those who have disbelieved in Him and His Messenger. The verse indicates that those who have rejected God's guidance and disobeyed His commands will not be forgiven, and that God will not guide them towards the righteous path. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and disobey His commands, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم ذلك بأنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And they were delighted in their refusal, and they were averse to spending their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. And they said, 'Do not rush into the heat of the fire.' Say, 'The fire will be more severe in heat on the Day of Recompense.'
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of those who refused to follow the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and opposed the idea of spending their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah. They were reluctant to sacrifice their material possessions and themselves for the sake of their faith. Instead, they preferred to stay away from the heat of the battlefield. The verse warns them that the fire of Hell will be much more intense on the Day of Judgment, indicating that their reluctance to sacrifice for their faith will lead to a severe punishment in the afterlife.
orig: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله وكرهوا أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله وقالوا لا تنفروا في الحر قل نار جهنم أشد حرا لو كانوا يفقهون

translation: So let them laugh a little and weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who have earned evil deeds. They will be made to laugh a little, perhaps in mockery or scorn, and weep much, as a recompense for their misdeeds. The verse suggests that their punishment will be proportionate to their sins, and that they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's justice.
orig: فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So indeed, Allah will send their wealth and children to destruction, and they will cry out to them, 'Where is your place of refuge?' Indeed, their refuge is not except in Al-Fajr (the morning), and indeed, their punishment will not be averted.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. Their wealth and children, which they believed were sources of comfort and security, will ultimately be destroyed, and they will be left with no refuge or escape from God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that their punishment will not be averted, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا ولن تقاتلوا معي عدوا إنكم رضيتم بالقعود أول مرة فاقعدوا مع الخالفين

translation: And do not approach any of the orphan's property except in the way of improving it until he reaches maturity. Indeed, that is what will be best for him, and if you consume their property unjustly, it will be a consumption of fire into your bellies, and you will be burned by it.
interpretation: The verse prohibits the mistreatment of orphans and their property. It emphasizes the importance of preserving their rights and assets until they come of age. The verse warns against exploiting or consuming their property unjustly, likening such actions to consuming fire that will ultimately burn the perpetrator. The verse serves as a reminder to protect the vulnerable and uphold justice, highlighting the severe consequences of violating this principle.
orig: ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله وماتوا وهم فاسقون

translation: And do not be surprised at their wealth and their children. Indeed, Allah only wants to punish them in this world and to purify their souls and leave their wealth and children as an inheritance for the believers.
interpretation: The verse explains that the punishment of the unjust will not only be limited to the hereafter but will also manifest in this world. The wealth and children they have accumulated will not save them from God's punishment. Instead, God will purify their souls through punishment in this life, leaving their wealth and children as an inheritance for the believers. This verse serves as a reminder that true purification and inheritance come from God, and that material wealth and offspring are not a guarantee of salvation.
orig: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And when a chapter was revealed, stating: 'Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger,' the elders of the hypocrites said: 'Leave us alone, sit still.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the hypocrites when a chapter of the Qur'an was revealed, urging people to believe in Allah and support His Messenger. The hypocrites, who were pretending to be Muslims but secretly opposed the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asked to be left alone and not be bothered with the call to faith. The verse highlights their reluctance to embrace the truth and their desire to maintain their status quo of disbelief and injustice. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of standing up for what is right and not being deterred by those who resist the truth.
orig: وإذا أنزلت سورة أن آمنوا بالله وجاهدوا مع رسوله استأذنك أولو الطول منهم وقالوا ذرنا نكن مع القاعدين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him struggled with their wealth and their souls, and those were the ones who were successful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the sacrifices made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers who accompanied him. They did not only risk their wealth and lives but also strove with their souls, that is, they dedicated their entire being to the cause of Islam. Their struggle was not limited to physical combat but also involved spreading the message of Islam, guiding people towards righteousness, and establishing a just society. Their sacrifices were not in vain, for they were the ones who ultimately succeeded in their mission, and their efforts continue to bear fruit to this day.
orig: لكن الرسول والذين آمنوا معه جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم وأولئك لهم الخيرات وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And indeed, We have given them a Scripture which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessing of the Qur'an, which is a comprehensive guide, containing knowledge, guidance, and mercy for believers. The use of the word 'detailed' emphasizes the precision and clarity of the Qur'an's teachings. The verse underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a means of obtaining God's mercy. It serves as a reminder to believers to cherish and follow the teachings of the Qur'an, leading them to a righteous life and a closer connection with God.
orig: أعد الله لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And the punishment was due from Al-Mu'adhirun (the tribes of Arabs) so that they may learn a lesson, and (the punishment) was severe on those who were ungrateful (and disobedient to Allah).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that was due to the tribes of Arabs, known as Al-Mu'adhirun, who were deserving of punishment due to their disobedience and ingratitude towards Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment, indicating that it was a consequence of their disbelief and disobedience. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and choose to disobey Allah, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they continue on their path of disobedience.
orig: وجاء المعذرون من الأعراب ليؤذن لهم وقعد الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله سيصيب الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: And not upon the weak nor upon the sick nor upon those who have nothing to spend, those who do not have the means to do so, in order to obtain the blessings of Allah and His Messenger. Indeed, those who have been given knowledge before it - they are the ones who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the call to Allah and His Messenger is not directed towards those who are weak, sick, or unable to spend anything. Instead, it is aimed at those who have been given knowledge and understanding, and who are capable of recognizing and fearing Allah. The verse highlights the importance of knowledge and understanding in one's relationship with Allah, and suggests that those who have been blessed with knowledge have a greater responsibility to live up to Allah's expectations.
orig: ليس على الضعفاء ولا على المرضى ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون حرج إذا نصحوا لله ورسوله ما على المحسنين من سبيل والله غفور رحيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophetic nature of Muhammad's mission, which was not to bring destruction or vengeance, but rather to spread God's message of mercy and guidance to all people. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message was not limited to a particular community or time, but was intended for all humanity, past, present, and future. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and compassion, and highlights the importance of spreading love and kindness to all people.
orig: ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم قلت لا أجد ما أحملكم عليه تولوا وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حزنا ألا يجدوا ما ينفقون

translation: Indeed, the path is only open to those who are humble and submissive, and they are few in number.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of humility and submissiveness in the path to guidance and righteousness. The phrase 'few in number' suggests that only a select few are able to achieve this state of humility and submissiveness, making it a rare and precious quality. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate these qualities in their own lives and to be mindful of their relationship with God.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يستأذنونك وهم أغنياء رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون

translation: They will apologize to you when you return to them. Say, 'Do not apologize to us; indeed, we will not believe you.
