The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord, there is no creature but He will take it by the forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: The verse expresses the Prophet Abraham's trust and reliance on God, acknowledging that all creatures are subject to God's control and that He is the only one who can guide and protect. The phrase 'there is no creature but He will take it by the forelock' suggests that God has complete authority and power over all things, and that nothing can escape His grasp. The second part of the verse emphasizes that the Prophet's Lord is on a straight path, indicating that God's guidance is clear and straightforward, and that those who follow it will be led to righteousness and salvation.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness upon you, just as We sent a Messenger to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a violent seizure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the role of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad) who was sent by God to guide the people. The verse draws a parallel between the Messenger and the prophet who was sent to Pharaoh, highlighting the similarity in their missions. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Messenger, as Pharaoh did, reminding them of the consequences of disobedience and the power of God to seize and punish those who defy Him.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Hud and his followers, who were saved by God's mercy from a severe punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's mercy and grace are not limited to specific individuals or groups, but are available to all who believe and follow His commandments. The verse also highlights the idea that God's punishment is severe and certain, but those who believe and follow His commandments will be saved from it.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا هودا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ونجيناهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And they have denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers, and they followed every stubborn tyrant.
interpretation: The verse describes the disobedience of a community that rejected the signs and messengers of their Lord, choosing instead to follow every stubborn tyrant. The verse highlights the rejection of divine guidance and the pursuit of worldly power and control, which is symbolized by the phrase 'every stubborn tyrant'. This verse serves as a warning against the dangers of rejecting God's guidance and following one's own desires and worldly leaders, which can ultimately lead to destruction and punishment.
orig: وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم وعصوا رسله واتبعوا أمر كل جبار عنيد

translation: And follow not the disbelievers, for they will surely be punished in this world and in the Hereafter. Their punishment will not be lightened, and they will not be aided.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to follow the disbelievers, as they will face punishment both in this life and the Hereafter. The punishment will be severe and unrelenting, with no respite or aid available to them. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay on the righteous path and avoid the company of those who reject God's teachings.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة ألا إن عادا كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لعاد قوم هود

translation: And to Thamud, We sent their brother Salih, saying: 'Worship Allah, you have no other god besides Him. He created you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness from Him and then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is near, responsive.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Salih, who was sent by God to the people of Thamud, urging them to worship only Allah and to turn to Him in repentance. The verse emphasizes God's power and authority as the creator and sustainer of life, and encourages the people to seek forgiveness and guidance from Him. The phrase 'my Lord is near, responsive' suggests that God is always near and ready to respond to those who turn to Him in faith and repentance.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها فاستغفروه ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي قريب مجيب

translation: They said, 'O Salih, we were in a state of ignorance and foolishness before this. We were worshiping our forefathers' idols. Do you think we are in a state of confusion and doubt about what you are calling us to?',
interpretation: The verse highlights the response of the disbelievers to the prophet Salih's call to worship only Allah. They admit their previous state of ignorance and foolishness in worshiping idols, but they express their confusion and doubt about the new message. The verse emphasizes the idea that the people were not only misguided in their beliefs but also unwilling to accept the truth and leave their old ways. It serves as a reminder that guidance and enlightenment come from Allah alone, and that true faith requires a willingness to let go of old beliefs and embrace the truth.
orig: قالوا يا صالح قد كنت فينا مرجوا قبل هذا أتنهانا أن نعبد ما يعبد آباؤنا وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا إليه مريب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني منه رحمة فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته فما تزيدونني غير تخسير

translation: And indeed, this Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing its authority and authenticity as a revelation from God. The use of the phrase 'Lord of the worlds' highlights God's sovereignty over all creation and underscores the Qur'an's universality and relevance to all people, regardless of their cultural or geographical background. The verse serves as a reminder of the Qur'an's sacred nature and the importance of treating it with respect and reverence.
orig: ويا قوم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب قريب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فعقروها فقال تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك وعد غير مكذوب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved the righteous and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and from the shame of that day. Indeed, your Lord is the Powerful, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when God's command to destroy the town was carried out, and how the righteous and believers were saved by God's mercy. The verse highlights the contrast between the fate of the wicked and the righteous. While the wicked were destroyed, the righteous were saved, indicating that God's punishment is not indiscriminate and that He always distinguishes between the faithful and the disobedient. The phrase 'and from the shame of that day' suggests that the punishment was not only physical destruction but also a source of shame and disgrace for those who were destroyed. The verse ends by emphasizing God's power and wisdom in His judgment.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا نجينا صالحا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ومن خزي يومئذ إن ربك هو القوي العزيز

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, so there was no repentance for Thamud.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of towns near the Prophet Salih's people, the Thamud, who were warned by Salih to repent and turn to God, but they refused and continued to live in disobedience. Their punishment was their destruction, and the verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain and final, leaving no room for repentance or second chances.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

translation: And indeed, Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings. They said, 'Peace!' He said, 'Peace!' and came not with haste.
interpretation: The verse describes the visit of God's messengers to the Prophet Abraham, who were sent to deliver good news. The messengers greeted Abraham with the word 'peace' (salaam), which Abraham returned, indicating his hospitality and welcome. The verse highlights Abraham's composure and lack of haste in receiving the messengers, demonstrating his faith and trust in God's plan. The verse serves as an example for believers to emulate Abraham's virtues and to be prepared to receive God's blessings with patience and humility.
orig: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ

translation: And when We saw their hands did not extend to them, and We perceived from them aversion and hostility, and they denied Our signs, We said, 'Taste the punishment of burning!',
interpretation: This verse describes the situation where the people of Sodom refused to listen to the prophet Lot's message and instead showed hostility towards him. As a result, God punished them with a burning punishment. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's message and the prophets who bring it. It serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they continue to reject the truth.
orig: فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه نكرهم وأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم لوط

translation: And We gave Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, all three of them, an honorable mention. And We gave them a beautiful promise, a truthful prophecy, and We gave them a great reward, a generous provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor given to the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The phrase 'honorable mention' signifies their importance and reverence in Islam. The 'beautiful promise' refers to the divine promise of guidance and prosperity for their descendants. The 'truthful prophecy' indicates that their messages were true and divinely inspired. The 'great reward' and 'generous provision' refer to the spiritual and material blessings bestowed upon them by God. The verse emphasizes the significance of these prophets in Islamic tradition and their role in shaping the religious and moral values of their communities.
orig: وامرأته قائمة فضحكت فبشرناها بإسحاق ومن وراء إسحاق يعقوب

translation: I said, 'O my dear uncle! Verily, I have seen myself (in a dream) as a youth, old and decrepit, and I have seen you as an old man, and I have seen the people as pigs and dogs fighting each other.'
interpretation: The verse describes a dream that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had, in which he saw himself as an old man, his uncle as an old man, and the people as pigs and dogs fighting each other. The dream is a metaphorical representation of the state of the world before the advent of Islam. The pigs and dogs represent the ignorant and corrupt people who are fighting each other, while the Prophet and his uncle represent the righteous and wise who are striving to guide the people towards the truth. The dream serves as a warning to the people to turn away from their corrupt ways and towards the guidance of God.
orig: قالت يا ويلتى أألد وأنا عجوز وهذا بعلي شيخا إن هذا لشيء عجيب

translation: They said, 'We are amazed at the matter of Allah! How great is the Mercy of Allah and His Blessings upon you, O people of the household! Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people of the household (ahl al-bayt) to the blessings and mercy of Allah. They are amazed by the greatness of Allah's mercy and blessings upon them, and they acknowledge that He is worthy of praise and glorification. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings of Allah in our lives, and the need to glorify and praise Him for His generosity and mercy.
orig: قالوا أتعجبين من أمر الله رحمت الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت إنه حميد مجيد

translation: And when Abraham's fear had passed, he said, 'How will God bring life to the dead bones?',
interpretation: This verse describes Abraham's reaction to God's command to sacrifice his son Ismail. Abraham was initially afraid, but once he realized that God's command was true, he questioned how God would bring life to the dead bones of his son. This verse highlights Abraham's faith and trust in God's power and wisdom, as he is willing to sacrifice his most precious possession, his son, in obedience to God's command. It also emphasizes the idea that God has the power to bring life to the dead and that He is not limited by the natural order of things.
orig: فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a wise and gentle leader.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's leadership qualities, describing him as both wise and gentle. The use of the word 'halim' (wise) emphasizes Abraham's ability to make sound judgments and make wise decisions, while 'awah' (gentle) suggests that he was compassionate and kind in his leadership. This verse serves as an example to leaders, encouraging them to adopt these qualities in their own leadership styles.
orig: إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب

translation: O Abraham, turn away from this, for indeed, your Lord's command has come, and they have earned a punishment that is not respited.
interpretation: In this verse, God is commanding Prophet Abraham to distance himself from the people who have earned God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a result of their own actions and it is not something that can be delayed or avoided. The use of the phrase 'your Lord's command' highlights the authority and power of God, and serves as a reminder that God's decisions are final and absolute. The verse also underscores the importance of obedience to God's commands, even when they may seem difficult to understand or oppose human reasoning.
orig: يا إبراهيم أعرض عن هذا إنه قد جاء أمر ربك وإنهم آتيهم عذاب غير مردود

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed on their account and felt himself oppressed by their presence. And he said, 'This is a trying day.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) when the angels came to him as messengers of God. Lut was distressed and felt oppressed by their presence, indicating that he was aware of the gravity of the situation and the importance of the message they brought. The phrase 'This is a trying day' suggests that Lut knew that the arrival of the angels meant that a great trial was at hand, and that he and his people were about to face a severe test of their faith and obedience. The verse highlights the weight of responsibility that prophets carry, and the emotional toll that it can take on them as they strive to convey God's message to their people.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقال هذا يوم عصيب

translation: And his people came to him, rushing towards him, and they were previously doing evil deeds. He said, 'O my people, these are my daughters, they are purer for you. Fear Allah and do not shame me in front of my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene where Prophet Lot's people came to him, rushing towards him, and they were previously doing evil deeds. Prophet Lot tried to reason with them, saying that his daughters were purer for them and that they should fear Allah and not shame him in front of his guests. The verse highlights the moral decay and corruption of Prophet Lot's people, who were so consumed by their desires that they were willing to commit incest and disregard the laws of hospitality. The verse also emphasizes the importance of protecting one's guests and treating them with respect and dignity.
orig: وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات قال يا قوم هؤلاء بناتي هن أطهر لكم فاتقوا الله ولا تخزون في ضيفي أليس منكم رجل رشيد

translation: They said, 'We have learned that we have no power over your daughters, and indeed, you know what we desire.'
interpretation: The verse reveals the conversation between the disbelievers and the Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) regarding their desire to commit sodomy with his daughters. The disbelievers acknowledged that they had no power over the daughters and recognized that the Prophet Lot knew their intentions. This verse highlights the depravity and sinful nature of the disbelievers and their disregard for the sanctity of family relationships. It also underscores the importance of protecting the family and the community from such immoral behavior.
orig: قالوا لقد علمت ما لنا في بناتك من حق وإنك لتعلم ما نريد

translation: And if I had wished to have a son, I would have taken a companion from the angels. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet's (peace be upon him) response to the disbelievers who accused him of being a sorcerer or a madman. He (peace be upon him) says that if he had wanted a son, he would have chosen an angel as a companion, implying that he has no need for a human son. The verse highlights the prophet's (peace be upon him) humility and his reliance on Allah, emphasizing that he is a chosen servant of Allah and has no need for worldly things. The verse also underscores the importance of faith and submission to Allah, reminding believers that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and that He is sufficient for those who put their trust in Him.
orig: قال لو أن لي بكم قوة أو آوي إلى ركن شديد

translation: They said: O Lot! Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord; they shall not reach you. So travel with your family in the cover of the night, and let no one of you look back, except your wife. Indeed, destruction will befall them at dawn.
interpretation: The verse describes the conversation between the angels and Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) before the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The angels inform Lot that they are messengers of his Lord and that the punishment will not reach him and his family. They instruct him to leave the city with his family under the cover of night and not to look back, except for his wife, who will be destroyed along with the rest of the town. The verse highlights the gravity of the situation and the urgency of the instruction, emphasizing the certainty of the punishment and the need for Lot and his family to leave immediately.
orig: قالوا يا لوط إنا رسل ربك لن يصلوا إليك فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك إنه مصيبها ما أصابهم إن موعدهم الصبح أليس الصبح بقريب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: مسومة عند ربك وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد

translation: And to the town of Midian, We sent their brother Shu'aib, saying: 'Worship Allah, you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a near day.'
interpretation: The verse describes the prophet Shu'aib's message to the people of Midian, who were known for their corruption and injustice. Shu'aib, who was sent by God to guide them, told them to worship only Allah and not to cheat in their measurements and weights. He warned them of the punishment that would come if they did not mend their ways. The verse highlights the importance of justice and honesty in all aspects of life, and the consequences of neglecting these values.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط

translation: And O my people, do not devour the wealth among yourselves in falsehood, nor seek to multiply your wealth by taking bribes, and do not harm the people in their properties, and do not act corruptly in the land.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, reminding them to avoid engaging in unjust practices that involve devouring the wealth of others through false means, such as bribery or fraud. It also warns them against harming others in their properties and encourages them to act with integrity and honesty in their dealings. The verse highlights the importance of ethical behavior and fairness in all aspects of life, emphasizing that true wealth and success come from God and cannot be achieved through unjust means.
orig: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And Allah has blessed you, O believers, if you were to know, and I am not a watcher over you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's blessing upon the believers, indicating that they have been chosen for guidance and are under God's protection. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet (peace be upon him) as a guide and teacher, rather than a watcher or guardian over the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be grateful for God's blessings and to recognize the Prophet's role in guiding them towards a righteous life.
orig: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: They said, 'O Shu'aib, does your prayer command you to abandon what our fathers worshiped, or to do something new with our wealth? Indeed, you are the knowledgeable, the wise one.'
interpretation: The verse portrays the reaction of the disbelievers towards Prophet Shu'aib's message, who accused him of abandoning the traditional religion of their forefathers and introducing something new and strange. The verse highlights the conflict between the old and the new, the traditional and the innovative, and the tension between the preservation of tradition and the need for change and reform. It also underscores the importance of knowledge and wisdom in navigating such conflicts, as embodied by Prophet Shu'aib, who is described as the knowledgeable and wise one.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد

translation: And seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him, indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Compassionate.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from God and turning to Him in repentance. The use of the phrase 'and then repent to Him' suggests that seeking forgiveness is not enough, but it must be followed by a sincere effort to change one's ways and turn towards God. The description of God as 'Merciful and Compassionate' highlights His attribute of forgiveness and His willingness to accept those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي رحيم ودود

translation: They said, 'O Shu'aib, does your prayer command you to do this? You are quite convincing. Indeed, we are in doubt concerning what you invite us to. Indeed, we fear that you are a mighty sorcerer.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers towards the prophet Shu'aib's message. They doubted his message and accused him of being a sorcerer, suggesting that his words were so convincing that they must have been magic. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the people towards the prophets and their message, and how they often resort to accusing them of witchcraft or sorcery. It also underscores the importance of faith and the need to trust in God's message and the prophets who deliver it.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ولولا رهطك لرجمناك وما أنت علينا بعزيز

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا إن ربي بما تعملون محيط

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and We seized those who committed wrongdoing with a severe punishment because they used to rebel against the command of their Lord. And they became as if they had never prospered in their homes.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Shu'aib and his people. God sent a command to Prophet Shu'aib to warn his people of the impending punishment if they did not stop their wicked ways. Prophet Shu'aib and the believers were saved by God's mercy, while the wicked were punished severely. The verse highlights the idea that those who disobey God's command will face severe consequences, while those who believe and follow His command will be saved.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse describes the prophethood of Moses and the miracles and clear evidence that were given to him by God. The phrase 'clear authority' refers to the fact that Moses' prophethood was not just a matter of personal opinion or interpretation, but was based on clear and indisputable signs and evidence that were witnessed by the people. The verse emphasizes the certainty and clarity of Moses' mission and the responsibility that came with it.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: Go to Pharaoh and his nobles, for they have become rebellious.
interpretation: The verse commands the prophet Moses to go to Pharaoh and his nobles, who have become rebellious against God's commandments. The verse highlights the authority and leadership of Pharaoh and his nobles, who have deviated from the righteous path and are leading their people astray. The verse serves as a reminder that leaders have a great responsibility to guide their people towards righteousness and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد

translation: Their Lord gives them the punishment of Fire. Surely, the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and enduring.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who deny the truth and choose to live in disobedience to God's commands. On the Day of Judgment, they will be punished with the Fire of Hell, which is a severe and enduring punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And follow this path, [O Prophet], and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to follow the path of righteousness and not to follow the inclinations of those who are ignorant of the truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of God and not being swayed by the desires of those who are ignorant of the spiritual truth. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to stay on the path of righteousness and to be mindful of the temptations of the ignorant.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, so their gods which they called upon besides Allah did not avail them when the decree of your Lord came upon them. They only increased them in destruction.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the people's destruction was not caused by God's injustice, but rather by their own wrongdoing. The gods they worshipped besides Allah were powerless to save them when God's decree came upon them. The verse highlights the idea that the people's reliance on false deities and their rejection of the true God led to their downfall. The phrase 'their gods did not avail them' suggests that their idolatry was futile and could not protect them from the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who turn away from the truth and instead rely on false idols, reminding them that their actions will ultimately lead to destruction.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: And indeed, your Lord is not averted from the punishment of the cities, even if they are destroyed, while they are wicked. Indeed, His punishment will be severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God's punishment is inevitable and will not be averted, even if the cities are destroyed, as a result of their wicked deeds. The use of the word 'even' twice in the verse underscores the certainty and severity of the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that God's punishment is not to be taken lightly and that it will be severe.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. This is a day when mankind will be gathered together, and this is a day that will be witnessed.
interpretation: The verse highlights the significance of the Day of Judgment, where all humanity will be gathered and judged according to their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter, emphasizing the importance of living a righteous life and being prepared for the ultimate accountability. The phrase 'يوم مشهود' (a witnessed day) underscores the idea that the events of that day will be plainly visible and inescapable, serving as a warning to those who reject the idea of accountability.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: On the Day when they will not be able to speak, and they will not be allowed to excuse themselves. And their deeds will be fruitless, and they will be void.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when people will be unable to speak in their defense, and their deeds will be of no avail. It emphasizes the idea that on that Day, people will be held accountable for their actions, and no excuses or justifications will be accepted. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a virtuous life and being mindful of one's actions, as they will have consequences in the hereafter.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: As for those who have earned evil, their reward is in the Fire, where they will have boiling water and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have earned evil deeds. Their reward is the Fire of Hell, where they will suffer a painful punishment, symbolized by boiling water. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment is proportionate to the evil deeds committed by the individual. The boiling water is seen as a metaphor for the intense suffering that awaits those who have chosen to live a life of sin and injustice.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed the likes of you, but you are not aware. And indeed, the heavens and the earth are not exhausted by your Lord's decree, indeed, your Lord is Ever-Doer of what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and authority over the universe. The phrase 'And indeed, We have destroyed the likes of you' refers to the destruction of previous nations that were similar to the current generation, indicating that God's punishment is not limited to any particular group of people. The phrase 'but you are not aware' highlights the ignorance of the current generation towards God's past punishments, and serves as a warning to them. The second part of the verse, 'And indeed, the heavens and the earth are not exhausted by your Lord's decree', emphasizes God's power and control over the universe, indicating that nothing can escape His will. The final phrase, 'indeed, your Lord is Ever-Doer of what He wills', reinforces God's sovereignty and authority, emphasizing that He is the one who carries out His will, and no one can stop Him.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: And as for those who are fortunate, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift unending.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the righteous, who will dwell in Paradise for eternity. The verse emphasizes the idea that the duration of their stay in Paradise is not limited by the lifespan of the heavens and the earth, but rather it is a gift from God that will last forever. The verse also highlights the idea that God's will is the ultimate authority and He can change the duration of their stay in Paradise according to His will.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: And do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping only Allah, the Creator of the universe, and not to worship any other being or object, including the sun or the moon, which are often worshiped by pagans. The verse emphasizes the exclusive nature of worship and warns against the dangers of polytheism, reminding believers that Allah is the only one worthy of worship and that all other beings are mere creations of His.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And indeed, We have given Moses the Scripture, and it was disagreed upon by those who were given it, and had it not been for a word from your Lord, it would have been settled between them. And indeed, they are in doubt about it, confused.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation given to Prophet Moses, which was disputed by those who received it. The verse suggests that the disagreement among the recipients was due to their own limitations and lack of understanding, rather than any ambiguity in the revelation itself. The verse also implies that the true meaning of the revelation was only clear to those who were guided by God, and that others were left in confusion and doubt. The verse serves as a reminder that true understanding of God's revelation can only be achieved through faith and guidance from God, and that human understanding is limited and prone to error.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while its people were wrongdoers, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were inhabited by wrongdoers and how God's punishment came to them suddenly, either in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The verse emphasizes that this victory is clear and manifest, indicating that it is obvious and undeniable. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success and victory come from God's grace and support, and that they should not become arrogant or boastful about their achievements. Instead, they should remain humble and grateful to God for His blessings.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not incline towards those who are unjust, lest the Fire should touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah, then you will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to incline towards those who are unjust, lest they be touched by the Fire of Hell. The verse emphasizes the idea that the company one keeps has a significant impact on one's faith and ultimate destination. The phrase 'and you have no protectors other than Allah' underscores the idea that only God can protect and help those who are righteous. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their relationships and associations, lest they be led astray by the influence of those who are unjust.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and the Qur'an at the dawn. Indeed, the good deeds remove the evil deeds. That is a reminder for the mindful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer at the decline of the sun, which refers to the time when the sun begins to set, and continues until the darkness of the night. Additionally, the Qur'an should be recited at dawn. The verse highlights the significance of good deeds in offsetting evil deeds, signifying that the former cancels out the latter. This serves as a reminder for the mindful, encouraging them to engage in virtuous acts and avoid sinful behavior.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the trials and tribulations that believers may face in life, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges, promising good tidings for those who are patient and faithful. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials of life are a means of testing one's faith and that true believers will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many generations before you who were more powerful than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. And they enjoyed their time, but you have not been given an enjoyment like theirs, and you have been given a limited time.
interpretation: The verse highlights the transience of human life and the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and pleasures. The generations that came before were mightier and wealthier than the current generation, yet they were destroyed by God's punishment. Their enjoyment of life was short-lived, and they were not given a second chance. The verse serves as a reminder to the reader to not be too attached to the material world and to focus on the spiritual aspects of life, as it is the only way to achieve true happiness and eternal success.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the towns until He had sent to their mother city a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not have destroyed the towns except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's justice and mercy in dealing with the destruction of towns. The verse indicates that God would not have destroyed the towns if He had not first sent a messenger to warn the people of their wrongdoing and give them a chance to repent. The verse also suggests that the people of the towns were fully aware of their wrongdoing and had ample opportunity to change their ways, but chose not to do so. The verse serves as a reminder of God's justice and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And had your Lord willed, He would have made the people a single community, but they will continue to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of humanity and the fact that people have different beliefs, cultures, and ways of life. The verse suggests that despite these differences, people are all equal in the eyes of God and are all deserving of respect and dignity. The verse also highlights the idea that God's plan for humanity is not to make everyone the same, but to celebrate and appreciate the diversity of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to embrace and appreciate the differences between people, and to strive for unity and understanding, rather than trying to impose a single way of life on others.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: Except those who are spared by your Lord's mercy. And that is how their Creator originated their kind, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled that He may fill Hell with jinn and humans, all together.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to the destruction of towns that were unjust, specifically those who are spared by God's mercy. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's mercy is the reason for their survival, and that He is the one who created them and their destiny. The verse also mentions that the filling of Hell with both jinn and humans is a fulfillment of God's word, indicating that the punishment is not limited to one group but applies to all who reject God's message.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear proofs and signs in the stories of the prophets, and We have come to you with the truth and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the stories of the prophets in the Qur'an, which serve as clear proofs and signs for the believers. The verse highlights the importance of the prophets' stories as a means of guidance and a reminder for the believers, and underscores the truth and authenticity of the message conveyed by the prophets. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the Qur'an is a reminder and a source of guidance for the believers, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of not following the teachings of the prophets.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe, 'Act according to your ability, indeed we are acting.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and invites them to act according to their ability, indicating that the believers are also acting in accordance with their own beliefs and values. The verse emphasizes the idea of personal responsibility and the importance of taking action based on one's own beliefs and principles, rather than relying on others or waiting for external factors to change. The verse serves as a reminder that everyone has agency and the power to make choices and take action, and that it is up to each individual to take responsibility for their own life and beliefs.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And await the end of the world, indeed we are waiting.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and waiting for the inevitable end of the world. It serves as a reminder that the present life is temporary and that the ultimate destination is the hereafter. Believers are encouraged to focus on their spiritual growth and development while awaiting the end of the world, and to be prepared for the final judgment.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: And to Allah belong the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And the matter [of return] is not but to Him. So worship Him and rely upon Him, and sufficient is He as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah over all aspects of the universe, both seen and unseen. It reminds believers to focus their worship and reliance solely on Allah, acknowledging His sovereignty over all things. The verse also underscores the idea that Allah is the ultimate Disposer of affairs, and that He is sufficient to guide and manage all matters. This verse encourages believers to trust in Allah's plan and to seek guidance from Him in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Qur'an's revelation in Arabic, indicating its miraculous nature and the importance of the language in Islam. The verse also highlights the purpose of the Qur'an's revelation, which is to guide humanity towards understanding and righteousness. The use of the word "that" in the phrase "that you might understand" suggests a direct relationship between the Qur'an's revelation in Arabic and the intended understanding of its message. This verse underscores the significance of the Qur'an as a guide and a source of guidance for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And indeed, We have given you the clear victory and the manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the decisive victory that the believers achieved over their enemies, while the phrase 'manifest triumph' suggests that the victory was obvious and plain for all to see. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always with the believers and will grant them victory over their enemies, as long as they remain faithful and obedient to Him.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: And Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, I have seen in a dream eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph is sharing his dream with his father, Jacob. The dream includes a vision of eleven stars, the sun, and the moon, all of which are prostrating to Joseph. This dream is a sign of Joseph's future greatness and the fact that he will be elevated to a high position. The dream also symbolizes the submission of the celestial bodies to Joseph, indicating that he will have control over the natural world. The verse highlights Joseph's humility and his willingness to share his dream with his father, as well as Jacob's wisdom in interpreting the dream and recognizing its significance.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: And indeed, the devil will say to man, 'You have been following me, so will I not be your companion in the Hellfire?'
interpretation: The verse warns against following the temptations of Satan, who will try to mislead humans into sin and then abandon them in the Hereafter, leaving them to face the consequences of their actions alone. The verse emphasizes the deceptive nature of Satan and the importance of resisting his temptations in order to avoid falling into sin and earning God's punishment.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus your Lord has chosen you, and has taught you the interpretation of dreams, and has perfected His favor upon you, as He perfected it upon your fathers, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special relationship between God and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing God's choice of him as His messenger and His teaching him the interpretation of dreams. The verse also emphasizes the continuity of God's favor upon the Prophet and his ancestors, Abraham and Isaac, indicating that the Prophet's mission is a continuation of the mission of the previous prophets. The verse ends by emphasizing God's knowledge and wisdom, reminding the reader of God's omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: And certainly We gave to Moses and Aaron clear signs and manifest authority.
interpretation: The verse highlights the miraculous signs and clear authority given to Moses and Aaron by God to aid them in their mission to guide the Children of Israel. The phrase 'clear signs' refers to the miraculous acts that Moses and Aaron performed, such as turning the staff into a serpent and the parting of the Red Sea, which were tangible evidence of God's power and authority. 'Manifest authority' refers to the leadership and prophethood that was bestowed upon them, which was evident in their words and actions. The verse underscores the importance of God's support and assistance in the face of adversity and opposition.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: And they said: 'Yusuf and his brother are dearer to our father than us, though we are a group. Indeed, our father is in obvious error.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the jealousy and resentment of Joseph's brothers towards him and their father's favoritism towards him. The brothers believe that their father's love for Joseph and his brother is misplaced and that they are the ones who truly deserve his affection. The verse also suggests that the brothers are aware of their father's partiality towards Joseph, which may have contributed to their animosity towards him. The verse serves as a reminder that sibling rivalry and jealousy can lead to conflict and strife, and that it is important to address such issues before they escalate.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And kill Joseph or cast him into a land far away, so that your father's face may become bright and you may thereafter become a righteous people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the jealousy and hatred of Joseph's brothers towards him, and their plan to kill him or banish him from their father's land. The verse highlights the extreme measures they were willing to take to get rid of Joseph, and how their actions were motivated by their desire to please their father and appear righteous in his eyes. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of jealousy and the importance of treating others with kindness and compassion, rather than resorting to harmful and violent actions.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: And a speaker among them said, 'Do not kill Joseph or else you will be guilty of a great sin.' They agreed to throw him into a well, and his soul was likely to be lost in the bottom of the well. Indeed, in that were signs for those who are patient and grateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and how his brothers planned to kill him out of jealousy. One of them suggested that instead of killing him, they should throw him into a well, which they did. The verse highlights the moral of the story, which is that even in difficult situations, there are signs and lessons for those who are patient and grateful. The verse also emphasizes the importance of avoiding violence and finding alternative solutions to conflicts.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, 'O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph? Indeed, we are his sincere advisors.'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph, who had sold him into slavery, were trying to deceive their father Jacob by pretending to be concerned about Joseph's well-being and suggesting that they were his loyal advisors. However, their true intention was to get rid of Joseph and eliminate him as a potential threat to their own status and power. The verse highlights the brothers' cunning nature and their willingness to deceive their father in order to achieve their goals.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And I (Muhammad) say: 'My Lord! Surely these are a people who will not believe in me, and they are going to treat my warning as a lie.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his concern to Allah about the disbelievers who refuse to believe in his message. He fears that they will not only reject his message but also ridicule and mock him. The verse highlights the Prophet's anxiety and his desire for his people to believe and avoid the punishment that awaits them if they continue to disbelieve. It also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a warner and his responsibility to convey the message of Allah to his people.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said, 'We will eat the fruit of this date palm and ignore the owner.' Indeed, we will be victorious.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are determined to take the fruit of a date palm without the owner's permission. They believe that they will be successful in their plan and that they will not be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights the theme of rebellion and disobedience, as well as the consequences of such actions. It serves as a warning to those who seek to take what does not belong to them and to disregard the rights of others.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: And when they embarked on their journey, they were in a state of disagreement and disbelief, and they were saying, 'We will not be punished.'
interpretation: The verse describes the state of disbelief and arrogance of the people who embarked on a journey, thinking that they would not be held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights their state of disagreement and disbelief, indicating that they were not only rejecting the idea of accountability but also disputing among themselves about the possibility of punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that denying accountability and punishment is a sign of arrogance and disbelief, and that one should not be complacent in their actions, but rather be mindful of the consequences of their deeds.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their parents in the evening, weeping.
interpretation: The verse describes the regret and remorse of the people who have been warned of God's punishment. They come to their parents in the evening, weeping, indicating a sense of sorrow and repentance. The verse highlights the importance of family and the role of parents in guiding their children towards righteousness. It also emphasizes the idea that even in the face of certain punishment, there is still hope for forgiveness and a chance for redemption.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said, 'O our father, we have gone astray, and we have left Joseph with our belongings. A wolf has eaten him, and had we been truthful, we would not have been left with this disgrace.'
interpretation: The brothers of Joseph are trying to deceive their father, Jacob, by claiming that a wolf has eaten Joseph, and that they have left him with their belongings. They are attempting to cover up their crime of selling Joseph into slavery by blaming a wild animal for his disappearance. The verse highlights their dishonesty and the consequences of their actions, as they are now left with the guilt and shame of their betrayal.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they came upon a town that had been destroyed by a punishment from God. They said, 'Is this how God's judgment is? Rather, we have been oppressed.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a group of people come upon a town that has been destroyed by God's punishment. The people are shocked and ask if this is how God's judgment is. The verse highlights the idea that people often question God's justice when faced with calamities and destruction. The verse also suggests that people tend to blame their misfortunes on others, rather than recognizing and acknowledging their own mistakes and sins.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And a township came to pass, and their messenger said, 'Oh people, indeed we have been sent to you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner. And Allah is over all things a Witness.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a town that was visited by a prophet or messenger, who was sent by God to guide the people and warn them of the consequences of their actions. The messenger's message was one of hope and warning, inviting the people to turn towards God and live according to His commandments. The verse emphasizes the importance of the messenger's role as a witness and a bringer of good news, and serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of all that we do.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they were pursued by a curse and a manifest punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of the people's disobedience and their pursuit of worldly wealth and material possessions. The 'curse' refers to the spiritual punishment that befalls those who prioritize material wealth over their relationship with God. The 'manifest punishment' refers to the physical consequences that result from their actions, such as drought, famine, or other natural disasters. The verse warns against the dangers of materialism and the importance of living a life of spiritual integrity.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: And he who had bought him (Joseph) from Egypt, said to his wife: 'Make his stay comfortable, perhaps he will profit us or we shall adopt him as a son.' And thus We established Joseph in the land, and We taught him the interpretation of dreams. Indeed, God is predominant over His affair, but most people do not know.
interpretation: The verse describes how the man who bought Joseph from Egypt, presumably Potiphar, told his wife to make Joseph's stay comfortable, suggesting that they might profit from him or even adopt him as a son. The verse then goes on to state that God established Joseph in the land and taught him the interpretation of dreams. The verse emphasizes God's control and dominion over all affairs, but notes that most people are unaware of this fact.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when We gave the Scripture to Moses, he said, 'O my people, indeed I have harmed you through my absence. My Lord, forgive me and have mercy upon me in Your mercy.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is expressing his regret and remorse for his past actions, specifically, his absence from his people, which caused them harm. He recognizes that his absence was a mistake and seeks forgiveness from God and asks for His mercy. The verse highlights Moses' humility and willingness to take responsibility for his actions, as well as his dependence on God's mercy and forgiveness. It serves as a reminder to believers to acknowledge their mistakes, seek forgiveness, and rely on God's mercy.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own home, when you were unjust, and We gave you a promise, while you were in your home, and We tested you with a test. Then your Lord said, 'Get out of it, all of you! Indeed, My punishment will reach you.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of Prophet Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse emphasizes that the people were warned and tested by God, but they refused to change their ways and continued to live in sin. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse also highlights the idea that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of the individual's actions.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while they were unjust, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust, emphasizing that their punishment came suddenly, either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: And indeed, the Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting its status as a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The use of the phrase 'Lord of the worlds' emphasizes God's sovereignty over all creation and underscores the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance for all humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the Qur'an's sacred nature and its role in guiding humanity towards righteousness and spiritual growth.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: And indeed, Joseph brought his father's mistake. Indeed, We knew that you were mistaken, [O Joseph], so do not be sad over their deceit.
interpretation: The verse highlights the idea that Joseph's brothers had wronged him by selling him into slavery, but Joseph, who had been forgiven by God, chose not to hold a grudge against them. Instead, he sought to reassure them that they had not wronged him, but rather it was part of God's plan. The verse teaches the importance of forgiveness and the idea that our mistakes can be used for good in the hands of God. It also shows Joseph's maturity and faith in God's plan, as he chooses not to hold onto past wrongs, but instead, focuses on moving forward in a positive way.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And the wife of the righteous man, who was obedient to her husband, said: 'I see a light emerging from the direction of the city, and it is about to burn us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of a righteous woman who is aware of the coming punishment of God. She sees a light emerging from the city, which symbolizes the divine retribution that is about to befall the people. The verse highlights the wife's obedience to her husband and her concern for their safety. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be vigilant and mindful of the consequences of their actions, and to seek protection in God's mercy and guidance.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: And the Lord of the Throne will say: `Ah, I wish that I had not been invoked by them, for they have been led astray by their own desires and have been prevented from returning to Me. Their hands have been sealed and their ears have been blocked, and they have been left in the darkness of ignorance.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is expressing His regret over the fact that His servants have turned away from Him and have been led astray by their own desires. The phrase `I wish that I had not been invoked by them' suggests that God had been invoked by them, but they have not responded to His call. The phrase `their hands have been sealed and their ears have been blocked' is a metaphor that indicates that they have been prevented from returning to God, and are unable to hear His message or respond to His call. The phrase `they have been left in the darkness of ignorance' suggests that they are living in a state of spiritual darkness, unable to see the truth and follow the right path. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who reject God's message and continue to live in sin will be left in a state of spiritual ignorance and separation from God.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: And He (Abraham) said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' He (Allah) said, 'Do you not believe?' He (Abraham) said, 'Yes, but I ask in order to have certainty.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is curious about the process of resurrection and asks God to show him how He gives life to the dead. God responds by asking Abraham if he believes, to which Abraham replies that he does, but he wants to have certainty. This verse highlights Abraham's desire to understand the nature of resurrection and his faith in God's power to bring the dead back to life. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding in faith, as well as the relationship between faith and certainty.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then after them came generations who lost the spiritual capacity to recognize the signs of God, so they became heedless.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of ignoring the signs of God and the eventual loss of spiritual capacity to recognize them. The verse suggests that the people became heedless and lost their ability to recognize and appreciate the signs of God, leading to a spiritual decline. This serves as a warning to those who neglect the signs of God and live in disregard of His teachings.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين
