translation: He said, 'Do not be fooled by the fact that I have been given food and knowledge before you. Indeed, your Lord has given me wisdom and has taught me before that. Indeed, I have left behind a people who do not believe in Allah and are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Solomon's response to the people who were amazed by his wisdom and the food that was brought to him. Solomon explains that his wisdom and knowledge are not the result of his own efforts, but are a gift from God. He reminds them that he has left behind a people who do not believe in God and are disbelievers in the Hereafter, indicating that he has a deeper understanding of spiritual matters and is not impressed by their superficial amazement. The verse highlights the importance of faith and spirituality, and warns against being impressed by worldly possessions and knowledge, but instead, one should seek guidance from God and have faith in the Hereafter.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And We have followed the religion of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is from the grace of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the prophets, specifically Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who were known for their righteousness and faith in one God. The verse also highlights the idea that the blessings and grace of God are not limited to a particular group of people, but are available to all, yet many people fail to recognize and appreciate these blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for the blessings we have received and to recognize the source of those blessings, which is the grace of God.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, how I wish that instead of us, the punishment of Allah would come to those who are unjust!
interpretation: The verse is a supplication made by Prophet Joseph while he was in prison, expressing his desire that the punishment of God would come to the unjust people instead of himself and his two companions. The verse highlights the prophet's compassion and concern for others, even in the midst of his own suffering. It also underscores the idea that the punishment of God is reserved for those who are unjust and that the righteous should not be subjected to it.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: And most of the people do not believe in Allah except that they attribute partners to Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the common sin of shirk, or associating partners with Allah. The verse emphasizes that people tend to attribute partners to Allah, thereby denying the oneness of God. The verse warns against this practice and reminds the reader that Allah is the only one worthy of worship and that the belief in the oneness of God is a fundamental aspect of Islam.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his lord a drink of wine, and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the bird will eat from his head, the matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse speaks about two prisoners, one of whom will be executed and the other will be spared. The verse uses metaphors to describe their fates. The first prisoner will be given a drink of wine, symbolizing his impending execution, while the second prisoner will be crucified and have birds eat from his head, representing his humiliation and suffering. The verse highlights the contrast between the two prisoners' fates and emphasizes the predetermined nature of their destinies.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And he who had been granted wisdom from the Qur'an, he said, 'My Lord, indeed I fear that they will be destroyed by Your punishment.' So he invoked his Lord, 'Indeed, I have been wronged by my enemies, so take me out of this prison, Lord, and make me victorious over them.'
interpretation: The verse describes a wise person who, upon reflecting on the Qur'an, realizes that the people who have wronged him will be destroyed by God's punishment. The wise person then prays to God, acknowledging their wrongdoing and asking for deliverance from their enemies. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from the Qur'an and the power of prayer in times of hardship.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes of wheat and others dried up. O my dear women, inform me, for I see a vision',
interpretation: The king's dream is a metaphorical representation of the cycle of life and death, where the seven fat cows represent prosperity and abundance, while the seven lean cows represent famine and scarcity. The seven green spikes of wheat represent growth and abundance, while the dried up ones represent decay and death. The dream is a reminder that life is full of ups and downs, and that we must be prepared for both prosperity and adversity. The king's request for interpretation from his women reflects his recognition of the prophetic nature of dreams and his desire to understand the message being conveyed to him.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, 'We have been overcome by a great calamity; what have we neglected in our fathers' religion that we have been punished in this way?',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been punished by God for their sins. They are in disbelief and shock, wondering what they have done wrong and how they have failed in their religious duties. The verse highlights the idea that the punishment is a consequence of their neglect and disobedience, and that they have ignored the lessons and guidance of their ancestors. The verse serves as a reminder to the reader to reflect on their actions and to learn from the mistakes of the past in order to avoid similar consequences.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: And he who was saved from them both (the men) said: "I will inform you of (the tiding) which has been revealed to me, that I have been given knowledge of the interpretation of the verse."
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the two men who were punished by God for their sins. One of them, who was saved, reveals that he has been given knowledge of the interpretation of the verse, indicating that he has been chosen by God to spread His message. The verse highlights the idea that those who are chosen by God are given the knowledge and understanding to interpret and spread His message, and that they have a responsibility to do so.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: And Joseph said to his brother, 'I will seek forgiveness for you from your Lord, indeed, He is merciful.'
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph is speaking to his brother after he has been reunited with him after many years. Joseph has been through a lot of hardships and trials, and he recognizes that his brother has also suffered. Joseph is seeking forgiveness for his brother from God, acknowledging that God is merciful and that He has the power to forgive. This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the power of mercy. It also shows the close relationship between Joseph and his brother, and how they are able to support each other through difficult times.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'We have been destroyed for seven years of famine.' Then, when they saw the punishment, they said, 'Alas, this is what we deserved! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been punished by God for their wrongdoing. They acknowledge that they have been suffering from a seven-year famine, but instead of repenting and turning to God, they blame their misfortunes on their own sins. The verse highlights the tendency of people to acknowledge their mistakes only when they are faced with the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'indeed, we have been wrongdoers' suggests a sense of regret and recognition of their own guilt.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then there came after them seven fat cows which ate up all that they had left behind.,
interpretation: The verse speaks about a series of seven consecutive years of abundance, represented by the seven fat cows, which consumed all the excess wealth and resources that the people had hoarded during the previous years of plenty. The verse suggests that the people had become complacent and self-sufficient, relying on their own abilities and wealth rather than recognizing and being grateful for God's provision. The seven fat cows represent the natural consequences of excessive materialism and the depletion of resources that result from human greed and neglect of God's blessings.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then after that, there will come a year in which the people will be abundant, and in it, they will be relieved.
interpretation: The verse describes a time of prosperity and abundance that will come after a period of hardship and destruction. The phrase 'yaghath al-nas' (يغاث الناس) means 'the people will be relieved' or 'the people will be at ease', indicating a time of peace and prosperity. The verse suggests that this period of abundance will be a time of blessing and comfort for the believers, who will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance during the previous period of hardship.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: And the king said, 'Bring me this prophet so that he may come to me.' But when the messenger came to him, he said, 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to increase my share of knowledge.' Indeed, my Lord is knowledgeable of the unseen.
interpretation: The king in this verse is depicted as someone who is eager to learn from the prophet and seek his guidance. However, the prophet refuses to comply with the king's request and instead advises him to seek knowledge from God. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge from God and recognizing His power and wisdom. The prophet's response also suggests that true knowledge and wisdom come from God, and that one should seek guidance from Him directly rather than relying solely on human sources.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: And certainly, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like carded wool.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's punishment and its proximity, indicating that it is near and imminent. The verse also uses vivid imagery to describe the Day of Judgment, likening people to scattered moths and mountains to carded wool, suggesting a scene of chaos and disorder. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human beings and the need to prepare for the hereafter.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I (the Prophet) do not absolve myself (of blame). Indeed, the human soul is prone to evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's humility and awareness of his own fallibility. He acknowledges that he is not immune to making mistakes and that his soul, like all human souls, is prone to evil thoughts and actions. However, the Prophet also recognizes that he has received God's mercy and forgiveness, which has helped him to overcome his own shortcomings. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers that they too are susceptible to sin and must seek God's mercy and forgiveness in order to overcome their own flaws and achieve spiritual growth.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: And the king said, 'Bring me a wicked man, so that he may do my bidding.' But when the wicked man came, the king said, 'Indeed, I will give you a reward today, for you have been faithful to me.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a king who is looking for a wicked person to carry out his evil deeds. The king's intention is to use this person for his own benefit, promising him a reward in return for his loyalty. The verse highlights the king's manipulative nature and his willingness to use others for his own gain. It also suggests that the wicked person is aware of the king's intentions and is willing to go along with them in exchange for a reward. The verse serves as a warning against seeking power and wealth through immoral means and the consequences of such actions.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: And He said, 'Make me a minister over the stores of the earth, indeed I am a faithful keeper.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Joseph is asking for authority over the stores of the earth, indicating his desire to be a ruler or a leader. The phrase 'faithful keeper' suggests that Joseph is a trustworthy and reliable individual who can be entrusted with such authority. This verse highlights Joseph's ambition and leadership qualities, as well as his belief in his own abilities to govern and manage resources effectively.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have given you (O Muhammad) a clear conquest and a victory. And We have aided you with wealth and children and made you a respected and blessed leader.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community. The verse emphasizes the idea of a clear victory and a manifest triumph, indicating that the Prophet's mission was successful and that he was able to convey the message of Islam effectively. Additionally, the verse mentions the prosperity and abundance that God has granted the Prophet and his followers, including wealth, children, and respected leadership. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and blessings upon the Muslim community and encourages them to continue following the teachings of the Prophet to maintain these blessings.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and were pious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the superiority of the reward in the Hereafter for those who believe and lead a pious life. The phrase 'خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون' emphasizes that the reward is not just for belief, but also for good deeds and righteousness. The verse encourages believers to focus on their spiritual growth and development, as the ultimate reward lies in the Hereafter, rather than in this world.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And Joseph's brothers came and charged him with a false accusation, and they were aware of his identity, but he did not recognize them.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene where Joseph's brothers, who were jealous of his status and feared his dreams, plotted against him and falsely accused him of a crime. The verse highlights the irony that while Joseph's brothers were aware of his identity, Joseph himself did not recognize them, indicating that they were strangers to him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and appreciating the people around us, and how neglecting to do so can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when they had come to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been forbidden this rich pasture, so either you come with us or we will leave it.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the people of the town are being prohibited from accessing a rich pasture, and they are asking their father to either join them in leaving it or to come with them to find another place. The verse highlights the importance of family and community, as well as the challenge of making difficult decisions together. It also touches on the theme of sacrifice and the willingness to give up something valuable for the greater good.
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: And indeed, if you do not bring it to me, [I shall take] no compensation from you, and My punishment will not be averted from you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the seriousness of the warning given to the people. The speaker is telling the people that if they do not bring the punishment upon themselves by their own actions, then God's punishment will still come to them. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is inevitable and that it will not be averted by any means. The speaker is essentially saying that they have a choice, either they bring the punishment upon themselves or God will bring it upon them. The verse also highlights the idea that God's punishment is not something to be taken lightly and that it should be taken seriously.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, 'We will slaughter the son of this woman, and indeed we will be forgiven.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Prophet Abraham's town, who planned to sacrifice his son Ismail as a test of their faith. They believed that by sacrificing Ismail, they would be forgiven for their sins. The verse highlights the misguided beliefs of the people, who thought that they could earn God's forgiveness through such a drastic act, rather than recognizing the true purpose of sacrifice, which is to submit to God's will and obey His commandments.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: And he said to his servants, 'Let them be dressed in their finery and adornments, and let them be parade before them, for they will be recognized by their appearance.'
interpretation: The verse describes the instructions given by a leader to his servants, commanding them to dress up in their finest attire and adornments, and to parade before him. The purpose of this command is to showcase the beauty and splendor of the leader's entourage, and to create an impression of grandeur and power. The verse highlights the importance of appearance and presentation in creating an image of authority and majesty, and serves as a reminder of the significance of projecting power and influence in leadership.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been forbidden to enjoy the king's food, for we have promised to eat nothing but the fruit of the tree until our brother is restored to us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the conversation between Joseph's brothers and their father, Jacob, after they had sold Joseph into slavery. The brothers are trying to explain why they cannot enjoy the king's food, revealing that they had promised to eat nothing but the fruit of the tree until their brother is restored to them. The verse highlights the brothers' remorse and guilt for their past actions and their desire to make amends. It also underscores the importance of family and the bond between siblings, as the brothers are willing to make sacrifices for the sake of their brother's return.
orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And He said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate, but enter from different gates. And I will not avail you against Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah. In Him I have put my trust, and in Him those who have faith should put their trust.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Abraham is advising his sons to enter the city through different gates, indicating that they should not put all their trust in one path or strategy, but rather diversify their approach and put their trust in God. The verse emphasizes the idea that ultimate success and guidance come from God alone, and that relying solely on one's own plans and efforts will not be enough. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in God's plan and to trust in His guidance, rather than relying solely on their own abilities.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And they have entered into their Lord's wrath, for they were not guided by what their fathers were guided by, and they were not given any share in the knowledge of their Lord, but they denied it, and they will surely be subject to punishment for their sins.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where people have gone astray and are not following the guidance of their ancestors, and they have also failed to acquire any knowledge of their Lord. They have denied the truth and will therefore face punishment for their sins. The verse emphasizes the idea that knowledge and guidance come from God, and those who reject this guidance will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he brought his brother to himself and said, 'I am your brother, so do not grieve over what they used to do.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Joseph's brothers, who had sold him into slavery and lied to their father about his fate, finally meet him again. Joseph, who has since risen to a high position in Egypt, greets his brother with kindness and compassion, reassuring him that he is his brother and that he should not worry about the past. The verse highlights Joseph's forgiving nature and his ability to overcome past hurts and betrayals. It also serves as a reminder to believers to forgive those who have wronged them and to treat their families with kindness and compassion.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And when they had covered themselves with their covering, he said: 'Ask forgiveness from your Lord, indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of Prophet Joseph's brothers who had wronged him and were seeking forgiveness. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness from God, who is merciful and forgiving. The use of the word 'Perpetual Forgiver' emphasizes God's attribute of forgiveness and His willingness to forgive those who seek forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness for their sins and to turn to God in repentance.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, 'We have been oppressed. We have been neglected.' They were told, 'What have you been neglected in?',
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been oppressed and neglected. They are complaining about their situation and feeling abandoned. The response they receive is a question, asking them what they have been neglected in, implying that they have not been neglected in anything significant or important. The verse highlights the theme of oppression and the lack of empathy and understanding from those in power towards those who are suffering.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said, 'We have lost our wealth and children, and our people have come to us with nothing but worthless talk.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers in Mecca when they were confronted with the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They were skeptical and dismissive of the message, saying that they had lost their wealth and children and that the Prophet's message was nothing but empty words. The verse highlights the disbelievers' arrogance and unwillingness to listen to the message of Islam, which ultimately led to their downfall.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, 'We have been destroyed, indeed we have been cut off. Are we to be punished for what we did while we were in a state of intoxication?',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been destroyed and are now facing the consequences of their actions. They are in a state of denial and disbelief, questioning the justice of their punishment. They are essentially asking if they are being punished for their actions while they were in a state of intoxication, indicating that they do not remember their actions or take responsibility for them. The verse highlights the theme of accountability and the idea that one's actions have consequences, regardless of whether they were committed in a state of intoxication or not.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said, 'What! Shall we give up our gods and worship him?',
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelief and resistance of the polytheists towards the message of Prophet Abraham. They were asked to give up their false gods and worship the one true God, but they refused, indicating their unwillingness to let go of their misguided beliefs and practices. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and submitting to the truth, and the consequences of rejecting the message of the prophets.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They said, 'We have lost our wealth and children.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the regret and remorse of the unbelievers on the Day of Judgment, when they will realize the consequences of their disbelief and the loss of their wealth and children, who were a source of joy and comfort in this life, but will not be of any avail in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly possessions and the importance of seeking guidance and righteousness in order to attain true success and happiness.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, 'He has stolen.' And they were saying, 'We have found nothing with him.' And Joseph kept it hidden within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are worse than this. Allah is aware of what you describe.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where Joseph's brothers accused him of stealing and claimed that they found nothing with him. However, Joseph knew that they were lying and had actually stolen from him. He chose not to reveal this to them and instead, he kept it hidden and trusted in God's justice. The verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's justice, even in the face of false accusations and betrayal. It also emphasizes the gravity of slander and false accusations, and how they can cause harm to others and damage their reputation.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, 'O noble one! Indeed, he has a father who is a respected elder. So, we will give you his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people are addressing a noble person, possibly a leader or a person of high social status. They are suggesting that the noble person's father is a respected elder and that they will give him a place of honor. The verse highlights the respect and deference shown to the noble person and his father, as well as the perception of the noble person as a righteous individual.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: And indeed, We will take revenge from the oppressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's promise to take revenge on behalf of the oppressed. The verse addresses the oppressors, warning them that they will face God's punishment for their injustices. The phrase 'من وجدنا متاعنا عنده' (from those who wronged us) suggests that God will take revenge on behalf of those who have been wronged, indicating that He is the protector of the oppressed and the just. The verse serves as a warning to oppressors, reminding them that their actions will not go unpunished and that God will bring justice to those who have been wronged.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: And they had sought victory and revenge, but every mighty man was defeated. He said, 'Indeed, I have won to Allah, and to my Lord is the return. Indeed, I have been wronged, so Allah will judge between me and you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of Prophet Joseph's brothers when they realized that their plan to harm him had failed. They had sought victory and revenge, but their efforts were thwarted. The eldest brother, who had been the leader of the group, acknowledges that he has been defeated and recognizes that his actions were wrong. He accepts responsibility for his mistakes and acknowledges that he will face judgment from God. The verse highlights the importance of accountability and the recognition of one's mistakes, as well as the belief in a higher power that will ultimately bring justice.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: And they have come back to their father, and said, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not witness except what we knew, and we were not watchful over the unseen.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene where the brothers of Joseph return to their father, Jacob, and confess that they have been deceived by their brother's theft. They explain that they did not witness the the theft itself, but only knew about it through their knowledge of their brother's character. The verse highlights the brothers' attempt to cover up their own wrongdoing by blaming their brother, and their failure to take responsibility for their actions. It also emphasizes the importance of honesty and integrity, as the brothers' deception is contrasted with Joseph's honesty and integrity, which is evident in his response to their accusations.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the village that was struck by the storm and the dawn that was brought near.
interpretation: The verse is a continuation of the previous verse, where God is commanding the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to ask the people of the village that was struck by a storm and the dawn that was brought near. The verse is referring to the story of the people of the village who were punished by God for their sins and how they were warned by the Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) before the punishment came. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobeying God's commands and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And indeed, We will support you with a mighty victory. And indeed, We will aid you with a triumphant aid. And indeed, We will guide you to a straight path. And indeed, We will grant you a manifest triumph. And indeed, We will give you a clear victory. And indeed, We will aid you with a mighty victory. And indeed, We will support you with a triumphant aid.
interpretation: This verse is a series of promises from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. God promises to give them a clear victory, a manifest triumph, and a mighty victory. He also promises to aid them with a triumphant aid and guide them to a straight path. This verse is a source of encouragement and hope for the believers, reminding them that God is always with them and will support them in their struggles. The repetition of the phrase "And indeed" emphasizes the certainty and magnitude of God's support and victory. The verse also highlights the importance of faith and perseverance, as the believers are reminded to remain steadfast and patient, knowing that God's help is always near.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow for Joseph!' And his eyes turned white with grief.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of Jacob, also known as Israel, upon learning about the supposed death of his son Joseph. The verse highlights Jacob's intense grief and sorrow, as he is described as turning away from the people and expressing his sorrow for Joseph. The phrase 'his eyes turned white with grief' emphasizes the depth of his sadness and emotional pain. The verse serves as an example of the intense love and attachment that a parent can have for their child, and the devastating impact that the loss of a child can have on a parent's life.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: And they said: 'Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If only we had been steadfast, we would not have been destroyed.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people who have been destroyed are speaking to God, acknowledging that they have wronged themselves and recognizing that their destruction is a result of their own actions. They express regret and a desire to have been steadfast in their faith, suggesting that they had been warned but did not heed the warning. The verse highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions and staying true to one's beliefs, as well as the consequences of neglecting this responsibility.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: And I (Muhammad) complain of my grief and my sorrow to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his deep sadness and grief to God, indicating that he is turning to God in his distress and seeking comfort and guidance from Him. The verse highlights the Prophet's strong faith in God and his dependence on Him, as well as his awareness of the limitations of human knowledge and the importance of seeking guidance from God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to turn to God in times of hardship and to seek guidance and comfort from Him.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: The verse is a command from Jacob to his sons to go and find out about the whereabouts of Joseph and his brother Benjamin. The verse also contains a message of hope and encouragement, reminding the sons that they should not lose faith in the mercy of God, as it is always available to those who believe and have faith. The exception is made for those who are disbelievers, who do not have faith in God's mercy and are thereby excluded from its benefits.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: And when they entered upon him, they said, 'O woe to us! Surely, we have been guilty of wrongdoing!'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the people of the town entered the presence of the prophet Lot and realized the gravity of their sinful actions. They acknowledged their guilt and the injustice they had committed, and they feared the punishment that was about to befall them. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging one's mistakes, and seeking forgiveness before it's too late.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: And recall when Joseph said to his brother, 'Are you aware of what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf) and his brothers. Joseph, who had been thrown into a well and later became a powerful leader in Egypt, confronts his brothers who had betrayed him. He asks them if they remember what they did to him and his brother (Benjamin) when they were ignorant (of the consequences of their actions). The verse highlights the theme of justice and accountability. Joseph, who had forgiven his brothers, reminds them of their past wrongdoing to emphasize the importance of recognizing and learning from one's mistakes.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, 'You are but a man, Yusuf! Your father was a man before you, and his brother is with him. Indeed, Allah has chosen you, and He has taught you the interpretation of dreams and the Scripture. Indeed, you are one of the messengers.
interpretation: The verse is a response to Yusuf's (Joseph) brothers' accusation that he is just a man and that his father Jacob's favoritism towards him is unfair. Yusuf responds by acknowledging his humanity but also emphasizing that he has been chosen by God and has been given the ability to interpret dreams and understand the scripture. He is not just a regular man, but a prophet and a messenger of God, chosen to spread God's message and guide people towards righteousness.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, 'We have been harmed by our Lord. Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the reaction of the people who were destroyed by God's punishment. They acknowledged that they were wrongdoers and admitted that they had been harmed by their own actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of our actions will catch up with us, and that we must take responsibility for our mistakes and turn to God for forgiveness and guidance.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: And He said, 'Do not be grieved, for today I will forgive you, and Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, comforting them not to be sad, as their sins will be forgiven. The verse highlights God's mercy and grace, emphasizing that He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who seek it, and that they should not lose hope in His mercy.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Go forth, (O Muhammad), and fight with them in the way of Allah those who fight with you, but transgress not the limits. Truly, Allah does not like the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to fight against those who fight against him and his followers, but warns against transgressing the limits set by God. It emphasizes that God does not like those who commit aggression and injustice. The verse highlights the importance of fighting in the cause of God, but also emphasizes the importance of doing so in a just and righteous manner, without resorting to aggression or violence beyond what is necessary. It serves as a reminder to Muslims that their actions must always be guided by justice and compassion, even in the midst of conflict.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the brother of Joseph came to them with the news, their father said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph in the air.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the brother of Joseph, who had been sent by their father to search for him, returns and reports that he has found Joseph's scent in the air. The father, recognizing the scent of his son, realizes that Joseph is still alive and is filled with joy and hope. The verse highlights the father's love and longing for his son, as well as his faith in God's plan, and serves as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, God's blessings and mercy can be found.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have been in a state of confusion and ignorance, but now we have found our way, so bless us in this newfound guidance.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people are addressing God and acknowledging their past state of confusion and ignorance. They are expressing their gratitude for having found the right path and seeking God's blessing in their newfound guidance. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging one's mistakes and seeking guidance from God. It also emphasizes the idea that guidance is a blessing from God, and that it is only through His mercy and grace that people can find their way out of confusion and ignorance.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: And when the messenger came to them, he said, 'I have come to you with a clear sign from your Lord. Surely, I will cut off the hand of the liar.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene where the prophet Moses is confronting the Pharaoh and his magicians, who had been rejecting the message of God. The verse emphasizes the certainty and finality of the punishment that will befall those who reject God's message. The phrase 'I will cut off the hand of the liar' is a metaphor for the severing of the relationship between the Pharaoh and his people, and serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and choose to follow falsehood. The verse highlights the importance of following the messengers of God and accepting their message, lest one faces the consequences of rejecting the truth.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask for us forgiveness for our sins, indeed we have been mistaken.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people are asking their father to seek forgiveness for their sins, acknowledging that they have been mistaken and recognizing the need for divine mercy. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the role of spiritual leaders in interceding on behalf of their communities. It also emphasizes the idea that mistakes are a natural part of the human experience and that seeking forgiveness is a necessary step towards spiritual growth and reconciliation with God.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: And I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord, indeed, He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: Muhammad (peace be upon him) is seeking forgiveness for his people from Allah (God) who is known for His mercy and forgiveness. This verse emphasizes God's attribute of being Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, indicating that He is always ready to forgive those who seek forgiveness and that He is merciful towards those who turn to Him in repentance. The verse serves as a reminder that seeking forgiveness is a fundamental aspect of Islam and that God is always ready to accept those who seek forgiveness.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, his father said, 'Indeed, I have perceived a refined scent, like the scent of Joseph.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reunion of Prophet Joseph with his father, Jacob. Jacob, who had been grieving for his son's supposed death for many years, suddenly senses Joseph's presence and recognizes his scent, which he associates with his son's unique fragrance. The verse highlights the deep emotional connection between a father and son, and how even after many years, the memory of a loved one can evoke powerful emotions. The verse also underscores the idea that even in the face of adversity, faith and hope can be rewarded, as Joseph's brothers had wronged him, but ultimately, he rose to a position of power and was reunited with his family.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And my father exalted me upon the throne, and fell down to me in prostration, and said, 'O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream of old, which my Lord has made true. Indeed, He was good to me when He took me out of the prison and brought me out of the bed of sickness, after the devil had stirred up strife between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: In this verse, Joseph's father, Jacob, recognizes the fulfillment of his dream, in which his sons would bow down to him. Jacob acknowledges that his dream has come true and attributes it to God's power and wisdom. He expresses gratitude for God's favor upon him, citing specific instances of God's blessings in his life, such as his release from prison and recovery from illness. The verse highlights the theme of God's sovereignty and wisdom in shaping events and the lives of individuals. It also underscores the importance of gratitude and recognition of God's favors.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord has given me knowledge of the kingdom and has taught me the interpretation of the Scriptures. The Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, where the speaker asks God to grant them knowledge and understanding of the Scriptures and to be their guardian in this life and the hereafter. The verse also expresses the speaker's desire to die a Muslim and be joined with the righteous in the afterlife. The verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from God, and the belief in the afterlife and the desire to live a righteous life in order to be among the righteous in the hereafter.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: And indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day they will come out of their graves quickly, their minds in a state of confusion, their eyes downcast, and their hearts in their throats, and they will say, 'Woe to us! What have we been heedless of this Day?',
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the people will be resurrected and face the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the event, as the people will come out of their graves quickly and in a state of confusion, with their minds in a state of disarray and their eyes downcast in shame. The verse also highlights the regret and remorse that the people will feel on that Day, as they realize the gravity of their mistakes and the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and heedlessness, reminding them of the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the need to repent and change their ways.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And most of the people, even if they were to believe, would not have been able to do so.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the majority of people, even if they were to believe in God and His message, would not have been able to do so because of their own limitations and weaknesses. This could be due to various reasons such as lack of understanding, misconceptions, or even arrogance. The verse highlights the idea that true faith and belief require a deep understanding and commitment, and that not everyone is capable of achieving it.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And what they are asking for is not [comparable to] the reward of those who believe and do righteous deeds, as if they were [destined to live] forever.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the vast difference between the reward of those who believe and do righteous deeds and what the disbelievers are asking for. The disbelievers are asking for temporary and material gains, while the believers will receive a reward that is eternal and infinite. The verse also highlights the fact that the disbelievers' focus is on the temporary life of this world, while the believers' focus is on the eternal life of the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to not be distracted by the temporary temptations of this world.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And there are signs in the heavens and the earth, and they pass by them, yet they turn away.
interpretation: The verse highlights the apathy and disregard of people towards the signs and reminders that God has placed in the heavens and the earth. Despite the abundance of evidence and warnings, people choose to ignore and disregard them, illustrating their disconnection from the natural world and their Creator. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being mindful and reflective of the signs around us, and the consequences of neglecting them.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that many people in the world do not truly believe in the oneness of God, and instead, they associate partners with Him. This can be seen in various forms of polytheism, where other beings or objects are given divine status alongside God. The verse suggests that this tendency to associate partners with God is a result of human weakness and a lack of faith in the unity and uniqueness of God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of this tendency and to remain steadfast in their belief in the oneness of God.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, 'This is my way, I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah, and I am not one of the polytheists.'
interpretation: The verse is a call to monotheism and a rejection of polytheism. The speaker invites others to follow them in their belief and worship of Allah, the one and only God, and rejects the idea of associating partners with God. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the right path and not succumbing to the temptation of idolatry or polytheism. The speaker is confident in their belief and invites others to join them in their devotion to Allah, the all-powerful and all-knowing God.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We have not sent before you any but men to whom We sent revelation, so ask the village dwellers about the truth of their stories.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that all prophets before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were also human beings, just like the people they were sent to guide. The verse challenges the disbelievers to ask the villagers about the stories of the previous prophets and the consequences they faced for their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new, but rather a continuation of the same message brought by all prophets, and that the consequences of rejecting the message will also be the same.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: And indeed, the messengers have been denied before you, and they were given a Scripture and a rational argument, but the unjust ones denied the truth, and they were arrogant and said, 'We will not be punished.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the messengers of God have been rejected and denied by people throughout history. Despite being given clear evidence and rational arguments, the wicked and arrogant people refused to believe in the message and instead denied the truth. They were convinced that they would not be held accountable for their actions and were skeptical of the idea of punishment. The verse serves as a reminder that denying God's message and being arrogant towards His messengers is a dangerous attitude, and that one should be mindful of the consequences of such behavior.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, but they did not perceive the warning.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God has destroyed many generations before the current one, but the people of the current generation are not paying heed to the warning signs and are repeating the same mistakes as their ancestors. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of their actions will be the same as those who came before them, and that they will face the same fate if they do not change their ways.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And how many a sign has come to them from their Lord, but they have disbelieved in it. Indeed, they are not going to believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the disbelievers have been given numerous signs and evidence of God's existence and prophethood, but they have chosen to reject them. The verse suggests that the disbelievers will not believe in the signs until they experience the painful punishment, indicating that they will not be convinced until it is too late. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and prophets, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah is He Who raised the heavens without any pillars, then He rose above the Throne, and He subjected the sun and the moon, each one runs to its appointed term, and He regulates the affair, distinguishing between the signs, that you may know that Allah is Able to do all things and that He is Able to reckon the number of His signs, indeed, He is aware of everything.
interpretation: This verse describes Allah's power and authority over the universe, emphasizing His ability to create and sustain all things without any need for support or assistance. The image of the sun and moon running their courses and fulfilling their appointed terms underscores the idea of Allah's sovereignty and control over all aspects of creation. The phrase 'He regulates the affair' suggests that Allah is actively involved in the management of the universe, ensuring that all things are in their proper place and functioning according to His will. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, encouraging believers to trust in His ability to guide and provide for them.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And He is the One Who has spread the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers, and from all fruits He has made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day; indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse describes God's power and wisdom in creating the earth and all that is in it. The verse highlights the balance and harmony in creation, as seen in the contrast between day and night, and the complementary nature of male and female in plants and animals. The verse also emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation, suggesting that the signs of God's creation are not just physical phenomena, but also spiritual and moral lessons for humanity. The verse encourages people to reflect on the beauty and harmony of creation and to recognize the power and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And on the earth are signs, plain to see, of the meeting of the Lord of the Worlds. Within themselves, in their ownselves, and in the alternation of night and day, and in the provision that God sends down from the sky, bringing life to the earth after its death, and in the turning about of the winds, are signs indeed for those who use their reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights the various signs that God has placed on earth, including the alternation of day and night, the provision of sustenance from the sky, and the turning of the winds. These signs are not only physical phenomena, but also symbolize the cycle of life and death, and the sustenance and provision that God provides for all living things. The verse emphasizes the importance of reason and reflection in recognizing and appreciating these signs, and encourages people to use their intellect to understand and appreciate the beauty and complexity of God's creation.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And indeed, they were, in their intoxication, unaware of Our signs, so they were, in their transgression, rejecting them.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who are ignorant of God's signs and reject His message. The word 'intoxication' (fa'jab) suggests a state of heedlessness and neglect, where the individuals are so consumed by their own desires and passions that they are oblivious to the signs of God's existence and wisdom. The phrase 'in their transgression' (bi-thalathil-ughla) implies that their rejection of God's message is a result of their own perverse nature and their desire to rebel against God's commandments. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in ignorance and rebellion, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's authority.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they will be hastening with you to do evil before good, and they have been preceded by the examples of their ancestors, and your Lord is Forgiving to people despite their wrongdoing, and your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse highlights the tendency of people to hasten towards evil deeds, and how they are influenced by the negative examples of their ancestors. Despite this, God's mercy and forgiveness are still available to them, but if they continue to persist in their wrongdoing, they will face the severity of God's punishment.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every nation is a guide.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to prove his prophethood. The verse responds by saying that the Prophet is only a warner, and that his role is to convey the message of God's Oneness and the consequences of disbelief. The verse also emphasizes that every nation has had its own guide, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not responsible for the guidance of the disbelievers. Rather, his duty is to convey the message, and guidance is only possible through God's grace.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: And Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs lose (i.e. miscarry) and what they grow (i.e. the fetus). And everything with Him is measured.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge and control over all aspects of creation, including the development and growth of fetuses in the womb. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of everything, from the smallest details of fetal development to the largest events in the universe. The verse also underscores the idea that everything in the universe, including human life, is accountable to God and subject to His will. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and sovereignty, and encourages believers to trust in His plan and wisdom.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: And they ask you about the spirit, say the spirit is from the command of my Lord, and the knowledge you have been given is but a little.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question about the nature of the spirit and its relationship to God's command. The verse emphasizes that the spirit is a part of God's command and is not something that can be fully comprehended or controlled by humans. The phrase 'the knowledge you have been given is but a little' suggests that human understanding of the spirit and its workings is limited, and that it is not something that can be fully known or mastered. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and the importance of humility in the face of God's vast and mysterious power.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: For them are angels in attendance, in front and behind, who guard them from Allah's command. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change their own condition. And when Allah wills harm for a people, there is no turning it back. And they have no protector besides Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the role of angels as guardians and protectors of the faithful, who are assigned to watch over them from both the front and the back. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God will not change the fate of a people unless they first change their own condition by turning back to Him. The verse warns that when God wills harm for a people, there is no escape or protection from it, and they will have no one to turn to for help except Him.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: And He it is Who shows you the lightning, causing fear and aspiration, and generates the heavy clouds.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and control over the forces of nature. The lightning is a symbol of God's wrath and punishment, striking fear in the hearts of those who see it. At the same time, it also inspires awe and wonder at the beauty and majesty of God's creation. The heavy clouds are a reminder of God's mercy and provision, as they bring forth rain to nourish the earth and sustain life. The verse serves as a reminder of God's dual role as a punisher and a provider, and encourages believers to reflect on their own relationship with God and their responsibility to live a righteous life.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: And the thunder praises Him, and the angels [too], out of fear of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, and they dispute about Allah, and He is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fear and reverence that the thunder and angels have for God, as they praise and glorify Him. The verse also highlights God's power and control over the forces of nature, as He sends thunderbolts and strikes those who disobey Him. The verse ends by mentioning that despite the signs and evidence of God's power, people still dispute and argue about the existence and attributes of God, and that He is severe in punishing those who disobey Him.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And to Allah prostrate all the stars and the angels, and the mountains, the trees, the animals, and many of the people. And many there are upon whom the punishment is justified.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of God's power and authority, as even the stars, angels, mountains, trees, and animals all submit to His will and prostrate to Him. The verse also mentions that many people are deserving of punishment, indicating that the consequences of their actions will be severe. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and being mindful of one's actions, as well as the consequences of not doing so.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then taken besides Him allies not to lose anything, but they will not benefit you, nor will they harm Him? Indeed, the wrongdoers are partners in the punishment. Those who have gone astray, and they have made for Allah partners, they have created partners for themselves. But Allah is the Creator of everything, and He is the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and warns against the dangers of polytheism. It questions the idea of taking other beings as allies or partners with God, suggesting that it is futile to do so, as they cannot benefit or harm Him. Instead, those who associate partners with God will be punished. The verse also highlights the idea that God is the sole creator of everything and is the only one worthy of worship.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: And We sent down from the sky water in quantity, and We caused it to stay with them, and We have made their cattle and their children to live in it, and We have made it (as) a sign for them, (and said), 'Have fear and obey Me, My servants, and I will give you a good life, certainly, I will give you a good life, certainly, I will give you a good life', and certainly, We will give them a good life, certainly, We will give them a good life.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of God upon the people, where He sent down rain from the sky in abundance, providing for their cattle and children, and making it a sign for them to have fear and obey Him. The verse emphasizes the idea of God's mercy and provision for His servants, and the promise of a good life for those who obey Him. The repetition of the phrase 'certainly' emphasizes the certainty of God's promise and the assurance of a good life for those who follow His commandments.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord with obedience, the reward is multiplied manyfold. But those who have not responded to Him, if they had all that is on earth and the like of it with them, they would have offered it as a ransom to avoid the evil reckoning. Theirs will be a painful punishment, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the righteous and the wicked. The former are rewarded abundantly for their obedience, while the latter, despite having all the riches and resources at their disposal, cannot escape the punishment for their disobedience. The verse emphasizes the idea that material wealth and possessions are of no use in the face of divine retribution. The wicked will face a painful punishment, and their final abode will be an evil place.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And those who are faithless to their covenant with Allah and they break their oaths.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who disregard their covenant with God and break their oaths. The verse implies that such individuals have failed to uphold their end of the agreement they made with God, which is to live according to His commandments and follow His teachings. By breaking their oaths, they have demonstrated their lack of commitment to God and their disregard for the responsibilities that come with being a member of God's community. This verse serves as a reminder that our relationship with God is built on trust and loyalty, and that breaking our promises with Him has consequences.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who are prayerful in their prayer and give zakat and have fear of their Lord, and fear the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of righteous individuals who are mindful of their prayer and give charity (zakat) regularly. They also have a deep fear of their Lord and the punishment of the Hereafter, which motivates them to live a virtuous life and avoid sin. The verse emphasizes the importance of a strong spiritual foundation, which is reflected in one's relationship with God and their commitment to acts of charity and good deeds.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, and they avert the evil deeds; those will have a reward of the Home,
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous, who are patient and seek the pleasure of God. They establish prayer and give charity, both secretly and openly, and avoid evil deeds. Their reward will be the Home, which refers to Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and happiness. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience, prayer, charity, and avoiding evil deeds as key aspects of a righteous life, and the reward that awaits those who live according to these principles.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: And the angels enter upon them from every gate, saying: 'Peace be upon you, because you were patient. How excellent is the final abode!'
interpretation: The verse describes the entrance of the angels into Paradise, greeting the righteous believers with peace and congratulating them on their excellent final abode. The verse emphasizes the reward of patience and the joy of entering Paradise, which is a result of their good deeds and faith. The angels' greeting serves as a reminder of God's mercy and grace, and the verse encourages believers to strive for a life of righteousness in order to attain this ultimate reward.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: And peace is upon you, O dwellers of the dwelling place, from the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse addresses the inhabitants of the dwelling place, which refers to the grave or the Hereafter. The verse wishes peace upon them, but it also implies that they have been afflicted with a great punishment in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that the punishment of the Hereafter is a reality and that it is a consequence of one's actions in this life. It also emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life to avoid the punishment of the Hereafter.
