orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after it has been ratified, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption in the land, it is they who are cursed, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who break God's covenant and go against His commands. They are warned of a severe punishment and cursed for their actions. The verse emphasizes the importance of keeping God's covenant and not breaking the rules and regulations set forth by Him. It also highlights the consequences of spreading corruption and severing what God has commanded to be joined, indicating that such actions will not go unpunished.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And Allah provides for whom He wills and restricts [the provision of] whom He wills. And they rejoice in the life of this world, and this world's life is not but a provision [compared to the Hereafter].
interpretation: The verse highlights God's sovereignty over the provision of sustenance and resources. God grants provision to whom He pleases and withholds it from whom He pleases, and people should not assume that their wealth and resources are solely the result of their own efforts. The verse also emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly life and its pleasures, reminding believers to focus on the eternal life to come and not to be distracted by the fleeting joys of this world.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who question the prophethood of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and demand a miraculous sign from God to prove his authenticity. The verse responds by saying that Muhammad is only a warner, and that his role is to convey the message of God, not to perform miracles. The verse also implies that the Qur'an itself is a guide for those who seek guidance, and that the signs and miracles mentioned in it are sufficient proof of its truth. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to God's will, rather than relying on miracles or signs to guide one's beliefs.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah, the hearts are assured.
interpretation: The verse highlights the positive impact of remembering Allah on the believers' hearts. The phrase 'الذين آمنوا' (those who believed) refers to those who have accepted Islam and submitted to Allah's will. 'تطمئن' (and their hearts are assured) implies that their faith has brought them a sense of peace and security. 'بذكر الله' (by the remembrance of Allah) shows that the act of remembering Allah, whether through prayer, recitation of the Qur'an, or other forms of worship, has a calming effect on the believers' hearts. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah as a means of attaining peace and tranquility in one's heart.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will reward them with a good reward and a high station.
interpretation: The verse highlights the relationship between faith and good deeds, emphasizing that both are necessary for a believer to attain a high station in the hereafter. The phrase 'الذين آمنوا' (those who believed) refers to those who have accepted Islam and submitted to God's will, while 'وعملوا الصالحات' (and did righteous deeds) highlights the importance of good deeds as a manifestation of one's faith. The reward promised by God is not limited to this life, but extends to the hereafter, where believers will be granted a high station in paradise. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a life of righteousness and to strive for spiritual excellence.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus, We have sent you (O Muhammad) to a community that was astray, to recite to them Our verses and purify them. They had indeed been disbelieving in the Most Merciful (God), saying, 'There is no god but He. He has taken care of us, and to Him we will return.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a mercy to humanity, sent by God to guide people who have gone astray. The verse highlights the importance of the Prophet's mission to recite God's verses and purify the people, implying that the message of Islam is not limited to mere intellectual understanding but also encompasses spiritual purification. The verse also references the disbelief of the disobedient communities who refused to acknowledge God's oneness, instead ascribing partners to Him. The verse ends with a statement of faith, affirming that there is no god but Allah, and that He is sufficient for us and to Him we will return.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if We had sent this Qur'an to mountains, you would have seen them humbled and come down, trembling, from fear of Allah. Or if We had caused the earth to swallow them or caused the heaven to fall upon them, behold, they would have cried out: 'Alas! Surely we did wrong.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the power and authority of the Qur'an, indicating that even the mountains would be humbled and tremble in fear of Allah if the Qur'an were sent to them. The verse also emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the message of the Qur'an, suggesting that those who refuse to believe will face severe punishment, either in this life or the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message, reminding them that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you [O Muhammad] from your Lord a revelation, a clear proof, a written book, and a Qur'an that We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a revelation from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The Qur'an is described as a 'clear proof' and a 'written book' that contains guidance and mercy for believers. The verse highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a mercy for those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. It also underscores the idea that the Qur'an is a detailed and comprehensive guide that contains knowledge and wisdom for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a decrease in wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that people may face in life, including fear, hunger, financial loss, and the loss of loved ones. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and resilience in the face of these challenges, and encourages believers to remain steadfast and faithful to God. The verse also reminds believers that these trials are a means of testing their faith and that they will ultimately be rewarded for their patience and perseverance.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: And indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity and eternal nature of the punishment in the Hereafter for those who disbelieve and lead a life of sin. The word 'far more severe' suggests that the punishment in the Hereafter is not only worse than any earthly punishment but also eternal, lasting forever. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live a life of disobedience, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face in the Afterlife.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those who were given knowledge before it, when they saw the verses of Allah, they fell upon their faces, prostrating, saying, 'Glory to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.' And they fall upon their faces weeping, and Allah's reward is not but for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of the people who were given knowledge before the revelation of the Qur'an. When they saw the verses of Allah, they were overcome with emotion and fell to the ground in prostration, acknowledging the glory of God and the fulfillment of His promise. They wept in humility and submission, recognizing the greatness of God and their own limitations. The verse highlights the importance of humility and submission to God, and the reward that awaits those who live righteously.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have followed it up with a warner in case they deny you, [O Muhammad], saying, 'Your Lord is not a guardian over them, and for you is no reward or protection from Allah',
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fact that the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic and that it serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet as a warner, whose duty is to convey the message of God, and the consequences of rejecting this message. The verse also touches upon the theme of the relationship between the Prophet and his people, emphasizing that the Prophet is not responsible for the guidance or protection of those who reject the message, and that his only responsibility is to convey the message clearly.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And indeed, We have sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by the permission of Allah. For every term, there is a book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of God's message and the unity of the prophetic mission. The verse states that God has sent messengers before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and that they too had families and descendants. The verse also highlights the fact that the prophets were not able to perform miracles or come with a sign except by the permission of God. This verse serves as a reminder that the prophets were not superhuman beings, but rather ordinary people chosen by God to convey His message. The verse also emphasizes the importance of the scriptures and the fact that there is a book for every term, indicating that God's message has been consistent throughout history.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: And God erases and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over His creation. The phrase 'yamhuwallah' (God erases) suggests that God has the power to erase or abolish anything He wills, while 'wa yuthbut' (and confirms) indicates that God also has the power to confirm and validate what He desires. The phrase 'wa `inda huwa ummu al-kitab' (and with Him is the Mother of the Book) is a reference to the fact that the Qur'an is the ultimate source of guidance and wisdom, and that it is with God that the knowledge and secrets of the universe are preserved. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the importance of seeking guidance from the Qur'an.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse encourages the believers to be patient and steadfast in the face of these challenges, assuring them that they will be rewarded for their perseverance. The verse also serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith, and that the true believers will be those who remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: And they did not apprehend that indeed We have been destroying the earth, diminishing it from its edges, and Allah's command is coming [upon them].
interpretation: The verse highlights the people's lack of awareness and appreciation of God's power and control over the earth. Despite the signs and warnings, they failed to recognize that God has been gradually reducing the earth's resources and boundaries. The verse serves as a reminder that God's command and judgment are imminent and inescapable, and that humans must be mindful of their actions and the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: And indeed, the plotters have planned their plot, but their plot was known to God, and their plot will be foiled. The disbelievers will be defeated in the end.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of those who reject God's message to plot against the believers and the Prophet (peace be upon him). However, their plots will ultimately fail, and they will be defeated. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of their schemes and will thwart them. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to put their trust in God and not to fear the plots of the disbelievers.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you [that] when you have gone forth in the earth, you will have no shelter or protection except that you come back to your Lord? And to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and refuse to believe in the Hereafter. They are asked rhetorically if they can be directed to a person who can inform them about what will happen to them after they leave this world. The answer is that they will have no refuge or protection except to return to their Lord, indicating that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions in this life and will face judgment from God. The verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and sovereignty of God and the inevitability of the Hereafter.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif, Lam, Mim. This is the revelation of the Book; in it is guidance sure, without a doubt, to those who fear God.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of the revelation of the Qur'an, which is a source of guidance for those who fear God. The letter Alif, Lam, Mim are used to emphasize the importance of the verse and to draw attention to the message being conveyed. The verse highlights the certainty of the guidance contained in the Qur'an and underscores the idea that it is only those who fear God that can truly benefit from it. The verse serves as a reminder of the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to guide humanity from darkness to light, and to encourage people to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all creation and serves as a warning to disbelievers of the severe punishment that awaits them if they continue to reject faith in Allah. The use of the word 'woe' suggests a sense of urgency and alarm, highlighting the gravity of the situation and the importance of heeding Allah's message.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: And those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and prevent [others] from the way of Allah, and they are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mistake of those who prioritize the temporal pleasures of this life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. Not only do they themselves choose to follow the path of disobedience, but they also try to mislead others and prevent them from following the path of Allah. Their actions are a result of their extreme ignorance and misguidance, and they will face severe consequences in the Hereafter.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except in the language of his people, so that he may clarify to them. But God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fact that all prophets were sent to their own people, speaking their language, in order to communicate effectively with them. The verse also highlights the power of God, who has the ability to guide or misguide whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of the prophets is not limited to a particular group, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their language or culture. It also underscores the idea that God's guidance and misguidance are not based on human will or effort, but are a manifestation of His divine power and wisdom.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, We have sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], 'Lead your people out of the darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah.' Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Moses and his mission to lead his people out of darkness and into the light. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and being grateful for the blessings of God, and how this is a sign of faith and patience. The phrase 'days of Allah' refers to the days of blessings and prosperity that God has given to His servants, and the importance of recognizing and appreciating them. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in darkness and ignorance, encouraging them to turn towards the light of guidance and truth.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, killing your sons and sparing your women.' Indeed, that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses reminds his people of the blessings they received from God, specifically the salvation He granted them from the Pharaoh and his people who were inflicting them with extreme punishment, killing their sons and sparing their women. The verse highlights the severity of the trial and the magnitude of God's favor in saving them from it. It serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and to recognize the magnitude of His favor, especially in times of hardship.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And indeed, your Lord is generous to you. But if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's generosity and bounty towards His creation, but also warns of the severe punishment that awaits those who reject His message and deny His existence. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of being grateful for God's blessings. It also highlights the contrast between the mercy and generosity of God and the severe punishment that awaits those who reject Him.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said, 'If you disbelieve, you and all who are on the earth, indeed God is free from need of you, and He is not pleased with disobedience.
interpretation: Moses is addressing the people who are rejecting God's message and warning them of the consequences of their disbelief. The verse emphasizes God's independence and lack of need for humanity's belief or obedience. It also highlights the idea that disobedience to God's commands is not acceptable and will result in punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human beings to God and the importance of living a life in accordance with His commands.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, "We are but men, like yourselves, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants. Indeed, we have come to you with a clear authority. So fear Allah and obey us, perhaps you may be given mercy."
interpretation: The verse highlights the humility and humbleness of the prophets and messengers of God. They are described as being like other men, with no superiority or divine nature. They emphasize that their message is not their own, but rather a favor and mercy from Allah. The verse also emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and His messengers, as a means of receiving mercy and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to humble themselves before God and to follow the guidance of His messengers, in order to receive His blessings and mercy.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: I told them: 'We are only human beings like yourselves, but God favors whom He wills of His servants. And it is not for us to bring a sign except by the permission of God. And upon God let the believers rely.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is addressing the disbelievers who were demanding a miracle or a sign from him to prove his prophethood. He tells them that he and his companions are only human beings like them, and that they have no power to bring a sign or perform a miracle except by the permission of God. The verse emphasizes the idea that God chooses whom He wills to be the recipients of His blessings and favors, and that the believers should put their trust in God alone. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to have faith in God's plan and to rely on Him alone for guidance and support.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And the disbelievers said to their messengers, 'We will drive you out of our land, or you will return to our religion.' But their Lord inspired to them, 'We will destroy the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers to the message of the prophets. They threaten to expel the prophets from their land or force them to convert to their religion. However, God reveals to the prophets that the wicked will be destroyed. The verse highlights the conflict between the believers and the disbelievers, with the latter trying to suppress the message of the former. The verse also underscores the powerlessness of the disbelievers against God's will and their ultimate fate of destruction.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will enable you to recite the Qur'an, and you will not forget except what Allah wills. Indeed, We will enable you to recite it, and it will not be forgotten,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its preservation. The verse assures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God will enable him to recite the Qur'an and that he will not forget any part of it, except what God wills. The verse also emphasizes that the Qur'an will not be forgotten and will be preserved for all time. This verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet and a reminder to future generations of the importance of preserving and memorizing the Qur'an.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And they have been commanded no more than this: 'Worship Allah, your Lord, and do not associate anything with Him.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the simplicity and clarity of the message of Islam, which is to worship Allah alone and avoid associating partners with Him. The verse highlights the fact that this message is not a burden or a difficult task, but rather a straightforward and clear guidance. The use of the word 'jabbar' (giant) to describe the polytheists, who associate partners with Allah, suggests that their beliefs and practices are oppressive and unjust. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and not to be swayed by the pressures of society or the temptations of the world.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: And from the evil of the hot wind which brings fiery smoke.
interpretation: This verse describes the suffering and punishment that will be faced by those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The 'hot wind' symbolizes the fiery anger of God, and the 'fiery smoke' represents the suffering and destruction that will befall those who reject God's mercy. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: And they denied their Lord's messenger, so the punishment overtook them in the morning, and We utterly destroyed them. Verily in this is a sign for people who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. Have you seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad? They were destroyed by a furious wind on a day of continuous calamity.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who denied their Lord's messenger and refused to believe in God's message. The punishment described in the verse is a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief. The use of the word 'furious wind' emphasizes the severity of the punishment and the suddenness of the destruction. The verse serves as a reminder to those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter and encourages them to believe in God's message and follow His commandments.
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? Indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and majesty of Allah as the Creator of the universe. The use of the phrase 'with truth' (bi-al-haqq) underscores the idea that Allah's creation is based on justice and righteousness. The verse also highlights the ease with which Allah created the universe, with the phrase 'and there touched Us no weariness' indicating that the creation of the heavens and the earth was effortless for Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's greatness and the importance of living according to His will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And they all came out to God, and the weak said to those who were arrogant, 'We were your followers, so will you now shield us from God's punishment?' They replied, 'Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us, whether we are patient or impatient, there is no escape from God's decree.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment where all people will be gathered before God, and the weak will confront the arrogant, asking for their protection from God's punishment. The arrogant will respond that they cannot protect them, as they themselves are also subject to God's decree, and that patience or impatience will not change their fate. The verse highlights the reality that no one can escape God's judgment, and that true guidance comes from God alone.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And the Satan said, when the matter was decided, 'Indeed, Allah has promised you the truth and promise of Allah is true, and I am afraid that you will not be able to bear the punishment which will befall you, so I will divert you from the command of Allah and entice you to my command. And if I had authority over you, I would not have left you in the world, but indeed, you will curse yourselves.
interpretation: In this verse, Satan is speaking to the people, trying to deceive them and lead them astray. He acknowledges that Allah's promise is true and that the punishment for their sins is certain. However, he tries to convince them that they will not be able to bear the punishment and that he will protect them from it by diverting them from Allah's command and enticing them to follow his own command. He also threatens that if he had the authority, he would not have left them in the world, implying that he would destroy them. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan and his attempts to mislead people from the right path.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein by permission of their Lord, their greeting therein: 'Peace!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who believed in God and did righteous deeds. They will be admitted to gardens, a place of eternal bliss and happiness, where they will live forever. The verse emphasizes the idea of eternity, using the phrase 'خالدين فيها' (abiding eternally) to emphasize that their stay in the gardens will never end. The verse also mentions the 'rivers' that flow beneath the gardens, indicating an abundance of provision and beauty. The greeting of 'peace' in the gardens highlights the sense of tranquility and peace that the believers will experience in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder of the rewards that await those who lead a righteous life and have faith in God.
orig: وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء

interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message and underscores the importance of spreading love, kindness, and compassion to all people.
orig: ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار

translation: Allah confirms those who believe with the sure word in this life and the Hereafter, and Allah misleads the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God's power and authority are supreme, and that He has the ability to guide and mislead as He sees fit. The phrase 'the sure word' refers to the promise of God, which is certain and true, and is a source of comfort and guidance for believers. The verse also highlights the contrast between the fate of believers and wrongdoers, with the former being guided and the latter being misled. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and adhering to God's commandments in order to receive His guidance and blessings.
orig: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء

translation: Have you not seen those who have exchanged the blessings of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of destruction?
interpretation: The verse addresses the ingratitude of those who have rejected Allah's blessings and instead chosen to live in disbelief, leading their people astray and inviting them to dwell in a place of destruction. The verse suggests that those who reject Allah's blessings will be punished in the hereafter, and their actions will lead to their own downfall.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار

translation: Hellfire will they invoke, and woeful indeed will be their resting place.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. They will be cast into Hellfire, which is a place of intense suffering and punishment. The verse emphasizes the horror of this fate, describing it as a 'woeful' place where they will have no peace or respite. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار

translation: And they set up rivals to Allah that they may lead astray from His way. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who set up rivals to Allah, such as idols or other deities, in order to lead others astray from Allah's path. The verse warns those who engage in such practices that they will ultimately end up in the Fire, indicating that their actions will lead to their destruction and eternal punishment.
orig: وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار

translation: Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes when there will be no trade nor friendship.
interpretation: In this verse, God instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remind the believers of the importance of establishing prayer and giving charity from the wealth that God has provided them. The verse emphasizes the need for both public and private worship, indicating that the believers should practice their faith openly and privately, without hypocrisy or show. The verse also warns of a future Day of Judgment when all worldly transactions and relationships will cease to exist, emphasizing the urgency of living a righteous life and preparing for the hereafter.
orig: قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم وسخر لكم الفلك لتجري في البحر بأمره وسخر لكم الأنهار

translation: By the sun and the moon, by the day and the night, by the heaven and the earth, and by the self and the soul.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of taking oaths seriously and the gravity of breaking them. The mention of celestial bodies like the sun, moon, day, and night, and the heaven and earth, serve as a reminder of the vastness and majesty of creation and the insignificance of human beings in comparison. The inclusion of the "self" and "soul" highlights the personal responsibility and accountability of individuals in keeping their promises and commitments. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and words, and to always strive to act with integrity and honesty.
orig: وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر دائبين وسخر لكم الليل والنهار

translation: And whatever calamity befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the calamities that befall humans are a result of their own actions and choices. It emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is a consequence of humanity's sins and injustices. The verse also highlights God's mercy and forgiveness, as He pardons much of what humans have done. This verse serves as a reminder that humans should reflect on their actions and seek forgiveness in order to avoid the consequences of their wrongdoing.
orig: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار

translation: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this town a secure and peaceful place, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping the idols.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is praying to God to make the town he is in a secure and peaceful place, and to protect him and his sons from the influence of idolatry. The verse highlights Abraham's faith in God and his commitment to monotheism. It also underscores the importance of protecting oneself and one's family from the negative influences of society and staying true to one's beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to seek God's protection and guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many people. Whoever follows me - indeed, I am a warner, and from the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is imploring his Lord to guide him and protect him from the evil of those who have strayed from the right path. He recognizes that many people have been misled and that he is a warner, a reminder to those who have gone astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet and the consequences of not doing so, which is the punishment of the Fire. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay on the right path and to be mindful of the consequences of their actions.
orig: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم

translation: Our Lord, indeed I have settled a small group of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer and fear You. O our Lord, make the hearts of the people incline towards them and provide for them sustenance, so they may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication made by Prophet Abraham, peace be upon him, to God, asking for His blessings and guidance for his descendants who were settled in a valley near the Sacred House of God. The verse highlights the importance of prayer and fear of God, and how these values are essential for a community's spiritual and moral growth. The verse also emphasizes the significance of sustenance and provision, and how God's blessings can bring about gratitude and appreciation in people's hearts. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize their relationship with God and to seek His guidance and blessings in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم وارزقهم من الثمرات لعلهم يشكرون

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what is hidden and what is declared, and nothing is hidden from God on the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power, highlighting that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it be on earth or in the heavens. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that nothing can escape His knowledge or jurisdiction. It also underscores the idea that God's knowledge encompasses everything, including what is hidden and what is manifest, and that nothing can be hidden from Him.
orig: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: And indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], clear authority and evidence [in the Qur'an].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and evidence for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role in providing clear guidance and serving as a criterion to distinguish right from wrong. It also underscores the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam and his accountability to God for fulfilling his prophetic mission.
orig: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق إن ربي لسميع الدعاء

translation: My Lord, make me established in prayer, and from my offspring, our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of the Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in which he asks Allah to make him and his descendants steadfast in their prayer and to accept their supplications. The verse highlights the importance of prayer and the belief that it is a means of seeking guidance and forgiveness from Allah. It also emphasizes the significance of family and the desire to have one's offspring follow in the footsteps of righteousness.
orig: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي ربنا وتقبل دعاء

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which he asks God to forgive himself, his parents, and all believers on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from God and highlights the significance of the Day of Judgment, when all human beings will be held accountable for their actions in this life. The verse also underscores the belief in the unity of the Muslim community, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) includes himself, his parents, and all believers in his prayer for forgiveness.
orig: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

translation: And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. Indeed, He grants them respite until a Day when the eyes will be turned over,
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the actions of the wrongdoers and will grant them respite until a day when they will be punished. The phrase 'the eyes will be turned over' suggests a day of reckoning, when the wrongdoers will be held accountable for their actions and their eyes will be turned over in horror as they face the consequences of their deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing, reminding them that God is always aware of their actions and will eventually bring them to justice.
orig: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار

translation: And their heads are bent down, and their eyes are humbled, and their hearts are in their throats, and they are not able to dispute with Him in the matter of His signs, and they are returned defeated.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the disbelievers when they are confronted with the signs and evidence of God's existence and power. Their heads are bowed down in shame and their eyes are cast down, unable to look up to God. Their hearts are filled with fear and they are unable to speak or argue against God's signs. They are defeated and returned to their state of disbelief, unable to refute the truth of God's existence.
orig: مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء

translation: And warn the people of a day when the punishment will come to them, those who did wrong say: 'Our Lord, respite us until a near term, so we may respond to your call and follow the messengers.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of warning people of the impending punishment and encouraging them to repent and follow the teachings of the messengers. The phrase 'a near term' signifies that the punishment is imminent and could come at any moment, and the phrase 'so we may respond to your call' suggests that the people are being called to respond to God's message and follow the guidance of the messengers. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain and that people must be prepared to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own homes, and you have seen it
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that God has destroyed the homes of those who were unjust and wicked, just as He had destroyed the homes of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The use of the word "And indeed" at the beginning of the verse emphasizes the certainty and reality of the destruction that has been wrought upon the wicked. The phrase "and you have seen it" serves as a reminder that the destruction is not just a theoretical concept, but a tangible reality that the believers have witnessed with their own eyes.
orig: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم وتبين لكم كيف فعلنا بهم وضربنا لكم الأمثال

translation: And they have planned their plan, but their plan is with Allah, though their plan was to keep themselves from having to turn back to Him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' plan to reject God's message and avoid being accountable to Him. The verse suggests that their plan is futile, as it is already known to God and is part of His plan. The phrase 'their plan was to keep themselves from having to turn back to Him' implies that deep down, they know they need to turn back to God, but they are trying to avoid it. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of all things and that trying to reject Him is futile.
orig: وقد مكروا مكرهم وعند الله مكرهم وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال

translation: And indeed, Allah will not delay the reward of the believers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's promise to reward the believers and assures them that their reward will not be delayed. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and hope for the believers, reminding them that their faith and good deeds will not go unrewarded. It also highlights God's justice and fairness, as He will not delay the reward of those who have earned it through their belief and actions.
orig: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله إن الله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: On the Day when the earth will be replaced by a new earth, and the heavens, and they will be brought forth to Allah, the One, the Supreme.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene of the Day of Judgment, when the current earth and heavens will be replaced by a new earth and the inhabitants of the universe will be brought before Allah, the One and Only, for judgment. The verse emphasizes the idea that the present world is temporary and will be replaced by a new one, and that all creatures will be held accountable for their actions in front of the supreme deity.
orig: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار

translation: And you will see the criminals on that day bound in chains, their garments made of pitch, and the Fire covering their faces.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the wicked on Judgment Day. They will be bound in chains and their garments will be made of pitch, signifying their sinfulness and deserving of punishment. The image of the Fire covering their faces is a metaphor for the intense suffering they will endure. The verse serves as a warning to those who lead a life of sin and crime, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's justice.
orig: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: And We have destroyed towns around you, and We have varied the phases of the moon, that they may be reminded, and they have come to their Lord in the morning, prostrate.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of towns that were nearby, emphasizing God's power and the consequences of disobedience. The phrase 'and We have varied the phases of the moon' is significant as it highlights God's control over the natural world and His ability to bring about change and transformation. The verse also emphasizes the importance of remembering and worshiping God, as the people are described as coming to their Lord in the morning, prostrate, indicating submission and humility.
orig: سرابيلهم من قطران وتغشى وجوههم النار

translation: And indeed, God will defer the reward of each soul until the Day of Resurrection, so that He may recompense them in accordance with what they have earned. Indeed, God is swift in account.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's justice and the certainty of reward or punishment for every individual's actions. The phrase 'defer the reward' implies that God is delaying the punishment or reward until the Day of Judgment, indicating that it is not necessary to receive immediate gratification or retribution in this life. The second part of the verse highlights God's ability to keep track of and calculate every individual's deeds, signifying that no one can escape God's judgment. The verse encourages people to live a righteous life, as they will eventually face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ليجزي الله كل نفس ما كسبت إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And indeed, We have sent this reminder to the people, that they may be warned and that they may know that He is One God, and that those of understanding may take heed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to serve as a reminder to humanity of the oneness of God and to encourage people to reflect and take heed of the message. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the unity of God, and the role of the Qur'an in conveying this message to humanity. The phrase 'those of understanding' refers to those who are willing to listen and reflect on the message of the Qur'an, and take heed of its warning.
orig: هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد وليذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين

translation: And if those who disbelieved had only known when they will be resurrected, [it will be] the Day when their tongues, hands, and feet will testify against them, and what they had earned will be destroyed, and what they had fabricated will be lost.
interpretation: The verse highlights the regret and shame that disbelievers will experience on the Day of Judgment when they realize the consequences of their disbelief. Their tongues, hands, and feet will testify against them, indicating that their actions and words will be used as evidence against them. The verse emphasizes the idea that their deeds and fabrications will be of no avail, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the Day of Reckoning and the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين

translation: They will eat their own fruit and have their own enjoyment, but the end is for Us.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who deny the truth and choose to live in disobedience to God. Despite their rejection of God's message, they will still enjoy the fruits of their labor and experience temporary pleasure in this life. However, the ultimate end and destination is with God, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the enjoyment of this life is fleeting, and the true reward or punishment will come in the hereafter.
orig: ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل فسوف يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: And they say, 'O you to whom the reminder has been sent, surely you are a madman!'
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he received the revelation of the Qur'an. They accused him of being a madman or a possessed person, suggesting that the revelation he received was not from God but rather a result of his own mental illness. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the people towards the Prophet's message and the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

translation: And if We had sent angels to them as companions, certainly, We would have punished them. And indeed, it is a test, so let them be for a while.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even if God were to send angels as companions to the disbelievers, they would still be subject to punishment. The verse implies that the disbelievers' rejection of faith is so strong that even the presence of angels among them would not change their attitude. The verse also mentions that this situation is a test for the believers, and that they should be patient and not be hasty in their expectations of God's punishment.
orig: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And We sent not the angels except with truth, and they were not deviating from the truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the truthfulness of the angels and their message. The verse is a response to the disbelievers who accused the prophets of lying and claimed that the angels were not sent by God. The verse affirms that the angels were indeed sent by God and that their message was true and not fabricated. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in the message of the prophets and the angels, and to be mindful of the consequences of rejecting their message.
orig: ما ننزل الملائكة إلا بالحق وما كانوا إذا منظرين

translation: Indeed, We have sent the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardians.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a reminder to humanity, sent by God to guide and warn people. The second part of the verse highlights God's promise to protect and preserve the Qur'an, ensuring that its message remains unchanged and uncorrupted until the end of time. This verse serves as a reassurance to believers that the Qur'an is a reliable source of guidance and that its teachings will endure forever.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you [O Muhammad] from before, in the footsteps of the early ones.
interpretation: This verse refers to the fact that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not the first prophet sent by God. Rather, he was part of a long line of prophets who were sent to guide humanity. The verse highlights the continuity of the prophetic tradition and emphasizes that Muhammad's message was not new or unique, but rather a reaffirmation of the same message that had been conveyed by previous prophets. The use of the phrase 'in the footsteps of the early ones' suggests that Muhammad's mission was a continuation of the mission of the earlier prophets, and that he was following in their footsteps.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك في شيع الأولين

translation: And nothing prevents their Messengers from coming to them, except that they (the Messengers) are sent as a trial for them, and they are being accused (of lying).
interpretation: This verse explains that the reason why God's messengers are not sent to certain communities is not because they are unable to come to them, but rather because they are being sent as a trial for them. The verse suggests that the messengers are sent to test the people's faith and obedience, and to see if they will accept the message and follow the guidance. The verse also implies that the people are accusing the messengers of lying and not believing in their message, which is a common response to the prophets and messengers throughout history.
orig: وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We will set up the just balance on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged in the least, and if there be the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We to take account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be judged based on their deeds in this life. The verse emphasizes God's justice and fairness, assuring that even the smallest good or bad deed will be accounted for. The image of a just balance suggests a precise and impartial weighing of each person's actions, leaving no room for error or injustice. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a virtuous life and the consequences of one's actions, as well as the certainty of being held accountable for them in the afterlife.
orig: كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: And they did not believe in it, for they had already denied the truth before it came to them, while they were still in a state of arrogance and disbelief.
interpretation: The verse highlights the people's refusal to believe in the message of the Prophet (peace be upon him) despite the clear signs and evidence presented to them. Their disbelief was rooted in their arrogance and unwillingness to submit to the truth. The verse suggests that their denial was not based on a lack of evidence or understanding, but rather a result of their own pride and stubbornness. The verse serves as a reminder that true belief requires humility and openness to the truth, rather than being driven by ego and preconceived notions.
orig: لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين

translation: And if We had opened to them a gate from the heaven, they would have remained in their pride, refused to ascend.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even if God had provided a clear and direct path to heaven, the wicked would still have refused to repent and change their ways. The phrase 'they would have remained in their pride' implies that their arrogance and haughtiness would have prevented them from seeking forgiveness and guidance. The verse highlights the idea that the wicked are often resistant to change, even when faced with the possibility of redemption.
orig: ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون

translation: And they say, 'Indeed, we have been oppressed, rather, we were mistaken.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who have been oppressed and mistreated, and how they have come to realize that their suffering is a result of their own mistakes and wrongdoing. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and recognizing the consequences of one's mistakes. It also serves as a reminder that the oppressed should not resort to oppression themselves, but rather seek justice and correction through peaceful means.
orig: لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون

translation: And indeed, We have put forth in the heavenly bodies (stars) great signs and We have beautified them for the beholders.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's creation of the stars and other celestial bodies as signs of His power and majesty. The phrase 'great signs' refers to the stars' beauty and their ability to guide humans in navigation, agriculture, and timekeeping. The verse also emphasizes the aesthetic value of the stars, suggesting that their beauty is not just functional but also meant to be appreciated and enjoyed by humanity. The phrase 'We have beautified them for the beholders' implies that the stars are not just random celestial bodies but have been intentionally designed by God to be a source of wonder and inspiration for those who look up at the night sky.
orig: ولقد جعلنا في السماء بروجا وزيناها للناظرين

translation: And We have protected it (the Qur'an) from every devilish creature.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the protection of the Qur'an from any evil or satanic influence. The use of the word 'every' suggests that all forms of evil are included, and the phrase 'devilish creature' implies a malevolent being that seeks to distort or corrupt the message of the Qur'an. The verse serves as a reassurance to believers that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, protected by God from any form of corruption or distortion, and that its message is preserved in its original form.
orig: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

translation: Except for him who snatches away the hearing, then comes the Shadow (of death) with the clear evidence.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the inevitability of death and the fact that it can come suddenly and unexpectedly. The phrase 'except for him who snatches away the hearing' refers to those who are so engrossed in their own desires and material pursuits that they are unable to hear the call of God and the warning signs of impending death. The 'Shadow (of death)' represents the angel of death, who comes with clear evidence of the person's fate in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to prepare for the ultimate judgment day.
orig: إلا من استرق السمع فأتبعه شهاب مبين

translation: And the earth, We have spread it out, and cast therein mountains and created in it ravines and rivers.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the earth by God, specifically highlighting the formation of mountains, valleys, and rivers. The use of the verb 'spread' emphasizes the idea that the earth was flattened and prepared for habitation. The creation of mountains and valleys served to create a diverse landscape, allowing for various ecosystems to thrive. The rivers, which are mentioned separately, are a vital source of life and sustenance for the inhabitants of the earth. The verse emphasizes the careful planning and design that went into the creation of the earth, and serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون

translation: And We have made for you therein means of living and [for] those whom you are not providers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision and sustenance that God has provided for humanity. The phrase 'means of living' refers to the resources and blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity, such as food, water, shelter, and clothing. The second part of the verse emphasizes that these provisions are not only for the individual, but also for those who are in need and cannot provide for themselves. The verse highlights God's generosity and care for all of humanity, and serves as a reminder to be grateful for what we have and to share our blessings with others, especially those who are less fortunate.
orig: وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش ومن لستم له برازقين

translation: And indeed, We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the fact that the Prophet's mission is not to destroy or punish, but rather to bring mercy and guidance to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular time or place, but is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time.
orig: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

translation: And We sent the winds as a harbinger, so We brought down water from the sky, and We gave it to you to drink, and you were not its guardians.
interpretation: The verse describes how God sent the winds as a warning before bringing down rain from the sky. The verse emphasizes that the rain was a gift from God, and the people were not its guardians, meaning they had no control over it. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and generosity, and how He provides for all living things without any expectation of payment or reward. It also highlights the importance of being grateful for God's blessings and recognizing that everything we have is a gift from Him.
orig: وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح فأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأسقيناكموه وما أنتم له بخازنين

translation: And indeed, We will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and the promise of the Hereafter is certainly true.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and dominance over the earth and all living things. The phrase 'We will inherit the earth' signifies that God will ultimately inherit all that exists on earth, including all creatures and their deeds. The verse also alludes to the idea that the life of this world is temporary, and that the real reward or punishment will be in the Hereafter. The phrase 'the promise of the Hereafter' refers to the promise of God to reward the righteous and punish the wicked in the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their spiritual growth and not to become too attached to the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: وإنا لنحن نحيي ونميت ونحن الوارثون

translation: And indeed, We have known the preceding ones from among you, and indeed, We have known the later ones.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his community, acknowledging that God is aware of both the earlier generations of Muslims and those who came later. The verse serves as a reminder that God's knowledge encompasses all things, including the past and the future, and that He is aware of the actions and deeds of all people. It also emphasizes the continuity of God's message and the responsibility of the believers to uphold and spread it.
orig: ولقد علمنا المستقدمين منكم ولقد علمنا المستأخرين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is He who will gather them together; indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in gathering the people for judgment. The use of the phrase 'indeed' twice emphasizes the certainty of this event. The description of God as 'Wise' and 'Knowing' highlights His attribute of wisdom and knowledge, indicating that His judgment is fair and just, and that all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن ربك هو يحشرهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind from the extract of clay.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble origins of humanity, emphasizing that humans were created from a lowly substance such as clay. The use of the word 'extract' (salsal) suggests a process of purification, implying that humanity was created through a process of refinement. The verse serves as a reminder of humanity's humble beginnings and the need for humility and gratitude towards the Creator.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity's innermost thoughts and feelings, and His proximity to them. The verse suggests that God is aware of the hidden whispers of human's soul, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and emphasizes the intimate relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم

translation: And when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when God announced to the angels His plan to create a new creature, humanity, and to make them His successive authority on earth. The verse emphasizes the idea that humanity was created to be a steward of the earth and to carry out God's will. The use of the word 'successive authority' highlights the idea that humanity was meant to be a continuous and enduring presence on earth, with each generation building upon the accomplishments of the previous one. The verse also underscores the idea that humanity's role is not limited to personal salvation but also includes the responsibility to govern and care for the earth.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And when We gave unto him a gentle breeze, he went down to his people, crying (in alarm).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Salih and his people who were warned by God through a gentle breeze. The breeze was a sign from God to warn the people of their impending punishment. Salih, who was sent by God to guide his people, was alarmed and warned his people of the punishment that was to come. The verse highlights the importance of heeding the signs of God and taking them seriously, lest one suffers the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: All the angels bow down, prostrating themselves before God.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in which all the angels in heaven are bowing down and prostrating themselves before God, indicating their submission and reverence for God's power and majesty. The verse emphasizes the unity and harmony among the angels, as they are all described as being together in their worship of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and submission to God, and encourages believers to follow the example of the angels in their devotion to God.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except for Iblis, they were all prostrating.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene in which all the angels, except for Iblis (Satan), prostrated before Adam, the first human, as a sign of respect and obedience to God's command. Iblis, however, refused to prostrate, out of pride and arrogance, and was subsequently expelled from paradise. The verse highlights the importance of humility and submission to God's will, as well as the consequences of disobedience and pride.
orig: إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

translation: And Satan will say: 'What anguish is mine! doth mine apostleship perish? My summoning hath been rejected. (I have been vanquished). In the abyss (of hell) will I be the third (of the three).
interpretation: In this verse, Satan is lamenting his own fate and the fact that his apostleship has been rejected. He realizes that his efforts to lead humans astray have been in vain, and that he will be punished in the afterlife. The verse highlights Satan's regret and disappointment, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of rebelling against God's will.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما لك ألا تكون مع الساجدين

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whispers of human beings, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of human actions and thoughts, and that He is nearer to us than we think.
orig: قال لم أكن لأسجد لبشر خلقته من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you; will you then not take heed?
