interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that God has destroyed nations before them who were similar in nature and disobedient. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, encouraging them to take heed of the lessons from history and to repent before it's too late. The use of the word "kind" (rajim) emphasizes that the destruction was not just physical, but also spiritual, as they were destroyed because of their disobedience and rejection of God's signs.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: The verse implies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is cursed by the disbelievers, but the curse will ultimately turn into a blessing on the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the idea that the Prophet's mission is not to seek revenge or punishment but to spread God's message and guide people to the right path. The 'Day of Recompense' refers to the Day of Judgment when everyone will be held accountable for their deeds, and the curse will be lifted from the Prophet, and he will be vindicated.
orig: وإن عليك اللعنة إلى يوم الدين

translation: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me, I will respond to you.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the closeness and accessibility of God, inviting believers to call upon Him and assuring them of a response. It highlights the personal nature of the relationship between the believer and God, and encourages the believer to turn to God in prayer and supplication. The use of the first person pronoun 'I' in the verse adds a sense of intimacy and immediacy, underscoring the idea that God is always present and available to those who call upon Him.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: And indeed, you are of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and acknowledges him as one of the messengers of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role and responsibility to convey the message of Islam to the people. It also highlights the importance of the Prophet's mission and the impact it had on the world. The verse is a source of encouragement and motivation for the Prophet and the believers, reminding them of their purpose and the significance of their efforts in spreading the message of God.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until, when the Messengers (angels) came to them, and said: "What! Are you (the people of the town) in doubt about the Messengers (angels)?"
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's reaction when the Messengers (angels) came to them. The verse suggests that the people were in disbelief and doubted the Messengers (angels) and their message. The verse highlights the idea that the people were skeptical and questioned the authenticity of the Messengers (angels) and their message, indicating a lack of faith and conviction among the people.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: And your Lord has said: 'I will indeed decree to punish myself, for My servants, what they have earned of evil deeds, and I will surely give them a taste of the punishment of the Hereafter.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is emphasizing His role as the ultimate judge and punisher of those who have committed evil deeds. The use of the first person pronoun 'I' underscores God's personal involvement in the process of punishment, indicating that it is not just a natural consequence of sin, but a deliberate act of divine justice. The phrase 'what they have earned of evil deeds' highlights the idea that the punishment is a direct result of the individual's actions, and the use of the word 'taste' suggests that the punishment will be a foretaste of the suffering that awaits them in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that God is always watching and will ultimately hold them accountable for their actions.
orig: قال رب بما أغويتني لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your servants among them, the sincere ones.
interpretation: This verse refers to the exception of the righteous servants of God, who are excluded from the punishment that will befall the wicked. The phrase 'al-mukhlisin' (the sincere ones) refers to those who have sincerely devoted themselves to God, and have avoided the temptations of the world and the devil. The verse serves as a reminder that even in the midst of destruction and punishment, there will always be a remnant of righteous individuals who remain faithful to God.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: And He said, 'This is a path that is straight.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is referring to the path of righteousness and guidance that He has laid out for humanity. The word 'straight' (مستقيم) emphasizes the idea that this path is clear and unwavering, and that it leads directly to God. The verse can be seen as a reminder to believers to stay on this path and to avoid straying from it, as well as a warning to those who have strayed to return to the straight path.
orig: قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم

translation: Indeed, My servants have no authority over them, except for those who follow you from among the deviators.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the believers have no authority or control over the disobedient and deviant individuals, except for those who follow and obey God's commandments. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger, and serves as a warning to those who choose to disobey and follow their own desires instead of God's guidance.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

translation: And indeed, Hell is their appointed place.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Hell is the ultimate destination for those who reject God's message and choose to live in sin and disobedience. The use of the word 'appointed' (موعدهم) underscores the idea that this fate was predestined for them, and that they cannot escape it. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of their fate if they do not repent and turn to God.
orig: وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين

translation: For them are seven gates; for each gate there is a separate portion.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gates of hell, which are seven in number. Each gate has a separate portion, indicating that the punishment for sinners will be varied and proportionate to their crimes. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the righteous in the afterlife. The phrase 'gardens and springs' symbolizes a state of eternal bliss and happiness, where the believers will be surrounded by lush vegetation and refreshing waters. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of living a virtuous life, which is to attain salvation and happiness in the hereafter.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Enter upon them through the gate with peace, secure.
interpretation: The verse speaks about entering a town or a place with peace and security. It emphasizes the importance of peaceful entry, indicating that one should not enter a place with hostility or violence. Rather, one should enter with a sense of peace and security, indicating that the entry is for a positive purpose, such as trade, dialogue, or seeking knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of peace and security in all aspects of life, and the importance of conducting oneself with kindness and compassion.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to bring people out of darkness and into the light of faith and righteousness.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لا يمسهم فيها نصب وما هم منها بمخرجين

translation: Warn my servants, I am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: The verse is a command from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn his servants about the consequences of their actions and to remind them of God's mercy and forgiveness. The verse emphasizes God's attribute of being the Forgiving and the Merciful, indicating that He is a God of mercy and compassion, but also a God of justice who will punish those who disobey Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to turn to God in repentance and to seek His forgiveness, knowing that He is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in sincerity.
orig: نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

translation: And My punishment is the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of God's punishment, describing it as 'painful'. The use of the personal pronoun 'My' in 'My punishment' highlights God's direct involvement in the punishment, underscoring the idea that it is a divine decree that cannot be avoided or escaped. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they continue on their current path.
orig: وأن عذابي هو العذاب الأليم

translation: And warn them of a Day when the retribution will come to them, and those who were followed will be of no avail, and they will not be reprieved.
interpretation: The verse warns of a future Day of Judgment when everyone will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes that those who followed false leaders and ignored God's signs will not be spared from punishment. The verse also implies that those who were misguided will not be able to excuse themselves by claiming that they were simply following others. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to follow God's guidance, rather than blindly following others who may be misleading.
orig: ونبئهم عن ضيف إبراهيم

translation: And when they entered upon him, they said, 'Peace!' He said, 'We are from you, so peace!'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a group of people entered upon a man, possibly a prophet or a wise person, and greeted him with the word 'peace' (As-salamu alaykum). The man replied by saying 'We are from you, so peace' (Wa alaykum assalam), indicating that he and his companions were also at peace with them. The verse highlights the importance of peace and harmony among people, and how it is a mutual greeting that signifies a sense of unity and respect among individuals. It also emphasizes the idea that peace is a reciprocal concept, where it is not only a gesture of kindness but also a responsibility to maintain peaceful relationships.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال إنا منكم وجلون

translation: They said, 'Do not become too proud, for We will surely humiliate you, and We will certainly give you a terrible punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the warning given by God to those who are proud and arrogant, threatening them with humiliation and punishment. The use of the word 'ghulam' (youth) in the address suggests that the addressees are young and inexperienced, and the warning serves as a reminder that their youth and inexperience do not exempt them from the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to remain humble and mindful of God's power and judgment.
orig: قالوا لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون

translation: They said, 'You are following a man who is crazy! Indeed, you will be brought to destruction.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. They accused him of being crazy and warned that he would lead them to destruction. The verse highlights the opposition and ridicule that the Prophet faced, but it also emphasizes the persistence and determination of the believers in following the truth, despite the challenges and criticisms they faced.
orig: قالوا بشرناك بالحق فلا تكن من القانطين

translation: And who is more astray than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them, forgetting the meeting of his Lord? Indeed, We have given them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of ignoring or rejecting the signs and verses of God, which are meant to guide and bless humanity. The verse emphasizes that those who turn away from God's reminders are not only neglecting their spiritual growth but also forgetting the ultimate meeting with their Lord, which is a severe consequence. The verse also underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of knowledge, guidance, and mercy for those who believe.
orig: قال ومن يقنط من رحمة ربه إلا الضالون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals.
interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the messengers sent by God to a community of criminals. The messengers are stating that they have been sent to a people who are known for their wicked deeds and that they have come to warn them of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the idea that the messengers are not responsible for the destruction that will befall the community, but rather it is the community's own actions that will bring about their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of sin and the importance of heeding the warnings of God's messengers.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: Except the family of Lot, indeed we are angels, brought together.
interpretation: The verse mentions the exception of the family of Prophet Lot, who were saved from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse emphasizes that the angels, disguised as travelers, were brought together to deliver Lot and his family from the impending punishment. The verse highlights the mercy and grace of God towards the righteous, even in the midst of destruction and chaos.
orig: إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين

translation: Except for the one who is being punished, surely it is an inevitable decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment of God is inescapable and unavoidable. The phrase 'except for the one who is being punished' suggests that the punishment is already in progress, and that there is no way to avoid it. The word 'qadar' (قدر) in the original Arabic text implies a sense of fate or destiny, emphasizing that the punishment is a preordained decree from God. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God's commands, reminding them that they cannot escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: إلا امرأته قدرنا إنها لمن الغابرين

translation: And when the angels came to the family of Lot
interpretation: The verse describes the arrival of the angels at the house of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the fact that the angels came to Lot's family, indicating that they were sent by God to deliver a message or carry out a specific task. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of hospitality and the role of prophets and messengers in conveying God's message to humanity.
orig: فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون

translation: And indeed, you are a nation that will be questioned.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, emphasizing that they will be held accountable for their actions on Judgment Day. The verse serves as a reminder that every individual will be questioned about their deeds in this life, and that they must be prepared to answer for their actions. It also highlights the importance of living a virtuous life and being mindful of one's accountability to God.
orig: قال إنكم قوم منكرون

translation: They said, 'We have been destroyed by what we used to mock!
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who were destroyed by the punishment they had been warned about. They admit that they had been mocking the idea of the punishment and the messengers who had come to warn them. Now that the punishment has come to pass, they realize the error of their ways and are filled with regret. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding warnings and taking the message of the prophets seriously, lest one suffers the same fate as those who mocked and ignored the warnings.
orig: قالوا بل جئناك بما كانوا فيه يمترون

translation: And We have certainly given you the truth, and indeed We will surely support the truth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's support for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the truth of his message. The verse is a reassurance that God is on the side of the believers and will support them in their struggle against falsehood and injustice. The phrase 'And We have certainly given you the truth' refers to the Qur'an itself, which is considered the ultimate truth and the final revelation from God to humanity. The second part of the verse, 'and indeed We will surely support the truth', is a promise from God that He will aid and assist those who stand up for justice and righteousness.
orig: وأتيناك بالحق وإنا لصادقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل واتبع أدبارهم ولا يلتفت منكم أحد وامضوا حيث تؤمرون

translation: And We have destroyed many a town while they were unjust, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين

translation: And the people of the city came rejoicing.
interpretation: The verse describes the people of the city rejoicing at the arrival of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. The word 'rejoicing' in Arabic is 'istabsharoon' which implies a deep sense of joy and happiness. This verse highlights the warm welcome and hospitality extended to the Prophet and his companions by the people of Medina, who were eager to hear his message and accept Islam. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of hospitality and the value of welcoming guests with kindness and respect.
orig: وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون

translation: And indeed, those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its role in recognizing and accepting the truth of God's revelation. The phrase 'those who have been given knowledge' refers to those who have been blessed with the ability to understand and recognize the truth, and the phrase 'what has been revealed to you from your Lord' refers to the Qur'an itself. The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a guide to the straight path, the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy, indicating that it is a source of guidance and wisdom for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: قال إن هؤلاء ضيفي فلا تفضحون

translation: And fear Allah and do not disobey Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and not disobeying His commands. The fear of Allah is the foundation of faith and the key to a righteous life. It means to have a deep reverence and respect for Allah's power, wisdom, and justice, and to be mindful of His presence in all aspects of life. Disobeying Allah's commands leads to sin and injustice, and ultimately invites His punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay on the path of righteousness and avoid actions that may displease Allah.
orig: واتقوا الله ولا تخزون

translation: They said, 'We have been harmful (in the past).',
interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They admitted that they had been harmful and wrongdoers in the past, but they refused to accept the message and instead chose to reject it and oppose the Prophet. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who were unwilling to admit their mistakes and turn to God for guidance.
orig: قالوا أولم ننهك عن العالمين

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, why have you destroyed our towns while they were inhabited by people who were doing wrong?
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of towns that were inhabited by people who were doing wrong, and the question posed by the people is why God would destroy their towns when they were inhabited by people who were living in sin. The verse highlights the idea that God's punishment is not limited to individuals, but can also extend to entire towns or communities that are living in disobedience to God's commands. The verse serves as a warning to communities to turn away from sin and live according to God's will, lest they face the same fate as the destroyed towns.
orig: قال هؤلاء بناتي إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: And indeed, they are in a state of confusion and madness.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who reject the message of God and continue to live in sin and disobedience. The Arabic word 'sukrat' used in the verse implies a state of confusion, bewilderment, and madness, indicating that those who reject God's message are in a state of moral confusion and spiritual disorientation. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and the state of confusion and chaos that results from such rejection.
orig: لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون

translation: Then We seized them with punishment, while they were still in a state of neglect.
interpretation: The verse describes how God seized the people with punishment while they were still in a state of neglect, indicating that they were not paying attention to the signs and warnings that God had sent them. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment was a direct result of their neglect and disobedience, and serves as a reminder to those who are living in a state of neglect, warning them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين

translation: And We have made the high places low and have broken them into pieces, and have made their fruits to fall down, and have made their rivers to flow with pebbles.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of the arrogant and proud people who had turned away from God. The 'high places' refer to the lofty positions and prestige they had attained, which God has brought low. The 'fruits' represent their wealth and material possessions, which have been taken away. The 'rivers' symbolize the blessings and favors that God had bestowed upon them, which have now dried up. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate authority, and that those who reject Him will face the consequences of their arrogance and disobedience.
orig: فجعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

translation: Indeed, in this are signs for those who are endowed with understanding.
interpretation: The verse highlights the presence of signs and indications in the world around us that point to the existence and oneness of God. The phrase 'for those who are endowed with understanding' suggests that these signs are not necessarily apparent to everyone, but rather require a certain level of insight and discernment to recognize. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate their understanding and faith, and to be mindful of the signs of God's presence in their lives.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين

translation: And indeed, it is a path that leads to the path of your Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being a guidance and a path that leads to the path of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a guide for those who seek to live a righteous life and to attain the nearness of Allah. The verse also underscores the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book, but a path that guides humanity towards a righteous and just life, and ultimately, towards the pleasure of Allah.
orig: وإنها لبسبيل مقيم

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the destruction of the unjust towns serves as a sign or a lesson for the believers. The 'sign' refers to the punishment that the unjust towns received, which serves as a reminder to the believers of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a righteous life. The verse encourages the believers to reflect on the fate of those who were destroyed and to take heed of the warning signs that God has given them.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, the companions of the Ayka were unjust.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people of the Ayka, who were known for their injustice and corruption. The word 'Ayka' is derived from the Arabic word 'ayk', which means 'a great river'. The verse suggests that the people of the Ayka were living in a state of moral decay and injustice, and were therefore deserving of God's punishment.
orig: وإن كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين

translation: So We punished them, indeed they were criminals.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that was inflicted upon the people who were guilty of criminal behavior. The use of the word 'indeed' emphasizes that the punishment was well-deserved and a direct consequence of their actions. The verse highlights the idea that the punishment was not arbitrary or unjust, but rather a direct result of their own actions. It serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences and that we must be held accountable for our behavior.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم وإنهما لبإمام مبين

translation: And indeed, the companions of the trench were schemed against, and the punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the companions of the trench, who were persecuted and schemed against. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of persecution and injustice, and the certainty of God's punishment for those who commit such acts.
orig: ولقد كذب أصحاب الحجر المرسلين

translation: And We have sent them signs, but they turned away from them, rejecting them.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people's rejection of God's signs and messages, despite their clear and convincing nature. The verse emphasizes the idea that the people were not ignorant of God's signs, but rather, they chose to reject them, turning away from the truth and instead, they followed their own desires and false beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's signs and the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth.
orig: وآتيناهم آياتنا فكانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And they were secure in their homes, (feeling) safe.
interpretation: The verse describes a state of false sense of security and complacency among the people who were living in their comfortable homes, feeling safe and secure. The use of the word 'بيوتا' (homes) emphasizes the idea that they were living in a state of comfort and tranquility, oblivious to the impending danger that was about to strike. The verse serves as a reminder that a false sense of security can lead to complacency and a lack of preparedness for the unexpected events that may occur in life.
orig: وكانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا آمنين

translation: Then We seized them with punishment, while they were still in their wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse describes how God seized the people with punishment while they were still engaging in wrongdoing and disobedience. The use of the word 'صيحة' (seizure) emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, indicating that it was not a gradual process but rather a sudden and swift act of justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them that God's punishment can come at any moment, without warning.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مصبحين

translation: And what has happened to them is what they used to mock.
interpretation: The verse refers to the fate of those who were warned by God's messengers but refused to believe and instead mocked the warning. The verse suggests that they were punished in a way that was fitting for their mockery, implying that they were caught off guard and were not able to escape the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not to be taken lightly and that those who reject the message of God's prophets will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We have not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth, and indeed, the Hour is coming, so forgive with a beautiful forgiveness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the purpose of creation, which is to worship Allah and live according to His commandments. The verse also mentions the coming of the Hour, which is the Day of Judgment, when all humans will be judged based on their deeds. The verse ends with a call to forgiveness, reminding believers to forgive others and seek forgiveness from Allah.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وإن الساعة لآتية فاصفح الصفح الجميل

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's role as the Creator and His attribute of knowledge. The use of the word 'khaliq' (creator) signifies God's power to bring things into existence, while 'alim' (knowing) highlights His infinite wisdom and understanding. This verse serves as a reminder that God is the source of all knowledge and the one who has created everything with a purpose. It encourages believers to reflect on the beauty and complexity of creation and to recognize the wisdom and power of God in everything that exists.
orig: إن ربك هو الخلاق العليم

translation: And indeed, We have given you seven of the seven pairs and the Great Qur'an.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the seven pairs of things that were given to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a sign of God's favor and blessing. These seven pairs include the seven heavens, the seven earths, the seven days, the seven nights, the seven months, the seven seas, and the seven directions. Additionally, the verse mentions the Great Qur'an, which is considered the greatest of all revelations and the ultimate guidance for humanity. The verse emphasizes the magnitude of this blessing and the responsibility that comes with it, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) was chosen to convey the message of Islam to the world. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of their role in spreading the message of Islam and living according to its teachings.
orig: ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم

translation: And do not incline towards those who are unjust, lest you be swept away by their wicked deeds, and be patient with the believers.
interpretation: The verse advises believers not to incline towards those who are unjust, lest they be swept away by their wicked deeds. This means that believers should not associate themselves with people who are engaged in sinful or unjust behavior, lest they become corrupted by their influence. Instead, they should be patient with the believers, showing compassion and understanding towards those who are committed to living a righteous life.
orig: لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, I am the Clear Warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a clear and distinct warner to his people. The word 'Nadhir' in Arabic means 'one who warns' and 'Mubin' means 'clear' or 'manifest'. The verse highlights the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam and warn his people of the consequences of not following it. The verse also underscores the clarity and clarity of the Prophet's message, leaving no excuse for those who choose to ignore it.
orig: وقل إني أنا النذير المبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كما أنزلنا على المقتسمين

translation: And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy to remember and understand. Then is it that those who desire to be reminded have been reminded, and those who are turned away have been turned away.
interpretation: The verse highlights the accessibility and clarity of the Qur'an, indicating that it is a book that can be easily understood and remembered by those who seek guidance. The verse also emphasizes the dual nature of the Qur'an's impact, where it serves as a source of guidance for those who are receptive to its message, while simultaneously serving as a warning and punishment for those who reject its teachings.
orig: الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various difficulties, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and failure of crops. However, the verse also assures that those who are patient and persevering will receive good tidings. The verse highlights the importance of patience and resilience in the face of adversity, and serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith.
orig: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: عما كانوا يعملون

translation: And leave what is past and forgotten, and do not seek to enquire about it.
interpretation: The verse advises believers to focus on the present and future, rather than dwelling on past mistakes or sins. It encourages them to move forward and not to dwell on past errors, but rather to learn from them and seek forgiveness. The verse also emphasizes the importance of not seeking to investigate or pry into matters that are not their concern, as this can lead to unnecessary trouble and harm.
orig: فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: Indeed, We have destroyed many a generations before you, do you not see them?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed many generations before him. The verse is a reminder to the Prophet and the believers that God's punishment is not limited to the present generation, but is a recurring theme throughout history. The verse also serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that they will face the same fate as the previous generations that were destroyed by God's punishment, if they do not repent and turn to God.
orig: إنا كفيناك المستهزئين

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will soon know.
interpretation: The verse warns those who practice shirk (associating partners with Allah) that they will soon come to know the truth and be held accountable for their actions. The verse implies that those who commit shirk are living in a state of delusion and ignorance, and that they will eventually be confronted with the reality of their actions and the consequences that follow. The verse serves as a warning to those who are involved in idolatry or polytheism, reminding them that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship and that associating partners with Him is a grave sin.
orig: الذين يجعلون مع الله إلها آخر فسوف يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were older than yours.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed towns before that were older and more established than his own. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and authority, and that He is not limited by time or space. The verse also implies that the destruction of these towns was a consequence of their disobedience and rejection of God's messengers, and serves as a warning to the Prophet's contemporaries who were also rejecting God's message.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

translation: Praise be to God, who hath made the heavens and the earth, and hath made the angels messengers, and hath made the spirits His servants, and hath not been proud.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to God for His creation and sovereignty. The use of the word "sajidin" (prostrating) emphasizes the humble nature of the believers, who recognize God's greatness and submit to His will. The verse also highlights God's power and authority, as He is the one who has created the heavens and the earth, and has appointed angels and spirits to serve Him. The phrase "and hath not been proud" suggests that God's power and majesty are not to be taken for granted, and that humility is a necessary quality for those who seek to serve Him.
orig: فسبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين

translation: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty (of death).
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping God until the very end of one's life. The phrase 'until there comes to you the certainty (of death)' indicates that one should continue to worship God until the moment of death, signifying that the believer's faith and devotion to God should be unwavering and unshakeable until the very end. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to not waver in their devotion to God, even in the face of death.
orig: واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين

translation: And indeed, the matter of the Hour is coming, so do not hasten it, Glory to your Lord, the Lord of Honor, and humiliation will be upon the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the coming of the Hour of Judgment and warns against hastening it. The verse emphasizes the glory and honor of God, and the humiliation that will befall the disbelievers on that day. The verse serves as a reminder of the impending judgment and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for it.
orig: أتى أمر الله فلا تستعجلوه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: The angels descend upon the prophets by the Spirit of God, that they may warn whom they will that there is no god but Me, so fear Me.
interpretation: In this verse, God is emphasizing the importance of the message delivered by the prophets, which is a warning to those who reject the idea of the oneness of God. The use of the phrase 'by the Spirit of God' highlights the divine origin of the message, and the phrase 'that they may warn whom they will' suggests that the message is not limited to a specific group, but is universal and applicable to all people. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the only deity worthy of worship, and that all other gods or objects of worship are false and should be rejected. The verse also emphasizes the importance of fearing God and living a life in accordance with His will.
orig: ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده أن أنذروا أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاتقون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in truth, and the Most High is the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and oneness of God, and the fact that He is the Creator of the universe. The phrase 'in truth' suggests that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not a myth or a story, but a reality that is supported by evidence and reason. The phrase 'the Most High is the Most Great' is a reference to God's greatness and supremacy over all things, and serves as a reminder of His power and majesty.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق تعالى عما يشركون

translation: And He created man from a sperm-drop, and behold, this same (man) becomes an open disputer!
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human nature. Despite being created from a tiny sperm-drop, human beings have a tendency to become argumentative and disputatious. The verse suggests that this tendency towards argumentation is a result of humanity's failure to recognize and appreciate the sign of God's power and wisdom in their own creation. The verse serves as a reminder to reflect on the miraculous nature of human creation and to recognize the limits of human knowledge and understanding.
orig: خلق الإنسان من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And He has created animals for you, from them are warmth and benefits, and from their bellies you drink.
interpretation: This verse highlights the provision and blessings that God has bestowed upon humans through the creation of animals. The verse emphasizes the utility and benefits that animals provide, such as warmth and nourishment, and how humans rely on them for survival. The verse also underscores the idea that humans are interconnected with animals and the natural world, and that our well-being is linked to their well-being. It serves as a reminder to appreciate and respect all forms of life, and to recognize the intrinsic value of all creatures.
orig: والأنعام خلقها لكم فيها دفء ومنافع ومنها تأكلون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human hearts, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and emphasizes the idea that God is always near and aware of human actions and thoughts.
orig: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

translation: And We will burden them with heavy weights on their necks, so that they will not be able to rise up all, though they will remain in a state of subjugation.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. They will be burdened with heavy weights, symbolizing the consequences of their actions, which will prevent them from rising up or achieving spiritual growth. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who reject God's message will be subjugated and unable to escape the consequences of their choices.
orig: وتحمل أثقالكم إلى بلد لم تكونوا بالغيه إلا بشق الأنفس إن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: By the horses, and the night, and the moon, and the day, and the sun, and the stars, and the mountains, and the sea, and the trees prostrate with their fruit, and the heavens and the earth
interpretation: N
orig: والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة ويخلق ما لا تعلمون

translation: And upon Allah is the direction of the way, and there is no changing of His words. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and control over all things. The phrase 'direction of the way' refers to the fact that Allah has set the course of events and the path that humanity must follow. The phrase 'no changing of His words' underscores the idea that Allah's decisions and commands are final and cannot be altered. The verse also highlights Allah's omniscience, as He is the 'Hearing, the Knowing', indicating that He is aware of all things and has knowledge of all that is hidden and manifest. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is in control of all things and that they must submit to His will.
orig: وعلى الله قصد السبيل ومنها جائر ولو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: And He it is Who sends down rain from the sky, and We bring forth with it gardens and the harvest grain.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and provision, as He is the one who sends down rain from the sky, which brings forth gardens and grain for human consumption. The verse highlights the importance of rain for agriculture and the growth of crops, and how it is a blessing from God. The verse also underscores the idea that God's provision is not limited to just food, but also includes the beauty and abundance of nature, represented by the gardens. The verse serves as a reminder of God's generosity and the importance of gratitude for His blessings.
orig: هو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء لكم منه شراب ومنه شجر فيه تسيمون

translation: And He has subjected to you, as from Him, all that is in the heavens and on earth: behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and dominion over all things in the heavens and earth, and how everything in creation is subservient to Him. The verse also highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation, suggesting that the signs of God's greatness and wisdom are evident in the natural world, and that people should observe and appreciate them. The verse encourages people to reflect on the wonders of creation and to recognize the majesty and grandeur of God.
orig: ينبت لكم به الزرع والزيتون والنخيل والأعناب ومن كل الثمرات إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: By the night and the day, and by the sun and the moon, and by the stars, they are all in harmony, prostrating themselves to their Lord.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and harmony of the natural world, in which all creatures, including the stars, sun, moon, and night, are obedient to God's will and submit to His command. The verse serves as a reminder to humans, who are also expected to submit to God's will and live in harmony with the natural world. The use of the word "prostrating" (sajidin) emphasizes the idea of submission and humility before God, and serves as a reminder of the proper relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And what We have created for you on earth of varying colors, indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember.
interpretation: The verse highlights the diversity of colors in the natural world and the beauty of God's creation. The use of the word 'varying' (makhluf) emphasizes the idea that the colors are not just limited to two or three, but rather there are numerous shades and hues that can be seen in nature. The verse also suggests that the diversity of colors is a sign of God's power and wisdom, and that it serves as a reminder for people to reflect and remember the Creator. The word 'remember' (yadhkuruna) implies a deep and sincere reflection, and not just a casual acknowledgement. The verse encourages people to pause and appreciate the beauty and complexity of creation, and to recognize the One who created it all.
orig: وما ذرأ لكم في الأرض مختلفا ألوانه إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يذكرون

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His knowledge of all human actions. It suggests that God is always with believers, watching over them and aware of their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that God's presence is not limited to any particular place or time, and that He is always aware of human actions, thoughts, and intentions. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to live a life that is pleasing to God, in order to receive His blessings and guidance.
orig: وهو الذي سخر البحر لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا وتستخرجوا منه حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك مواخر فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has subjected to you, in the earth, all that is in it, and the sea, to the extent that you are enabled to sail through it, and He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both constantly, and He has subjected to you the night and the day, and He has subjected to you what is in the wombs of your mothers, and He has subjected to you what is in the bellies of your fathers, and He has subjected to you the treasures of the heavens and the earth, and He has subjected to you what is between the two, and He has subjected to you the treasures of the light and the darkness, and He has subjected to you the keys of the heavens and the earth, and He has subjected to you what is between the two
interpretation: N
orig: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وأنهارا وسبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kinds of old, but do you not remember?
interpretation: The verse addresses the arrogance and ignorance of the disbelievers, reminding them that God has destroyed entire nations in the past for their sins and injustices. The use of the phrase 'your kinds' emphasizes that these nations were as haughty and rebellious as the disbelievers of Mecca, who were being addressed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, urging them to remember and learn from the lessons of history, and to turn to God in repentance before it is too late.
orig: وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون

translation: And how many a sign have We given you, so that they may remember, but they do not remember.
interpretation: The verse highlights the numerous signs and proofs that God has given to humanity, yet many people choose to ignore them and reject the truth. The verse emphasizes the idea that the signs are a means of remembrance, but those who refuse to remember and accept the truth will not benefit from them. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the signs of God and encourages them to reflect on their actions and remember the blessings and signs of God in their lives.
orig: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق أفلا تذكرون

translation: And indeed, Allah will not forgive the favor of the disbelievers, for they have denied the blessings of Allah, so do not forgive them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's refusal to forgive those who reject His blessings and deny His existence. The phrase 'the favor of the disbelievers' refers to the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon all humanity, regardless of their beliefs. The verse warns against denying these blessings and rejecting Allah's existence, as it will lead to His wrath and punishment. The verse also serves as a reminder to believers to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to acknowledge their source, lest they face the same fate as the disbelievers.
orig: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها إن الله لغفور رحيم

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you declare.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and awareness of all things, including the secrets that humans keep hidden and the things they openly declare. It serves as a reminder that nothing is hidden from Allah, and that He is aware of all our thoughts, actions, and intentions. It also highlights the idea that our attempts to hide things from others or from Allah are futile, as He is all-knowing and all-seeing.
orig: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون

translation: And those who call upon other than Allah, they create nothing, and they are themselves created.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshiping anything else but Allah. Those who worship idols or other deities are ultimately reliant on Allah for their creation and sustenance, yet they are oblivious to this fact. The verse highlights the irony of their situation, where they are created beings themselves, yet they attribute their existence to something else. The verse serves as a reminder that true worship and reliance should only be directed towards Allah, the sole Creator and Sustainer of all things.
orig: والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أموات غير أحياء وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Your god is one God, there is no god but He, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. The description of God as 'the Entirely Merciful' and 'the Especially Merciful' highlights His attribute of mercy and compassion, which is extended to all creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to have faith in God's unity and to reject any form of polytheism, and also to remember that God's mercy is all-encompassing and available to all who turn to Him.
orig: إلهكم إله واحد فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون

translation: And indeed, Allah knows what they keep hidden and what they declare. Indeed, He does not love the proud and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and awareness of human actions and intentions, both hidden and public. The verse warns against pride and boasting, as these traits are disliked by Allah and can lead to a person's downfall. It serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate humility and humbleness in their actions and interactions with others.
orig: لا جرم أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه لا يحب المستكبرين

translation: And when it was said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' They said, 'Fables of the former peoples.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the disbelievers were asked about the revelation sent by God to their Prophet, and they dismissed it as mere fables or stories from the past. The verse highlights their arrogance and disbelief, as they rejected the idea of a divine message without even giving it a chance. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message without properly investigating it, and serves as a reminder that the truth is not always immediately apparent and must be sought with an open mind.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they will bear their own burdens on the Day of Resurrection, and also the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Evil is what they will bear!
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the responsibility of individuals for their own actions and the consequences of misleading others. On the Day of Judgment, each person will be held accountable for their own deeds, and those who misled others will also bear the burden of their followers' sins. The verse warns against blindly following others without seeking knowledge and understanding, as it can lead to harm and destruction. The phrase 'Evil is what they will bear' underscores the gravity of the consequences of such actions.
orig: ليحملوا أوزارهم كاملة يوم القيامة ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم بغير علم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And indeed, those before them had plotted, but Allah demolished their building from the foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the disbelievers who plotted against the believers. The verse emphasizes that their destruction was not only sudden but also came from an unexpected source, the roof falling on them from above. The verse serves as a warning to those who seek to harm the believers, reminding them that God is always watching and will punish those who seek to harm His followers.
orig: قد مكر الذين من قبلهم فأتى الله بنيانهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم وأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Then on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them and say, 'Where are My 'partners' for whom you used to oppose [the believers]? Those who were given knowledge will say, 'Today, disgrace and evil are upon the disbelievers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment when God will confront the disbelievers with their misdeeds and disgrace them in front of all creation. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who associated partners with God and opposed the believers will be held accountable and punished. The phrase 'where are My partners' suggests that God is asking the disbelievers where are the partners they associated with Him, implying that they have no excuse for their actions. The second part of the verse highlights the role of knowledgeable people who will testify against the disbelievers on Judgment Day, stating that they were warned about the consequences of their disbelief but chose to ignore the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and associate partners with Him, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face on Judgment Day.
orig: ثم يوم القيامة يخزيهم ويقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تشاقون فيهم قال الذين أوتوا العلم إن الخزي اليوم والسوء على الكافرين

translation: And those who are angels, they are not unjust towards themselves, they used to do good deeds, perhaps they will be reminded of the evil that they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the angels who are not unjust towards themselves. They are not selfish or oppressive and always do good deeds. The verse suggests that even the angels, who are considered to be pure and righteous, may be reminded of their past mistakes or wrongdoings. This serves as a reminder to both the angels and humans that everyone will be held accountable for their actions and that no one is above criticism or improvement.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم فألقوا السلم ما كنا نعمل من سوء بلى إن الله عليم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein, miserable is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: The verse commands the unbelievers to enter the gates of Hell, indicating that they will be punished for their arrogance and disbelief. The description of the abode as 'miserable' emphasizes the suffering and distress that the unbelievers will experience in Hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who are proud and arrogant, reminding them of the consequences of their attitude and the importance of humility and submission to God.
orig: فادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And it was said to those who were blessed with knowledge: What has your Lord revealed? They said: A good thing for those who do good in this world, and in the Hereafter is a better reward for the righteous.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who possess knowledge and faith, and asks them about the revelation they have received from God. They respond by saying that the revelation is a blessing for those who do good deeds in this life and will also bring a better reward in the Hereafter for the righteous. The verse highlights the connection between faith and good deeds, and emphasizes the importance of living a virtuous life in order to attain a better reward in the Afterlife.
orig: وقيل للذين اتقوا ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا خيرا للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة ولدار الآخرة خير ولنعم دار المتقين

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far from them, with its rivers flowing beneath them, and they will be immersed in what they desire, in joy and pleasure, and they will be rewarded with the reward of the righteous.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings that await the righteous in Paradise. The phrase 'not far from them' suggests that Paradise is within reach, and the image of rivers flowing beneath them emphasizes the abundance and beauty of the reward. The phrase 'they will be immersed in what they desire' implies that the righteous will be fully satisfied with their reward and will be able to enjoy all the pleasures they desire. The verse also highlights the idea that the righteous will be rewarded with a reward that is commensurate with their good deeds.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها تجري من تحتها الأنهار لهم فيها ما يشاءون كذلك يجزي الله المتقين

translation: And those who are angels will descend upon them, saying, 'Peace be upon you! Enter Paradise because of what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the righteous people entering Paradise, where they will be greeted by angels who will welcome them with the message of peace and blessings. The verse highlights the idea that the righteous will be rewarded for their good deeds in this life, and that their entrance into Paradise is a result of their pious actions. The verse also underscores the idea that the angels are tasked with the responsibility of guarding and protecting the righteous, and that they will be the ones to welcome them into Paradise.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة طيبين يقولون سلام عليكم ادخلوا الجنة بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Do they await anything but the angels to come to them or your Lord's command to come? Thus did those before them reject, and the wrongdoers among them were punished.
interpretation: The verse questions the disbelievers' expectation of waiting for the angels or God's command to come before they believe. The verse highlights that such an expectation is misplaced, as the punishment for disbelief will come suddenly and unexpectedly, just as it did for those who rejected the prophets before them. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a result of their own wrongdoing and rejection of the truth.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي أمر ربك كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم وما ظلمهم الله ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And they were struck by the evil consequences of their deeds, and what they used to mock surrounded them.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of the people's evil deeds, which they had once mocked and thought were insignificant. The word 'saya' (سيأ) in the verse implies a gradual and accumulative punishment that matched the severity of their sins. The phrase 'what they used to mock' suggests that their punishment was a direct result of their own actions and disbelief. The verse warns against the dangers of disobeying God's commands and ignoring the consequences of one's actions.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And those who associated others with Allah in the past said: Had Allah willed, we would not have worshiped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything without His permission. Likewise, those before them did deny the Messengers until they tasted Our punishment.
interpretation: The verse addresses the excuses made by those who associated others with Allah, such as idol worshipers, who claimed that if God had willed, they would not have worshiped anything besides Him. The verse refutes this excuse by pointing out that if God had willed, He would have prohibited such worship and informed them of it. The verse also highlights the similarity between the denial of the Messengers by those before them and the current denial of the idol worshipers, emphasizing that both groups will face God's punishment.
orig: وقال الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه من شيء نحن ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من دونه من شيء كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: And We have sent in every nation a messenger, saying, 'Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut.' And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the prophetic message throughout history, as God has sent a messenger to every nation, calling people to worship Him alone and avoid the worship of false deities (Taghut). The verse also highlights the dual nature of humanity's response to the prophets: some are guided by God, while others are doomed to error and destruction. The verse concludes by encouraging people to reflect on the consequences of rejecting God's message, as seen in the fate of those who denied the prophets in the past.
orig: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Indeed, Allah will not guide those who disobey Him, and they will have no allies.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that those who disobey God and reject His guidance will not be guided by Him. Not only that, but they will also not have any allies or supporters, indicating that they will be alone and without help, both in this life and in the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are disobedient and encourages them to turn back to God and follow His guidance in order to avoid the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: إن تحرص على هداهم فإن الله لا يهدي من يضل وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And they have sworn by Allah their strongest oaths that Allah will not cause the death of anyone, but they are lying.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who have sworn by Allah, swearing that Allah will not cause the death of anyone, implying that they are invincible and will never face punishment for their sins. However, the verse reveals that they are lying and that their oaths are false. This verse serves as a warning to those who rely on their own strength and power, reminding them that they are not invincible and that Allah's punishment is certain.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت بلى وعدا عليه حقا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We will suffice them with a clear explanation of the Qur'an, that they may be reminded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's ability to clarify the meaning of the Qur'an for those who are skeptical or dismissive of its message. The phrase 'a clear explanation' suggests that the Qur'an contains a clear and convincing argument that leaves no room for doubt or confusion. The verse also implies that the purpose of the Qur'an is not only to convey information but also to serve as a reminder to those who have forgotten or ignored God's message. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the Qur'an's message, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their disbelief.
orig: ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه وليعلم الذين كفروا أنهم كانوا كاذبين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to spread God's message of peace, love, and forgiveness to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. It serves as a reminder to Muslims to follow the Prophet's example and strive to be a source of mercy and guidance for others.
orig: إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who have fled their homes for the cause of Allah after they had been wronged, We will certainly give them a good life in this world, and indeed, the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have been wronged and have fled their homes for the sake of Allah. God promises them a good life in this world and a greater reward in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who have been wronged and have stood up for their beliefs will be rewarded in both this life and the next. The verse also highlights the importance of perseverance and faith in the face of adversity, as those who have fled their homes for Allah's cause have demonstrated their commitment to their beliefs and their trust in God's plan.
orig: والذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا لنبوئنهم في الدنيا حسنة ولأجر الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And those who are patient and rely on their Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of patience and trust in God as a key characteristic of the righteous. It emphasizes that those who are patient and have faith in God's plan and timeline, will be rewarded and will receive God's help and support. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate patience and trust in God, especially during times of hardship and difficulty, and to know that God is always with them and will never abandon them.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And We have not sent before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We sent revelation, so ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophetic tradition and the continuity of the message of Islam. The verse states that all Prophets, including Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), were sent by God to guide humanity. The verse encourages the believers to seek knowledge and guidance from the People of the Book, who are the custodians of the divine scriptures and have a deep understanding of the message of God. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of Islam is not new or unique, but rather a continuation and completion of the messages of previous Prophets.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: By the dawn and the ten nights, and We have sent down to you the Reminder so that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them, and so that they may reflect.
interpretation: The verse begins with an oath by the dawn and the ten nights, emphasizing the importance and gravity of the message that follows. The 'Reminder' refers to the Qur'an itself, which has been sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey to the people. The purpose of the Qur'an is to clarify the message that has been sent down to the people, and to encourage them to reflect on their actions and beliefs. The verse highlights the importance of reflecting on the signs of God and the consequences of one's actions, and serves as a reminder to the people to turn back to God and live according to His commandments.
orig: بالبينات والزبر وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ولعلهم يتفكرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفأمن الذين مكروا السيئات أن يخسف الله بهم الأرض أو يأتيهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Or He would have seized them in their confusion, and they would have been unable to recover.
interpretation: The verse suggests that God's punishment is not limited to the physical destruction of towns, but also extends to the spiritual realm. The phrase 'in their confusion' implies that the people were in a state of spiritual confusion, unable to distinguish right from wrong. The verse warns that if God were to seize them in this state, they would be unable to recover, indicating that the punishment would be severe and final. This serves as a warning to those who are living in a state of spiritual confusion, encouraging them to seek guidance and turn to God before it's too late.
orig: أو يأخذهم في تقلبهم فما هم بمعجزين

translation: Or He may take them away in their fear (in a state of) abasement, for your Lord is indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the mercy and compassion of God, who may choose to take away the lives of sinners in a state of fear and humiliation, rather than punishing them severely. The verse emphasizes God's attribute of being Most Kind and Most Merciful, indicating that even in His punishment, God is still showing mercy and compassion to those who have disobeyed Him. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's justice.
orig: أو يأخذهم على تخوف فإن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: Have they not looked at the things that Allah has created, how their shadows incline towards the right and the left, prostrating to Allah while they are in the evening and the morning?
interpretation: The verse invites people to reflect on the natural world and how it points to the existence and majesty of Allah. The verse specifically mentions the way shadows incline towards the right and left, indicating the movement of the sun and the passage of time. The verse suggests that all creation, including inanimate objects like shadows, submits to Allah and acknowledges His greatness. The verse serves as a reminder to humans to also submit to Allah and recognize His power and majesty.
orig: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله وهم داخرون

translation: And to Allah prostrate all that is in the heavens and all that is on earth, willingly or unwillingly, and so do the angels, and they are not proud.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and submission of all creation to Allah, including both living and non-living things. The phrase 'willingly or unwillingly' highlights the idea that even those who resist or reject Allah's sovereignty are still subject to His will and power. The verse also underscores the humility of the angels, who, despite their exalted status, do not feel proud or arrogant before Allah's greatness.
orig: ولله يسجد ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من دابة والملائكة وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their Lord had not yet removed them, so they were overwhelmed by what they were warned of.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people in question had been warned of the consequences of their actions, but they did not heed the warning and continued to live in disobedience to God's commands. As a result, they were overwhelmed by the punishment that they had been warned of, and their Lord did not intervene to prevent it. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding God's warnings and living a righteous life, lest one suffers the same fate as those who were punished before.
orig: يخافون ربهم من فوقهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: And Allah says, 'Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and warns against the worship of any other being or object, including celestial bodies like the sun and the moon. It emphasizes that all creation, including the sun and the moon, is a sign of God's power and majesty, and that worship should be directed only to the Creator, not the created.
