translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be punished in this life and the Hereafter. Indeed, they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of hypocrisy, which is defined as claiming to be a believer but acting otherwise. The hypocrites will face punishment both in this life and the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who pretend to be believers but do not truly follow the teachings of Islam. The punishment mentioned in the verse is not limited to physical punishment but also includes spiritual and moral suffering. It also implies that the punishment will be severe and prolonged, as described as 'painful'.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: And indeed, they had sought [from their Lord] a blessing, a tremendous punishment was about to befall them.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people of the town had sought blessings from God, but instead, a severe punishment was about to befall them. This highlights the idea that God's punishment can be both a blessing and a curse, depending on the actions of the people. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and punishment are both aspects of His justice, and that those who seek His blessings must also be prepared to face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And do not extend your hand to the orphan's property, nor diminish the rights of the poor.
interpretation: The verse prohibits unjust treatment of the orphan and the poor. It emphasizes the importance of protecting the rights of the vulnerable and ensuring that they receive their due share of inheritance or property. The verse also warns against exploiting the weak and the poor, and encourages believers to stand up for justice and fairness in all aspects of life.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in providing for and sustaining His creation. The verse highlights God's ability to grant provision to whomever He chooses, indicating that all provision comes from Him and is not solely the result of human effort. The verse also underscores God's wisdom in restricting provision to some, which serves as a test for humanity and a means of purifying their faith. The verse reminds believers to trust in God's wisdom and provision, acknowledging that He is the ultimate source of sustenance and guidance.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We will provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing was a great mistake.
interpretation: The verse prohibits parents from killing their children due to fear of poverty, assuring them that God will provide for both the children and the parents. The verse emphasizes the gravity of the mistake of killing one's children, considering it a grave error that has severe consequences. The verse highlights the value of human life and the importance of protecting and caring for the vulnerable, particularly children who are dependent on their parents for sustenance and protection.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in the way of improving it until he reaches maturity.
interpretation: The verse prohibits people from approaching or touching an orphan's property, except in the way of improving it, until the orphan reaches maturity. The verse aims to protect the rights of the orphan and ensure that their property is not misused or misappropriated. It emphasizes the importance of preserving the orphan's assets and ensuring their well-being until they are able to manage their own affairs.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority, so let him not exceed in the killing. Indeed, he will be supported.
interpretation: This verse prohibits the killing of a soul that Allah has forbidden to be killed, except in cases where it is justified, such as in self-defense or in the punishment of a crime. The verse emphasizes the importance of not exceeding the limits in punishment, and reminds the heir of the victim that they have been given authority to seek justice, but not to seek revenge or exceed in killing. The verse serves as a reminder of the value of human life and the importance of justice and fairness in society.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in the way of improving it until he reaches maturity, and fulfill the covenant, indeed, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: The verse prohibits people from approaching or misusing the property of an orphan, except in a way that benefits the orphan and improves their situation, until they reach adulthood. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling covenants and promises, as they will be questioned about them on Judgment Day. The verse serves as a reminder to treat the vulnerable with kindness and respect, and to uphold one's responsibilities and obligations.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - all of them will be questioned about that.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of one's limitations and not seeking knowledge that is beyond one's capacity. The verse warns against pursuing things that are beyond one's understanding, as it can lead to misguidedness and misinterpretation. The verse also highlights the accountability of individuals for their actions, thoughts, and beliefs, as they will be questioned about them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not spread corruption in the land after its reformation. Indeed, you will not be able to corrupt the land, and you will not reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preserving the land and not engaging in corrupt practices that can harm the environment and the community. The second part of the verse highlights the idea that humans are limited in their ability to control and manipulate nature, and that they will never be able to reach the height of mountains, indicating the powerlessness of human beings in the face of nature's grandeur.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: And indeed, that was a evil deed, that they were punished for their sins.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that the people of the destroyed towns received from God, describing it as a 'evil deed' that they were punished for their sins. The verse suggests that the punishment was not only a consequence of their actions, but also a manifestation of God's justice and wrath. The use of the word 'indeed' at the beginning of the verse serves to emphasize the gravity of the situation and the certainty of the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have sent down to you a clear Book, which We have detailed with knowledge, guidance, and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and guidance that God has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community. The 'clear victory' refers to the triumph of Islam over the disbelievers, and the 'manifest triumph' refers to the evident and clear nature of the Prophet's mission. The 'clear Book' that God has sent down is the Qur'an, which contains knowledge, guidance, and mercy for those who believe. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a means of mercy for those who follow it.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whispers of humans, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and emphasizes the idea that humans are never alone, and that God is always with them, watching over them and aware of their thoughts and actions.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: And indeed, We have given them a Qur'an wherein they are reminded, but most of them have forgotten, except the evildoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to serve as a reminder to people of their Creator and their ultimate purpose in life. However, the verse also notes that many people have forgotten this message and instead chosen to live in disobedience to God. The phrase 'except the evildoers' suggests that those who have forgotten the message of the Qur'an are not just passive forgetters, but are actively living in opposition to God's commandments. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of remembering and living according to God's guidance, and the consequences of neglecting this reminder.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: And if there were a Qur'an whereby the mountains could be moved, or the earth could be torn apart, or the heavens could be climbed, they would not have believed in its message.
interpretation: The verse highlights the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, implying that even if a Qur'an were to be revealed that could move mountains, split the earth, or climb the heavens, the disbelievers would still not believe in its message. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book, but a miraculous sign from God, and that the disbelievers' rejection of it is not due to a lack of evidence, but rather due to their own stubbornness and refusal to accept the truth.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: And they say: What is the matter with this Messenger, that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why has not an angel been sent down to him, so that he should have been accompanied by a warner?
interpretation: The verse addresses the criticism of the disbelievers who question the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). They wonder why he eats food and walks in the markets like a common person, and why he has not been accompanied by an angel as a warner. The verse highlights the disbelievers' skepticism towards the Prophet's message and their demand for a miraculous sign, which they believe would be a proof of his prophethood. The verse also emphasizes the Prophet's human nature and his role as a warner and a reminder for the people, rather than an angel or a supernatural being.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is within them glorify Him, and there is not a thing except that it glorifies His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of God's sovereignty and the fact that everything in the universe, including the seven heavens and the earth, glorifies Him. The verse also highlights the fact that all creation, including humans, are required to glorify God and acknowledge His greatness. The verse ends by emphasizing God's attribute of Forbearance and Forgiveness, indicating that He is patient with humanity's sins and is always willing to forgive those who repent and turn to Him.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We put between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an's ability to create a spiritual barrier between the believers and the disbelievers. The word 'hidden' emphasizes that this barrier is not physical but spiritual, and it serves as a protection for the believers from the influence of the disbelievers. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role in creating a distinction between the two groups and reinforces the idea that the Qur'an is a divine revelation that guides and separates the righteous from the wicked.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have put a barrier in front of their hearts, so they understand it not, and in their ears, and We have put a covering on their eyes, so they see not.
interpretation: This verse describes how God has placed obstacles in the hearts and minds of those who reject faith, preventing them from understanding and perceiving the truth. The 'barrier' in front of their hearts symbolizes their spiritual blindness and inability to comprehend the message of the Qur'an. The 'covering' on their eyes represents their physical and spiritual blindness, which prevents them from seeing the signs of God's existence and the truth of His message. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting faith and the importance of seeking guidance from God.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were far more powerful than your town, and the punishment came to them suddenly, while they were unaware.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers who are skeptical of the Prophet Muhammad's message. God is reminding them that He has destroyed many powerful towns in the past, and their punishment came suddenly, without warning. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that they too will face the consequences of their actions if they continue to reject God's message.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they said, 'When we are bones and crumbled particles, shall we indeed be raised up as a new creation?',
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' mocking response to the idea of resurrection. They find it absurd that they will be brought back to life as a new creation, suggesting that their current state of being is so deteriorated that they cannot fathom how they could possibly be restored to a previous state of existence, let alone a new and improved one. The verse highlights the disbelievers' skepticism and lack of faith in the possibility of resurrection, which is a central tenet of Islamic belief.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Most High, the Most Great.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a warner, reminding his listeners of the importance of heeding God's message. The verse also highlights the oneness of God, emphasizing that He is the only deity worthy of worship. The use of the phrase 'the One, the Most High, the Most Great' reinforces God's majesty and dominance over all creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain mindful of their relationship with God and to live according to His will.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or He creates a tendency in their hearts to disagree with each other, so they will say: 'Converse not with him! He had a quarrel with us the first time.' And they will turn their heads away, and they will say: 'It may be that he will be occupied and not be able to answer.'
interpretation: The verse suggests that God can create dissension and disagreement among people, causing them to turn against each other and reject the message of the prophet. The verse also implies that people may try to avoid the prophet, thinking that he is too busy or preoccupied to respond to their queries. The verse serves as a reminder that God is in control of all things and can influence people's hearts and actions, and that people should not underestimate the power of the divine message.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: And on the Day when He will call you and you will respond with praise, and you will think that you have been delayed only a little.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when all humans will be summoned by God and will respond with praise. The verse highlights the idea that the delay between the life of this world and the Hereafter will seem insignificant in comparison to the eternal nature of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the impending judgment and the need for preparedness for the Hereafter, as well as the importance of living a life of righteousness and obedience to God.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces [doubt] in them, for Satan is to humanity a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse instructs Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to command his followers to speak what is good and righteous. The verse also highlights the role of Satan in promoting evil and doubt among humans. Satan is described as a clear enemy of humanity, constantly seeking to mislead people and turn them away from the righteous path. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of Satan's influence and striving to resist his temptations in order to live a virtuous life.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord knows that indeed He may show mercy to you or punish you, and We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], against them as a guardian over them. And your Lord is sufficient as a witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over His creation. He is aware of the actions of humanity and has the authority to show mercy or punish as He sees fit. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger, not a guardian or ruler over the people. The verse serves as a reminder that God is sufficient as a witness over all things and that He is the ultimate authority in the universe.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is aware of what is in the heavens and the earth, and We have given some of the prophets preference over others, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power, encompassing all aspects of the universe, including what is hidden and unknown to humanity. The verse also highlights the special status of certain prophets, such as David, who received divine revelation in the form of the Psalms. The verse serves as a reminder of God's authority and the importance of following the teachings of the prophets, particularly in regards to justice and righteousness.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim besides Him, for they do not possess the ability to remove the harm from you, nor can they change it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the issue of polytheism and the idea that some people believe in calling upon other deities besides Allah for help and protection. The verse emphasizes that those deities are powerless and unable to remove harm or change the situation. It is a reminder that only Allah has the power to help and protect, and that seeking help from other sources is futile. The verse encourages the reader to put their trust in Allah and to seek His help alone.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: And those who pray, 'Our Lord, let us not be punished with the wicked people, and we are eager for Your mercy, and we fear Your punishment.' Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is fearsome.
interpretation: This verse describes the prayer of the righteous, who beg God to spare them from the punishment that will befall the wicked. They acknowledge their own vulnerability and the mercy of God, and they fear the consequences of His justice. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's mercy and the fear of His punishment, which is a central theme in Islamic spirituality. The phrase 'the punishment of your Lord is fearsome' underscores the gravity of God's justice and the severity of His punishment for those who disobey Him.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town before you. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, they will be brought forth [for judgment].
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has destroyed many towns in the past as a punishment for their wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of these towns was a consequence of their own actions, and serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds on Judgment Day.
orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And We have not sent the signs except to warn and make them afraid, but the wicked ones deny them, and they are turned away from them, and they are not reminded except in a little. And We have not sent the signs except as a threat, and a reminder for those who fear [Allah].
interpretation: The verse explains the purpose of the signs and miracles sent by God to humanity. They are meant to serve as warnings and reminders for those who are wicked and have turned away from God's guidance. The signs are not intended to be taken lightly or ignored, but are meant to instill fear and awe in those who see them, and to remind them of the consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights the fact that even when signs and miracles are presented, some people will still reject them and refuse to believe.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And indeed, We have warned you that your Lord is (as) near (as) the observers and what We have made the vision that We show you, (it is) only a trial for the people, and the tree cursed in the Qur'an, and We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
interpretation: The verse warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God is near and watching, and that the visions and signs He sends are a trial for the people. The 'cursed tree' refers to the tree of evil and disobedience, and the verse suggests that even when people are warned and frightened by God's punishment, they continue to commit great sins and transgressions.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they all prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant and said, 'I am better than him. I was created from fire, while he was created from clay.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene in which God commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam, the first human, as a sign of respect and obedience. All the angels complied, except Iblis (Satan), who refused to submit to God's command. Iblis's arrogance and pride led him to believe that he was superior to Adam, who was created from clay, while he was created from fire. This verse highlights the dangers of pride and arrogance, and serves as a warning against rebelling against God's commands.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: And indeed, Hell is the punishment for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reality of Hell as a punishment for those who reject the message of Islam and choose to disbelieve in Allah. The use of the word 'indeed' suggests that this is a certain and definitive truth, and the description of Hell as a 'punishment' underscores the idea that it is a consequence of one's actions in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them that their disbelief will lead to a terrible fate in the Hereafter.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, my servants have no authority over them. Your Lord is sufficient as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power, highlighting the fact that even the prophets and messengers of God have no authority over the wicked. Instead, God is the only one who has the power to guide and protect His servants. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the importance of relying solely on Him for guidance and protection.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is the One who speeds forth the ships for you in the sea, that you may seek of His bounty, indeed, He has been with you merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and generosity in providing for humanity. The image of ships sailing across the sea, carrying goods and people, is a reminder that God's blessings are not limited to land-based resources. The verse emphasizes that God's mercy and provision are all-encompassing, extending even to those who venture out into the vast ocean. The phrase 'He has been with you merciful' underscores the idea that God's mercy is not just a one-time event, but a constant and ongoing presence in our lives.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: And when the suffering reached us in the sea, those who were oppressed cried out to Us for help, but when We saved you to the shore, you turned away and forgot about Us.
interpretation: The verse refers to a specific incident where the Israelites were suffering in the sea and cried out to God for help. God saved them and brought them to the shore, but instead of being grateful and remembering God's favor, they turned away and forgot about God. The verse highlights the ingratitude of the Israelites and serves as a reminder to all believers to be thankful for God's blessings and to remember God's favors upon them.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Have you thought that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you up or send upon you a violent storm? Then you will not find a guardian or a savior.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of God and His ability to punish those who disobey Him. The verse describes two possible ways in which God could punish the disobedient: either by causing the ground to swallow them up or by sending a violent storm upon them. The verse emphasizes that there will be no escape from God's punishment, and that no one will be able to protect or save those who have been warned. The verse serves as a warning to those who are disobedient, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's wrath.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Have you not considered, if We were to return you to your Lord, that you would meet Him with shame, and that you were in a state of rebellion?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and asks them to consider the consequence of their actions. If they were to be returned to their Lord, they would be met with shame and embarrassment, as they had rebelled against Him and refused to follow His commandments. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability of human beings to God and the consequences of their actions in this life and the hereafter.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam, and We have carried them on land and sea, and We have provided for them good and pure sustenance, and We have preferred them over many of those whom We have created with a marked preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and dignity that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. God has blessed them with the ability to inhabit both land and sea, and has provided them with good and pure sustenance. Additionally, God has preferred human beings over many other creatures, indicating their elevated position in the hierarchy of creation. This verse serves as a reminder of the inherent value and dignity of human life, and encourages believers to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: And the Day when We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who were followed: 'Where are those who were followed?', and their only argument will be: 'Lord, we did not wrong anyone, but we were only following what our fathers used to follow.'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered together and those who followed false leaders will be asked about their actions. The verse highlights the fact that the followers will have no excuse but to say that they were only following their ancestors' traditions. The verse warns against blindly following others and emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever was blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray from the Path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the consequences of spiritual blindness in this life, which will lead to further astrayness in the Hereafter. The verse implies that those who are spiritually blind in this life, unable to see the truth and guidance of God, will also be blind in the Hereafter, unable to find their way to salvation. The verse serves as a warning to those who are spiritually blind, encouraging them to seek guidance and enlightenment from God, lest they become even more lost in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from what We have revealed to you, that you might fabricate something else against Us, and then they would have taken you as a friend.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers were trying to manipulate the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and lead him astray from the message revealed to him by God. They wanted him to invent a different message, one that would be more palatable to them and would not challenge their beliefs and practices. The verse highlights the deceptive nature of the disbelievers and their attempt to undermine the Prophet's authority and credibility. It also emphasizes the importance of staying true to God's message and not compromising one's beliefs to appease others.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not made you (Prophet Muhammad) stand firm, you would have almost inclined to them a little.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, saying that if God had not given him strength and stability, he would have been tempted to follow the disbelievers and incline towards their ways. The verse highlights the Prophet's human side and his potential weakness in the face of adversity. It also underscores God's protection and support for the Prophet, without which he would have been swayed by the disbelievers' arguments and actions. The verse serves as a reminder that even the greatest prophets are not immune to temptation and need God's guidance and support to stay on the righteous path.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with His creation. Despite the people's disobedience and rebellion, God does not immediately punish them. Instead, He gives them respite in this life, allowing them time to repent and turn back to Him. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's mercy and continue to live in disobedience. The punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe than any punishment that could be inflicted in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are rebellious and a reminder of God's justice and mercy.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from the land to drive you out of it, but they will not succeed except in a little way.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of the disbelievers to drive the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) out of the land. They wanted to tempt him into leaving the land, but their efforts were futile. The verse indicates that the Prophet was steadfast in his faith and determination, and the disbelievers were unable to achieve their goal. The verse serves as a reminder that those who seek to spread the message of God will face opposition and persecution, but they must remain steadfast and not be deterred by the attempts of their enemies to drive them out.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their background, race, or religion. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message and underscores the importance of spreading love, kindness, and forgiveness to all people.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: And establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night and the Qur'an at the dawn. Indeed, the Qur'an at the dawn is witnessed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer at the decline of the sun, indicating the time for the afternoon prayer, and until the darkness of the night, indicating the time for the evening prayer. It also highlights the significance of reciting the Qur'an at dawn, which is a time of spiritual reflection and intimacy with God. The verse suggests that the Qur'an recited at dawn is a witnessed act, implying that it is a time when believers are more likely to be mindful of their relationship with God and their responsibilities towards Him.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And during the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him, perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.
interpretation: The verse encourages the believers to prostrate and glorify God during the night, indicating the importance of worship and humility. The phrase 'perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station' suggests that those who worship God sincerely and consistently may be elevated to a high position in this life or in the hereafter. The verse highlights the potential for spiritual growth and reward for those who dedicate themselves to God's service.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say, 'My Lord, admit me into the entrance of truth, and cause me to exit the exit of truth, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is asking God to guide them towards the path of truth and to grant them the ability to remain on that path until the end. The phrase 'entrance of truth' refers to the beginning of the journey towards righteousness, and the 'exit of truth' refers to the ultimate goal of achieving salvation. The speaker is seeking God's guidance and support throughout their journey, asking for the strength and courage to stay on the path of righteousness and to overcome any obstacles that may come their way. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's guidance and support in all aspects of life, and serves as a reminder that true success and happiness can only be achieved through submission to God's will.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And the truth has come, and the falsehood has vanished. Indeed, the falsehood was bound to vanish.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate victory of truth over falsehood. The phrase 'wa qal' (and say) is used to emphasize the certainty and finality of the statement that follows. The word 'haq' (truth) refers not only to the revelation of God but also to all that is good and right. On the other hand, 'batil' (falsehood) encompasses all that is false, evil, and misleading. The second part of the verse emphasizes that falsehood is bound to disappear, indicating that it lacks the substance and staying power of truth. The verse serves as a reminder that truth will ultimately prevail, and those who adhere to it will ultimately triumph.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We have sent down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of the Qur'an. On one hand, it serves as a source of guidance, healing, and mercy for the believers, providing them with spiritual nourishment and guidance on the path to righteousness. On the other hand, for those who reject the message of the Qur'an and choose to live in disobedience to God, the Qur'an serves as a source of punishment and increase in loss. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a source of benefit for the disbelievers, but rather a source of condemnation and punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to cherish and follow the guidance of the Qur'an, while also warning the disbelievers of the consequences of their rejection.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. The verse emphasizes the special status of humanity, created in the image of God, and distinguishes them from other creatures. The phrase 'We have honored' signifies the inherent worth and dignity of every human being, regardless of their race, gender, or social status. The verse serves as a reminder of the great potential and responsibility that comes with being human, and encourages individuals to live up to their divine calling.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Each one acts according to his own way; your Lord is fully aware of who is guided onto the right path.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that individuals have free will and are responsible for their own actions. The phrase 'each one acts according to his own way' suggests that people have agency and can choose their own path in life. The second part of the verse, 'your Lord is fully aware of who is guided onto the right path', indicates that God is aware of who is following the righteous path and who is not. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, it is up to the individual to make the right choices and follow the path of righteousness, and that God is aware of and will judge each person's actions.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you about the Spirit. Say, 'The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord, and you have not been given except a little knowledge of it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of the nature of the Spirit, which is a mystery that is not fully comprehensible to human understanding. The verse suggests that the Spirit is a part of God's domain and is not fully accessible to human knowledge. The phrase 'a little knowledge' implies that humans have been given some understanding of the Spirit, but it is limited and incomplete. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and understanding in the face of God's vast and mysterious power.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with His creation. Despite the people's disobedience and rebellion, God did not destroy them immediately. Instead, He gave them respite, allowing them to repent and turn back to Him. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message in the Hereafter, indicating that it is far more severe than any punishment that could be inflicted in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are rebellious and a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: Except for the mercy of your Lord, [their punishment] would have been inevitable [and they would have been destroyed].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the only reason the people are not being punished is due to the mercy of God. The use of the word 'except' suggests that the punishment would have been inevitable had it not been for God's mercy. This verse serves as a reminder of God's grace and mercy towards humanity, and how it is only by His grace that we are not punished for our sins. It also highlights the idea that God's mercy is not something that can be earned or deserved, but rather it is a gift from God that we should be grateful for.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over the destruction of towns and nations. The verse suggests that if God had wanted to destroy the wicked people, He could have done so in this life, but instead, He has reserved a more severe punishment for the Hereafter. This verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment in the afterlife.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And indeed, We have given examples in this Qur'an for people, but most of the people refuse to believe in Me, except the disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has provided numerous examples and signs in the Qur'an to guide people towards the truth and righteousness, but despite this, many people choose to reject and disbelieve in God's message. The verse emphasizes that the majority of people who reject God's message are the disobedient ones, who refuse to submit to God's will and instead choose to follow their own desires and sinful ways.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they say, 'We will not believe you until you make a spring gush forth from the earth for us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' demand for a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a condition for their belief. They asked him to make a spring gush forth from the earth, which was an impossible request, as it was not within the Prophet's power to control nature in such a way. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of the disbelievers, who were unwilling to accept the message of Islam and instead sought to test the Prophet's authority with impossible demands. The verse serves as a reminder that true belief cannot be forced or coerced, and that it must come from a sincere heart that recognizes and submits to the truth.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or have you thought that the Companions of the Garden will be in a state of security from the punishment of Allah?
interpretation: The verse questions whether the companions of the Garden, who are the righteous believers, will be secure from God's punishment. The verse suggests that even the righteous believers are not immune to God's punishment, and that they must always be mindful of their actions and remain obedient to God's commandments. The verse serves as a reminder that no one is exempt from God's justice, and that everyone will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or the heaven falls and comes down upon us in pieces, as you have believed, or the angels come down, or Jesus, son of Mary, descends, or the heavens are opened and the angels ascend, or the dead are raised, or for a sign is given to you, until the people are in confusion and the matter is decided, and they are in a state of intoxication, and the angels are near, and the Trumpet is blown, and the people are gathered, and the heavens are opened, and the angels are ascending, and the dead are raised, and the judgment is passed, and the matter is decided, and the heavens are closed, and the Trumpet is blown, and the people are terrified, and the angels are near
interpretation: N
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or [consider] the one who has been given a life of ease and prosperity, who says, 'I will not believe in [the message of] the Most Merciful [God] until I see an angel descending from the sky.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has been blessed with wealth and luxury, but is skeptical of the message of God's mercy and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The person in question demands a miraculous sign, such as an angel descending from the sky, before they will believe. The verse highlights the arrogance and ingratitude of this person, who is so consumed by their wealth and worldly desires that they refuse to acknowledge the truth of God's message. The verse serves as a warning to those who are similarly skeptical of God's message and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), reminding them that faith requires humility and submission to God's will, rather than relying on material possessions or worldly signs.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And what prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said: 'God has sent a human messenger'?
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of the people's reaction to the arrival of a prophet sent by God. Instead of embracing the guidance, they reject it, claiming that God would not send a human messenger. This reaction is seen as a form of denial and a refusal to accept the truth. The verse emphasizes the idea that the people's disbelief is not due to a lack of evidence or convincing arguments, but rather due to their own preconceived notions and biases. The verse serves as a reminder that guidance and prophethood are not limited to a particular race or species, and that God's messengers can come in many forms.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: And if there were angels on earth, walking around and feeling secure, We would have sent down to them from the sky a messenger angel as a Warner.
interpretation: The verse suggests that if there were angels living on earth, they would have been destroyed by God's punishment, just like the people of the towns that were destroyed in the past. The verse emphasizes the idea that even the angels, who are considered to be close to God and pure, would not be spared from God's punishment if they were to commit sins and become complacent. The verse serves as a warning to believers, reminding them that no one is immune to God's punishment, and that everyone will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you, He is certainly aware of His servants' state.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God is sufficient as a witness between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people. God is all-aware of the state of His servants and is fully cognizant of their deeds, thoughts, and intentions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of everything that happens, and that He will ultimately bring to justice those who have been unjust and reward those who have been righteous.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whoever is guided by Allah - He will be the one who is guided. And whoever is misguided - then they will have no guardians besides Him. And on the Day of Resurrection, their faces will be humiliated, and their tongues will be tied, and their hands and feet will be bound. Then they will be burned in Hell, and they will be given to drink boiling water, and their punishment will be increased.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of guidance from Allah and the consequences of being misguided. The verse states that those who are guided by Allah will be successful, while those who are misguided will have no one to protect them from God's punishment. The verse describes the punishment of those who are misguided, including shame, inability to speak, and physical restraints. They will be burned in Hell and forced to drink boiling water, and their punishment will be increased. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of seeking guidance from Allah.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: And they have been punished with the punishment of the Hereafter, because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'When we are bones and crumbled particles, shall we indeed be raised up as a new creation?',
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that those who disbelieve in God's signs and reject the idea of resurrection will face in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the mocking tone of the disbelievers, who question the possibility of their own resurrection, comparing it to the idea of being recreated from crumbled particles. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the idea of resurrection and the possibility of being held accountable for their actions in this life, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: And they did not apprehend that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the like of them, and He has appointed for them a doom from which there is no escape. Then the wrongdoers will have no helper.
interpretation: The verse highlights the power of Allah as the Creator of the universe, emphasizing that He is capable of creating similar beings to those who reject His signs. The verse also emphasizes the certainty of punishment for those who reject Allah's signs and do wrong. The phrase 'there is no escape' underscores the idea that the punishment is inescapable and that there will be no helper or intercessor for the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, 'If you owned the treasures of my Lord's mercy, you would have held back from fear of poverty.' And indeed, man has been created impatient.
interpretation: The verse addresses the human tendency to be impatient and desperate in the face of financial difficulties. The verse suggests that if people had control over God's mercy and blessings, they would have been more cautious in their spending and would have avoided falling into poverty. However, since humans are inherently impatient, they often fail to appreciate the value of what they have and are prone to squandering God's blessings. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate and be mindful of God's favors and to be grateful for what we have.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses nine clear signs. Ask the Children of Israel when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, 'I think you, Moses, are bewitched.'
interpretation: The verse mentions the nine miraculous signs given to Prophet Moses by God, which were performed in front of the Children of Israel. The verse also highlights Pharaoh's reaction to Moses' miracles, where he accused Moses of being bewitched or under the influence of magic. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the truth of Moses' prophethood, and also highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and refusal to believe in Moses' message.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: And Moses said: 'I have knowledge that you have been sent as a Messenger by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and I am convinced of this, O Pharaoh.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing Pharaoh and expressing his belief that he has been sent by God as a Messenger. Moses is emphasizing his conviction that God has sent him on a mission to guide Pharaoh and his people towards the right path. The verse highlights Moses' confidence in his prophetic role and his belief in the authority and power of God. It also underscores the idea that God's message is not limited to a particular group or individual, but is universal and applicable to all people, including Pharaoh, who is considered one of the most powerful rulers of his time.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: And he wanted to incline the city to the ground, so We made it swallow him up, and all who were with him.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a city that was unjust and its people were warned by a righteous man, but they refused to listen. The verse describes how the city was swallowed up by the earth, along with all its inhabitants, as a punishment from God. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and continue to live in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's wrath.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after Pharaoh to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in crowds.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the promise made by God to the Children of Israel after the time of Pharaoh, in which they were commanded to dwell in the land and wait for the promise of the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Children of Israel were not forgotten by God, and that they would be brought forth in crowds at the time of the promise. The verse serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness to His promises and His ability to fulfill His plans for His chosen people.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And indeed, We have sent it down, and indeed, We are its guardians.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an, highlighting that it was sent down by God and that God Himself is its guardian. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, and its message is meant to be preserved and protected. The verse also underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a warning to those who reject its message.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse also underscores the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, as he was sent to bring people closer to God and to guide them towards a righteous and just life. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to this world, but it also encompasses the hereafter, indicating that his message has implications for both this life and the next.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, 'Believe in it or do not believe in it, indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, they fall down upon their faces in prostration.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the people to believe or not believe in the Qur'an. The verse then describes the reaction of those who were given knowledge before it, indicating that they would fall down in prostration upon hearing it. This verse highlights the impact of the Qur'an on those who are knowledgeable about the scriptures and its ability to evoke a sense of submission and humility in those who truly understand its message.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, 'Glory to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the people of Sodom when they were informed of the impending destruction of their town. They exclaimed 'Glory to our Lord!', acknowledging the greatness and power of God, and recognizing that the punishment they were about to face was a fulfillment of God's promise. The verse highlights the idea that even in the face of destruction, one should remember and glorify God, and that His promises are always fulfilled.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they will be driven to the edge of the Fire, and they will be brought forth from it, and it will be said to them: 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire!',
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. They will be driven to the edge of the Fire, signifying their proximity to the punishment they have earned. The use of the word 'edge' suggests that they are on the brink of falling into the Fire, and the phrase 'and they will be brought forth from it' implies that they will be forced to endure the agony of the Fire. The phrase 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire!' is a warning to those who refuse to believe, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment is not just a physical one, but also a spiritual and emotional one, as they will be forced to face the consequences of their disobedience.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, 'Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful, whichever you call upon, for to Him belong the most beautiful names.' Do not raise your voice in prayer, nor speak softly, but seek a way between that.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of invoking Allah, the Most Merciful, and using the most beautiful names to address Him. It also instructs the believers to maintain a moderate tone during prayer, avoiding both shouting and whispering. Instead, they should seek a middle ground in their supplications, indicating a balance between humility and confidence in their communication with Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that the believers should establish a strong connection with Allah through their prayers and supplications, using the most beautiful names to glorify Him.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say: 'Praise be to Allah, Who has not taken a son, nor has He a partner in sovereignty, nor does He have any weakness or vulnerability.'
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the theme of the greatness and uniqueness of Allah, emphasizing His absolute perfection and independence. The verse highlights four aspects of Allah's uniqueness: 1) He has no son or offspring, indicating that He is eternal and has no need for procreation or succession. 2) He has no partner in sovereignty, signifying that His authority and dominion are absolute and unshared. 3) He has no weakness or vulnerability, underscoring His infinite power and strength. 4) He is above any need for help or support, as indicated by the phrase 'ولي من الذل' (and has no weakness or vulnerability). The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's transcendence and majesty, and encourages believers to reflect on and appreciate the greatness of their Lord.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: And indeed, We have sent down to you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Qur'an itself, which is described as a 'clear victory' and a 'manifest triumph' for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The verse emphasizes the clarity and manifest nature of the Qur'an, indicating that its message is clear, straightforward, and easy to understand. The verse also highlights the triumph and victory that comes with following the teachings of the Qur'an, leading to a life of guidance, righteousness, and success in this world and the hereafter.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various difficulties, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and fruits. However, the verse also assures the believers that they will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is tested through adversity, and that the believers who remain patient and steadfast will receive their reward in the Hereafter.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And warn those who say, 'God has taken a son.'
interpretation: The verse warns those who claim that God has taken a son, which is a belief that is not supported by Islamic theology. The verse emphasizes that God is unique and indivisible, and cannot be compared to human beings who have children. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the only one worthy of worship and that the belief in the oneness of God is a fundamental principle of Islam.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: And they have no knowledge of the Hereafter, nor do they have any insight into the matter. They only make guesses and spread falsehood.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance and lack of understanding of the disbelievers, who not only reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but also spread falsehood and make baseless accusations against him. The verse emphasizes that they have no real knowledge or insight into the spiritual realm or the Hereafter, and their arguments against the Prophet and Islam are based on mere speculation and falsehood. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and instead choose to follow their own desires and misguided beliefs.
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: And indeed, We will suffice for their lies (and) indeed, they will be losers who will be punished.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of lying and spreading falsehood. The phrase 'We will suffice for their lies' implies that God is aware of their lies and will take care of them. The second part of the verse 'indeed, they will be losers who will be punished' emphasizes that those who engage in such behavior will face consequences in this life and the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in lies and falsehood, reminding them of the negative consequences of their actions.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on earth as an adornment for it, so that We may test them as to which of them is the best in deed.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has created the beauty and riches of the earth as a test for humanity. The verse implies that the material world is a means to evaluate the faith and deeds of humans. The verse also implies that the beauty and riches of the earth are not an end in themselves but a means to an end, which is to live a righteous life and to be tested in one's faith. The verse emphasizes the idea that the true purpose of human existence is not to indulge in worldly desires but to live a virtuous life and to be accountable to God.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We have made that which is on earth as a decoration, and We have made it a testing ground for them.
interpretation: The verse explains that the things on earth, including the beautiful and attractive things, are not an end in themselves, but rather a means to an end. They are a test for humanity, to see who will use them in a responsible and righteous way, and who will be distracted by them and led astray. The verse warns against attachment to worldly things and encourages a focus on spiritual growth and development.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: And certainly, We have destroyed the owners of the garden, the people of the trench, who were arrogant because of their wealth and their rejecting of the signs of Allah.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of the trench, who were destroyed because of their arrogance and rejection of God's signs. The verse emphasizes the connection between their arrogance and their rejection of God's signs, suggesting that their arrogance led them to reject the message of God and His prophets. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and reject the signs of God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: And when the boy was old enough, he went to the well and said, 'O Lord, give me from Your mercy and grant me a wise judgment in my affair.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the young man who was raised by the Prophet Joseph, who after reaching maturity, went to the well to ask for God's mercy and guidance in his affairs. The verse highlights the young man's faith in God and his reliance on Him for guidance, indicating that he was a righteous person who sought divine assistance in his life. The verse also emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from God and the role of faith in times of need.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: And We have put a barrier in front of them, blocking them from the cave for three years.
interpretation: The verse describes how God blocked the entrance to the cave where the people of the town were hiding, trapping them inside for three years. The barrier was a punishment from God, preventing them from escaping or seeking help. The verse highlights God's power and control over all things, and how He can isolate and punish those who disobey Him. The three years also symbolize a period of trial and testing, where the people were given time to reflect on their actions and repent, but they failed to do so.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We sent forth Our messengers to inform them of the punishment, that they might be reminded of their Lord's command, and they might be brought back from their evil ways.
interpretation: In this verse, God describes how He sent prophets and messengers to warn the people of the punishment that was coming their way due to their disobedience and sin. The purpose of the messengers was to remind the people of God's commandments and to bring them back to the right path. The verse emphasizes the mercy and compassion of God, who wants to guide His creation towards righteousness and away from destruction. The verse also highlights the importance of listening to the message of the prophets and heeding their warnings, in order to avoid the consequences of disobedience.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various difficulties, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. However, the verse also reassures the believers that those who are patient and persevering will receive good news. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of testing one's faith and that the true believers will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We have put a barrier over their hearts, so they do not understand it, and a covering over their ears, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse describes how God has placed a barrier over the hearts and ears of those who reject faith, preventing them from understanding and hearing the message of the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes the idea that the obstacle to faith is not intellectual, but rather a spiritual one. The verse serves as a warning to those who are resistant to faith, reminding them that their stubbornness and rejection of God's message will only lead to their own spiritual blindness and deafness.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: Those before them had schemed, but the plan of Allah is supreme. And Allah knows what they do not know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of previous nations to defy God's will and their ultimate failure. The verse emphasizes that despite their schemes and plans, God's plan is supreme and will ultimately prevail. The verse serves as a reminder that human beings are limited in their knowledge and understanding, and that God's wisdom and power are superior to all human schemes and plans.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when We sent to them a group of angels, they rejoiced not, nor did they remember their prayer, for they had denied before, and they used to oppress the believers, and they used to say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who were sent a group of angels as a sign of God's mercy and guidance. However, instead of being grateful and remembering their prayer, they rejected the sign and continued to oppress the believers. They even questioned why a sign had not been sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from his Lord. The verse highlights the ingratitude and arrogance of those who reject God's signs and messengers, and serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and persecute the believers.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you see the sun when it rose, it will be a hastening of Doom for those who were in the shade of their homes, and when it set, it will be a darkness for them, and they will be overtaken by a torment, there is no escape from Allah's punishment. That is a sign for those who fear My warning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The rising and setting of the sun serves as a metaphor for the impending doom that awaits those who reject God's warning. The image of the sun rising and setting also emphasizes the inescapable nature of God's punishment, which will envelop those who reject the truth like a dark shadow. The verse ends with a reminder that there is no escape from God's punishment, and that it is a warning for those who fear His wrath.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And they have been warned against (the punishment of) the day that is coming, but they have been heedless and have played, and their covering (of excuses) has been (a) shame and a (false) hope, and their judgments have been (as) weak as a broken thread. And they have been warned against (the punishment of) the day that is coming, but they have been heedless and have played, and their covering (of excuses) has been (a) shame and a (false) hope, and their judgments have been (as) weak as a broken thread.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have been warned about the coming punishment but have chosen to ignore it. They have been heedless and have been occupied with their own desires and false hopes, instead of taking heed of the warning. Their attempts to cover up their wrongdoing have been in vain, and their justifications have been weak and unconvincing. The verse serves as a reminder that the punishment is near and that those who have ignored the warning will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And thus We have sent them (the prophets) to various towns to ask questions and (then) We destroyed them. (The people) said, 'How long have you remained (in this state)?' They said, 'We have been here for a day or a part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord is most knowledgeable about what you have done. So, send one of you with this scroll to the city, and let him see which of you has the most knowledge about food, and let him come back to you with provision and do not harm anyone.'
