orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: And We have sent to them a spirit that would speak to them in their sleepless nights, but they were turned away from it and they were being neglectful.
interpretation: The verse describes how God sent a spirit to guide the people, but they ignored it and were too arrogant to listen. The spirit tried to speak to them in the dead of night when they were alone with their thoughts, but they refused to listen. This verse highlights the people's stubbornness and unwillingness to listen to God's message, which ultimately led to their downfall.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from your evil.
interpretation: The verse expresses the speaker's seek for refuge in Allah, the Most Merciful, from the evil of the person being addressed. It implies that the speaker believes the person is capable of evil actions or intentions and seeks protection from Allah's mercy and protection.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: And indeed, I am a messenger of your Lord, to warn you of a severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse introduces the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger of God, sent to warn the people of a severe punishment that awaits those who reject God's message. The verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and highlights the gravity of the situation, as the punishment is described as 'severe'. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human beings and the importance of heeding the warning of God's messengers.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: And I (Muhammad) say: 'My Lord! Indeed, my people have abandoned this Qur'an.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his grief and sadness over the fact that his people have rejected the Qur'an and abandoned its teachings. The verse highlights the Prophet's deep concern for his community and his desire for them to accept the message of the Qur'an. It also underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: And indeed, your Lord said: 'I will indeed decree a penalty for them, and I will make it a sign for the people, and a lesson for the wise.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of the towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes that the punishment was not only a punishment but also a sign and a lesson for the people. The sign is a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse also highlights the wisdom and knowledge that can be gained from reflecting on the destruction of these towns and the reasons for their downfall.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: And We have destroyed many a town while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you; do you not take heed?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed previous nations that disobeyed Him. The verse is a warning to the Prophet and his followers, encouraging them to learn from the mistakes of the past and to take heed of the consequences of disobedience. The verse also emphasizes the power and authority of God, who has the ability to destroy entire nations if they reject His commands.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And We have sent you (O Muhammad) to all the people as a witness, and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a witness and a warner to all people. The verse highlights the dual nature of the Prophet's mission: to bring good news to those who follow God's commandments and to warn those who disobey God of the consequences of their actions. The use of the word 'all' emphasizes the universal nature of the Prophet's message, indicating that it is applicable to all people regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of God and the accountability of those who receive it.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So We have destroyed communities, and We have given you (O Muhammad SAW) a clear victory and a manifest triumph (over them).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the destruction of communities that were unjust and refused to heed the warnings of God's prophets. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is a manifestation of His justice and that it is a clear victory for the believers who have been oppressed by these communities. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he has been given a clear victory and a manifest triumph over his enemies, and that he should not be afraid to speak out against injustice.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into it Our Spirit and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was one of the devout.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the virtues of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her devotion to God. The verse highlights her chastity and her belief in God's words and scriptures. The phrase 'We blew into it Our Spirit' refers to the moment when God breathed life into Mary, signifying the divine nature of Jesus' conception. The verse serves as an example to believers, emphasizing the importance of faith, chastity, and devotion to God.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O my mother, how my father was humiliated, and my mother was in a bad way, and how my father was turned away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) father, Abdullah, who was humiliated and his mother, Aminah, who was in a difficult situation. The verse highlights the struggles and hardships that the Prophet's parents faced, and how they were tested by God. The verse serves as a reminder that even the closest relatives of the Prophet (peace be upon him) were not spared from the trials and tribulations of life. It also emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, as exemplified by the Prophet's parents.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: And I (Muhammad) was a witness over them as long as I remained among them, but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You were witness over all things.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is referring to his role as a witness over the people of Mecca, who were entrusted to his care. He reminds God that he had fulfilled his duty as a prophet and a witness among them, and now that he has been taken up (either in a spiritual sense or in his night journey to Jerusalem and ascension to heavens), God is the only witness over them. The verse highlights the responsibility of prophethood and the importance of God's witnessing and care over His creation.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And make me blessed wherever I may be, and grant me piety and Taqwa (righteousness) as long as I live.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God to grant the speaker blessings and righteousness throughout their life. The first part of the verse, 'وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت', means 'And make me blessed wherever I may be', indicating that the speaker wants to be blessed in all aspects of their life, no matter where they are or what their circumstances are. The second part of the verse, 'وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا', means 'and grant me piety and Taqwa (righteousness) as long as I live', highlighting the importance of prayer and charity in the life of a believer. The verse emphasizes the desire to live a life that is pleasing to God and to be blessed with His guidance and provision.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And He has subjected to you, as from Him, all that is in the heavens and on earth: behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things in the universe, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'as from Him' suggests that everything is a manifestation of God's will and exists only through His permission. The verse encourages reflection and contemplation on the signs of God's creation, which are evident in the natural world and in the events that occur in life. The verse invites people to reflect on the wonders of creation and to recognize the power and wisdom of God, who is the source of all that exists.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: And peace be upon the day when I was born, and the day when I die, and the day when I shall be raised alive.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) wish for peace on three significant days of his life: his birth, his death, and his resurrection. The verse emphasizes the importance of these events in the Prophet's life and the blessings that came with them. The verse also serves as a reminder to believers to seek peace and blessings in their own lives, especially on significant occasions such as birth and death.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: And indeed, Jesus, the son of Mary, said: 'O children of Israel, I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said: 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus, who is referred to as 'the son of Mary', is quoted as saying that he is a prophet sent by God to confirm the teachings of the Torah and to give news of a future prophet named Ahmad (who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad). However, when Jesus presented clear evidence of his prophethood, the people rejected him and accused him of practicing magic. This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief that often greets divine messengers and the importance of faith in their messages.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: And it is not for Allah to take a son to Himself, when He decrees an affair, He only says to it: 'Be', and it is.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the uniqueness of God's power and authority, highlighting that He does not need to have a son or any form of assistance to carry out His will. The verse also underscores the idea that God's sovereignty is not limited by any external factors or agents, but rather, He alone has the power to decree and bring into existence whatever He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of God's absolute authority and the futility of any attempt to challenge or question His power.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, my Lord is your Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the fact that He is the Lord of all creation, including the speaker and the audience. The verse encourages the audience to worship God and follow the straight path that leads to righteousness and salvation. The use of the word 'straight' (مستقيم) suggests that the path is clear and without deviation, and that it is the only path that leads to the truth and to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the purpose of human existence, which is to worship and obey God, and to follow His commandments as revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And they were divided into groups from among them, woe to those who were rebellious on a Great Day.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, when they will be divided into groups and face the consequences of their disbelief. The phrase 'woe to those who were rebellious' emphasizes the severity of their punishment and the regret they will feel for their disobedience. The phrase 'on a Great Day' refers to the Day of Judgment, which is a day of great significance and importance, when all souls will be judged based on their deeds in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you, but do you not remember?
interpretation: The verse addresses the arrogance and ignorance of the disbelievers, reminding them that they are not the first to be destroyed for their sins. The phrase 'your kind' refers to previous nations that were destroyed for their injustice and disobedience. The verse highlights the fact that the current generation is no better than those who came before them and that they too will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the inevitability of God's punishment.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in a state of heedlessness and do not believe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of warning people about the Day of Judgment, when their deeds will be evaluated, and their fate will be sealed. The verse highlights the fact that people are often heedless and disbelieving, which makes them oblivious to the reality of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to continue warning people of the impending Day of Judgment, even if they may not heed the warning.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind, and what have they availed them?
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that God has destroyed entire nations in the past for their sins and injustices. The phrase 'And indeed, We have destroyed your kind' refers to the destruction of previous nations, while 'and what have they availed them?' emphasizes that their power and wealth were of no use in preventing their downfall. The verse serves as a warning to those living in the present to avoid the same fate by living righteously and following God's commandments.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention in the Book, Abraham, indeed he was a sincere friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's exceptional quality of being a sincere friend to God. The use of the word 'sincere' emphasizes his genuine and unwavering commitment to his relationship with God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to emulate Abraham's example of true friendship with God, which is characterized by sincerity, loyalty, and obedience.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship what does not hear, nor see, nor benefit you in any way?',
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between Prophet Abraham and his father, where Abraham questions his father's practice of worshiping idols. The verse highlights the futility of worshiping objects that are unable to hear, see, or provide any benefit. Abraham's question is a challenge to his father's beliefs and an invitation to reflect on the true nature of worship. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and worshiping only the One True God, who is worthy of worship and can provide true guidance and benefit.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: O my father, indeed knowledge has come to me that has not come to you, so follow me and I will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse is a dialogue between Prophet Abraham and his father, where Abraham is inviting his father to follow him and adopt the righteous path that he has discovered. The verse highlights the importance of knowledge and guidance, and how it is the responsibility of those who have received guidance to share it with others and invite them to follow the righteous path. The verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and respect for one's parents, as Abraham addresses his father with kindness and respect, despite his father's lack of knowledge and understanding.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father, do not worship the devil, for the devil has been rebellious to the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the father-son relationship and the importance of guiding one's children towards righteousness. The father is advised not to worship the devil, which symbolizes evil and rebellion against God's commandments. The verse emphasizes the father's responsibility to teach his children the right path and protect them from the influence of evil. The phrase 'the devil has been rebellious to the Most Merciful' highlights the devil's disobedience to God and his attempts to mislead humans. The verse serves as a reminder to parents to be mindful of their children's spiritual well-being and to raise them with a strong foundation of faith and morality.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that the punishment of the Most Merciful will befall us, so that we will become the companions of the devil.
interpretation: The speaker in this verse is expressing their fear of God's punishment, which they believe will befall them due to their sins. They liken themselves to the companions of the devil, suggesting that they have strayed from the righteous path and are now in danger of facing the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the fear and anxiety that comes with living a life of sin and neglecting one's relationship with God.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: And Abraham said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will be established.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is imploring God to forgive not only himself, but also his parents and the believers on the Day of Judgment. This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the belief in the afterlife. It also emphasizes the significance of family ties and the responsibility to pray for the salvation of one's loved ones. Additionally, the phrase 'the Day when the reckoning will be established' underscores the idea that there will be a day of judgment, when all deeds will be accounted for, and justice will be served.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: And say, 'Peace be upon you, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, indeed, He is the Forgiving.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Abraham's supplication to God, in which he asks for forgiveness for his people. The verse highlights Abraham's compassion and concern for his people, as well as his belief in God's mercy and forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness from God and to intercede for others, as well as to emphasize God's attribute of being the Forgiving.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, Who has sanctified it and to Whom belongs all things. My Lord, grant me that I may not be disappointed in my prayer to You, nor that I may not be prohibited from Your blessings, O Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication made by the Prophet Abraham, peace be upon him, in which he implores God to grant him success in his prayers and to not deprive him of His blessings. The verse highlights the importance of prayer and the belief in the power of God's blessings. It also emphasizes the idea that God is the Lord of the universe and that He is the One who sanctifies and blesses places and people. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to rely on God and to seek His guidance and blessings in all aspects of their lives.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse underscores the compassionate nature of the Prophet's teachings and his role as a guide and a source of hope for humanity. It also highlights the significance of the Prophet's mission in bringing people closer to God and encouraging them to live a virtuous life.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We have given them a tongue that they may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favor upon the believers by giving them the ability to express gratitude through their tongues. The 'tongue' in this context represents the ability to communicate and express one's thoughts and feelings. The verse emphasizes the importance of being grateful to God for His blessings and favors, and encourages believers to use their tongues to praise and glorify God. The use of the word 'لسان' (tongue) is significant, as it implies that the ability to express gratitude is a gift from God, and that it is through this gift that believers can demonstrate their gratitude and obedience to God.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And remember in the Book, Moses, indeed, he was chosen and he was a messenger, a prophet.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of the prophethood and messengership of Moses, who was chosen by God to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. The verse emphasizes Moses' role as a messenger of God, who received divine revelation and conveyed it to the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of prophethood in the history of God's relationship with humanity, and how prophets like Moses have played a crucial role in guiding people towards the right path.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. The verse emphasizes the special status of humanity in creation, indicating that humans are superior to other creatures and have been given a unique role in the universe. The phrase 'We have certainly honored' expresses the idea that this honor is a gift from God, and it is not something that humans can achieve on their own. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with this honor, and encourages humans to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We had given him (Aaron) from Our mercy his brother Harun as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the prophet Aaron, who was the brother of Moses and a prophet in his own right. The verse emphasizes that Aaron was chosen by God as a prophet and was given the responsibility of guiding the Israelites alongside Moses. The use of the phrase 'from Our mercy' highlights the divine nature of Aaron's appointment and emphasizes that his prophethood was a manifestation of God's mercy towards the Israelites. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prophethood and the role that prophets play in guiding humanity towards righteousness and the worship of one God.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And remember in the Book, Ismail, indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger, a prophet.
interpretation: The verse mentions the prophet Ismail (Ishmael) and highlights his integrity and truthfulness. It emphasizes that he was a messenger of God, chosen to convey His message to the people. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being truthful and trustworthy, and how these qualities are essential for those who carry the responsibility of spreading God's message.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And he used to enjoin on his family the prayer and the giving of zakah, and was merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Abraham's practice of enjoining his family to perform the daily prayers and give zakah (charity). The verse highlights his compassion and mercy towards the believers, indicating that he was not only a spiritual leader but also a kind and caring individual. The verse serves as an example for Muslims to follow, emphasizing the importance of leading a virtuous life, caring for one's family, and contributing to the well-being of the community through acts of charity.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And remember in the Book, Idris, he was a man of truth, a prophet.
interpretation: The verse mentions the prophet Idris, who is considered to be a righteous and truthful person. The verse highlights his status as a prophet and a man of God, emphasizing his role in guiding people towards the right path. The mention of Idris in the Qur'an serves as a reminder of the importance of following the teachings of the prophets and living a virtuous life, as well as the significance of truthfulness and integrity in one's faith.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We have raised the high place (of the Ka'bah) to be a sign for the people and a sure guidance from the Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the significance of the Ka'bah, a sacred site in Mecca, and its role as a symbol of guidance for believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Ka'bah as a focal point for Muslims, representing their unity and devotion to God. The verse also highlights God's authority and guidance, as the Ka'bah serves as a physical reminder of God's presence and direction for believers.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah. And had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you, [O Muhammad], seeking forgiveness from Allah, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a mercy to humanity, and the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and the Prophet's intercession on behalf of those who have wronged themselves. The verse highlights the merciful nature of Allah, who is ever ready to accept repentance from those who seek it, and the importance of seeking forgiveness as a means of seeking guidance and redemption.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: And they have forgotten the lesson of the destruction of the communities that came before them, so they became the heirs of the punishment.
interpretation: The verse refers to the tendency of people to forget the lessons of history and the consequences of their actions. The communities that came before them were destroyed because of their sins and injustices, but the current generation has forgotten this lesson and continues to commit the same mistakes. As a result, they will inherit the same punishment that was inflicted upon their predecessors.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, for they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to the destruction of towns that were unjust. The exception is for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds. These individuals will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least, indicating that they will be treated with justice and kindness in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, faith, and good deeds as a means of avoiding God's punishment and attaining a positive outcome in the afterlife.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies that the triumph was evident and indisputable, while 'manifest triumph' emphasizes that the victory was obvious and plain for all to see. The verse highlights the idea that the success achieved by the believers was not due to their own strength or efforts, but rather it was a blessing and favor from God, bestowed upon them due to their faith and righteousness.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: And they will not hear therein ill speech or commission of sin. Only the saying of peace and the averment of truth. And their provision therein is fruit and olives.
interpretation: The verse describes the nature of the inhabitants of Jannah (Paradise) and their surroundings. The people in Jannah will not engage in any negative or sinful speech or actions. Instead, they will only speak words of peace and truth. The verse also mentions the provision of food and drink in Jannah, describing it as fruit and olives, indicating a life of abundance and joy.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights that Muhammad's mission is not to destroy or punish, but rather to spread God's message of love, compassion, and guidance to all people, regardless of their race, religion, or background. The verse also underscores the universality of Muhammad's message and its relevance to all people, regardless of their time or place. The phrase 'worlds' in the verse refers to all creation, including humans, jinn, and other living beings, signifying that Muhammad's message is meant for the benefit of all creation, not just a select few.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, worship Him and be patient in His worship, do you know who He is?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and uniqueness of God, highlighting His power and authority over all creation. The phrase 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them' underscores God's sovereignty over all that exists, including the spiritual and physical realms. The verse also encourages believers to worship God with sincerity and to persevere in their worship, suggesting that true faith requires both devotion and patience. Finally, the rhetorical question 'do you know who He is?' serves as a reminder of the vastness of God's power and knowledge, inviting believers to reflect on the majesty and mystery of the divine.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And the human says, 'When I die, shall I indeed be brought out alive?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and skepticism of humans towards the idea of life after death. The use of the word 'alive' emphasizes the idea that the person will continue to exist in some form after death, which is a concept that many people struggle to comprehend. The verse suggests that humans often fail to understand the true nature of existence and the afterlife, and it serves as a reminder that our current lives are but a brief moment in the grand scheme of things.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: And indeed, mankind was created from a male and a female, and indeed, they will be gathered to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that all human beings are created by God, and that they will all be accountable to Him on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the equal status of men and women in the eyes of God, as both are created from a male and a female. The verse also serves as a reminder of the eventual return to God and the need for individuals to prepare for that day by living righteously.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: So let them be, until they meet their Day in which they will be burned in the Fire, [26] And the wicked sinners will be punished, [27] Who are forbidden from the Mercy of their Lord, [28] And will not believe in Him until they see the painful punishment. [29] Then they will be told, "This is what you used to be skeptical of."
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to live in sin and disbelief. They will be left alone to their own devices until the Day of Judgment, when they will be punished in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, describing it as a burning in the Fire. The phrase "forbidden from the Mercy of their Lord" suggests that they have been given every opportunity to repent and turn to God, but have chosen not to. The final line of the verse, "Then they will be told, 'This is what you used to be skeptical of,'" serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their disbelief will not save them from the punishment.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We have made the particles (of the Qur'an) to be a means of seeking refuge in the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of the Qur'an in providing comfort and refuge to those who seek it. The phrase 'particles of the Qur'an' refers to the individual verses or ayat, which are believed to have a profound impact on the believer's soul. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book of guidance, but also a source of solace and refuge for those who seek it. The phrase 'Most Merciful' refers to God's attribute of mercy and compassion, indicating that the Qur'an is a means of seeking refuge in God's mercy and finding peace in times of distress.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then let us surely exact punishment on those who are guilty.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of punishing those who have committed crimes and are deserving of punishment. The use of the word 'surely' suggests that this punishment is inevitable and will certainly be carried out. The verse serves as a reminder that justice will be served and that those who have committed wrongdoing will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And indeed, there is not a single soul among you but will come to its Lord in a state of utter loss, except him who has been granted mercy by his Lord.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the fact that everyone will ultimately return to God. The verse suggests that without God's mercy, every soul will be in a state of loss and regret on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a righteous life and seeking God's forgiveness in order to avoid the pitfalls of sin and earn a place in paradise.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We destroyed those who were unjust, leaving them as a lesson for the wicked.
interpretation: The verse describes how God destroyed the unjust people, leaving their remnants as a lesson for those who come after them. The verse emphasizes the idea that the destruction of the unjust serves as a warning to others, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and encouraging them to turn to righteousness.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieved say to those who believed, 'Which of the two groups has a better position and a better place of gathering?'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the disbelievers, out of jealousy and arrogance, mock the believers and question their faith. They ask which group, the believers or the disbelievers, has a better position and a better place of gathering. The verse highlights the contrast between the two groups and suggests that the believers are on a higher moral ground, spiritually and socially. The verse also implies that the disbelievers are envious of the believers' faith and their relationship with God.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were better in wealth and in appearance?
interpretation: The verse mentions the destruction of previous generations who were better off in terms of wealth and appearance than the current generation. The verse serves as a reminder that material wealth and outward appearances are not a guarantee of salvation or protection from God's punishment. It also highlights the idea that the current generation should not feel complacent or self-assured, as they too could face a similar fate if they do not turn to God and live righteously.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, 'How many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were better than them in strength and more abundant in wealth and children? Yet they pursued what they were commanded to avoid - the evil of their deeds - until their time was up.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of previous generations who were stronger and wealthier than the current generation, yet they were destroyed because of their disobedience and pursuit of evil deeds. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them that they too will face the consequences of their actions if they do not change their ways and follow the commandments of God.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah will bless those who were guided, the righteous offspring, good in the sight of their Lord, and good in their inheritance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that await those who are guided by God and live righteously. The phrase 'good in the sight of their Lord' suggests that their good deeds are not only beneficial for themselves but also pleasing to God. The verse also highlights the importance of leaving a righteous legacy for future generations, as the phrase 'good in their inheritance' implies that the good deeds of the parents will have a positive impact on their offspring. The verse serves as a reminder that living a righteous life and leaving a positive impact on future generations is a key aspect of Islam and will be rewarded by God.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Have you seen the one who has disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will be given wealth and children'?
interpretation: The verse addresses the issue of disbelief and the consequences that come with it. The phrase 'our verses' refers to the Qur'anic revelations sent by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse questions the attitude of those who reject these revelations and instead, seek wealth and children as a sign of success and happiness. The verse implies that true happiness and success come from following God's commandments and living according to His will, not from material possessions or worldly desires.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which was not limited to a specific group or community, but rather extended to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message was intended for all people, past, present, and future, and that his teachings were meant to bring people together and promote peace, love, and understanding among them. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's important role in promoting compassion, forgiveness, and kindness, and encourages believers to follow his example in their interactions with others.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be helped.
interpretation: The verse refers to the practice of polytheism, where people have taken gods besides Allah, hoping to receive help and support from them. The verse suggests that this practice is futile, as only Allah has the power to help and support. The verse serves as a reminder that true help and support come from Allah alone, and that relying on other sources of power is futile and a form of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: And they will be veiled from the mercy of Allah as they were veiled from the truth. So they will not be able to see it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have turned away from the truth and have rejected the mercy of Allah. They are so engrossed in their own desires and false beliefs that they are unable to see the truth and are veiled from the mercy of Allah. The verse suggests that those who reject the truth and persist in their disbelief will be deprived of Allah's mercy and will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: And indeed, We will enable them to taste torment good and plenty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment that will be inflicted upon the disbelievers. The phrase 'good and plenty' refers to the severity and duration of the punishment. The verse indicates that the punishment will be so intense that it will be perceived as enjoyable, signifying that the punishment will be proportionate to the severity of their disbelief and evil deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: On the Day when the believers will rejoice in the victory of their Lord, and the disbelievers will be filled with regret and despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when the believers will be triumphant and the disbelievers will be filled with remorse. The believers will rejoice in their faith and the blessings they received from God, while the disbelievers will regret their rejection of God's message and their disobedience. The verse highlights the contrast between the two groups and emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience to God.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will extract the criminal sinners on the Day of Resurrection, in groups, tied up in chains, their heads shaved off, and their hearts removed.,
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of sinners on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase 'We will extract' implies a forceful and violent removal of the sinners from their graves, emphasizing the severity of their punishment. The phrase 'tied up in chains' suggests a sense of restriction and confinement, while 'their heads shaved off' and 'their hearts removed' serve as graphic descriptions of the physical and spiritual destruction that awaits the sinners. The verse serves as a warning to those living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: They have no intercessor beside Allah, but He accepts whoever approaches Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no one can intercede on behalf of those who have earned God's punishment. It highlights God's sovereignty and the idea that only He can forgive sins and accept those who turn to Him in repentance. The verse also underscores the importance of personal responsibility and the need for individuals to seek God's forgiveness directly, rather than relying on intermediaries or hoping for intercession from others. Ultimately, the verse reminds us that God is the sole source of guidance and forgiveness, and that we must turn to Him alone in order to receive His mercy and grace.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the belief of some polytheists in Arabia during the time of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who claimed that the Most Merciful (a name of God) had taken a son. This belief was a result of their misunderstanding of the concept of prophethood and the relationship between God and His prophets. The verse rejects this belief, emphasizing that God is far removed from having a son or any other form of offspring. The verse highlights the uniqueness of God's nature and refutes any notion that He could have a son or equal.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you did not know.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) opponents, reminding them that God has destroyed similar communities in the past for their wrongdoing. The phrase 'your kind' refers to the disbelievers and wrongdoers, emphasizing that they are not new in their actions. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to a particular nation or time period. The phrase 'but you did not know' suggests that the people of Mecca were unaware of their ancestors' history and the consequences of their actions, indicating that they should learn from the past and avoid repeating the same mistakes.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heaven and the earth are about to burst forth with joy, and the mountains are about to break apart in delight.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of great joy and celebration, where even the inanimate objects like the heavens, earth, and mountains are personified as if they are rejoicing and bursting with happiness. The use of the verb 'to burst' (tfra) emphasizes the intensity of the joy, suggesting that the objects are unable to contain their excitement. The verse may be interpreted as a metaphor for the joy and happiness that one experiences when they are close to God or when they are experiencing spiritual ecstasy. It could also be seen as a description of the end of the world, when the heavens and earth will be renewed and the mountains will crumble, indicating a time of transformation and renewal.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: And call upon your Lord with humility and in private, indeed He does not love transgressors.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and privacy in prayer. It suggests that one should call upon Allah with humility, recognizing one's weaknesses and limitations, and in private, away from the public eye. The verse also highlights Allah's dislike for those who transgress and commit injustices, indicating that true worship requires a deep sense of humility and a commitment to righteousness.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: And not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of the Garden.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the contrast between the fate of those who are destined for hellfire and those who are destined for paradise. The phrase 'not equal' highlights the vast difference between the two groups, indicating that they are not comparable. The verse serves as a reminder that the choices we make in life will determine our ultimate destination, and that those who choose to live a life of righteousness will be rewarded, while those who choose to live a life of sin will be punished.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: Indeed, all who are in the heavens and the earth belong to the Most Merciful (God) as His slaves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of creation and the fact that all beings in the heavens and the earth, including humans, are servants of the Most Merciful (God). It highlights the idea that everything in existence belongs to God and is subject to His will, and that humans must recognize and acknowledge this reality. The verse also underscores the idea of the oneness of God and the interconnectedness of all creation, and serves as a reminder of the responsibility of humans to live in accordance with God's will.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation after Noah.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of communities after the time of Prophet Noah. The use of 'generation' (عدا) instead of 'people' (قوم) emphasizes that these communities were not just punished for their sins, but were completely wiped out, leaving no descendants. This verse serves as a reminder of God's power and justice, and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And all of them will be brought before God on the Day of Resurrection, [as] feeble.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that all human beings will be judged by God on the Day of Resurrection, regardless of their social status, wealth, or power. The description of them being 'feeble' highlights their vulnerability and helplessness before God's judgment. It serves as a reminder that no one is above God's law and that everyone will be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Garden of Pleasure.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward for those who have faith and do good deeds. The phrase 'their Lord will guide them because of their faith' implies that God will personally guide and protect them, ensuring their safe passage to Paradise. The image of rivers flowing beneath them in the Garden of Pleasure is a vivid description of the beauty and tranquility that awaits the righteous in the afterlife. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to live a virtuous life and have faith in God's guidance and reward.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: And indeed, We have sent it down in a Clear Qur'an, so that they may be reminded, and that it may warn them, and that they may avoid (sin) and be mindful of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the Qur'an, which is meant to serve as a reminder and warning to those who are willing to listen. The verse highlights the dual purpose of the Qur'an: to remind the believers and to warn the disobedient. The use of the word ' Clear' (mubin) emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of the Qur'anic message, making it accessible to all people, regardless of their background or intellect. The verse also underscores the importance of heeding the warning contained in the Qur'an, as a means of avoiding sin and being mindful of one's relationship with God.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them, who were more powerful than they in strength and cultivation?
interpretation: The verse highlights the idea that the destruction of past generations serves as a warning to the present generation. The use of the word 'qarn' (generation) emphasizes the idea that the people of the past were not just individuals, but entire communities that were wiped out by God's punishment. The phrase 'more powerful than they in strength and cultivation' suggests that the people of the past were not just physically strong, but also had advanced civilizations and technologies. The verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or advanced a civilization may be, it is still subject to God's judgment and wrath if it does not follow His commandments.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: طه

translation: And indeed, We have sent the Qur'an down to you that you may clarify to them what has been revealed to them, and so that they may reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an's revelation, which is to provide clarity and guidance to the people. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role in helping people understand and reflect on the messages and signs contained within it. The verse also underscores the importance of the Prophet's duty to convey the message of the Qur'an to the people, as well as the responsibility of the people to reflect on and understand the message.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation after Noah.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God has destroyed many generations in the past, specifically mentioning those who lived after the time of Prophet Noah. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to a particular nation or time period, and that He is aware of the deeds of all people. It also emphasizes the idea that the destruction of these generations was not because of their sins alone, but also because they refused to believe in the warnings and signs sent by God's messengers. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of heeding God's message.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except to all the people as a witness, and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of the Prophet Muhammad's message, which is addressed to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The Prophet is described as a witness, bearing witness to the truth of God's Oneness and the accountability of all human beings before Him. He is also a bringer of good news, announcing the glad tidings of God's mercy and forgiveness to those who repent and turn to Him. Additionally, he is a warner, warning those who reject God's message of the severe consequences they will face in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Merciful [God] rose above the Throne.
interpretation: This verse describes the exalted status of God, the Most Merciful, who is above all creation and sits on the Throne, a symbol of His power and authority. The verse emphasizes God's greatness and majesty, and serves as a reminder of His transcendence and unity.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: And whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and control over all aspects of creation, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, such as the atmosphere, and everything beneath the soil, such as minerals and underground water. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the interconnectedness of all things, and encourages the reader to reflect on the beauty and complexity of creation and to recognize the power and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and fruits. However, the verse also reassures the believers that if they remain patient and steadfast during these trials, they will receive good tidings and ultimately triumph over their challenges. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is tested during difficult times, and that patience and perseverance are essential qualities for any believer.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah, there is no god but He, the Most Beautiful Names belong to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and uniqueness of God, affirming that there is no other deity worthy of worship except Allah. The phrase 'the Most Beautiful Names belong to Him' highlights the majesty and glory of God, indicating that He is the owner of all attributes of perfection and beauty. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus their devotion solely on Allah and to avoid associating partners with Him in worship.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: And when he saw the fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here, for I have perceived a fire, perhaps I may bring you a burning brand from it or find guidance at the fire.'
interpretation: Musa's encounter with the fire is significant as it represents a turning point in his life. The fire symbolizes both physical and spiritual enlightenment. The verse highlights Moses' curiosity and determination to investigate the source of the fire, which ultimately leads him to the discovery of God's message. The phrase 'perhaps I may bring you a burning brand from it' suggests that Moses was not sure what he would find, but he was willing to take a risk and investigate. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance, even in the face of uncertainty.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: Moses was instructed by God to remove his sandals before entering the sacred valley of Tuwa, indicating a state of spiritual purity and humility before God. The removal of shoes symbolizes the shedding of worldly attachments and a readiness to approach the divine with humility and reverence. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and submission to God's will, and the need to purify oneself before encountering the divine.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And indeed, I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and emphasizing the importance of listening to the revelations that are being sent to him. The verse highlights the special relationship between God and the Prophet, and the responsibility that comes with being chosen by God. The verse also serves as a reminder to all believers to listen to and follow the teachings of the Qur'an, which are a source of guidance and wisdom for all humanity.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah, there is no god except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of worshiping only Him. The use of the phrase 'there is no god except Me' reinforces the idea that God is unique and peerless, and that He alone is worthy of worship. The phrase 'so worship Me' indicates that worship is a way of acknowledging and expressing one's belief in God's oneness. The phrase 'and establish prayer for My remembrance' highlights the importance of prayer as a means of remembering and glorifying God. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the only one worthy of worship and that prayer is a fundamental aspect of a believer's relationship with God.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the coming of the Day of Judgment, which is described as an hour that is almost concealed, indicating its sudden and unexpected arrival. The verse emphasizes that every soul will be recompensed for its deeds, good or bad, and that no one will escape God's judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their spiritual responsibilities and a reminder to those who are righteous, that their deeds will not go unrewarded.

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so be content with your Lord's decree and be patient. Indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans are limited in their understanding and knowledge. They are unable to comprehend all of God's secrets and plans. Therefore, they should be content with what has been revealed to them and not question God's wisdom. The verse also encourages patience and resignation to God's decree, as humans are not capable of understanding the full extent of God's plan. The verse serves as a reminder to trust in God's wisdom and justice, even when things may seem difficult or unfair.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

It also emphasizes the consequences of spreading falsehood and the importance of fearing God's punishment in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: And they dispute among themselves about their affair, but they (the disbelievers) are in doubt about their religion, so they are being hasty.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of confusion and disagreement among the disbelievers regarding their religion. They are uncertain and divided about their beliefs and are hasty in their actions, which indicates a lack of conviction and faith. The verse highlights the contrast between the believers, who are steadfast and united in their beliefs, and the disbelievers, who are uncertain and divided.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said, 'These two are magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your exemplary way of life.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Moses and Aaron when they came to Egypt to confront the Pharaoh. The disbelievers saw the miracles performed by Moses and Aaron as magic and accused them of trying to drive them out of their land and destroy their way of life. The verse highlights the theme of opposition and resistance to the message of the prophets, and how the disbelievers often resort to accusing the prophets of using magic or trickery to deceive people. The verse also underscores the importance of standing firm in one's beliefs and not allowing the opinions of others to sway one's convictions.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: So gather your hands and then come [at once] to a place of safety and success has been achieved today for whoever has risen [in obedience]
interpretation: The verse is an encouragement to the believers to gather their strength and unite in their efforts to achieve success. The phrase 'a place of safety' refers to a place of spiritual safety, where one can feel secure and protected from the negative influences of the world. The verse emphasizes the importance of taking immediate action and not delaying one's obedience to God's command. The phrase 'has been achieved today' indicates that success is within reach for those who rise to the challenge and obey God's command. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to strive for success in their spiritual journey and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw first or we will be the first to throw down our staffs.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Moses was confronted by the magicians of Pharaoh, who challenged him to a showdown. The magicians, confident in their abilities, suggested that either Moses should throw his staff first or they would be the first to throw down their staffs. This verse highlights the arrogance and confidence of the magicians, who were unaware of Moses' divine mission and the power of God. It also underscores the importance of faith and trust in God's plan, as Moses, despite being faced with a seemingly impossible challenge, remained steadfast in his belief and ultimately emerged victorious.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, why have you afflicted us with this punishment?', while they are the ones who have been wicked.
interpretation: In this verse, the people who have been destroyed by God's punishment are complaining and asking why they were afflicted with such punishment. However, the verse reveals that they are the ones who have been wicked and deserve the punishment. The verse highlights the idea that people often blame God for their suffering, but they fail to recognize their own wrongdoing and the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the punishment from God is a result of humanity's disobedience and wickedness.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: And Moses was inwardly troubled by his brother's crying, and he said: 'How can I bear this burden alone?',
interpretation: The verse describes Moses' emotional state as he struggles to cope with the responsibility of leading the Israelites and dealing with his brother Aaron's criticism. Moses feels overwhelmed and unsure of how to handle the situation. The verse highlights Moses' human side and his vulnerability, as well as his deep sense of responsibility and concern for his people. It also underscores the challenges of leadership and the emotional toll it can take on those in positions of authority.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims over their enemies. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies a decisive and unambiguous triumph, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is evident and obvious to all. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and continue to strive for righteousness.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And what is in your right hand, O Musa?
interpretation: The verse is a question posed by God to Prophet Moses, asking him what he has in his right hand. The verse is often interpreted as a reminder that God's power and support are always with His prophets, and that they should have faith in God's ability to help them, even in the face of adversity. The phrase 'what is in your right hand' is seen as a metaphor for the power and authority that God has given to His prophets, and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: And Moses threw down his staff and it was a serpent, and he fled from it. And he looked back and saw that it had become a snake, and he was amazed.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is commanded by God to throw down his staff, which transforms into a serpent. Moses is initially frightened and runs away, but when he looks back, he sees that the staff has transformed back into a snake. This miraculous event serves as a sign of God's power and Moses' faith in God is reaffirmed. The verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in God, even in the face of seemingly impossible situations.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you; do you not take heed?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers, reminding them that God has destroyed previous nations who were similar to them in their disbelief and disobedience. The verse implies that the disbelievers should take heed of the lessons from history and not repeat the mistakes of the past. The verse also emphasizes the severity of God's punishment, suggesting that it is not limited to physical destruction, but also extends to spiritual destruction, as indicated by the phrase 'We will cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides.' The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, 'We will not be affected by the warnings that have come to us from the prophets, and we will not be punished for our sins.' But they have lied to themselves, and their sins have been adorned to them, so they will be punished in this life and the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who reject the warnings of the prophets and refuse to believe in the consequences of their sins. They have deluded themselves into thinking that they will not be held accountable for their actions, and they have made their sins appear beautiful to themselves. However, their denial and self-deception will not save them from the punishment that they have earned. They will face the consequences of their actions in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, We have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what we used to attribute to Him [in falsehood].
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief in God's forgiveness and the recognition that past mistakes and misdeeds can be forgiven through repentance and faith in God. The verse also highlights the importance of recognizing and rejecting false beliefs and attributions that were previously associated with God. The use of the word 'sins' (خطايانا) plural form, indicates that the verse is referring to both small and great sins. The phrase 'what we used to attribute to Him [in falsehood]' refers to the incorrect beliefs and ideas that people may have had about God, and the recognition that these were misguided and false. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith in God involves recognizing and rejecting false beliefs and seeking forgiveness for past mistakes, in order to establish a strong and genuine relationship with God.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, he who comes to his Lord as a criminal will have Hell, where he will neither die nor live.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment for those who lead a life of sin and disobedience to God. The criminal referred to in the verse is one who has consistently rejected God's commands and has lived a life of disobedience. The verse warns that such a person will be punished in Hell, where they will not die, indicating that the punishment is eternal, and they will not be able to escape it. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - they will have the highest ranks,
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and good deeds as the key to attaining high ranks in the hereafter. The phrase 'مؤمنا' (mu'min) refers to those who have faith in Allah and 'عمل الصالحات' (did righteous deeds) signifies those who have acted upon their faith. The verse emphasizes that these individuals will be rewarded with the highest ranks in paradise, indicating that faith and good deeds are the criteria for attaining a high status in the afterlife.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
