The verse assures that God will not fail in His promise and that His punishment will come suddenly and unexpectedly, just as a day with God is like a thousand years for those who are being punished. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's power and reminds them that God's punishment is always near and certain.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكأين من قرية أمليت لها وهي ظالمة ثم أخذتها وإلي المصير

translation: Say, O mankind, indeed I am to you a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a clear warner to the people, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of the Hereafter. The use of the word 'O mankind' addresses all people, regardless of their background or beliefs, and stresses the universal nature of the message. The verse serves as a call to reflection and a reminder of the purpose of the Prophet's mission, which is to guide people towards the truth and the right path.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إنما أنا لكم نذير مبين

translation: And (as for) those who believe and do good deeds, for them are forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who lead a righteous life, believing in God and performing good deeds. The phrase 'forgiveness' refers to the pardoning of their sins, while 'noble provision' refers to the sustenance and blessings they will receive in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the idea that living a virtuous life has both spiritual and material benefits, and serves as an incentive for people to adopt a righteous lifestyle.
orig: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who seek to discredit Our signs, it is they who will be brought to destruction.
interpretation: This verse warns those who try to discredit or deny the signs and revelations sent by God. The verse indicates that those who reject God's signs will be the ones who will ultimately be destroyed. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and misguided beliefs. It emphasizes the idea that rejecting God's signs will lead to destruction and that it is only through submission to God's will that one can find true guidance and salvation.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And We have not sent before you any messenger or prophet except that Satan throws into his dreams when he is sleeping a falsehood, but Allah erases it, and Allah establishes His verses, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse explains how Satan tries to deceive people by planting false ideas in their minds, especially when they are asleep and most vulnerable. However, God protects His messengers and prophets by erasing those falsehoods and ensuring that His true message is revealed to them. The verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in protecting His message and guiding His messengers, and serves as a reminder to believers to be vigilant against Satan's tricks and to seek guidance from God alone.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقى الشيطان في أمنيته فينسخ الله ما يلقي الشيطان ثم يحكم الله آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And let not the devil hinder you. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to let the devil hinder them in their faith and actions. The devil is described as a clear enemy who seeks to mislead and lead astray those who are weak in their faith. The verse serves as a reminder to be vigilant and mindful of the devil's schemes and to seek protection and guidance from God to avoid falling into his traps.
orig: ليجعل ما يلقي الشيطان فتنة للذين في قلوبهم مرض والقاسية قلوبهم وإن الظالمين لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: And indeed, those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, so they believe in it, and their hearts are humbled. And indeed, Allah will guide those who have believed to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the response of those who have been given knowledge, that is, the believers, to the revelation received by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They recognize the truth in the revelation and believe in it, and their faith humbles their hearts. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its impact on the believers' hearts, leading them to submission to God and His guidance. The verse also underscores God's guidance of the believers, directing them to a straight path, which is the path of righteousness and obedience to God.
orig: وليعلم الذين أوتوا العلم أنه الحق من ربك فيؤمنوا به فتخبت له قلوبهم وإن الله لهاد الذين آمنوا إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And those who disbelieve are in a state of confusion and madness until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of disbelievers who are unaware of the impending punishment that awaits them. The verse suggests that they are in a state of confusion and madness, unable to see the reality of their situation. The verse also emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment that will befall them, likening it to the sudden arrival of the Hour or the punishment of a barren day. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولا يزال الذين كفروا في مرية منه حتى تأتيهم الساعة بغتة أو يأتيهم عذاب يوم عقيم

translation: And the kingdom on that day shall be for Allah, the One, the Dominant. He will judge between them, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: The verse describes a future scene where God's kingdom will be established and He will be the sole authority, judging between all people. The believers who lived righteously will be rewarded with gardens of pleasure, indicating a state of happiness and bliss in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and good deeds as the criteria for judgment and the reward of paradise.
orig: الملك يومئذ لله يحكم بينهم فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في جنات النعيم

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, their punishment will be humiliating.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the truth. The verse warns that they will face a humiliating punishment, indicating that their disbelief and denial will lead to a state of shame and disgrace. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا فأولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and then were killed or died, Allah will provide them with a good provision. Indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the reward of those who migrated for the sake of Allah and sacrificed their lives for His cause. The verse assures them that Allah will provide them with a good provision in the afterlife, indicating that their sacrifice will not go unrewarded. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is the best of providers' emphasizes Allah's ability and willingness to provide for those who are devoted to Him, and serves as a reminder that true provision comes from Allah alone.
orig: والذين هاجروا في سبيل الله ثم قتلوا أو ماتوا ليرزقنهم الله رزقا حسنا وإن الله لهو خير الرازقين

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that people may face in life, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and loved ones. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and resilience in the face of these challenges, and assures believers that they will be rewarded for their perseverance. The verse also highlights the wisdom and knowledge of God, who is aware of all things and has a plan for humanity's spiritual growth and development.
orig: ليدخلنهم مدخلا يرضونه وإن الله لعليم حليم

translation: And certainly, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse mentions that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these trials, and assures the believers that they will receive good tidings if they remain steadfast in their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that the tests and tribulations of life are a means for spiritual growth and purification, and that true faith is revealed in times of hardship.
orig: ذلك ومن عاقب بمثل ما عوقب به ثم بغي عليه لينصرنه الله إن الله لعفو غفور

translation: And Allah causes the night to enter the day, and causes the day to enter the night, and Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's control over the cycle of day and night, and how He is constantly observing and aware of all that occurs within His creation. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is always watching and listening, and that nothing escapes His knowledge or attention. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to live their lives in accordance with Allah's will, as they are always being observed by Him.
orig: ذلك بأن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وأن الله سميع بصير

translation: And that Allah is the Truth and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and that Allah is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the falsehood of all other deities that people may worship. The verse declares that Allah is the only truth and that all other gods are false and inferior. Additionally, the verse highlights the supremacy of Allah, describing Him as the Most High and the Great, indicating His power, wisdom, and majesty. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus their worship on Allah alone and to reject all other false deities.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه هو الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: And have you seen the rain that comes from the sky and makes the earth alive again? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: The verse highlights the miracle of rain, which comes from the sky and revives the dead earth, symbolizing the power and mercy of Allah. The use of the word 'subtle' (latif) to describe Allah emphasizes His ability to work in subtle ways, beyond human comprehension. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's constant care and attention to His creation, and encourages believers to appreciate and respect the delicate balance of nature.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: For Him is what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's ownership and sovereignty over all of creation, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'For Him is what is in the heavens and what is on the earth' underscores God's supremacy and control over all things. The second part of the verse, 'and indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy' highlights God's self-sufficiency and lack of need for anything or anyone else. The phrase 'the Praiseworthy' emphasizes God's worthiness of praise and highlights His infinite greatness and majesty.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن الله لهو الغني الحميد

translation: And have you seen that Allah has subjected to you, [as a blessing], what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and has completed His favor upon you, both apparent and hidden? And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, encompassing all aspects of life, from the heavens to the earth, and including both visible and hidden favors. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate and recognize the magnitude of Allah's blessings in our lives, and to be mindful of the fact that Allah is aware of all our actions and deeds.
orig: ألم تر أن الله سخر لكم ما في الأرض والفلك تجري في البحر بأمره ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His knowledge of all human actions. It suggests that God is always with us, watching over us, and aware of everything we do. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions are not hidden from God, and that we will be held accountable for them. It encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive to live a righteous life, as they are constantly being watched and judged by God.
orig: وهو الذي أحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم إن الإنسان لكفور

translation: For every nation, We have made their indulgence seem fair, but they are in disagreement. Now call upon your Lord, and follow the straight path. Indeed, you are on a clear guidance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God has made it easy for every nation to follow their own path, but they are still in disagreement. The verse encourages the believers to call upon their Lord and follow the straight path, which is the guidance that God has provided. The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's guidance and not being swayed by personal desires or opinions.
orig: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه فلا ينازعنك في الأمر وادع إلى ربك إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم

translation: And indeed, We will suffice you against the scoffers,
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reassuring him that He will be sufficient for him against the mockers and disbelievers. The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to protect and support the believers, and serves as a reminder that ultimately, God is the One who will judge and punish the wicked. The verse also highlights the importance of ignoring the mockery and ridicule of those who reject the message of Islam and instead, focusing on spreading the message of God's oneness and righteousness.
orig: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

translation: And Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that on the Day of Resurrection, God will be the ultimate judge between people regarding their differences and disputes. It highlights the idea that people will be held accountable for their actions and beliefs, and that God's judgment will be the final and absolute truth. The verse serves as a reminder to people to be mindful of their actions and beliefs, and to strive for unity and understanding, rather than division and conflict.
orig: الله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And indeed, Allah knows what is in the heavens and on the earth. Indeed, it is all in a Clear Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and the idea that everything in the universe, including human deeds and destinies, is recorded in a divine book. The verse suggests that God's knowledge encompasses all things, including what is hidden and what is manifest, and that nothing escapes His attention. The phrase 'Clear Book' may refer to the Preserved Tablet, an Islamic concept of a heavenly book that contains the knowledge of all things past, present, and future. The verse serves as a reminder of God's all-encompassing knowledge and the idea that human actions have consequences, and that everything is accounted for in the eyes of God.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم ما في السماء والأرض إن ذلك في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which does not harm them, and they believe not in the Hereafter, and they have no proof of what they follow. And they are not guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshiping anything other than Allah, as it does not bring any harm or benefit to the worshipers. It also emphasizes the lack of evidence or proof for their beliefs, and how they are not guided towards the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance and wisdom come from Allah alone, and that following anything else is futile and misguided.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وما ليس لهم به علم وما للظالمين من نصير

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, 'This is nothing but a man who wishes to turn you away from what your fathers were worshiping.' And they say, 'This Qur'an is nothing but a fabrication.' Those who disbelieve say, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and do not let it be recited to you. Perhaps you will be influenced by it and become like them.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they hear the Qur'an being recited. They dismiss the Qur'an as a fabrication and try to dissuade others from listening to it, fearing that it may have an influence on them. The verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth and instead try to turn others away from it. It serves as a warning to those who are resistant to the message of the Qur'an, reminding them that their denial will lead to their own destruction.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات تعرف في وجوه الذين كفروا المنكر يكادون يسطون بالذين يتلون عليهم آياتنا قل أفأنبئكم بشر من ذلكم النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا وبئس المصير

translation: O mankind, listen to this parable. Those you call upon besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they all gather together to do so. And if the fly were to take something from them, they would not be able to retrieve it from him. Weak is the seeker, and powerless is the sought.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of a fly to illustrate the powerlessness of those who are sought (the idols) and the weakness of those who seek them. The fly, though small and insignificant, is able to take something from the idols, symbolizing the futility of their power. The verse emphasizes that those who put their faith in idols are weak and powerless, while Allah is the only one who can truly help and assist.
orig: يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له إن الذين تدعون من دون الله لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا لا يستنقذوه منه ضعف الطالب والمطلوب

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with the true appraisal, indeed Allah is powerful and exalted in might.
interpretation: The verse highlights the failure of people to recognize and appreciate the true power and greatness of Allah. The phrase 'they did not appraise Allah with the true appraisal' implies that people have underestimated Allah's abilities and attributes, and have not given Him the recognition He truly deserves. The second part of the verse emphasizes Allah's power and exalted status, indicating that He is capable of achieving anything and is above all weaknesses or limitations. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to have a proper understanding of Allah's majesty and to never underestimate His power and abilities.
orig: ما قدروا الله حق قدره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Allah chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and power to choose whomever He wills as His messengers, whether from the angels or from humanity. The verse highlights Allah's ability to see and hear all things, indicating that nothing escapes His knowledge and attention. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is always watching and aware of their actions, and that they will be held accountable for their deeds. It also serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's message, as they will be held accountable for their disbelief and disobedience.
orig: الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا ومن الناس إن الله سميع بصير

translation: And indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare, and We are greater than what they know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and power over all things, including the secrets and hidden thoughts of human beings. The verse suggests that humans may think they can hide their thoughts and actions from God, but in reality, God is fully aware of everything, including what they conceal and what they reveal. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and the fact that ultimately, all matters will be returned to Him for judgment.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who have believed, bow down and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good - that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of worship and obedience to God as the key to success in this life and the hereafter. The verse addresses the believers, encouraging them to humble themselves before God through bowing and prostration, and to dedicate their lives to doing good deeds. The verse links the act of worship with the attainment of success, suggesting that true success is not limited to worldly achievements, but rather it is the result of a deep spiritual connection with God and adherence to His commandments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اركعوا واسجدوا واعبدوا ربكم وافعلوا الخير لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And strive in the way of Allah with a striving that is due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. It is the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you Muslims before and in this [Qur'an] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Indeed, Allah is your Patron and He is the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the way of Allah and adhering to the religion of Islam, which was also followed by Prophet Abraham. Muslims are encouraged to be witnesses to the people and to establish prayer and give zakah. The verse also highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness over the believers and the believers as witnesses over the people. The verse concludes by emphasizing the power and wisdom of Allah, who is the ultimate authority and guide for Muslims.
orig: وجاهدوا في الله حق جهاده هو اجتباكم وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ملة أبيكم إبراهيم هو سماكم المسلمين من قبل وفي هذا ليكون الرسول شهيدا عليكم وتكونوا شهداء على الناس فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واعتصموا بالله هو مولاكم فنعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: And indeed, the believers have succeeded.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the ultimate success of the believers in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that the believers have been granted success in their faith and that their efforts in this life will be rewarded in the afterlife. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for believers to continue on the path of righteousness and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: قد أفلح المؤمنون

translation: And those who are in their prayer are in a state of humility and submission.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of humility and submission that believers should exhibit in their prayer. The Arabic word 'khāshiʿūn' means 'humbled, submissive', and describes those who are fully aware of their weaknesses and limitations before God. This verse emphasizes the importance of humility in prayer, indicating that those who are truly devoted to God will exhibit this quality in their worship. It serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate humility and submission in their spiritual practices, recognizing their dependence on God and their need for His guidance and forgiveness.
orig: الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

translation: And those who are neglectful of their prayer
interpretation: The verse refers to those who are negligent in performing their daily prayers, which is a fundamental obligation for Muslims. The verse implies that neglecting prayer is a sign of a lack of faith and a indication of a person's distance from God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize their spiritual obligations and to remain mindful of their relationship with God.
orig: والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون

translation: And those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of wealth, so they do not give it to the way of Allah, except a little.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who are stingy with the wealth that Allah has given them, and do not spend it in the way of Allah, except a little. The verse implies that those who are miserly with their wealth are not using it to help others or to support good causes, and are instead hoarding it for themselves. The verse serves as a warning to those who are stingy with their wealth, reminding them that true wealth is not measured by how much one has, but by how much one gives to others and to good causes.
orig: والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون

translation: And those who are patient, seeking their Lord's Countenance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of patience and its significance in seeking God's pleasure. The phrase 'li-furoojahum' (for their Lord's Countenance) suggests that the believers' ultimate goal is to attain God's satisfaction and approval, and that they are willing to endure hardships and difficulties with patience and perseverance in order to achieve this goal. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the spiritual journey and the rewards that come with it.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except upon the wives of the prophet, for they are not lawful for anyone to marry after you, nor can they be lawful for their husbands after you
interpretation: N
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: And those who have sought absolution after that will be the losers.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who, after having been warned and admonished, still refuse to repent and continue to live in disobedience to God's commands. The verse warns that such people will be the ultimate losers in the Hereafter, facing God's punishment and wrath. The verse serves as a reminder that seeking forgiveness and turning back to God is essential for a person's spiritual well-being and salvation.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are maintained by their Lord, and their pledge is with Him.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have a close relationship with God and are faithful to their covenant with Him. The phrase 'maintained by their Lord' suggests that they are under God's protection and care, and the phrase 'their pledge is with Him' implies that they have made a commitment to follow God's commandments and live according to His will. The verse highlights the idea that those who are faithful to God and follow His commandments will be rewarded and protected by Him.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who are maintained by their Lord, they are the ones who are kept on their prayer.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between spiritual discipline and divine sustenance. The phrase ' maintained by their Lord' implies that those who are faithful and committed to their prayer are also provided for and cared for by God. The verse suggests that the act of prayer is not just a means of communication with God but also a means of purifying oneself and seeking guidance. The phrase 'kept on their prayer' emphasizes the importance of consistent and regular prayer, indicating that those who prioritize their spiritual practice are the ones who are truly sustained and cared for by God.
orig: والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولئك هم الوارثون

translation: And they will be given to drink a cup whose mixture is of ginger, a foul and loathsome drink.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The 'ginger' in the cup symbolizes the bitter consequences of their actions, and the 'foul and loathsome' nature of the drink represents the unpleasant and distressing experience that awaits them. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind from clay, from mire,
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble origins of humanity, created from a lowly substance such as clay, and the process of shaping and molding that clay to form a human being. The use of the word 'mire' emphasizes the idea that humanity's origins are not glorious or noble, but rather humble and earthy. This verse serves as a reminder of humanity's dependence on God and the fragility of human life.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

translation: Then We made it a punishment for those who successively inherited the Book, that they would disbelieve in it, and they will have a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disbelief and the punishment that awaits those who reject the message of God. The phrase 'successively inherited the Book' refers to the fact that the message of God has been passed down through generations, and those who reject it are held accountable for their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message, serving as a warning to those who are skeptical or indifferent to the message of Islam.
orig: ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

translation: Then We created the drop of sperm, then We created the clot, then We created the little lump, then We created the bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh, and then We brought forth another creation. Blessed be Allah, the Best of creators.
interpretation: This verse describes the various stages of fetal development, emphasizing the miraculous nature of God's creation. The verse begins with the smallest unit of life, the sperm, and then describes the progression to the clot, the little lump, and finally the fully formed bones clothed with flesh. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom in creating life, and the phrase 'Blessed be Allah, the Best of creators' underscores the idea that God's creation is perfect and unparalleled.
orig: ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين

translation: Then indeed, after their punishment, your Lord will never leave them in the state they are in, until they become a people who are obedient to Allah, the One, the Dominant.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's mercy and grace, as He does not leave the people in their state of punishment forever. Instead, He allows them to return to a state of obedience and submission to Him, indicating a chance for redemption and forgiveness. The verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to God's will and living according to His commandments, and serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not eternal, but rather a means to guide people towards righteousness.
orig: ثم إنكم بعد ذلك لميتون

translation: Then indeed, you will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the resurrection of all human beings. It serves as a reminder that the present life is not the end, and that there will be a day of reckoning when all individuals will be held accountable for their actions. The verse also implies that the resurrection will be a time of great transformation, when the current order of things will be turned upside down and the righteous will be rewarded and the wicked will be punished.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة تبعثون

translation: And indeed, We have created above you seven paths, and We have not been neglectful of the creation.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the seven heavens and the fact that God has not neglected or forgotten about His creation. The seven paths refer to the seven heavens, which are mentioned in several places in the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over the universe and serves as a reminder to humans of their place in the grand scheme of things. It also highlights the idea that God is aware of all that occurs in the universe and is actively involved in its management.
orig: ولقد خلقنا فوقكم سبع طرائق وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين

translation: And We sent down from the sky water in measure, then We made it stay in the earth, and indeed We are Able to take it away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God and His ability to control the natural resources of the world. The verse specifically mentions the water that was sent down from the sky and how it was made to stay on earth. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity that God is the ultimate authority and has the power to give and take away as He pleases. It also highlights the importance of water, a vital resource for human survival, and how it is a blessing from God that should not be taken for granted.
orig: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء بقدر فأسكناه في الأرض وإنا على ذهاب به لقادرون

translation: And indeed, We have created for you gardens of palm trees and grapes, wherein are abundant fruits and from them you eat.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings that God has bestowed upon humanity in the form of gardens filled with palm trees and grapes, providing an abundance of fruits for sustenance. The verse highlights God's generosity and provision for humanity's needs, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and appreciation for His blessings. It also serves as a reminder of the responsibility to use these blessings in a responsible and sustainable manner, as they are a trust from God.
orig: فأنشأنا لكم به جنات من نخيل وأعناب لكم فيها فواكه كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And a tree emerges from the earth, swaying to the breeze, its roots are firm and its branches are in the sky.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a tree that grows from the earth and its growth is compared to a person's spiritual growth. The tree's roots represent faith and the branches represent the actions that stem from that faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of having a strong foundation of faith (represented by the tree's roots) in order to produce good deeds (represented by the branches) that reach up to the sky, meaning they are pleasing to God.
orig: وشجرة تخرج من طور سيناء تنبت بالدهن وصبغ للآكلين

translation: And indeed, in the cattle, there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and you have many benefits in them, and of them, you eat.
interpretation: The verse highlights the lesson that can be learned from cattle. Just as cattle provide humans with numerous benefits, such as milk, meat, and leather, humans can also benefit from reflecting on the characteristics of cattle. For example, cattle are known for their strength, resilience, and hard work, qualities that humans can aspire to emulate. Additionally, the verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of all living beings and the importance of appreciating and respecting the role that animals play in our lives.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونها ولكم فيها منافع كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And upon it (the earth) are signs, clear signs, and (in) the alternation of the night and the day, and (in) what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs indeed for people who are not sure (of the meeting with their Lord).
interpretation: The verse highlights the signs of God's creation that are evident in the natural world, including the alternation of day and night and the heavens and earth. These signs are meant to serve as reminders for humans to believe in God and their eventual meeting with Him. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who are uncertain about their meeting with God are the ones who are in need of these signs, indicating that they are those who are not fully convinced of God's existence or are neglectful of their spiritual responsibilities.
orig: وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And We sent Noah to his people, saying, 'O my people, worship Allah, you have no god other than Him. Will you not fear Him?
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Noah's message to his people, calling them to worship only Allah and to abandon any other deities they may have been worshiping. The verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's divinity and the importance of recognizing and fearing Him. The verse serves as a reminder that true worship can only be directed towards Allah, and that the worship of any other being or thing is futile and will not be accepted.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: And the disbelievers say, 'This is not but a mortal like you. He eats and drinks, just like you. If Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels. We have heard this before.'
interpretation: The disbelievers in this verse are questioning the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and suggesting that he is just a mortal like them. They argue that if God had willed to send a prophet, He would have sent angels instead of a human being. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the disbelievers, who are unwilling to accept the message of Islam. It also emphasizes the idea that the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a sign of God's power and mercy, as He chooses to send a human being with a message that is both mercy and a reminder for all of humanity.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يريد أن يتفضل عليكم ولو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: Indeed, he was a man with a garden, to whom his Lord had given a beautiful garden, and he had torn it apart, so his Lord called out to him in the morning, 'Indeed, We will destroy your garden.'
interpretation: The verse tells the story of a man who was given a beautiful garden by his Lord, but instead of being grateful, he tore it apart. The verse serves as a metaphor for those who reject God's blessings and instead choose to live in disobedience. The verse warns of the consequences of such actions, as the man's garden was destroyed by God as a punishment. The verse highlights the importance of gratitude and obedience to God's commands, and serves as a warning to those who take God's blessings for granted.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل به جنة فتربصوا به حتى حين

translation: And they say: Our Lord! Condemn us not to (suffer) punishment, for we have been unjust.
interpretation: In this verse, the people are asking God not to punish them for their injustices. They recognize that they have been unjust and are seeking mercy from God. The verse highlights the idea that even those who have committed wrongdoing can still seek forgiveness and mercy from God, and that God is a merciful and forgiving God who may spare them from punishment if they repent and turn to Him.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a universal message that is meant to encompass all of humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" emphasizes the idea that the Prophet's message is not limited to this life, but it extends to the hereafter as well. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's mission and the importance of his message, and it encourages believers to spread his message to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs.
orig: فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا فإذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور فاسلك فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول منهم ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And when you were on the mountain, you were all called to the right side of the valley, when the people were iniquitous.
interpretation: The verse refers to the time when the Prophet Moses was on Mount Sinai receiving the Ten Commandments from God. The verse suggests that the Israelites, who were wandering in the wilderness, were rebellious and disobedient. They were called to the right side of the valley, indicating that they were being summoned to a place of judgment and punishment for their sins. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the need for repentance and obedience to God's commands.
orig: فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك فقل الحمد لله الذي نجانا من القوم الظالمين

translation: And my Lord, indeed He has made me of the housemates, the one who is blessed and the best of the housemates.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his gratitude to Allah for being chosen as a noble guest in Jannah. The phrase "منزلا مباركا" means "housemate" in Arabic, indicating that the Prophet will be blessed with a place in Paradise. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Prophet is not just a guest in Paradise but a beloved and honored one, chosen by Allah to be among the best of the righteous. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to follow the Prophet's example and strive to be among the righteous, in order to earn a place in Paradise.
orig: وقل رب أنزلني منزلا مباركا وأنت خير المنزلين

translation: Indeed, in this [Qur'an] are signs, indeed, We are warning.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a revelation from God, containing signs and warnings for humanity. The word 'indeed' is used twice to stress the certainty and importance of the message. The first 'indeed' indicates that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and wisdom, while the second 'indeed' highlights the fact that the Qur'an serves as a warning to those who choose to ignore or reject God's message. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is not just a collection of stories or poetry, but a divine communication from the Creator to humanity, containing guidance, wisdom, and warnings for those who are willing to listen and heed its message.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات وإن كنا لمبتلين

translation: Then We succeeded them with generations later.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the succession of generations. The use of the word 'ثم' (thumma) indicates a transition from one stage to another. The verse emphasizes that the new generations that came after the destroyed towns were also guilty of the same sins and injustices, and thus, they too will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the cycle of sin and punishment continues until people turn back to God and live according to His commandments.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And We sent to them a messenger from among themselves, saying, 'Worship Allah, there is no god for you other than Him. Will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the message of the prophets sent by God to guide people to the right path. The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the fact that there is no other deity worthy of worship except Him. The verse also highlights the importance of fearing God and living a life according to His commands. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have strayed from the right path, encouraging them to turn back to God and live a life of obedience to Him.
orig: فأرسلنا فيهم رسولا منهم أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: And the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe than the punishment of this life, and they will not be helped from their punishment in the Hereafter, and they will not be given any respite.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment in the Hereafter compared to the punishment in this life. The verse warns that the punishment in the Hereafter is not like the punishment in this life, which can be bearable or even temporary. The verse also warns that the punishment in the Hereafter will not be alleviated, and those who are punished will not be given any respite or relief. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical about the Hereafter and the punishment that awaits them, reminding them of the severity of God's punishment and the certainty of their fate.
orig: وقال الملأ من قومه الذين كفروا وكذبوا بلقاء الآخرة وأترفناهم في الحياة الدنيا ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

translation: And if you obey most of those who are on the earth, they will lead you astray from God's way. Indeed, they follow none but conjecture and they are only speculating.
interpretation: The verse warns against following the majority of people on earth, as they are likely to lead one astray from God's path. The verse emphasizes that the majority of people follow only conjecture and speculation, rather than true knowledge and guidance from God. It highlights the importance of relying on divine guidance rather than human opinion or speculation, and serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of the potential for misguidance and to seek truth and guidance only from God.
orig: ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هيهات هيهات لما توعدون

translation: Indeed, we are but mortal, and our life is but a fleeting dream.
interpretation: The verse highlights the transience of human life and the temporary nature of our existence. The phrase 'mortal' emphasizes our vulnerability and the inevitability of death, while 'fleeting dream' suggests that our time on earth is short-lived and ephemeral. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate the present moment and to make the most of the time we have, as our lives are but a brief flicker in the grand scheme of things.
orig: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And indeed, he is but a man who has invented a lie against Allah and we are not aware of any revelation that has been sent to him.
interpretation: The verse is a response to the Prophet's (peace be upon him) critics who accused him of inventing the Qur'an and attributed it to God. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet (peace be upon him) is only a human being who has not received any revelation from God, and that he is not aware of any revelation that has been sent to him. The verse serves as a refutation of the accusations against the Prophet (peace be upon him) and highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, revealed through the angel Gabriel, and not something that the Prophet (peace be upon him) has invented.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل افترى على الله كذبا وما نحن له بمؤمنين

translation: And they say: Our Lord! Certainly we disbelieve in that which you bring unto us, and we are not going to abandon our gods.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' response to the Prophet Muhammad's message. They reject the message and refuse to abandon their idols, indicating their deep-seated attachment to their false deities. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who are unwilling to accept the truth and persist in their misguided ways. It serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining steadfast in one's beliefs and not being swayed by the disbelievers' rejection of the truth.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال عما قليل ليصبحن نادمين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creations. The verse highlights that the Prophet's mission was not to destroy or punish, but to bring guidance and mercy to all people, regardless of their beliefs or backgrounds. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form indicates that the Prophet's message is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims that their religion is one of compassion, love, and mercy, and that their role is to spread peace and kindness to all people, regardless of their beliefs or backgrounds.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة بالحق فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: Then We made their descendants who were after them inheritors of the Book,
interpretation: The verse speaks about how God made the descendants of the previous nations, who were unjust and disobedient, inherit the Book, which refers to the Qur'an. This indicates that the message of the Qur'an is not limited to a particular nation or generation, but is a universal message that is meant for all people until the end of time. The verse also highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a reminder for those who come after, serving as a warning to them to avoid the mistakes of their predecessors and to follow the righteous path.
orig: ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Whenever a messenger came to a community, they denied him, so We seized them with Our punishment. Thus, We made their stories a lesson for those who fear the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes how God sent prophets and messengers to various communities, but they were consistently rejected and denied. As a result, God punished them, and their stories serve as a lesson for those who fear the consequences of disobedience. The verse emphasizes the idea that the stories of past communities serve as a warning to those who come later, and that rejecting God's messengers and disobeying His commands leads to punishment.
orig: ثم أرسلنا رسلنا تترى كل ما جاء أمة رسولها كذبوه فأتبعنا بعضهم بعضا وجعلناهم أحاديث فبعدا لقوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophets Moses and Aaron, whom God sent to the Pharaoh and his people with clear signs and authority. The verse emphasizes the legitimacy and authenticity of their prophethood, as they were chosen and sent by God. The verse also highlights the importance of the message they conveyed, which was a call to worship only God and to reject all other deities. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and mercy, as He sent prophets to guide humanity and provide them with the opportunity to repent and turn towards Him.
orig: ثم أرسلنا موسى وأخاه هارون بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were arrogant and became a haughty people.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of Pharaoh and his people towards God's message and the prophet Moses. Instead of humbling themselves and submitting to God's will, they became arrogant and haughty, rejecting the message and refusing to believe in God's power and authority. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of pride and arrogance, reminding believers to remain humble and submissive to God's will.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما عالين

translation: And they say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Allah and the Last Day, but their actions and behavior contradict their claims. They may utter the words of faith, but their hearts are devoid of true faith and conviction. Their lack of sincerity is evident in their treatment of others, as they do not treat people with kindness and compassion, which is a hallmark of true faith. The verse serves as a reminder that mere lip service is not enough; true faith must be reflected in one's actions and behavior.
orig: فقالوا أنؤمن لبشرين مثلنا وقومهما لنا عابدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكذبوهما فكانوا من المهلكين

translation: And indeed, We have given Moses the Scripture, that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Scripture (the Torah) given to Moses, which serves as a guide for the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the purpose of the Scripture, which is to guide people towards righteousness and away from sin. The use of the word 'indeed' at the beginning of the verse suggests that this is a reiteration of a previous statement or a reminder of an important fact. The verse also underscores the idea that guidance is not limited to the Israelites, but is available to all people through the Scripture.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We gave them refuge on a high ground, secure and tranquil.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the miraculous birth of Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother Mary. God made their existence a sign for humanity, a sign of God's power and mercy. God also provided them refuge on a high ground, a place of safety and tranquility, away from the harm and envy of those who rejected Jesus' message. The verse highlights God's care and protection for the righteous and the pious, and serves as a reminder of God's constant watchfulness and guidance over the believers.
orig: وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية وآويناهما إلى ربوة ذات قرار ومعين

translation: O messengers, eat from the good things and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.
interpretation: The verse addresses the prophets and messengers, encouraging them to partake in lawful and good food, indicating that they should enjoy the blessings of life while also being mindful of their responsibility to act righteously. The verse emphasizes that God is fully aware of their actions and that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to religious leaders and believers alike, to lead a life that is pleasing to God, and to always act with integrity and righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الرسل كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون عليم

translation: And indeed, this ummah of yours is one ummah, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Muslim community and the oneness of God. The use of the word 'ummah' (nation or community) signifies that all believers are part of one large family, united in their faith and their worship of one God. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers to fear God and to live according to His commandments, as He is the only one who can guide and protect them.
orig: وإن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاتقون

translation: And they split their affair between them, all of them, each party pleased with their (own) partners.
interpretation: The verse describes how the people of the town were divided and content with their respective cliques, indicating a sense of complacency and satisfaction with their current state, which prevented them from recognizing and addressing the impending punishment. The use of the word 'zabara' (partners) suggests a sense of mutual pleasure and enjoyment among the different groups, which further highlights their lack of awareness and preparedness for the coming punishment.
orig: فتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم زبرا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And they were followed by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Evil is the end of the wicked ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disobedience and disbelief. The phrase 'فذرهم في غمرتهم' means that they were cursed in this life and will be cursed on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase 'حتى حين' indicates that the curse will continue until the Day of Judgment. The verse warns against the dangers of disobedience and disbelief, emphasizing that those who choose to live a life of sin and disobedience will face the wrath of God both in this life and in the hereafter.
orig: فذرهم في غمرتهم حتى حين

translation: And they think that what they have been given is sufficient for them, but they are unaware of what is to come.
interpretation: The verse suggests that people tend to become complacent with what they have and lose sight of the future consequences of their actions. They are oblivious to the fact that their current state of prosperity or happiness is not a guarantee of a secure future. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and not to become too comfortable with the present, lest one becomes blind to the potential dangers that lie ahead.
orig: أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين

translation: And they are not hastening to do good deeds, but they are hastening to do evil deeds.
interpretation: The verse highlights the contrast between the righteous and the wicked. The righteous are eager to perform good deeds and race towards them, while the wicked are hastening to do evil deeds, indicating their eagerness to engage in sinful behavior. The verse emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds and the negative consequences of engaging in evil actions.
orig: نسارع لهم في الخيرات بل لا يشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who are apprehensive of their Lord's punishment are the ones who fear their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of reverence and awe that believers should have towards Allah. It emphasizes that those who truly fear Allah are those who are mindful of His punishment and are conscious of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that the fear of Allah is a fundamental aspect of faith and that it should be a driving force in the lives of believers.
orig: إن الذين هم من خشية ربهم مشفقون

translation: And those who are with their Lord are not afraid of the punishment, they are believers in their Lord's signs.
interpretation: The verse highlights the characteristic of true believers, who have faith in their Lord and are not afraid of the punishment. The verse emphasizes that these believers are aware of their Lord's signs and are convinced of His power and authority. They have a strong faith and trust in God, which gives them the strength to face any challenge or difficulty without fear. The verse serves as a reminder to all believers to cultivate this quality of faith and trust in God, which will ultimately lead to their salvation.
orig: والذين هم بآيات ربهم يؤمنون

translation: And those who do not implore any other deity along with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism in Islam. It emphasizes that true believers are those who do not associate any other being or entity with Allah, and that they do not seek help or guidance from any other source but Allah. This verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the only one who can provide true guidance and help, and that seeking assistance from other sources is a form of shirk (associating partners with Allah), which is a grave sin in Islam.
orig: والذين هم بربهم لا يشركون

translation: And those who are Grateful for what We have given them, and their hearts are not puffed up with pride, and they are not haughty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of gratitude and humility in those who have been blessed with wealth and material possessions. It emphasizes that true gratitude is not just about giving thanks, but also about being humble and not letting wealth and pride corrupt one's heart. The phrase 'their hearts are not puffed up with pride' suggests that true gratitude is accompanied by a sense of humility and modesty, while 'and they are not haughty' implies that those who are truly grateful do not look down on others or feel superior to them. The verse serves as a reminder that true gratitude is a sign of faith and a means of spiritual growth.
orig: والذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون

translation: And they will be rewarded with the reward of the former ones,
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward that those who do good deeds will receive in the afterlife. The phrase 'former ones' refers to the righteous people who came before them, indicating that the reward for good deeds is not limited to this life, but will continue in the hereafter. The verse serves as an encouragement for people to do good deeds and live a righteous life, promising them a reward that will be even greater than what they have done in this life.
orig: أولئك يسارعون في الخيرات وهم لها سابقون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam, which is a source of guidance and light for humanity, and serves as a reminder that the Prophet's mission is not to bring harm or destruction, but rather to bring people closer to God and to guide them towards a righteous and just life.
orig: ولا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ولدينا كتاب ينطق بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Their hearts are in utter ignorance of this, and they have deeds which they are doing.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who are heedless of God's signs and are engrossed in their own desires and worldly pursuits. Their hearts are ignorant of the truth and they are consumed by their own deeds, which are devoid of any spiritual significance. The verse highlights the contrast between the ignorance of the people and the knowledge and wisdom that comes from recognizing and acknowledging God's signs. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are neglectful of God's message to turn back to Him and seek guidance.
orig: بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا ولهم أعمال من دون ذلك هم لها عاملون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed them, and theirs is a punishment in the Hereafter, and for them there will be no helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and the certainty of punishment in the afterlife. The use of the word 'indeed' emphasizes the certainty of the punishment, and the phrase 'and theirs is a punishment in the Hereafter' underscores the idea that the punishment is not limited to this life, but will extend into the afterlife. The final phrase, 'and for them there will be no helper' reinforces the idea that there will be no escape or reprieve from the punishment, and that the individuals in question will be left to face the consequences of their actions alone.
orig: حتى إذا أخذنا مترفيهم بالعذاب إذا هم يجأرون

translation: Do not be sad, for you will not be reprimanded. Indeed, you will not be reminded.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, comforting them that they will not be reprimanded or criticized for their beliefs and actions. The verse implies that the disbelievers will not be able to harm the believers, and that they will ultimately be defeated. The verse also serves as a reminder that the believers will be victorious and that their faith will be triumphant.
orig: لا تجأروا اليوم إنكم منا لا تنصرون

translation: And indeed, We have sent you (O Muhammad) to all the people as a witness, and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of the Prophet Muhammad's message, as he was sent to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse also highlights the dual nature of the Prophet's role: he was both a bearer of good news (the promise of Paradise for believers) and a warner (of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message). The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam to all people, and the importance of his role as a mercy to humanity.
orig: قد كانت آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم على أعقابكم تنكصون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: مستكبرين به سامرا تهجرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفلم يدبروا القول أم جاءهم ما لم يأت آباءهم الأولين

translation: And they did not recognize their messenger, so they denied him.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people's rejection of their prophet, who was sent by God to guide them towards the right path. The verse implies that the people were so consumed by their own desires and arrogance that they failed to recognize the prophet's authority and message. As a result, they denied him and his message, which ultimately led to their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and respecting God's messengers, who are sent to guide humanity towards righteousness and salvation.
orig: أم لم يعرفوا رسولهم فهم له منكرون

translation: And they say, 'He is a madman.' But it is the truth from your Lord, and a warning to the Children of Israel.
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. They label him as a madman, but the verse emphasizes that he is actually speaking the truth from Allah, and that his message is a warning to the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the rejection and opposition that the Prophet faced, and serves as a reminder that the truth is often met with resistance and disbelief.
orig: أم يقولون به جنة بل جاءهم بالحق وأكثرهم للحق كارهون

translation: And if they had believed in Me and My verses, and had not denied Me, I would have given them a reward from the heaven and the earth, and would have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the consequence of not believing in God and denying His verses. The verse indicates that those who reject God's message will not only face punishment but also miss out on the rewards that come with faith. The verse also highlights God's mercy, as He would have guided those who believed in Him to a straight path, indicating a path of righteousness and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder to those who reject God's message, that they are not only risking punishment but also missing out on the rewards of faith.
orig: ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لفسدت السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن بل أتيناهم بذكرهم فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون

translation: And ask them about the town that was situated by the sea, when they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, and their punishment came to them on the day of their Sabbath, and they were overtaken by the flood, and Allah's punishment was severe.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the people of Prophet Salih, who were punished by God for their disobedience and disbelief. The verse highlights the fact that their punishment came on a Saturday, the day they were commanded to observe the Sabbath and refrain from work. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of following God's commands.
orig: أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And indeed, you will surely call them to the straight path
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commanding him to invite the people to the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and obedience to God. The verse emphasizes the importance of guidance and the role of the Prophet as a guide for humanity. It also highlights the responsibility of believers to invite others to the right path and to guide them towards a righteous life.
orig: وإنك لتدعوهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are astray from the path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the spiritual loss and confusion of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. The phrase 'astray from the path' suggests that they are wandering aimlessly, without a clear direction or purpose in life. The verse implies that belief in the Hereafter is essential for a person's spiritual well-being and moral guidance, as it provides a sense of accountability and responsibility for one's actions in this life.
orig: وإن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة عن الصراط لناكبون

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with His creation. Despite the people's disobedience and sin, God did not destroy them immediately. Instead, He gave them a chance to repent and mend their ways. The verse suggests that the punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe than any punishment that could be inflicted in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that God's patience is not infinite and that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولو رحمناهم وكشفنا ما بهم من ضر للجوا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed them, and theirs was a punishment in the morning and at noon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and finality of God's punishment for those who reject His signs and continue to live in sin. The use of the past tense 'We have destroyed them' underscores the fact that the punishment has already been carried out and is not something that can be avoided or reversed. The phrase 'theirs was a punishment' highlights the idea that the punishment was well-deserved and appropriate for their crimes. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them that God's justice is inescapable and that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولقد أخذناهم بالعذاب فما استكانوا لربهم وما يتضرعون

translation: And indeed, We have opened upon them a door of severe punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of rejecting God's message and refusing to believe in Him. The 'door of severe punishment' refers to the consequences that come from disobeying God and rejecting His prophets. The verse suggests that the punishment is certain and inevitable, and that it will come suddenly and unexpectedly, catching the disbelievers off guard. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face if they continue to disbelieve.
orig: حتى إذا فتحنا عليهم بابا ذا عذاب شديد إذا هم فيه مبلسون

translation: It is He who has created for you hearing and vision and understanding, little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and generosity in creating human beings with the ability to hear, see, and understand. The verse highlights the ingratitude of humans, who often take these blessings for granted and fail to recognize and appreciate the source of their abilities. The verse serves as a reminder to be thankful for God's blessings and to recognize the magnitude of His favors upon us.
orig: وهو الذي أنشأ لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: It is He who has made you successors (Khalifah) on the earth and has raised some of you above others in ranks, so that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and dominion over the earth, and how He has appointed human beings as His successors (Khalifah) on earth. The verse also highlights the fact that God has given some people a higher status than others, whether in terms of knowledge, wealth, or authority, in order to test them in their faith and obedience. The verse ends by reminding the believers that God is swift in punishment for those who disobey Him, but also Forgiving and Merciful to those who repent and turn to Him.
orig: وهو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And He is the One who gives life and causes death, and to Him is the alternation of the night and the day. Have you not reasoned?
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power over life and death, emphasizing that He is the ultimate authority who can give life and take it away. The verse also draws attention to the cyclical nature of time, with the alternation of night and day, reminding humans of the passage of time and the need to reflect on their actions and turn back to God. The question at the end of the verse, 'Have you not reasoned?', serves as a call to introspection and reflection, inviting humans to ponder on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world and to recognize His greatness.
orig: وهو الذي يحيي ويميت وله اختلاف الليل والنهار أفلا تعقلون

translation: And they say, 'Follow such and such a person, for they will guide you.' But how can they guide you when they are not guided themselves?
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who are misguided and are following false leaders who claim to be guides but are themselves lost. The verse warns against blindly following such individuals and emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from God and His Messenger instead. It highlights the irony of people claiming to guide others when they themselves are in need of guidance, and serves as a reminder to be cautious of those who claim to have all the answers but are themselves confused and misguided.
orig: بل قالوا مثل ما قال الأولون

translation: They said, 'We have been oppressed and impoverished, and our wealth has been destroyed.' And they call themselves patient and patiently persevere.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been oppressed and impoverished, and their wealth has been destroyed. Despite their difficult circumstances, they proclaim themselves to be patient and patiently persevering. The verse highlights the contrast between their outer appearance of patience and their inner feelings of oppression and hardship. It serves as a reminder that true patience is not just about enduring difficult circumstances, but also about maintaining a positive attitude and trust in God's justice and mercy.
