orig: قالوا أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: And indeed, We have warned you and your parents before, but the warning has been neglected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fact that the warning of God's punishment has been repeatedly given to the current generation and their ancestors, but it has been consistently ignored. The verse highlights the idea that the warning is not a new concept, but rather a reminder of what has been said before. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of not heeding the warning will be severe and that the excuse of not knowing or being unaware will not be accepted.
orig: لقد وعدنا نحن وآباؤنا هذا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Say, 'To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?'
interpretation: This verse is a question posed by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking him to consider who has ownership of the earth and everything in it. The verse serves as a reminder that everything in the world, including the earth and all that it contains, belongs to God. It is He who created it, sustains it, and has the power to take it away. The verse is a reminder to the believers to recognize God's sovereignty over all things and to live their lives in accordance with His will.
orig: قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, 'Exalted is Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the throne, the Exalted, the Great.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people who have been destroyed by God's punishment are speaking, acknowledging Allah's greatness and authority. They are saying that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Creator and Sustainer of all things, and the One who is worthy of all praise and worship. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and glory, and serves as a reminder to all people of the importance of recognizing and submitting to Allah's authority.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تذكرون

translation: Say: 'Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the great throne?'
interpretation: This verse is a question that asks who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the great throne. It is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the greatness and majesty of God, implying that He is the one who is worthy of worship and obedience. The seven heavens refer to the highest heavens, which are considered the dwelling place of God and the angels. The great throne is a symbol of God's power and authority, emphasizing His sovereignty over the universe. The verse is a call to acknowledge and submit to God's greatness and authority.
orig: قل من رب السماوات السبع ورب العرش العظيم

translation: They will say, 'God, we have heard a caller calling to prayer, [calling] us to the religion of Allah,'
interpretation: In this verse, the people who have been guilty of injustice and disobedience are speaking to God, acknowledging that they have heard a caller (the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him) inviting them to the religion of Allah. They are admitting that they have been negligent in their duties towards God and have not followed the guidance of the Prophet. The verse highlights the importance of responding to the call of God and following His commandments, and serves as a warning to those who neglect their spiritual responsibilities.
orig: سيقولون لله قل أفلا تتقون

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' He has given you the name of Malik (King) until the Day of Judgment. Indeed, the wicked will be in Hell, where they will not be taken out of it, and they will not be able to be relieved from it.
interpretation: This verse is a question posed by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking him to affirm that the Lord of the heavens and the earth is indeed Allah. The verse then goes on to emphasize the grandeur and sovereignty of Allah, stating that He has given Himself the name of Malik (King) until the Day of Judgment. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, stating that they will be in Hell, where they will not be able to escape or be relieved from it.
orig: قل من بيده ملكوت كل شيء وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: They will say, 'God is poor and we are rich.'
interpretation: The verse describes the mindset of the disbelievers who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and refuse to believe in the Hereafter. They mockingly say that God is poor and they are rich, implying that they do not need God's help or blessings. The verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who reject faith and choose to live in disobedience to God's commands. It serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their own wealth and status, and to not let it lead them astray from the path of righteousness.
orig: سيقولون لله قل فأنى تسحرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بل أتيناهم بالحق وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما اتخذ الله من ولد وما كان معه من إله إذا لذهب كل إله بما خلق ولعلا بعضهم على بعض سبحان الله عما يصفون

translation: And they will not be granted a share of the hidden wealth and the Day of Resurrection.,
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and choose to live in disbelief. They will not have a share in the hidden wealth and will not participate in the Day of Resurrection, which is the day when all souls will be judged and rewarded or punished according to their deeds. The verse warns against the consequences of disbelief and encourages the reader to reflect on the hereafter and seek guidance to avoid such a fate.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة فتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Say, 'Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their presence.'
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to God, seeking refuge in Him from the whispers and temptations of devils. The use of the word 'Lord' twice emphasizes the speaker's dependence on God and their recognition of His power and protection. The phrase 'from their presence' suggests that the speaker is seeking protection not just from the devils' whispers, but also from their very presence, indicating a desire to avoid even the possibility of being influenced by their evil suggestions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking refuge in God and relying on His protection in times of temptation or danger.
orig: قل رب إما تريني ما يوعدون

translation: My Lord, do not make me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication made by the Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, in which he asks God to not include him among the wrongdoing people. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's protection and guidance in order to avoid being among those who are destined for hell. It also emphasizes the significance of living a righteous life and avoiding the company of those who engage in wrongdoing, in order to attain salvation.
orig: رب فلا تجعلني في القوم الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We will show them Our signs and verses, but they will not believe them.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that even though God's signs and verses are clear and evident, those who are determined to disbelieve will still refuse to accept them. This verse emphasizes the idea that denial and disbelief are not due to a lack of evidence or convincing arguments, but rather a result of a person's unwillingness to submit to the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is not based on empirical evidence, but rather on the willingness to submit to God's will.
orig: وإنا على أن نريك ما نعدهم لقادرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة نحن أعلم بما يصفون

translation: And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whispers of the devils.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer to God for protection against the whispers and temptations of the devils. The verse emphasizes the seekers' reliance on God's protection and their recognition of the devils' ability to whisper and tempt. The verse serves as a reminder of the constant need for spiritual vigilance and the importance of seeking refuge in God from the evil whispers that can lead astray.
orig: وقل رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they should come near me.
interpretation: The verse is a prayer of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which he seeks refuge in Allah from the evil of the wicked people who were trying to harm him. The verse highlights the Prophet's trust and reliance on Allah for protection and safety. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking refuge in Allah from the evils of the world and the hereafter.
orig: وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون

translation: And when death came to one of them, he said, 'My Lord, send me back.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in which a person is facing death and requests to be sent back to life. The verse highlights the fear and regret that comes with death, as the person realizes that they have not prepared for the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder to the living to prepare for their own death and to live a life that is pleasing to God, so that they may avoid regret and fear in the hereafter.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أحدهم الموت قال رب ارجعون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you, but do you not remember?
interpretation: The verse is a reminder to the disbelievers that God has destroyed nations before them, and yet they continue to disbelieve and reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes the forgetfulness of the disbelievers, who have forgotten the lessons of history and the warnings of God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that God's punishment is imminent and that they should take heed of the signs of God's power and wrath.
orig: لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت كلا إنها كلمة هو قائلها ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask after one another.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where the Trumpet will be blown, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the judgment. On that day, the verse says, there will be no familial ties or relationships between people, and no one will ask after another. Everyone will be too busy worrying about their own fate and trying to justify their actions to God. The verse emphasizes the idea that on the Day of Judgment, everyone will be held accountable for their own deeds, and that no one will be able to rely on their family or friends to save them. It is a reminder to believers to focus on their own spiritual development and not to rely on their relationships with others to save them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فإذا نفخ في الصور فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ ولا يتساءلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who have been effaced by their ownselves, they are the ones who have lost their souls to Hell, eternally.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have lost their souls to Hell. The phrase 'effaced by their ownselves' suggests that they have been consumed by their own desires and worldly pursuits, and have lost sight of their spiritual well-being. The verse emphasizes that those who have lost their souls in this way will be punished in Hell for eternity, highlighting the gravity of their spiritual loss.
orig: ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون

translation: Their faces will be turned into the Fire, and they will be grilled in it.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The image of their faces being turned into the Fire and being grilled in it is a vivid and powerful metaphor for the intense suffering they will experience in Hell. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who reject God's mercy and guidance will be faced with the consequences of their choices, and that they will be unable to escape the punishment that awaits them.
orig: تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون

translation: And how many a sign have We given you, but you denied it, and you were among those who belied.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who rejected the signs and miracles that God had given them. Despite the clear evidence and guidance, they chose to deny and reject the truth. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who refuse to accept the signs of God, and serves as a warning to those who are skeptical and resistant to faith.
orig: ألم تكن آياتي تتلى عليكم فكنتم بها تكذبون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, we have been oppressed, and our sins have overcome us. We were a people astray.'
interpretation: The verse describes the people's admission of their sins and their recognition of their need for God's forgiveness. The phrase 'غلبت علينا شقوتنا' (ghulibat `alayna shuqutnah) means 'our sins have overcome us' and indicates that the people have realized that their sins have taken control of their lives. The second part of the verse, 'وكنا قوما ضالين' (wa kana qawma dhalin) means 'and we were a people astray' and emphasizes that the people have strayed from the right path and are seeking guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing one's sins and seeking forgiveness, and serves as a model for those who seek to repent and turn towards God.
orig: قالوا ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين

translation: Our Lord, extract us from this town, for its people are oppressors.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication to God to deliver the speaker and their community from an oppressive town. The use of the word 'extract' emphasizes the idea of being removed from a difficult or harmful situation. The description of the town's people as 'oppressors' highlights the injustice and suffering they inflict on others. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the only one who can provide relief and protection from oppression.
orig: ربنا أخرجنا منها فإن عدنا فإنا ظالمون

translation: And they denied him, so they will surely be brought to the punishment.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who denied the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and refused to believe in God's revelation. The verse warns them that they will be brought to account for their disbelief and will face punishment in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to those who reject God's message, that they will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: قال اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون

translation: Indeed, my Lord has commanded me to pray, 'O my Lord, forgive me and have mercy upon me, for You are the Best of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which he is asking God for forgiveness and mercy. The use of the word 'indeed' (innahu) at the beginning of the verse emphasizes the importance and certainty of the command. The phrase 'my Lord' (rabbuni) is used to address God in a personal and intimate way, signifying a close relationship between the Prophet and God. The request for forgiveness (aghfirlani) and mercy (wajhatan) is a recognition of the Prophet's own imperfections and the need for God's grace and compassion. The phrase 'You are the Best of the merciful' (antar-rahman) is a declaration of God's attribute of mercy and emphasizes God's infinite compassion and forgiveness.
orig: إنه كان فريق من عبادي يقولون ربنا آمنا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you are succeeding them in their misdeeds.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers, reminding them that their ancestors were also destroyed by God's punishment. The verse implies that the disbelievers are following in their ancestors' footsteps, continuing their misdeeds and disobedience. The verse serves as a warning, reminding the disbelievers of the consequences of their actions and the fate that awaits them if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: فاتخذتموهم سخريا حتى أنسوكم ذكري وكنتم منهم تضحكون

translation: Indeed, I will give them a reward for what they patiently endured. They are the victors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers who have been patient in the face of adversity and hardship. God promises to reward them for their patience and perseverance, and declares them to be the true victors in life. The verse highlights the importance of patience and resilience in the face of challenges, and serves as an encouragement to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in God's promise of reward and victory.
orig: إني جزيتهم اليوم بما صبروا أنهم هم الفائزون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

translation: They said, 'We have been destroyed, (and) there is no escape.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been warned of God's punishment. They have realized that they are in a state of destruction and that there is no escape from God's wrath. The verse highlights the hopelessness and despair of those who have been consumed by their sins and are facing the consequences. It serves as a reminder that once the punishment has been decreed, there is no escape, and the only way to avoid it is to turn to God in repentance and seek His mercy.
orig: قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم فاسأل العادين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to a decisive and unambiguous victory, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is clear and evident to all. The verse is often interpreted as a reference to the triumph of Islam over other religions and ideologies, and serves as a reminder to believers that their faith will ultimately triumph over all obstacles and challenges.
orig: قال إن لبثتم إلا قليلا لو أنكم كنتم تعلمون

translation: Have we not created you from a worthless sperm and yet you deny us?
interpretation: The verse highlights the idea that human beings were created from a mere sperm, which is considered worthless and insignificant. Despite this humble beginning, human beings have a tendency to deny and disregard their Creator. The verse serves as a reminder of the greatness of God's power and the ingratitude of human beings who refuse to acknowledge and worship their Creator.
orig: أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا وأنكم إلينا لا ترجعون

translation: Glorified be Allah, the True King! There is no god except Him, the Lord of the Honorable Throne.
interpretation: The verse proclaims the greatness and uniqueness of Allah as the one and only God, emphasizing His sovereignty and power. The phrase 'al-Malik al-Haqq' (the True King) highlights Allah's kingship and authority over all creation. The verse also emphasizes the majesty and honor of Allah, referring to Him as the Lord of the 'arsh al-karim' (the Honorable Throne), indicating His exalted status and glory. The verse serves as a declaration of Allah's greatness and a reminder of His oneness and uniqueness.
orig: فتعالى الله الملك الحق لا إله إلا هو رب العرش الكريم

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the guilty will not be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of inventing lies against Allah or denying His signs. The guilty party will not prosper, and their actions will not go unpunished. The verse serves as a warning to those who deliberately spread falsehoods or reject the truth, reminding them that their actions are not only unjust but also futile in the face of God's ultimate justice.
orig: ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به فإنما حسابه عند ربه إنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: And say: My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the Best of the merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness and mercy from God. The use of the phrase 'My Lord' signifies a personal and intimate relationship between the speaker and God, and the request for forgiveness and mercy is a recognition of human frailty and the need for divine grace. The description of God as 'the Best of the merciful' highlights His attribute of mercy and emphasizes His willingness to forgive and show compassion to those who seek it.
orig: وقل رب اغفر وارحم وأنت خير الراحمين

translation: And indeed, We have sent it down, and We will continue to send down upon you. And indeed, We have revealed it with clear signs and warnings, perhaps you will remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the revelation of the Qur'an as a mercy and guidance from God to humanity. The use of the word 'We' in the verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, and the phrase 'perhaps you will remember' suggests that the ultimate purpose of the revelation is to guide humanity towards righteousness and obedience to God. The verse also highlights the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and warning, and serves as a reminder to those who reject its message that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها وأنزلنا فيها آيات بينات لعلكم تذكرون

translation: The adulterer and the adulteress, lash each one of them a hundred lashes, and do not let compassion for them detract you from the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Hereafter. And let a group of believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: This verse commands the punishment of lashing for those who commit adultery, emphasizing the importance of upholding justice and morality in society. The verse also highlights the importance of faith in Allah and the Hereafter as a motivation for upholding these values. The requirement for a group of believers to witness the punishment serves as a deterrent and a reminder of the consequences of such actions, and also provides an opportunity for the community to reinforce its values and norms.
orig: الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا كل واحد منهما مائة جلدة ولا تأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله إن كنتم تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وليشهد عذابهما طائفة من المؤمنين

translation: The adulterer shall not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress shall not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist. That is forbidden to the believers.
interpretation: This verse outlines the consequences of committing adultery and the prohibition of marrying someone who has committed adultery. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who commit adultery are not worthy of marrying a chaste person, and that they can only marry someone who is equally guilty of immoral behavior. This verse serves as a deterrent against adultery and a reminder of the importance of upholding moral values and purity in society.
orig: الزاني لا ينكح إلا زانية أو مشركة والزانية لا ينكحها إلا زان أو مشرك وحرم ذلك على المؤمنين

translation: And those who harm the believing men and believing women, then they do not repent, they will have a painful punishment, and they will not have any advocates or supporters besides Allah. And those are the ones who are disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave consequences for those who persecute and harm believers, both men and women. The verse emphasizes that they will not have any advocates or supporters on Judgment Day, and their punishment will be severe and painful. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are disobedient and refuse to repent, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: والذين يرمون المحصنات ثم لم يأتوا بأربعة شهداء فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة ولا تقبلوا لهم شهادة أبدا وأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Except those who repented after that and made amends. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the possibility of forgiveness and redemption for those who have committed wrongdoing. The phrase 'after that' refers to the period of time after the destruction of the unjust towns, indicating that even in the face of such destruction, there is still hope for forgiveness and a chance to make amends. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance and making amends as a means of seeking forgiveness and avoiding punishment. The description of Allah as 'Forgiving and Merciful' underscores the idea that God is always willing to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that indeed, they are truthful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the situation where a husband accuses his wife of unchastity without any witnesses except himself. In such cases, the husband's testimony is considered invalid, and he must swear four times by Allah that he is telling the truth. The verse aims to protect the rights of women and prevent false accusations, emphasizing the importance of reliable testimony and the gravity of making false accusations.
orig: والذين يرمون أزواجهم ولم يكن لهم شهداء إلا أنفسهم فشهادة أحدهم أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الصادقين

translation: And the fifth is that the curse of Allah be upon the liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to the consequences of lying and the curses that come with it. The phrase 'الخامسة' (the fifth) indicates that lying is considered a serious offense, among the five greatest sins, and those who engage in it are subject to Allah's curse. The verse serves as a warning to those who lie and deceive others, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the need to repent and speak the truth.
orig: والخامسة أن لعنت الله عليه إن كان من الكاذبين

translation: And they will be exposed to the Fire, morning and evening, and on the Day when the Hour will be established: 'Certainly, you are the ones who are liars.'
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and live a life of sin. They will be exposed to the Fire, both in this life and the next, as a manifestation of God's wrath. The phrase 'morning and evening' emphasizes the constant and unrelenting nature of this punishment, while the mention of the Day of Judgment serves as a reminder that their deceit and disbelief will ultimately be exposed and judged by God. The final phrase, 'Certainly, you are the ones who are liars,' underscores the idea that their denial of the truth and rejection of God's message will not be tolerated, and they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ويدرأ عنها العذاب أن تشهد أربع شهادات بالله إنه لمن الكاذبين

translation: And the fifth (reason) is that Allah's anger was upon them, indeed they were among the truthful.
interpretation: The fifth reason for the destruction of the towns is that Allah's anger was upon them, indicating that they were deserving of punishment due to their sinful nature. The use of the word 'truthful' suggests that they were truthful in their actions and words, but this did not save them from the consequences of their wrongdoing. The verse highlights the idea that even those who are considered truthful and righteous are not immune to punishment if they engage in sinful behavior.
orig: والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها إن كان من الصادقين

translation: Were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been destroyed. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the believers' salvation is solely due to God's grace and mercy, rather than their own deeds. It serves as a reminder that even when they were on the brink of destruction, God's mercy and grace intervened and saved them. The verse also highlights God's attribute of being the 'Accepting of repentance', indicating that He is always willing to accept the repentance of those who turn back to Him. The verse concludes by emphasizing God's wisdom in His dealings with humanity.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله تواب حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who came with falsehood are a group of you. Do not think it is bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every woman among them is what she has earned, and they will be punished with a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have come together to spread falsehood and lies. The verse tells the believers not to think that this is a bad thing, but rather it is a good thing for them, as it will lead to their spiritual growth and purification. The verse also warns the disbelievers that they will face a severe punishment for their actions, and that each person will receive what they have earned, whether it be good or bad.
orig: إن الذين جاءوا بالإفك عصبة منكم لا تحسبوه شرا لكم بل هو خير لكم لكل امرئ منهم ما اكتسب من الإثم والذي تولى كبره منهم له عذاب عظيم

translation: And if they had believed in Me and My Messengers, they would have believed in what I revealed to them, and it would have been better for them. And We would have given them a double reward in this life and in the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in God and His Messengers. The verse suggests that those who believe in God and His Messengers will receive a double reward, both in this life and in the Hereafter. The verse also implies that the reward is not limited to the believers, but also extends to their descendants, indicating the importance of passing on the message of faith to future generations.
orig: لولا إذ سمعتموه ظن المؤمنون والمؤمنات بأنفسهم خيرا وقالوا هذا إفك مبين

translation: And if they had come to you with four witnesses against them, then they would have been punished by God, but they did not come, so they are liars in the sight of God.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were required to produce four witnesses to support their claim. However, they failed to do so and were therefore considered liars in the eyes of God. The verse highlights the importance of honesty and truthfulness, and serves as a warning to those who try to deceive others or make false claims. It also emphasizes the consequences of lying and the importance of being truthful, as it is a fundamental aspect of a person's faith and relationship with God.
orig: لولا جاءوا عليه بأربعة شهداء فإذ لم يأتوا بالشهداء فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

translation: Were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, you would have been punished for your sins and consumed by your own desires.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that humans are prone to sin and would be consumed by their own desires if it were not for Allah's grace and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and being grateful for Allah's blessings in our lives, as well as the potential consequences of our actions if we were to ignore or reject His guidance. The verse also highlights the idea that the punishment for sin is not limited to the Hereafter, but can also manifest in this world.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته في الدنيا والآخرة لمسكم في ما أفضتم فيه عذاب عظيم

translation: And when you heard it, you laughed at it and said, 'Are we to be destroyed by what is not lifeless?'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' reaction to the message of the Qur'an, which they found amusing and dismissed as mere words without any substance. The verse highlights their arrogance and lack of understanding, as they failed to recognize the power and significance of the message. The phrase 'Are we to be destroyed by what is not lifeless?' is a rhetorical question, implying that they believed the message to be insignificant and unable to harm them. The verse serves as a rebuke to those who underestimate the power of God's word and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: إذ تلقونه بألسنتكم وتقولون بأفواهكم ما ليس لكم به علم وتحسبونه هينا وهو عند الله عظيم

translation: And if We had destroyed you, you would have said, 'If only we had been given a chance to live, we would have been better in our behavior!',
interpretation: This verse addresses the tendency of humans to regret and repent when faced with the consequences of their actions, but only after it's too late. The verse suggests that even when given the opportunity to change their ways, humans tend to neglect their responsibilities and continue to act in their own self-interest. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that they will not be given a second chance to repent once the punishment has been delivered.
orig: ولولا إذ سمعتموه قلتم ما يكون لنا أن نتكلم بهذا سبحانك هذا بهتان عظيم

translation: May Allah forgive you, [O Muhammad], and have mercy upon you, and upon the believers.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of forgiveness and mercy upon the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. It is a request to God to show His mercy and forgiveness upon them, indicating that they are deserving of His grace and compassion. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, and serves as a reminder to believers to lead a righteous life and seek God's guidance and protection.
orig: يعظكم الله أن تعودوا لمثله أبدا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And Allah clarifies the verses to you, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of God's revelations, indicating that they are easy to understand and comprehend. The verse also highlights God's omniscience and wisdom, suggesting that His teachings are not only clear but also profound and wise. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to reflect on the Qur'an and its teachings, and to recognize the wisdom and knowledge that they contain.
orig: ويبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, those who desire that immorality should spread [or be publicized] among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against the spread of immorality and the desire to publicize it among the believers. The punishment for those who engage in such activities will be severe, both in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and awareness of such actions, while humans may not be aware of the full extent of the consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in immoral behavior and a reminder of the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إن الذين يحبون أن تشيع الفاحشة في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم في الدنيا والآخرة والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been destroyed. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the believers were on the brink of destruction, but Allah's grace and mercy intervened and saved them. The verse emphasizes Allah's kindness and mercy, reminding the believers that they owe their survival to Allah's grace and not their own strength or efforts. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to recognize that their survival is not due to their own power or abilities but rather due to Allah's mercy and grace.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته وأن الله رءوف رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he commands immorality and wrongdoing. And were it not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure. But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding the footsteps of Satan and not following his commands, which lead to immorality and wrongdoing. The verse also highlights the grace and mercy of Allah, who purifies and guides whom He wills. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and seek guidance from Allah, and to be grateful for His favor and mercy. It also underscores the fact that Allah is all-knowing and all-hearing, and is aware of all our actions and thoughts.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان ومن يتبع خطوات الشيطان فإنه يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته ما زكى منكم من أحد أبدا ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء والله سميع عليم

translation: And let not those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of wealth and property (i.e., the unbelievers) think that they will be forgiven.
interpretation: This verse addresses the unbelievers who are stingy with the wealth and resources that God has given them. They are warned that their miserliness will not be forgiven, and that they will face consequences for their actions. The verse highlights the importance of being generous and charitable, and serves as a reminder that true wealth and success come from God, and that we must use our resources in a way that pleases Him.
orig: ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى والمساكين والمهاجرين في سبيل الله وليعفوا وليصفحوا ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who oppress the believing men and believing women, they will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who oppress and persecute believing men and women. The punishment is not limited to the oppressors' lifetime, but extends to the Hereafter as well. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in such behavior, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face in this life and the next.
orig: إن الذين يرمون المحصنات الغافلات المؤمنات لعنوا في الدنيا والآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On a day when their tongues, hands, and feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse describes a day of judgment when people's body parts, including their tongues, hands, and feet, will testify against them for their actions in this life. This verse emphasizes the idea that people will be held accountable for their deeds, and that every action, good or bad, will be recorded and brought to light on the day of judgment. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to strive to live a virtuous life, as everything we do will have consequences in the hereafter.
orig: يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And on the Day when He will gather them together, (it will seem) as if they had not stayed (in the world) but an hour of a day, (and) they will recognize each other, (and) will say: 'Surely we were in a state of intoxication, (and) we had no connection with the truth!'
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will gather all people together and it will seem as if they had not lived in the world for more than an hour. They will recognize each other and realize that they were in a state of spiritual intoxication, disconnected from the truth and oblivious to the reality of their actions. The verse highlights the sudden and unexpected nature of the Day of Judgment and the fact that people will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: يومئذ يوفيهم الله دينهم الحق ويعلمون أن الله هو الحق المبين

translation: The wicked are astonished at the upright, and the wicked women are astonished at the upright women, the good men are astonished at the good women, and the good women are astonished at the good men, those are the ones who have been forgiven much, and they have been given a generous provision.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the contrast between the wicked and the righteous, and how the wicked are amazed at the good deeds and characteristics of the righteous. The verse emphasizes that the righteous have been forgiven much and have been given a generous provision, indicating that their good deeds and righteousness are a result of God's grace and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to strive to be among the righteous and to be grateful for God's blessings and forgiveness.
orig: الخبيثات للخبيثين والخبيثون للخبيثات والطيبات للطيبين والطيبون للطيبات أولئك مبرءون مما يقولون لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses, lest you trespass and intrude upon their privacy. That is better for you, that you may not remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting people's privacy and personal space. Believers are commanded not to enter other people's homes without permission, as this is considered trespassing and disrespectful. The verse also implies that entering someone's home without permission can lead to harmful consequences and can damage relationships. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to always seek permission before entering someone's home, as this is a sign of respect and consideration for others' privacy and personal space.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها ذلكم خير لكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, so do not feel secure, for destruction can come to you suddenly, either at midday or in the evening.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the readers, reminding them that God's punishment can come at any moment, without warning. The use of the phrase 'around you' emphasizes the proximity of the destroyed towns and the certainty of God's judgment. The verse encourages the readers to reflect on their actions and turn to God, rather than feeling secure in their ways and ignoring the warning signs. The phrase 'either at midday or in the evening' underscores the sudden and unexpected nature of God's punishment, indicating that no one is immune from His judgment.
orig: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم وإن قيل لكم ارجعوا فارجعوا هو أزكى لكم والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: And there is not upon you any caretaking of the uninhabited houses, and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that believers should not feel obligated to take care of uninhabited houses, as it is not their responsibility. The verse also reminds them that God is aware of their actions and intentions, whether they are revealed or hidden. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that their ultimate accountability is to God, and that they should act with integrity and sincerity in all their actions, whether they are being observed or not.
orig: ليس عليكم جناح أن تدخلوا بيوتا غير مسكونة فيها متاع لكم والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say to the believing men that they should lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: The verse instructs believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, emphasizing the importance of modesty and self-control. The verse highlights the purity and dignity that comes with such behavior, and serves as a reminder that God is aware of all that humans do, and that their actions have consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم ويحفظوا فروجهم ذلك أزكى لهم إن الله خبير بما يصنعون

translation: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and not to reveal their adornment except to their husbands or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or their sisters, or the women of their religion, or the captives of their hands, or the young boys who have not yet attained knowledge of women's private parts. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And all of you, beg Allah to forgive you all, O believers, that you may be successful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and chastity for believing women. They are instructed to lower their gaze and guard their chastity, and not to reveal their adornment except to specific individuals such as their husbands, fathers, sons, brothers, and certain close relatives. The verse also prohibits them from stamping their feet in a way that reveals their hidden adornment. The verse concludes by encouraging all believers to seek forgiveness from Allah in order to be successful in their faith.
orig: وقل للمؤمنات يغضضن من أبصارهن ويحفظن فروجهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا ما ظهر منها وليضربن بخمرهن على جيوبهن ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا لبعولتهن أو آبائهن أو آباء بعولتهن أو أبنائهن أو أبناء بعولتهن أو إخوانهن أو بني إخوانهن أو بني أخواتهن أو نسائهن أو ما ملكت أيمانهن أو التابعين غير أولي الإربة من الرجال أو الطفل الذين لم يظهروا على عورات النساء ولا يضربن بأرجلهن ليعلم ما يخفين من زينتهن وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your slaves and maidservants. If they be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, Knowing.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to marry the unmarried and the righteous among their slaves and maidservants, emphasizing that poverty is not a barrier to marriage. The verse also assures that God will enrich those who are poor and faithful, indicating that God's blessings and provision are not limited to material wealth. The verse highlights God's knowledge and power to provide for all His creation, and serves as a reminder to believers to trust in God's provision and plan for their lives.
orig: وأنكحوا الأيامى منكم والصالحين من عبادكم وإمائكم إن يكونوا فقراء يغنهم الله من فضله والله واسع عليم

translation: And let not those who do not believe in Allah's favors think that they will escape. Indeed, Allah's punishment will come to them suddenly, or at noon, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse warns those who reject Allah's blessings and refuse to believe in Him, that they should not think they can escape His punishment. The verse emphasizes that Allah's punishment will come unexpectedly, either suddenly or at noon, while they are unaware, indicating that the punishment will be swift and certain. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's favors and reminds them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم على البغاء إن أردن تحصنا لتبتغوا عرض الحياة الدنيا ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, We have sent you clear verses and examples from those who were before you, and a warning for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the verses sent by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also highlights the importance of learning from the examples of those who came before us, both the righteous and the wicked, and the need for fear of God to be a driving force in our lives. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a guidance and a warning for those who are willing to listen and heed its message.
orig: ولقد أنزلنا إليكم آيات مبينات ومثلا من الذين خلوا من قبلكم وموعظة للمتقين

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth, like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass is like a glittering star, kindled from a blessed olive tree, neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil nearly shines out, the oil would have almost shone out, but God willed not but to perfect His light, though the parable of God is as if there were a niche, and within it a lamp, the lamp is the light in the niche, and God is the Guardian of the lamp, He gives light to whom He wills, and God sets forth parables for mankind, and God is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of light to describe God's guidance and the role of faith in guiding humanity. The lamp in the niche represents the light of faith, which is kindled from a blessed olive tree, symbolizing the blessed nature of faith. The glass that surrounds the lamp represents the protective nature of God's guidance, safeguarding the light of faith from being extinguished. The verse emphasizes that God is the source of all light and the guardian of the lamp, and He is the one who gives light to whom He wills. The parable serves as a reminder that God's guidance is available to all, but it is up to the individual to seek it out and embrace it. The verse also highlights the importance of faith in guiding humanity and the role of God's parables in helping people understand and appreciate the beauty and value of faith.
orig: الله نور السماوات والأرض مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة كأنها كوكب دري يوقد من شجرة مباركة زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور يهدي الله لنوره من يشاء ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon humanity, specifically the descendants of Adam. The use of the phrase 'children of Adam' emphasizes the special status that human beings have in the eyes of God, and the fact that they have been honored by God. The verse serves as a reminder of the inherent worth and dignity of every human being, and encourages believers to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life, which is to worship and glorify God.
orig: في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

translation: Men whom neither trade nor sale diverts from the remembrance of Allah and performance of prayer and giving of zakah. They fear a day in which the hearts and eyes will be turned upside down.
interpretation: The verse describes a group of righteous men who are not distracted by worldly pursuits such as trade or business, and instead focus on remembering Allah, performing their prayers, and giving zakah (charity). The verse highlights their fear of a day of reckoning when their hearts and eyes will be turned upside down, indicating a deep sense of accountability and the importance of living a virtuous life.
orig: رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار

translation: May Allah reward them for their deeds, and increase them in His bounty and grace. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer for those who have done good deeds and sought to live a righteous life. The speaker is asking God to reward them for their efforts and to increase His bounty and grace upon them. The verse also emphasizes that God is the ultimate provider and sustainer, and that He provides for whom He wills, without needing to be repaid or asked for account.
orig: ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله والله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: And those who disbelieved - their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. They think they will have water, but indeed, it is a mirage. until they reach it, they will find nothing but God's judgment, and what they have earned will be lost to them.
interpretation: The verse describes the actions of those who disbelieve in God and His punishment. Their deeds are likened to a mirage in the desert, which appears to be a source of water but ultimately leads to nothing. Similarly, those who reject God's message and continue to live in disobedience will find that their efforts are ultimately futile and will lead to nothing but God's judgment. The verse warns against the consequences of disbelief and encourages the reader to recognize the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والذين كفروا أعمالهم كسراب بقيعة يحسبه الظمآن ماء حتى إذا جاءه لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده فوفاه حسابه والله سريع الحساب

translation: Or [consider] the one who passed by a town that was in ruins and said, 'How will God bring it to life after its death?'
interpretation: This verse speaks about a person who sees a town in ruins and questions how God could possibly bring it back to life. The verse serves as a reminder that God has the power to bring life to anything, even something that seems as lifeless as a ruined town. It emphasizes God's ability to revive and restore, and encourages the reader to have faith in God's power and wisdom.
orig: أو كظلمات في بحر لجي يغشاه موج من فوقه موج من فوقه سحاب ظلمات بعضها فوق بعض إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها ومن لم يجعل الله له نورا فما له من نور

translation: And have you not seen that Allah is praised by whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and by the birds, with wings outstretched in the sky? Each knows its prayer and its glorification, and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, as everything in the universe, from the heavens to the earth, and even the birds in the sky, praise and glorify Him. The verse highlights the fact that every creature, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem, has a purpose and a role to play in the grand scheme of things. The verse also underscores Allah's knowledge and awareness of all that occurs in the universe, and serves as a reminder to humanity of the importance of recognizing and acknowledging Allah's greatness and majesty.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسبح له من في السماوات والأرض والطير صافات كل قد علم صلاته وتسبيحه والله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of God over the heavens and the earth, and the fact that all things ultimately belong to Him. The verse also underscores the idea that the ultimate destination of all creation is God, and that everything will eventually return to Him. This verse serves as a reminder of God's power and authority, and the fact that human beings will ultimately be held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وإلى الله المصير

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله ركاما فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد فيصيب به من يشاء ويصرفه عن من يشاء يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار

translation: And Allah alternates the night and the day, indeed in that is a lesson for those who have insight.
interpretation: The verse highlights the cyclical nature of time, with day and night succeeding each other. This cycle is not just a natural phenomenon, but also a reminder for humans to reflect on their actions and turn towards God. The word 'insight' in the verse emphasizes the idea that one needs to be perceptive and reflective to understand the signs of God in the natural world. The verse encourages people to ponder on the meaning of the alternation of day and night, and to use their intellect to comprehend the message behind it.
orig: يقلب الله الليل والنهار إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: And God created all moving living creatures from water. And some of them move on their bellies, and some move on two legs, and some move on four. God creates what He wills. Indeed, God is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and authority as the creator of all living things. It emphasizes that God has created a diverse range of creatures, each with their unique characteristics and abilities. The verse also underscores the idea that God has a plan and purpose for everything He creates, and that He is capable of achieving whatever He wills. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and wisdom in creating and sustaining the universe.
orig: والله خلق كل دابة من ماء فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع يخلق الله ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, We have sent clear signs and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of the signs and messages sent by God, which are clear and easy to understand for those who are willing to listen and follow. The verse also highlights the power of God's guidance, which can lead even the most misguided individuals to the right path, if they allow themselves to be guided. The verse serves as a reminder that God's guidance is available to all, but it is up to the individual to accept and follow it.
orig: لقد أنزلنا آيات مبينات والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And they say, 'We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey'; then a group of them turn away after that, and they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in God and the Messenger, but their actions contradict their words. They obey God's commandments and follow the Messenger's teachings only when it suits them, but they quickly turn away and disregard their beliefs when it no longer serves their interests. The verse warns against such insincerity and emphasizes the importance of consistent belief and obedience to God's commands.
orig: ويقولون آمنا بالله وبالرسول وأطعنا ثم يتولى فريق منهم من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: And when they are told to follow what Allah has revealed, they say, 'We will follow what we found our fathers doing.' Even if their fathers had no knowledge or guidance?
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of some people to blindly follow their ancestors' traditions and beliefs, even if they are contrary to the teachings of Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance and not relying solely on tradition or cultural practices. It is a reminder that true guidance comes from Allah and that it is the responsibility of every individual to seek and follow the truth, regardless of what their ancestors may have believed or practiced.
orig: وإذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم إذا فريق منهم معرضون

translation: And indeed, they have a right to come to Him [i.e., the Prophet] unhindered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the people's access to the Prophet, indicating that they have a right to come to him without any obstacles or barriers. This verse highlights the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and wisdom, and underscores the idea that he is available to all who seek his counsel and guidance. It also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a leader and guide for the community, and serves as a reminder that he is approachable and accessible to all who seek his guidance.
orig: وإن يكن لهم الحق يأتوا إليه مذعنين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفي قلوبهم مرض أم ارتابوا أم يخافون أن يحيف الله عليهم ورسوله بل أولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And the saying of the believers, when they appeal to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is only that they say, 'We have heard and we obey. [May Allah bless us in this world and the Hereafter, and may we be guided to the straight path]' And those are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of the believers when they are faced with conflicts or disputes among themselves. Instead of resorting to violence or worldly means to resolve their differences, they turn to Allah and His Messenger for guidance and judgment. The phrase 'We have heard and we obey' signifies their willingness to submit to Allah's commandments and their acceptance of the guidance provided by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also emphasizes the success and blessings that await those who adopt this approach, both in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is cautious (of His punishment) - those will be the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger, as well as the fear of God's punishment. It emphasizes that those who are mindful of their actions and strive to live righteously will be the ones who will ultimately succeed. The verse serves as a reminder that success is not just limited to worldly gains, but also includes spiritual success and the attainment of God's pleasure. It encourages believers to live a life that is pleasing to God, and to be mindful of their actions and their impact on their relationship with God.
orig: ومن يطع الله ورسوله ويخش الله ويتقه فأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that they would certainly leave (their homes) and go out (to fight) in the morning. But they did not go out, except a few of them.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people swore to Allah that they would leave their homes and go out to fight in the morning. However, only a few of them actually followed through on their promise, while the rest failed to do so. The verse highlights the importance of being truthful and fulfilling one's commitments, as well as the consequences of breaking one's oaths and failing to act on one's convictions.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن أمرتهم ليخرجن قل لا تقسموا طاعة معروفة إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. If you turn away, then upon him is what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And obey the Messenger, but the duty of the Messenger is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger. The verse reminds the believers that they will be held accountable for their actions, just as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will be held accountable for his duty of conveying the message of Islam. The verse also highlights the limitation of the Prophet's role as a messenger, emphasizing that his duty is only to convey the message clearly, without any obligation to enforce it. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to adhere to the teachings of Islam and to follow the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in order to attain guidance and success in this life and the Hereafter.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن تولوا فإنما عليه ما حمل وعليكم ما حملتم وإن تطيعوه تهتدوا وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah has promised those who believe from among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession in the land, just as He granted it to those before them, and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, a security, they will worship Me, and not associate anything with Me. But those who disbelieve after that, they are the wicked ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God to the believers, that they will be granted succession in the land, just like the righteous people before them. The verse also mentions that God will substitute for them, after their fear, a security, indicating that they will be protected and guided by God. The verse also emphasizes that the believers will worship God alone and not associate anything with Him, signifying the importance of monotheism and the rejection of polytheism. The verse ends by stating that those who disbelieve after this promise will be considered wicked.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم الذي ارتضى لهم وليبدلنهم من بعد خوفهم أمنا يعبدونني لا يشركون بي شيئا ومن كفر بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And establish prayer and give zakah, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of establishing a strong spiritual foundation through prayer and giving zakah (charity), and submitting to the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse promises that by doing so, one may receive God's mercy and blessings. The verse highlights the interconnectedness of these three aspects of faith: prayer, charity, and obedience to the Prophet's teachings, and how they lead to spiritual growth and divine mercy.
orig: وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And do not think those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are pleased with their rejection, for they are angered by the Fire, and they will be punished.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who reject the idea of the Hereafter and the accountability in the afterlife. The verse warns them that their rejection of faith will not save them from the punishment of God, which is described as a fierce fire that will anger them. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: لا تحسبن الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض ومأواهم النار ولبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask for exemption from fighting those who have been given a Scripture before you [i.e., Jews and Christians] and do not exceed the limits in the sacred months. Fighting in the sacred months is a violation of the limits, and violating the limits is a great sin. And fight against them a little, and subdue them, and prepare against them whatever you can of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, instructing them not to ask for exemption from fighting against the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) during the sacred months. The verse emphasizes that fighting during these months is a violation of the limits set by God and is considered a great sin. The verse then encourages the believers to fight against their enemies, using whatever means necessary, including preparing weapons and steeds of war, in order to terrify the enemy of Allah and their own enemy. The verse concludes by assuring the believers that whatever they spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to them and they will not be wronged.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليستأذنكم الذين ملكت أيمانكم والذين لم يبلغوا الحلم منكم ثلاث مرات من قبل صلاة الفجر وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ومن بعد صلاة العشاء ثلاث عورات لكم ليس عليكم ولا عليهم جناح بعدهن طوافون عليكم بعضكم على بعض كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات والله عليم حكيم

translation: And when the children among you reach the age of puberty, let them ask for permission as those before them used to ask for permission, thus does Allah make clear His signs for you, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking permission from one's parents or guardians before embarking on any journey or undertaking any significant action. It also highlights the responsibility of parents to guide their children and teach them the value of seeking permission, just as previous generations did. The verse also underscores the idea that Allah's signs and teachings are a guide for believers, and that He is all-knowing and wise in His commands.
orig: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: And the women who are guilty of lewdness, their punishment is that they be imprisoned in a house until death takes them or God ordains for them a way
interpretation: This verse speaks about the punishment for women who are found guilty of lewdness or immoral behavior. The punishment is that they be imprisoned in a house until death takes them or until God ordains a way for them, indicating that they are to be isolated from society and given time to reflect on their actions and repent. The verse highlights the importance of modesty and purity in Islam, and serves as a warning to those who engage in immoral behavior.
orig: والقواعد من النساء اللاتي لا يرجون نكاحا فليس عليهن جناح أن يضعن ثيابهن غير متبرجات بزينة وأن يستعففن خير لهن والله سميع عليم

translation: And there is not upon the blind any guidance, nor upon the blind in the way (of religion); and there is not upon the mute any guidance, nor upon the mute in the way (of religion); and there is not upon the sick any guidance, nor upon the sick in the way (of religion); and there is not upon you any guidance, nor upon you in the way (of religion), that you should eat from the homes of your mothers or the homes of your fathers or the homes of your brothers or the homes of your sisters or the homes of your paternal uncles or the homes of your paternal aunts or the homes of your maternal uncles or the homes of your maternal aunts or the homes of your friends or the homes of your acquaintances, that you may share (the reward) with them in the Hereafter. But in this world, (the reward) will be increased manifold, and blessed is the reward of the Hereafter. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses (and) that you may understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that guidance and spiritual growth are not dependent on one's physical abilities or social status. The blind, mute, and sick are not excluded from the possibility of guidance, and neither are those who are related to them. The verse also highlights the importance of treating others with kindness and respect, as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, 'The believers who have the most perfect faith are those who have the best behavior.' The verse also warns against exploiting others' wealth or properties, and encourages sharing the reward of good deeds with others, as Allah says, 'And whatever good you do, indeed Allah of it (is) seeing.' (Qur'an 22:41) The verse concludes by emphasizing the importance of understanding and reflecting on the Qur'an, as Allah says, 'And indeed, We have sent down to you clear verses and examples from the past, and (We have sent) a messenger to you from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of Allah (and) purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know.' (Qur'an 2:151)
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers who believed in Allah and His Messenger and when they were with him on a collective matter, they did not go away until they asked for permission. Indeed, those who ask for permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So, when they ask for permission, they should ask for permission from those who are entrusted with authority among them and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking permission and respecting authority. Believers should not act unilaterally, but rather seek permission from those in authority, such as their leaders or scholars. This verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and seeking forgiveness from Allah. It reminds believers that they should not act arrogantly, but rather seek guidance and forgiveness from Allah, who is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do not make your calling the Messenger among you as the calling of some of you to others. Allah knows those who sneak away, hiding themselves from the truth. Let those who oppose his command beware, for a trial or a painful punishment may afflict them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and following the Messenger's teachings, and warns against opposing or disobeying him. The verse also highlights the consequences of disobedience, which may include a trial or a painful punishment from God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay true to their faith and to be mindful of the consequences of their actions.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, whatever is in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, and indeed, on the Day of Judgment, they will be returned to Him, and He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over all things, both in the heavens and on earth. It also reminds us that everything we do will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment, and that Allah is All-Knowing and aware of all our actions. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives in accordance with Allah's will and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them in the Hereafter.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And We have sent down the Book to you, [O Muhammad], truthfully, confirming what was before it, and a guardian over the Scriptures,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a confirmation and clarification of the previous scriptures. The Qur'an is considered a guardian or a protector of the scriptures, ensuring that the message of God remains pure and uncorrupted. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a warning to those who reject or distort the message of God.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear authority and a clear victory and a manifest triumph, and We have given you a clear and noble Qur'an as a reminder and a mercy, perhaps you may be mindful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the greatness and power of God, who is the sole owner of the heavens and the earth, and has no son or partner in His kingdom. He is the creator of everything and has predestined all things. The verse also mentions the Qur'an as a clear and noble book, a reminder and a mercy for those who believe and follow its teachings. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to be mindful of God's blessings and to live according to His commandments.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, which create nothing, while they are created themselves, and they do not own for themselves any harm or benefit, and they do not own death or life, or resurrection.
interpretation: The verse describes the foolishness of idolatry, where people worship gods other than Allah, who are themselves created and have no power to harm or benefit themselves. The verse emphasizes that these gods are powerless and cannot even control their own destiny, let alone the fate of their followers.
