orig: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما وجعلني من المرسلين

translation: And indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) miraculous night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and his ascension to the heavens, known as the Isra and Mi'raj. The verse describes the event as a 'clear conquest' and a 'manifest triumph' for the Prophet and the Muslim community. It signifies the significance of the event as a proof of the Prophet's prophethood and the truth of his message. The verse also underscores the idea that the Prophet's journey was not just a physical one, but also a spiritual one, as he was raised to the highest heaven, where he received divine revelation and guidance for his community.
orig: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

translation: Pharaoh said: 'And what is the Lord of the worlds?'
interpretation: Pharaoh's question reflects his arrogance and disbelief in the existence of a higher power. He is questioning the authority and power of the Lord of the worlds, indicating his own lack of submission to a higher authority. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and submission to God.
orig: قال فرعون وما رب العالمين

translation: And the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them indeed, you are being punished.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, and serves as a reminder that those who reject God's message will be punished. The use of the word 'موقنين' (being punished) in the verse indicates that the punishment is ongoing and continuous, signifying that those who reject God's message will be constantly punished until they repent and turn back to Him.
orig: قال رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: And He said to the one who had been blessed: 'What prevents you from prostrating to one whom I have created with My own hands?',
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the angels and asking them why they do not prostrate to Adam, the first human, whom He has created with His own hands. The verse highlights the special status of Adam and the fact that he is a unique creation of God, deserving of respect and obedience. The verse also emphasizes the importance of submission to God's will and the authority of His prophets.
orig: قال لمن حوله ألا تستمعون

translation: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the ancient.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder that God is not only the Lord of the current generation, but also the Lord of past generations. The use of the phrase 'the ancient' emphasizes God's eternal nature and His presence throughout history. The verse serves as a reminder to the readers that they are not the first people to worship God, but rather they are part of a long line of believers who have worshipped God throughout history. It also emphasizes the idea that God's authority and power are not limited by time or generations, but are eternal and all-encompassing.
orig: قال ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: Your messenger is not but a madman.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was accused of being a madman by his enemies. This accusation was likely due to his message of monotheism and the warnings he gave to the people of Mecca about the punishment of God. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's message was not from his own imagination, but was indeed a revelation from God. It also highlights the opposition and ridicule that the Prophet faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam.
orig: قال إن رسولكم الذي أرسل إليكم لمجنون

translation: He said, 'Lord of the east and the west and what is between them, if you are aware.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is addressing God, referring to Him as the Lord of the east and the west, indicating His dominion over all creation. The speaker is acknowledging God's power and authority, suggesting that they are aware of His greatness and majesty. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the importance of recognizing and submitting to His will.
orig: قال رب المشرق والمغرب وما بينهما إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: And if I were to take a god other than Allah, I would surely make you a target of my punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the exclusive nature of Allah's divinity and the consequences of associating partners with Him. The verse warns those who are inclined to worship other deities or entities alongside Allah that they will face His punishment. The use of the first person pronoun 'I' in the verse underscores the personal nature of the warning, as if the speaker is addressing the listener directly. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship, and that associating partners with Him is a grave offense that will not go unpunished.
orig: قال لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال أولو جئتك بشيء مبين

translation: And indeed, I (Muhammad) have come to you (O people of Makkah) with the truth, a clear warner.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is emphasizing the authenticity of his message and his role as a warner to the people of Makkah. The phrase 'min al-sadiqin' (from the truth) suggests that the Prophet's message is based on truth and sincerity, and that he is not deceiving or misleading people. The word 'munthir' (warner) implies that the Prophet's primary role is to warn people of the consequences of their actions and to call them to the right path. The verse highlights the importance of the Prophet's mission and his commitment to conveying the message of Islam to the people, despite the opposition and resistance he faced.
orig: قال فأت به إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And He released him, [from the belly of the fish], at the place where he was [originally] called out.
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when Prophet Jonah was released from the belly of the fish after being inside for three days and nights. The phrase 'at the place where he was [originally] called out' suggests that Jonah was released at the exact spot where he had initially been swallowed by the fish, emphasizing the idea of a full circle. This verse highlights God's power and mercy in saving Jonah from a seemingly impossible situation and serves as a reminder of God's ability to rescue and guide His servants.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the universal nature of the Prophet's message, indicating that his teachings are not limited to a particular group or community, but are rather a blessing for all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse also underscores the significance of the Prophet's compassion and kindness, which serves as a model for believers to emulate in their own lives.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all of humanity. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message, which aims to bring people closer to God and to promote peace, forgiveness, and understanding among all people.
orig: قال للملإ حوله إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: And indeed, We will bring forth the believers and the disbelievers out of the earth, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their knees, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, they will be burned in the Fire. That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'When we are bones and crumbled remains, shall we indeed be raised as a new creation?'
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when both believers and disbelievers will be brought out of their graves and gathered on their knees, unable to speak or hear. They will be judged based on their deeds in life, and those who disbelieved in God's verses will be punished in Hell. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the afterlife and the consequences of disbelief. It also highlights the idea that the resurrection of the dead is a new creation, a transformation from a state of lifelessness to a state of life, and that it is a sign of God's power and mercy.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم بسحره فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said: 'We have been hurt; we have been hurt! Get us a sorcerer, an apostle, or one sent by Us!'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's reaction to the destruction of their town. They are in denial and disbelief, and they ask for a sorcerer, an apostle, or someone sent by God to help them. The verse highlights the people's lack of faith and their unwillingness to accept the reality of their situation. They are more interested in seeking external solutions rather than turning to God for help. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and submission to God, especially in times of hardship.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وابعث في المدائن حاشرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يأتوك بكل سحار عليم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights the universal nature of his message, indicating that it is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a mercy that encompasses all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to this world, but it also encompasses the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and mercy for all people, regardless of their background or beliefs.
orig: فجمع السحرة لميقات يوم معلوم

translation: And He says to the people, 'What! Are you (now) convinced?',
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the people, asking them if they are now convinced of the truth of His message and the reality of the Hereafter. The use of the word 'What!' at the beginning of the verse emphasizes the urgency and importance of the question being asked. The verse serves as a reminder that belief in God and the Hereafter is not just a matter of intellectual assent, but a matter of the heart, requiring a deep-seated conviction and commitment. The verse also highlights the importance of introspection and self-reflection, as individuals are encouraged to examine their own beliefs and actions in light of God's message.
orig: وقيل للناس هل أنتم مجتمعون

translation: And indeed, We have followed the same pattern with the prophets We sent before you. And surely, you will find no change in Our ways.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency of God's ways and the continuity of His message throughout history. The verse suggests that the prophets who came before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were also sent by God and that their message was similar to his. The verse also serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not the first prophet to be sent by God, and that he is part of a long line of prophets who were all sent to convey the same message of submission to God. The verse also emphasizes that God's ways do not change, and that His message remains the same throughout history.
orig: لعلنا نتبع السحرة إن كانوا هم الغالبين

translation: And when the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh: 'Surely we shall have a reward for our skill, if we are the prevailing ones.'
interpretation: The verse describes the encounter between the sorcerers and Pharaoh, where they boastfully claim that they will receive a reward for their magic skills if they emerge victorious. The verse highlights the arrogance and self-assurance of the sorcerers, who are confident in their abilities and believe that they will be rewarded for their skills. The verse also underscores the theme of competition and rivalry, as the sorcerers seek to outdo Moses and Aaron in a display of magical prowess.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قالوا لفرعون أئن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the special status that humans have been given, which sets them apart from other creatures. This verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with this honor, and encourages humans to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life, which is to worship and obey God.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم إذا لمن المقربين

translation: And Moses said to them, 'Cast down what you have in your hands, O sons of Israel!',
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is commanding the Israelites to throw down their idols and other objects of worship that they have in their hands, signifying their willingness to turn away from their false deities and worship only Allah. The verse highlights Moses' leadership and his role as a prophet who is guiding his people towards the right path. It also underscores the importance of recognizing and rejecting false idols and focusing one's devotion solely on Allah.
orig: قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: And they rejected them, and their arrogance, and said: 'We are the exalted ones, we will not be overcome.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people of Pharaoh when Moses and Aaron came to them with a message from God. The people rejected the message and became arrogant, boasting that they were superior and would not be defeated. The verse highlights the dangers of pride and arrogance, as well as the tendency of people to reject the truth and resist the call to submit to a higher power. It serves as a warning to believers to avoid these traits and to remain humble and open to God's guidance.
orig: فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم وقالوا بعزة فرعون إنا لنحن الغالبون

translation: And Moses threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, manifesting what they were concealing.
interpretation: The verse describes the miraculous transformation of Moses' staff into a serpent, which symbolizes the power and authority given to him by God. The phrase 'manifesting what they were concealing' suggests that the serpent represented the inner truth and reality of the people's hearts, which were full of disbelief and rebellion against God's commandments. The verse highlights the significance of God's signs and miracles in revealing the truth and exposing the falsehood, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and disobeying His commands.
orig: فألقى موسى عصاه فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: And they were followed by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Evil is the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. The 'curse' mentioned in the verse refers to the punishment that those who disbelieve in God and engage in wrongdoing will face, both in this life and on the Day of Resurrection. The verse emphasizes the idea that the ultimate end of those who choose to reject God's guidance and engage in evil actions is a negative one, and serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief and sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning back to God.
orig: فألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and we have obeyed His messenger.,
interpretation: In this verse, the believers declare their faith in the one true God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and their obedience to His Messenger, acknowledging his authority and submitting to his guidance. This declaration of faith serves as a witness to their belief in the oneness of God and their commitment to follow the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands as the foundation of a believer's relationship with God.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people! You have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. Turn to your Creator and kill yourselves, that He may forgive you.' And that is the nearest [way] to your Lord.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is urging his people to repent and turn to God for forgiveness. He tells them to abandon their worship of the golden calf, which they had created, and to seek forgiveness from God. The phrase 'kill yourselves' is a metaphorical expression, indicating that they should sacrifice their own ego and desires in order to seek forgiveness. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and seeking forgiveness from God, and serves as a reminder that the closest way to God is through turning to Him in repentance and seeking His forgiveness.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest triumph. For Allah has returned you to your enemy, and We have sufficed for you in the manpower. And We have restrained their hands from you, and their feet, that they may not cross over into your land, and We have destroyed their bridges. And if they had come to you, they would have been disciplined. Indeed, We have destroyed them, and theirs is a clear defeat.
interpretation: This verse describes the victory of the Muslims over their enemies, which is seen as a manifestation of God's power and a sign of His favor towards the believers. The verse emphasizes that the victory was not due to the Muslims' own strength or numbers, but rather due to God's intervention and support. The verse also highlights the complete defeat of the enemies, who were unable to even approach the Muslims' land, and their destruction is described as a clear and decisive victory. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the importance of relying on Him in times of struggle.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلسوف تعلمون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, 'We have been oppressed. Surely, to our Lord we will return.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's recognition of their oppression and their acknowledgment that they will return to their Lord. The verse implies that the people have been suffering from injustice and oppression, and they have come to the realization that their only hope for relief is to turn to their Lord and seek His justice. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the ultimate authority and that those who are oppressed should turn to Him for help and relief.
orig: قالوا لا ضير إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, for we were the first of those who believed.
interpretation: This verse expresses the hope of the believers that God will forgive their sins, acknowledging that they were the first to believe in Him and His Messenger. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the belief in the mercy and forgiveness of God. It also underscores the idea that faith is not a guarantee of salvation, but rather a means to seek forgiveness and to live a righteous life.
orig: إنا نطمع أن يغفر لنا ربنا خطايانا أن كنا أول المؤمنين

translation: And We inspired to Moses, 'Strike the sea with your staff', and it split, and each part became a tremendous mountain.
interpretation: The verse describes the miracle of Moses striking the sea with his staff, which resulted in the sea splitting and creating a path for the Israelites to cross safely. The use of the phrase 'a tremendous mountain' emphasizes the magnitude of the miracle and the power of God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's ability to overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles and the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي إنكم متبعون

translation: So Pharaoh sent gatherers to the cities,
interpretation: Pharaoh, the ruler of Egypt, sent out people to gather the Israelites who were living in the cities, in order to persecute and oppress them. This verse highlights the tyranny and oppression that the Israelites faced in Egypt, and foreshadows the events that led to their eventual liberation by Moses.
orig: فأرسل فرعون في المدائن حاشرين

translation: Indeed, those who have been indulging in evil deeds will be punished.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who have been engaging in evil deeds will face punishment. The word ' Indeed' at the beginning of the verse suggests that this is a certainty and not a matter of doubt. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were unjust, and We have made their destruction a lesson for those who are aware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust, emphasizing that their destruction served as a lesson for those who are aware of God's power and justice. The verse underscores the idea that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of people's actions. The use of the word 'lagha'iz' (lesson) suggests that the destruction of these towns is not just a punishment, but also a teaching moment for those who are willing to learn and repent.
orig: وإنهم لنا لغائظون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while they were wrongdoers, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse stresses the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وإنا لجميع حاذرون

translation: And We have brought them out from gardens and springs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt, where they were surrounded by gardens and springs. The verse emphasizes the idea of God's favor and provision for His people, as He brought them out of a place of abundance and luxury. The image of gardens and springs also symbolizes the idea of spiritual nourishment and growth, indicating that God's blessings are not limited to material prosperity but also extend to spiritual sustenance.
orig: فأخرجناهم من جنات وعيون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and success granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. The phrase 'clear conquest' refers to the decisive victory at the Battle of Mecca, which marked the beginning of the spread of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula. The phrase 'manifest triumph' refers to the ultimate triumph of Islam and its spread to all corners of the world. The verse emphasizes the idea that the success of the Muslims is a result of God's favor and support, and serves as a reminder to the believers to remain grateful and obedient to God.
orig: وكنوز ومقام كريم

translation: And We have made the descendants of Israel inherit what was said to them.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the inheritance of the descendants of Israel, which refers to the promises and blessings that God bestowed upon them. The verse highlights the idea that the Israelites were chosen by God to inherit the land of Canaan and to be a light unto the nations, spreading God's message and teachings to the world. The verse serves as a reminder of God's covenant with the Israelites and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها بني إسرائيل

translation: And follow them, O Muhammad, and say, 'I am with you; indeed, I am, before you, of those who warn.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to follow the previous prophets and messengers who came before him, and to proclaim that he is with them in spirit and in their mission to guide people to the truth and warn them against falsehood. The verse emphasizes the continuity of the prophetic message and the unity of the prophets in their call to righteousness and obedience to God. It also highlights the important role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a warner and guide for his people.
orig: فأتبعوهم مشرقين

translation: And when the two groups saw each other, the companions of Moses said: 'We are sure to be overtaken.'
interpretation: The verse describes the moment when the Israelites, led by Moses, saw the approaching army of Pharaoh and felt certain that they would be overwhelmed. The verse highlights the fear and uncertainty of the Israelites, who had been oppressed for centuries and were now facing the powerful army of their oppressors. The verse serves as a reminder of the struggles that the Israelites faced and the hopelessness they felt in the face of their oppressors. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and trust in God, as Moses and his companions ultimately trusted in God's plan and were saved from Pharaoh's army.
orig: فلما تراءى الجمعان قال أصحاب موسى إنا لمدركون

translation: And my Lord will guide me to a Straight Path.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his faith in God's guidance. He acknowledges that his Lord will guide him to the right path, indicating his trust in God's wisdom and providence. The verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance from God and relying on Him for support and direction in life. It also emphasizes the belief in the Hereafter and the desire to live a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: قال كلا إن معي ربي سيهدين

translation: And We inspired to Moses: 'Strike the sea with your staff', and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain.
interpretation: The verse describes the miraculous event where Moses was instructed by God to strike the sea with his staff, which caused the sea to part and create a path for the Israelites to cross safely. The verse emphasizes the immense power of God and the faith of Moses in following God's command. The image of the parted sea is also symbolic of the power of faith and obedience to God, as it shows how seemingly insurmountable obstacles can be overcome with divine intervention. The verse serves as a reminder of God's ability to overcome any challenge, and the importance of faith and obedience in achieving success.
orig: فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق فكان كل فرق كالطود العظيم

translation: And We have destroyed the likes of them, (i.e., the towns), then they (the people) cried out when there was no longer time for escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetition of history, where nations before were destroyed due to their sins and injustices. The use of ' Azalafna' (And We have destroyed) in the past tense emphasizes God's power and authority in annihilating those who disobey Him. The phrase 'then they cried out' signifies the remorse and regret of those who realized their mistakes when it was too late, serving as a warning to future generations. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is inescapable and that one should repent before it's too late.
orig: وأزلفنا ثم الآخرين

translation: And We saved Moses and those with him, all together.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses and his followers, who were saved by God from the Pharaoh and his army. The verse emphasizes the unity of the believers, indicating that they were all saved together, suggesting a sense of community and solidarity among the believers. The verse also highlights God's power and mercy in saving His chosen people, and serves as a reminder of God's promise to protect and guide those who believe in Him.
orig: وأنجينا موسى ومن معه أجمعين

translation: And then We drowned the others.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the people who were not destroyed in the previous verse. The use of the word 'others' indicates that the people being referred to were different from the ones destroyed in the previous verse. The verb 'drowned' suggests a sudden and violent end, emphasizing the power and finality of God's judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the inevitability of God's justice.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign and most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the destruction of the unjust towns serves as a sign for those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The phrase 'most of them were not believers' implies that the majority of the people in these towns were not followers of the Islamic faith, and therefore, were not spared from God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the importance of turning towards God and living a righteous life.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Free of Need, the Generous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attribute of being free of need, indicating that He is self-sufficient and does not require anything from anyone. The description of God as 'Generous' highlights His generosity and bounty towards His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is the ultimate source of provision and that He is the one who provides for all of His creation. It also encourages believers to emulate God's generosity and be generous towards others, as this is a quality that is pleasing to God.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And We gave them a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Abraham and his followers. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies a decisive and unambiguous triumph, while 'manifest triumph' implies a victory that is evident and clear for all to see. The verse highlights the blessings and favors bestowed upon Abraham and his followers, and serves as a reminder of God's power and grace.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم

translation: And when he said to his father and his people, 'What do you worship?',
interpretation: The verse highlights the question posed by Prophet Abraham to his father and his people, which serves as a powerful critique of idolatry and the worship of false deities. By questioning the very foundation of their beliefs, Abraham challenges his people to reflect on their misguided ways and consider the possibility of a single, all-powerful Creator. The verse emphasizes the importance of questioning one's beliefs and seeking guidance from God, rather than blindly following tradition and cultural norms.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما تعبدون

translation: They said, 'We will not cease to worship our idols, for they are our intercessors.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's refusal to give up their idols, which they believed were their intercessors and would intercede on their behalf. The verse highlights the people's misconception about the role of idols and their false belief that idols could intercede on their behalf. The verse serves as a warning against idolatry and the false hope that idols can provide salvation or protection.
orig: قالوا نعبد أصناما فنظل لها عاكفين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون

translation: Or He would have tormented them with a painful doom, (and they would have been) expelled from their homes.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of disobedience and disbelief. The phrase 'Or He would have tormented them' suggests that God's punishment is a consequence of human action, and it is not an arbitrary or unjust act. The 'painful doom' refers to the suffering that will befall those who disobey God, and the phrase 'expelled from their homes' suggests a complete upheaval of their lives. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires.
orig: أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون

translation: They said, 'We found our fathers astray, so we followed in their footsteps.
interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the disbelievers when they were asked about their reasons for not following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They admitted that they were following the ways of their ancestors, implying that they were continuing the practices of their forefathers, even though they knew they were misguided. The verse highlights the tendency of people to blindly follow the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors, even if they are wrong, and the need to question and challenge such beliefs in the light of reason and revelation.
orig: قالوا بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the companions of the elephant, who were destroyed by God for their arrogance and refusal to believe in the prophet Jonah. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God and the consequences of rejecting His message. The use of the phrase "Have you not seen" emphasizes the importance of learning from past examples and the warning signs that God has given to humanity through history.
orig: قال أفرأيتم ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your ancient ancestors.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of the ancient ancestors of the disbelievers who rejected the prophets and messengers sent by God. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that they are not superior to their ancestors and that they will also face the consequences of their actions if they continue to reject God's message.
orig: أنتم وآباؤكم الأقدمون

translation: And indeed, they were enemies to me, but not the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet's (peace be upon him) response to those who rejected him and plotted against him. He acknowledges that they were his enemies, but he also recognizes that they were not the Lord of the worlds, implying that their power and authority were limited and that they would ultimately be held accountable by the One who is the true Lord of the worlds. The verse serves as a reminder that true power and authority belong to God alone, and that those who reject and oppose His message will ultimately be brought to justice.
orig: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين

translation: And He who created me guides me
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the creator of all things, including humans, is also the one who guides and directs them. It emphasizes the idea that God is not just a creator who set the universe in motion and then stepped back, but rather He is actively involved in guiding and directing His creation. This verse serves as a reminder that God is always present and actively involved in our lives, guiding us towards righteousness and justice.
orig: الذي خلقني فهو يهدين

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His ability to be with His creation at all times. The verse is a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, reminding them that they are never alone and that God is always with them, watching over them and guiding them. The verse also serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with knowing that God is always present, encouraging believers to live their lives in accordance with His will and to strive for righteousness in all their actions.
orig: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

translation: And when I am ill, He (God) heals me.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the close relationship between the speaker and God. The speaker recognizes that God is the one who heals them when they are ill, indicating a deep trust and dependence on God's power and mercy. The verse also highlights the idea that God's healing is not just physical, but also spiritual, as it is a manifestation of His love and care for His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to turn to God in times of need and to trust in His ability to heal and guide them.
orig: وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His constant watchfulness over His creation. It assures believers that God is always with them, no matter where they are or what they are going through. The verse is a source of comfort and reassurance, reminding believers that they are never alone and that God is always aware of their circumstances. It also serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and thoughts, as God is always watching and aware of all that we do.
orig: والذي يميتني ثم يحيين

translation: And whoever hopes for forgiveness from his Lord should do so before the time when the punishment comes to him, for then there will be no escape for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from God before it's too late. The verse suggests that once the punishment comes, there will be no escape or chance for forgiveness. It serves as a reminder to those who have committed sins and injustices to seek forgiveness and repent before they face the consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of God, who is willing to forgive those who seek forgiveness and turn to Him.
orig: والذي أطمع أن يغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين

translation: My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God for wisdom and righteousness. The speaker is seeking guidance and knowledge from God, and asking to be counted among the righteous. The verse highlights the importance of wisdom and righteousness in one's life, and serves as a reminder that true guidance and wisdom come from God alone.
orig: رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: And make me a tongue of truth in the hereafter.
interpretation: The verse is a supplication made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to God, asking Him to make his tongue a source of truth in the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of speaking the truth and being truthful, not just in words but also in actions. It serves as a reminder that our words and actions will be judged on the Day of Judgment, and that we should strive to live a life of honesty and integrity.
orig: واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين

translation: And make me among the heirs of the Garden of Bliss.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) supplication to God to make him one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss (Jannah). The verse highlights the Prophet's longing for the blessings and happiness of the afterlife, and his desire to be among those who will inherit the eternal reward of Paradise. It serves as a reminder to believers to strive for righteousness and obedience to God, in the hope of attaining a similar reward in the Hereafter.
orig: واجعلني من ورثة جنة النعيم

translation: And forgive my father, indeed he was of those who strayed.
interpretation: The verse is a request made by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to God, seeking forgiveness for his father, Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who did not accept Islam during his lifetime. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness for one's parents and loved ones, even after they have passed away. It also underscores the idea that guidance and forgiveness are ultimately in God's hands, and that even the Prophets and their families are not immune to misguidance and sin. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek forgiveness for their loved ones and to pray for their guidance, even after they have passed away.
orig: واغفر لأبي إنه كان من الضالين

translation: And do not be grieved on their account, the Day they shall meet their Lord, (it will be) a Day when they will be scattered and turned into dust.
interpretation: The verse tells the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be sad or grieved on the Day of Judgment when the wicked people will be punished. The Day will be a day of reckoning when everyone will be gathered and judged according to their deeds. The verse emphasizes that the wicked will be scattered and turned into dust, indicating their utter destruction and lack of power in front of God's wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in sin, reminding them of the Day of Reckoning and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولا تخزني يوم يبعثون

translation: A day in which wealth and children will not benefit, except those who come to Allah in a state of submission.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance of living a life of submission to God, as it is the only way to truly benefit from one's wealth and children. On the Day of Judgment, material possessions and family will not be of any use to those who have not lived according to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's relationship with God and live a life of righteousness, as it is the only way to truly prosper.
orig: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون

translation: Except for those who come to God with a sincere heart.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to the general rule of God's punishment for those who are unjust. The verse emphasizes that those who have a sincere heart and turn to God in devotion are spared from the punishment. The phrase 'qalb salim' means a heart that is sound, pure, and free from any defects. It refers to those who have a genuine desire to seek God's guidance and are willing to submit to His will. The verse serves as a reminder that God is merciful and that those who seek Him with sincerity will be protected from His wrath.
orig: إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the special status that humans have been given, which sets them apart from other creatures. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with this honor and the need for humans to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life, which is to worship and obey God.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين

translation: And the Hell-fire will be brought forth for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to disbelieve. The Hell-fire is a place of intense suffering and punishment, and it is reserved for those who have denied the truth and refused to submit to God's will. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم للغاوين

translation: And they were told: 'Where is what you used to worship?',
interpretation: The verse is addressing the people who were previously worshiping idols and false deities. The question 'Where is what you used to worship?' is a reminder that the idols they worshiped have failed to provide them with any help or support in their time of need. The verse serves as a reminder that only Allah, the one true God, is worthy of worship and that all other forms of worship are futile and misguided.
orig: وقيل لهم أين ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: And who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and uniqueness of God, highlighting the fact that no one can intercede with Him or mediate on behalf of others without His permission. It underscores God's sovereignty and power, reminding believers that all intercession and supplication should be directed to Him alone.
orig: من دون الله هل ينصرونكم أو ينتصرون

translation: So they denied them, and they were turned away. And Allah's punishment came to them from where they did not expect.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation where the people denied the warning signs and messengers sent by God, and as a result, they were turned away from the right path. The punishment from God came to them unexpectedly, indicating that they were not prepared for it and had no chance to repent or make amends. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكبكبوا فيها هم والغاوون

translation: And the soldiers of Iblis, all of them, were gathered.
interpretation: The verse describes the gathering of the soldiers of Iblis (Satan), indicating that they are united in their opposition to God and their desire to lead humans astray. The use of the word 'junood' (soldiers) emphasizes the idea that they are a well-organized and formidable force, determined to spread evil and corruption. The verse serves as a reminder of the constant struggle between good and evil, and the need for believers to remain vigilant and steadfast in their faith.
orig: وجنود إبليس أجمعون

translation: And they say, 'We will not believe you until you break open for us from the earth a spring, or you have a garden of date palms and grapes, and you make rivers flow through it.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers' demand for a miracle from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a condition for their belief. They ask him to bring forth a spring or a garden of date palms and grapes, and to make rivers flow through it, as a proof of his prophethood. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the people, who were unwilling to accept the message of Islam without tangible proof. It also underscores the idea that true belief cannot be based on material signs or miracles, but rather on faith and submission to God's will.
orig: قالوا وهم فيها يختصمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, but they did not believe in their Messengers, so We punished them in this world, and certainly the punishment of the Hereafter will be more severe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repetitive nature of human history, where each generation is tested with the message of the prophets, but often rejects it, leading to their destruction. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them of the consequences of rejecting the message of the prophets, and the severity of the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter if they continue to reject the message.
orig: تالله إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the day when the sky will be like murky oil and the mountains will be like wool.
interpretation: The verse warns of an impending punishment that is near, describing a scene of a dark and gloomy sky and mountains that resemble wool. The imagery suggests a day of reckoning, when the world will be turned upside down and the wicked will be punished. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have been warned, to turn back to God and mend their ways before it's too late.
orig: إذ نسويكم برب العالمين

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were the ones who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the destruction of the unjust towns was not a result of God's injustice, but rather it was a consequence of their own actions. The phrase 'wronging themselves' implies that they brought destruction upon themselves through their own choices and deeds. The verse highlights the idea of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions, and serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: وما أضلنا إلا المجرمون

translation: And what is left for us from the Shāfiʿīs?
interpretation: The verse is a question that asks what is left for the believers from the Shāfiʿīs, indicating that the Shāfiʿīs have been exhausted or depleted in some way. The verse can be interpreted as a commentary on the state of the Muslim community at the time, suggesting that the community has been drained of its spiritual vitality and is in need of revitalization.
orig: فما لنا من شافعين

translation: And no friend will be of avail, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that in the hereafter, people will be alone and no friend or relative will be able to help or avail them. It highlights the fact that in the afterlife, everyone will be judged based on their own deeds and no one will be able to intercede or interfere with God's judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the individual's responsibility and accountability before God and the futility of relying on worldly relationships in the face of divine justice.
orig: ولا صديق حميم

translation: And if we had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with those who disbelieve and oppose His command. Despite their rebellion, God does not immediately punish them in this life. Instead, He gives them respite, allowing them to reflect and repent. The verse suggests that the punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe than any punishment that could be inflicted in this life. It serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will face a severe reckoning in the Hereafter.
orig: فلو أن لنا كرة فنكون من المؤمنين

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign and most of them were not believers.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the destruction of the unjust towns is a sign of God's power and justice, and that the majority of the people who lived in those towns did not believe in God's message and were therefore deserving of punishment. The verse highlights the idea that the punishment is not just a random event, but a deliberate act of God's justice, intended to serve as a warning to those who reject faith.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Free of need, the Generous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's self-sufficiency and generosity. The description of God as 'Free of need' means that He is independent of all creation and does not require anything from them. At the same time, He is also 'Generous', bestowing His favors and blessings upon all creation without any expectation of return or compensation. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that their worship and obedience to God should stem from a deep sense of gratitude for His blessings, rather than any expectation of personal gain or reward.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And Noah's people, they denied the messengers,
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people of Prophet Noah and their denial of the messengers sent by God. The verse highlights their arrogance and disbelief, which led them to reject the message of the prophets and ultimately face the wrath of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين

translation: And Noah said to his people, 'Do not be wicked, fear God, and obey me.'
interpretation: In this verse, Noah is urging his people to refrain from evil deeds and to fear God. He is also emphasizing the importance of obeying him as a prophet and messenger of God. Noah's message is not just a call to worship God but also a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a righteous life. The verse highlights the leadership role of Noah and his responsibility to guide his people towards the right path.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم نوح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a trustworthy messenger of God. The word 'amin' (trustworthy) highlights the Prophet's integrity and reliability in conveying God's message to humanity. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to trust and follow the Prophet's teachings, as he is the chosen one by God to guide humanity to the right path.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away, then Our Messenger has delivered what he was sent with, and Allah will suffice him from you. And Allah will not hold you accountable for what you are forgetful of.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger. The verse indicates that the Prophet has delivered the message and fulfilled his duty, and now it is up to the people to choose to obey or disobey. The verse also reminds the believers that Allah will not hold them accountable for what they are forgetful of, indicating that Allah is aware of human limitations and that He will not punish people for things that are beyond their control.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And what I ask you to spend (in God's cause) is not but a small compensation for what He has given you, and Allah is of infinite worth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that what God has given us is far greater than what we can ever give back to Him. The verse encourages us to spend in God's cause, but not out of obligation or duty, but rather as a small token of gratitude for all that He has given us. The verse also highlights the infinite worth of God, indicating that our efforts to please Him are but a small fraction of what He truly deserves.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away, then Our Messenger has already fulfilled his duty.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger. The use of the word 'fa'taqoo' (وأطيعون) which means 'therefore obey' or 'so obey', indicates that obeying God and His Messenger is a natural consequence of recognizing and acknowledging their authority. The verse also highlights the Prophet's role as a messenger and his responsibility to convey the message, and that he has fulfilled his duty regardless of whether people choose to accept or reject it.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And they say, 'We believe in it; indeed, we will follow the religion of our fathers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to accept Islam. They claimed to believe in the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions, but they were not sincere in their belief. They wanted to follow their ancestral religion, which was polytheism, instead of submitting to the one true God. The verse highlights the contradiction in their statement, as they claim to believe but still insist on following their ancestors' religion. It serves as a warning to those who claim to believe in God but do not follow His commands, and it emphasizes the importance of following the truth and not just following tradition for tradition's sake.
orig: قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, their reckoning is only with my Lord, if you could perceive.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the ultimate judgment and accountability for the disbelievers' actions will be with God alone. The phrase 'if you could perceive' suggests that the true nature of their reckoning is beyond human comprehension, and that it is only God who can fully understand and judge their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of one's actions will be faced ultimately by the individual, and that God is the ultimate authority who will judge and recompense accordingly.
orig: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون

translation: And I (God) will certainly keep hidden (the sins of) the believers, those who have been brought near (to Me).
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's promise to protect the sins of the believers who have been brought near to Him. The verse emphasizes God's mercy and forgiveness towards those who have faith in Him and live righteously. The phrase 'those who have been brought near' refers to those who have achieved a close spiritual relationship with God through their belief and good deeds. The verse serves as a comfort and reassurance to believers that their sins will be forgiven and hidden from public view, and that God will protect their privacy and dignity.
orig: وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

translation: Indeed, I am a clear warner.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a clear and distinct warner to his people. The word 'clear' suggests that the message he is conveying is free from any ambiguity or obscurity, and that it is plainly visible to those who are willing to see. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's mission is not to force people to believe, but rather to convey the message of Islam in the clearest possible terms, leaving the decision to believe or not to the individual.
orig: إن أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: They said, 'We will not stop, O Noah, until we have been drowned or become Muslims.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers to Prophet Noah's message, warning them of the impending flood. The disbelievers, determined to reject God's message, told Prophet Noah that they would not stop opposing him until they were either drowned or forced to convert to Islam. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject God's message and their reluctance to submit to His will. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of submitting to His will.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح لتكونن من المرجومين

translation: My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Moses is speaking to God, saying that his people have denied him and refused to believe in his message. The verse highlights the struggle that prophets often face in their mission to spread God's word, and the sadness and frustration that comes with it. It also underscores the importance of perseverance and faith in the face of adversity, as Moses continues to turn to God for guidance and support despite the rejection he faces from his people.
orig: قال رب إن قومي كذبون

translation: And He opened up between them and between the believers a door of mutual hate and enmity and they were enemies. And God guides not the disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the division between the believers and the disobedient people. The phrase 'door of mutual hate and enmity' suggests a complete breakdown of relations between the two groups, with no possibility of reconciliation. The verse emphasizes that God does not guide those who disobey Him, indicating that they are on a path that is opposite to the will of God. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to disobey God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين

translation: Then We saved him and those with him, in the laden ark.
interpretation: The verse describes the story of Prophet Noah and his salvation from the flood. The use of the word 'ark' emphasizes the idea of safety and protection, as the ark was a means of rescue for Noah and his companions. The verse highlights God's power and mercy in saving the righteous believers, even in the face of destruction and chaos. It serves as a reminder of God's promise to protect and guide those who follow His commands.
orig: فأنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك المشحون

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of the people who were not destroyed by the flood. Instead of learning from the lesson of the flood and turning to God, they continued to live in disobedience and were eventually destroyed. The verse emphasizes the completeness of God's judgment, leaving no one behind, and serves as a warning to those who refuse to heed the lessons of history.
orig: ثم أغرقنا بعد الباقين

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign, but most of them do not believe.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the destruction of the unjust towns serves as a sign of God's power and justice, but despite this, many people continue to disbelieve and reject the message of the Qur'an. The verse highlights the irony of the situation, where the people who are being punished are the ones who should be most aware of God's power and justice, yet they continue to reject the message and persist in their disbelief.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Free of all imperfections, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attribute of being free from all imperfections and His merciful nature. The use of the word 'وإن' (and indeed) at the beginning of the verse suggests a sense of certainty and emphasis on the attribute of God being described. The adjectives 'العزيز' (the Free of all imperfections) and 'الرحيم' (the Merciful) both describe God's nature, highlighting His power and mercy. This verse serves as a reminder to believers of God's greatness and His role as a source of guidance and protection.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كذبت عاد المرسلين

translation: And he said to them, 'I am the one who warns you of a punishment like the punishment of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the warning given by Prophet Lot to his people, who were engaged in homosexuality and other immoral acts. The warning is a reminder that God's punishment can come at any moment, just as it did to the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were destroyed for their sins. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are living in sin, that they must repent and turn to God, lest they face a similar fate.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a trustworthy messenger of God. orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون

translation: And you will be turned into fuel for hell, you and your idols, and you will be punished in the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and instead worship idols. They will be cast into hell, along with their idols, and will be punished eternally in the Fire. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who reject God's message will have no helpers or allies to save them from the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

translation: And when you slew them, you slew them (in such a way) as if you were killing them not (in anger), but Allah has made it to be a source of sorrow for you
interpretation: The verse refers to the slaying of the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) by the disbelievers. The verse highlights the gravity of their actions and its impact on the believers. The phrase 'you slew them' is used to emphasize the brutality of the act, and the fact that it was done without any justification or cause. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the killing was not done out of anger or self-defense, but rather as a result of hatred and oppression. The final part of the verse 'Allah has made it to be a source of sorrow for you' serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that their actions will have severe consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away, then Our Messenger has only been commanded to convey clearly.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger. The phrase 'fatq' (فاتقوا) which means 'therefore obey' is used to emphasize the urgency of the command. The verse also indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been commanded by God to convey the message clearly, indicating that the responsibility of the Prophet is to deliver the message, but it is up to the people to choose to obey or disobey.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And fear the One who has given you knowledge.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God, the one who has given us knowledge and the ability to understand and interpret the signs of nature and the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder that knowledge is a blessing from God and should be used for good and not for evil. It also highlights the responsibility that comes with knowledge and the need to use it wisely, lest one be held accountable for their actions.
orig: واتقوا الذي أمدكم بما تعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'an-naṣr' (the victory) is used to describe a decisive and clear victory, while 'al-fatḥ' (the manifest triumph) suggests a victory that is evident and obvious to all. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: أمدكم بأنعام وبنين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all of humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to guide people to the right path and to bring them closer to God. It also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role in bringing people together and spreading love, peace, and harmony among them.
orig: وجنات وعيون

translation: I fear for you the punishment of a great day.
interpretation: The verse expresses the Prophet Muhammad's fear for his people, who were not heeding his warnings and continued to live in disobedience to God's commands. The 'great day' refers to the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be judged according to their deeds in this life. The verse serves as a warning to believers to live a righteous life and to be mindful of the consequences of their actions, lest they face the wrath of God on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, 'Let us summon a witness from among our men, and you may not be blamed.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who are trying to avoid blame and responsibility for their actions. They suggest calling a witness from among their own men to testify on their behalf, implying that they do not trust their own words and actions and feel the need for external validation. The verse highlights the theme of accountability and the tendency of humans to shift blame and avoid taking responsibility for their mistakes.
orig: قالوا سواء علينا أوعظت أم لم تكن من الواعظين

translation: Indeed, this is the creation of the first ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of the first human beings, Adam and Eve. The phrase 'first ones' refers to their status as the first humans to be created by God. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of their creation, highlighting the power and wisdom of God in bringing them into existence. The verse also serves as a reminder of the unique role that humans have in the eyes of God, as the first and most important of all His creations.
orig: إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a mercy and a guide, and highlights the importance of compassion, forgiveness, and kindness in the spreading of God's message.
orig: وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكذبوه فأهلكناهم إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Free of need, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attribute of being free of need, indicating that He is self-sufficient and does not require anything from His creation. The phrase 'ar-rahman ar-rahim' (the Most Merciful) highlights God's mercy and compassion towards His creation, and serves as a reminder that God's mercy is all-encompassing and available to all who turn to Him. The verse as a whole underscores the idea that God's sovereignty and mercy are intertwined, and that He is the ultimate source of guidance and support for those who seek it.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كذبت ثمود المرسلين

translation: And when their brother Salih said to them, 'Will you not fear Allah?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Prophet Salih and his people, who were warned by Salih to fear God and mend their ways. The verse highlights the importance of listening to wise counsel and admonition, especially when it comes from a righteous and knowledgeable person like Salih. It also underscores the responsibility of the prophets and righteous individuals to guide their communities towards the right path and warn them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم صالح ألا تتقون

translation: Verily, I am a trustworthy messenger to you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a trustworthy messenger of God. The word 'amin' in Arabic, translated as 'trustworthy', conveys the idea of reliability, sincerity, and authenticity. The verse is a declaration of the Prophet's integrity and his commitment to convey the message of God without any alteration or manipulation. It is a reminder to the believers to have faith in the Prophet's message and to trust in his guidance.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away, then Our messenger has only been commanded to convey clearly.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger. The use of the word 'fatq' (فاتق) which means 'therefore' or 'so' indicates a cause and effect relationship between obeying God and His Messenger and the consequences of not doing so. The verse warns that if one turns away from this command, the Messenger's duty is only to convey the message clearly, and the responsibility for the person's disobedience falls on their own shoulders.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And what I ask you to spend on me is nothing but a small part of what I have created for you, and what I have created for you is nothing but a small part of what I own.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the rewards that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) receives for his efforts in spreading God's message are insignificant compared to the greatness of God's creation and the rewards that He has prepared for those who believe and do good deeds. The verse also highlights the idea that everything in the universe, including the Prophet's rewards, belongs to God and is a small part of His vast creation.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين
