The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما جاءت قيل أهكذا عرشك قالت كأنه هو وأوتينا العلم من قبلها وكنا مسلمين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while they were unjust, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of injustice and disobedience to God. The use of the phrase 'وصدها' (wasadaha) emphasizes the completeness and finality of the destruction, indicating that the towns were utterly destroyed and left desolate. The phrase 'من دون الله' (min doon Allah) suggests that the people of these towns had turned away from God and were living in disobedience to Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the need to turn back to Him.
orig: وصدها ما كانت تعبد من دون الله إنها كانت من قوم كافرين

translation: And he was told: 'Enter Paradise.' He said: 'How can I enter Paradise while my people are in hell?' He was told: 'We will put a barrier between you and the fire.' He said: 'I have been wronged, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse describes a conversation between a righteous servant of God and God Himself. The servant has been instructed to enter Paradise, but he expresses his concern that his people are in hell and he cannot bear the thought of being separated from them. God assures him that a barrier will be placed between him and the fire, indicating that the servant's faith and good deeds have earned him a place in Paradise, despite the fate of his people. The servant, with a deep sense of submission and humility, acknowledges his wrongdoing and declares his devotion to God, aligning himself with King Solomon, who also submitted to God's will. The verse highlights the importance of submitting to God's will and recognizing one's own mistakes, while also acknowledging the power of faith and good deeds in earning a place in Paradise.
orig: قيل لها ادخلي الصرح فلما رأته حسبته لجة وكشفت عن ساقيها قال إنه صرح ممرد من قوارير قالت رب إني ظلمت نفسي وأسلمت مع سليمان لله رب العالمين

translation: And indeed, We sent to Thamud their brother Salih, saying, 'Worship Allah,' but they were divided into two quarreling groups.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Salih, who was sent by God to the people of Thamud to guide them towards the worship of one God. However, the people were divided into two groups, one supporting Salih's message and the other opposing it, leading to conflict and quarrels among them. The verse highlights the challenges faced by prophets in their efforts to guide people towards the right path and the consequences of not heeding their messages.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا أن اعبدوا الله فإذا هم فريقان يختصمون

translation: And He said, 'O my people, why do you seek to hasten the evil before the good? Why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah that you may receive mercy?
interpretation: The verse addresses the tendency of people to prioritize worldly gains and immediate gratification over seeking forgiveness and mercy from God. The speaker, probably the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), questions his people about their reluctance to seek forgiveness and their eagerness to hasten the evil. The verse implies that seeking forgiveness and mercy from God should be the utmost priority for believers, as it leads to spiritual growth and salvation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their spiritual well-being and not to be distracted by worldly desires.
orig: قال يا قوم لم تستعجلون بالسيئة قبل الحسنة لولا تستغفرون الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: They said, 'You are following a man who is bewitched.' And he to whom they refer is the Messenger of God. But they are a people who are being destroyed.
interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to Islam by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They mocked him, saying that he was bewitched and under the influence of magic. The verse emphasizes the irony of their statement, as they were the ones who were truly under the spell of disbelief and ignorance, while the Prophet was the one who was guiding them towards the truth and salvation. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and following the truth, and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: قالوا اطيرنا بك وبمن معك قال طائركم عند الله بل أنتم قوم تفتنون

translation: And there were in the city six men who were causing corruption in the land, but they did not reform.
interpretation: The verse speaks about six men in a city who were spreading corruption and destruction. The verse implies that they were not only engaging in immoral acts, but also actively preventing others from living a righteous life. Their corruption was not limited to their own actions, but also had a negative impact on the community as a whole. The verse serves as a reminder that corruption and injustice can have far-reaching consequences and that it is the responsibility of the believers to stand up against it and work towards justice and righteousness.
orig: وكان في المدينة تسعة رهط يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, 'Let us divide up the Qur'an into parts and take turns reciting it, so that we may hear it and remember it better.' But when they were about to do so, they were overwhelmed by its grandeur and the truth it contained, and they realized that they could not do it justice. They were humbled by the realization that the Qur'an was not something that could be easily divided or shared, and that it was a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, worthy of reverence and respect.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of a group of people to divide the Qur'an into parts and take turns reciting it. However, they soon realized that the Qur'an is not a book that can be easily divided or shared, as it contains the truth and wisdom of God. The verse highlights the grandeur and magnificence of the Qur'an, and the fact that it is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, worthy of reverence and respect. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of approaching the Qur'an with humility and respect, and recognizing its divine origin and authority.
orig: قالوا تقاسموا بالله لنبيتنه وأهله ثم لنقولن لوليه ما شهدنا مهلك أهله وإنا لصادقون

translation: And they plotted and planned, but their plots were known to God, even though they were not aware of it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of the disbelievers to plot and plan against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. Despite their efforts to conceal their plans, God was aware of their schemes and plans, and they were ultimately unsuccessful in their attempts to harm the Muslims. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-aware, and that no secret is hidden from Him. It also highlights the futility of plotting against God's will and the inevitability of His plan.
orig: ومكروا مكرا ومكرنا مكرا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فانظر كيف كان عاقبة مكرهم أنا دمرناهم وقومهم أجمعين

translation: So We destroyed them, and their homes were left empty, as a lesson for those who fear disaster.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of a community that was destroyed by God due to their wrongdoing. Their homes were left empty, serving as a lesson for those who fear God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is a certainty for those who disobey Him, and that it is a lesson for those who are aware of the consequences of their actions and fear God's retribution.
orig: فتلك بيوتهم خاوية بما ظلموا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعلمون

translation: And We saved those who believed and were righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fate of the wicked towns that were destroyed and the blessed end of the righteous believers. The verse emphasizes that the believers were not only saved from the destruction but were also rewarded with a life of righteousness. The phrase 'And We saved' indicates that the believers were not only passive recipients of God's mercy but were also active in their faith, having demonstrated their belief and righteousness. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is not limited to belief but is accompanied by good deeds and a righteous lifestyle.
orig: وأنجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And (remember) when Lot said to his people: 'You commit such immorality! Surely, you are a people who are ignorant (of the punishment).'
interpretation: The verse refers to the prophet Lot's warning to his people, who were engaging in sodomy and other immoral acts. Lot's message was met with disbelief and disregard, and his people refused to listen to his warnings. The verse highlights the prophet's frustration and sadness at his people's behavior, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of such actions. It also underscores the importance of listening to divine guidance and the consequences of rejecting it.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة وأنتم تبصرون

translation: And certainly We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity's innermost thoughts and feelings, and His proximity to them. The use of the metaphor of the jugular vein emphasizes the intimate nature of God's relationship with humanity, indicating that He is closer to them than their own blood flowing through their veins. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and ever-present, and that humans cannot hide their thoughts or actions from Him. It also underscores the idea that God's knowledge and power are not limited by spatial or temporal constraints, and that He is always with His creation, watching over them and guiding them towards righteousness.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم تجهلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوا آل لوط من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: And We have saved you and your family, except your wife; she was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of Prophet Noah and his family, who were saved by God from the flood that destroyed the rest of the world. The verse highlights the fact that Noah's wife was not among those who were saved, as she did not believe in her husband's message and was left behind. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands, and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته قدرناها من الغابرين

translation: And We sent upon them a storm of punishment, a punishment of ruin, destruction, and devastation.
interpretation: The verse describes the severity of God's punishment upon the wicked people. The use of the word 'storm' emphasizes the sudden and overwhelming nature of the punishment, while the description of the punishment as 'ruin, destruction, and devastation' underscores the severity of God's wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Say, 'Praise be to Allah and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen.' Is Allah better, or what they associate with Him?
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the previous verse, where Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded to tell the polytheists that Allah is the only one worthy of worship and that the believers are those who have been chosen by Allah. The verse emphasizes the superiority of Allah over any other deity that the polytheists may associate with Him. The phrase 'Is Allah better, or what they associate with Him?' is a rhetorical question that highlights the absurdity of associating partners with Allah and emphasizes the uniqueness of Allah's sovereignty and lordship.
orig: قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى آلله خير أما يشركون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create, as well as the magnitude of His creation. The mention of six days refers to the six days of creation as described in the Qur'an, where God created the heavens, earth, and all that is between them. The verse also underscores the idea that God's creation is not limited by time or weariness, as He is not subject to the limitations of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the significance of His creation, and encourages believers to reflect on and appreciate the beauty and complexity of the universe.
orig: أمن خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل لكم من السماء ماء فأنبتنا به حدائق ذات بهجة ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها أإله مع الله بل هم قوم يعدلون

translation: And indeed, We have made the earth a wide expanse and placed therein mountains and rivers, and We have made it a habitable place for you, and made the atmosphere suitable for you, and sent down water from the sky, and thereby We have brought forth various types of plants. All this is in order that you may not be able to know your Creator, and that you may not be grateful to Him. Indeed, most of them do not know Allah, except a few.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's creation of the earth and its resources, emphasizing the variety and abundance of His provisions for humanity. The verse also underscores humanity's ignorance and ingratitude towards God, despite the numerous signs and blessings He has bestowed upon them. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and generosity, and humanity's responsibility to recognize and appreciate these qualities.
orig: أمن جعل الأرض قرارا وجعل خلالها أنهارا وجعل لها رواسي وجعل بين البحرين حاجزا أإله مع الله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then indeed, you have already been sent to warn, and their punishment will not be delayed until the Day of Resurrection,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a warner to his people. Despite their rejection and denial of his message, he is reminded that his duty is to continue warning them of the consequences of their actions and that their punishment will not be delayed until the Day of Resurrection. The verse highlights the urgency of the message and the importance of the Prophet's role in conveying it to his people.
orig: أمن يجيب المضطر إذا دعاه ويكشف السوء ويجعلكم خلفاء الأرض أإله مع الله قليلا ما تذكرون

translation: And who is it that can guide whom thou art not able to guide? And who is it that can warn whom thou art not able to warn? And who is it that can show the way to him whom thou art not able to show the way? And who is it that can guide whom thou art not able to guide?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things, including the ability to guide and warn. It suggests that God is the only one who can truly guide and warn, and that human efforts to do so are ultimately futile. The verse also highlights the idea that God's guidance and warnings are not limited to specific individuals or groups, but are available to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the importance of recognizing and submitting to His will.
orig: أمن يهديكم في ظلمات البر والبحر ومن يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته أإله مع الله تعالى الله عما يشركون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create the universe and all that is in it, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, in just six days. The verse also highlights the fact that God was not tired or wearied by this creation, indicating His infinite power and strength. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of God's majesty and ability to do anything, and encourages them to have faith in His power and wisdom.
orig: أمن يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ومن يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أإله مع الله قل هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that only God has knowledge of the unseen, including the time of resurrection. The verse is a response to the disbelievers who were questioning the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the timing of the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the limitation of human knowledge and the power of God, reminding the believers to have faith in God's knowledge and timing. The verse also serves as a warning to those who deny the Day of Judgment, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: And they have no knowledge about the Hereafter, they are in doubt about it, nay, they are blind to it.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance of the disbelievers regarding the Hereafter. They lack understanding of the concept of the Afterlife and are uncertain about what will happen to them after death. The verse emphasizes that they are not just uncertain, but they are also blind to the reality of the Hereafter, indicating a willful rejection of the idea. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the existence of the Hereafter, reminding them that their denial will not change the reality of the Afterlife and the eventual judgment they will face.
orig: بل ادارك علمهم في الآخرة بل هم في شك منها بل هم منها عمون

translation: And the disbelievers say, 'If we were to be destroyed, we would be as ashes, and our ancestors would be as dust.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' response to the warning of God's punishment. They mockingly say that if they were to be destroyed, they would be reduced to ashes, and their ancestors would be reduced to dust. The verse highlights their arrogance and disbelief in the afterlife, as they believe that their destruction would be the end of their existence. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of disbelief and disobedience are severe and that one should not take their existence for granted.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا أإذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أئنا لمخرجون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the decisive victory that the believers achieved over their enemies, while the phrase 'manifest triumph' suggests that the victory was not only clear but also obvious and evident to all. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is not due to their own strength or power, but rather due to the favor and support of God. It also serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that their opposition to the Prophet and the believers will only lead to their own downfall.
orig: لقد وعدنا هذا نحن وآباؤنا من قبل إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: Tell them to travel through the earth and see how the criminals were punished.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to tell the disbelievers to travel through the earth and see the consequences of the wicked. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are ignorant of the consequences of their actions and the punishment that awaits them. By traveling through the earth, they will see the remains of past civilizations that were destroyed by God's punishment, such as the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, and the people of Noah. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that the punishment of God is real and that they will face it if they continue to reject the message of Islam.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And do not grieve over them, nor be in distress because of what they conspire.
interpretation: The verse advises believers not to grieve or be distressed over the plots and conspiracies of those who seek to harm them. Instead, believers are encouraged to put their trust in God and remember that God is aware of all things and has the power to protect and guide those who are faithful to Him. The verse serves as a reminder that true victory and success come from God, and that believers should focus on their own spiritual growth and development rather than worrying about the actions of others.
orig: ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تكن في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' skepticism and mocking of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. They question the authenticity of the promise of punishment and ask when it will come to pass, suggesting that they do not believe in the truth of the message. The verse serves as a reminder that the promise of punishment is indeed true and will come to pass, and that the disbelievers will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'Have you considered, if your Lord were to punish you with a punishment, or if He were to delay it, what remedy will there be for you?',
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and instructing him to ask the disbelievers about their thoughts on the possibility of God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment could come at any moment, without warning, and that there will be no escape or remedy for those who have been warned but chose to reject the message. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قل عسى أن يكون ردف لكم بعض الذي تستعجلون

translation: And indeed, your Lord is rich in favor upon the people, but most of them do not show gratitude.
interpretation: This verse highlights the abundance of God's blessings and favors upon humanity, despite which, majority of people do not express gratitude. The verse emphasizes the contrast between God's generosity and humanity's ingratitude, suggesting that people often take God's blessings for granted and fail to recognize and appreciate the source of their blessings.
orig: وإن ربك لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of the secrets and intentions of all human beings. It suggests that God is aware of both the hidden thoughts and feelings of individuals, as well as their public declarations and actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that nothing is hidden from Him. It also implies that God's knowledge encompasses both the internal and external aspects of human behavior, and that He is aware of the motivations and intentions behind people's actions.
orig: وإن ربك ليعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And there is not a thing but it has its source in the clear Book.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that everything in the universe, whether in the heavens or on earth, has a source or origin that can be found in the Qur'an. The 'clear Book' refers to the Qur'an itself, which is considered the ultimate source of guidance and wisdom. The verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, which covers all aspects of life, including the natural world, moral guidance, and spiritual growth. It also underscores the idea that the Qur'an is a guide and a source of knowledge for those who seek to understand the mysteries of the universe.
orig: وما من غائبة في السماء والأرض إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an narrates upon the Children of Israel most of what they differ in.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an provides detailed accounts of the stories of the Children of Israel, which were previously unknown or distorted. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a means of clarification and guidance for those who seek the truth and want to understand the history of the Children of Israel. The verse also suggests that the Qur'an provides a comprehensive and accurate account of the history of the Children of Israel, which was not available before. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and enlightenment for those who seek to understand the history of the Children of Israel and the messages they were sent by God.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يقص على بني إسرائيل أكثر الذي هم فيه يختلفون

translation: And indeed, it is a guide and a mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Qur'an as a guide and a source of mercy for the believers. The word 'guide' refers to the fact that the Qur'an provides guidance on all aspects of life, including beliefs, values, and practices. The word 'mercy' highlights the compassionate and forgiving nature of God, who reveals His will in the Qur'an and offers guidance to those who seek to live according to His commandments. The verse underscores the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book of rules, but a source of spiritual nourishment and guidance for those who seek to deepen their faith and their relationship with God.
orig: وإنه لهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them with His judgment, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and judgment over all things. The phrase 'between them' refers to the various factions and groups that may have differing beliefs and opinions. The verse assures that God will ultimately judge and settle all disputes with His perfect knowledge and wisdom. The description of God as 'Exalted in Might' and 'Knowing' highlights His power and omniscience, underscoring the idea that His judgment is absolute and final.
orig: إن ربك يقضي بينهم بحكمه وهو العزيز العليم

translation: And rely upon Allah for guidance. Indeed, you are upon the clear truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on God for guidance, as the path to righteousness and truth is often unclear and uncertain. The phrase 'Indeed, you are upon the clear truth' serves as a reassurance that those who put their trust in God will be guided to the right path, and that God's guidance is always available to those who seek it.
orig: فتوكل على الله إنك على الحق المبين

translation: You do not hear the dead, nor do you hear the silent appeal when they are in their graves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the dead cannot be heard, nor can their voices be heard, as they are in a state of silence. The verse can be interpreted as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the futility of trying to communicate with the dead. It also highlights the powerlessness of the dead to communicate their thoughts or feelings to the living. The verse can also be seen as a reminder to the living to make the most of their time on earth and to not take their lives or their relationships with others for granted.
orig: إنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?',
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' skepticism regarding the Day of Judgment. They question the prophets about the timing of the promise, implying that they do not believe in its fulfillment. The verse emphasizes that the fulfillment of the promise is a certainty, and that it will come to pass when God wills it. The verse also highlights the contrast between the disbelievers' disbelief and the believers' faith, as the latter submit to God's will and trust in His promises.
orig: وما أنت بهادي العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: And when the word came to them, We brought forth a beast from the earth, speaking to them in a clear voice that the people may understand Our signs, but they were not convinced.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the people were rejecting God's signs and messages, despite the clear evidence and warnings. In response, God sent a beast from the earth to speak to them in a clear voice, emphasizing the urgency and importance of the message. The beast's voice was meant to convey the gravity of the situation and the consequences of their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's signs and the importance of heeding His warnings.
orig: وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تكلمهم أن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون

translation: And on a Day when He will gather them all together, (it will seem) as if they had not stayed (in the world) but an hour of a day, they will recognize one another, (and) will be able to proffer excuses to one another!
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered together and it will seem as if they had not lived on earth for more than an hour. They will recognize each other and try to make excuses for their actions. The verse emphasizes the suddenness and unexpectedness of the Day of Judgment and the fact that people will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to prepare for the Hereafter.
orig: ويوم نحشر من كل أمة فوجا ممن يكذب بآياتنا فهم يوزعون

translation: And when they came to Him, they said, 'We have been guilty of injustice against ourselves.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where people have realized their mistakes and have come to God, acknowledging their wrongdoing. The phrase 'We have been guilty of injustice against ourselves' implies that they have harmed themselves through their own actions, rather than God punishing them. The verse highlights the importance of taking responsibility for one's actions and recognizing the consequences of one's own mistakes. It also emphasizes the idea that God is always ready to forgive and accept those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: حتى إذا جاءوا قال أكذبتم بآياتي ولم تحيطوا بها علما أماذا كنتم تعملون

translation: And the word has been realized against them, because of their wrongdoing, so they will not speak.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of the people's wicked deeds, which have led to their destruction. The phrase 'the word has been realized' implies a prophecy or a warning that has been fulfilled, indicating that the people were aware of the consequences of their actions but chose to ignore them. The second part of the verse, 'because of their wrongdoing, so they will not speak,' emphasizes that the people's inability to speak is a result of their own actions, and they have no one to blame but themselves. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and ignoring the warnings and prophecies will only lead to our downfall.
orig: ووقع القول عليهم بما ظلموا فهم لا ينطقون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم يروا أنا جعلنا الليل ليسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And on the Day when the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are in the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. And all the angels will be gathered together, and the heavens will be opened, and the judgment will be pronounced. And the books will be spread, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the Day of Judgment, when the Trumpet will be blown, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the judgment. The verse emphasizes the terror and fear that will grip all creatures, both in heaven and on earth, except those whom God has exempted from this fear. The verse then describes the gathering of the angels, the opening of the heavens, and the pronouncement of the judgment. The verse also mentions the spreading of the books, the bringing of the prophets and witnesses, and the judgment being made between them in truth, with no injustice being done to anyone.
orig: ويوم ينفخ في الصور ففزع من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله وكل أتوه داخرين

translation: And you see the mountains and think them solid, but they pass away like the passing of a cloud.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the impermanence of seemingly solid and enduring things, such as mountains. The verse uses the metaphor of a cloud to convey the idea that even the most solid and enduring things are subject to change and impermanence. The verse serves as a reminder of the transience of human life and the fleeting nature of worldly things, and encourages the reader to focus on seeking what is truly lasting and enduring, which is the pleasure of God.
orig: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب صنع الله الذي أتقن كل شيء إنه خبير بما تفعلون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'manifest triumph' signifies that the victory is clear and evident to all, leaving no doubt or confusion. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is a result of God's favor and blessings, and that they should remain grateful and obedient to God.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها وهم من فزع يومئذ آمنون

translation: And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned in the Fire, [and they will be told], 'Are you recompensed for what you used to do?'
interpretation: This verse warns those who engage in evil deeds that they will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. The verse describes a scene where the sinners' faces will be overturned in the Fire, indicating their shame and regret, and they will be asked if they are being recompensed for their deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to live a life of sin and disobedience, reminding them of the severe punishment that awaits them if they do not repent and change their ways.
orig: ومن جاء بالسيئة فكبت وجوههم في النار هل تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has sanctified it and to whom belongs everything, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Abraham's realization that the city he is in is sacred and belongs to God, and that he has been commanded to worship God and be among the Muslims. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's authority and the obligation to worship Him alone. It also emphasizes the importance of being part of a Muslim community and living in accordance with God's commandments.
orig: إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها وله كل شيء وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: And indeed, We have sent the Qur'an down to you, O Prophet, truly as a guidance for the children of Adam, and those who follow you, the believers, and those who follow the believers, and those who follow the disbelievers
interpretation: N
orig: وأن أتلو القرآن فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فقل إنما أنا من المنذرين

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear signs and examples from the past, and lessons from what We have punished those who were before you, and warnings to those who are careful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of learning from the past and taking heed of the lessons and warnings that God has provided through His punishment of previous nations. The verse emphasizes the significance of reflecting on the signs and examples from the past, recognizing the consequences of disobedience, and being mindful of God's wrath. It serves as a reminder to those who are heedless and rebellious, encouraging them to take heed of the warnings and admonitions contained in the Qur'an.
orig: وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته فتعرفونها وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: طسم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: And recite to them the news of Moses and Pharaoh, when Moses said to his people: 'O my people! Surely I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Moses and his encounter with Pharaoh. Moses, who was chosen by God to lead the Israelites out of Egypt, declared himself a messenger of the Lord of the worlds. This verse serves as a reminder of the authority and legitimacy of Moses' prophethood and the message he conveyed to his people. It also highlights the importance of recognizing and submitting to the divine authority, as Pharaoh's refusal to believe in Moses and his message ultimately led to his downfall.
orig: نتلو عليك من نبإ موسى وفرعون بالحق لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group of them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was of the corruptors.
interpretation: The verse describes the tyrannical rule of Pharaoh, who divided the people into different groups and oppressed one group, killing their sons and sparing their women. This verse highlights Pharaoh's cruelty and injustice, and serves as a warning against the dangers of absolute power and the importance of justice and compassion.
orig: إن فرعون علا في الأرض وجعل أهلها شيعا يستضعف طائفة منهم يذبح أبناءهم ويستحيي نساءهم إنه كان من المفسدين

translation: And We wish to confer a favour upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's intention to bestow His favor upon the oppressed people and elevate them to leadership positions. The verse highlights God's desire to empower the marginalized and oppressed, and to make them the leaders and inheritors of the land. This verse serves as a reminder that God is on the side of the oppressed and that He will ultimately bring justice to those who have been wronged.
orig: ونريد أن نمن على الذين استضعفوا في الأرض ونجعلهم أئمة ونجعلهم الوارثين

translation: And We have made them (the people of Pharaoh) as tales (in the land), and (We have made) the son of Haman and (the people of) Thamud as warnings.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of Pharaoh, Haman, and Thamud. The verse uses the metaphor of 'tales' to indicate that the people of Pharaoh have become a cautionary story, a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and disbelief. The verse also mentions the son of Haman, who was a prominent figure in the court of Pharaoh and was known for his wisdom and knowledge. The mention of Thamud, who was a prosperous and powerful nation, serves as a reminder that even the most powerful nations can fall when they reject God's message. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ونمكن لهم في الأرض ونري فرعون وهامان وجنودهما منهم ما كانوا يحذرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" (alam) suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but is universal and applicable to all people. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's role is not to bring destruction or punishment, but rather to guide people towards a life of peace, compassion, and mercy. It also highlights the importance of the Prophet's character as a mercy to others, and sets an example for believers to follow in their interactions with others.
orig: وأوحينا إلى أم موسى أن أرضعيه فإذا خفت عليه فألقيه في اليم ولا تخافي ولا تحزني إنا رادوه إليك وجاعلوه من المرسلين

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his army pursued them in tyranny and enmity until the truth came to them.
interpretation: This verse describes the Israelites' exodus from Egypt, led by Moses, and their crossing of the Red Sea. Pharaoh, who had oppressed the Israelites for centuries, pursued them with his army, but God intervened and parted the sea, allowing the Israelites to cross safely. The verse highlights the oppression and injustice faced by the Israelites and the power of God in delivering them from their oppressors. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of standing up against oppression and fighting for justice, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
orig: فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا إن فرعون وهامان وجنودهما كانوا خاطئين

translation: And the wife of Pharaoh said: 'A comfort of the eye for me! Not that I may not be sad, nor that my heart be not sorrowful.'
interpretation: The wife of Pharaoh, Asiya, is speaking to her husband, Pharaoh, and asking him not to kill the baby Moses, who was a comfort to her eyes. She is expressing her sadness and sorrow at the thought of losing him and imploring Pharaoh to spare his life. This verse highlights Asiya's compassion and maternal instincts, as well as her desire to protect the innocent child. It also contrasts with Pharaoh's harshness and lack of empathy, as he is determined to kill Moses out of fear of his own rule being threatened.
orig: وقالت امرأت فرعون قرت عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to spread God's message of peace, love, and forgiveness. It also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role in bringing people closer to God and guiding them towards a righteous and just life.
orig: وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغا إن كادت لتبدي به لولا أن ربطنا على قلبها لتكون من المؤمنين

translation: And I (the Prophet) said to my brother (in faith), 'Follow me.' But he did not follow me. Instead, he diverged from me and did not perceive the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) invitation to his brother (in faith) to follow him and the truth he had received from God. However, the brother did not heed the Prophet's call and instead chose to diverge from the path of truth. The verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet and the consequences of not doing so.
orig: وقالت لأخته قصيه فبصرت به عن جنب وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form indicates that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to guide people towards the right path, and serves as a reminder that the purpose of prophethood is not to condemn or punish, but rather to guide and show compassion to all people.
orig: وحرمنا عليه المراضع من قبل فقالت هل أدلكم على أهل بيت يكفلونه لكم وهم له ناصحون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form suggests that the scope of his message is universal and not limited to a particular nation or community. The verse serves as a reminder that the purpose of prophethood is not to bring destruction or punishment, but rather to guide people towards a better way of life and to show them the path to salvation.
orig: فرددناه إلى أمه كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن ولتعلم أن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And when the boy reached the age of puberty, We granted him wisdom and knowledge, and thus We rewarded the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Joseph, who was granted wisdom and knowledge by God at a young age. The verse emphasizes the idea that God rewards those who do good deeds and that wisdom and knowledge are a form of reward from God for those who are righteous. The verse also highlights the importance of puberty as a milestone in a person's life, marking the transition from childhood to adulthood and the beginning of personal responsibility.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده واستوى آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And enter the city at noon, when its people were unaware, and they found two men fighting, this one from his sect and that one from his enemy's sect. And the one from his sect sought help from the one from his enemy's sect, and the one from his enemy's sect killed him. Moses struck him, and it was said to him, 'This is from the work of the devil. Indeed, he is a manifest enemy.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the entrance of Prophet Moses into a city, where he found two men fighting. One of them was from his own sect, and the other was from the enemy's sect. The man from Moses' sect sought help from Moses, who belonged to the enemy's sect, but the man from the enemy's sect killed him. Moses, in turn, struck the killer and was told that this was the work of the devil, who is a manifest enemy. The verse highlights the destructive nature of Satan's work and the importance of being aware of his influence in our lives. It also emphasizes the importance of seeking help from the righteous and avoiding the company of those who are influenced by Satan.
orig: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين

translation: And He said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' And He forgave him, indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks about a person who has recognized their own sin and has turned to God in repentance. The verse highlights the person's acknowledgment of their wrongdoing and their seeking of forgiveness from God. The verse also emphasizes God's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful, indicating that God is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of recognizing their own sins and seeking forgiveness from God, and the assurance that God is always ready to forgive those who turn to Him.
orig: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين

translation: And he entered the city at dawn, fearful and cautious, and said, 'I will certainly find out what has happened to my people.'
interpretation: The verse describes Moses' entry into the city, where he is searching for his people, the Israelites. The use of the word 'khafid' (fearful) and 'mubin' (cautious) emphasizes Moses' state of mind, indicating that he is both anxious and vigilant. The phrase 'I will certainly find out' suggests determination and a strong desire to uncover the truth about his people's fate. The verse highlights Moses' leadership qualities and his concern for his people, as well as his willingness to take risks to gather information and make informed decisions.
orig: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين

translation: And Moses said: 'I wish not to kill you as I killed the soul yesterday. If you want to be sure, then make me imam (leader) over the children of Israel.'
interpretation: Moses is expressing his reluctance to kill the Egyptian who was mistreating an Israelite, as he had killed a soul the day before. Moses suggests that if the Egyptian wants to be sure that he will not be killed, he should make Moses the leader of the children of Israel. This verse highlights Moses' compassion and his desire to avoid violence, as well as his willingness to take on a leadership role to protect his people.
orig: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

translation: And a man came running from the farthest end of the city, saying, 'O Moses, the people are killing each other, for they have received orders to kill you. Therefore, leave my advice and go away, for I am one of your sincere advisors.'
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where a man from the farthest end of the city is warning Prophet Moses of an imminent threat to his life. The man is urging Moses to leave the city immediately, as the people have received orders to kill him. The verse highlights the loyalty and sincerity of the man, who is risking his own life to save Moses, and serves as an example of selflessness and courage in the face of danger. It also underscores the importance of seeking advice and guidance from trusted individuals, as the man is described as one of Moses' sincere advisors.
orig: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين

translation: So We seize it with destruction in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a town that was unjust and faced God's punishment. The use of the word 'seize' emphasizes the sudden and forceful nature of the punishment, indicating that it was not a gradual process but a sudden and decisive intervention by God. The verse also underscores the idea that the punishment was not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of the town's wicked deeds. The phrase 'or at noon' suggests that the punishment could come at any time, whether in the morning or in the middle of the day, emphasizing the element of surprise and the lack of warning. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the need to repent and change their ways.
orig: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And when he turned to leave, he said, 'I will surely return to you, [O Muhammad], if Allah wills.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Abraham is bidding farewell to his wife Hagar and his son Ishmael, whom he has been commanded by God to leave in the desert. Abraham is expressing his hope and faith that he will return to them if God wills, indicating his trust in God's plan and his belief that he will be reunited with his family in the future. The verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in God's plan, even in the face of difficult circumstances.
orig: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. orig: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير

interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. orig: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير

interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. orig: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين

interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: And indeed, I want to marry my two daughters to you, one on condition that you pay me ten camels and the other on condition that you perform the Hajj with me. If you complete ten (good deeds), I will give you my daughter in marriage. And if you desire, I will ransom you with ten camels, and if you desire, I will ransom you with ten camels, and if you desire, I will ransom you with ten good deeds. Indeed, I want to marry my daughters to good men.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a father who wants to marry off his two daughters to a righteous man. He sets two conditions for the marriage: either the suitor must pay him ten camels or perform the Hajj pilgrimage with him. The father is looking for a good man to marry his daughters, indicating the importance of finding a suitable partner for marriage. The verse also highlights the importance of performing good deeds and the Hajj pilgrimage as a means of purifying one's soul and seeking God's blessings.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said: 'Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to your parents. Whether one of them or both of them reach old age, say no word that shows disrespect to them, and do not repel them, but speak to them a gentle word.',
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's parents with kindness and respect, regardless of their age or health. The verse prohibits speaking harshly to them or repelling them, and instead encourages using gentle words when communicating with them. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of honoring one's parents and treating them with compassion, as they have spent their lives caring for and raising their children.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And when Moses' term was fulfilled, and he departed from his people, he saw a fire on the side of the mount. He said to his people: 'Wait, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you news or a burning brand from the fire that you may warm yourselves.'
interpretation: The verse describes Moses' experience when he departed from his people and saw a fire on the side of the mount. Moses' statement suggests that he was drawn to the fire and thought it might be a source of warmth and comfort for his people. The verse highlights Moses' leadership and his desire to provide for his people's needs, as well as his curiosity and willingness to explore the unknown. The verse also foreshadows the significance of the fire in the upcoming events, as it will play a crucial role in the revelation of God's message to Moses.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you, so do you not take heed?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them of the destruction of nations that came before them. The use of the phrase 'your kind' emphasizes that the people being addressed are not necessarily direct descendants of the previous nations, but are similar in their actions and behaviors. The verse encourages the disbelievers to reflect on the past and learn from the mistakes of those who came before them, and to recognize that God's punishment is not limited to any particular nation or group of people. The use of the phrase 'Rab al-Alamin' (Lord of the Worlds) at the end of the verse emphasizes God's power and authority over all creation.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your likenesses, the former peoples. So, do you perceive any reminder in this?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Moses, reminding him of how God destroyed previous nations that were similar to his own people. The verse is a warning to Moses and his people, implying that they too will face destruction if they do not change their ways and heed God's message. The verse also serves as a reminder to future generations, serving as a reminder of God's power and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: And put your hand into your bosom, it will come out white without evil, and draw your arm in to your side, those who follow the desire of the people of the Pharaoh and the people of the Romans.
interpretation: The verse speaks about Moses' miracle of turning his staff into a serpent and his hand becoming white as a sign of God's power and authority. The verse also mentions the people of the Pharaoh and the Romans, who were known for their oppression and tyranny. The verse warns against following the desires of such people and encourages believers to follow God's guidance instead.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: And He said, 'I will kill you, I fear that they will kill me.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the fear and concern of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he was commanded by God to go to Pharaoh and ask him to let the Israelites go. Moses was afraid that Pharaoh would kill him, and this fear was a natural response to the immense power and authority that Pharaoh held. The verse highlights the human side of Prophet Moses and his vulnerability, while also showing his faith and obedience to God's command despite his fear. It also serves as a reminder that even the greatest prophets experienced fear and doubt, but their faith and trust in God ultimately allowed them to overcome their fears and fulfill their missions.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I, so send him with me as a helper to confirm my truthfulness, for I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: Musa is acknowledging his own limitations in speech and requests the assistance of his brother Aaron, who is more eloquent, to help convey the message of God to the people. Moses is aware of the possibility of the people rejecting his message, and therefore, he seeks Aaron's help to confirm his truthfulness and lend credibility to his prophethood.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but rather it is a universal message that applies to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a mercy and a guidance for those who are willing to listen and follow his teachings, and serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with being a follower of the Prophet.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: And when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, 'This is not except invented magic, and we have not heard of this among our forefathers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people of Pharaoh when Moses came to them with the signs and miracles given to him by God. They rejected the signs and accused Moses of practicing magic, claiming that they had never heard of such things from their ancestors. The verse highlights the people's arrogance and unwillingness to accept the truth, instead choosing to cling to their old beliefs and traditions. It serves as a reminder that the truth is not always accepted or welcomed, and that people may reject it in favor of their own beliefs and desires.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, 'My Lord, I have knowledge of who has come with guidance from You, and who will be punished in the Hereafter. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is expressing his faith in God's justice and the idea that those who are righteous will be rewarded, while those who are wicked will be punished. Moses is acknowledging that he has been given knowledge by God of who among his people will be guided and who will be punished in the afterlife. The verse highlights the idea of accountability and the belief that our actions have consequences in the hereafter. It also emphasizes the idea that the righteous will ultimately succeed, while the wicked will not.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said: O chiefs! I know of no god for you except myself, so kindle for me a fire upon the clay, and make for me a lofty tower, that I may mount up to Moses' God. Indeed, I think he is a liar.
interpretation: Pharaoh, in his arrogance and ignorance, claims to be the only god worthy of worship and rejects the idea of a higher power. He orders his people to build a tower made of clay and fire, a symbol of his own ego and defiance of God. Pharaoh's delusion is evident in his belief that he can reach the God of Moses through his own efforts, rather than submitting to the will of the one true God. This verse highlights the dangers of pride and self-deception, and serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and instead choose to follow their own desires and false idols.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And they think that they will not be returned to Us, but they are Our enemies, and their multitude will be destroyed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the arrogance and delusion of those who reject God's message and believe that they will not be held accountable for their actions. They are described as 'enemies' of God and their multitude will be destroyed, indicating that their numbers will not save them from God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their denial of God's existence will not save them from His punishment.
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: So We seized him and his army, and We threw them into the sea, and see how was the end of the wrongdoers!
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of Pharaoh and his army, who were punished by God for their oppression and disbelief. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, which was drowning in the sea, and serves as a warning to those who oppress and reject God's signs. The phrase 'see how was the end of the wrongdoers' suggests that the punishment was a direct consequence of their actions, and serves as a reminder of the accountability of all actions in front of God.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We have made them leaders, calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the leaders who have led their people astray and called them to follow the path of destruction. The leaders are described as calling to the Fire, indicating that they are leading their followers towards a path that will ultimately lead to their destruction. The verse also mentions that on the Day of Resurrection, these leaders will not be helped, indicating that they will not be able to escape the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those in positions of leadership, reminding them of their responsibility to guide their people towards righteousness and not towards destruction.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We will follow them up in this world with punishment and on the Day of Resurrection. They will be from the ones who are losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the consequences of leading a life of sin and injustice. The punishment that the wicked will face in this life is a warning to those who are living in sin, and serves as a reminder of the certainty of God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. The phrase 'from the ones who are losers' suggests that those who are punished in this life and the Hereafter are those who have lost the opportunity to live a righteous life and face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And indeed, We have given Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations, as an enlightenment for the people and a guidance and mercy, that they may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse describes the revelation of the Torah to Prophet Moses after the destruction of the previous generations. The verse emphasizes the purpose of the revelation, which is to serve as a guidance and mercy for the people, and to remind them of the consequences of their actions. The verse highlights the importance of remembering and learning from the past, and the role of divine guidance in shaping the lives of individuals and communities.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And I was not absent from your side when We gave Moses the command, and I was a witness to the event.
interpretation: The verse refers to the moment when God gave Moses the command to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The speaker, who is believed to be the Prophet Muhammad, was not present in person at the time of the event, but was a witness to it through divine revelation. The verse highlights the significance of the event and the speaker's connection to it, emphasizing the continuity between the prophetic traditions and the importance of the Prophet Muhammad's role in the history of divine revelation.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed generations before you, but you do not remember them. And you were not a dweller in those cities, nor were you a witness to their destruction.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority, reminding the reader that God has destroyed entire generations in the past, and the current generation should not feel secure from similar punishment. The verse also highlights the idea that the current generation is not unique and that they will be held accountable for their actions just like previous generations. The verse also emphasizes that the current generation is not immune to destruction and that they should learn from the lessons of the past.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if not for the harm that would have afflicted them, they would have said, 'Our Lord, why did you not send us a messenger? We would have followed your signs and become believers.'
interpretation: The verse suggests that people tend to reject the idea of accountability and punishment until they experience harm or suffering. Only then do they begin to question their ways and seek guidance. The verse highlights the tendency of humans to ignore the signs and messages sent by God until they are faced with consequences. It also underscores the idea that belief and faith are not genuine unless they are accompanied by action and obedience to God's commands.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: And when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'This is obvious magic.' They denied it, while they were denying the truth that came to them, out of envy and pride. They said, 'This is a conspiracy, a fabrication.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the truth of Islam. Instead of accepting it, they dismissed it as magic and accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating it out of envy and pride. The verse highlights the psychological denial and unwillingness of the disbelievers to accept the truth, which led them to conspire against the Prophet and reject the message of Islam.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, 'Bring forth your witnesses against me, God's Book, which is the truth, and let the followers of earlier revelations bear witness to it.'
interpretation: In this verse, God commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to challenge his opponents to bring forth their witnesses against him, and to rely on the Qur'an as the ultimate evidence of the truth of his message. The verse emphasizes the authority and authenticity of the Qur'an as a revelation from God, and highlights its role as a source of guidance and evidence for those who seek the truth. The verse also underscores the importance of the testimony of the followers of earlier revelations, who are called upon to bear witness to the truth of the Qur'an and to support the Prophet's message.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And indeed, if they had been willing to obey, they would have followed the guidance, but their hearts were blocked by their desires, and their misdeeds were their only concern.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people who are being addressed have been given the opportunity to follow the guidance and submit to God's will, but they have chosen not to do so. Their hearts are blocked by their own desires and they are consumed by their own misdeeds. The verse highlights the idea that the people have been given the ability to choose between right and wrong, but they have chosen to follow their own desires rather than the guidance of God. The verse serves as a reminder that God's guidance is always available, but it is up to the individual to choose to follow it or not.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And indeed, We have conveyed to them the message that they may remember.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fact that God has already sent a message to the people, through earlier prophets and revelations, with the intention of guiding them towards righteousness and reminding them of the consequences of their actions. The use of the word 'لعلهم' (li-tadhkirun) in the verse suggests that the message was not only conveyed but also made clear and understandable to the people, so that they may reflect and remember the lessons and warnings contained within. The verse serves as a reminder that God's message has been consistently delivered throughout history, and that people have been given the opportunity to recognize and follow the truth.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And those whom We have given the Book before this, they believe in it
interpretation: The verse refers to the people who were given the Scripture before the Qur'an, specifically the Jews and Christians. The verse indicates that they have faith in the Qur'an and recognize its authenticity, as they have been awaiting its arrival. The verse emphasizes the continuity of the message of the Qur'an with the previous Scriptures and highlights the unity of the prophetic message. The belief of the People of the Book in the Qur'an serves as a witness to its truth and reinforces the idea that the Qur'an is a confirmation of the previous Scriptures, rather than a replacement.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in it (the Qur'an)', they say, 'We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. We were, before this, Muslims (submitting to Allah).
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the believers when they are invited to embrace the Qur'an. They readily accept it, acknowledging that it is the truth from God and that they were already Muslims, submitting to God's will, before they heard the Qur'an. The verse highlights the idea that the Qur'an is not a new revelation, but rather a confirmation of the truth that was already present in the hearts of the believers. It also underscores the idea that Islam is not a new religion, but rather a continuation of the same message that has been sent by God throughout history.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse highlights the response of those who have been given knowledge, that is, the believers, to the revelation sent by God. They recognize the truth in the message revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and see that it guides to the path of God, the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its role in guiding people to the right path. It also underscores the significance of the revelation as a source of guidance and a means of attaining spiritual growth and enlightenment.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they heard the vain talk, they turned away from it and said, 'We have our deeds, and you have your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant.'
