interpretation: The verse describes a situation where some people were engaging in vain talk, perhaps spreading false rumors or gossip. The believers, instead of engaging with them, chose to distance themselves from such conversation and focus on their own deeds and actions. They replied by saying 'We have our deeds, and you have your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant.' This verse highlights the importance of being mindful of the company we keep and the conversations we engage in, as well as the importance of prioritizing our own actions and deeds over engaging with those who may be spreading negativity or ignorance.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you guide not whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is aware of the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of the Prophet's ability to guide people and the ultimate authority of God's guidance. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) cannot guide anyone he wishes, but only those whom God wills to guide. This verse highlights the importance of God's sovereignty and the Prophet's role as a mere servant of God, delivering His message. The verse also underscores the idea that guidance is a divine prerogative, and that God is aware of those who are guided and those who are not.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, 'Following the guidance will bring us astray from our land, and we will be cut off from our forefathers' way.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the resistance of the disbelievers to follow the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They believed that following the guidance would lead them astray from their traditional way of life and cut them off from their ancestors' customs. The verse highlights the reluctance of people to leave their old beliefs and traditions, even if they are misguided, and their fear of change and the unknown. It also emphasizes the importance of following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in order to attain true knowledge and guidance.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And your Lord would not have destroyed the towns until He had sent to their mother a messenger, reciting to them Our verses. And We would not have destroyed the towns but for their wrongdoing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and mercy in dealing with the destruction of towns. The verse states that before destroying a town, God always sends a messenger to warn its people and give them a chance to repent. The messenger recites God's verses to them, reminding them of their accountability to God and the consequences of their actions. The verse also emphasizes that the destruction of towns is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of the people's wrongdoing and rejection of God's message.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: And what you have been given of the wealth of this world and its embellishment is (but a passing) enjoyment, and that which is with Allah is better and more lasting. Would you not then understand?
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly wealth and material possessions, and contrasts them with the eternal nature of what is with Allah. The verse encourages people to look beyond the superficial attractions of this life and to focus on seeking what is truly lasting and valuable, which is the reward that comes from living a righteous life and pleasing God. The verse serves as a reminder that true happiness and fulfillment come from seeking spiritual enrichment and a strong relationship with God, rather than pursuing fleeting material possessions.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And on the Day when He shall call out to them, saying: 'Where are My (so-called) partners whom you imagined?',
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, God will call out to those who associated partners with Him, asking them where their imagined partners are. The verse emphasizes the idea that those who were deceived by their own desires and false beliefs will be confronted with the reality of their mistake. The phrase 'Where are My (so-called) partners whom you imagined?' highlights the fact that those who were associated with God will be held accountable for their actions and will be asked to produce their partners, who they thought would help them in their time of need. The verse serves as a warning to those who are tempted to associate partners with God, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their false beliefs will not save them from God's punishment.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and guidance in recognizing the truth of God's revelation. The phrase 'those who have been given knowledge' refers to those who have been blessed with understanding and insight, and they recognize the truth of God's word as revealed in the Qur'an. The verse highlights the role of knowledge in guiding people to the straight path, which is the path of the Exalted in Might and the Praiseworthy. This verse serves as a reminder to those who are seeking guidance and enlightenment, to seek it through the pursuit of knowledge and understanding, and to recognize the truth of God's revelation.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And they were told, 'Call upon your Lord for help.' But they refused and were arrogant, and they did not receive an answer, and they saw the punishment. If only they had been guided!
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were invited to call upon God for help, but they refused and were too arrogant to do so. As a result, they did not receive an answer and were punished. The verse highlights the importance of humility and seeking help from God, and serves as a warning to those who are too proud to ask for guidance or help. The verse also emphasizes the consequences of refusing to seek guidance and the importance of being open to receiving help from God.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And on the Day when He will call them and say, 'What answer did you give the Messengers?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the Day of Judgment when God will question the people about their response to the Messengers (Prophets) He sent to guide them. The verse emphasizes the accountability of individuals for their actions and the responsibility they have towards the Messengers and their message. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting or ignoring the message of God's Prophets, and the importance of heeding their warnings and guidance.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: And they have been warned by the signs of the approaching Day, but they did not comprehend and were not mindful.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people's lack of understanding and heedlessness in the face of the signs and warnings that God has sent them. The 'signs' refer to the miraculous events and prophecies that precede the coming of the Day of Judgment. The verse suggests that despite these warnings, the people have not taken heed and have failed to understand the significance of these signs. The word 'comprehend' in the translation is a more accurate reflection of the Arabic word 'fa-hum' which means 'they did not comprehend, understand or perceive'. The word 'mindful' is also a more accurate reflection of the Arabic word 'yatasiloon' which means 'they did not become mindful or aware'. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of God's signs and encourages them to be mindful of the approaching Day of Judgment.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: Then as for him who will be given his record in his right hand, he will say: 'Take, read my record! Surely I thought that I should be judged (in my deeds)',
interpretation: This verse describes the scene of judgment day, where the righteous will be given their record of deeds in their right hand, signifying their good deeds and their preparation for the afterlife. The verse highlights the confidence and contentment of the righteous, who are eager to have their deeds evaluated and rewarded by God. The phrase 'I thought that I should be judged (in my deeds)' underscores the idea that the righteous have lived their lives with the awareness of being accountable to God and have strived to do good deeds to earn their place in paradise.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice; glory to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate (with Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power to create and choose as He wills, without any input or choice given to His creation. The verse also highlights the idea that human beings have no say in the matter of their own destiny and that God is above any partners or associates that they may assign to Him. The phrase 'glory to Allah' is a declaration of God's greatness and majesty, and 'exalted is He above what they associate (with Him)' is a rejection of any attempt to equate Him with other beings or deities.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of the hidden thoughts and intentions of human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of both the concealed thoughts and the open declarations of people, indicating that nothing is hidden from God's sight. This verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-aware, and that humans will be held accountable for their thoughts and actions.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him, the Praised One, in the first and the Hereafter, and His is the praise, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. It stresses that God is the only one worthy of praise and that all creation will eventually return to Him. The verse also highlights God's sovereignty and control over all things, both in this life and in the hereafter. It serves as a reminder to believers to focus their worship and devotion solely on God, and to reject any other objects of worship or sources of guidance.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered, if Allah were to make the night continuous until the Day of Judgment, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?
interpretation: The verse poses a rhetorical question, asking the disbelievers to consider the consequences of a world without the light of God. It emphasizes the idea that God is the only source of light and guidance, and that without Him, the world would be plunged into darkness. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions on Judgment Day.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah were to make the night perpetual until the Day of Judgment, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then see?
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers and asks them to consider the possibility of Allah making the night perpetual until the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the idea that only Allah has the power to bring light in such a situation, and that no other deity can do so. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and authority, and encourages the disbelievers to reflect on their beliefs and turn to Allah for guidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And He has subjected to you, night and day, that you may rest therein and [that] you may seek from His bounty and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings of God, who has given us the night and day to rest and seek His bounty. The verse emphasizes the idea of gratitude, reminding us that our ability to rest and seek God's blessings is a result of His mercy and grace. It serves as a reminder to be thankful for the blessings we have and to recognize that they are a result of God's generosity and love.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And on the Day when He will call out to them, saying: 'Where are My partners, those who were supposed to help Me?',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, when God will call out to those who claimed to be His partners or associates in the worldly life. The verse suggests that those who were supposed to help God will not be found, implying that they were not true to their claims of loyalty and devotion to God. The verse serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not live up to their claims, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that their association with God is not a license to disobey Him.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We have not sent any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah. And had they, when they were unjust to themselves, come to you seeking forgiveness, then they would have found Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's messengers and the consequences of disobedience. The verse indicates that those who have been unjust to themselves and have ignored the messages of the prophets will not be forgiven, and their punishment will be severe. The verse also highlights the mercy and forgiveness of God, indicating that those who seek forgiveness will find it, but those who reject God's message will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them and We gave him of the treasures, which he hoarded. And he said to his people, 'Do not rejoice, for indeed, Allah does not love the rejoicing.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about Qarun, a member of the Israelites, who was given wealth and power by God. However, he used his position to oppress his own people and hoarded the wealth that was given to him. He warned his people not to rejoice, indicating that he was aware of the negative impact of his actions and the displeasure of God. The verse serves as a warning against oppression and the misuse of wealth and power, reminding believers to be mindful of their actions and the consequences of their deeds.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: And seek, through means of the Hereafter, the Home of the Hereafter, and do not neglect your portion of this world, and do good as Allah has been good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like the corruptors.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to strive for the Hereafter, the ultimate goal of human existence, while also fulfilling their duties in this world. It emphasizes the importance of leading a virtuous life and doing good deeds, as Allah has been good to us. The verse also warns against seeking corruption and causing harm to others, as Allah does not like those who spread corruption and destruction.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: And those who were given knowledge said: Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for him who believes and does righteousness, and none will be given except for the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the opinion of the knowledgeable people regarding the reward of Allah. They believe that the reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and that it is only given to those who are patient and persistent in their faith. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in faith, and serves as a reminder that true reward and happiness can only be achieved through righteousness and faith in Allah.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to spread God's message of peace, love, and forgiveness to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. It serves as a reminder that the Prophet's teachings are a source of guidance and inspiration for all those who seek to live a virtuous and righteous life.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And the ones who had been desirous of the place of the Hereafter, in the morning, they say, 'Indeed, Allah gives provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for whom He wills. Indeed, Allah is Aware of all things.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who desire the reward of the Hereafter, and how they recognize that God is the one who provides for His servants and restricts provision for whom He wills. The verse highlights God's knowledge and awareness of all things, indicating that He is aware of the intentions and actions of all His servants. The verse serves as a reminder that God is the sole provider and sustainer of all creation, and that He is aware of all things, including the actions and intentions of human beings.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: And whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed, then those who did evil deeds will not be rewarded except what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that individuals will be rewarded or punished based on their deeds, and that no one will be treated unfairly. The verse also highlights the difference between those who do good and those who do evil, and how their actions will determine their fate. The verse serves as a reminder to people to strive to do good and avoid evil, as it will ultimately lead to a better outcome for them in the afterlife.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder to you, [O Muhammad], and your people from the All-Merciful, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Qur'an as a reminder and a source of guidance for both Prophet Muhammad and his people. The use of 'Indeed' at the beginning of the verse underscores the importance of the message that follows. The phrase 'from the All-Merciful, the All-Knowing' highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a revelation from God, who is both merciful and all-knowing. The verse serves as a reminder to Prophet Muhammad and his people to adhere to the teachings of the Qur'an and to seek guidance from it in all aspects of their lives.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And had I not feared the persecution of the disbelievers, I would have been sent to you as a mercy from your Lord.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker expresses their desire to be sent as a mercy from God to the disbelievers, but they fear the persecution that they may face from those who reject the message. The verse highlights the struggle between the desire to spread God's message and the fear of persecution, and serves as a reminder that even the messengers of God faced challenges in their mission. It also emphasizes the idea that the message of Islam is one of mercy and guidance, and that it is intended to bring people closer to God and to guide them towards a righteous life.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And do not obscure the signs of Allah after they have been sent down to you, and invite your Lord and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and respecting the signs of Allah, which include the revelations and messages sent through prophets. The verse warns against obscuring or concealing these signs, which can be done by ignoring, denying, or distorting them. The verse also encourages the believers to turn to Allah and to avoid being among those who practice polytheism, that is, associating other deities with Allah. The verse highlights the significance of monotheism and the exclusive worship of Allah.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and warns against the worship of any other being or object, including celestial bodies like the sun and the moon. The verse instructs believers to prostrate only to Allah, the Creator of all things, and to no one else. The verse also highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's sovereignty and authority, and serving Him alone.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed generations before you, so that Allah may know those who believe and may know the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that God has destroyed entire generations in the past, emphasizing that their destruction was a means for God to distinguish between the believers and the disbelievers. The verse underscores the idea that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a means of testing and refining humanity's faith. The verse serves as a reminder to the reader that their actions have consequences in this life and the hereafter, and that God is always aware of their beliefs and actions.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: And whoever desires to meet Allah, the Term of Allah will come to him, and whoever meets Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the desire to meet God and the certainty of meeting Him. The phrase 'the Term of Allah' refers to the Day of Judgment, when everyone will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes that those who desire to meet God will indeed meet Him, and that God is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, indicating that He is aware of all our thoughts, words, and deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a life that is pleasing to God, as they will eventually face Him and be judged according to their deeds.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives, strives only for himself, indeed, Allah is Free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that those who strive in life, do so only for their own benefit, as Allah is self-sufficient and does not need anything from anyone. The verse encourages individuals to strive for their own spiritual growth and development, rather than seeking to impress or gain favor from Allah. It also highlights the idea that true success and fulfillment come from striving for what is good and righteous, rather than seeking material wealth or worldly gain.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will certainly remove from them their evil deeds and We will certainly reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between faith and good deeds. It emphasizes that belief and righteous actions are interconnected and that one cannot exist without the other. The verse also emphasizes the idea of reward and punishment, where those who have believed and done good deeds will have their sins forgiven and will be rewarded with the best of what they have done. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences and that living a life of faith and righteousness is essential for a better life in this world and the hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam by carrying them on the land and sea and providing them with good and pure things, and We have preferred them over many of those whom We have created with a marked preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon humanity, particularly in comparison to other creatures. The verse emphasizes the provision of good and pure things, indicating that God has provided for humanity's needs and well-being. Additionally, the verse notes that humanity has been preferred over other creatures, indicating a special status and responsibility for humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the blessings and favors that God has bestowed upon humanity and encourages gratitude and responsible action.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who believed in God and did good deeds. The phrase 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' describes a place of eternal bliss and happiness, where the believers will reside forever. The verse emphasizes the idea that the reward for faith and good deeds is not limited to this life, but extends into the afterlife, where the believers will enjoy eternal happiness and peace.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but when he is faced with tribulations, he says, 'This is not from Allah.' He will say, 'Evil has afflicted me. Surely Allah has no knowledge of what is in the breasts (of men).'
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who claim to believe in God and the Hereafter, but when they face difficulties or tribulations, they question God's authority and wisdom. They may say that the hardships they are facing are not from God, implying that God is either unaware of their suffering or unable to help them. The verse highlights the hypocrisy of such individuals, who claim to have faith but lack trust in God's plan and wisdom. It serves as a reminder that true faith is tested during times of hardship, and that one's belief in God should not waver in the face of adversity.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And God will know the believers and the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God is aware of those who truly believe in Him and those who are pretending to be believers, but are actually hypocrites. The verse suggests that God's knowledge of the believers and hypocrites is not limited to their outward appearances or actions, but rather He has complete knowledge of their inner states and intentions. This verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that ultimately, everyone will be judged based on their true beliefs and actions, not just their outward appearances.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And the disbelievers say to those who believe: 'Follow our way and we will bear your sins.' Never will they bear anything from their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who try to deceive the believers by telling them to follow their way of life and promising to bear their sins. However, the verse reveals that this promise is nothing but a lie, and that the disbelievers will not bear any of the believers' sins. The verse serves as a warning to the believers, reminding them to be cautious of such deceitful tactics and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they will carry their own burdens and the burdens of those whom they misled, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will be asked about the lies they fabricated.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who misled others and themselves, carrying the weight of their own sins and the burdens of those they misled. On Judgment Day, they will be held accountable for their actions and questioned about the lies they told and the falsehoods they spread. The verse serves as a warning against spreading false information and misleading others, reminding us of the consequences of such actions in the afterlife.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed among them for a thousand years, except for fifty years, and then the flood came and took them away, and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophet Noah and his mission to his people. The verse highlights the duration of Noah's stay among his people, which was a thousand years, and how he was patient and persistent in his efforts to guide them to the right path. Despite his efforts, the people refused to listen and continued to live in sin and injustice. The verse ends by mentioning the consequences of their actions, which was the flood that came and destroyed them. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding the warnings of God's messengers and living a righteous life, lest one suffers a similar fate.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a source of mercy and guidance for all people, rather than a source of destruction or punishment. The use of the plural "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to spread love, forgiveness, and peace among all people.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And Abraham said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him, for that is better for you, if you were to know.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is urging his people to worship Allah and live in obedience to Him. He reminds them that this is the best way to live, as it is the key to their well-being and happiness. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the greatness and power of Allah, and the need to submit to His will. It also emphasizes the importance of knowledge and understanding, indicating that the people should strive to learn and grow in their faith. Abraham's message is a reminder that true prosperity and success come from living a life of obedience to Allah, and that this is the only way to achieve true happiness and fulfillment.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You worship besides Allah only idols, and you create falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah have no provision. So, seek your provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: The verse addresses the issue of polytheism and the futility of worshiping anything else besides Allah. The verse emphasizes that the idols and false deities that people worship besides Allah have no power to provide for them or protect them. Instead, the verse encourages people to seek their provision and guidance from Allah alone, and to worship Him with gratitude. The verse serves as a reminder that ultimately, all provision and guidance come from Allah, and that true worship and gratitude are due to Him alone.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And indeed, they had already denied the truth before, so they wove a plot against the Prophet, saying, 'You are nothing but a clear magician!',
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who denied the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and plotted against him, accusing him of being a magician. The verse emphasizes that their denial and plotting were not new, but rather a continuation of the same behavior exhibited by previous nations who rejected the prophets sent to them. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's message is not based on magic or trickery, but is a clear and plain message from God, and that those who reject it will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe and everything in it by God in six days. The use of the word 'six days' is significant, as it emphasizes the idea that creation was a deliberate and deliberate process, rather than a random or accidental one. The verse also emphasizes God's power and ability to create, as well as His role as the sole creator of the universe. The phrase 'and there touched Us no weariness' underscores the idea that God's power is limitless and that He is not subject to fatigue or weakness.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, 'Travel through the earth and observe how He initiated the creation, then Allah will initiate the final creation. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.'
interpretation: This verse invites people to reflect on the signs of God's creation in the universe and to recognize His power and ability to bring about the final judgment. The verse emphasizes the idea that God is capable of anything and that He is the same God who initiated the creation in the first place. The verse encourages people to look around them and observe the beauty and complexity of creation, and to recognize that it is a sign of God's existence and power. The verse also serves as a reminder that God is the same God who will bring about the final judgment, and that He is capable of doing so at any moment.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you are receiving the Qur'an from the One who is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is not a human invention but a revelation from the Wise and Knowing God. The use of the name Muhammad in the verse serves to emphasize the prophetic role of Muhammad as the recipient of the Qur'an. The verse highlights the wisdom and knowledge of God, implying that the Qur'an contains guidance and wisdom for all aspects of life.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you are not [as great] in the earth nor in the heaven, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the weakness and vulnerability of human beings, both in the face of God's power and in their own existence. The verse suggests that humans are not as powerful as they think they are, and that they have no one to rely on or seek help from except Allah. The verse serves as a reminder of human limitations and the need to humble oneself before God, recognizing one's dependence on Him and seeking His guidance and protection.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and meeting with Him, such ones shall be despaired of My mercy, and such ones shall have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who reject the signs of God and deny the idea of meeting with Him. The verse warns that those who reject God's signs and do not believe in the Hereafter will be excluded from God's mercy and will face a painful punishment. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, indicating that it will be harsh and unrelenting.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And they had no answer except that they said, 'Kill him or burn him.' But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the truth of the Prophet Abraham. Instead of accepting the truth, they resorted to violence and suggested killing or burning the Prophet. However, God saved the Prophet from their evil plans and the fire they had kindled. The verse highlights the miraculous nature of the Prophet's deliverance and serves as a reminder to believers that God is always with those who believe in Him and will protect them from harm.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And He said, 'You have taken gods besides Allah as a means of mutual support between you in this life, then on the Day of Resurrection you will disown one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of polytheism and the futility of relying on false deities. The verse warns that on the Day of Judgment, those who worshiped idols will turn against each other, denying their association with one another, and will be left alone to face the punishment of God. The verse emphasizes the idea that only God can provide true help and support, and that those who put their faith in false deities will be left with nothing but the Fire of Hell as their refuge.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: And indeed, Abraham said, 'My Lord, I will migrate to my Lord, for He is the Almighty, the Wise.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham expresses his intention to migrate to his Lord, indicating his submission and devotion to God. The use of the phrase 'my Lord' twice emphasizes the personal relationship between Abraham and God, and the recognition of God's power and wisdom. The verse highlights Abraham's faith and trust in God's guidance and his willingness to follow God's commandments, even when it means leaving his home and family behind. It serves as an example for believers to follow in Abraham's footsteps and submit to God's will.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and made him a prophet, and We revealed to him the Book and gave him a reward in this world, and indeed, he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the prophets Isaac and Jacob, whom God gave as a gift to Abraham, and how God made them prophets and revealed the Book to them. The verse also mentions that Abraham will be among the righteous in the Hereafter. The verse highlights the importance of prophethood and the revelation of the Book as a means of guidance and a source of reward in both this life and the Hereafter. It also emphasizes the idea that the righteous will be rewarded in the Hereafter, serving as a reminder to believers to live a virtuous life in order to attain God's mercy and blessings.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And (remember) when Luqman said to his people, 'Indeed, you will be destroyed by the retribution (of God) if you continue to commit such sins.'
interpretation: Luqman, a wise and knowledgeable man, warned his people of the consequences of their sinful actions. He reminded them that they would face destruction if they continued to commit such sins. The verse highlights the importance of wisdom and knowledge in guiding people towards the right path and the consequences of ignoring such guidance.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the various trials and tribulations that people may face in life, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges, and assures those who are patient that they will receive good tidings and reward from God. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of testing one's faith and character, and that those who are patient and steadfast will be rewarded.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: And He said, 'I will certainly assist you against the wicked people.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is assuring the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that He will support him against the wicked people who are trying to harm him and his followers. The verse highlights God's promise to protect and assist those who are righteous and just, and serves as a reminder that God is always on the side of those who are oppressed and mistreated. The verse also emphasizes the importance of standing up against injustice and oppression, and seeking help from God in times of need.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town, for its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the arrival of God's messengers to Prophet Abraham with the news of the impending destruction of a town whose people had been unjust and sinful. The verse highlights the justice and mercy of God, as He sends His messengers to warn the people of the town of their impending punishment, giving them a chance to repent and change their ways. The verse also underscores the responsibility of the messengers to convey the message of God faithfully and the consequences of rejecting the message.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: And they say, 'We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the arrogance and complacency of those who think they are immune to God's punishment because of their wealth and children. They believe that their material possessions and offspring will protect them from accountability and punishment. The verse highlights the foolishness of this thinking and serves as a warning to those who are indulged in worldly riches and neglecting the spiritual aspect of life. It reminds them that material wealth and children are not a guarantee against God's punishment and that true protection comes from living a righteous life and following God's commands.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed and embarrassed by them, and they said, 'Do not fear, nor be sad, for we are with you, and your wife will be among the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene where the angels sent by God to Prophet Lot (AS) came to him and he was initially afraid and embarrassed by their presence. The angels reassured him, telling him not to fear or be sad, and that they were there to help and protect him and his family. The verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in God's plan, and how it can bring comfort and peace even in the face of adversity. It also underscores the role of the believers in supporting and encouraging one another in their faith.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town like this one while its people were unjust, so We razed them from the earth.
interpretation: This verse describes the destruction of towns that were similar to the one being addressed, where the people were unjust and deserving of punishment. The use of the word ' Razed' emphasizes the completeness of the destruction, leaving nothing but ruins. The verse serves as a warning to the current inhabitants of the town, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God to destroy those who reject His message.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And indeed, We have left behind a clear sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God has left behind a clear sign, a clear message, for a people who possess intellect and reasoning abilities. The verse emphasizes the importance of using one's intellect to understand and reflect on the signs of God, and to recognize the truth and wisdom in His message. It serves as a reminder that guidance and understanding come from God, but also requires human effort and responsibility to use one's intellect to recognize and follow the truth.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to the town of Midian, We sent their brother Shu'aib, saying, 'O my people, worship Allah, and fear the Day of Reckoning, and do not roam the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: In this verse, God sends Prophet Shu'aib to the town of Midian to warn them of the consequences of their evil deeds and to invite them to worship Allah and live righteously. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing the Day of Reckoning, indicating that the people of Midian were engaging in corrupt practices and needed to change their ways. The verse also highlights the role of prophets as messengers of God, sent to guide and warn their communities, and the responsibility of people to heed their message and live according to God's will.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And We have destroyed many a town like Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman, and Moses had come to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they could not outrun (the punishment).
interpretation: This verse mentions the destruction of several towns, including Qarun and Pharaoh, and attributes their downfall to their arrogance and rejection of God's message. The verse emphasizes that even though they had been warned through clear signs and prophets, such as Moses, they chose to ignore the warnings and continued to live in disobedience. Their punishment was inevitable and they could not escape it, despite their power and might. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and rejection of God's message, and encourages believers to remain humble and obedient to God.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: So, We punished each one of them because of their sins. Some were struck by the punishment of being buried alive in their homes, some were impaled by the horns of dams, and some were swallowed up by the earth, and some were drowned. It was not that Allah wronged them, but they wronged their own selves.
interpretation: The verse describes the various ways in which God punished different communities in the past for their sins. The punishments included being buried alive, being impaled by the horns of animals, being swallowed up by the earth, and drowning. The verse emphasizes that these punishments were not inflicted by God out of injustice or malice, but rather because of the people's own wrongdoing and disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder to those living in sin, warning them of the consequences of their actions and encouraging them to turn back to God and live righteously.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And those who took the calf [for worship] will surely come to know, and the angry [wrath] will surely come to know, and the foolish will surely come to know. And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon besides Him, and He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and power, indicating that He is aware of all things, including the idols and false deities that people worship besides Him. The phrase 'and He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise' serves to reinforce Allah's grandeur and wisdom, highlighting His ability to guide and protect His followers. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to put their trust in Allah and to recognize His ultimate authority and wisdom.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And such examples We strike for people, but none understand them except the wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the examples and lessons provided in the Qur'an are not just mere stories, but are meant to be taken as warnings and lessons for people to learn from. The phrase 'وما يعقلها إلا العالمون' suggests that only the wise and knowledgeable individuals are able to truly understand and appreciate the deeper meanings and significance behind these examples. The verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and wisdom in understanding the Qur'an and its teachings, and serves as a reminder to believers to strive for wisdom and understanding in their faith.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that the creation of the heavens and the earth is a manifestation of God's power and truth. The verse is a reminder to believers that the creation of the universe is not a random event, but rather a deliberate act of God's will. The verse also suggests that the creation of the universe is a sign of God's power and a reminder of His existence, and that believers should find comfort and guidance in this knowledge.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you from the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of reciting the Qur'an and establishing prayer as a means of avoiding immorality and wrongdoing. The verse also highlights the significance of remembering Allah, which is considered greater than any other form of worship. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of all human actions and is a warning to those who neglect their spiritual duties.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is better, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of respectful dialogue and coexistence between Muslims and People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians). It encourages Muslims to engage in discussions with them in a peaceful and respectful manner, focusing on the commonalities between the two groups, rather than the differences. The verse also highlights the unity of God, emphasizing that both Muslims and People of the Scripture worship the same God, and that submission to Him is the essence of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to approach interfaith dialogue with kindness, respect, and an open mind, and to seek common ground with people of other faiths.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And indeed, We have sent down to you the Book, and those who are given knowledge before it, they believe in it, and of the believers, some of them are those who believe in it, and none deny Our verses except the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the authenticity and authority of the Qur'an as a revelation from God. The verse states that those who were given knowledge before the Qur'an, such as the prophets and the angels, believe in it, and so do some of the believers. The verse also notes that only the disbelievers deny the verses of God, indicating that the rejection of the Qur'an is a sign of disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to hold fast to their faith and to be mindful of the consequences of rejecting God's revelation.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: And indeed, We have sent forth clear signs and portents to those who were given knowledge, but they have disputed the signs of Allah, out of pride and arrogance. Indeed, they are the ones who will be brought to account for their rejection of faith.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between those who have been given knowledge and those who reject the signs of God. The verse suggests that those who have been given knowledge are aware of the truth of God's signs, but they reject them out of pride and arrogance. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their rejection of God's signs and their lack of humility.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they say, 'If only signs were sent down to him from his Lord!' Say, 'The signs are with God, and I am a clear warner.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for miraculous signs from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to prove his prophethood. The verse responds by saying that the signs are with God, and that the Prophet's role is to convey the message and warn people clearly. The verse emphasizes that the signs are not necessary for the believers, as they have already recognized the truth, but rather for the disbelievers who are stubborn and arrogant. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's mission is not to perform miracles, but to convey the message of God's oneness and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah as a witness between me and you, and He is aware of what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - they are the losers.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that Allah is sufficient as a witness between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people. The verse also highlights the contrast between those who believe in Allah and those who reject Him. The phrase 'sufficient for me is Allah' signifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) relies solely on Allah as his witness, indicating his trust and faith in Him. The second part of the verse highlights the fate of those who reject Allah, describing them as losers. The verse serves as a reminder that true success and victory come from faith and obedience to Allah, while disbelief and rejection of Allah lead to loss and destruction.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment, but the punishment will come to them either at night or in the morning, and when it comes, they will be uprooted.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who reject God's message and instead of heeding the warning, they ask for the punishment to come quickly. The verse warns them that the punishment will come unexpectedly, either at night or in the morning, and when it does, they will be completely destroyed. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and their ultimate destruction.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They wish that the punishment would be hastened, but Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of those who reject God's message and refuse to believe in the hereafter. They mock the idea of punishment in the afterlife and wish for it to be hastened, thinking that it will never come to pass. However, the verse warns that Hell will ultimately encompass the disbelievers, signifying that their denial and disobedience will not save them from the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the certainty of the hereafter and the punishment that awaits them if they do not repent and turn to God.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: On a day when the punishment will overtake them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say: 'Taste what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of the Day of Judgment, where the punishment from God will come upon the wicked people from all directions, both from above and below. The verse emphasizes the idea of retribution, where the sinners will be made to experience the consequences of their own actions. The phrase 'Taste what you used to do' suggests that the punishment is a direct result of their own deeds, and that they have no one to blame but themselves. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the Day of Reckoning and the consequences of their actions.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O my servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the vastness of God's creation and the importance of worshiping Him alone. The use of the word 'My earth' signifies God's ownership and dominion over all of creation. The verse is a reminder to believers that they should direct their worship solely to God, without associating any partners or intermediaries. The verse also underscores the idea that God's blessings and provisions are abundant and available to all, and that humans should recognize and appreciate this bounty by worshiping Him with gratitude and devotion.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul shall taste death, then to Us they shall be returned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the afterlife. It reminds every individual that they will eventually die and be held accountable for their actions in this life. The verse also implies that the soul's journey does not end with death, but rather, it continues on to the afterlife, where each person will be judged based on their deeds in this life. The verse serves as a reminder to live a righteous life and to prepare for the hereafter.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, as a reward from God, and that which is with God is best for the righteous,
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for those who believed in God and did righteous deeds. The phrase 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' is a metaphor for Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and joy. The verse emphasizes the idea that the reward for the righteous is not limited to this life, but extends into the afterlife, where they will abide eternally. The phrase 'as a reward from God' highlights the idea that the reward is not something earned or deserved, but rather a gift from God's grace and mercy. The final phrase, 'and that which is with God is best for the righteous,' serves as a reminder that God's reward is not limited to material wealth or worldly success, but is something far greater and more valuable, a spiritual and eternal reward.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: And those who are patient and rely on their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of patience and trust in God, which are essential for believers. Patience is necessary to endure the difficulties and hardships of life, while trust in God means relying on Him for guidance and support. The combination of these two qualities is a sign of a strong faith and a deep connection with God. It emphasizes that true believers are those who are patient and have faith in God, and that these qualities are essential for a successful and fulfilling life.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kinds of old, the owners of the lofty buildings and the pleasant places, and the enemies of the messengers, and the punishment came to them in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of nations that were unjust and rejected God's messengers. The verse emphasizes the destruction of their 'lofty buildings and pleasant places', indicating that material possessions and worldly success are not a guarantee of salvation. The verse also highlights the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, which came 'in the morning or at noon', reminding the reader of the certainty of God's justice and the need to be mindful of one's actions.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: And Allah provides for whom He wills and restricts [the means of subsistence] unto whom He wills. Indeed, Allah of all things is Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the provision and sustenance of all living things. He is the one who provides for whom He wills and restricts the means of subsistence for whom He wills. The verse highlights Allah's knowledge and wisdom in managing the affairs of His creation. It serves as a reminder to believers that their sustenance and provision are in Allah's hands, and they should trust in His wisdom and plan. The verse also warns against the idea that wealth and provision are solely the result of one's own efforts, reminding us that true prosperity comes from Allah's blessings.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if We had sent a angel down to them, and he had spoken to them, they would have been excused, [and they would have been reprieved], and they would have not been destroyed, but [instead] they denied, so they were not reprieved.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even if God had sent an angel to the people, they would have still denied and disbelieved, leading to their destruction. The verse highlights the idea that the people's disbelief was not due to a lack of evidence or proof, but rather due to their own stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of humanity's own actions and choices.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And this worldly life is not but amusement and diversion, and indeed, the Hereafter is the real life, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary and fleeting nature of worldly life, which is compared to amusement and diversion. In contrast, the Hereafter is described as the real life, implying that it is the true and eternal existence. The verse suggests that people often prioritize the immediate pleasures and distractions of this life, neglecting the ultimate purpose and reality of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to keep their priorities in order and not be distracted by the temporary attractions of this world.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And when they embark on a ship, they call upon Allah, making their faith pure for Him alone, but when He delivers them to the shore, behold, they associate others with Him.
interpretation: The verse highlights the tendency of people to turn to God in times of need or distress, but once they are saved, they often forget their promise and start associating others with God, thereby showing ingratitude and a lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder to remain steadfast in one's belief and not to forget the favors of God once tribulations have passed.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: And they will be punished for what they have earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea of retribution and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that individuals will be held accountable for their deeds and will receive punishment or reward accordingly. The verse also underscores the idea of justice, implying that no one will be wronged and that everyone will receive what they deserve. This serves as a reminder to individuals to be mindful of their actions and to strive to live a virtuous life in order to avoid punishment and earn God's favor.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is not hell a dwelling place for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of inventing lies against Allah or denying the truth when it is presented. The verse equates such actions with disbelief, which leads to hell being the dwelling place for those who commit such acts. The verse warns against the dangers of lying and denying the truth, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of such actions in the hereafter.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And those who strive in Our cause, We will certainly guide them to Our ways.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the rewards that await those who strive in God's cause. The phrase 'strive in Our cause' refers to those who work towards spreading God's message and fighting against injustice. The verse promises that God will guide those who strive in His cause to the right path, indicating that they will be rewarded with spiritual enlightenment and guidance. The verse serves as an encouragement to believers to continue their efforts in promoting justice and righteousness, and to have faith that God will guide and support them in their endeavors.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين
