translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: And they will be brought low in the earth, and they will have no victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to follow their own desires and lusts. They will be humiliated and brought low in this life, and they will have no victory or success in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of submitting to God's will.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: In a few years, the matter of God will be accomplished, and those who have been oppressed will be triumphant.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate victory of the oppressed and the fulfillment of God's plan. The phrase 'In a few years' indicates that the wait will not be long, and that the oppressed will soon see justice served. The phrase 'the matter of God' refers to the ultimate triumph of good over evil and the establishment of God's rule on earth. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for those who are suffering injustice, reminding them that their oppression is only temporary and that God will ultimately bring justice and peace.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God will support and aid those who support and aid His cause, indicating that the believers will have the backing of God in their endeavors. The description of God as 'Powerful and Exalted in Might' serves to emphasize His authority and ability to help those who seek His assistance. The verse serves as a reminder that the believers should work towards promoting justice and righteousness, knowing that God is on their side and will support them in their efforts.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And Allah has not failed in His promise, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's faithfulness to His promises. The verse asserts that God's promise is always fulfilled, and His threats are not empty. The verse also highlights the ignorance of many people regarding God's promises and warnings, which can lead to their destruction. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are heedless of God's signs and warnings, reminding them of the consequences of their ignorance and the certainty of God's justice.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know the outer appearance of the life of this world, but they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse describes people who are knowledgeable about the superficial aspects of this life, such as material possessions and worldly success, but they are oblivious to the spiritual aspects of life and the hereafter. They are so consumed by their worldly pursuits that they neglect the importance of preparing for the afterlife. The verse serves as a reminder that true knowledge and wisdom come from recognizing the value of both this life and the hereafter, and that one should not be neglected at the expense of the other.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: And they have not apportioned the Merciful a share in their souls, so their reckoning is not except in error.
interpretation: The verse suggests that people have failed to recognize and appreciate the greatness and power of Allah, who is the Most Merciful. They have not given Him the due share in their lives, thoughts, and actions. As a result, their reckoning, or judgment, will be in error, and they will face consequences for their neglect and disbelief.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then there was punishment for those who did wrong, because they denied the verses of Allah and mocked at them.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of denying and mocking Allah's signs and revelations. The word 'punishment' emphasizes the severity of the consequences, indicating that those who reject Allah's message will face severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: Allah begins the creation, then He will repeat it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of creation and the eventual return of all things to God. The verse suggests that God is the originator of all creation and that everything will eventually return to Him. This can be interpreted as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly existence and the importance of living a life that is pleasing to God in order to achieve a positive outcome in the afterlife.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when the hour of judgment comes, the criminals will be filled with despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of judgment day when the wicked will be filled with despair and regret for their past deeds. The verse emphasizes the idea that the criminals will be overwhelmed by the realization of their own guilt and the severity of their punishment, leading them to feel hopeless and helpless in the face of God's justice. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, encouraging them to repent and turn to God before it is too late.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And they had no one to protect them from Allah's punishment, and they were not helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete helplessness and isolation of those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. Not only do they lack any effective intercessors or allies to protect them from God's punishment, but they are also deprived of the guidance and support that comes from faith in Allah. Their rejection of Allah's message has left them spiritually vulnerable and without any hope of protection or rescue from the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And the Day when the Hour will rise, the guilty ones will be struck with despair.
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when the guilty will be filled with despair as they face the consequences of their actions. The 'Hour' refers to the Day of Judgment, which will be a time of reckoning and punishment for those who have lived in disobedience to God's commands. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the event, indicating that the guilty will be taken by surprise and will have no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the certainty of God's judgment and the need to turn to righteousness.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون

translation: And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in gardens of pleasure, rejoicing in their Lord's gift.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for those who believed in God and lived a righteous life. The phrase 'gardens of pleasure' refers to Paradise, where believers will enjoy the blessings and favors of God. The phrase 'rejoicing in their Lord's gift' highlights the fact that the believers will be grateful for the blessings they received and will be content with their fate. The verse emphasizes the idea that living a righteous life and having faith in God leads to a joyful and fulfilling outcome in the afterlife.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: And as for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, and the meeting of the Hereafter, they are the companions of the Fire; they will be therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the idea of an afterlife. They will be punished in the Fire of Hell, where they will remain forever. The verse emphasizes the severity of their disbelief and the certainty of their punishment, serving as a warning to those who reject God's message.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Praise be to Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, and Who made the angels messengers having wings, two, three, four. And He adds to creation what He wills.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for His power and wisdom in creating the universe and all that it contains. The mention of the angels with wings, two, three, and four, is a reference to their role as messengers and protectors, emphasizing their submission to Allah's will. The verse also highlights Allah's ability to add to His creation as He pleases, indicating His infinite power and wisdom.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: And to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and when the angels and the Spirit descend therein.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and dominion over all creation, both in the heavens and the earth. The mention of the angels and the Spirit descending suggests a connection between the spiritual realm and the physical world, highlighting God's presence and control over all aspects of existence. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the importance of acknowledging and praising Him for His blessings.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: And the life comes out of the dead, and the dead comes out of the life, and the earth is revived after its death, and similarly you will be brought out (of the graves).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the cyclical nature of life and death, where life emerges from death and death emerges from life. The verse also highlights the revival of the earth after its death, indicating the cyclical nature of life and death in the natural world. The verse serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of life and death, and the certainty of our own resurrection, just as the earth is revived after its death.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind from clay, then We made you into tribes and nations, that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that all human beings are created from the same source, clay, and are equal in the eyes of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and respecting the diversity of humanity, where people are divided into tribes and nations, not to create divisions or hierarchies, but to allow for the recognition and appreciation of each other's unique qualities and attributes. The verse also reminds us that true nobility is not based on race, ethnicity, or nationality, but on righteousness and piety. God, the All-Knowing and Acquainted, is aware of all human actions and intentions, and will judge each person based on their deeds and faith.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And among His signs is that He created for you, from your own selves, spouses that you may find comfort in them, and He has placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of God's creation of spouses for humanity. The verse emphasizes that the creation of spouses is a sign of God's power and wisdom, as it is a testament to His ability to create harmony and love between individuals. The verse also emphasizes the importance of affection and mercy in relationships, indicating that these qualities are a manifestation of God's divine attributes. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate the beauty and complexity of human relationships and to recognize the divine origin of love and companionship.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and there is no god except Allah, and indeed, the Hour is coming, so forgive with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and dominion over the universe, highlighting His role as the sole creator of the heavens, earth, and everything in between. The verse also mentions the coming of the Hour, a time of judgment and reckoning, and encourages believers to forgive others with kindness and compassion. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and the importance of living a virtuous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And from His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, the One who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse highlights the beauty and majesty of God's creation, specifically mentioning the night, day, sun, and moon. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and respecting the Creator, rather than the creation itself. The verse warns against idolizing the celestial bodies, and instead, encourages believers to direct their worship towards the One who created them. This verse serves as a reminder of the proper object of worship and the relationship between the Creator and the created.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and He sends down from the sky water, reviving the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: The verse highlights the miraculous nature of lightning and rain, which are both powerful natural phenomena that evoke feelings of awe and fear in humans. The verse suggests that these natural events are not just random occurrences, but rather signs from God that demonstrate His power and control over the universe. The verse also emphasizes the reviving effect of rain on the earth, which is seen as a metaphor for the spiritual revival that people can experience through their belief in God. The verse encourages people to reflect on these signs and to recognize the presence of God in their lives.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among His signs is that the heavens and the earth are held in His command, then when He calls you, you will be brought out of the earth.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and control over the universe, emphasizing that both the heavens and the earth are under His command. The verse also mentions the eventual return of the souls to God, indicating that the present life is a testing ground and that ultimate judgment will come when God calls us back to Himself. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human actions and the certainty of the afterlife.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and there is not a single thing but that it has a protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that God is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe, and that everything in it, including the heavens, the earth, and all that is between them, has a protector or guardian. The verse suggests that God's sovereignty and control extend to every aspect of creation, and that nothing exists outside of His knowledge and power. The verse also serves as a reminder of the responsibility that comes with this knowledge, and encourages believers to live their lives in accordance with God's will and to seek His protection and guidance in all things.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe and everything in it by God in six days. The use of the phrase 'and there touched Us no weariness' emphasizes God's infinite power and lack of fatigue in creating the universe, indicating that the creation was effortless and easy for God. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and majesty, and the infinite distance between God and His creation.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And put forward an example for them, [that of] a man who owned a slave whom he had bought and then had sex with him. Thus, do you believe in your Lord's punishment?
interpretation: The verse presents an example to illustrate the concept of God's punishment. The example is that of a man who owns a slave and has sexual relations with him. The verse asks the reader to consider whether they believe in God's punishment, implying that the punishment is a consequence of the man's actions. The verse serves to emphasize the idea that God's punishment is not limited to the afterlife, but can also be experienced in this life. The use of the metaphor of the slave and his master highlights the power dynamics at play in situations of oppression and injustice, and serves as a warning to those who exploit and mistreat others.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And adopt the way of your Lord, the upright religion, the nature in which Allah has created the people, there is no change to the creation of Allah, that is the upright religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the natural way of life that Allah has created for humanity, which is the upright religion. The verse stresses that this natural way of life is unchangeable and that it is the only correct religion. However, the verse also notes that most people are unaware of this fact and are not following the upright religion. The verse serves as a reminder to people to adopt the natural way of life and to avoid straying from it.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And remember Abraham said: 'My Lord, make this city a secure and peaceful place, and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham prays to God to make Mecca a safe and peaceful place and to protect him and his descendants from idolatry. The verse highlights Abraham's devotion to God and his commitment to monotheism. It also underscores the importance of avoiding the worship of idols and remaining faithful to the one true God. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid the temptation of polytheism.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: And those who have divided their religion and have become sects, every faction rejoicing in what they have.
interpretation: The verse refers to the division of religion and the emergence of different sects, each group rejoicing in their own beliefs and practices. The verse highlights the diversity of religious beliefs and practices, and how each group has its own unique interpretation of religious truth. The verse serves as a reminder that religion is a deeply personal and subjective aspect of human identity, and that there is no one universally accepted truth. Instead, people have different perspectives and understanding of the divine, and it is up to each individual to seek their own spiritual path.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when the people were touched by the adversity, they called upon their Lord, entreating Him in secret; then when He gave them a taste of mercy, behold, a group of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights the tendency of humans to turn to God in times of adversity, but also their propensity to forget and associate others with God's blessings when they are granted relief. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's favors and not attributing them to other sources. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of God's blessings and to avoid slipping into polytheism.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: They will be punished for their sins, and they will not be able to escape the punishment. They will be surrounded by it, and they will be filled with regret and sorrow for their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting God's message and the punishment that awaits those who choose to disobey Him. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a result of their own actions and that they will not be able to escape it. The use of the word 'surrounded' suggests that the punishment will be all-encompassing and inescapable. The final phrase, 'and they will be filled with regret and sorrow for their deeds', underscores the idea that the punishment will not only be physical but also emotional and spiritual, leading to deep remorse and regret for their actions.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his role as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message and serves as a reminder to Muslims to follow his example and spread love, kindness, and mercy to all people.
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We bestowed upon them a favor, they rejoiced in it, but if they were afflicted by a calamity, they were consumed by despair.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ingratitude of people who forget God's blessings and become arrogant during times of prosperity, but when faced with adversity, they lose hope and faith. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude and trust in God's plan, even in the face of hardship. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain mindful of God's favors and to maintain their faith during both good times and bad.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: And indeed, We have seen the opulence of the heavens and the earth, and We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the conquest of Mecca, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers were able to conquer the city and establish Islam as the dominant religion. The verse emphasizes the idea that the victory was not due to the Prophet's own strength or power, but rather due to the will of God, who gives victory to whom He pleases. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is not due to their own efforts, but rather due to the blessings and mercy of God.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And give to the near relative his right, and to the poor and the wayfarer. That is best for those who desire the countenance of Allah, and it is they who will be successful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving to the needy, specifically the near relative, the poor, and the wayfarer. It stresses that this act of charity is not only a moral obligation but also a means of seeking God's pleasure and blessings. The verse also highlights the connection between generosity and success, indicating that those who are generous and give to others will be successful in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And what you give in charity, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah, it will be increased for you in reward, and you will be given a generous reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of giving charity with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure, rather than seeking to show off or gain praise from others. The verse promises that such charity will be rewarded with an increase in blessings and a generous reward in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that true charity is done for the sake of Allah alone, and that it is not about seeking recognition or praise from others, but rather about seeking to please Allah and earn His reward.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: It is Allah who has created you, then He will cause you to die, and then He will bring you back to life, then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you back to life, and then to Us will be your return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and control of Allah over all aspects of human life and death. It highlights the cyclical nature of life and death, where humans are created, live, die, and are brought back to life, only to return to Allah ultimately. The verse serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of human existence and the certainty of death and the afterlife. It also underscores the idea that humans will be held accountable for their actions in this life, and that their ultimate destiny is to return to Allah. The verse is a call to reflection and a reminder of the purpose of human existence, which is to worship and serve Allah alone.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, 'Travel through the earth and see how was the end of the criminals.'
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to invite people to reflect on the fate of those who lived in the past and were destroyed by God's punishment. The verse suggests that the people of the past were more powerful and numerous than the polytheists of Mecca, but they were still destroyed for their sins. The verse serves as a warning to the Meccans, reminding them that they too will face the same fate if they continue to reject God's message.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: Therefore turn your face towards the religion of pure monotheism, before there comes a Day from Allah which cannot be averted.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of embracing the true monotheistic faith and turning away from all forms of polytheism and idolatry. The phrase 'before there comes a Day from Allah which cannot be averted' suggests that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and will bring about a complete transformation of the current state of affairs. The verse serves as a reminder that one should not procrastinate in their spiritual journey and should turn towards God before it's too late.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: And whoever disbelieves in the Oneness of Allah, then surely his deeds are vain; and whoever does righteous deeds, then surely they will be rewarded with the most excellent reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of belief in the Oneness of Allah and the consequences of disbelief. It warns that those who reject the idea of the Oneness of Allah, their deeds will be in vain and they will not be rewarded in the afterlife. On the other hand, those who do righteous deeds will be rewarded with the most excellent reward, indicating that the reward is directly proportional to the good deeds done in this life. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of belief and good deeds in Islam and the consequences of rejecting the fundamental principle of the Oneness of Allah.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Righteous deeds will be their recompense, and they will have an honored return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between faith and good deeds. It emphasizes that true belief is not just a matter of professing one's faith, but also involves doing good deeds. The verse promises that those who believe and do righteous deeds will be guided by their Lord and will receive a reward for their good deeds. The phrase 'an honored return' suggests that their ultimate reward will be in the afterlife, where they will be honored and respected for their faith and good deeds.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And among His signs is that He sends forth the winds as bearers of good tidings and to warn them of His mercy, and to cause the ships to sail at sea by His command, and to seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and mercy, as demonstrated through His control over the winds. The winds are described as 'bearers of good tidings' and 'warners' of God's mercy, indicating that they bring both blessings and warnings to humanity. The verse also mentions the role of winds in sailing ships, which represents the facilitation of travel and trade, and the provision of sustenance for humanity. The verse concludes by emphasizing the importance of gratitude, as humans are encouraged to recognize and appreciate God's bounty in their lives.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And indeed, We have sent messengers before you to their own people, and they came to them with clear signs. But those who were unjust rejected them, and We punished them. And it was rightfully due upon Us to help the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the pattern of God's justice throughout history. God has consistently sent prophets to guide people and warn them of the consequences of their actions. However, those who reject the prophets and continue to live in sin will face punishment. The verse emphasizes that it is a just and necessary act for God to help the believers and punish the wicked. The phrase 'it was rightfully due upon Us' underscores the idea that God's intervention is not a personal vendetta, but rather a necessary act of justice to maintain balance and order in the world.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: And Allah is He who sends the winds as a glad tiding before His mercy, and We drop from the sky pure water that Our servants may thereby be reminded.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah sends winds as a sign of His mercy and drops pure water from the sky to remind His servants of His power and grace. The verse highlights the idea that Allah's mercy and blessings are not limited to one group of people, but are available to all who are willing to recognize and acknowledge His greatness. The use of the word 'glad tiding' suggests that the winds and the rain are a source of joy and happiness for those who are grateful for Allah's blessings.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And indeed, they were about to be misled before it was sent to them, and they were in a state of confusion and doubt.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people were on the verge of being misled and were in a state of confusion and doubt before the revelation of the Qur'an. The verse implies that the people were searching for guidance and were in a state of spiritual turmoil, and that the revelation of the Qur'an was a response to their search for truth and guidance. The verse highlights the idea that the Qur'an is a source of guidance and clarity for those who are seeking the truth and seeking to be guided.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: And indeed, We have given you clear signs and examples from the past, and We have given you a warning from the punishment of Allah, so that you may be mindful and fear Allah, and that it may serve as a lesson to those who are endowed with understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of learning from past events and examples, and how they can serve as a warning for those who are endowed with understanding. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment of Allah is a reality that should be taken seriously, and that it is a lesson for those who are willing to learn and be mindful of their actions. The verse also underscores the idea that the Qur'an itself is a clear sign and a warning for those who are willing to listen and reflect.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We had sent a wind and they had been annihilated, they would have said, 'Indeed, it was but a single blow, and they would have been destroyed by a fierce hurricane.
interpretation: This verse suggests that even in the face of destruction, people tend to downplay the severity of the situation and attribute it to a single, unfortunate event rather than acknowledging the true nature of their destruction. The verse highlights the tendency of people to deny the consequences of their actions and to shift the blame away from themselves. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of our actions are not to be taken lightly and that we must take responsibility for our choices.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: And indeed, you will not cause the dead to hear, nor will you cause the deaf to hear the call when they turn their backs in retreat.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in front of the disbelievers who refuse to listen to his message. The verse uses the metaphor of the dead and the deaf to convey the idea that just as the dead cannot hear the call of the living, and the deaf cannot hear the call of those who speak to them, similarly, the disbelievers who turn their backs in retreat cannot be made to listen to the Prophet's message. The verse highlights the limitations of the Prophet's mission and the fact that he cannot force people to believe or listen to him. It also serves as a reminder that guidance is only from Allah, and that the Prophet's role is only to convey the message.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And had not God turned back their evil deeds, they would have been destroyed. And indeed, the punishment will come to them suddenly, while they are unaware.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's mercy and patience with those who have strayed from the righteous path. Despite their wrongdoing, God has not yet destroyed them, giving them a chance to repent and turn to Him. However, the verse also warns that the punishment will come unexpectedly, when they least expect it, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's actions and recognizing the signs of God's mercy.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: Allah is He Who created you from weakness, then He gave you strength after weakness, then He gave you weakness after strength, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Able.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and wisdom of Allah in creating and guiding humanity. The verse emphasizes the transformation of human beings from a state of weakness to strength and then back to weakness, indicating the cyclical nature of life and the constant need for dependence on Allah. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, as He is the All-Knowing and All-Able, capable of creating and guiding humanity according to His will.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: And on the day when the hour will rise, the criminals will sweat, their sweat will be (like) blood, and their faces will be twisted in horror.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of judgment day, where the wicked will be filled with fear and anxiety as they face their punishment. The sweat that they produce will be like blood, indicating the severity of their guilt and the terror they feel. The twisting of their faces in horror is a sign of their anguish and remorse for their past deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith said: 'Indeed, you have remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. This is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of those who were given knowledge and faith when they saw the Day of Resurrection. They recognized that the Day of Resurrection had arrived, but they also realized that they had not taken advantage of their knowledge and faith during their lifetime. The verse highlights the importance of acting upon one's knowledge and faith, rather than just possessing it. It also emphasizes the idea that one's actions will be of no use on the Day of Resurrection if they did not live according to their knowledge and faith during their lifetime.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: On that day, those who were unjust will not benefit from their excuses, nor will they be able to appease [Allah].
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who have lived a life of injustice and disobedience will not be able to offer any excuses or appease God on the Day of Judgment. Their attempts to justify their actions or seek forgiveness will be futile, as their deeds have already been recorded and their fate has been sealed. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that they cannot rely on empty excuses or pleas for mercy. The only way to avoid this fate is to repent and make amends for their wrongdoing while they still have the chance.
orig: فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And indeed, We have put forth for the people in this Qur'an from every example, that they may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the abundance of examples and lessons found in the Qur'an, which are intended to serve as reminders for humanity. The verse specifically addresses those who reject faith, implying that they are neglecting the signs and warnings contained within the Qur'an. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role in conveying moral lessons and serving as a reminder to those who have forgotten or turned away from God's message.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون

translation: Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: The verse describes how God seals the hearts of those who are ignorant and do not seek knowledge. The verse implies that the lack of knowledge and understanding leads to spiritual blindness and hardening of the heart. The phrase 'Thus does Allah seal over' signifies that the sealing is a divine intervention, a consequence of the individual's choice to remain in a state of ignorance. The verse warns against the dangers of ignorance and emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding in order to spiritually grow and connect with God.
orig: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, and those who were given knowledge know that it is the truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty and truth of God's promise, which is a recurring theme throughout the Qur'an. The verse specifically addresses those who have knowledge and understanding, indicating that they are aware of the truth of God's promise and its inevitability. The verse serves as a reminder to those who are skeptical or doubtful, encouraging them to trust in God's promise and to live their lives accordingly.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies a decisive and unambiguous triumph, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is plainly visible and evident to all. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is not due to their own efforts alone, but is a result of God's favor and blessing. It encourages them to continue on the path of righteousness and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: هدى ورحمة للمحسنين

translation: And they who are constant in their prayer and give zakah and they, in the Hereafter, are sure.
interpretation: The verse describes the characteristics of the righteous people who are consistent in their prayer and charity. They are certain of their faith in the afterlife and are confident that their good deeds will be rewarded. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and charity as means of purifying one's soul and ensuring a place in paradise.
orig: الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

translation: Those are the ones who are on the right path from their Lord, and they will be successful.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who follow the guidance of their Lord and are on the path of righteousness. The verse indicates that they will be successful in this life and the hereafter. The phrase 'على هدى من ربهم' means 'on the path of their Lord' and implies that they are following God's guidance and are under His protection. The word 'مفلحون' means 'successful' and implies that they will achieve their goals and be rewarded for their good deeds.
orig: أولئك على هدى من ربهم وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And among the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead from the way of Allah, and they will have a degrading punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about those who use their words and speech to mislead others from the path of God. They may use eloquent language, humor, or other forms of entertainment to distract people from the truth and lead them astray. The verse warns that such individuals will face a humiliating punishment for their actions, as they have chosen to prioritize temporary pleasure and fame over the eternal reward of living a righteous life.
orig: ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث ليضل عن سبيل الله بغير علم ويتخذها هزوا أولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he says: 'Fables of the ancient ones!'
interpretation: The verse describes a person who, when confronted with the Qur'anic verses, dismisses them as mere fables or stories of old. The word 'fables' in Arabic is 'amthal', which implies a lack of substance or truth. The person's response indicates a lack of faith and a refusal to accept the message of the Qur'an. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Qur'an and highlights the consequences of such rejection.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليه آياتنا ولى مستكبرا كأن لم يسمعها كأن في أذنيه وقرا فبشره بعذاب أليم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them are gardens of Paradise as a reward for their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith and do good deeds. The phrase 'gardens of Paradise' is used to describe the reward, emphasizing the beauty and joy that awaits the righteous in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the idea that faith and good deeds are interconnected, and that one cannot exist without the other. The verse serves as a motivation for believers to live a righteous life and to strive for spiritual growth and development.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات النعيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own kind, and the example of the peoples of 'Ad and Thamud.
interpretation: The verse mentions the destruction of the people of 'Ad and Thamud as an example of God's power and judgment. The people of 'Ad were known for their arrogance and refusal to listen to the prophet Hud, who was sent to guide them. As a result, God destroyed them with a fierce wind that lasted for seven days and nights. The people of Thamud, on the other hand, were known for their ingratitude and disobedience, and they were destroyed by an earthquake. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobeying God and ignoring His signs.
orig: خالدين فيها وعد الله حقا وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of the word 'worlds' signifies that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all of humanity. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his mission to spread love, peace, and forgiveness among people. It also underscores the idea that the Prophet's teachings are not limited to religious aspects but also encompass social, moral, and ethical values that promote the well-being of humanity.
orig: خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وبث فيها من كل دابة وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity's innermost thoughts and feelings. The phrase 'We know what their own selves whisper to them' suggests that God is aware of the secret thoughts and desires that people may not even share with others, and that He is closer to them than their own jugular vein. This verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-present, and that He is always aware of the thoughts and actions of humanity. It also emphasizes the idea that humans cannot hide anything from God, and that He is always near, watching and guiding them.
orig: هذا خلق الله فأروني ماذا خلق الذين من دونه بل الظالمون في ضلال مبين

translation: And indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], the clear victory and the manifest triumph. And indeed, We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest triumph. And We have given you [O Muhammad], the praise and the gratitude [of Allah] and that you may be grateful [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes that this victory is both clear and manifest, indicating that it is evident and undeniable. The verse also emphasizes the importance of gratitude and praise to God, as a means of expressing appreciation for the blessings bestowed upon the Prophet and the Muslim community. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and expressing gratitude to God for His favors, and the responsibility of the Prophet and the Muslim community to do so.
orig: ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة أن اشكر لله ومن يشكر فإنما يشكر لنفسه ومن كفر فإن الله غني حميد

translation: And recall when Luqman said to his son, while advising him, 'My son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, associating partners with Allah is a great injustice.'
interpretation: Luqman, a wise and righteous man, advises his son to avoid associating partners with Allah, emphasizing that shirk (the act of associating partners with Allah) is a grave injustice. This verse highlights the importance of monotheism and the belief in the Oneness of God, which is a central tenet of Islam. It also underscores the significance of parents' guidance and advice to their children, as Luqman is depicted as a father who values his son's spiritual well-being and seeks to protect him from the grave consequences of shirk.
orig: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. The verse emphasizes the value and worth of human life, and serves as a reminder that humans are special and unique in the eyes of God. It also underscores the responsibility that comes with this honor, as humans are expected to live up to their potential and fulfill their purpose in life, which is to worship and obey God. The verse also speaks to the importance of parents and the role they play in shaping the next generation, as they are responsible for guiding their children and teaching them the ways of God.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حملته أمه وهنا على وهن وفصاله في عامين أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind before you, but you do not know it. And indeed, We have warned you with examples of the previous generations, but you are a people who deny the warning.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the disbelievers and reminding them that they are not the first people to be destroyed for their sins. The verse warns them that they will face the same fate as those who came before them if they continue to reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also emphasizes that the disbelievers are ignoring the lessons of history and the warnings of God, which are evident in the destruction of previous nations. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to any particular nation or time period, and that those who reject the message of Islam will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي ثم إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O my son, indeed this world is a mere illusion, but the Hereafter is the real life, if only they knew.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the temporary and fleeting nature of this world and encourages people to focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter. The use of the phrase 'mere illusion' suggests that worldly things are not only temporary but also deceptive and unreliable. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing the true nature of this world and the significance of the Hereafter, which is the ultimate reality. The verse also implies that those who are aware of this reality are the ones who truly know and understand the purpose of life.
orig: يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل فتكن في صخرة أو في السماوات أو في الأرض يأت بها الله إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: O son of Adam, perform the prayer and command what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what has afflicted you, indeed that is from the steadfastness of the matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prayer, righteousness, and patience in the face of adversity. It encourages the believer to stay steadfast in their faith and to remain committed to doing good deeds, even in the face of hardship. The verse also highlights the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil, indicating that these actions are a part of the believer's responsibility towards God and their community. The verse serves as a reminder that patience and perseverance are essential qualities for a believer, and that they will be rewarded for their steadfastness in the face of adversity.
orig: يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك إن ذلك من عزم الأمور

translation: And do not strut arrogantly on the earth, for you will certainly not tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: The verse prohibits people from strutting arrogantly on earth and warns them against feeling superior to others. It emphasizes that no matter how powerful or great a person may feel, they are still subject to God's will and cannot change the natural order of things. The verse also implies that arrogance can lead to a person's downfall and that humility is a necessary quality for a righteous life.
orig: ولا تصعر خدك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إن الله لا يحب كل مختال فخور

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the compassionate nature of the Prophet Muhammad's mission. He was sent by God to guide humanity and bring them out of darkness and ignorance. The use of the word 'mercy' highlights the Prophet's role as a source of compassion and guidance, rather than a source of punishment or vengeance. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims that their faith should be centered around compassion, mercy, and the well-being of all people, rather than harshness, judgment, or vengeance.
orig: واقصد في مشيك واغضض من صوتك إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير

translation: Have you not seen how Allah has given you examples in the heavens and the earth, and in the provision He has given you, both visible and hidden? Yet there are people who argue about Allah without knowledge, without guidance, and without an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs and evidence of God's existence and power that are present in the natural world and in the blessings He has bestowed upon humanity. The verse also admonishes those who argue against the existence of God without proper knowledge or guidance. It emphasizes that these individuals are lacking in both understanding and a divine scripture that could enlighten them. The verse serves as a reminder to appreciate and recognize the signs of God's greatness and to seek guidance from Him through His revelations.
orig: ألم تروا أن الله سخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they said, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing, even though the devil was calling them to the punishment of the burning.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to follow the revelation of Allah. Instead of embracing the truth, they chose to cling to their ancestral traditions and beliefs, even though they knew that those traditions were based on falsehood and led to destruction. The verse highlights the danger of blindly following tradition and the importance of questioning and challenging established beliefs in the light of divine revelation. The devil's role in misleading people is also emphasized, as he invites people to reject the truth and follow falsehood, leading them to the punishment of the burning.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله قالوا بل نتبع ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان الشيطان يدعوهم إلى عذاب السعير

translation: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good, then he will have a reward from his Lord. And whoever turns away, then indeed, Allah will bring about, after hardship, ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submission to God and doing good deeds. The phrase 'submits his face' signifies a person's willingness to surrender their will to God's will, and to live according to His commandments. The reward for such submission is a reference to the spiritual and worldly benefits that come from living a righteous life. The second part of the verse addresses those who turn away from God's path and warns them that after a period of ease and prosperity, they will face hardship and difficulty. The verse encourages believers to persevere and remain steadfast in their faith, as the ultimate reward for their efforts will come from God.
orig: ومن يسلم وجهه إلى الله وهو محسن فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى وإلى الله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And none can escape Allah's punishment, so do not feel sorry for them, for Allah will not forgive them, and their destination is hell, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that no one can escape God's punishment, and therefore, believers should not feel sorry for those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The verse underscores the certainty of God's punishment and the fact that it is easy for God to execute it. The verse also highlights the final destination of those who reject God's message, which is hell. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره إلينا مرجعهم فننبئهم بما عملوا إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: نمتعهم قليلا ثم نضطرهم إلى عذاب غليظ

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns of people who were unjust, and We brought their destruction upon them in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of injustice and disobedience, emphasizing that God's punishment can come at any moment, without warning. The use of 'morning' and 'noon' underscores the idea that the punishment was sudden and unexpected, leaving the sinners no time to repent or make amends. The verse also underscores the idea that the destruction of these towns was not just a natural disaster, but a direct result of God's judgment and wrath upon those who had rejected His commands and lived in disobedience to Him.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, for Allah is the Most High, the Most Praised.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and ownership over all of creation, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'Allah is the Most High' signifies His supremacy and dominion over all things, while 'the Most Praised' highlights His glory and majesty. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's greatness and the importance of recognizing and submitting to His will.
orig: لله ما في السماوات والأرض إن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: And if We had wished to destroy the signs of God, We would have punished them [the disbelievers] with a painful punishment. But [instead], We leave the false gods they attribute to Us [alone], and We seal their ears and their hearts, so they do not understand.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over the disbelievers. The verse suggests that God could have destroyed the signs of disbelief and punished the disbelievers, but instead, He chooses to leave their false gods and allow them to continue in their disbelief. The verse also highlights the idea that God has sealed the ears and hearts of the disbelievers, indicating that they are unable to understand or hear the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and continue to live in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God.
orig: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: And your creation or your resurrection is not but as a single soul; indeed Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of humanity, suggesting that all human beings are equal in the eyes of God and that their creation and resurrection are interconnected. The verse also highlights God's attributes of hearing and seeing, signifying that He is aware of all human actions and thoughts, and that He will hold each individual accountable for their deeds in the afterlife.
orig: ما خلقكم ولا بعثكم إلا كنفس واحدة إن الله سميع بصير

translation: And have you not seen that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [on its course] to an appointed term, and that Allah is aware of what you do?
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and control of Allah over the natural world. The verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of time, with day and night constantly replacing each other, and the sun and moon following their predetermined courses. The verse serves as a reminder to humans that Allah is fully aware of their actions and is constantly observing them, emphasizing the accountability of human actions and the certainty of divine justice.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري إلى أجل مسمى وأن الله بما تعملون خبير

translation: And that Allah is the Truth and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and that Allah is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. It stresses that Allah is the only deity worthy of worship and that all other deities or objects of worship are false and inferior. The phrase 'Allah is the Most High, the Great' highlights God's supremacy and majesty, signifying that He is above all things and worthy of all praise. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to focus their devotion solely on Allah and to avoid associating partners with Him.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: And have you seen the ship sailing through the sea by the grace of Allah, that He may show you of His signs? Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful [person].
interpretation: This verse invites the reader to reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation, specifically the sailing ship, which moves gracefully through the vast ocean by Allah's grace. The verse highlights the connection between the natural world and the divine, emphasizing that the beauty and complexity of creation are signs of Allah's power and wisdom. The verse also underscores the importance of gratitude and patience, suggesting that these qualities are essential for recognizing and appreciating the signs of Allah's mercy and guidance.
orig: ألم تر أن الفلك تجري في البحر بنعمت الله ليريكم من آياته إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when a wave covers them like a shade, they call upon Allah, being sincere to Him in religion. But when He brings them to the shore, behold, they return to their ways, being ungrateful for Our signs.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation where people turn to God in times of hardship, but once they are saved, they quickly forget about their promises and return to their old ways, showing ingratitude towards God's blessings. The verse highlights the duality of human nature, where people are quick to seek help from God in times of need, but forget about Him when things are going well. This verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to show gratitude to God for His blessings.
orig: وإذا غشيهم موج كالظلل دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر فمنهم مقتصد وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا كل ختار كفور

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when a father will not avail his son, nor will a son avail his father. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the life of this world delude you, nor let the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God and the Day of Judgment, when family ties and worldly possessions will be of no avail. The verse warns against being deluded by the temporal life of this world and the deceitful nature of Shaitan (Satan), who tries to lead people astray from the path of God. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on one's spiritual well-being and to prioritize one's relationship with God, rather than being consumed by worldly pursuits.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم واخشوا يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده ولا مولود هو جاز عن والده شيئا إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs and knows what will happen tomorrow and knows what will happen in the land in which you will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's omniscience and power, emphasizing that He has knowledge of the Hour (the Day of Judgment) and controls the natural phenomenon of rain. Additionally, God is aware of the future, including what will happen tomorrow and what will happen in the land where one will eventually die. The verse underscores God's wisdom and knowledge, reminding believers that He is fully aware of all things and has a plan for the universe.
orig: إن الله عنده علم الساعة وينزل الغيث ويعلم ما في الأرحام وما تدري نفس ماذا تكسب غدا وما تدري نفس بأي أرض تموت إن الله عليم خبير

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: They say, 'Fables of the past!' But it is a truth from your Lord, a warning to people of understanding.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who reject the Qur'an, calling it mere fables or stories from the past. However, the verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a collection of stories, but a revelation from God, meant to serve as a warning and guidance for those who have understanding and are willing to listen. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing the truth and wisdom in the Qur'an, and not dismissing it as mere myths or fables.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه بل هو الحق من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يهتدون

translation: Allah is the one who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then He rose above the Throne. You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and dominion over the universe, highlighting His role as the sole creator of the heavens and the earth and everything in between. The verse also underscores the idea that Allah is separate from His creation, as He rose above the Throne, indicating His transcendence and majesty. The verse concludes by reminding the reader of their accountability to Allah and their need to remember and acknowledge His greatness.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش ما لكم من دونه من ولي ولا شفيع أفلا تتذكرون

translation: And the matter of the hour is not but a single blink, or nearer still. Then the moon will be darkened, and the sun will be brought near.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the end of the world and the events that will occur before the Day of Judgment. The 'matter of the hour' refers to the final hour of judgment, which will come suddenly and unexpectedly, like a blink of an eye. The verse also describes the darkening of the moon and the nearing of the sun, which are signs of the approaching Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the approaching end of the world and the need for people to prepare for the final judgment.
orig: يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض ثم يعرج إليه في يوم كان مقداره ألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed great punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of knowledge and the witnessing of a great punishment. The phrase 'al-ghayb' refers to knowledge of the unseen, which is known only to God. The phrase 'ash-shahada al-'azeez ar-rahim' refers to a great punishment that was witnessed by many people. The verse suggests that the punishment was so severe that it destroyed knowledge of the unseen, indicating the severity of the punishment and the power of God. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and reject the idea of accountability for their actions.
orig: ذلك عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الرحيم

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge of humanity and His proximity to them. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human beings, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and highlights the intimate relationship between the Creator and His creation. It also underscores the idea that God is always near and aware of humanity's thoughts, feelings, and actions.
orig: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه وبدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

translation: Then He made his offspring from the essence of despised water.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of Adam, the first human, from a lowly substance, such as clay or mud. The phrase 'despised water' refers to the humble origins of humanity, indicating that humans were created from a substance that is considered lowly and worthless. The verse highlights the power of God, who can create something noble and dignified from something seemingly insignificant. It also serves as a reminder of humanity's humble origins and the need for humility and gratitude towards God.
orig: ثم جعل نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين

translation: Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come willingly or unwillingly.' They both said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe by God, specifically the creation of the heavens and the earth. The verse emphasizes the idea that God commanded the heavens and the earth to come into existence, and they both responded willingly, indicating their submission to God's will. The verse highlights the power and authority of God as the creator of the universe, and serves as a reminder of the purpose of creation, which is to worship and obey God.
orig: ثم سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And they say, 'When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be recreated anew?' Indeed, they will be, but they are in [such] disbelief.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' skepticism regarding the idea of resurrection and their refusal to accept it. The verse emphasizes that resurrection is indeed possible and that it will surely happen, despite their disbelief. The use of the word 'بل' (bal) meaning 'indeed' emphasizes the certainty of resurrection and highlights the contrast between the disbelievers' disbelief and the reality of the situation. The verse serves as a reminder that resurrection is a fundamental aspect of Islamic belief and that it is a certainty that will come to pass.
orig: وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض أإنا لفي خلق جديد بل هم بلقاء ربهم كافرون

translation: Say, 'O death, you have been decreed upon every soul, then to your Lord will be the return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the fact that every soul will eventually return to its Creator. The use of the word 'malak' (angel of death) in the first part of the verse underscores the idea that death is a messenger of God, sent to collect the souls of the deceased and bring them before their Lord for judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of death and the need for individuals to prepare for their eventual return to God.
orig: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون

translation: And if only the angels could see when the criminals are punished, how their heads are being crushed by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and our Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene in which the angels are witnessing the punishment of the criminals, who have been condemned to Hell. The verse emphasizes the power and authority of God, who is described as the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and highlights the idea that God is aware of all actions and will bring justice to those who have committed evil deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون
