translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience in not destroying the wicked people immediately. Instead, He gives them respite in this life, allowing them to repent and change their ways. However, the verse also warns that the punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe for those who refuse to mend their ways. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of sin and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها ولكن حق القول مني لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: So taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns of the eternal punishment that awaits those who have committed evil deeds. The phrase 'taste the punishment' suggests a suffering that is both intense and prolonged, emphasizing the severity of God's retribution. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and that we will ultimately be held accountable for our deeds. The phrase 'for what you used to do' underscores the idea that our actions have a direct impact on our future, and that we must be mindful of the impact our actions have on ourselves and others.
orig: فذوقوا بما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا إنا نسيناكم وذوقوا عذاب الخلد بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Only those who believe in Our verses and remember them when they are reminded of them, prostrate and glorify their Lord with praise, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the quality of true believers, who when reminded of Allah's verses, not only believe in them but also remember and reflect on their own shortcomings. They respond to the reminder by humbling themselves in prostration and glorifying their Lord with praise. The verse also emphasizes that true believers are not arrogant, recognizing that their strength and knowledge come from Allah alone. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain humble and grateful for Allah's blessings and to constantly reflect on their actions and beliefs.
orig: إنما يؤمن بآياتنا الذين إذا ذكروا بها خروا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: Their sides were bent in the morning, and they were called upon to prostrate, but they did not respond to their Lord, and they denied Our signs.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of a group of people who were called upon to prostrate and worship their Lord, but they refused to do so. They were stubborn and arrogant, and they denied the signs and warnings that were sent to them by God. The verse suggests that this refusal to submit to God's will and ignore His signs led to their downfall and destruction.
orig: تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع يدعون ربهم خوفا وطمعا ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And they did not know that Allah's punishment was coming to them from beneath their feet, so He caused them to be overturned and put them in a lasting punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's ignorance of the impending punishment from God, which came upon them unexpectedly. The phrase 'from beneath their feet' suggests that the punishment came from a place they least expected, catching them off guard. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment can come at any time, even when people are least aware of it. The phrase 'put them in a lasting punishment' indicates that the punishment was not temporary, but rather a permanent state of suffering, emphasizing the severity of God's wrath.
orig: فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين جزاء بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن كان مؤمنا كمن كان فاسقا لا يستوون

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward for those who believed in God and lived righteously. The phrase 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' is a metaphor for Paradise, where believers will spend eternity in happiness and peace. The verse emphasizes the idea that their faith and good deeds will be rewarded with a life of bliss and joy, free from the suffering and hardships of this world. The image of rivers flowing beneath the gardens also symbolizes the abundance and beauty of Paradise, where believers will be able to enjoy the blessings of God forever.
orig: أما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فلهم جنات المأوى نزلا بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And as for those who were oppressors, they will be in the Fire, where they will be humiliated and exhausted, crying for help, 'Our Lord, take us out of this; we will not be unjust anymore!'
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who oppressed others and lived in injustice. They will be in Hell, suffering from humiliation and exhaustion, begging for help and promising to change their ways. However, their pleas will fall on deaf ears, as they had been warned in life but chose to ignore the signs and continue their oppressive ways. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأما الذين فسقوا فمأواهم النار كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها أعيدوا فيها وقيل لهم ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And We will punish them with a punishment shorter than the greater punishment, that they may return.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's mercy and forgiveness, even towards those who have committed great sins. The verse indicates that God will first punish them with a lesser punishment, in the hope that they will repent and turn back to Him. The greater punishment refers to the ultimate punishment of Hell, which is reserved for those who refuse to repent and continue to live in sin. The verse serves as a reminder that God's mercy and forgiveness are always available to those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the signs of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will punish the wicked ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting God's signs and messages, and the severe punishment that awaits those who do so. The verse describes those who are reminded of God's signs, yet deliberately turn away from them, as being among the wicked. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, and serves as a reminder of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه ثم أعرض عنها إنا من المجرمين منتقمون

translation: And indeed, We gave Moses the Book, and We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Torah, which was given to Moses by God and served as a guidance for the Children of Israel. The verse highlights the significance of the Torah as a source of guidance and direction for the Israelites, and by extension, for all believers. The verse also underscores the idea that the Torah is not just a historical text, but a living guide that remains relevant and applicable to this day.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل

translation: And We made from among them leaders, guiding them according to Our command, so long as they were patient and were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the selection of leaders from among the believers, who were chosen by God to guide the community according to His command. The verse emphasizes the quality of patience as a necessary characteristic for leadership, indicating that the leaders were required to be patient in the face of adversity and to remain steadfast in their faith. The verse also highlights the importance of certainty in God's signs, suggesting that the leaders were chosen because they had a deep understanding and conviction in God's revelations. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to follow the guidance of their leaders, who are appointed by God to guide them on the righteous path.
orig: وجعلنا منهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا لما صبروا وكانوا بآياتنا يوقنون

translation: Indeed, your Lord will separate them on the Day of Resurrection, for they were in disagreement within themselves.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Resurrection, when God will separate the righteous from the wicked. The verse suggests that the wicked will be in disagreement and disarray, while the righteous will be united in their belief and actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يهد لهم كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون يمشون في مساكنهم إن في ذلك لآيات أفلا يسمعون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا تأكل منه أنعامهم وأنفسهم أفلا يبصرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this conquest come to pass, if you are truthful?
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' mocking question to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the promise of victory and conquest that he had been prophesying. The verse indicates that the disbelievers were skeptical about the idea of a Muslim conquest, and they challenged the Prophet to show them when this victory would come to pass. The verse serves as a reminder that the fulfillment of God's promise is not dependent on human timelines or expectations, but rather on God's own will and timeline. The verse also highlights the importance of patience and faith in the face of adversity and doubt.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الفتح إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood cannot come at all.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that truth and falsehood are mutually exclusive, and that the truth will always prevail in the end. The verse is a reminder to those who have rejected faith, that their disbelief will not be of any benefit to them, and that they will not be able to escape the truth. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are on the side of falsehood, reminding them that their actions will not be able to overcome the truth, and that they will ultimately be defeated.
orig: قل يوم الفتح لا ينفع الذين كفروا إيمانهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And turn away from them and wait, indeed they are being awaited.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from the disbelievers and wait for their punishment, indicating that their fate is sealed and they are being watched and awaited by God. The verse emphasizes the idea that the disbelievers are unable to escape God's punishment and that it is only a matter of time before it befalls them. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and choose to disbelieve, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that God is always watching.
orig: فأعرض عنهم وانتظر إنهم منتظرون

translation: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to fear Allah and not to follow the disbelievers and hypocrites. The verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of Allah's knowledge and wisdom in all aspects of life. The Prophet is being reminded that Allah is fully aware of all things and has the power to guide and misguide, and that He is the only source of true wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and all believers to seek guidance from Allah alone and not to be swayed by the opinions and actions of those who reject faith.
orig: يا أيها النبي اتق الله ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the revelations sent by God, indicating that He is fully aware of human actions and is closely observing them. The verse serves as a reminder that God is fully cognizant of human behavior and that our actions have consequences in this life and the hereafter. It is a call to obedience and a reminder that God's knowledge encompasses all things, including human actions, and that we will be held accountable for our deeds.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك من ربك إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And rely upon Allah and sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah and having faith in His ability to guide and protect. The phrase 'wa kafa billah' means 'and sufficient is Allah' which signifies that Allah is enough to rely on and that He is the sufficient provider and protector of all affairs. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to put their trust in Allah and to seek His guidance in all aspects of their lives.
orig: وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: And what has made you understand, [O men], that your Lord will not break His promise to you? Indeed, Allah will fulfill His promise. And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of why the wicked are not immediately punished, as it seems that God's promise to punish the wicked has not been fulfilled. The verse responds by stating that God's punishment will indeed come, but it will come unexpectedly, like a thief in the night. The verse warns the wicked not to be deceived by the delay in punishment, as it will surely come, and they will not be able to escape it. The verse also serves as a reminder that God's promise is true and He will fulfill it, just as He has fulfilled it in the past by destroying towns that were unjust.
orig: ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه وما جعل أزواجكم اللائي تظاهرون منهن أمهاتكم وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم ذلكم قولكم بأفواهكم والله يقول الحق وهو يهدي السبيل

translation: And they have invoked upon their Lord, saying, 'Our Lord, we have been unjust to ourselves. If You do not forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people are acknowledging their own sinfulness and appealing to God for forgiveness. They recognize that they have wronged themselves and are at risk of being among the losers if God does not forgive them. The verse highlights the importance of recognizing one's own mistakes and seeking forgiveness, rather than blaming others or making excuses. It also emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of God, who is eager to pardon those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله فإن لم تعلموا آباءهم فإخوانكم في الدين ومواليكم وليس عليكم جناح فيما أخطأتم به ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, and his wives are their mothers, and the believers who have migrated and the supporters are more entitled to be closer to one another in the Book of God, except that you do so to your friends in a way that is known.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the close relationship between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, and how he is closer to them than they are to themselves. It also highlights the importance of the bond between the believers and their mothers, and the special relationship between the Muhajirun (those who migrated to Medina) and the Ansar (the supporters). The verse also emphasizes the importance of treating friends with kindness and respect, as mentioned in the phrase "except that you do so to your friends in a way that is known." This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of building strong relationships within the Muslim community and treating one another with love and respect.
orig: النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وأزواجه أمهاتهم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله من المؤمنين والمهاجرين إلا أن تفعلوا إلى أوليائكم معروفا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And indeed, We have taken from the prophets their covenant, and from you [O Muhammad] and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary, and We have taken from them a firm covenant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has taken a covenant from all the prophets, including Muhammad, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary. The covenant refers to the responsibility and obligation that God has placed upon them to convey His message to humanity. The verse emphasizes the importance of the prophets' role in guiding people towards the right path and the consequences of not adhering to their teachings. It serves as a reminder to believers of the significance of following the teachings of the prophets and the covenant that they have with God.
orig: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: And question not the faithful concerning their loyalty, and indeed, the disbelievers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and faithfulness among believers. It warns against questioning the loyalty of those who have proven their faith and dedication to God. The verse also serves as a warning to disbelievers, threatening them with a painful punishment for their disbelief and disobedience. The verse highlights the contrast between the faithful and the disbelievers, emphasizing the importance of faith and loyalty in avoiding God's punishment.
orig: ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم وأعد للكافرين عذابا أليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to you and We sent upon them a wind and soldiers you did not see. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of the favor of Allah upon them, specifically during a time of war when they were outnumbered and outmatched. The verse emphasizes the divine intervention that saved them from their enemies, citing the example of the wind and the unseen soldiers that were sent to their aid. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to be grateful for Allah's blessings and to remember that He is always watching and aware of their actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جاءتكم جنود فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا وجنودا لم تروها وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: When they came upon you from above you and from beneath you, and when the eyes grew wild and the hearts reached the throats, and you harbored doubts about Allah.
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the believers were surrounded by enemies from all sides, and they were in a state of fear and panic. The phrase 'from above you' refers to the enemy forces that were attacking them from the hills and high places, while 'from beneath you' refers to those who were attacking them from the lower ground. The phrase 'and when the eyes grew wild' suggests that the believers were in a state of confusion and disorientation, and 'the hearts reached the throats' indicates that they were experiencing extreme fear and anxiety. The phrase 'and you harbored doubts about Allah' suggests that the believers were questioning Allah's power and protection, and were struggling with their faith in the face of these overwhelming challenges. The verse serves as a reminder that even in the most difficult and desperate situations, one should not lose faith in Allah's ability to protect and guide.
orig: إذ جاءوكم من فوقكم ومن أسفل منكم وإذ زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر وتظنون بالله الظنونا

translation: And the believers, men and women, are Auliya' (helpers, supporters, friends, etc.) of one another; they enjoin good and forbid evil, and they establish worship and give Zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. (Muhammad SAW).
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity and solidarity among believers, both men and women. They support and help each other in doing good deeds and forbidding evil actions. They also establish prayer and give charity, demonstrating their obedience to God and His Messenger. This verse emphasizes the importance of community and cooperation among believers in living a righteous life and promoting good values in society.
orig: هنالك ابتلي المؤمنون وزلزلوا زلزالا شديدا

translation: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say, 'These people have been deceived by their religion.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the criticism of the hypocrites and those with diseased hearts who accuse the believers of being deceived by their religion. The verse suggests that their criticism stems from their own inner disease and lack of faith, rather than any actual flaw in the believers' beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith is not based on external appearances or worldly success, but rather on the sincerity and purity of one's heart and actions.
orig: وإذ يقول المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض ما وعدنا الله ورسوله إلا غرورا

translation: And when a group of them said: 'O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return.' And they turned back, while the Prophet and those who were with him were staying in the mosque, and they were saying: 'Our homes are vulnerable and our children are weak. If they want to fight, they will not be able to fight us.'
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where a group of people from Yathrib, who were likely to be attacked by their enemies, were told by some of their fellow citizens to return home as there was no place for them. However, the Prophet and his companions, who were taking refuge in the mosque, were not deterred by the threat and were determined to defend themselves. The verse highlights the bravery and determination of the Prophet and his followers in the face of danger, as well as their concern for the safety of their homes and families.
orig: وإذ قالت طائفة منهم يا أهل يثرب لا مقام لكم فارجعوا ويستأذن فريق منهم النبي يقولون إن بيوتنا عورة وما هي بعورة إن يريدون إلا فرارا

translation: And if We had entered upon them with punishment, they would have been destroyed, so the punishment was turned away from them for a while.
interpretation: The verse suggests that God's punishment was imminent for the disobedient people, but it was temporarily withheld, giving them a chance to repent and change their ways. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is not immediate, and that there is always a chance for redemption before it is too late. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them that God's punishment is always looming and can strike at any moment.
orig: ولو دخلت عليهم من أقطارها ثم سئلوا الفتنة لآتوها وما تلبثوا بها إلا يسيرا

translation: And indeed, they had promised Allah before that they would not turn their backs on each other, and Allah's covenant will indeed be questioned.
interpretation: The verse refers to the promise made by the Israelites to God that they would not turn their backs on each other and would stand firm in their faith. However, they broke this promise and turned away from God's covenant. The verse warns that God's covenant will be questioned and those who break it will face consequences. It serves as a reminder to believers to stay true to their faith and not to break their promises to God.
orig: ولقد كانوا عاهدوا الله من قبل لا يولون الأدبار وكان عهد الله مسئولا

translation: Say, 'Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, for then you will not enjoy life except for a little while.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that trying to escape death or killing by fleeing will not be effective, as death is inevitable and will eventually catch up with those who try to flee. The verse also highlights the temporary nature of life, indicating that even if one manages to escape death, they will only live for a short while before meeting their ultimate fate. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of death and the importance of preparing for the afterlife, rather than trying to escape the inevitable.
orig: قل لن ينفعكم الفرار إن فررتم من الموت أو القتل وإذا لا تمتعون إلا قليلا

translation: Say, 'Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intended harm or intended mercy?' They will not find for themselves, apart from Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness of human beings in the face of God's will. The verse suggests that no one can protect a person from God's punishment or wrath if He intends harm, nor can anyone intercede on their behalf to avert the punishment. The verse also implies that humans cannot rely on anyone or anything else for protection or help, except Allah. It is a reminder of the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's authority and the futility of seeking help from other sources.
orig: قل من ذا الذي يعصمكم من الله إن أراد بكم سوءا أو أراد بكم رحمة ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, God knows the hidden enemies among you and the ones who (feign) obedience while they are (in fact) refusing (to follow the Prophet).
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of the hypocrites among the Muslim community, who outwardly appear to be obedient but in reality are rebellious and resistant to the Prophet's teachings. The verse serves as a warning to these hypocrites, reminding them that God is aware of their true intentions and actions, and that they will face consequences for their disobedience.
orig: قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم والقائلين لإخوانهم هلم إلينا ولا يأتون البأس إلا قليلا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أشحة عليكم فإذا جاء الخوف رأيتهم ينظرون إليك تدور أعينهم كالذي يغشى عليه من الموت فإذا ذهب الخوف سلقوكم بألسنة حداد أشحة على الخير أولئك لم يؤمنوا فأحبط الله أعمالهم وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: The tribes of Israel were punished for their sins, and the punishment came to them in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the punishment of the tribes of Israel for their sins. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the punishment, which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يحسبون الأحزاب لم يذهبوا وإن يأت الأحزاب يودوا لو أنهم بادون في الأعراب يسألون عن أنبائكم ولو كانوا فيكم ما قاتلوا إلا قليلا

translation: Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a good example for him who hopes for Allah and the Last Day, and remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a role model for believers. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's behavior and character are an excellent example for those who hope for Allah's mercy and wish to live a righteous life. The verse also stresses the importance of remembering Allah often, indicating that constant remembrance of Allah is a key aspect of living a life pleasing to Him. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow the Prophet's example and to remember Allah frequently in their daily lives.
orig: لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر وذكر الله كثيرا

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said: 'This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.' And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the believers when they saw the confederate armies gathered against them. Instead of feeling fear or doubt, the believers recognized the fulfillment of God's promise and the truthfulness of the Prophet's words. This realization strengthened their faith and submission to God, demonstrating their trust in God's plan and their commitment to His cause.
orig: ولما رأى المؤمنون الأحزاب قالوا هذا ما وعدنا الله ورسوله وصدق الله ورسوله وما زادهم إلا إيمانا وتسليما

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah, and among them are men who have not. They have fulfilled their vow, and among them are men who are waiting, and they have not changed their condition.
interpretation: The verse highlights the diversity among believers, where some have remained true to their covenant with God, while others have not. The verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's promises and commitments, and encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith. The verse also acknowledges that there are those who are still waiting and have not yet fulfilled their vow, indicating that the path to righteousness is not always straightforward and that patience and perseverance are essential.
orig: من المؤمنين رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه فمنهم من قضى نحبه ومنهم من ينتظر وما بدلوا تبديلا

translation: Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. And that, indeed, is a great attainment. And those who are faithless and who deny Our verses - those will be companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the ultimate fate of believers and non-believers. The righteous will be rewarded with eternal life in paradise, described as gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. On the other hand, those who reject God's message and deny His verses will suffer eternal punishment in the Fire. The verse emphasizes the significance of faith and righteous deeds as the key to a successful and blessed life, while rejection of God's teachings leads to a wretched and miserable end.
orig: ليجزي الله الصادقين بصدقهم ويعذب المنافقين إن شاء أو يتوب عليهم إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And Allah turned back the disbelievers in their rage; they did not obtain any good. Allah is sufficient for the believers in combat. And Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah thwarted the plans of the disbelievers and prevented them from achieving their goals. The verse emphasizes that Allah is sufficient for the believers and that He is the One who provides them with victory and support in times of need. The phrase 'Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might' highlights God's immense power and authority, indicating that He is above all things and that nothing can stand in His way.
orig: ورد الله الذين كفروا بغيظهم لم ينالوا خيرا وكفى الله المؤمنين القتال وكان الله قويا عزيزا

translation: And We have sent down to you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the clarity and certainty of the message of Islam, which is a victory in itself, while the phrase 'manifest triumph' refers to the tangible and evident success that believers will experience in this life and the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their faith and efforts will be rewarded, and that they will ultimately triumph over their enemies and adversaries.
orig: وأنزل الذين ظاهروهم من أهل الكتاب من صياصيهم وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب فريقا تقتلون وتأسرون فريقا

translation: And He has made you successors in the earth and has raised some of you above others in ranks, so that He may test you in what He has given you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has given humans a position of authority on earth and has blessed them with various favors and blessings. However, this verse also serves as a reminder that these blessings are not solely for personal enjoyment, but rather, they are a means of testing and evaluating human behavior. The verse emphasizes that God is swift in punishing those who misuse His blessings and become arrogant or ungrateful. On the other hand, He is also Forgiving and Merciful, and those who repent and turn to Him will find His mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم وأرضا لم تطئوها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: O prophet, tell your wives that if they desire the life of this world and its adornment, then let them turn back from their marriage contract. And if they desire Allah and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then indeed Allah has prepared for them a great reward.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and instructing him to convey a message to his wives. The message is that if they desire the fleeting pleasures of this life and its material adornments, then they should renounce their marriage to the Prophet and return to their families. However, if they desire a greater reward in the Hereafter and seek to be close to God and His Messenger, then God has prepared a great reward for them. The verse highlights the importance of prioritizing one's relationship with God and the Hereafter over the temporary pleasures of this life.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك إن كنتن تردن الحياة الدنيا وزينتها فتعالين أمتعكن وأسرحكن سراحا جميلا

translation: And indeed, We have sent forth the Messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners. But Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the Prophets as both bearers of good news and warning. They were sent to guide humanity towards righteousness and to warn them of the consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights God's omniscience and His role as a witness over all things, indicating that He is aware of all human actions and will hold them accountable. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live their lives in accordance with God's will and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable in the hereafter.
orig: وإن كنتن تردن الله ورسوله والدار الآخرة فإن الله أعد للمحسنات منكن أجرا عظيما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an open immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and warns them against committing open immorality. The verse states that if any of them commit such an act, their punishment will be doubled. The verse emphasizes that this is an easy matter for Allah, indicating that He is all-powerful and capable of enforcing His punishment. The verse serves as a warning to the wives of the Prophet and all believers, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of living a virtuous life.
orig: يا نساء النبي من يأت منكن بفاحشة مبينة يضاعف لها العذاب ضعفين وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will give them a double reward and We will grant them a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse promises a double reward and a noble provision for those who obey Allah and His Messenger and do righteous deeds. The verse highlights the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger as a means of attaining a blessed life in this world and the hereafter. The phrase 'We will grant them a noble provision' suggests that the reward for righteousness is not limited to the spiritual realm, but also extends to the material and worldly aspects of life. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to lead a virtuous life and to strive for righteousness in all aspects of their lives.
orig: ومن يقنت منكن لله ورسوله وتعمل صالحا نؤتها أجرها مرتين وأعتدنا لها رزقا كريما

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an open immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and warns them against committing open immorality. The verse emphasizes that the punishment for such an act will be doubled, indicating the gravity of the offense and the severity of the punishment. The verse also underscores the ease with which God can mete out punishment, highlighting His power and authority. The verse serves as a warning to all believers, reminding them of the importance of leading a virtuous life and avoiding immoral behavior.
orig: يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض وقلن قولا معروفا

translation: And remember when We said: 'Enter this town and eat therefrom freely, and enter the gate prostrating and say: 'Relieve us of our sins, O Lord!' But the wicked ones among them changed the word, which had been told to them. So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky because of their wicked deeds.
interpretation: The verse recounts the story of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were commanded by God to enter the town and eat freely, but they were also instructed to enter the gate prostrating and to ask for forgiveness from God. However, the wicked among them changed the word and disobeyed God's command, which led to their destruction. The verse serves as a warning to those who disobey God and His messengers, and the consequences of their actions.
orig: وقرن في بيوتكن ولا تبرجن تبرج الجاهلية الأولى وأقمن الصلاة وآتين الزكاة وأطعن الله ورسوله إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس أهل البيت ويطهركم تطهيرا

translation: And remember when Moses said to his people: 'Allah commands you to slaughter a cow, surely, Allah will give you a clear sign, so do what you are commanded.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is reminding his people of the commandment given by God to slaughter a cow, which would serve as a sign of their obedience and faith. The verse highlights the importance of following God's commands, even when they may seem unclear or difficult to understand. It also emphasizes the idea that God's signs and miracles are a manifestation of His mercy and wisdom, and that they should be recognized and appreciated. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to trust in God's guidance and to follow His commands without hesitation or questioning.
orig: واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة إن الله كان لطيفا خبيرا

translation: Indeed, the believers and believers, men and women, and the devout men and devout women, and the truthful men and truthful women, and the patient men and patient women, and the humble men and humble women, and the charitable men and charitable women, and the fasting men and fasting women, and the men and women who guard their private parts, and the men and women who remember Allah frequently, Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of various virtues and qualities that are essential for a believer to attain salvation. The verse emphasizes the equality of men and women in the eyes of God and stresses the importance of faith, piety, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, and remembrance of God. The verse also assures believers that those who possess these qualities will be rewarded with forgiveness and a great reward from God.
orig: إن المسلمين والمسلمات والمؤمنين والمؤمنات والقانتين والقانتات والصادقين والصادقات والصابرين والصابرات والخاشعين والخاشعات والمتصدقين والمتصدقات والصائمين والصائمات والحافظين فروجهم والحافظات والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات أعد الله لهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: And there is not for a believer or a believer any course of action against the decree of Allah and the Messenger. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that believers have no choice but to follow the decree of God and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Any attempt to go against God's will and the Prophet's teachings is considered a clear error and a departure from the right path. The verse underscores the importance of submitting to God's will and following the guidance of the Prophet, and serves as a reminder that the consequences of disobedience can be severe.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن ولا مؤمنة إذا قضى الله ورسوله أمرا أن يكون لهم الخيرة من أمرهم ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد ضل ضلالا مبينا

translation: And remember when you said to the one whom Allah had blessed with grace, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah, and hide your affair, for Allah will bring forth what you fear.'
interpretation: The verse refers to an incident where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was advised by his wife Khadija to keep his marriage with her a secret, as she was worried about the reaction of the people. The verse highlights the Prophet's obedience to Allah and his fear of Him, as well as his concern for his wife's well-being. The verse also underscores the importance of fearing Allah and hiding one's private matters, especially in matters of faith and religion. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize their relationship with Allah and to be mindful of their actions and their impact on others.
orig: وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه وأنعمت عليه أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه وتخشى الناس والله أحق أن تخشاه فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا زوجناكها لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: And nothing was on the prophet from harm, for what Allah had decreed for him was a year of Allah in the people who had passed away before him, and the command of Allah was preordained.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not harmed by the fact that he had to migrate from Mecca to Medina, as it was part of God's decree for him. The verse highlights that the Prophet's migration was not a sign of weakness or defeat, but rather a part of God's plan for him. The phrase 'a year of Allah' refers to a specific period of time that was designated by God for the Prophet's mission. The verse also underscores the idea that God's command is preordained and cannot be changed or altered by anyone.
orig: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا

translation: And those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and do not fear anyone except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of conveying God's message and living in fear of Him. The phrase 'And sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner' implies that God is sufficient as a witness and judge of our actions, and that we will be held accountable to Him. The verse emphasizes the responsibility of those who spread God's message to live in accordance with it and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be accountable to God alone.
orig: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique status of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the final prophet sent by Allah. He is not the father of any man, signifying that he is not a biological father to anyone, but he is the spiritual father of all believers. The verse also highlights his role as the Seal of the Prophets, indicating that he is the last prophet sent by Allah to guide humanity. The verse ends by emphasizing Allah's knowledge of all things, signifying that He is aware of everything and has knowledge of all that exists.
orig: ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah frequently and abundantly. The verb 'ذكر' (dhikr) implies a deep and sincere remembrance of Allah, not just a mere mention of His name. The verse encourages believers to remember Allah's favors, His power, and His guidance, and to reflect on their own lives in light of His teachings. By doing so, believers will be able to live a life that is pleasing to Allah and benefit from His blessings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the clarity and certainty of the message of Islam, which leaves no room for doubt or confusion. The phrase 'manifest triumph' refers to the tangible and evident success that the believers experienced, such as the conquest of Mecca and the spread of Islam. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and encourages them to continue their efforts in spreading the message of Islam.
orig: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: It is He who prays upon you and His angels to bring you out of darkness into light, and He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of God as the one who guides and protects the believers. The verse emphasizes that God's mercy and guidance are not limited to this life, but will continue in the afterlife. The phrase 'to bring you out of darkness into light' symbolizes the spiritual journey of the believers, from a state of ignorance and disobedience to a state of enlightenment and obedience to God. The verse also underscores the importance of God's mercy and compassion towards the believers, indicating that He is always ready to guide and support them.
orig: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the clarity and manifestation of the truth of Islam, which was revealed through the Qur'an and the Prophet's teachings. The phrase 'manifest triumph' refers to the tangible and obvious success that the believers experienced in their lives, such as the spread of Islam and the establishment of a just and righteous society. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of God's favor and blessings upon them, and encourages them to continue to live according to the teachings of Islam.
orig: تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

translation: O prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner. As a witness, he testified to the truth of God's Oneness and the message of the Qur'an. As a bringer of good news, he brought hope and reassurance to those who embraced Islam and lived according to its teachings. As a warner, he cautioned those who rejected the message, warning them of the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience. The verse highlights the Prophet's critical role in conveying God's message and serving as a guide for humanity.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And to Allah belong the east and the west. Whither so ever ye turn, there is Allah's countenance (and His) blessings.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipresence and the fact that He is the source of all blessings. The verse suggests that no matter which direction one turns, they will always face Allah and receive His blessings. It is a reminder that Allah is always present and watching over His creation, and that His blessings are available to all, regardless of their location or direction.
orig: وداعيا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجا منيرا

translation: And good news to the believers, for they will have a great favor from God.
interpretation: The verse announces good news for the believers, informing them that they will receive a great favor from God. The word 'favor' (فضل) in Arabic connotes a sense of generosity, kindness, and grace. The verse emphasizes that this favor is a manifestation of God's mercy and grace towards the believers, and it serves as a reminder that God's blessings are not limited to this life but extend to the Hereafter. The verse encourages the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and righteous deeds, as they will be rewarded with a great favor from God.
orig: وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلا كبيرا

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and ignore their insults, and rely on Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Walī.
interpretation: The verse instructs believers not to follow the disbelievers and hypocrites, and to ignore their insults. Instead, they should put their trust in Allah and rely on Him for support and guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and reliance on Allah, and serves as a reminder that Allah is sufficient as a supporter and protector for those who believe in Him.
orig: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you touch them, then there is not upon you any waiting period to count against them. So, provide for them and give them a gracious release.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of divorce in the context of marriage between believers. Specifically, it addresses the situation where a man marries a believing woman, but then decides to divorce her before consummating the marriage. The verse makes it clear that in such cases, the man is not required to observe a waiting period before remarrying, as the divorce is considered valid immediately. However, the verse also emphasizes the importance of treating the divorced woman with kindness and respect, providing for her needs and giving her a gracious release, indicating that the man should not exploit the situation to harm or punish the woman. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of treating all people, including former spouses, with compassion and respect.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their dowries, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [as a gift] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [as a gift] and the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not for the believers. We know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and what their rights hands possess, so that there may be no blame upon you. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and clarifies which women are lawful for him to marry. The verse states that the Prophet's wives who have given their dowries, as well as those whom his right hand possesses (i.e., those who were given to him as gifts), are lawful for him. Additionally, the daughters of his paternal and maternal uncles and aunts who emigrated with him are also lawful for him to marry. The verse also allows for a believing woman to give herself to the Prophet as a gift, and for the Prophet to marry her exclusively. The verse emphasizes that this permission is only for the Prophet and not for the believers in general. The verse also mentions that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم لكيلا يكون عليك حرج وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the value and worth of every human life, regardless of their gender, race, or social status. The verse also underscores the responsibility that comes with this honor, as humans are accountable to God for their actions. The phrase 'وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا' (and God is witness over everything) reinforces the idea that God is aware of all human actions and is present in every aspect of life, further emphasizing the importance of living a virtuous life.
orig: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج ولو أعجبك حسنهن إلا ما ملكت يمينك وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission has been given to you for a meal, and if you are invited, then enter. And when you enter, then eat and do not linger to engage in conversation. Indeed, that was troublesome for the Prophet, and he would feel shy to ask you to leave. But if you ask them for a meal, then ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not appropriate for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him. Indeed, that is near to Allah a great sin.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the privacy and personal space of the Prophet and his household. Believers are prohibited from entering the Prophet's house without permission, and if they are invited, they should eat and leave without lingering. The verse also emphasizes the importance of modesty and purity in the believers' interactions with the Prophet and his household. The verse further emphasizes that it is a grave sin to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after his death.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما

translation: Indeed, Allah has knowledge of all things, even before they are created.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His knowledge of all things, including the future, before they come into existence. It highlights the idea that Allah's knowledge is not limited by time or space, and that He is aware of all things, past, present, and future. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and the fact that He is the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, and the All-Powerful.
orig: إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so be content with your Lord's decree and be patient. Indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans are limited in their understanding and knowledge, and that there are things that are beyond their comprehension. It encourages people to be content with God's decree and to be patient in the face of challenges and difficulties. The verse also highlights the idea that every soul has its own capacity and limit, and that God will not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
orig: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن واتقين الله إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and honoring the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and acknowledging his status as a divine messenger. The verse encourages believers to send blessings upon the Prophet and greet him with peace, signifying their acceptance of his message and their commitment to following his teachings. The verse also highlights the special relationship between Allah and His prophet, as well as the angels' reverence for the Prophet, underscoring his exalted status in the eyes of Allah.
orig: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما

translation: Indeed, those who defame Allah and His Messenger - for them is a punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and Allah has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who defame or insult Allah and His Messenger of a severe punishment in both this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of their offense and the certainty of their punishment, which is described as 'humiliating'. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of respecting and honoring Allah and His Messenger, and the consequences of failing to do so.
orig: إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who harm the believing men and believing women, unjustly, bear the guilt of slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of the sin committed by those who wrong or harm believers, both men and women, without any just cause. The phrase 'bear the guilt of slander' implies that their actions are not only unjust but also malicious and false, and they will be held accountable for their deeds. The phrase 'manifest sin' suggests that their actions are openly and unashamedly sinful, leaving no doubt about their guilt. The verse serves as a warning to those who would harm believers, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to lower their jalabib (cloaks) over them. That will be better, so that they will be recognized (as Muslim women) and not be harassed. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to advise the women of the believers to wear their cloaks in a way that covers their beauty and modesty, so that they are not harassed or mistreated. The verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and purity for Muslim women, and serves as a reminder that they should be recognized and respected for their piety and faith. The verse also highlights the forgiving and merciful nature of Allah, who is always ready to forgive those who repent and turn to Him.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And if the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and those who spread rumors in the city do not cease, We will surely bring you (O Muhammad) a victory (or a clear sign) and will surely cut them off (from the good people),
interpretation: This verse speaks about the hypocrites and those with ill intentions in their hearts who spread rumors and cause strife in the city. The verse warns them that if they do not stop their harmful behavior, God will grant the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) a clear victory and separate them from the righteous people. The verse emphasizes the importance of purifying the community from those who seek to cause harm and promote discord.
orig: لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind (of towns) in the past. Then, they did injustice, and We gave them a taste of the punishment. Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest and the day for them to see? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, and We have made their nations pass away, and their remnants have not been seen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fact that God has destroyed many generations before the current one, and has caused their nations to pass away, leaving behind no trace of their existence. This serves as a reminder to the current generation that they too will face the same fate if they do not mend their ways and live according to God's commandments.
orig: سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: They ask you about the Hour, when will be its time? Say, 'Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time but He.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the question of the Hour of Judgment, which is a recurring theme in the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes that only God has knowledge of the exact time of the Hour, and that no one else, including the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), has access to this knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder of the limitations of human knowledge and the importance of humility in the face of God's mysteries. It also underscores the idea that the Hour will come unexpectedly, and that people should be prepared for it at all times.
orig: يسألك الناس عن الساعة قل إنما علمها عند الله وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Flaming Fire.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the severe punishment that awaits those who reject the message of Islam and choose to disbelieve in Allah. The use of the word 'cursed' highlights the severity of their state and the fact that they have brought this punishment upon themselves. The phrase 'prepared for them a Flaming Fire' underscores the idea that the punishment is not only severe but also eternal, indicating that the disbelievers will be punished in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of their punishment.
orig: إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own people in the past, but you are not aware of it, nor did you witness it.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) opponents, who were skeptical of his message and denied the possibility of resurrection and punishment. The verse reminds them that God has destroyed many nations in the past, but they were not aware of it, nor did they witness it. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that God's punishment is not limited by time or space, and that He is capable of destroying nations and resurrecting them for judgment. The verse also emphasizes the importance of heeding the lessons of history and learning from the mistakes of past nations.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: On a Day when their faces will be turned upside down in the Fire, they will say: 'If only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where the wicked will be punished in Hell. The verse highlights the regret and remorse that the sinners will feel when they realize the consequences of their disobedience. They will wish they had listened to God's commands and the Prophet's teachings, but their regret will be of no avail. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of following God's commands and the Prophet's teachings.
orig: يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا

translation: And they said, 'Our Lord, we have obeyed our leaders and our great ones, and they have led us astray from the way.'
interpretation: The verse describes the people's admission of their guilt and their recognition that they have been misled by their leaders and rulers. The verse highlights the tendency of people to follow those in positions of authority, even when they know that they are being led astray. The verse serves as a reminder that true guidance comes from God alone, and that people should not blindly follow their leaders or their desires, but rather seek guidance from God and His messengers.
orig: وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا

translation: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God to grant the believers patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity, and to give them victory over their enemies. The phrase 'disbelieving people' refers to those who reject the message of Islam and oppose the believers. The verse suggests that the believers are facing persecution and oppression, and are seeking God's help and support to overcome their challenges and achieve victory. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and faith in God's plan, and encourages the believers to remain steadfast and trust in God's assistance.
orig: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب والعنهم لعنا كبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and denied Moses, while God was angry with them. Their case is with God, and their fate is severe.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, urging them not to follow in the footsteps of those who disbelieved and rejected Prophet Moses. The verse warns that those who reject God's message will face severe consequences, as was the case with the disbelievers in Moses' time, who were punished by God for their disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to avoid the mistakes of those who came before them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين آذوا موسى فبرأه الله مما قالوا وكان عند الله وجيها

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate balance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of speaking truthfully and with measured speech, as well as the need to fear God and be mindful of His presence in all aspects of life. It encourages believers to be honest and sincere in their communication, avoiding both extremes of being too lax or too strict in their speech. The verse also serves as a reminder that one's speech reflects their faith and that it is an integral part of a believer's practice to communicate in a way that is pleasing to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have forgiven you your sins, and We have forgiven the believers who were with you. And God has favored you and made pleasing to you your deeds and your religion. And God has granted you an excellent recompense.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers who were with him. The verse emphasizes that this victory is a manifestation of God's favor and forgiveness, and that it is a reward for their righteous deeds and faith. The verse also highlights the idea that God has forgiven the sins of the believers, indicating that their faith and obedience have been accepted by God. The verse serves as a reminder that God's favor and forgiveness are not limited to this life, but are also extended to the hereafter, where believers will be rewarded with an excellent recompense.
orig: يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have entrusted the human being with the responsibility of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, but he is prone to injustice and ignorant of his own fate.
interpretation: The verse highlights the magnitude of the responsibility that God has entrusted to human beings, which includes the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. However, the verse also acknowledges that humans have a tendency to act unjustly and ignore their own fate. This verse serves as a reminder of the great responsibility that comes with being human and the need to live up to that responsibility by acting justly and being mindful of one's actions and their consequences.
orig: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

translation: Let the hypocrites not think that they can outwit God. Indeed, God will bring their deeds to nothing, for God is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites, who pretend to be believers but are actually insincere and deceitful. The verse warns them that their attempts to deceive God and their fellow human beings will ultimately fail, and that their deeds will be brought to nothing. The verse also emphasizes God's knowledge and wisdom, implying that He is aware of their hypocrisy and will not be fooled by their pretenses. The verse serves as a warning to those who are insincere and hypocritical, reminding them that God sees through their actions and will ultimately bring them to justice.
orig: ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: All praise to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs all praise in the Hereafter, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for His infinite blessings and acknowledges His ownership of all that exists in the universe. It also highlights Allah's wisdom and knowledge in the context of His sovereignty over all things. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of Allah's greatness and to live in accordance with His will, as the All-Wise and All-Knowing God is aware of all things and has a plan for the universe.
orig: الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وله الحمد في الآخرة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: And He knows what is in the land and in the sea, and what has been revealed to Him is from the heavens and what has been hidden from the heavens, and He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's infinite knowledge and power. He has knowledge of everything in the land and sea, and what is revealed to Him from the heavens, indicating that He is aware of all that is hidden and seen. Additionally, the verse highlights God's attribute of being the Most Merciful and Oft-Forgiving, indicating that despite His knowledge of all things, He is still merciful and forgiving towards His creation.
orig: يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو الرحيم الغفور

translation: And the disbelievers say, 'Never will the Hour come to us.' Say, 'Indeed, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. Allah is the Knower of the unseen.' Not a single atom's weight [of punishment] will befall them [on Judgment Day] except that He will know it. And not the weight of a speck of dust in the heavens or on the earth or anything smaller than that, escapes Him, except that it is in a Clear Book.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers who deny the coming of the Hour of Judgment. The speaker is commanded to respond by affirming that the Hour will indeed come, and that Allah is aware of all things, including the smallest details. The verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and the fact that nothing, not even an atom's weight of punishment, can escape His knowledge. The verse also highlights the idea that everything, no matter how small, is recorded in a clear book, indicating that everything is accounted for and will be taken into account on Judgment Day.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the relationship between faith and good deeds. It emphasizes that faith without good deeds is not enough, and that true belief is reflected in righteous actions. The verse also emphasizes the reward for those who believe and do good deeds, which is forgiveness and a noble provision. The word "provision" can also be interpreted as a spiritual sustenance, indicating that those who lead a righteous life will be spiritually fulfilled and content.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who disputed about the signs of Our Lord, it is they who will have the severest punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject and dispute the signs and verses of the Qur'an, and instead, they will face the severest punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, indicating that they will face a painful and unbearable retribution for their disbelief and rejection of God's signs. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny and reject God's revelations, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's authority.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the authority and authenticity of the Qur'an as a revelation from God. The phrase 'those who have been given knowledge' refers to those who have been blessed with understanding and insight, and they recognize the truth of the Qur'an. The verse highlights the guidance provided by the Qur'an, which leads to the path of God, the Exalted in Might, and the Praiseworthy. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have received knowledge to follow the guidance of the Qur'an and to live according to its teachings.
orig: ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: And the disbelievers say, 'Shall we point out to you a man who will inform you that when you are destroyed, you will be raised again in a new creation?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' mocking response to the idea of resurrection. They sarcastically ask the believers if they can point out a man who can inform them about the afterlife, implying that the concept of resurrection is absurd and unbelievable. The verse highlights the disbelievers' disdain for the belief in the afterlife and their unwillingness to accept the idea of being held accountable for their actions in this life.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق إنكم لفي خلق جديد

translation: Then, it was said to him: 'Fear not, My servant, for I am with you; and do not be afraid, for I am your God. Indeed, I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.'
interpretation: This verse is a message of reassurance and comfort from God to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). God is telling the Prophet not to fear, because He is always with him and will protect him with His righteous right hand. This verse emphasizes God's power and protection, and serves as a reminder that God is always present and watching over His servants. It also highlights the special relationship between God and the Prophet, and the trust and faith that God has in him. The verse also serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for believers, reminding them that God is always with them and will protect them through difficult times.
orig: أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
