interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماء والأرض إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We gave David a distinction over the mountains, (and) the birds, and the beasts, and the wind, and the devils (also).
interpretation: This verse describes the blessings and favors that God bestowed upon Prophet David. The verse mentions specifically the mountains, birds, beasts, wind, and even the devils, indicating the extent of God's grace and mercy towards David. The verse highlights David's righteousness and his special status in God's eyes. The mention of the wind and the devils serves to emphasize the idea that even the natural world and the forces of nature are subject to God's will and are at His disposal to carry out His plans and purposes.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود منا فضلا يا جبال أوبي معه والطير وألنا له الحديد

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that God tests people through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience during these difficult times, and assures those who are patient that they will receive good news. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of testing one's faith and that those who are patient and persevering will be rewarded.
orig: أن اعمل سابغات وقدر في السرد واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

translation: And to Solomon, We subjected the wind, its morning and evening; and We made the devils (of jinn) to work in between, by the command of his Lord, and whoever of them turned aside from Our command, We will cause him to taste of the punishment of the burning fire.
interpretation: The verse describes the power and authority given to Prophet Solomon over the wind and the jinn. The wind was subjected to him, both in the morning and evening, indicating a total control over nature. Additionally, the jinn were made to work for him, but only by the command of God. The verse also warns those who disobey God's command, threatening them with the punishment of the burning fire. This verse highlights Solomon's wisdom and the extent of his power, as well as the consequences of disobedience to God's will.
orig: ولسليمان الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر وأسلنا له عين القطر ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه ومن يزغ منهم عن أمرنا نذقه من عذاب السعير

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [O Prophet], and We have shown [their people] no sign except that they denied and were arrogant, and they were not given to humility. Their hearts were as stones or even harder.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him of the destruction of the towns that were destroyed before, such as Sodom and Gomorrah. The verse highlights that the people of these towns were arrogant and refused to believe in the signs and warnings sent by God. Their hearts were as hard as stones, indicating their lack of compassion and unwillingness to listen to the message of the prophets. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in arrogance and pride, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of humility and submission to God.
orig: يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات اعملوا آل داوود شكرا وقليل من عبادي الشكور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلما قضينا عليه الموت ما دلهم على موته إلا دابة الأرض تأكل منسأته فلما خر تبينت الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And We have given you a noble and blessed town, and We have sufficed for you the good things. And We have given you a praiseworthy and beautiful reputation, and We have forgiven you your evil deeds, and We have given you a recompense without [ending].
interpretation: The verse is a message from God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, acknowledging their struggles and hardships. The verse assures them of God's favor and support, citing the conquest of Mecca as a manifestation of God's power and mercy. The verse also highlights the importance of gratitude and recognizing God's blessings, as well as the promise of forgiveness and reward for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continue to do good deeds, as well as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience.
orig: لقد كان لسبإ في مسكنهم آية جنتان عن يمين وشمال كلوا من رزق ربكم واشكروا له بلدة طيبة ورب غفور

translation: So they denied him, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their people with others.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a community that denied the prophet sent to them. The verse describes the punishment that was sent upon them, a flood that came from the dam, and how their people were replaced by others. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying God's message and the punishment that follows. The verse also highlights the power of God and His ability to replace one community with another.
orig: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved and bartered their reward for the life of this world, so that they will have a punishment that is timeless.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who rejected God's message and chose to live a life of disbelief. Their reward for this choice is a punishment that will last forever, indicating that their decision to reject God's message has consequences that extend beyond this life and into the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment is timeless, indicating that it will not end, and serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

translation: And We have made between them and the towns which We have blessed with Our blessing, towns which are apparent, and We have made between them easy stages, that they may journey therein by night and by day in security.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the provision of easy transportation and security for the people of the blessed towns, indicating that they have been given the opportunity to travel safely and easily between their towns and the surrounding areas, both by night and by day. The verse emphasizes the idea of accessibility and the facilitation of movement, suggesting that the people are able to travel freely and without fear, which is a sign of God's blessing and favor upon them.
orig: وجعلنا بينهم وبين القرى التي باركنا فيها قرى ظاهرة وقدرنا فيها السير سيروا فيها ليالي وأياما آمنين

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, put distance between our journeys and our selves, and make our hearts steadfast, and make us not objects of temptation.' Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the supplication of the believers, who ask God to distance them from evil and to make their hearts steadfast. They also ask God not to make them objects of temptation. The verse highlights the importance of steadfastness and gratitude, and serves as a reminder that God's help and guidance are always available to those who are patient and grateful. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God's signs and blessings are abundant and accessible to those who seek them.
orig: فقالوا ربنا باعد بين أسفارنا وظلموا أنفسهم فجعلناهم أحاديث ومزقناهم كل ممزق إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And indeed, Satan had whispered to them, so their faith was weakened, except for a group of believers.
interpretation: The verse suggests that Satan, also known as Iblis, had a significant influence on the faith of the people, causing their beliefs to waver. However, there were some believers who remained steadfast in their faith, despite Satan's attempts to mislead them. The verse highlights the ongoing struggle between good and evil, and the importance of staying true to one's beliefs in the face of temptation and adversity.
orig: ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه فاتبعوه إلا فريقا من المؤمنين

translation: And there was no superiority for them over the people of Tûba except that they were there first, so that they might know that the messenger is truthful and that they might be witnesses to the revelation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the people of Tûba had no superiority over others except that they were the first to believe in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. The verse highlights the significance of being a witness to the revelation and the importance of believing in the messenger. It also underscores the idea that faith is not based on worldly power or status, but rather on the recognition of the truth and the willingness to submit to God's will.
orig: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah. They do not possess a speck of dust in the heavens or on earth, nor do they have any partnership [with Him] in either of them. And it is not for them to have a share in His dominion, and neither do they have any support from Him.
interpretation: The verse is a call to those who associate others with Allah to invoke their supposed deities and prove their power. The verse emphasizes that those deities have no control over even a small speck of dust in the heavens or on earth, and they have no partnership or share in God's dominion. The verse is a rejection of polytheism and emphasizes the oneness of God, highlighting the futility of worshipping anyone or anything else besides Him.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض وما لهم فيهما من شرك وما له منهم من ظهير

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so be content with your Lord's decree and be patient. Indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans should be content with the decree of God and be patient in the face of adversity. The verse suggests that humans are not capable of understanding the hidden aspects of God's plan and that they should trust in God's wisdom and justice. The verse also highlights the idea that God will not burden a soul with more than it can bear, indicating that God's tests and trials are tailored to the individual's strength and capacity. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to trust in God's plan and to be patient in the face of challenges, knowing that God will not burden them with more than they can handle.
orig: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم قالوا ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الحق وهو العلي الكبير

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Say, 'Allah. Indeed, we have been in a clear error.'
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and instructing him to ask the disbelievers who it is that provides for them from the heavens and the earth. The answer, of course, is Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that all provision and sustenance comes from God alone, and that humans are dependent on Him for their very existence. The second part of the verse, 'Indeed, we have been in a clear error', suggests that the disbelievers have strayed from the right path and are in a state of confusion and disobedience. The verse is a call to reflection and repentance, encouraging the disbelievers to recognize their error and turn back to the truth.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I am not able to obtain benefit or harm for myself, nor do I have knowledge of the future.',
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) humility and lack of control over events. He is instructed to say that he cannot bring benefit or harm to himself, indicating that he is not the source of power or authority. Instead, all power and knowledge belong to God. The verse also highlights the Prophet's role as a mere messenger, who can only convey the message of God, but does not have the ability to alter the course of events. It serves as a reminder to believers that they should not place their trust in human beings, but rather in God alone.
orig: قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Our Lord is the One who has gathered us together, and then He will judge between us with truth, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.'
interpretation: This verse is a call to worship and a declaration of faith. It acknowledges that Allah is the one who has brought believers together and will be the one to judge between them on judgment day. The verse also emphasizes Allah's omniscience and ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood. It serves as a reminder to believers to live righteously and with integrity, as they will be held accountable for their actions on judgment day.
orig: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم

translation: Say, 'Shall I take as a friend one who has made a partner of Allah, indeed, Lat and Uzza are both enemies to me. How then can I take them as friends?',
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to ask the pagans of Mecca a rhetorical question, pointing out the absurdity of their beliefs. The verse highlights the contradiction between their belief in Allah as the one true God and their practice of worshipping other deities, specifically Lat and Uzza. The verse emphasizes that these deities are not worthy of worship and are in fact enemies of Allah and His Prophet. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of the company they keep and to avoid associating with those who reject the Oneness of God.
orig: قل أروني الذين ألحقتم به شركاء كلا بل هو الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophetic nature of Muhammad's mission, which is a mercy to all people, not just the Muslim community. It highlights the universality of the Prophet's message and its relevance to all humanity, regardless of their faith or background. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to one particular community or generation, but is relevant to all people until the end of time. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and mercy for humanity, and encourages believers to emulate his compassionate and merciful nature in their interactions with others.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' skepticism and mocking of the believers' belief in the promise of God's punishment. The disbelievers are asking when this promised punishment will come to pass, suggesting that they do not believe in its imminence or authenticity. The verse highlights the theme of doubt and disbelief, as well as the impatience and restlessness of those who reject the idea of a higher power and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'The truth has come, and the falsehood will neither begin nor repeat itself.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of truth and the futility of falsehood. The Prophet Muhammad is commanded to declare that truth has come, indicating that it is a reality that cannot be denied or ignored. The phrase 'the falsehood will neither begin nor repeat itself' suggests that falsehood is powerless and cannot prevail against the truth. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to stand firm in their beliefs and not be swayed by falsehood or deceit.
orig: قل لكم ميعاد يوم لا تستأخرون عنه ساعة ولا تستقدمون

translation: And the disbelievers say, 'We will not believe in this Qur'an, nor in what is between its hands.' But if they see the punishment, the wicked will say, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if we return to You, we will be among the believers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the disbelievers' refusal to believe in the Qur'an and their rejection of its message. They are warned that if they continue to reject God's message, they will face punishment. The verse also highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but do not act accordingly. The phrase 'between its hands' refers to the Scriptures that were revealed before the Qur'an, indicating that the disbelievers reject not only the Qur'an but also the previous revelations. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment is a consequence of their own actions and that they have no one to blame but themselves. The verse also serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not act accordingly, reminding them that their actions will have consequences.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لن نؤمن بهذا القرآن ولا بالذي بين يديه ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون عند ربهم يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

translation: And those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, 'Surely we will turn you out from our religion, then you will not worship the One who created you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the attitude of the arrogant people towards the oppressed, who are being persecuted for their beliefs. The arrogant people are determined to turn the oppressed out of their religion, and they think that by doing so, they will be able to prevent them from worshipping the One who created them. This verse highlights the theme of oppression and persecution, and serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and dismissive of others' beliefs.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم بل كنتم مجرمين

translation: And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, the night and the day are both yours. You take turns in which we were ordered to deny Allah and make rivals for Him, and we obeyed you. So, how is the outcome now?'
interpretation: In this verse, the oppressed people speak to the arrogant, acknowledging that they have been oppressed and forced to deny Allah and worship other deities. They recognize that they have been following the arrogant ones' orders and obeying their commands, but now they wonder about the outcome of their actions. The verse highlights the theme of oppression and the consequences of following those who lead astray. It serves as a reminder that those who oppress others and lead them astray will face consequences, and those who are oppressed should turn back to Allah and seek justice.
orig: وقال الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا بل مكر الليل والنهار إذ تأمروننا أن نكفر بالله ونجعل له أندادا وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وجعلنا الأغلال في أعناق الذين كفروا هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We did not send any warner to a town but its affluent ones said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the response of the affluent people in a town when a warner or prophet is sent to them. They reject the message and disbelieve in the prophet's mission. The verse suggests that the wealthy and powerful people in a society often resist the message of the prophets, possibly because they feel threatened by the call to justice and equality that the prophets bring. The verse serves as a reminder that the message of the prophets is not limited to a particular social class, but is meant for all people, regardless of their social status.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And they say, 'We are more in wealth and children, and we are not going to be punished.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the arrogance and complacency of those who believe that their wealth and children will protect them from God's punishment. They are deluded into thinking that their material possessions and offspring will shield them from the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are indulged in worldly possessions and have forgotten the ultimate accountability to God. It emphasizes the idea that no amount of wealth or progeny can save a person from God's wrath if they continue to live in disobedience to Him.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it, but most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's control over the provision and sustenance of all living things. The verse indicates that God is the sole provider and sustainer of all creation, and that He has the power to grant or withhold provision as He sees fit. The verse also highlights the ignorance of many people who do not recognize or appreciate God's role in providing for them. The verse serves as a reminder to be grateful for God's blessings and to recognize His power and control over all aspects of life.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And what is with you will be exhausted, and your children, against Us, except for he who believes and does righteous deeds. Their reward will be forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that all material possessions and children are temporary and will eventually perish. The only thing that will remain is one's belief and good deeds. The verse encourages the reader to focus on their faith and actions, rather than worldly possessions, in order to attain forgiveness and a great reward in the afterlife.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: And those who distort Our signs are in a delusion, those are the ones who will be brought to destruction.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who deliberately twist and distort the clear signs and messages of God, either by misinterpreting them or by using them out of context. These individuals are described as being in a state of delusion and are warned that they will face destruction as a consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who manipulate religious teachings to suit their own agendas, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions and that they will not be able to escape the punishment of God.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it to whom He wills. But whatever thing you spend – He will compensate it. And He is the Best of Providers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and control over the provision of sustenance for His creatures. The verse indicates that God is the sole provider of sustenance and that He can give or withhold it as He pleases. The verse also highlights the fact that God is aware of everything that is spent, no matter how small or insignificant it may seem, and that He will reward it generously. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's spending habits and to always remember that God is the ultimate provider of all things.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And on a day when He will muster them all together, He will say, 'You were rebellious towards your Lord and disobedient.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where God will gather all the rebellious and disobedient people and confront them with their sins. The use of the word 'muster' emphasizes the idea that all humanity will be gathered together, without exception, and that no one will be able to escape judgment. The phrase 'You were rebellious towards your Lord and disobedient' highlights the fact that the people's disobedience was not just towards their fellow human beings, but ultimately towards God, who is the ultimate authority and source of all morality. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in rebellion against God, reminding them that they will be held accountable for their actions on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They said, 'Glory to You, You are our Lord, rather, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the response of the people who were destroyed by God's punishment. They acknowledged that they were wrongdoers and admitted their mistake. The verse highlights the mercy of God, as He is addressed as 'You are our Lord', indicating that the people recognized His power and authority. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the people were aware of their wrongdoing and were willing to accept the consequences of their actions.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: And on the Day of Judgment, no soul will avail another, neither will intercession be accepted from them, nor will compensation be taken from them, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that on the Day of Judgment, no one will be able to help or intercede for another person, and no amount of wealth or status will be able to save them from God's punishment. The verse highlights the concept of personal responsibility and the fact that each individual will be held accountable for their own actions. The verse also warns against the idea of relying on intercession or compensation to save oneself from God's wrath, as it will be of no avail. Instead, the verse suggests that the only way to escape punishment is to live a righteous life and follow God's commands.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, 'This is not but a man who wishes to turn you away from what your fathers were worshipping.' And they say, 'This is not but a fabricated lie.' And those who disbelieve say, 'This is not but a magical spell.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they hear the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reciting the Qur'an. They reject the message and accuse the Prophet of trying to turn people away from their traditional religion. They also call the Qur'an a fabricated lie and a magical spell. The verse highlights the resistance and denial of the disbelievers and their unwillingness to accept the truth. It also emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and the power of its message.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creations. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a universal message of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to this world, but it also encompasses the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and mercy for all people, regardless of their background, race, or religion.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: And those before them had also denied, and how terrible was My punishment and My warning.
interpretation: The verse mentions that the people who denied the prophets before them were also punished severely. The phrase 'My punishment' refers to the punishment that God sent to those communities that rejected His messengers. The phrase 'My warning' refers to the warning that God gave to those communities before the punishment came. The verse serves as a reminder that denying God's message and messengers has severe consequences and that God's warnings should not be taken lightly.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I warn you of a severe punishment, that which afflicts those who are unjust, and they will have no helper against God.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of heeding the warning of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and avoiding the path of injustice and disobedience. The verse warns of a severe punishment that will afflict those who are unjust and have no helper against God. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is inevitable and that no one can escape it, and that the only way to avoid it is to follow the path of righteousness and justice.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I have not asked you for any wage in return for my affair, nor have I asked you to feed me. Indeed, the reward of my affair is only upon Allah, and He is witness over all things.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to inform the people that he has not asked for any payment or reward from them in exchange for his prophethood. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's reward is only from God, and that God is witness over all things, indicating that the Prophet's mission is not motivated by personal gain or recognition, but rather by the desire to serve and please God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their reward is also from God, and that their actions should be motivated by their love and obedience to God, rather than by personal gain or recognition.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: My Lord, indeed my Lord is the One who brings the truth of the Hidden (things) to light.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is expressing their belief in God's ability to reveal the truth of hidden things. The phrase 'alām al-ghayb' refers to knowledge that is hidden from human comprehension, and only God has access to it. The verse suggests that God is the only one who can reveal this hidden knowledge, and the speaker is acknowledging this power of God. This verse can be seen as a declaration of faith in God's omniscience and the belief that He is the source of all knowledge and truth.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: And the truth is coming, and the falsehood is vanishing away.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the inevitable triumph of truth over falsehood. The phrase 'جاء الحق' (jā'a al-haqq) means 'the truth has come', indicating the ultimate victory of truth. The phrase 'وما يبدئ الباطل' (wamā yabda' al-bātil) means 'and falsehood is vanishing away', indicating that falsehood will eventually disappear. The verse emphasizes the idea that truth will ultimately prevail over falsehood, and that those who adhere to truth will be vindicated, while those who engage in falsehood will be exposed and defeated.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I have been lost, so I have strayed from myself, and I have been guided by what my Lord has revealed to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and Near.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is expressing his own human weakness and fallibility. He acknowledges that he has strayed from the right path and has been lost. However, he also testifies that he has been guided by the revelation he received from God, which is a reminder that even in our darkest moments, God's guidance is always available to us. The verse also emphasizes God's attribute of being 'Hearing and Near', signifying that He is always ready to listen and respond to our prayers and supplications.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: And if they had seen it, they would have been terrified, so they will be filled with regret when they are seized suddenly, and they will be filled with sorrow and despair.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people who are living in sin and injustice will be filled with regret and sorrow when they are suddenly seized by God's punishment. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment will be unexpected and will come suddenly, catching the sinners by surprise. The verse also suggests that the people will be filled with despair, indicating that they will have no hope of escape or respite from the punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the importance of repenting and turning to righteousness.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they said, 'We have believed in it, and how will our belief benefit us if we are not given a share of the reward?',
interpretation: The verse speaks about the response of the disbelievers when they were invited to believe in God and His Messenger. They said they believed, but questioned the benefit of their belief if they were not given a share of the reward. The verse highlights the self-centered nature of their response, as they were more concerned with personal gain than with the truth and righteousness of their beliefs. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not about personal gain, but about submission to God and living according to His commands.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: And they have denied Him before, and they will deny Him again, while they are in a state of confusion and doubt, and they are being punished for their disbelief.
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who have denied God's signs and messengers in the past and will continue to do so in the future. They are in a state of confusion and doubt, unable to distinguish between truth and falsehood. As a result, they will be punished for their disbelief, which is a consequence of their own actions.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And between them and their desire, is a barrier, as was done to their companions before, indeed they were in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of people who are torn between their desires and the truth. The 'barrier' refers to the obstacles that prevent them from achieving their desires, which are often a result of their own actions and choices. The phrase 'as was done to their companions before' suggests that this is a recurring pattern, and that the people have not learned from the past. The phrase 'indeed they were in disquieting doubt' implies that they are uncertain and confused, and that their doubts and fears are a result of their own actions.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: All praise to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who appointed angels as messengers, bearing wings, two, three, and four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse praises Allah for His power and wisdom in creating the universe and appointing angels as messengers. The verse highlights Allah's ability to control and manage His creation, and emphasizes that He is capable of doing whatever He wills. The mention of angels with wings, two, three, and four, signifies their role as messengers and guardians, and their ability to move quickly and efficiently in carrying out Allah's commands. The verse also underscores the idea that Allah is all-powerful and capable of achieving His purposes in creation, and serves as a reminder to humanity of Allah's greatness and majesty.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the concept of reciprocity in the context of faith and good deeds. The verse suggests that when individuals work towards promoting the cause of God, they will receive divine assistance and support in return. The phrase 'Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might' underscores the idea that God possesses the ultimate authority and strength, and that His support is not limited by any means. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that their efforts towards righteousness will not go unrewarded, and that God will empower them to achieve their goals.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the grace of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth? There is no god except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: The verse is an invitation to reflect on the blessings of Allah and to recognize that He is the sole provider and sustainer of all creation. The phrase 'Is there any creator other than Allah' is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the uniqueness of Allah as the only creator and provider. The verse also implies a warning against the delusion of polytheism, reminding the readers that there is no god except Allah, and thus, all worship and reliance should be directed towards Him alone.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - surely they have been deceived by the devils, and they will come to know [the truth].
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who reject God's messages and instead, choose to follow the whispers of Satan. They will eventually come to know the truth, but it will be too late for them, as they will have already faced God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's revelations, reminding them that they are being misled by Satan and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the life of this world delude you, and let not the deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity that the promise of Allah is true and certain, and that the material life of this world should not be allowed to distract from the pursuit of spiritual truth and righteousness. The verse also warns against the deception of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from the path of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of living a life that is pleasing to Allah, and not being swayed by the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the enmity between Satan and humanity, and encourages believers to view Satan as a formidable foe who seeks to mislead them. The verse also highlights the fate of those who follow Satan, describing them as the 'companions of the Blazing Fire', implying that they will suffer a terrible fate in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant against Satan's schemes and to resist his temptations, lest they succumb to his influence and face the consequences.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fate of those who reject faith and those who embrace it. The disbelievers will face a severe punishment, while the believers who lead a righteous life will receive forgiveness and a great reward. The verse emphasizes the idea that faith and good deeds go hand in hand, and that the ultimate goal of a believer's life is to attain God's forgiveness and reward in the hereafter.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were unjust, emphasizing the sudden and unexpected nature of God's punishment, which came either in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment, while also emphasizing God's knowledge and power over all things.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And Allah is He Who sends the winds that stir up clouds, then spreads them in the sky as He wills, and breaks them into fragments, so you see the rain coming from within them...
interpretation: This verse describes the process of rain formation and highlights Allah's control over it. The verse emphasizes that Allah is the one who sends the winds that stir up the clouds and spreads them in the sky as He wills, and then breaks them into fragments, resulting in rain. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's power and control over the natural world, and how He uses it to sustain and nourish His creation. It also underscores the idea that the natural world is a reflection of Allah's mercy and provision for His creatures.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of these challenges, promising good tidings for those who are patient and faithful. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations of life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith, and that those who persevere will be rewarded.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a drop of sperm, then from a clot, and then He brings you forth as infants, and then [He develops you] into youth, and then [further] until you reach old age. And among you is he who is taken in death before [that], and that which he knew not will be seen.
interpretation: This verse describes the various stages of human development, from the initial creation of humanity from dust, to the formation of a fertilized egg, to the growth of a fetus, and finally to the birth of a child. The verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of God in creating and guiding human life, and serves as a reminder of the eventual return to God that all humans will experience. The final phrase suggests that the knowledge and understanding that one gains in life is ultimately from God, and that it is He who determines the length of one's life and the timing of death.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe than the punishment of this life, and the provision of this life is nothing compared to the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disparity between the punishment in this life and the punishment in the Hereafter. The former is temporal and limited, while the latter is eternal and far more severe. The verse also emphasizes the importance of focusing on the spiritual provision and preparation for the Hereafter, rather than being preoccupied with the material provision of this life. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being and not to be distracted by the fleeting pleasures of this world.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: By the night as it conceals (the light of the sun), and by the day as it appears in brightness, and by the sun and the moon, surely these are the signs of the All-Mighty, the Owner of the Dominion, the One whom you worship.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of God, who is the owner of the dominion and the one who is worshiped. The verse mentions three natural phenomena - night, day, sun, and moon - and uses them as evidence of God's majesty and control over the universe. The verse suggests that these natural phenomena are signs of God's power and that they serve as reminders of His greatness and the need to worship Him alone.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: And indeed, they were not hearing/listening, so they will not hear/listen, even if they were to hear/listen, they would not have responded/answered you, and on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny/disavow your share/partnership, and they will not be informed/alerted of/about the news/information.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the people who are being addressed have a history of not listening to the Prophet's message and are unlikely to change their ways. The verse also emphasizes that even if they were to hear the message, they would not respond positively, and instead, they would reject the Prophet's message and deny any association with him on the Day of Resurrection. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of being mindful of one's actions and beliefs.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are the poor, in relation to Allah, and Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disparity between human beings and Allah in terms of wealth and status. The word 'faqir' (poor) is used to describe human beings, emphasizing their dependence on Allah for sustenance and provision. On the other hand, Allah is described as 'al-Ghani' (the Rich) and 'al-Hameed' (the Praiseworthy), signifying His infinite wealth and praiseworthiness. The verse serves as a reminder to humans of their limited capacity and the need to turn to Allah for guidance and provision. It also underscores the idea that true wealth and richness come from Allah, and that humans should be mindful of their dependence on Him.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: Indeed, He will give you what He has promised and bring to pass a new creation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to fulfill His promises. The phrase 'يشأ يذهبكم' (He will give you) is in the future tense, indicating that God's promise is not yet fulfilled, but will be in the future. The phrase 'ويأت بخلق جديد' (and bring to pass a new creation) suggests that this fulfillment will be a new and unexpected event, a transformation that will bring about a new reality. The verse encourages the reader to have faith in God's promises and His ability to bring about change and transformation in their lives.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so be content with your Lord's decree and be patient. Indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans should be content with the decree of God and be patient in the face of adversity. The verse suggests that humans have limited knowledge and cannot perceive everything that is hidden from them, and therefore, they should trust in God's wisdom and plan. The verse also highlights the importance of self-reflection and personal growth, as individuals are encouraged to focus on their own spiritual development and not compare themselves to others. Ultimately, the verse reminds humans that they will only be held accountable for what they can bear, and that they should strive to live a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: And there are no darknesses nor lights
interpretation: The verse speaks about the absence of both darkness and light. The word 'darknesses' refers to the darkness of ignorance and sin, while 'lights' refers to the light of guidance and knowledge. The verse suggests that there is no room for either of these extremes in the believer's life. Instead, the believer should strive for balance and moderation in their actions and beliefs, seeking guidance from God and His Messenger (peace be upon him). The verse serves as a reminder to avoid both the darkness of ignorance and the excessive pride that can come with knowledge and enlightenment.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: And neither shade nor shelter
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the unbelievers in the afterlife, where they will not have any shade or shelter to protect them from the intense heat and suffering. The verse emphasizes the idea that they will be left without any protection or relief, and will be fully exposed to the wrath of God. The absence of shade and shelter also symbolizes the lack of any comfort or security in the afterlife for those who reject God's message.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And the life of this world is not but a delusion, and indeed, the Hereafter is far better for the righteous. Indeed, Allah will hear the one who fears Him and does righteous deeds. And indeed, He does not like the arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly life and encourages believers to focus on the eternal life in the Hereafter. The verse also emphasizes the importance of humility and righteous deeds, as Allah is pleased with those who fear Him and do good deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that true success is not measured by worldly wealth or status, but by one's fear of Allah and obedience to His commands.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: Indeed, you are a warner
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a warner to the people, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of his responsibility to convey the message of Islam and warn the people of the consequences of their actions, and it also serves as a reminder to the people of the importance of heeding the warning and following the guidance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a clear warner and a reminder to all nations.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood and the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the purpose of his mission, which is to convey the message of truth and to serve as a warning and a reminder to all nations. The use of the phrase 'all nations' indicates the universality of the message and the Prophet's role as a mercy to all of humanity. The verse also underscores the importance of the Prophet's message as a clear warning and reminder, emphasizing the urgency and gravity of the message.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve are deceiving themselves, for their messengers had come to them with clear signs, and Allah's wrath has come to them in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: The verse suggests that those who disbelieve in God's message are deceiving themselves, as they have been warned through clear signs and messengers sent by God. The verse emphasizes the certainty of God's wrath and punishment, which will come unexpectedly, either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people will have no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then He destroyed the disbelievers, and how was the punishment!
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who rejected God's message and refused to believe in Him. The verb 'akhatha' (أخذت) implies a sudden and violent destruction, emphasizing the severity of God's punishment. The phrase 'fakayfa kana nikaru' (فكيف كان نكير) adds to the severity, suggesting that the punishment was so terrible that it cannot be described in words. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to disbelieve, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the power of God's wrath.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: And indeed, We have sent down from the sky water and We have brought forth with it gardens of date palms and grapes. And from the mountains are springs pouring forth, white and red, of various colors, and dense groves of sugar cane and corn, and palm trees, similar and dissimilar. Look at their fruits when they bear fruit and their ripeness. Verily, in this are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse describes the blessings of Allah upon humanity, specifically in the form of water and the various fruits and crops that grow as a result. The verse highlights the diversity of colors and types of fruits, indicating the beauty and richness of Allah's creation. The mention of date palms, grapes, springs, and sugar cane specifically emphasizes the importance of these crops in the Arabian Peninsula. The verse also encourages people to reflect on the signs of Allah's greatness and wisdom in His creation, and to believe in Him. The use of the phrase 'similar and dissimilar' suggests that Allah's creation is full of variety and contrast, and that there is always more to discover and appreciate. Overall, the verse invites people to appreciate and be grateful for Allah's blessings, and to recognize the beauty and wonder of His creation.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among people and moving creatures and livestock are various colors. Indeed, only God fears the knowledgeable servants. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: The verse highlights the diversity of colors found among people, animals, and livestock, signifying the beauty and complexity of God's creation. The second part of the verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and fear of God, suggesting that those who possess knowledge and understanding are the ones who truly fear and worship God. The verse also underscores God's power and mercy, as He is described as both Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend [in charity] from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a trade that will not fail.
interpretation: The verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous people who recite the Qur'an, perform their prayers and give charity, both secretly and openly, with the hope of earning a profit that will not fail. The verse emphasizes the importance of reciting the Qur'an, performing prayers, and giving charity as a means of seeking guidance and purifying one's soul. The phrase 'a trade that will not fail' suggests that the righteous people believe that their good deeds will bring them reward in this life and the hereafter, and they are willing to make sacrifices to attain that reward.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various difficulties, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. However, the verse also reassures the believers that they should not lose hope, as these tests are a means of purifying their faith and increasing their patience. The verse encourages the believers to remain patient and steadfast in the face of these challenges, promising them that they will be rewarded for their perseverance.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which was before it. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It confirms that the Qur'an is a confirmation of the previous scriptures and that God is fully aware of His servants and their deeds. The verse highlights the special relationship between God and His prophets, and how God chooses them to convey His message to humanity. The verse also underscores the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a reminder for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We bequeathed the Book to those whom We chose from Our servants, but some of them wronged themselves, and some followed the moderate way, and some hastened on in advance in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his companions. The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a blessing and a guidance from God, but also acknowledges that some people may misuse or disregard this guidance. The 'great bounty' refers to the Qur'an itself, which is a source of guidance and wisdom for those who follow it, and a means of forgiveness and mercy for those who repent and turn to God.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: And gardens of palm-trees and vineyards and crops, and goodly places of resort.
interpretation: The verse describes the beauty and abundance of the gardens, vineyards, crops, and resorts that the people of the towns that were destroyed had enjoyed. The use of the word 'goodly' to describe these places emphasizes their attractiveness and appeal. The verse serves as a reminder that these material blessings are not permanent and can be taken away at any moment, as they were in the case of the towns that were destroyed.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they said, 'Praise be to Allah who has removed from us the sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Grateful.'
interpretation: The verse expresses the gratitude of the believers upon the removal of a great sorrow or hardship. The phrase 'al-hamdu lillah' (praise be to Allah) is a common expression of gratitude in Islam, and it is often used in response to good news or the alleviation of a difficult situation. The verse highlights the attribute of Allah as 'al-Ghafoor' (the Forgiving) and 'ash-Shakur' (the Grateful), emphasizing His mercy and grace towards His servants. The believers recognize that their Lord is not only Forgiving but also Grateful, acknowledging their gratitude and responding to their prayers.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: And for those who disbelieve, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they want to get away from it, they will be forced back into it, and they will be punished with a never-ending punishment.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who disbelieve in God and His message. Their refuge is the Fire of Hell, which they will not be able to escape. Every time they try to escape the punishment, they will be forced back into it, indicating that there is no escape from God's wrath. The punishment is described as 'never-ending', signifying that it will not cease or come to an end. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they will cry out, 'Our Lord! Take us out of this; if we do indeed have to face the punishment, we shall be punished in this world before the Hereafter!' They will be told, 'Remain in it with ignominy! You have forgotten the favors We bestowed upon you, so taste the punishment for your misdeeds!',
interpretation: In this verse, the people who have been destroyed by God's punishment are depicted as pleading with God to take them out of their suffering. However, their plea is not out of repentance or a desire to change their ways, but rather out of a desire to avoid the punishment. They are unwilling to acknowledge the favors that God has bestowed upon them and instead choose to ignore the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not to be taken lightly, and that those who ignore His signs and continue to live in sin will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is Knowledge of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of the subtleties, the Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and awareness of all things, both in the heavens and on earth. The phrase 'ghayb al-samawat wa al-ard' (غيب السماوات والأرض) suggests that Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, including the hidden and the manifest, the seen and the unseen. The word 'Aleem' (عاليم) further emphasizes Allah's omniscience, indicating that He is aware of even the smallest details. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is all-knowing and all-aware, and that nothing escapes His knowledge or attention.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: It is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in ranks, so that He may test you through what He has given you. Surely, your Lord is swift in retribution, and certainly He is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that God has given humans a position of authority on earth and has created differences in rank among them as a means of testing their faith and character. The verse also highlights God's justice and mercy, indicating that He is quick to punish those who disobey Him, but also forgives those who repent and turns to Him in mercy. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and the consequences of their choices, and to seek God's forgiveness and guidance in their lives.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, 'Have you considered your partner-gods whom you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth or have they any share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so that they are on clear guidance? Indeed, the wrongdoers promise one another only in deceit.'
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the theme of the Qur'an's earlier verses, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded to confront the polytheists with rational arguments against their beliefs. Here, the focus is on the fact that the idols they worship have no power to create or control anything, neither on earth nor in the heavens. The verse also mocks the idea that these idols have a share in the heavens, implying that they are nothing but mere objects without any real power or authority. The last sentence of the verse highlights the deceitful nature of the polytheists' beliefs, as they promise one another false hopes and assurances, which will ultimately lead to their downfall.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease, and if they were to cease, indeed, He would have been merciful and forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over the universe. The verse suggests that the heavens and the earth are dependent on Allah's will and power to exist, and if they were to cease to exist, it would be due to His mercy and forgiveness. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's greatness and the idea that everything in the universe is dependent on Him. It also highlights Allah's attribute of being merciful and forgiving, emphasizing His compassion towards His creation.
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than any other nation. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in aversion,
interpretation: The verse highlights the hypocrisy of the disbelievers who claimed to be eagerly waiting for a prophet to guide them. However, when a prophet finally came, they rejected him and became even more stubborn in their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the idea that the coming of a prophet is a test from God, and those who reject the prophet fail the test and are thus punished.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: And they belied them, the signs of their Lord, and denied them, so their deeds are lost, and they are not being recompensed except what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who rejected the signs of their Lord and denied the truth. Their deeds are deemed useless and they will not be rewarded for them. The verse emphasizes the idea that the disbelievers' actions will not be of any benefit to them on Judgment Day, and they will not be compensated for their deeds, as they have denied the truth and rejected the signs of their Lord.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on angels, the heavens and the earth and those in them would be destroyed. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's mercy and patience in dealing with humanity's sins. Despite the angels' desire for God to punish the wicked, God chooses to delay punishment, giving people time to repent and change their ways. The verse emphasizes God's omniscience and wisdom in His dealings with humanity, reminding us that God's ways are not our ways, and His mercy and patience are beyond human comprehension.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, and We have shown them no warning.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of towns and cities that were annihilated by God's punishment. The verse emphasizes that these towns were destroyed without any warning, indicating that the punishment was sudden and unexpected. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يس

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: And indeed, you are of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and confirms his status as a messenger of God. The verse emphasizes the importance of his role and the responsibility that comes with it. The word 'messenger' (rasul) is used to convey the idea of a representative or an ambassador, indicating that the Prophet was chosen by God to convey His message to humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's mission and the significance of his role in conveying God's message to the world.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: And certainly, We have warned the people of Mecca, but most of them are stubborn and refuse to listen.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people of Mecca, who were stubborn and refused to listen to the warnings and messages of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the fact that the people were aware of the message and the warning, but chose to ignore it, which is a sign of their arrogance and disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of rejecting God's message will be severe and that people should not take God's patience for granted.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: And indeed, We have sent it down in a Clear Qur'an, perhaps they may be reminded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the Qur'an, suggesting that its message is clear and easy to understand. The use of the word 'perhaps' indicates that the ultimate decision to accept or reject the message is left to the individual. The verse highlights the purpose of the Qur'an, which is to serve as a reminder to those who are willing to listen and reflect. It also implies that the Qur'an is not a new message, but rather a reiteration of previous messages sent by God to previous prophets.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And We have put forth examples for them, in order that they might understand, but it increases them in aversion.
interpretation: The verse suggests that God has provided numerous examples and signs for humans to understand and believe in His existence and message, but instead of acknowledging and accepting the truth, people tend to reject and oppose it, which only increases their aversion and resistance to the message.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون

translation: And We have put forth examples for them, and We have blinded them, so they do not see.
interpretation: The verse speaks about how God has provided examples and signs for people to understand and believe in His existence and message, but instead of recognizing and acknowledging the signs, people have been blinded and unable to see the truth. The verse highlights the idea that people's inability to see and understand is a result of God's will, indicating that they have been spiritually blinded as a punishment for their disbelief and refusal to accept the truth.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: And had We destroyed them, they would have said, 'Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger, we would have been believers!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to reject the truth and blame others for their own misfortunes. Even when faced with the consequences of their own actions, they would still refuse to believe and instead claim that they would have been believers if only they had been sent a messenger. This verse serves as a reminder that belief is not something that can be forced upon someone, but rather it must be embraced willingly and sincerely.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, on the day when the sky will be like murky oil, and the mountains will be like wool, and the close friends will be like scattered moths.
interpretation: The verse warns of an imminent punishment that will come suddenly and unexpectedly, like a dark cloud or a storm. The image of the sky being like murky oil and the mountains like wool suggests a world turned upside down, where everything familiar and comforting has been transformed into something strange and frightening. The image of close friends being like scattered moths implies that even those who were once united and supportive will be scattered and disconnected in the face of the coming punishment. The verse serves as a reminder to be mindful of one's actions and to be prepared for the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم
