translation: Indeed, We will suffice the dead, and We will record what they have presented and their traces, and everything We have counted in a clear register.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things, including the lives and deeds of human beings. The phrase 'We will suffice the dead' suggests that God is capable of reviving the dead and judging them based on their deeds. The verse also highlights the idea of accountability, as every action and trace of an individual's life is recorded and kept in a 'clear register'. This serves as a reminder to believers that their actions have consequences and that they will be held accountable for them in the afterlife.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And put forward an example for them of the people of the town, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: The verse refers to the story of the people of the town who were visited by messengers, possibly angels or prophets, who brought them a message of warning and guidance. The verse is encouraging the listener to consider the example of the people of the town, who were given a chance to repent and change their ways, but refused to listen and were ultimately punished. The verse serves as a reminder that God's messengers have been sent to guide people towards the right path, and those who reject their message will face the consequences.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: And indeed, We sent to them two messengers, but they denied them both, so We strengthened them with a third, and they said, 'Surely we are messengers sent to you.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the story of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were warned by three messengers sent by God to turn away from their sinful ways. The people of the town rejected the messengers and their message, and as a result, God destroyed the towns with a rain of brimstone and fire. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's message and the importance of heeding His warnings.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They say: 'We are nothing but mortals like you, and the Most Merciful has revealed nothing but a human being like us.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was just a human being like them and that he did not receive any divine revelation from the Most Merciful (God). The verse refutes this claim by pointing out that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was indeed a human being, but he was chosen by God to receive revelation and convey it to humanity. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not just a human being like them, but he was chosen by God for a higher purpose. The verse also emphasizes the idea that the revelation he received was not from a human being but from the Most Merciful (God) himself.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, 'Our Lord knows that we are messengers unto you.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers when the Prophet Abraham and his son Ismail were building the Kaaba. They were amazed by the structure and asked who could have built such a magnificent building. Abraham replied that his Lord knew that they were messengers sent to them. The verse highlights the belief of Abraham and Ismail in one God, and their conviction that they were on a divine mission to spread God's message. It also underscores the idea that the Prophets of God are divinely appointed and guided, and that their message is not of human origin, but rather from the Creator Himself.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And nothing has been revealed to me except the clear warning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of the message revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse suggests that the message is not ambiguous or complicated, but rather clear and straightforward. The word 'balagh' (revelation) implies a message that is conveyed in a clear and eloquent manner, without any ambiguity or obscurity. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and the believers that the message of Islam is a clear guidance, and it is the responsibility of the believers to convey it to others in a clear and unambiguous manner.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we have been sent to you as punishment, if you do not cease, we will stone you and cause a painful punishment to come upon you.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the warning given by the prophet Lot to the people of Sodom, who were known for their wickedness and immorality. The verse emphasizes the severity of their punishment, which would come in the form of stoning and a painful torment, if they did not stop their sinful ways. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a virtuous life.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, 'You are no more than a magician, and the Most Merciful has revealed to you [this Qur'an] to mislead people from their religion.',
interpretation: The disbelievers of Mecca accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of being a magician and claimed that the Qur'an was a fabrication designed to mislead people from their traditional religion. This verse highlights the opposition and skepticism that the Prophet faced in his mission to spread the message of Islam. It also underscores the idea that the Qur'an is a revelation from God, sent to guide people to the truth and to warn them of the consequences of their actions.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And a man from the farthest part of the city came running, saying, 'O people, follow the messengers!',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene where a man from the outskirts of the city is urging the people to follow the messengers of God. The man is described as coming from the farthest part of the city, indicating that he is an outsider, not part of the mainstream society. His urging the people to follow the messengers suggests that he has received a message from God and is now spreading it to others. The verse highlights the importance of listening to and following the guidance of God's messengers, even if they come from outside the mainstream society.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: Follow those who do not ask you for a wage, and they are guided.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following spiritual leaders who are guided by God and do not seek material reward or recognition. The phrase 'do not ask you for a wage' suggests that these leaders are not motivated by personal gain, but rather by their devotion to God and their desire to guide others on the path of righteousness. The word 'guided' in the second part of the verse implies that these leaders are themselves following God's guidance and are worthy of emulation. The verse encourages believers to seek out such leaders and follow their example in order to deepen their faith and spiritual practice.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: And what is left for me that I should not worship Him Who created me and to Whom you shall return?
interpretation: The verse is a question posed by the Prophet Abraham, addressing his father, who was an idolater. Abraham is asking his father what benefit he gets by not worshiping the One who created him and to Whom he will eventually return. The verse emphasizes the idea that worshiping idols is futile and that ultimately, all will return to Allah. It is an invitation to reflect on the purpose of worship and the futility of worshiping anything other than Allah.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, that they might be helped. They cannot help them, and they will be brought forward as a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of polytheism and the inability of idols to provide any real help or assistance. The verse emphasizes that those who worship idols are actually harming themselves, as they are not only disobeying God but also putting their trust in false deities that cannot provide any real support or protection. The verse also serves as a warning to those who are inclined towards polytheism, reminding them that their idols will ultimately be used as evidence against them on Judgment Day.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I am lost in clear error.
interpretation: The verse expresses the idea of being lost in clear error, suggesting a state of confusion or misguidance. The use of the word 'lost' implies a sense of helplessness and confusion, while the phrase 'clear error' emphasizes the obvious nature of the mistake. The verse may be interpreted as a reflection on the human condition, highlighting the fragility of human understanding and the ease with which one can stray from the right path. It serves as a reminder of the need for guidance and self-reflection in order to avoid falling into such errors.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is expressing their belief in God and requesting that others listen to their words. The use of the phrase 'فاسمعون' (so listen to me) emphasizes the importance of listening and paying attention to the message being conveyed. The verse suggests that the speaker has a deep conviction in their belief and is urging others to do the same. It serves as a call to action, encouraging others to listen and follow the teachings of the speaker, who is seen as a believer and a guide.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: And he said, 'Enter Paradise.' He said: 'O would that my people knew',
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who has been granted entry into Paradise, and he wishes that his people could also experience the same blessing. The verse highlights the regret and longing of the person for his community, who are still living in ignorance and sin. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of guiding others towards righteousness and the value of spreading knowledge and awareness of God's teachings.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: And my Lord has forgiven me, and made me of the honored ones.
interpretation: The verse expresses the speaker's gratitude towards God for forgiving them and granting them a high status among the righteous. The use of the phrase "my Lord" emphasizes the personal relationship between the speaker and God, and the phrase "and made me of the honored ones" highlights the idea that God's forgiveness has elevated the speaker to a state of honor and respect. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God's forgiveness and the importance of seeking His mercy and guidance.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We have not sent any apostle except that he should be obeyed by Allah's permission.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's messengers and the authority that they have been given by God. The verse suggests that the messengers were sent by God's permission and that their message is not their own, but rather a revelation from God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to follow the teachings of the messengers and to submit to God's will, as disobedience to the messengers is disobedience to God.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: Indeed, I was only a single loud cry, and they were deafened.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Prophet's frustration and sadness at the people's refusal to listen to his message. The metaphor of a 'single loud cry' emphasizes the clarity and simplicity of the message, which should have been enough to awaken the listeners from their spiritual slumber. The phrase 'and they were deafened' suggests that the people's refusal to listen was not due to a lack of clarity in the message, but rather a result of their own stubbornness and unwillingness to hear. The verse highlights the importance of listening to the message of the Prophet and the consequences of ignoring it.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: O woe is me! Would that I had not been sent to them!
interpretation: The verse expresses the Prophet's frustration and sadness at the people's reaction to his message. The phrase 'O woe is me' is an expression of despair and disappointment, indicating that the Prophet felt a deep sense of sorrow and regret for having been sent to a people who were not receptive to his message. The verse highlights the Prophet's emotional struggle in dealing with a people who refused to listen and accept the truth, and serves as a reminder of the challenges that prophets and messengers have faced throughout history.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them, whom We had established in the earth as We have not established you? And We poured down upon them the rain in abundance, and We made the rivers flow beneath them. Yet, We destroyed them for their sins, and created after them other generations.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of human history, where generations come and go, and how God's judgment and punishment are a constant factor throughout. The verse emphasizes the idea that God has been consistent in His treatment of previous generations, and that the current generation should not feel secure from His punishment. The mention of the rain and rivers emphasizes God's provision and favor, but also serves as a reminder of His power to destroy those who reject Him. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, everything will be destroyed, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is in them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the impermanence of all things in this world and the ultimate destruction of everything. It serves as a reminder that nothing lasts forever and that everything will eventually return to God, the ultimate owner and controller of all things. The verse also underscores the importance of recognizing and acknowledging God's sovereignty and praising Him for His blessings and favors. It is a call to humility and gratitude, reminding believers to focus on what truly matters in life and to live in accordance with God's will.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And We have made the earth a sign for them, and We have grown grain from it, and from it they eat, and their livestock they have,
interpretation: The verse highlights God's favor upon humanity by making the earth a sign of His mercy and provision. The verse emphasizes the abundance of God's blessings, as the earth produces grain for human consumption and provides sustenance for their livestock. The verse serves as a reminder of God's generosity and the responsibility that comes with it, as humans are accountable for their actions and are encouraged to use these blessings wisely and in a way that pleases God.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We have made therein gardens of date-palms and grapes, and We have caused springs to gush forth therein.
interpretation: The verse describes the beauty and abundance of the destroyed towns, which were blessed with gardens of date-palms and grapes, and had springs flowing through them. The verse emphasizes the idea that the towns were not just punished for their injustice, but were also blessed with natural beauty and resources, which they failed to appreciate and utilize properly. The verse serves as a reminder to the reader to appreciate and utilize the blessings they have been given, and to avoid falling into the same mistakes as the people of the destroyed towns.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: And they will eat of the fruit of their deeds, and they will not be increased except in destruction.
interpretation: The verse suggests that people will eventually face the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'fruit of their deeds' refers to the outcome of their actions, whether it be positive or negative. The second part of the verse, 'and they will not be increased except in destruction', implies that the consequences of their actions will not lead to any positive outcome, but rather to further destruction and punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in negative behavior, reminding them that their actions will have negative consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create the universe and all that is in it, including the heavens, earth, and everything in between, in just six days. The verse also highlights the fact that God was not tired or weakened by this creation, indicating His infinite power and strength. This verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and majesty, and encourages believers to reflect on the beauty and complexity of creation and the power of the Creator.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And We have made the night a cloak for them, so that they may sleep in it, and at dawn, they will be in a state of confusion.
interpretation: The verse describes how God has given the wicked people a period of respite during the night, allowing them to sleep and be oblivious to the coming punishment. The phrase 'وآية لهم الليل' (and the night is a cloak for them) suggests that the night serves as a protective covering for them, allowing them to rest and be unaware of the impending doom. The phrase 'نسلخ منه النهار' (and at dawn, they will be in a state of confusion) implies that when the punishment arrives, it will catch them off guard, and they will be confused and disoriented, unable to escape the consequences of their actions.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term appointed; that is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: The verse describes the sun's movement in the sky as a sign of God's power and wisdom. The phrase 'fixed course' suggests a predetermined path that the sun follows, indicating the idea of a predestined fate. The phrase 'term appointed' implies a sense of limitation and accountability, suggesting that everything in the universe, including the sun, is subject to God's decree. The description of God as 'All-Mighty' and 'All-Knowing' emphasizes God's omnipotence and omniscience, highlighting God's ability to control and guide all things in the universe.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And the moon, We have determined its phases until it returns, like an old date palm, to complete its cycle.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the moon and its phases, which are a symbol of the cyclical nature of time and the passage of life. The comparison of the moon to an old date palm emphasizes the idea that just as the moon goes through different phases, so too does life go through different stages, from youth to old age. The verse serves as a reminder of the passing nature of life and the need to make the most of the time we have.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: The sun cannot catch up to the moon, nor can the night outstrip the day. Each one is traveling in its own orbit, swimming in its own sphere.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the natural order of the universe, where each celestial body has its own path and purpose. The sun and the moon are used as metaphors for the believers and the disbelievers. The believers are like the sun, shining bright and steady on their path, while the disbelievers are like the moon, sometimes visible and sometimes hidden. The verse reminds us that both groups have their own role to play in the grand scheme of things and that each one is accountable for their own actions.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message, which is meant to bring people closer to God and to guide them towards a righteous and harmonious life.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We have created for them similar ones to which they ride,
interpretation: The verse speaks about the creation of horses and other mounts that people use for transportation. The verse suggests that these animals are a blessing from God and a means of transportation that people should be grateful for. The use of the word 'similar' (mithl) suggests that these animals are not exact copies of each other, but rather similar in nature and purpose. The verse also highlights the idea that humans have a tendency to take things for granted and forget the blessings that God has bestowed upon them.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And indeed, We have drowned them, and they had no cry for help, nor were they able to be saved.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who were destroyed by the flood. The use of the word 'nashaa' (نشأ) emphasizes the idea that they were overwhelmed and engulfed by the water, leaving them with no chance of escape or rescue. The phrase 'sariik' (صريخ) means 'a cry for help' and the fact that they had no such cry suggests that they were completely helpless in the face of the disaster. The final phrase 'walam yanqaliboon' (ولا هم ينقذون) reinforces the idea that they were unable to save themselves, leaving them at the mercy of the floodwaters. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God and the consequences of disobeying His commands.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: Except for mercy from Us and a provision until a specified time.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the exception to the destruction of towns that were unjust. The verse indicates that the destruction was not absolute and that there was a chance for the people to repent and change their ways. The 'mercy' and 'provision' refer to the opportunity given to the people to reform and turn to God before the punishment came. The phrase 'until a specified time' indicates that the reprieve was temporary and that the punishment was inevitable if the people did not change their ways. The verse serves as a reminder of God's mercy and the possibility of redemption, while also emphasizing the certainty of punishment for those who refuse to repent.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, perhaps you will receive mercy',
interpretation: The verse addresses the people who have been warned of the consequences of their actions. They are told to fear God and be mindful of their deeds, both in their present and in their past. The verse implies that the people have been given a chance to repent and change their ways, and that if they do so, they may receive God's mercy. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-seeing, and that our actions have consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And how many a sign from their Lord have they rejected, so they will be overcome by the encounter of their reckoning.
interpretation: The verse refers to the many signs and miracles that were sent by God to guide humanity, but were rejected by those who chose to disbelieve. The verse warns that these individuals will be overcome by the encounter of their reckoning, suggesting that they will be held accountable for their actions and will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Spend from what Allah has provided for you,' those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Shall we feed those whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' response to the believers' call for them to spend from what God has provided. The disbelievers argue that if God had willed to feed the believers, He would have done so Himself, and that the believers' request for them to spend is baseless. The verse highlights the disbelievers' misunderstanding of God's role in providing sustenance and their lack of faith in His ability to do so. It also underscores the believers' conviction that God's provision is not limited to material sustenance but also encompasses spiritual nourishment and guidance.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' skepticism and mocking of the believers' belief in the promise of God's punishment. The disbelievers are asking when this promised punishment will come to pass, implying that they do not believe it will ever happen. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not bound by human timelines or expectations and that it will come when it is least expected, just as it did with the towns that were destroyed in the past.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They do not await aught but a single cry, which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of disbelief and arrogance of those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are so engrossed in their disputes and arguments that they are oblivious to the warning signs of the impending punishment. The verse suggests that they will be taken by surprise, suddenly and unexpectedly, just as they are engrossed in their disputes and arguments, emphasizing the certainty and suddenness of God's punishment.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: And they will not be able to give a justification, nor will they be able to receive advice.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of those who have gone astray and are unable to find their way back to the right path. They are unable to offer any justification for their actions, and they are also unable to receive advice or guidance from others. This verse highlights the state of spiritual deprivation and confusion that those who have strayed from God's path may find themselves in.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And they have been commanded no more than to worship Allah Alone, keeping the religion pure for Him, and to worship none but Him Alone, and to perform the prayer and give the charity, and that is the right religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the simplicity and purity of the message of Islam, which is to worship Allah alone and to follow the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse highlights the importance of maintaining the purity of one's faith and not associating partners with Allah. It also emphasizes the importance of performing the obligatory prayers and giving charity, which are fundamental aspects of the Islamic faith. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay on the right path and to avoid being distracted by worldly temptations or deviating from the true teachings of Islam.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! We have been left behind from our dear friend.' That is how the Merciful One promised and the messengers spoke the truth.
interpretation: The verse describes the regret and remorse of those who have been left behind after the departure of the Prophet and his companions. They realize that they have missed out on the opportunity to accompany the Prophet and experience the blessings that came with it. The verse emphasizes the idea that the promise of God is true and that the messengers of God speak the truth. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have been left behind to reflect on their actions and to make amends for their mistakes, and to be mindful of the promise of God and the truth of His messengers.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: And indeed, I (Muhammad) was only a single cry away from the angels, when they came to me in response to my call.
interpretation: The verse highlights the proximity and accessibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the angels and the divine realm. The use of the word 'cry' emphasizes the immediacy and urgency of the connection between the Prophet and the angels. The verse suggests that the Prophet was constantly connected to the divine realm and that the angels were always ready to respond to his call, signifying the Prophet's status as a chosen servant of God and the efficacy of his prayers and supplications.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And on the Day of Judgment, no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will not be recompensed except what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fairness and justice of the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be judged based on their deeds. No one will be wronged or treated unfairly, and everyone will receive exactly what they deserve, according to their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability and responsibility that comes with being human, and the need to live a life that is pleasing to God in order to receive a positive judgment on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: And the companions of the Garden will today be in a state of loss and regret.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the companions of the Garden, who are now in a state of loss and regret. The verse suggests that they were once living a life of luxury and indulgence, but now they are faced with the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'في شغل فاكهون' implies that they are now in a state of remorse and regret, realizing that their indulgence has led them astray and that they have squandered their opportunity to live a righteous life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in luxury and excess, reminding them of the importance of living a life of purpose and righteousness.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you do not remember.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of previous nations who were destroyed by God due to their sins and injustices. The verse is a reminder to the current generation that they too will face similar consequences if they continue to live in disobedience to God's commands. The verse also emphasizes the idea that people tend to forget the lessons of history and continue to repeat the same mistakes, leading to their downfall.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace, a word from the Merciful Lord.
interpretation: The verse speaks of the peace that comes from the Merciful Lord. The word 'peace' is a greeting that is often used in Islam, and it is a reminder of the peace and tranquility that can be found in the mercy and grace of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the source of peace and the importance of seeking peace and mercy from God.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: And they were left astonished and confused on the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the wicked on the Day of Judgment, when they will be left astonished and confused, unable to defend themselves or deny their crimes. The verse suggests that their confusion will be a result of their own actions and the consequences they have brought upon themselves. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the certainty of their accountability on the Day of Judgment and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the whispers of human's inner thoughts and is closer to them than their own jugular vein, indicating a deep and intimate connection between the Creator and His creation. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always aware of human's thoughts, feelings, and actions, and that He is always near to guide and assist them.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And worship Me, for this is a straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping God and following a righteous path. The use of the word 'straight' (مستقيم) suggests a path that is clear, direct, and without deviation. It implies that the path of worship is a straightforward one, and that those who follow it will be guided to a righteous and just life. The verse serves as a reminder that the purpose of human existence is to worship God and to live according to His commandments, and that this path is the only way to achieve true happiness and fulfillment.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many generations after Noah's time, and you will surely be destroyed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the repetition of history, where previous generations were destroyed by God due to their sins and injustices. The verse serves as a warning to the current generation, reminding them that they too will face the consequences of their actions, just like the generations before them. It emphasizes the idea that the destruction of previous generations should serve as a lesson and a warning to the current generation, and that they should not be complacent in their sins, thinking that they will not face the same fate.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is the Hell that you were promised.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Hellfire that was promised to the disbelievers and sinners. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the punishment and the fact that it is a consequence of their own actions. The use of the word 'promised' implies that the punishment was inevitable and that it was foretold. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: And they were reprimanded on the day they were destroyed, 'Taste the punishment of eternal suffering!'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the disbelievers and the punishment they faced on the day of their destruction. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment is eternal and that they will suffer forever. The verse also implies that the disbelievers were warned and reprimanded before their destruction, but they refused to believe and continued to disobey God. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of judgment day when the wicked people will be silenced and their bodies will testify against them. The verse implies that the people's actions and deeds will be exposed and judged by God, and they will have no excuse or justification for their wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the day of reckoning and the consequences of their actions.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience in not destroying the disbelievers immediately. Instead, He gives them respite in this life, allowing them to repent and turn back to Him. The verse also warns that the punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe than any punishment in this life, and serves as a warning to those who reject God's message.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with His creation. Despite the people's disobedience and sin, God does not immediately punish them. Instead, He gives them respite and time to repent and turn back to Him. The verse highlights the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's mercy and continue to live in disobedience. The punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe than any punishment that could be inflicted in this life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of God's signs and encourages them to reflect on their actions and turn back to God.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophetic nature of Muhammad's mission, which was not to destroy or condemn, but rather to bring mercy and guidance to all people. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message was not limited to a particular community or time, but was universal and timeless. The verse highlights the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and compassion, and serves as a reminder that the purpose of religion is to bring people closer to God and to promote peace, love, and understanding.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: And warn those who say, 'God has taken a son.'
interpretation: The verse orders the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn those who claim that God has taken a son, which is a belief held by some polytheists and Christians. The verse emphasizes the gravity of this claim, as it implies that God, who is considered the all-powerful and self-sufficient, needs a son to help Him or to be a mediator between Him and humanity. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of shirk (associating partners with God) and the importance of maintaining the oneness of God in belief and worship.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: And indeed, We have created for them livestock which they own, and they do not dismount them, and they do not feed them, and they do not drink their milk, and they do not ride them, and they do not benefit from them at all, and they do not realize that they will be raised, and they will be returned to their Lord, and they will be asked.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ingratitude of the disbelievers who fail to recognize and appreciate the blessings of Allah, particularly in the livestock they own. The verse emphasizes that these livestock are a means of sustenance, transportation, and other benefits, yet the disbelievers fail to utilize them properly. The verse also warns that these blessings will ultimately be taken away from them and they will be held accountable for their ingratitude on Judgment Day.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We have destroyed them, and theirs is a lesson to those who come after them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the destruction of the previous nations and how their downfall serves as a lesson and warning to those who come after them. The verse highlights the idea that the destruction of these nations is not just a historical event, but a lesson for future generations. It serves as a reminder that God's punishment is real and that those who disobey and disregard His commands will face similar consequences.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And for them are benefits and honors in this life, but they do not thank.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of the disbelievers' behavior, who, despite enjoying the blessings and favors of God in this life, do not express gratitude to Him. Their ingratitude is a reflection of their arrogance and lack of humility, and serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their own attitude towards God's blessings and to cultivate a spirit of gratitude and thankfulness.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be helped.
interpretation: The verse refers to the practice of idolatry, where people have taken gods other than Allah, hoping to receive help and support from them. The verse highlights the futility of this practice, as only Allah has the power to provide true help and support. The verse serves as a reminder that putting faith in anything other than Allah is futile and that true help and support come only from Allah.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: And they will not be able to help themselves, and they will have a group of supporters.
interpretation: The verse describes the situation of those who have strayed from the path of righteousness and are unable to find any support or aid, whether from themselves or from others. The phrase 'they will not be able to help themselves' emphasizes their powerlessness and inability to change their situation. The phrase 'and they will have a group of supporters' suggests that despite their inability to help themselves, they will still have a group of people who will support and encourage them in their misguided ways. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: And their saying: 'We have believed in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey His command.' But then they continue to commit oppression, and they are not believers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who claim to believe in God and the Messenger, but their actions contradict their words. They continue to commit oppression, which shows that their faith is not genuine. The verse highlights the importance of actions over mere words and emphasizes that true faith is reflected in righteous deeds. It serves as a warning to those who claim to be believers but do not act accordingly, reminding them that true faith requires obedience to God's commands and justice towards others.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind from a sperm-drop, and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights the miraculous creation of human beings from a mere sperm-drop, emphasizing God's power and wisdom in bringing forth life from something so small and insignificant. The verse also underscores the idea that God is fully aware of the thoughts and whispers of human beings, and is closer to them than their own jugular vein, indicating God's omnipresence and intimate connection with His creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's proximity and knowledge of human beings, and encourages them to reflect on their own creation and relationship with their Creator.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And He strikes an example for us, forgetting the creation of the first creation. He said: 'Who will give life to the bones while they are decayed and turned into dust?',
interpretation: The verse uses the metaphor of the creation of the first human being, Adam, to illustrate God's power to bring life to the dead. The verse emphasizes that just as God breathed life into the lifeless body of Adam, He can also bring life to those who are spiritually dead, those who have forgotten their purpose of creation. The verse is a reminder to those who have forgotten their purpose in life, to turn back to God and remember their ultimate goal, and to seek guidance from Him. It also serves as a reminder of the power of God and His ability to bring life to those who are spiritually dead.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, 'He will give life to whom He will, and He will kill whom He will.' Indeed, He is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and power over life and death. The use of the word 'He' in the verse underscores God's agency and control over all things. The phrase 'He will give life to whom He will' suggests that God has the power to grant life to whomever He chooses, and the phrase 'and He will kill whom He will' indicates that God also has the power to take life away. The verse serves as a reminder of God's authority and wisdom in all matters, and encourages believers to trust in God's judgment and submit to His will.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: And He has made for you from the green tree, fuel, and from it you ignite a fire.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the blessings of God upon humanity, specifically the provision of fuel from trees for cooking and heating. The verse highlights the importance of gratitude and appreciation for God's blessings, as well as the responsibility to use these blessings in a responsible and sustainable manner. The image of fire, which is both a source of warmth and light, symbolizes the divine guidance and wisdom that is available to those who seek it.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed; He is the All-Knowing Creator.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create, suggesting that if He can create the heavens and the earth, then He certainly has the power to create similar things. The phrase 'Yes, indeed' is used to emphasize the idea that God's power is not limited by anything, and that He is capable of creating anything He wills. The description of God as the 'All-Knowing Creator' highlights His infinite knowledge and wisdom, suggesting that He is aware of all things and has a plan for everything.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: And indeed, Our Word has gone forth unto Our servants the messengers, (saying): Verily, We have caused the destruction of the wicked peoples.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority over His creation. The phrase 'Our Word' refers to God's decree or command, which is always carried out and never fails. The verse states that God's messengers were instructed to warn the wicked people of their impending destruction, and that the destruction was indeed carried out as promised. The verse serves as a reminder of God's justice and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is capable of everything.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and praise, indicating that everything belongs to Him and He has the power to control and manage all affairs. The verse also highlights God's ability to do anything, indicating that nothing is impossible for Him. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is the ultimate authority and that they should submit to His will and trust in His abilities.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Your god is one God. There is no god but He, the All-Merciful, the Very Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, affirming that the God worshiped by the believers is the only God, and that there is no other deity worthy of worship. The description of God as 'the All-Merciful, the Very Merciful' highlights His attribute of mercy and compassion, indicating that He is a God who is forgiving and slow to anger, and who desires to show mercy to His creation.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the sunrises.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over the entire universe, encompassing all that exists between the heavens and the earth, including all celestial bodies and everything on earth. The phrase 'Lord of the sunrises' specifically highlights God's control over the cycles of day and night, reminding us of His power and dominion over all creation. It is a reminder to believers to recognize and acknowledge God's greatness and to submit to His will.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and an adornment of the stars.
interpretation: The verse describes how God has embellished the lowest heaven with lamps and stars. The lamps refer to the stars that are visible in the night sky, while the stars are a metaphor for the angels who are responsible for the affairs of the universe. The verse emphasizes the beauty and majesty of God's creation, and how He has adorned the heavens with celestial bodies that serve as signs for guidance and inspiration for humanity. The verse also highlights the greatness of God's power and wisdom in creating such a magnificent universe.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirms the Scripture that came before it, and We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which is confirmed by its consistency with previous scriptures. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the triumph of Islam over other religions and the spread of its teachings, while 'manifest triumph' signifies the clarity and clarification of divine guidance. The verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, reinforcing their faith and confidence in the divine message.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: And they will not listen to the exalted angels, and they will be deaf to every side.
interpretation: The verse describes the people's refusal to listen to the messages of the prophets and the warnings of the angels. The phrase 'they will not listen to the exalted angels' suggests that the people have become stubborn and arrogant, refusing to heed the advice of even the most respected and revered spiritual authorities. The phrase 'and they will be deaf to every side' emphasizes the extent of their disobedience, indicating that they have become completely impervious to reason and guidance, unwilling to listen to anyone or anything that contradicts their own desires and beliefs.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except for him who snatches off the spoils of war, followed by a burning flame.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the exception to the general rule of the destruction of towns. The exception is the one who snatches off the spoils of war, indicating that even in the midst of destruction, there is a chance for redemption and forgiveness. The image of a burning flame following the spoils of war suggests a purifying and transformative process, signifying that even in the midst of destruction, there is the potential for spiritual growth and renewal.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come willingly or unwillingly.' They both said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe and everything in it by God. The verse emphasizes the idea that everything in the universe, including the heavens and the earth, was created by God's command, and that they all submitted to His will. The verse also highlights the idea of submission, which is a recurring theme in the Qur'an, and serves as a reminder to believers of their duty to submit to God's will.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: The verse suggests that even when the unjust people are reminded of their wrongdoing and the consequences of their actions, they still do not remember or reflect on their behavior. Their hearts are hardened, and they continue to live in denial, refusing to acknowledge the truth and change their ways. The verse highlights the importance of self-reflection and the need to listen to advice and admonition in order to avoid the consequences of one's actions.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they saw a sign, they ridiculed it.
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers when they were shown a miracle or a sign from God. Instead of believing and submitting to God, they ridiculed and mocked the sign, rejecting its authenticity and the message it conveyed. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who refuse to acknowledge the truth and instead choose to mock and belittle the signs of God. It serves as a warning to those who reject God's signs and messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the severity of God's punishment.
orig: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون

translation: And they said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the miraculous signs and revelations of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismissed the signs as mere magic and illusions, refusing to acknowledge the divine origin of the Prophet's message. The verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of the disbelievers, who were unwilling to accept the truth and instead chose to attribute the Prophet's miracles to sorcery or magic. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of recognizing and accepting the truth, even when it goes against our preconceived notions and beliefs.
orig: وقالوا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were far more powerful than you, and the punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power of God and His ability to destroy even the most powerful towns and cities. The use of the phrase 'far more powerful than you' suggests that the towns being referred to were not only larger and more prosperous than the town being addressed, but also more arrogant and rebellious against God's commandments. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that no matter how powerful they may think they are, they are still accountable to God and will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظاما أإنا لمبعوثون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were older than you, and the retribution was [deserved].
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of towns that were older than the Prophet Jonah's town, and emphasizes that the punishment was justified and well-deserved. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that God's punishment is not limited to any particular nation or time, and that it will come to those who persist in their wrongdoing.
orig: أوآباؤنا الأولون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, we have been forbidden from saying ugly things.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is commanded to say that they have been forbidden from saying ugly things. The word 'ugly' can refer to anything that is morally or ethically wrong, such as lies, gossip, or obscenity. The verse emphasizes the importance of speaking truthfully and avoiding any speech that may be harmful or offensive to others. It serves as a reminder to be mindful of the impact of our words on others and to always strive to speak with kindness and respect.
orig: قل نعم وأنتم داخرون

translation: And indeed, it is a single punishment, but they are differing.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the punishment that will befall the wicked will be a single, unified one, despite their differences and disputes. The verse suggests that the people are ignoring the warning signs and are too caught up in their own disputes to heed the warning of the impending punishment. The use of the word 'zajra' (single) emphasizes the idea that the punishment will be indiscriminate and will affect all those who are deserving of it, regardless of their differences.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم ينظرون

translation: And they say, 'O woe to us! What is this day of reckoning?
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they are faced with the reality of the Day of Judgment. They are shocked and dismayed, exclaiming 'O woe to us!' indicating their regret and remorse for their past actions. The phrase 'What is this day of reckoning?' suggests that they are confused and unaware of what is happening, highlighting their lack of preparedness for the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglectful of their spiritual responsibilities and serve as a reminder of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقالوا يا ويلنا هذا يوم الدين

translation: This is the Day of Judgment that you used to deny.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Day of Judgment, which is a central concept in Islamic eschatology. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, which was previously denied by those who disbelieved in God's revelations. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of all human actions and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, when everyone will be judged according to their deeds.
orig: هذا يوم الفصل الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: And warn those who have been unjust and their wives and what they worship besides Allah.
interpretation: The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn those who have been unjust and their wives, indicating that they are equally responsible for their actions and will face consequences. The verse also emphasizes the gravity of their situation by mentioning their false deities, indicating that their idolatry is a serious offense and will not be tolerated by God. The verse serves as a reminder that everyone, regardless of their gender or beliefs, will be held accountable for their actions and must turn to the one true God for guidance and redemption.
orig: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم وما كانوا يعبدون

translation: And lead them to the path of hell;
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to follow their own desires and false deities. The verse describes God's punishment for those who disobey Him, leading them to the path of hell, which is a symbol of eternal suffering and punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: من دون الله فاهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم

translation: And We have put forth examples for the people in this Qur'an, so that they may take heed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and warning for humanity. The use of the word 'examples' (qasas) suggests that the Qur'an contains stories and parables that serve as lessons for people to learn from. The verse highlights the responsibility of individuals to reflect on the teachings of the Qur'an and to take heed of its warnings, lest they suffer the same fate as previous nations who ignored God's messages.

interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the disbelievers to the Prophet Ibrahim's call to worship only one God. They accused him of following his father's religion, implying that his beliefs were not based on reason or evidence, but only on blind tradition. The verse highlights the tension between following tradition and following reason and faith. It emphasizes the importance of questioning one's beliefs and not blindly following the beliefs of one's ancestors.

They refused to believe and arrogantly declared that they would not be convinced or become believers. Their reaction reflects their stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth. The verse highlights the importance of faith and the consequences of rejecting it.

interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers had no authority or control over the disbelievers. The verse refutes the argument that the Prophet and his followers were responsible for the disbelievers' misfortunes. The verse also underscores the fact that the Prophet and the believers were not capable of harming or helping the disbelievers in any way. Instead, the responsibility for their actions and consequences lies solely with the disbelievers themselves.

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to a decisive and unambiguous victory, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is plainly visible and evident to all. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success is not due to their own efforts alone, but rather it is a blessing from God, and that they should be grateful for His favor.
orig: فحق علينا قول ربنا إنا لذائقون

translation: And We have destroyed towns before you, while they were unjust; indeed, We have been averse to wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and justice, emphasizing that He has destroyed entire towns in the past due to their injustice and disobedience. The use of 'ghawa' (we have destroyed) in the Arabic text emphasizes the sudden and complete nature of the destruction, signifying that the towns were completely erased from existence. The verse serves as a warning to those living in sin and injustice, reminding them that God's punishment is real and imminent, and that He will not tolerate wrongdoing.
orig: فأغويناكم إنا كنا غاوين

translation: And indeed, they are, in the punishment, shareholders.
interpretation: The verse suggests that those who are destined for punishment in the afterlife will be shareholders in the suffering, implying that they will all receive their due punishment, and that no one will escape it. The use of the word 'mushatikoon' (shareholders) emphasizes the idea of collective responsibility and shared guilt, indicating that all those who have committed sins and injustices will be held accountable and punished accordingly.
orig: فإنهم يومئذ في العذاب مشتركون

translation: And indeed, We will punish the criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of punishment for those who commit crimes and injustices. The use of the word 'indeed' (كذلك) suggests a sense of certainty and inevitability, implying that the punishment is a natural consequence of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in criminal behavior, reminding them that they will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: إنا كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين

translation: They were arrogant and proud when it was said to them: 'There is no god but Allah'; they were scornful and disbelieving.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were told that there is no god but Allah. They were arrogant and proud, and they scorned and disbelieved the message. The verse highlights the attitude of those who reject the truth and refuse to submit to the will of God. It serves as a reminder that true faith requires humility and submission to the divine, and that arrogance and pride can be barriers to recognizing and accepting the truth.

interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been practicing polytheism and worshiping multiple gods, but are now expressing their desire to leave their false deities and turn to the one true God, the Lord of the heavens and the earth. The verse highlights the recognition of the people that their previous beliefs were misguided and that they are now seeking guidance and forgiveness from the only true God.

translation: And indeed, the truth has come, and the falsehood has vanished. Indeed, the falsehood is vanquished, and the truth has prevailed.
interpretation: The verse declares the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. The phrase 'the truth has come' refers to the arrival of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the revelation of the Qur'an, which is the embodiment of truth. The phrase 'the falsehood has vanished' signifies the disappearance of all false beliefs, ideologies, and ways of life that oppose the truth. The final phrase, 'the falsehood is vanquished, and the truth has prevailed', emphasizes the ultimate victory of truth and the defeat of falsehood. This verse serves as a reminder to believers that despite the challenges they may face, truth will ultimately prevail, and they must remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

translation: Indeed, you are dear to Me, O guilty ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers, addressing them as 'dear' and 'guilty ones'. The term 'dear' signifies God's love and mercy towards them, while 'guilty ones' refers to their state of sin and need for repentance. The verse serves as a reminder that, despite their sins, the believers are still dear to God and are worthy of His love and guidance. It encourages them to turn towards God in repentance and seek His forgiveness.
orig: إنكم لذائقو العذاب الأليم

translation: And what have they not been reprimanded for their evil deeds?
interpretation: The verse addresses the fact that the wicked are not reprimanded for their evil deeds, suggesting that they will face consequences for their actions. The verse implies that the lack of punishment in this life does not mean that they will escape punishment altogether, as they will still face God's judgment in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in evil deeds, reminding them that their actions will have consequences, even if they are not immediately punished.

interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed towns in the past that were more powerful than Makkah, where the Prophet was living. The verse emphasizes that these towns were destroyed because of their sins and disobedience to God. The verse serves as a warning to the people of Makkah, reminding them that they too will face similar consequences if they continue to reject God's message and disobey His commands.
orig: قال تالله إن كدت لتردين

translation: Were it not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among the destroyed.
interpretation: The verse expresses gratitude to God for His favor and protection. The speaker acknowledges that they would have been destroyed or punished if it weren't for God's mercy and grace. The verse highlights the idea that God's favor and protection are essential for our well-being and survival, and that we should be grateful for His blessings in our lives.
orig: ولولا نعمة ربي لكنت من المحضرين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفما نحن بميتين

translation: Except the first death, and we will be the ones to be punished.
interpretation: The verse refers to the fact that everyone will eventually taste death, and that the first death (the death of the body) is not the end, as there will be a second death (the death of the soul) for those who have not lived righteously. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of death and the need to live a life that is pleasing to God in order to avoid the punishment that will come in the hereafter.
orig: إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the great triumph.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate victory of the righteous and the believers. The phrase 'Indeed, this is the great triumph' signifies that the path of righteousness and belief leads to ultimate success and triumph in both this life and the hereafter. It serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to remain committed to the path of righteousness, as it will ultimately lead to a successful and fulfilling life.
orig: إن هذا لهو الفوز العظيم
