The phrase 'fainnthur' (فانظر) draws attention to the fact that the punishment was so severe that it is beyond human comprehension. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, 'I am dissociating myself from what you worship',
interpretation: The verse describes Abraham's declaration of his faith and his rejection of the idolatry practiced by his father and his people. The verse highlights Abraham's courage and conviction in standing up against his family and community, and his commitment to monotheism. It also underscores the importance of recognizing and rejecting false worship and instead, devoting oneself to the worship of the one true God.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه وقومه إنني براء مما تعبدون

translation: Except the one who will be saved, he will be led to safety.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the exception to the general rule of destruction, referring to the person who is guided by God and will be saved from the punishment. The use of the word 'fatra' (except) emphasizes that this person is an exception to the general rule of destruction and highlights the idea that God is always aware of those who are righteous and deserving of His mercy. The phrase 'he will be led to safety' suggests that the person will not only be spared from destruction but will also be guided to a place of safety and security, indicating that God's mercy and guidance are not limited to this life but extend to the hereafter as well.
orig: إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين

translation: And We have made the Qur'an easy to remember, so is there anyone who will take heed?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the accessibility and clarity of the Qur'an, indicating that its message is straightforward and easy to understand. The verse poses a rhetorical question, asking if there is anyone who will take heed of the Qur'an's message and reflect on its teachings. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is a guidance and a warning for those who are willing to listen and take heed, and that its message is universal and applicable to all people.
orig: وجعلها كلمة باقية في عقبه لعلهم يرجعون

translation: But the evildoers dispute concerning their Lord, until they come to Us in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who argue and dispute with each other about the existence and oneness of God. The verse suggests that they will continue to do so until they face God's punishment, which will come suddenly and unexpectedly, either in the morning or at noon. The verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and reminds them that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: بل متعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين

translation: And when the truth came to them, they said, 'This is magic, and indeed we are disbelievers in it.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were confronted with the truth of Islam. They dismissed the message as magic and refused to believe in it. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who were unwilling to accept the truth and instead chose to reject it out of hand. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of being open-minded and receptive to the truth, and the dangers of allowing preconceived notions and biases to cloud one's judgment.
orig: ولما جاءهم الحق قالوا هذا سحر وإنا به كافرون

translation: And they say, 'If only this Qur'an was sent down upon a man from [one of] the two towns, we would have been guided,'
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' reaction to the Qur'an. They wish that the Qur'an was revealed to a prominent man from one of the two towns (Mecca or Ta'if), thinking that this would lend credibility to the message. The verse highlights their mistaken assumption that the Qur'an's authenticity is tied to the status of the person it was revealed to, rather than the content of the message itself. It also underscores the idea that guidance is not determined by the messenger's social standing, but by the message itself and the recipient's willingness to accept it.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل هذا القرآن على رجل من القريتين عظيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أهم يقسمون رحمت ربك نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم في الحياة الدنيا ورفعنا بعضهم فوق بعض درجات ليتخذ بعضهم بعضا سخريا ورحمت ربك خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if it were not for the fact that humankind would become one community (united in disbelief), We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful (God) roofs of silver and stairs (leading up) to their homes, and elevated them to a position of prominence.
interpretation: The verse expresses God's disappointment and anger towards those who reject and disbelieve in Him. Despite His infinite mercy and generosity, those who reject Him have been given the opportunity to live in luxury and abundance. The verse emphasizes that if all humans were united in their disbelief, God would have given them even more prosperity and power as a test of their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that material wealth and power are not signs of God's approval or love, and that true faith is tested through adversity and hardship.
orig: ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم سقفا من فضة ومعارج عليها يظهرون

translation: And We have destroyed their houses, with their roofs, and rained upon them stones of baked clay.
interpretation: The verse describes the destruction brought upon the people of Sodom and Gomorrah by God. The 'houses' mentioned in the verse refer not only to physical structures but also to the families and communities that lived in them. The 'stones of baked clay' that rained upon them symbolize the wrath of God, who punished them for their wickedness and perversion. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and justice, as well as the consequences of disobedience and sin.
orig: ولبيوتهم أبوابا وسررا عليها يتكئون

translation: And lost is he who has made his desire his god, and Allah - the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them - will not be a caretaker for him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of making one's desires the ultimate goal in life. The phrase 'lost is he who has made his desire his god' implies that those who prioritize their own desires above all else will ultimately fail and be disappointed. The verse also emphasizes that God, as the Lord of the heavens and the earth, will not be responsible for such individuals. This verse serves as a warning against the dangers of self-centeredness and the importance of keeping one's desires in check, lest they become an idol that replaces the worship of Allah.
orig: وزخرفا وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين

translation: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil as a companion.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who turn away from the remembrance of God, which is a punishment in itself. The companion referred to in the verse is none other than Satan, who becomes the constant companion of the one who has turned away from God's remembrance. This verse serves as a warning to those who neglect the remembrance of God and instead choose to live in disobedience to Him. It highlights the reality that by turning away from God, one is in fact, turning towards Satan and his evil influence. The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering God and living a life according to His commands, in order to avoid the negative consequences of neglecting His remembrance.
orig: ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا فهو له قرين

translation: And indeed, they will be turned away from the path, and they will be thought to be Muslims.
interpretation: The verse suggests that despite their outward appearance of being Muslims, those who reject the truth and refuse to follow the right path will ultimately be misguided and lost. The phrase 'turned away from the path' implies a deviation from the straight path of Islam, and the phrase 'thought to be Muslims' suggests that they may appear to be Muslims, but in reality, they are not. This verse serves as a warning to those who claim to be Muslims but do not follow the teachings of Islam in their actions and beliefs.
orig: وإنهم ليصدونهم عن السبيل ويحسبون أنهم مهتدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: حتى إذا جاءنا قال يا ليت بيني وبينك بعد المشرقين فبئس القرين

translation: And nothing will avail you today, for you have been unjust, in that you are sharing in the punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who have been unjust and have engaged in sinful behavior will not be able to escape the punishment of God. The phrase 'nothing will avail you' suggests that no amount of wealth, power, or intercession will be able to protect them from the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'you have been unjust' highlights the fact that their suffering is a direct result of their own actions, and that they have no one to blame but themselves. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them that they will face the consequences of their actions and that they cannot rely on external factors to save them.
orig: ولن ينفعكم اليوم إذ ظلمتم أنكم في العذاب مشتركون

translation: And indeed, We have sent you (O Muhammad) to all the people as a witness, and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and emphasizing the scope of his mission. The Prophet is described as a witness over all people, indicating his responsibility to convey the message of Islam to everyone, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse also highlights the dual nature of the Prophet's mission: he is a bringer of good news for those who accept Islam and a warner for those who reject it. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims that their role is not limited to preaching to the converted, but also to spread the message to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs.
orig: أفأنت تسمع الصم أو تهدي العمي ومن كان في ضلال مبين

translation: So, indeed We have brought you (Muhammad SAW) a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse declares that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been given a clear victory and a manifest triumph. The verse emphasizes the idea that the Prophet's victory is not just a personal triumph but a clear sign of God's support and approval. The phrase 'manifest triumph' suggests that the victory is not just a spiritual or moral one, but a tangible and visible one, manifesting in the worldly realm. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and his followers that their efforts are not in vain and that they will ultimately triumph over their opponents.
orig: فإما نذهبن بك فإنا منهم منتقمون

translation: Or have they not heard the news of those before them, the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and the people of Abraham, the people of Midian, and the cities that were overturned? Their Messengers came to them with clear signs. And Allah would never wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: The verse highlights the ignorance of those who reject God's message and refuse to learn from history. The verse refers to the stories of previous prophets and their communities, such as Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and the people of Abraham, who were all warned by God through His messengers but chose to ignore the warnings and continued to live in disobedience. The verse emphasizes that God's punishment is not unjust, but rather a consequence of the people's own actions. The phrase 'And Allah would never wrong them' emphasizes God's justice and mercy, while 'but they were wronging themselves' highlights the idea that it is the people's own actions that bring about their downfall.
orig: أو نرينك الذي وعدناهم فإنا عليهم مقتدرون

translation: And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah and do not separate.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of unity and holding fast to the teachings of God. The use of the metaphor 'rope of Allah' signifies that God's guidance is the only source of strength and support for believers. The verse warns against division and strife among believers, encouraging them to stay united under the banner of faith. It serves as a reminder that true strength and success come from adhering to God's teachings and supporting one another in righteousness and piety.
orig: فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك إنك على صراط مستقيم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory given by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies that the triumph was evident and indisputable, whereas the term 'manifest triumph' suggests that the victory was not only clear but also widely recognized and celebrated. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and continue to spread the message of Islam.
orig: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك وسوف تسألون

translation: And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers how We sent them as mercy from your Lord. Surely, We sent them with clear signs and scriptures, and We have sent down to you the Reminder so that you may clarify to the people what has been sent down to them, so that they may be mindful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of learning from the past messengers and their messages, which were sent as a mercy from God. The verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a reminder and a clarification of the messages that came before it. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers to convey the message of Islam to the people and to be mindful of the consequences of rejecting God's message.
orig: واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his council, and he said, 'I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse describes the prophethood of Moses and his mission to convey God's message to the Pharaoh and his council. The verse emphasizes Moses' claim of being a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, indicating his connection to the divine and his authority to convey God's message. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of prophethood and the role of prophets in guiding humanity towards righteousness and the worship of one God.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فقال إني رسول رب العالمين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say: 'We have heard, had we wanted, we would have said it (and thus it was).'
interpretation: This verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers when they were presented with the verses of the Qur'an. They dismissed the message by saying that they had heard it all before and could have come up with something similar themselves. The verse highlights their arrogance and unwillingness to listen to the message, as well as their lack of understanding of the true nature of the Qur'an as a revelation from God.
orig: فلما جاءهم بآياتنا إذا هم منها يضحكون

translation: And We have not sent any signs except that they were greater than their sister, and We seized them with punishment that they might turn back.
interpretation: The verse highlights the severity of God's punishment, emphasizing that the signs and warnings sent to the people were clear and numerous, yet they continued to disobey and reject God's message. The use of 'sister' to refer to the signs suggests a sense of familiarity and closeness, implying that the people had no excuse to ignore the signs. The phrase 'We seized them with punishment' underscores God's power and authority, and the phrase 'that they might turn back' indicates that the purpose of the punishment was to guide the people towards repentance and righteousness.
orig: وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها وأخذناهم بالعذاب لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And they said: O magician, call upon your Lord for us according to what has been agreed upon with you. Indeed, we are obedient.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the encounter between Moses and the magicians who were asked to confront him. The magicians, in their arrogance, asked Moses to call upon his Lord, implying that they did not believe in his God or his ability to perform miracles. The verse highlights the irony of the situation, where the magicians, who were known for their supposed mastery of magic, were now asking Moses, a prophet of God, to perform a miracle. The verse also emphasizes the obedience of the believers, who were willing to follow God's commandments and trust in His plan, in contrast to the disbelief and arrogance of the magicians.
orig: وقالوا يا أيه الساحر ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك إننا لمهتدون

translation: And when We revealed to them the punishment, behold, they began to flee.
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who were warned of God's punishment. Instead of repenting and changing their ways, they tried to flee from the punishment, indicating their lack of faith and unwillingness to confront their own wrongdoing. The verse highlights the futility of trying to escape God's punishment and the importance of facing one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم العذاب إذا هم ينكثون

translation: And Pharaoh said: 'O my people! Does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Can you not see?
interpretation: Pharaoh is boasting about his power and control over Egypt, claiming that the kingdom and its resources are his. He is also mocking the idea that Moses and the Israelites have a chance against him. The verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and pride, which will ultimately lead to his downfall.
orig: ونادى فرعون في قومه قال يا قوم أليس لي ملك مصر وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [which were] similar in [style of] construction to your town.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminding him that God has destroyed similar towns to Mecca before. The verse is emphasizing that the destruction of these towns was a result of their disobedience and disbelief in God's message. The verse serves as a warning to the people of Mecca, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and encouraging them to believe in God's message and follow His commandments.
orig: أم أنا خير من هذا الذي هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فلولا ألقي عليه أسورة من ذهب أو جاء معه الملائكة مقترنين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, but they did not perceive.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the current generation is not the first to be destroyed by God's punishment. The use of 'indeed' emphasizes the certainty and repetition of this phenomenon throughout history. The phrase 'but they did not perceive' suggests that the people of the past generations were also warned but failed to heed the warnings, leading to their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder to the current generation to learn from the past and avoid the same fate.
orig: فاستخف قومه فأطاعوه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: So when We decreed their destruction, We gave them no respite.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of a community that was destroyed by God's decree. The verse emphasizes the idea that the community was given no respite or reprieve before their destruction, indicating that their punishment was swift and inevitable. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God's commands, reminding them that God's justice is swift and sure.
orig: فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And We made them a precedent and an example to the later generations.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the destruction of the unjust towns and nations serves as a lesson and a warning to future generations. The phrase 'a precedent' suggests that their fate will be a lesson for others, and 'an example' implies that their story will be told and retold as a cautionary tale. The verse encourages people to learn from the mistakes of the past and to live righteously, lest they suffer a similar fate.
orig: فجعلناهم سلفا ومثلا للآخرين

translation: And remember when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the world.'
interpretation: The verse recounts the moment when the angels Gabriel and Michael appeared to the Virgin Mary and gave her the news that she had been chosen by God to bear His son, Jesus. The verse highlights Mary's purity and her exalted status among all women. The verse also underscores the idea that God's choice of Mary was not based on her own merits or actions, but on His grace and mercy. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power to choose and elevate whom He wills, and the importance of humility and submission to God's will.
orig: ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدون

translation: And they say, 'Our gods have been kind to us. If this be a lie, bring then a sign, but they were warned of Our punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and ask for a miraculous sign as proof of his prophethood. They are skeptical of the idea that their gods could be unjust and oppressive, despite the fact that they have been warned of God's punishment. The verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the disbelievers, who refuse to believe in the truth and instead demand a miracle, which they think would be a proof of the Prophet's authenticity. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an itself is a miracle and a sign of God's mercy, and that those who reject it will face severe punishment.
orig: وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون

translation: Indeed, he was a servant of Ours, a man of Our servant, to whom We granted insight and whom We made an example for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse describes the status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a servant of God and a leader for the Children of Israel. The verse emphasizes the special relationship between God and the Prophet, highlighting the fact that the Prophet was chosen by God and granted insight and wisdom. The verse also underscores the significance of the Prophet's role as an example for the Children of Israel, indicating that his character and conduct were meant to serve as a model for them to follow. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's status as a divine messenger and leader, and the importance of following his teachings and example.
orig: إن هو إلا عبد أنعمنا عليه وجعلناه مثلا لبني إسرائيل

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with humanity. Despite humanity's disobedience and sin, God does not immediately punish them. Instead, He gives them respite in this life, allowing them to repent and change their ways. However, the verse also warns that the punishment in the Hereafter will be far more severe for those who do not take advantage of God's mercy and continue to live in sin. The verse encourages the reader to reflect on their actions and turn to God before it's too late.
orig: ولو نشاء لجعلنا منكم ملائكة في الأرض يخلفون

translation: And indeed, We have knowledge of the hour, but they do not know it. And follow this path [which] is straight.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of the hour of judgment, which is unknown to humanity. The verse also encourages believers to follow the straight path, which is the path that leads to righteousness and salvation. The verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and all-aware, and that believers should strive to live according to His will and commandments.
orig: وإنه لعلم للساعة فلا تمترن بها واتبعون هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided, 'Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. I am a clear enemy to you.'
interpretation: In this verse, Satan is addressing the disbelievers and reminding them of God's promise to punish them for their sins. Satan is portrayed as a clear enemy, indicating that he has no power over the believers and that his only role is to mislead and deceive. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the reality of their situation. It also highlights the idea that Satan's enmity towards humanity is a result of his jealousy and spite towards God's creation.
orig: ولا يصدنكم الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And when Jesus came with clear signs, he said, 'I have come to you with wisdom and to clarify for you some of the things about which you differ. So fear God and obey me.'
interpretation: In this verse, Jesus is seen as a wise prophet who has been sent by God to guide people and clarify any misunderstandings they may have had. The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing God and following the teachings of Jesus, indicating that obedience to God and His prophets is key to living a righteous life. The verse also highlights the significance of wisdom and knowledge in understanding and following God's commands.
orig: ولما جاء عيسى بالبينات قال قد جئتكم بالحكمة ولأبين لكم بعض الذي تختلفون فيه فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity of God and the fact that He is the Lord of all creation, including the speaker and the audience. The use of the word 'indeed' suggests a statement of certainty and emphasis. The verse also serves as a reminder that worship is due only to Allah, and that following any other path than the 'straight path' leads to misguidance and destruction. The verse encourages the audience to focus their worship solely on Allah and to avoid the temptation of following other deities or false idols.
orig: إن الله هو ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين ظلموا من عذاب يوم أليم

translation: Do they await anything except the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly, while they do not perceive it?
interpretation: The verse questions the disbelievers' expectation of the Hour (the Day of Judgment) and suggests that they are unaware of its approaching and are unprepared for it. The verse implies that the disbelievers are heedless and neglectful of the warning signs and are too engrossed in their worldly lives to notice the approaching judgment. The verse serves as a reminder that the Hour will come suddenly and unexpectedly, catching the disbelievers off guard and emphasizing the importance of being prepared for the Hereafter.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the universal nature of the Prophet's message, indicating that his teachings are not limited to a specific group or community, but rather are intended for the benefit of all people. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is relevant to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or nationality. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's important role in guiding humanity towards a righteous and just life, and encourages believers to emulate his example in spreading love, compassion, and mercy to all people.
orig: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين

translation: O servants of Mine, there is no fear upon you today, nor will you be sad.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers as 'My servants', emphasizing their close relationship with God. The verse reassures them that they have nothing to fear on the Day of Judgment, and that they will not feel sad or regretful for their actions in this life. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for believers, reminding them of God's protection and mercy.
orig: يا عباد لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون

translation: And those who believed in Our signs and surrendered (to Allah).
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of belief and submission to God's will, emphasizing the connection between faith and obedience. It suggests that true belief is not just a matter of intellectual assent but a commitment to live according to God's commands. The use of the word 'surrendered' (muslimun) is significant, as it implies a total submission to God's will, indicating that the believers have accepted God's guidance and are committed to following it in their lives.
orig: الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your wives, in happiness and delight.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of Paradise for the believers, where they will enter with their spouses and enjoy eternal happiness and delight. The use of the word 'happiness' (تحبرون) emphasizes the state of joy and contentment that the believers will experience in Paradise, while the word 'delight' (وأزواجكم) highlights the intimate nature of the relationship between the believers and their spouses in Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of the believers and the reward that awaits them if they lead a righteous life.
orig: ادخلوا الجنة أنتم وأزواجكم تحبرون

translation: And We have destroyed them, and theirs has been the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of communities that were unjust and received their punishment in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the idea that the punishment was not only physical but also spiritual, affecting their souls and their lives in the hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment in the afterlife.
orig: يطاف عليهم بصحاف من ذهب وأكواب وفيها ما تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ الأعين وأنتم فيها خالدون

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims over their enemies, particularly in the Battle of Mecca. The phrase 'a clear victory' signifies that the triumph was decisive and indisputable, while 'a manifest triumph' emphasizes that the victory was evident and obvious to all. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers and a warning to those who oppose the Prophet and the Muslims.
orig: وتلك الجنة التي أورثتموها بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a town while they were unjust, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of multiple towns that were unjust, emphasizing the repetition of God's punishment. The use of 'indeed' at the beginning of the verse underscores the certainty and finality of the punishment. The verse also emphasizes the suddenness of the punishment, which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: لكم فيها فاكهة كثيرة منها تأكلون

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be in the punishment of Hell, eternally.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that those who commit crimes and injustices will face eternal punishment in Hell. The use of 'khālidōn' (eternally) emphasizes the duration of the punishment, indicating that it will never end. This verse serves as a warning to those who engage in criminal behavior, reminding them of the severe consequences they will face in the afterlife.
orig: إن المجرمين في عذاب جهنم خالدون

translation: And they will not be reprieved
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the punishment will not be averted or delayed, and that the people will not be able to escape or postpone it. The use of the word 'mablasoon' (مبلسون) in the verse suggests that the people are in a state of heedlessness and ignorance, and that they are not taking the warning signs seriously. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is certain and inevitable, and that those who reject the truth and continue to live in sin will face the consequences.
orig: لا يفتر عنهم وهم فيه مبلسون

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they were the ones who wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the people in question were responsible for their own downfall, rather than blaming their misfortunes on God. The phrase 'they were the ones who wronged themselves' suggests that their suffering was a direct result of their own actions, and that God's punishment was a natural consequence of their wrongdoing. The verse serves to refute the idea that God's punishment was unjust or unfair, and instead, it highlights the idea that individuals have agency in their own lives and must take responsibility for their actions.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا هم الظالمين

translation: And they say, 'O Malik, let your Lord hasten the punishment for us.' He said, 'Indeed, it will befall you soon, Allah willing.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's request to Malik (Angel of Death) to hasten the punishment for them. The people are impatient and want the punishment to come quickly. Malik responds by saying that the punishment will come soon, if God wills. The verse highlights the impatience of the people and their eagerness to face the consequences of their actions. It also emphasizes the idea that the punishment is not in the hands of Malik, but in the hands of God, who is the ultimate authority and decides when and how the punishment will come.
orig: ونادوا يا مالك ليقض علينا ربك قال إنكم ماكثون

translation: Indeed, We have brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that the truth has been made clear and delivered to the people, but the majority of them are resistant to it. The word 'kārhan' (كارهون) in the last part of the verse implies a sense of dislike, aversion, or even disdain towards the truth. The verse suggests that the people have become so accustomed to their false beliefs and misguided ways that they are unwilling to accept the truth, even when it is presented to them. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that the truth is not always welcomed or accepted, and that it is the responsibility of believers to continue to spread the message of Islam, even in the face of resistance and rejection.
orig: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم أبرموا أمرا فإنا مبرمون

translation: And they think that We do not hear their secrets and their whisperings, but We do indeed hear them, and Our messengers are with them, recording.
interpretation: The verse highlights the foolish notion of those who believe that their secret conversations and whisperings are hidden from God. The verse emphasizes that God is all-hearing and all-knowing, and that nothing escapes His knowledge. The verse also emphasizes the presence of God's messengers, who are always watching and recording the actions and words of humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and the accountability of human beings for their actions and words.
orig: أم يحسبون أنا لا نسمع سرهم ونجواهم بلى ورسلنا لديهم يكتبون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the Merciful has taken a son.' Indeed, I am the foremost of those who prostrate.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the belief held by some polytheists in Arabia that the Merciful (a reference to Allah) had taken a son. The verse refutes this belief by having the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) say that the Merciful has not taken a son. Instead, the Prophet declares that he (Muhammad) is the foremost of those who prostrate (i.e., the first to worship Allah), indicating that he is the leader of those who worship Allah and reject such false beliefs.
orig: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: The verse is a declaration of God's greatness and sovereignty. The phrase 'Lord of the heavens and the earth' emphasizes God's power and dominion over all creation. The phrase 'Lord of the Throne' signifies God's kingship and authority over all that exists. The final phrase, 'above what they describe', suggests that God's majesty and glory are beyond human comprehension and description. The verse encourages believers to acknowledge and praise God's transcendent greatness and to recognize the limitations of human understanding.
orig: سبحان رب السماوات والأرض رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: And they diverge in it (the Qur'an) and play with it, so play with it they will, until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who reject the message of the Qur'an and instead choose to play with its words and mock its teachings. They will continue to do so until they meet their promised Day of Judgment, when they will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and instead choose to indulge in frivolous pursuits.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: And He is the God in the heavens and the God on the earth, and He is the Wise, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's oneness and His presence in all of existence, both in the heavens and on earth. The verse also highlights God's wisdom and knowledge, indicating that He is not only the creator of the universe, but also the one who governs it according to His wise and just plan. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and our responsibility to acknowledge and submit to His will.
orig: وهو الذي في السماء إله وفي الأرض إله وهو الحكيم العليم

translation: And blessed is He who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse describes God's greatness and emphasizes His sovereignty over the heavens, earth, and everything in between. The phrase 'with Him is the knowledge of the Hour' refers to God's knowledge of the future and His power to control the passage of time. The verse ends with a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the fact that all will be returned to God, indicating that everyone will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وتبارك الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وعنده علم الساعة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And those who call for help from other than Allah are not able to aid them; they are only (servants) of destruction, and they are not aware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking help from other than Allah. Those who call upon others besides Allah, such as idols or other deities, are not able to provide any real assistance. In fact, they are only servants of destruction and lead people further away from the truth and towards destruction. The verse emphasizes that those who seek help from other than Allah are unaware of the reality of their situation and the consequences of their actions.
orig: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون

translation: And indeed, if I were to ask you for a ransom, in exchange for their release, I would ask for it from God, and they would surely be refused.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been commanded by God to demand a ransom from the captives taken in battle. The ransom is asked from God, indicating that it is not the Prophet's own desire but a command from God. The verse also implies that the captives are not worthy of being ransomed and will be refused, signifying their guilt and the justice of their punishment.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, indeed this people of ours has denied us, they do not believe in us.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were rejected and denied the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They accused the Prophet and his followers of lying and not believing in them. The verse highlights the disbelievers' arrogance and unwillingness to accept the truth, instead choosing to reject the message and accuse the Prophet of lying. This verse serves as a reminder that the disbelievers' denial and rejection of the truth will not stop the message of Islam from spreading and being victorious.
orig: وقيله يا رب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: So turn away from them and say, 'Peace!' For they will come to know.
interpretation: The verse tells the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who reject his message and to say 'peace' to them, indicating that he has fulfilled his duty of conveying the message and that he is not responsible for their rejection. The verse also indicates that the rejecters will eventually come to know the truth and reality of the message, suggesting that the Prophet's patience and peaceful response to their rejection is a sign of his faith and trust in God's plan.
orig: فاصفح عنهم وقل سلام فسوف يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were more powerful than your town, and they were more numerous in population and wealth, and We made them an example for you, and an illustration, so do not be deceived by their ornaments and luxuries. Indeed, We are the One Who destroys and punishes.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and authority, highlighting the fact that even the most powerful towns and civilizations are subject to His will and can be destroyed at any moment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are prideful and arrogant, reminding them that material wealth and power are fleeting and that God is the ultimate authority. The use of the phrase "and indeed" at the beginning of the verse adds emphasis to the message, indicating that what follows is a statement of great importance. The verse also emphasizes the idea of the "ornaments and luxuries" of the destroyed towns, implying that material possessions and worldly wealth are not a guarantee of protection from God's punishment.
orig: حم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down in a blessed night. Indeed, We have been warning [them].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the revelation of the Qur'an, which was sent down on a blessed night, believed to be the night of Laylat al-Qadr. The verse emphasizes the significance of the revelation and the importance of the message it carries. The phrase 'Indeed, We have been warning [them]' suggests that the revelation is a reminder and a warning to those who have been neglectful of God's commands and have turned away from His path. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of listening to God's message and adhering to His commands.
orig: إنا أنزلناه في ليلة مباركة إنا كنا منذرين

translation: And in it are signs, clear and distinct, of the Hour, and the moon, and the sun, and the stars, and the day and the night, and the sun and the moon; they do not make haste in the least
interpretation: The verse highlights the significance of the natural signs in the heavens and the earth that indicate the approaching Day of Judgment. The verse specifically mentions the moon, sun, stars, day, and night, emphasizing their role in serving as indicators of the passage of time and the impending arrival of the Hour. The verse underscores the idea that these celestial bodies, despite their seeming haste, do not actually hasten the coming of the Day of Judgment, for it is God who determines the timing of that Day.
orig: فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger from among yourselves, he is grieved by your suffering, anxious for your guidance, and merciful and compassionate to the believers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the proximity and relatability of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to his people. The use of 'min khalfikum' (from among yourselves) highlights that he is one of them, sharing their same human experiences and struggles. The verse also highlights the Prophet's emotional investment in his people's guidance, describing him as 'marasil' (grieved) by their suffering and 'murrah' (anxious) for their guidance. The description of the Prophet as 'rahham' (merciful) and 'sadiqun' (truthful) underscores his compassion and integrity, qualities that made him an effective guide for his people. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the Prophet's role as a source of comfort, guidance, and inspiration.
orig: أمرا من عندنا إنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And indeed, your Lord is Merciful. Indeed, He is Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's attribute of mercy and knowledge. The use of the word 'indeed' twice emphasizes the certainty and truth of this statement. The verse highlights the idea that God's mercy and knowledge are interconnected, and that His knowledge allows Him to understand and respond to the needs of His creation with mercy and compassion. This verse serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, reminding them of God's merciful nature and His ability to understand and care for them.
orig: رحمة من ربك إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, indeed, if you are sure.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, which includes all that exists in the universe. The phrase 'if you are sure' suggests that the believers' faith in God's lordship should be unwavering and absolute, without any doubt or hesitation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and dominion over all things, and it encourages the believers to have complete trust and confidence in God's power and authority.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: There is no god but He, the Living, the Everlasting. Slumber seizes Him not, nor does sleep overtake Him.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and rejects the idea of polytheism. It also highlights God's eternal nature, indicating that He is beyond human limitations and weaknesses, such as sleep and slumber. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the uniqueness and majesty of God, and encourages them to have faith and trust in His power and wisdom.
orig: لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [which were] similar in [quality] to your town [Makkah].
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his people in Makkah, reminding them that God has destroyed other towns similar to theirs because of their sins and injustice. The verse serves as a warning to the people of Makkah, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment if they continue to disobey and reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is not limited to a specific town or nation, but it can reach anyone who disobeys and disregards His commands.
orig: بل هم في شك يلعبون

translation: On the day when the sky will be like a molten brass, and the mountains will be like moving wool.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where the sky will be filled with thick clouds, and the mountains will be shaken and moved, as if they were soft wool. The image of the molten brass sky suggests a fiery, intense heat, while the moving mountains symbolize the turmoil and upheaval that will occur on that day. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Reckoning, when all humanity will be judged and the earth will be transformed.
orig: فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين

translation: The punishment will befall the people in the morning or at noon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty and suddenness of God's punishment, which will come unexpectedly, either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people will have no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يغشى الناس هذا عذاب أليم

translation: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and help us against the people of disbelief.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God to grant patience and steadfastness to the believers and to assist them in their struggle against the disbelievers. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity and the need for divine assistance in overcoming the challenges that come with living a life of faith. The phrase 'people of disbelief' refers to those who reject the message of Islam and oppose the believers, and the verse implies that they are a formidable force that requires God's help to overcome.
orig: ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب إنا مؤمنون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أنى لهم الذكرى وقد جاءهم رسول مبين

translation: And they turned away from him and said, 'Taught! Mad!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message. They rejected his teachings and accused him of being a madman or a possessed person. The verse highlights the opposition and ridicule that the Prophet faced in his early days of prophethood, and how the disbelievers dismissed his message without giving it any serious thought or consideration. It serves as a reminder of the challenges that the Prophet faced and the importance of standing firm in the face of opposition and ridicule.
orig: ثم تولوا عنه وقالوا معلم مجنون

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, on the day when the Trumpet will be blown and you will come in crowds;
interpretation: The verse warns the listeners of a near punishment, indicating that it is close at hand and will soon befall those who are being addressed. The mention of the Trumpet being blown suggests a divine intervention and a warning of a catastrophic event. The image of people coming in crowds suggests a scene of chaos and confusion, as people are gathered together to face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the need to be prepared for the ultimate reckoning.
orig: إنا كاشفو العذاب قليلا إنكم عائدون

translation: On the Day when the great calamity will overcome, We shall say to the wrongdoers, 'Taste the punishment of eternal suffering!',
interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment when the wicked will be punished. The phrase 'great calamity' refers to the Day of Judgment itself, which will be a day of great distress and destruction. The verse addresses the wrongdoers, warning them that they will taste the punishment of eternal suffering, indicating that the punishment will be severe and never-ending. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى إنا منتقمون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a people before them, and We will indeed destroy many a people after them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of many nations before the time of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and warns that many more will be destroyed in the future. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and judgment, emphasizing that no nation is immune to His punishment. It also highlights the importance of following God's commandments and living a righteous life, lest one faces the same fate as those who were destroyed before.
orig: ولقد فتنا قبلهم قوم فرعون وجاءهم رسول كريم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أن أدوا إلي عباد الله إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: And do not incline towards those who are unjust, lest the Fire should touch you, and you will not be requited except what you used to do.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against inclining towards those who are unjust and committing injustice, as it will lead them to the Fire (Hell) and they will be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the consequences of associating with the wicked and encourages believers to dissociate themselves from such people and their actions, lest they suffer the same fate. The verse also serves as a reminder that everyone will be held accountable for their actions and that no one will be excused or treated unjustly.
orig: وأن لا تعلوا على الله إني آتيكم بسلطان مبين

translation: And indeed, I have prohibited My servants from oppression, and I have not been neglectful of My remembrance.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's prohibition of oppression and injustice among His servants. The use of the first person pronoun 'I' emphasizes God's direct relationship with His creation and His responsibility in guiding and protecting them. The second part of the verse highlights God's remembrance and vigilance in monitoring the actions of His servants, indicating that He is always aware of their deeds and will hold them accountable for their actions. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to act justly and avoid oppression, as they will be held accountable by God.
orig: وإني عذت بربي وربكم أن ترجمون

translation: And indeed, if you do not believe in Me, then you will not worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of belief in God and the consequence of not believing in Him. The verse suggests that lack of belief in God leads to a lack of worship, which is a fundamental aspect of a believer's relationship with God. The verse serves as a reminder that belief and worship are interconnected and that belief is a necessary prerequisite for true worship.
orig: وإن لم تؤمنوا لي فاعتزلون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فدعا ربه أن هؤلاء قوم مجرمون

translation: And We have destroyed the companions of the town, so their dwellings remain empty after them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of a town whose inhabitants were wicked and corrupt. The use of the phrase 'companions of the town' implies that the people of the town were united in their evil ways and had abandoned God's teachings. The phrase 'their dwellings remain empty after them' emphasizes the completeness of their destruction, indicating that nothing was left of their homes or their way of life. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of living a life of sin and disobedience to God's commands.
orig: فأسر بعبادي ليلا إنكم متبعون

translation: And He has subjected to you, in the heaven and on earth, all that is in them, behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and dominion over all things in the heavens and the earth, and how everything in them serves a purpose and is subjugated to His will. The verse encourages people to reflect on the signs of God's creation and to recognize His greatness and wisdom in the intricate balance and interconnectedness of all things. It invites people to ponder and appreciate the beauty and complexity of the natural world and to recognize that everything in it serves a purpose and is subjugated to God's will.
orig: واترك البحر رهوا إنهم جند مغرقون

translation: And how many a garden have they left untended,
interpretation: The verse laments the abandonment of once-flourishing gardens, which have been left untended by their owners. The verse suggests that the owners have neglected their responsibility to care for the gardens, which were once a source of beauty and sustenance. The verse may also be seen as a metaphor for the spiritual neglect of one's inner self, which, like a garden, requires cultivation and care to flourish.
orig: كم تركوا من جنات وعيون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy for all people. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but rather it is universal and applicable to all people until the end of time. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message, which aims to guide people towards righteousness and salvation. The verse also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role as a mercy to humanity, and serves as a reminder to believers to emulate this quality of compassion and mercy in their interactions with others.
orig: وزروع ومقام كريم

translation: And certainly We have given to these people enjoyment, so let them enjoy it; they will soon come to know.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who are enjoying the pleasures of this life, but they will soon come to know the consequences of their actions. The verse indicates that the enjoyment they are experiencing is a temporary and fleeting pleasure, and it will soon be followed by the punishment they deserve. The verse serves as a warning to those who are indulging in sinful pleasures, reminding them that their actions will have consequences and that they will eventually face the repercussions of their deeds.
orig: ونعمة كانوا فيها فاكهين

translation: And We have made the verses clear to them, but they have turned away from them.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Qur'anic verses that have been clarified and elucidated for the people, yet they have chosen to ignore and reject them. The verse highlights the people's deliberate disregard for God's message and their unwillingness to listen, indicating that they have turned away from the truth and chosen to follow their own desires instead.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها قوما آخرين

translation: And We have not sent the sky and the earth and everything between them, except as a warning to the inhabitants of the world.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the purpose of God's creation of the universe and everything in it, including the sky, the earth, and all that lies between them. The verse suggests that the creation of the universe serves as a warning to humanity, reminding them of the power and majesty of God and the consequences of their actions. The verse also implies that the creation of the universe is a sign of God's mercy and grace, as it provides a means for humanity to live and flourish. Ultimately, the verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a virtuous life and being mindful of one's relationship with God.
orig: فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض وما كانوا منظرين

translation: And We have certainly destroyed the like of you; indeed, We have made an example of them, so fear the punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and disbelief of the disbelievers, reminding them that they are not exceptional and that God has destroyed nations before them who were similar in their disobedience. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of the previous nations was not only a punishment but also a lesson and a warning to those who come after them. The verse encourages the disbelievers to reflect on the fate of those who rejected God's messengers and were subsequently destroyed, and to fear the same punishment for themselves if they continue in their disbelief.
orig: ولقد نجينا بني إسرائيل من العذاب المهين

translation: And Pharaoh, he was excessive in the land, he was indeed one of the extravagant.
interpretation: The verse describes Pharaoh's tyrannical rule and his excessive pride, which led him to commit heinous crimes and oppress his people. The phrase 'one of the extravagant' suggests that Pharaoh's arrogance and haughtiness knew no bounds, and he saw himself as a god, above the law and accountability. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of absolute power and the corrupting influence it can have on those who wield it.
orig: من فرعون إنه كان عاليا من المسرفين

translation: And indeed, We have given them a clear victory and manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the believers. The use of the word 'clear' emphasizes the clarity and obviousness of the victory, indicating that it was a decisive and undeniable victory. The phrase 'manifest triumph' further emphasizes the idea that the victory was clear and obvious to all. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that God is always with them and will grant them victory over their enemies.
orig: ولقد اخترناهم على علم على العالمين

translation: And We have given them [the unbelievers] clear signs of the miracle, but they have turned away from them, avoiding [them].
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the unbelievers have been given clear and convincing signs of God's existence and power, but they have deliberately turned away from them, choosing to reject and ignore the evidence. The verse suggests that the unbelievers are not ignorant of the signs, but rather they are deliberately avoiding them because they do not want to acknowledge the truth and submit to God's will. The verse serves as a warning to those who are rejecting God's signs and serves as a reminder that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: وآتيناهم من الآيات ما فيه بلاء مبين

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to fabricate something other than the truth. And indeed, they desired to make you a friend of theirs, [Muhammad],
interpretation: The verse suggests that there were people who tried to tempt the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to alter the message revealed to him by God, and to make him a friend of theirs. This verse highlights the human tendency to try to manipulate religious leaders or scripture to suit one's own desires. It serves as a warning to believers to be cautious of those who try to distort the message of Islam and to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: إن هؤلاء ليقولون

translation: Indeed, We have destroyed your former companions. Do you not see them, or have you not been given insight?
interpretation: This verse is a continuation of the previous verse, where God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminding him of the destruction of the communities that were destroyed before. The verse is emphasizing that the destruction of the past communities is a lesson for the believers, and that they should learn from their mistakes and take heed of the warning signs. The phrase 'your former companions' refers to the people of the past who were destroyed, and the phrase 'Do you not see them' is a rhetorical question, suggesting that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) should reflect on the lessons of history. The final phrase 'or have you not been given insight' suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been given a special insight and understanding by God, and that he should use this insight to guide his people.
orig: إن هي إلا موتتنا الأولى وما نحن بمنشرين

translation: And come with your proofs, if you are truthful.
interpretation: The verse is an invitation to the disbelievers to bring forth their evidence and arguments against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an, if they truly believe in their false claims. The verse implies that the disbelievers will not be able to provide any convincing proof against the Prophet and the Qur'an, and thus, their arguments will be refuted and their disbelief will be exposed. The verse serves as a challenge to those who reject the message of Islam, encouraging them to examine their own beliefs and consider the truth of the Qur'an.
orig: فأتوا بآبائنا إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أهم خير أم قوم تبع والذين من قبلهم أهلكناهم إنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: And We have not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them for play.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the purposeful creation of the universe and everything in it, including the heavens, the earth, and all that lies between them. The verse rejects the idea that the creation is a form of play or entertainment for God. Instead, it suggests that the creation has a higher purpose, which is to worship and glorify God. The verse encourages humans to reflect on the signs of God's creation and to recognize the greatness and majesty of their Creator.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما لاعبين

translation: We created them not except for the truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the purpose of human creation is to worship and serve Allah, and that the majority of people are unaware of this purpose and instead live their lives in ignorance of their true nature and purpose.
orig: ما خلقناهما إلا بالحق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: The Day of Judgment will come when all the creatures will be gathered together.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when all creatures, including humans and jinn, will be gathered together to face judgment. The verse emphasizes the idea that everyone will be held accountable for their actions and that no one will be able to escape judgment. It serves as a reminder of the Hereafter and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن يوم الفصل ميقاتهم أجمعين

translation: A day in which no soul will be of any avail to another, and compensation will be given to no soul, neither will intercession be of any avail, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse describes a day of judgment where no one can help another, and no amount of wealth or status can save a person from their fate. The verse emphasizes the idea that on this day, each person will be alone and responsible for their own actions. The verse also highlights the idea that intercession, whether by prophets or saints, will not be of any avail on this day. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the importance of living a righteous life, as no one will be able to rely on their wealth, status, or connections on that day.
orig: يوم لا يغني مولى عن مولى شيئا ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Except those who repent, believe and do good deeds, for them is mercy from their Lord, and they are the ones who will prosper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to the destruction of towns that were unjust. The exception is for those who repent, believe and do good deeds. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, faith, and good deeds as a means of avoiding God's punishment and receiving His mercy. The phrase 'they are the ones who will prosper' indicates that these individuals will not only avoid punishment but also attain success and prosperity in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إلا من رحم الله إنه هو العزيز الرحيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down in a Clear Arabic Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and precision of the Qur'an, which is the word of God as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. The use of the word 'Shajarah' ( Clear) underscores the fact that the Qur'an is a clear and unambiguous guide for those who seek guidance. The verse also highlights the importance of the Arabic language in the transmission of God's message, as the Qur'an is the only book of its kind that has been preserved in its original language without any alteration or corruption. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a call to action.
orig: إن شجرت الزقوم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: طعام الأثيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كالمهل يغلي في البطون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كغلي الحميم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم

translation: Then they were followed by a generation who neglected the warning and were consumed by the enjoyment of their wealth and children.
interpretation: The verse describes the consequences of neglecting the warning of God's punishment. The people became engrossed in their material wealth and children, forgetting the lessons of the past and ignoring the warning signs of impending doom. The verse serves as a reminder to prioritize one's spiritual well-being over worldly possessions and to not let material success distract from the remembrance of God.
orig: ثم صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم

translation: And indeed, you are of great moral character.
interpretation: The verse highlights the exceptional character of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing his high moral standards and integrity. The phrase 'al-lazīz' means 'the one who is honored' or 'the generous one', indicating the Prophet's generosity and kindness towards others. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to strive for similar moral excellence and to follow the Prophet's example in their own lives.
orig: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, indicating its authority and authenticity. The use of the phrase "Lord of the worlds" highlights God's sovereignty over all creation, underscoring the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book, but a message from the Creator of the universe. The verse serves as a reminder of the Qur'an's sacred nature and its role as a guide for humanity.
orig: إن هذا ما كنتم به تمترون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the righteous in the afterlife, where they will be in a secure and peaceful place, free from all suffering and hardship. The word 'amn' (security) emphasizes the idea of safety and protection, indicating that the righteous will be shielded from all harm and will enjoy eternal bliss. The verse serves as a source of comfort and hope for believers, reminding them that their good deeds will ultimately lead them to a state of eternal happiness.
orig: إن المتقين في مقام أمين

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation.
