The phrase 'Taste the punishment and warning' suggests that they will face the consequences of their disbelief and be warned of God's punishment.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا للذين كرهوا ما نزل الله سنطيعكم في بعض الأمر والله يعلم إسرارهم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكيف إذا توفتهم الملائكة يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم

translation: And they followed what the devils had recited against the angels of God in the reign of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and teaching them what was revealed to the angels of God. And they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they cannot harm anyone except by God's permission, and they learned what harms them and does not profit them, and they knew that whoever bought it would have no share in the Hereafter, and evil was the price for which they sold their souls had they but known.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people who followed the devils and their teachings, which went against the teachings of God. The devils taught people magic and what was revealed to the angels of God, but they did not benefit from it. Instead, they caused harm to themselves and others, and they were aware that their actions would not bring them any benefit in the Hereafter. The verse warns against following false teachings and reminds people to stay on the path of righteousness.
orig: ذلك بأنهم اتبعوا ما أسخط الله وكرهوا رضوانه فأحبط أعمالهم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أم حسب الذين في قلوبهم مرض أن لن يخرج الله أضغانهم

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience with His creation. Despite the people's disobedience and sin, God does not immediately punish them in this life. Instead, He gives them respite and allows them to live their lives, giving them time to repent and turn back to Him. The verse contrasts the relatively minor punishments of this life with the severe punishment that awaits those who reject God in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder of God's justice and the consequences of rejecting His guidance.
orig: ولو نشاء لأريناكهم فلعرفتهم بسيماهم ولتعرفنهم في لحن القول والله يعلم أعمالكم

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth, and loss of lives. The purpose of these tests is to distinguish the true believers from those who are not sincere in their faith. The verse also assures the believers that they will receive good tidings if they remain patient and steadfast during these tests, indicating that the ultimate reward for their patience will be Paradise.
orig: ولنبلونكم حتى نعلم المجاهدين منكم والصابرين ونبلو أخباركم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after the guidance has become clear to them, they will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will nullify their deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of opposition to God's will and the consequences of rejecting the guidance of the Prophet. Those who reject faith and actively work against the way of God, despite having knowledge of the truth, will not be able to harm God in any way. Instead, their actions will be in vain, and their deeds will be rendered useless. This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and a reminder that their actions will not go unpunished.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله وشاقوا الرسول من بعد ما تبين لهم الهدى لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse warns believers against nullifying their good deeds by disobeying God and His Messenger. It serves as a reminder that true faith is demonstrated through obedience and submission to God's commandments, and that disobedience can lead to the loss of blessings and rewards in the Hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول ولا تبطلوا أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, those who have disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of Allah - they will not be forgiven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who reject faith and actively work against the will of God, leading others astray, will not be forgiven. The verse underlines the gravity of their actions and the severe consequences they face in the afterlife. It serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief and encourages them to reflect on their actions and seek guidance from God.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله ثم ماتوا وهم كفار فلن يغفر الله لهم

translation: And do not incline toward those who are unjust, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you are not among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse warns believers not to incline towards those who are unjust and wicked, lest they be touched by the Fire of Hell. The verse emphasizes the importance of staying away from evil and injustice, and not to be among those who will be punished on Judgment Day. The verse also serves as a reminder that God is always watching and aware of the actions of humanity, and that He will not neglect the deeds of the wicked.
orig: فلا تهنوا وتدعوا إلى السلم وأنتم الأعلون والله معكم ولن يتركم أعمالكم

translation: Indeed, the worldly life is but a game, and a diversion. And if you disbelieve, indeed, We will reward those who do not believe, their recompense will be nothing but Hell, and there will be no helper for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly life and its attractions, which are ultimately meaningless in the grand scheme of things. The verse warns those who disbelieve in God and His message, that their disbelief will not go unpunished. They will be rewarded with nothing but Hell, and they will have no one to help them on the Day of Judgment.
orig: إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا يؤتكم أجوركم ولا يسألكم أموالكم

translation: Indeed, they are confused in their intoxication, so they are stumbling about in their religion.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who are misguided and confused in their beliefs and actions. The word 'intoxication' here refers not only to physical drunkenness but also to the state of being spiritually and morally disoriented. The phrase 'stumbling about in their religion' suggests that they are lost and uncertain in their beliefs and practices, and are unable to find the right path. The verse serves as a warning to those who are neglecting their spiritual well-being and are at risk of falling into a state of confusion and disorientation.
orig: إن يسألكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا ويخرج أضغانكم

translation: Here you are, being called to spend in the cause of Allah, and among you are those who are stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy to himself. Indeed, Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor. And if you turn away, He will replace you with a people other than yourselves, and they will not be like you.
interpretation: The verse addresses the reluctance of some individuals to spend in the cause of Allah, highlighting their stinginess and unwillingness to part with their wealth. The verse emphasizes that such behavior is not only unbecoming but also harmful, as it deprives them of the opportunity to earn Allah's blessings and favors. The verse also warns that if they continue to be stingy, Allah will replace them with a people who are more willing to spend in His cause and who will not be as miserly. The verse serves as a reminder that true prosperity and success come from being generous and willing to sacrifice for the sake of Allah, and that stinginess only leads to loss and regret.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء تدعون لتنفقوا في سبيل الله فمنكم من يبخل ومن يبخل فإنما يبخل عن نفسه والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم

translation: Indeed, We have opened up for you a clear victory.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. The victory is described as 'clear' and 'manifest', indicating that it was a decisive and unambiguous triumph. The verse can also be interpreted as a reference to the victory of Islam over other religions and ideologies, as well as the victory of good over evil. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers and a warning to those who oppose the truth.
orig: إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا

translation: And indeed, God will forgive your mistake, and what is to come will be better for you, and God will give you a great reward.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's forgiveness and His promise of a better future for those who turn to Him in repentance. The verse emphasizes that God's forgiveness is not limited to the past, but also extends to future mistakes, and that God will guide those who seek forgiveness on a straight path. The verse serves as a source of hope and encouragement for those who seek to mend their ways and live a righteous life.
orig: ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid you with a mighty victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of God's assistance and victory for the believers. The phrase 'nusrah' means a mighty or great victory, indicating that God's help is not limited to a specific aspect of life but rather it encompasses all aspects. The verse is a source of encouragement and hope for believers, reminding them that God is always on their side and will aid them in times of need.
orig: وينصرك الله نصرا عزيزا

translation: It is He who has sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, that they may grow in faith, along with their faith. And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the role of God in instilling peace and tranquility in the hearts of believers, which in turn allows them to increase their faith. The verse also highlights the power and knowledge of God, who has control over the armies of the heavens and the earth. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that their faith should be rooted in the knowledge that God is all-knowing and all-wise, and that He is the source of peace and guidance in their lives.
orig: هو الذي أنزل السكينة في قلوب المؤمنين ليزدادوا إيمانا مع إيمانهم ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And the believing men and believing women will enter Gardens under which rivers flow, abiding eternally therein, and that is a great attainment.
interpretation: The verse describes the reward for the believing men and women, who will enter Paradise, a place of eternal bliss, where they will live in gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. The verse emphasizes the greatness of this reward and the joy and happiness that comes with it. The use of the word "khaledi" (eternal) emphasizes that this reward is not temporary, but will last forever. The verse also highlights the contrast between the state of the believers in this life, where they may face hardships and persecution, and their ultimate destination in the Hereafter, where they will live in peace and happiness. The verse serves as a source of comfort and motivation for believers, reminding them of the ultimate goal of their faith and the rewards that await them.
orig: ليدخل المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ويكفر عنهم سيئاتهم وكان ذلك عند الله فوزا عظيما

translation: And He punishes the hypocrites, both men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, who imagine an evil thought about Allah. They shall have a turn of evil fortune. Allah is angry with them, cursing them, and theirs is a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the punishment that awaits the hypocrites and polytheists who harbor evil thoughts about Allah. The verse emphasizes that both men and women who fall into these categories will be punished. The phrase 'imagine an evil thought about Allah' suggests that they have misconceptions about God's nature and attributes, and this misconception leads them to commit acts of disobedience. The punishment described is twofold: a turn of evil fortune in this life, and a lasting punishment in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ويعذب المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات الظانين بالله ظن السوء عليهم دائرة السوء وغضب الله عليهم ولعنهم وأعد لهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: For Allah has soldiers in the heavens and on earth, and Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over the universe, stating that He has soldiers in both the heavens and the earth. The phrase 'soldiers' can be interpreted metaphorically, indicating that everything in the universe obeys God's will and serves His purpose. The verse also highlights God's wisdom and might, suggesting that His power and knowledge are beyond human comprehension. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to trust in God's authority and to recognize His sovereignty over all things.
orig: ولله جنود السماوات والأرض وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner. As a witness, he testified to the truth of God's oneness and the reality of the hereafter. As a bringer of good news, he brought glad tidings of God's mercy and forgiveness to those who repent and believe. As a warner, he warned those who reject God's message of the severe consequences they will face in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and glorify him with praise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of belief in Allah and His Messenger, and the responsibility of believers to honor and respect the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse also encourages Muslims to glorify Allah with praise, indicating that the act of praising Allah is a way of expressing one's belief and gratitude towards Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the significance of faith and the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in guiding humanity towards the right path.
orig: لتؤمنوا بالله ورسوله وتعزروه وتوقروه وتسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], they are pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is above their hands. So, whosoever breaks his covenant, he will be held accountable for his breach of covenant with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of breaking a covenant or promise made to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It underscores that when individuals pledge allegiance to the Prophet, they are, in reality, pledging allegiance to Allah. The verse warns that breaking such a covenant has severe consequences, as it is a betrayal of trust not only against the Prophet but ultimately against Allah, who is the ultimate authority and witness to all covenants. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of keeping promises and upholding integrity, as it is a fundamental aspect of Islamic ethics and values.
orig: إن الذين يبايعونك إنما يبايعون الله يد الله فوق أيديهم فمن نكث فإنما ينكث على نفسه ومن أوفى بما عاهد عليه الله فسيؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And they say, 'O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are crazy!',
interpretation: The verse addresses the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an. They accused him of being crazy or possessed by a jinn, dismissing the message of Islam as nonsense. The verse emphasizes that it is not the Prophet who is crazy, but rather those who reject the message of God are the ones who are misguided. The verse also highlights the irony of the disbelievers' reaction, as they accuse the Prophet of being crazy, while they themselves are the ones who are rejecting the guidance and mercy of God.
orig: سيقول لك المخلفون من الأعراب شغلتنا أموالنا وأهلونا فاستغفر لنا يقولون بألسنتهم ما ليس في قلوبهم قل فمن يملك لكم من الله شيئا إن أراد بكم ضرا أو أراد بكم نفعا بل كان الله بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made to seem appealing to your hearts, and you were averse to it and wished for evil to befall you, and you were wicked people.
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' misconception that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers would never return to their families after their migration to Medina. The verse states that this notion was a mere illusion and that the disbelievers were misguided. The verse also highlights the disbelievers' malicious intentions and their desire for harm to befall the Muslims. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of such evil intentions and the importance of purifying one's heart and actions.
orig: بل ظننتم أن لن ينقلب الرسول والمؤمنون إلى أهليهم أبدا وزين ذلك في قلوبكم وظننتم ظن السوء وكنتم قوما بورا

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger - indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief in God and His Messenger. The verse warns of a fiery punishment awaiting those who reject faith. The verse underlines the certainty and severity of the punishment, using the phrase 'We have prepared' to convey that it is a matter that has already been decided and prepared for by God. The verse serves as a reminder and warning to those who reject faith, encouraging them to reconsider their disbelief and turn towards God.
orig: ومن لم يؤمن بالله ورسوله فإنا أعتدنا للكافرين سعيرا

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and His power to forgive or punish as He sees fit. The verse highlights Allah's mercy and forgiveness, while also acknowledging His justice and authority to punish those who disobey Him. It serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is the ultimate authority and that His forgiveness and mercy are not to be taken for granted.
orig: ولله ملك السماوات والأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, 'If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land.' Have they not been satisfied with what We have given them, [and they are] not commanded except to worship Allah and worship the Messenger? And they say, 'Indeed, the Merciful has begotten a son.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' objection to following the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their false claim that if they were to follow his guidance, they would be taken away from their land. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's message is not new, but rather a confirmation of the previous scriptures, and that the only thing required of them is to worship Allah and obey the Messenger. The verse also refutes the false notion that the Merciful (God) has begotten a son, which is a blasphemous statement that contradicts the Islamic belief in the Oneness of God (Tawhid).
orig: سيقول المخلفون إذا انطلقتم إلى مغانم لتأخذوها ذرونا نتبعكم يريدون أن يبدلوا كلام الله قل لن تتبعونا كذلكم قال الله من قبل فسيقولون بل تحسدوننا بل كانوا لا يفقهون إلا قليلا

translation: Say to those who have been given the Scripture: 'Believe in what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than the truth. Indeed, you were instructed to do good to the people, and Allah will question you about it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the People of the Book, specifically the Jews and Christians, and commands them to believe in the Qur'an, which is the latest revelation from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of following the truth and doing good deeds, as it is a responsibility entrusted to them by God. The verse also warns them that they will be questioned by God about their actions, implying that they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: قل للمخلفين من الأعراب ستدعون إلى قوم أولي بأس شديد تقاتلونهم أو يسلمون فإن تطيعوا يؤتكم الله أجرا حسنا وإن تتولوا كما توليتم من قبل يعذبكم عذابا أليما

translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, but whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obeying God and His Messenger, and the consequences of disobedience. The verse begins by highlighting that those who are physically unable to fight, such as the blind, lame, and sick, are not to be blamed for their condition. However, those who are able-bodied and refuse to obey God and His Messenger will face a painful punishment. The verse then describes the reward for those who obey God and His Messenger, which is admission into gardens beneath which rivers flow, a description of Paradise. The verse serves as a warning to those who choose to disobey God and His Messenger, reminding them of the consequences of their disobedience and the rewards of obedience.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ومن يطع الله ورسوله يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومن يتول يعذبه عذابا أليما

translation: Allah was pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.
interpretation: This verse refers to the occasion when the Muslims swore allegiance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) under a tree, known as the Pledge of Al-Ridwan. God was pleased with their faith and loyalty, and He rewarded them with a sense of tranquility and the promise of a near victory. The verse highlights the special relationship between God and the believers, and how He is aware of their inner thoughts and intentions. It also emphasizes the importance of loyalty and obedience to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a means of attaining God's blessings and guidance.
orig: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة فعلم ما في قلوبهم فأنزل السكينة عليهم وأثابهم فتحا قريبا

translation: And they were arrogant and proud of their wealth, but Allah seized them with punishment for their sins. They had been warned of the punishment, but they did not believe.
interpretation: The verse speaks about people who were proud of their wealth and looked down on others. Despite being warned of the consequences of their arrogance, they refused to believe and continued to live in sin. Their punishment was a result of their own actions and serves as a lesson to those who are living in arrogance and disobedience.
orig: ومغانم كثيرة يأخذونها وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And Allah has given you much wealth, much cattle, and many children, and prevented from you the hands of the people, and made for you a sign from the believers, and guided you to a straight path.
interpretation: The verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon the believers by Allah, including wealth, cattle, and children. The verse also mentions the protection of the believers from the hands of their enemies. Additionally, the verse mentions that the believers have been given a sign, which is a reference to the Qur'an itself, and that Allah has guided them to a straight path, indicating that they are on the right path towards righteousness and salvation.
orig: وعدكم الله مغانم كثيرة تأخذونها فعجل لكم هذه وكف أيدي الناس عنكم ولتكون آية للمؤمنين ويهديكم صراطا مستقيما

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأخرى لم تقدروا عليها قد أحاط الله بها وكان الله على كل شيء قديرا

translation: And if those who disbelieved had fought you, they would have certainly turned their backs (fled). Then (there would have been) no protection (for them), nor would they have been asked (to surrender).
interpretation: The verse describes a situation where the disbelievers, despite their numerical superiority, would have been defeated and fled if they had fought the believers. The verse emphasizes that the disbelievers would not have been given any quarter or protection, and they would not have been asked to surrender. The verse highlights the weakness and cowardice of those who reject faith and the certainty of their defeat in the face of righteousness.
orig: ولو قاتلكم الذين كفروا لولوا الأدبار ثم لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your likenesses, then do you not remember?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him of the destruction of nations that were similar to his own. The verse is a warning to the Prophet and his followers, reminding them of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of heeding the lessons of history. The verse also emphasizes the power and authority of God, who is capable of destroying entire nations for their sins.
orig: سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: And it is He who has restrained their hands from you and their hands from you, and the belly of Makkah, after He had granted you victory over them, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous victory of the Muslims over the Quraish tribe in Mecca. Despite being vastly outnumbered, the Muslims emerged victorious, and the Quraish were unable to harm them. The verse highlights God's intervention in the battle, citing it as evidence of His power and control over all things. The verse also emphasizes the idea that God is aware of all human actions and is witness to everything that occurs.
orig: وهو الذي كف أيديهم عنكم وأيديكم عنهم ببطن مكة من بعد أن أظفركم عليهم وكان الله بما تعملون بصيرا

translation: And indeed, those who have disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque and the offerings, and the sacrificial animals, that they may witness [their] destruction. And if they had been aware of the punishment, they would not have been kept from it, as they will be humiliated therein, and their destruction in the Hereafter will be greater, for they will be denied the pleasures [of life].
interpretation: The verse speaks about the disbelievers who barred the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his companions from the Sacred Mosque and the offerings. The verse indicates that their actions were a result of their disbelief and lack of faith in God. The verse also warns them of the punishment that awaits them in this life and the Hereafter. The verse emphasizes that they will be humiliated and their destruction will be greater in the Hereafter, and they will be denied the pleasures of life. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هم الذين كفروا وصدوكم عن المسجد الحرام والهدي معكوفا أن يبلغ محله ولولا رجال مؤمنون ونساء مؤمنات لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم فتصيبكم منهم معرة بغير علم ليدخل الله في رحمته من يشاء لو تزيلوا لعذبنا الذين كفروا منهم عذابا أليما

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve in their hearts - the pride of the disbelievers will be angered by the revelation of God, and so God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the believers, and imposed on them the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it, and God is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers to the revelation of God. The disbelievers' pride and arrogance will be angered by the revelation, but God will send down His tranquility upon the Messenger and the believers. The verse emphasizes the importance of righteousness and the believers' worthiness of it. The verse also highlights God's knowledge and awareness of all things.
orig: إذ جعل الذين كفروا في قلوبهم الحمية حمية الجاهلية فأنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وألزمهم كلمة التقوى وكانوا أحق بها وأهلها وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: And indeed, the truth has come to the Prophet from Allah. So let the believers rejoice at the good news, those who have believed and increased their faith. Indeed, they will be honored and forgiven, and Allah's reward is great.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the revelation of the truth to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from Allah. The verse commands the believers to rejoice at the good news, which refers to the fact that the truth has been revealed and that they have believed in it. The verse also mentions that the believers' faith has increased, indicating a growth in their faith and devotion to Allah. The verse then assures the believers that they will be honored and forgiven, and that Allah's reward is great. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and its impact on one's life, and serves as a reminder to the believers of the blessings and rewards that come with believing in Allah and His Messenger.
orig: لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق لتدخلن المسجد الحرام إن شاء الله آمنين محلقين رءوسكم ومقصرين لا تخافون فعلم ما لم تعلموا فجعل من دون ذلك فتحا قريبا

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and the universality of Islam. The phrase 'guidance and the religion of truth' refers to the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, which are considered the ultimate guide for humanity. The verse asserts that Islam is the only valid religion and that it supersedes all previous religions. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as Witness' underscores the idea that God's testimony is enough to validate the truth of Islam, and that no other witness or proof is needed. The verse serves as a declaration of the supremacy of Islam and a reminder that God is sufficient as a witness to the truth of His religion.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking blessings and good pleasure from Allah. Their mark is on their faces from the effect of prostration. That is their description in the Torah and their description in the Gospel: like a seed that puts forth its shoot, grows, and becomes strong and thick, and it stands on its stem, delighting the sowers that He may enrage the disbelievers by them.
interpretation: The verse describes the character of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions, who are described as being firm and steadfast against the disbelievers, while also being merciful and compassionate among themselves. The verse highlights their devotion to God, as they bow and prostrate in prayer, seeking blessings and good pleasure from Him. The verse also describes their distinctive mark, which is the effect of their frequent prostration, and compares them to a seed that grows and becomes strong, delighting the sowers. The verse serves as a reminder of the reward and recognition that believers will receive for their faith and good deeds, and as a warning to disbelievers of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: محمد رسول الله والذين معه أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم تراهم ركعا سجدا يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا سيماهم في وجوههم من أثر السجود ذلك مثلهم في التوراة ومثلهم في الإنجيل كزرع أخرج شطأه فآزره فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه يعجب الزراع ليغيظ بهم الكفار وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach the orphan's property except in the way of improving it until he reaches maturity. And fulfill the covenant. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating orphans with kindness and justice. It prohibits believers from approaching orphaned property except in the way of improving it, indicating that the property should not be misused or exploited. Instead, it should be managed in a way that benefits the orphan until they reach maturity. Additionally, the verse highlights the importance of fulfilling covenants and agreements, as they will be questioned about on Judgment Day. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to act with integrity and honesty in all their dealings, especially when it comes to vulnerable members of society like orphans.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله واتقوا الله إن الله سميع عليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud in your speech, lest your deeds become null and void while you perceive not.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the Prophet and his message. It warns believers not to raise their voices above the Prophet's voice, indicating that they should not consider themselves superior to him or their opinions above his. It also warns them against being loud in their speech, indicating that they should not be boastful or arrogant in their faith. The verse reminds them that their deeds will be null and void if they do not adhere to this advice, and they will not even realize it.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي ولا تجهروا له بالقول كجهر بعضكم لبعض أن تحبط أعمالكم وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Indeed, those who are humble in their prayer to their Lord are those who have been tested by their Lord, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of humility in prayer, specifically when addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It emphasizes that those who show humility in their prayer have been tested by God and have proven their devotion to Him. The reward for such humility is forgiveness and a great reward in the Hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of humility in one's relationship with God and serves as a reminder that true devotion is expressed through humility and submission to God's will.
orig: إن الذين يغضون أصواتهم عند رسول الله أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who call you from behind the walls, most of them do not understand.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who criticize and mock the believers from behind the walls, unaware of the true nature of their actions. The verse suggests that they lack understanding and are unable to see beyond their own limited perspective. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the opinions of those who lack wisdom and insight.
orig: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And if they had only been patient until you came to them, it would have been better for them, but Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the impatience of the people who were eager to see the Prophet (peace be upon him) and hear his message. They were told to wait until he came to them, but they were impatient and demanded to see him immediately. The verse suggests that if they had only been patient, it would have been better for them, as they would have been able to hear the message of Islam and possibly accepted it. The verse highlights the importance of patience and the rewards that come with it. It also emphasizes the forgiving and merciful nature of Allah, who is always willing to give people a second chance.
orig: ولو أنهم صبروا حتى تخرج إليهم لكان خيرا لهم والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists have deceived you concerning the doctrine of Tawhid, so come to a clear proof or evidence, so that they may be reminded, or they will say, when a calamity afflicts you, 'Indeed, Allah has caused us to forget you. Indeed, we were not ones who would supplicate to you.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers and warns them against the deception of the polytheists who try to mislead them from the true doctrine of Tawhid (the oneness of God). The believers are encouraged to seek clear evidence and proof to refute the polytheists' claims and to remind them of the truth. The verse also suggests that the polytheists will try to deny their neglect of God and their lack of supplication to Him when a calamity befalls them.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن جاءكم فاسق بنبإ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين

translation: And know that there is a Messenger among you; were he to obey you in much of the matter, you would surely suffer; but Allah has endeared faith to you and adorned it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to you. Such are they who are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Prophethood and the role of the Messenger in guiding the believers. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's obedience to the believers would lead to their destruction, indicating that the Prophet's guidance is not based on his own desires but rather on the revelation from God. The verse also emphasizes the beauty of faith and the hatred of disbelief, defiance, and disobedience, indicating that true guidance is only achieved through faith and obedience to God's commandments.
orig: واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله لو يطيعكم في كثير من الأمر لعنتم ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان أولئك هم الراشدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فضلا من الله ونعمة والله عليم حكيم

translation: And indeed, two factions from among the believers quarreled with each other, so one of them deviated from their companion. But then they (both) regretted it and fought each other until one of them (the deviant one) submitted (to the will of Allah). Indeed, (in the end), they both returned to the command of Allah, and they both sought judgment (from Allah) and were guided (to the truth). Indeed, Allah loves those who seek guidance.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a conflict between two groups of believers, where one group deviated from the righteous path and the other group fought against them to bring them back to the right path. The verse highlights the importance of unity and reconciliation among believers, and how they should strive to seek guidance from Allah and follow His command. The verse also emphasizes Allah's love for those who seek guidance and His mercy towards those who repent and return to the righteous path.
orig: وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما فإن بغت إحداهما على الأخرى فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله فإن فاءت فأصلحوا بينهما بالعدل وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: The believers are but brothers, so reconcile between your brothers and fear Allah that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the unity and brotherhood of believers, stressing the importance of reconciliation and harmony among them. It encourages believers to settle their differences and conflicts in a peaceful and respectful manner, reminding them that fearing Allah and following His commandments is the key to receiving His mercy and guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of brotherhood and unity in the Muslim community, and encourages believers to work towards peace and reconciliation, rather than division and strife.
orig: إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم واتقوا الله لعلكم ترحمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not let your riches or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and being just, even when it is difficult or unpopular. It warns against allowing wealth or children to distract from one's faith and encourages believers to act with justice, even towards those they may not like. The verse reminds believers that justice is closer to righteousness and that it is important to act with fairness and impartiality, regardless of personal feelings or biases.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسى أن يكن خيرا منهن ولا تلمزوا أنفسكم ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الإيمان ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, avoid much [empty] discourse, indeed some discourse is sin, and do not spy or backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah, indeed Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding unnecessary and harmful speech, as it can lead to sin and harm to others. The verse uses a powerful metaphor, comparing backbiting and spying to eating the flesh of one's dead brother, highlighting the repulsive nature of such actions. The verse also encourages believers to fear Allah and reminds them of Allah's mercy and acceptance of repentance, inviting them to turn to Allah in remorse and seek forgiveness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه واتقوا الله إن الله تواب رحيم

translation: O mankind! We have created you from a male and a female, and made you into nations and tribes, that you may know one another. Verily, the most honorable of you in the sight of Allah is the most pious of you. Verily, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equal status of all human beings, regardless of their gender, race, or nationality. It highlights the purpose of creation, which is to recognize and acknowledge the greatness of Allah and to live a righteous life. The verse also warns against pride and arrogance, reminding believers that true honor and status are not based on worldly possessions or lineage, but on one's relationship with Allah and their level of piety. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and the pursuit of spiritual growth.
orig: يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم إن الله عليم خبير

translation: The Arabs said, 'We believe.' Say, 'You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not diminish from your deeds anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Arabs who claimed to have embraced Islam, but their actions did not reflect their belief. The verse emphasizes that mere verbal submission is not enough; true faith must be reflected in one's actions. The verse encourages them to obey Allah and His Messenger, reminding them that their actions will not be in vain, as Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. The verse warns against hypocrisy and emphasizes the importance of aligning one's actions with one's beliefs.
orig: قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم وإن تطيعوا الله ورسوله لا يلتكم من أعمالكم شيئا إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, the believers who believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubted not and strove with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah. Those are the truthful ones.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of the believers who have faith in Allah and His Messenger and do not doubt. They are willing to sacrifice their wealth and lives for the cause of Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's faith into action and being willing to make sacrifices for the greater good. The phrase "strove with their wealth and their lives" indicates that the believers are not only willing to give up their material possessions but also their own lives for the sake of Allah. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain true to their faith and to be willing to make sacrifices for the cause of Allah.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered your partner-gods whom you appeal to instead of Allah? Show me what they have created from the heavens and the earth.' Indeed, Allah has knowledge of them, and He is with every thing acquainted.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the polytheists to reflect on their beliefs and consider the powerlessness of the gods they worship besides Allah. The verse asks them to consider the creation of the heavens and the earth and recognize that Allah is the only one who has the power to create and sustain all things. The verse emphasizes Allah's knowledge and control over all things, and serves as a reminder to those who reject Allah's message that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: قل أتعلمون الله بدينكم والله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: يمنون عليك أن أسلموا قل لا تمنوا علي إسلامكم بل الله يمن عليكم أن هداكم للإيمان إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Indeed, Allah knows the hidden of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all things, including the hidden aspects of the universe and the actions of human beings. The verse serves as a reminder that God is fully aware of all that we do, and that nothing is hidden from Him. It encourages believers to live their lives with the consciousness that God is always watching and to strive to do good deeds and avoid evil actions.
orig: إن الله يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض والله بصير بما تعملون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ق والقرآن المجيد

translation: And they were surprised that a warner came to them from among themselves. But the disbelievers said, "This is a strange thing. When we are dead and have become dust (shadow), shall we be brought forth (again)?"
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they were warned by a prophet from among their own people. They were surprised and skeptical, questioning the possibility of their being brought back to life after death. The verse highlights their disbelief and unwillingness to accept the message of the prophet, as well as their ignorance of the power of God to bring the dead back to life. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: بل عجبوا أن جاءهم منذر منهم فقال الكافرون هذا شيء عجيب

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you do not remember.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) opponents, who were skeptical of his message and denied the possibility of resurrection. The verse reminds them that God has destroyed entire nations in the past for their sins and injustices, but the people of Mecca were unaware of this history and failed to learn from it. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that God's punishment is real and that they will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: أإذا متنا وكنا ترابا ذلك رجع بعيد

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all creation. The use of the plural form of 'worlds' indicates that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or time period, but is universal and timeless. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to bring people closer to God and to guide them towards a righteous and peaceful life.
orig: قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ

translation: And they belied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state (now).
interpretation: The verse refers to a situation where people were presented with the truth, but they rejected it and chose to disbelieve. As a result, they are now in a state of confusion and disarray, unable to distinguish right from wrong. The verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and the negative impact it has on one's life.
orig: بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فهم في أمر مريج

translation: And have they not looked at the heaven above them, how We have made it and adorned it and there is no rifts in it?
interpretation: The verse highlights the beauty and majesty of the sky, emphasizing God's power and wisdom in its creation. The use of the word 'We' in the verse suggests a sense of unity and collaboration between God and the angels in the creation of the heavens. The verse serves as a reminder to humans to appreciate and reflect on the beauty of God's creation, and to recognize the greatness of God who is capable of creating such a magnificent work of art.
orig: أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج

translation: And the earth, We have spread it out, and placed therein mountains and rivers, and We have grown therein every noble kind.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of the earth and its various features, emphasizing the diversity and richness of God's creation. The use of the word 'spread' (maddadnaha) suggests a sense of vastness and expansiveness, while the placement of mountains and rivers highlights the contrast between the solidity of the earth's surface and the fluidity of its waterways. The phrase 'every noble kind' (kulli zawj bahiyy) underscores the variety and beauty of the natural world, and serves as a reminder of God's power and wisdom in shaping the earth and all that it contains.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج بهيج

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear conquest and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The verse emphasizes the clarity and manifest nature of this victory, indicating that it is a clear and evident sign of God's favor and support for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of God's power and ability to grant victory to those who follow His commandments and live according to His will.
orig: تبصرة وذكرى لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We sent down from the sky blessed water and brought forth gardens and grains.
interpretation: The verse describes the blessings of rain sent by God. The phrase 'min al-sama' (from the sky) emphasizes the divine origin of the rain, and 'mabarak' (blessed) highlights its beneficial effects. The verse mentions two specific ways in which the rain benefits people: it brings forth gardens (jannat) and grains (habb al-hasid). The phrase 'jannat' refers to lush green spaces, while 'habb al-hasid' refers to crops, indicating that the rain is essential for the growth of both vegetation and food. The verse reminds people of God's provision and encourages gratitude for His blessings.
orig: ونزلنا من السماء ماء مباركا فأنبتنا به جنات وحب الحصيد

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Muhammad and the Muslims. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies a decisive and unambiguous triumph, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is evident and obvious to all. The verse is often interpreted as a reference to the conquest of Mecca, where the Prophet Muhammad returned triumphantly after years of persecution and opposition. The verse serves as a reminder of God's support and assistance to those who are faithful and obedient to Him.
orig: والنخل باسقات لها طلع نضيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: رزقا للعباد وأحيينا به بلدة ميتا كذلك الخروج

translation: And We have not sent before you any but men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all prophets, including Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), are human beings, just like the people they are sent to guide. It highlights that the prophets are not supernatural beings, but rather chosen by God to convey His message to humanity. The verse also underscores the idea that the prophets are not unique in their ability to receive divine revelation, but rather, they are ordinary people who have been chosen by God for a specific purpose. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to respect and follow the teachings of the prophets, and to recognize that they are not infallible, but rather, they are human beings who have been guided by God.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وأصحاب الرس وثمود

translation: And We had given to the Children of Israel the Scripture, wisdom, and prophethood, and provided them with good things and preferred them over the nations.
interpretation: The verse highlights the special favors and blessings that God bestowed upon the Children of Israel. The verse mentions three specific gifts: the Scripture (the Torah), wisdom, and prophethood. The Scripture represents divine guidance and revelation, wisdom refers to the ability to understand and apply the teachings of the Scripture, and prophethood signifies the leadership and guidance provided by the prophets. Additionally, the verse states that God provided the Children of Israel with good things, such as fertile land, prosperity, and victory over their enemies. Finally, the verse emphasizes that the Children of Israel were preferred over other nations, indicating their unique status and relationship with God.
orig: وعاد وفرعون وإخوان لوط

translation: And the companions of the Ark and the people of Tubba` had already denied the messengers, so We seized them with a great seizure.
interpretation: The verse mentions two groups of people who denied the messengers sent by God: the companions of the Ark and the people of Tubba`. The verse states that God seized them with a great seizure, indicating a severe punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God's messengers, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأصحاب الأيكة وقوم تبع كل كذب الرسل فحق وعيد

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the whispers of human's inner thoughts and is closer to them than their own vital organs, indicating His intimate knowledge of their innermost thoughts and feelings. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and His ability to hear and know the secrets of human hearts, encouraging people to be mindful of their thoughts and actions.
orig: أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human hearts, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also underscores the nearness of God to human beings, using the metaphor of the jugular vein to convey the idea that God is closer to us than our own vital organs. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and it encourages humans to be mindful of their thoughts and actions, recognizing that they are always under God's watchful eye.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

translation: And the two angels will be sent down, one to the east and one to the west, to gather the wicked people to be thrown into Hell.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of the end of the world, where two angels will be sent down, one to the east and one to the west, to gather all the wicked people and bring them to Hell. The verse emphasizes the global scope of God's judgment, with the two angels covering the entire world, east and west, to gather all the sinners. The verse also highlights the certainty of God's punishment for those who have rejected His signs and warnings, and the finality of their fate, as they will be thrown into Hell. The verse serves as a warning to all people, reminding them of the Day of Judgment and the need to live a righteous life to avoid such a fate.
orig: إذ يتلقى المتلقيان عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد

translation: And not a word will they say except that there is a watcher ready to take it down.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that everything we say is being recorded and watched by God. The 'watcher' in the verse refers to the angels who are responsible for recording the deeds and words of humans. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions and words have consequences, and that we will be held accountable for them in the afterlife. It encourages us to be mindful of our speech and actions, and to strive to live a virtuous life.
orig: ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد

translation: And death will be brought forth, the truth will be manifest, and it will be said to the criminals, 'This is what you were trying to escape!
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of judgment day when death will be personified and brought forth, and the truth will be revealed. The verse addresses the criminals, reminding them that they tried to escape their consequences in life, but on judgment day, they will be confronted with their actions and held accountable. The verse serves as a warning to sinners, emphasizing the inevitability of their punishment and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد

translation: And We have destroyed the like of your town (Sodom), when the command of your Lord has been fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, which was annihilated by God's decree. The verse emphasizes that the destruction was a fulfillment of God's promise, as stated in the previous verse. The use of the phrase "the like of your town" suggests that the town of Sodom was similar to other towns that have been destroyed in the past, highlighting the idea that God's punishment is not limited to any particular community. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ونفخ في الصور ذلك يوم الوعيد

translation: And every soul has come with it, a driver and a witness.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment, when every person will be accompanied by two companions: a driver and a witness. The driver symbolizes the person's actions and deeds in life, while the witness represents the person's conscience and the knowledge of their own soul. The verse emphasizes the idea that every person will be held accountable for their actions and that they will have no excuse for their misdeeds. The driver and witness will serve as a reminder of the person's own agency and responsibility for their actions.
orig: وجاءت كل نفس معها سائق وشهيد

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind, and the example of the past generations has already passed. Do you not take heed?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed nations before him, just as they were destroyed in the past. The verse serves as a warning to those who refuse to heed the lessons of history and continue to live in disobedience to God's commands. It emphasizes the importance of learning from the past and recognizing that God's punishment is real and imminent.
orig: لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which was not limited to a specific group or community, but rather extended to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's responsibility to spread God's message of peace, love, and compassion to all people, and encourages believers to follow his example in their interactions with others.
orig: وقال قرينه هذا ما لدي عتيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار عنيد

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'manifest triumph' signifies that the triumph was evident and clear for all to see, leaving no doubt about the truth of the Prophet's message. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of God's favor and support, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and continue to spread the message of Islam.
orig: مناع للخير معتد مريب

translation: And he who associates with Allah another deity - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse warns against the sin of shirk, or associating partners with Allah. It emphasizes that those who commit this sin will be denied entry into Paradise and will instead be destined for Hell. The verse also underscores the idea that those who reject the oneness of God and instead choose to worship other deities or entities will have no one to help them on Judgment Day, and they will face the consequences of their actions alone.
orig: الذي جعل مع الله إلها آخر فألقياه في العذاب الشديد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال قرينه ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد

translation: And do not dispute with me, for I have come to you with clear proof.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of not disputing with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as he has been sent with clear evidence and guidance from God. It is a reminder to the people to accept the truth and not to argue or dispute with the Prophet, as he is the chosen one by God to convey His message. The verse also highlights the significance of the Prophet's role as a mercy to humanity, and that his message is a guidance and a reminder for those who want to live a righteous life.
orig: قال لا تختصموا لدي وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما يبدل القول لدي وما أنا بظلام للعبيد

translation: On the Day when He will say: 'Call upon My partners, those whom you assumed (to be My partners),' and they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will put a veil between them, and the wicked will say: 'You did not used to say this to us, (now) we have forgotten (the Message). Have you (now) forgotten your magic and your gathering?',
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, where Allah will call upon the idols and false deities that people worshiped instead of Him, to come and assist their followers. However, these idols will not respond, and a veil will be placed between them, separating them from the wicked people who worshiped them. The wicked will then realize that their idols are powerless and that they have been misled. They will accuse each other of forgetting the message of the Prophets and their teachings, and will realize that their magic and gatherings were of no avail on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم نقول لجهنم هل امتلأت وتقول هل من مزيد

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the believers. The use of the phrase 'children of Adam' emphasizes the idea that all human beings are equal in the eyes of God and are deserving of respect and dignity, regardless of their race, gender, or social status. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live up to their honorable status and to strive to maintain a strong connection with God.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين غير بعيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هذا ما توعدون لكل أواب حفيظ

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah's eye is upon the believers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His constant watchfulness over the believers. The phrase 'wherever you may be' signifies that God's knowledge and power encompasses all things, including the actions and thoughts of human beings. The second part of the verse highlights the special relationship between God and the believers, indicating that God is always aware of their circumstances and is watching over them with care and protection.
orig: من خشي الرحمن بالغيب وجاء بقلب منيب

translation: Enter Paradise in peace, that is the Day of Eternity.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the believers' entry into Paradise, describing it as a day of eternity, indicating that it is a state of everlasting joy and happiness, without end or departure. The verse emphasizes the peace and security that the believers will experience in Paradise, and serves as a comfort and encouragement to those who are striving to live a righteous life and looking forward to the reward of their efforts.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام ذلك يوم الخلود

translation: And indeed, We have given them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for those who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessing of the Qur'an, which is a comprehensive guide for believers, containing knowledge, guidance, and mercy. The use of 'We' in the phrase 'We have given them a Book' emphasizes God's role as the source of this guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a means of mercy for those who believe in it.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون فيها ولدينا مزيد

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أشد منهم بطشا فنقبوا في البلاد هل من محيص

translation: Indeed, in this is a reminder for those who have a heart or listen carefully.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance of listening to the message of the Qur'an and its impact on those who have a heart that is receptive to the message. The phrase 'or listen carefully' suggests that even those who may not have a heart that is naturally receptive to spiritual messages can still benefit from the reminder if they listen attentively and with an open mind. The verse highlights the importance of paying attention to the message of the Qur'an and its ability to resonate with those who are willing to listen and reflect.
orig: إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe and everything in it, including the heavens and the earth, as well as everything that exists between them, in a period of six days. The verse emphasizes that God did not feel any fatigue or weakness during this process, indicating that the creation of the universe was an effortless and easy act for God. The verse highlights the power and majesty of God, reminding believers of His greatness and dominance over all that exists.
orig: ولقد خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام وما مسنا من لغوب

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
interpretation: The verse encourages believers to be patient in the face of mockery and ridicule from non-believers. It emphasizes the importance of glorifying and praising Allah, particularly at the beginning and end of the day, signifying the importance of starting and ending each day with remembrance of Allah. It serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their relationship with Allah and not be affected by the opinions of others.
orig: فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل الغروب

translation: And by the night when it covers it (the earth) and by the morning when it brightens up (the earth).
interpretation: This verse speaks about the beauty and majesty of God's creation, specifically the night and the morning. The verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of time, with the night covering the earth and the morning brightening it up. The verse is a reminder of the power and greatness of God, who is the creator of such a magnificent universe and who is worthy of praise and worship.
orig: ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود

translation: And listen on the day when the caller will call out from a nearby place.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when a caller will call out from a nearby place, signaling the beginning of the judgment. The verse emphasizes the proximity of the caller, indicating that the event is imminent and that people should be prepared for it. The verse serves as a reminder of the nearness of the Hereafter and the need for people to be mindful of their actions and prepare for the final judgment.
orig: واستمع يوم يناد المناد من مكان قريب

translation: On a day when they will hear the (awful) cry, in truth, that is the day of coming out (from the tombs).
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment when the people will hear the dreadful cry signaling the resurrection of the dead and the beginning of judgment. The verse emphasizes that this day is a reality and not a myth, and it will be a day of reckoning for all humanity. The verse warns the reader to be prepared for this inevitable day and to live a life that is pleasing to God in order to avoid the horrors of the hereafter.
orig: يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق ذلك يوم الخروج

translation: Indeed, We will bring the dead to life, and We are witnesses to what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over life and death. The phrase 'We will bring the dead to life' refers to the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment, when all souls will be reunited with their bodies and judged according to their deeds. The second part of the verse, 'and We are witnesses to what they used to do', underscores the idea that God is all-knowing and aware of everything that humans do, and that their actions will be taken into account on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the Hereafter and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير

translation: And the earth will shake with a violent shaking, and the mountains will crumble, and become dust.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of the end of the world, where the earth will shake violently, and the mountains, which are considered solid and enduring, will crumble and turn into dust. The verse suggests a catastrophic event that will bring an end to the current state of affairs and usher in a new era. The verse serves as a reminder of the power of God and the impermanence of all things, and it warns people to be prepared for the ultimate judgment day.
orig: يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم سراعا ذلك حشر علينا يسير

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind, and how many a prophet We have sent among them. And when the messengers despaired and thought that they were denied, then came to them Our help, and whom We willed were saved. And Our punishment cannot be averted from the guilty people.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and authority, as well as the cyclical nature of human history.
