orig: ألم تر أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم أين ما كانوا ثم ينبئهم بما عملوا يوم القيامة إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Have you not seen those who were told: 'Do not commit evil deeds, for you will be punished'? But then they return to their Lord and ask for His forgiveness, and they were the ones who used to commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) and disbelieve in the Hereafter. And (now) they are the ones who are trying to bargain for another chance (to repent), saying: 'Our Lord, punish us not if we have been unjust. Indeed, we will be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where some individuals were warned not to commit evil deeds, but they continued to engage in shirk (associating partners with Allah) and disbelief in the Hereafter. Despite this, they have the audacity to ask for Allah's forgiveness and try to bargain for another chance to repent. The verse highlights their hypocrisy and lack of remorse, as they acknowledge their wrongdoing but still try to avoid the consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who take their relationship with Allah lightly and neglect His commands, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the need for genuine repentance.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نهوا عن النجوى ثم يعودون لما نهوا عنه ويتناجون بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وإذا جاءوك حيوك بما لم يحيك به الله ويقولون في أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger, and do not betray the trust. Indeed, the betrayal of the trust will be a great sin.
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, reminding them of their responsibility to uphold their covenant with God and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the gravity of betraying this trust, which is considered a great sin. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of loyalty and faithfulness to God and His Messenger, and the consequences of betraying that trust.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصيت الرسول وتناجوا بالبر والتقوى واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper - except for those who repent and correct themselves and hold fast to God and are sincere in their faith in God alone, for they will be with the believers, and God is their Protector and Guide.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the fate of hypocrites who pretend to be believers but are not sincere in their faith. They will be punished in the lowest depths of hell, and no one will be able to help them. However, those who repent and correct their ways, hold fast to God, and are sincere in their faith will be spared from this punishment and will be with the believers, under God's protection and guidance.
orig: إنما النجوى من الشيطان ليحزن الذين آمنوا وليس بضارهم شيئا إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, when it is said to you, 'Retreat in your gatherings,' then retreat in the gatherings. Allah will make for you a way out, and Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the believers and instructing them to retreat and make space when told to do so in gatherings. The verse promises that Allah will create a way out for the believers and raise their ranks, both in this life and the hereafter. The verse also emphasizes that those who have been given knowledge, indicating a deep understanding of the faith, will also be raised in rank. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their actions and obedience to Allah's commandments will be recognized and rewarded.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قيل لكم تفسحوا في المجالس فافسحوا يفسح الله لكم وإذا قيل انشزوا فانشزوا يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم درجات والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, will you do so in a manner that is proper and just? And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of doing good deeds and acting justly, particularly when striving in the cause of God. It encourages believers to act with compassion, kindness, and fairness, and reminds them that God loves those who do good deeds. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims that their actions should be guided by a desire to please God and to earn His forgiveness and blessings.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة ذلك خير لكم وأطهر فإن لم تجدوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات فإذ لم تفعلوا وتاب الله عليكم فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأطيعوا الله ورسوله والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a share of the Scripture? They were invited to the Book of Allah, but they turned away and refused.
interpretation: This verse addresses the behavior of those who were given a share of the Scripture, specifically the Jews and Christians, who were invited to follow the teachings of the Qur'an but refused. The verse suggests that they were arrogant and unwilling to submit to God's commandments, instead choosing to follow their own desires and misinterpretations of their holy books. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is the final and complete revelation of God's will, and that those who reject it will face consequences.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين تولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم ما هم منكم ولا منهم ويحلفون على الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We will punish them with a severe punishment, in recompense for their behavior.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of evil deeds and the certainty of God's punishment. The phrase 'severe punishment' emphasizes the gravity of the punishment and the severity of God's wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in negative behavior, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will be held accountable for their deeds. The verse also highlights the idea of retribution and the principle of recompense, where every action has a consequence, and every deed will be rewarded or punished accordingly.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they have been forbidden from the Garden, as they wronged themselves by losing their way from God's path, so they will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: The verse speaks about those who have been forbidden from the Garden, which symbolizes spiritual enlightenment and closeness to God. They have wronged themselves by straying from God's path and will therefore face a humiliating punishment. The verse highlights the consequences of straying from God's path and the importance of living a righteous life in accordance with God's will.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله فلهم عذاب مهين

translation: Their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that wealth and children will not protect the unbelievers from God's punishment. The verse suggests that material possessions and family ties will not be of any use on Judgment Day, and those who are disbelievers will be companions of the Fire, suffering eternally in Hell.
orig: لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And on a Day when He will gather them all together, (and) they will feel humiliated, and they will not be able to hide any saying from Allah. And (it will be said to them): This is what you used to lie about.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered before God and their deeds will be exposed. The verse emphasizes the shame and embarrassment that the unbelievers will feel when they realize that their lies and denial of God's signs will be of no use, and they will be held accountable for their actions. The phrase 'they will not be able to hide any saying from Allah' highlights the idea that nothing will remain hidden from God's knowledge, and all secrets will be revealed. The final phrase, 'This is what you used to lie about,' underscores the idea that the unbelievers will be confronted with the reality of their own deception and lack of faith.
orig: يوم يبعثهم الله جميعا فيحلفون له كما يحلفون لكم ويحسبون أنهم على شيء ألا إنهم هم الكاذبون

translation: And Satan has overtaken them, so he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. How they will be losers!
interpretation: The verse describes the situation where Satan has taken control of certain individuals, causing them to forget the remembrance of Allah. The phrase 'party of Satan' refers to those who have allowed themselves to be misled by Satan and have abandoned their faith in Allah. The verse serves as a warning to believers, reminding them of the danger of allowing Satan to influence their thoughts and actions, and the consequences of forgetting Allah's remembrance.
orig: استحوذ عليهم الشيطان فأنساهم ذكر الله أولئك حزب الشيطان ألا إن حزب الشيطان هم الخاسرون

translation: Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger - those will be among the most humbled.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the consequences of opposing God and His Messenger. Those who dare to challenge God's authority and resist His message will be brought low and humbled. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of Islam and choose to follow their own path, reminding them of the consequences of their defiance and the certainty of God's judgment.
orig: إن الذين يحادون الله ورسوله أولئك في الأذلين

translation: And Allah has revealed to me and to those who came before me that the believers will be tested with trials and tribulations, and Allah will test you with evil and good, and He will certainly make known those who are truthful and those who are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that believers will face trials and tribulations, and that these trials serve as a means of testing their faith and sincerity. The verse also emphasizes that God is all-powerful and all-knowing, and that He will ultimately distinguish between those who are truthful in their beliefs and those who are not. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي إن الله قوي عزيز

translation: And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, the honor will be yours on the Day of Judgment. Indeed, the punishment of the oppressors will be severe.
interpretation: The verse advises believers not to be grieved by the speech of disbelievers and to remain steadfast in their faith. It reassures them that they will be honored on the Day of Judgment and that the punishment for the oppressors will be severe.
orig: لا تجد قوما يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر يوادون من حاد الله ورسوله ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه ويدخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه أولئك حزب الله ألا إن حزب الله هم المفلحون

translation: Glory to Allah, who is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of Allah, who is the sole owner of the heavens and the earth. The phrase 'Glory to Allah' is a declaration of Allah's transcendence and majesty, indicating that all praise and glory belong to Him alone. The description of Allah as 'the Most High' signifies His supremacy and sovereignty over all creation, while 'the Most Wise' highlights His infinite wisdom and knowledge. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to recognize and acknowledge Allah's greatness and to submit to His will.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هو الذي أخرج الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب من ديارهم لأول الحشر ما ظننتم أن يخرجوا وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله فأتاهم الله من حيث لم يحتسبوا وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب يخربون بيوتهم بأيديهم وأيدي المؤمنين فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

translation: And if it were not for the decree of Allah that had been decreed, their punishment would have been hastened, and indeed, the punishment will befall them in this world and the Hereafter. They will have no victor or helper against Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The verse states that if it were not for God's decree that the punishment would have been hastened, indicating that the punishment is already overdue and that God's patience with them has been extended. The verse also emphasizes that the punishment will not only be in this life but also in the hereafter, and that no one can save them from God's punishment. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the severity of its consequences.
orig: ولولا أن كتب الله عليهم الجلاء لعذبهم في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب النار

translation: Those who have been hurt by the punishment of Allah and His Messenger, then surely Allah is Severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of God's punishment for those who have earned it by disobeying Him and His Messenger. The phrase 'شاقوا الله' (Shāqū Allāh) means 'they have been hurt' or 'they have been afflicted' by God's punishment, indicating that they have experienced a taste of His wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who are disobedient and disbelieving, reminding them of the severe consequences of their actions, and encouraging them to repent and turn back to God.
orig: ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله ومن يشاق الله فإن الله شديد العقاب

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما قطعتم من لينة أو تركتموها قائمة على أصولها فبإذن الله وليخزي الفاسقين

translation: And what has been given to the Messenger from them, but it has not diminished the bounty of Allah upon him. Indeed, it is a reminder to those who fear My warning and fear My punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the blessings and favors given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by Allah did not decrease the bounty of Allah upon him. Instead, it served as a reminder to those who fear Allah's warning and punishment. The verse highlights the importance of fearing Allah and being mindful of His punishment, as well as the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a reminder and a warner to those who are heedless of Allah's message.
orig: وما أفاء الله على رسوله منهم فما أوجفتم عليه من خيل ولا ركاب ولكن الله يسلط رسله على من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And what has been given to the Messenger from the people of the villages, so that it may not be a share between the rich among you, and the poor? And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, desist from it. And fear Allah, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the consequences of not adhering to them. The verse warns against the dangers of disobeying the Prophet's instructions and encourages the believers to fear Allah's punishment. The verse also highlights the importance of equality and justice, emphasizing that the Prophet's teachings are not meant to benefit only the rich, but also the poor and the weak. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to adhere to the teachings of the Prophet and to fear Allah's punishment if they disobey.
orig: ما أفاء الله على رسوله من أهل القرى فلله وللرسول ولذي القربى واليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل كي لا يكون دولة بين الأغنياء منكم وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking the Bounty and Good Pleasure of Allah and to support Allah and His Messenger, those are the truthful ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the early Muslims who were forced to migrate from Mecca to Medina due to persecution. Despite leaving behind their homes and possessions, they sought the blessings and pleasure of God and supported the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse emphasizes their truthfulness and sincerity in their belief and actions, highlighting their willingness to sacrifice everything for their faith. The verse serves as an example for believers to follow in their footsteps and be willing to make sacrifices for the sake of their faith.
orig: للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم وأموالهم يبتغون فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله ورسوله أولئك هم الصادقون

translation: And those who were settled in the home and in the faith before them, love those who have migrated to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and do not envy them for what they have been given, and they prefer them over themselves, even if they themselves were in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, these are the successful ones.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the righteous people who have settled in their faith and are content with what they have. They welcome those who have migrated to their land and do not feel jealous or resentful of what they have been given. Instead, they prefer the newcomers over themselves, even if it means they have to sacrifice their own needs. The verse highlights the importance of selflessness and generosity, and how those who are able to overcome their own selfish desires are the truly successful ones.
orig: والذين تبوءوا الدار والإيمان من قبلهم يحبون من هاجر إليهم ولا يجدون في صدورهم حاجة مما أوتوا ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And those who have come after them say: 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any resentment towards those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse speaks about the believers' request for forgiveness for themselves and their fellow believers who came before them. They ask God to forgive them and their brothers in faith, and to purify their hearts from any resentment or hatred towards those who have also believed. The verse highlights the unity and brotherhood among believers, and their desire to maintain a positive relationship with one another. It also emphasizes God's attribute of being Kind and Merciful, which gives hope to those who seek His forgiveness.
orig: والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا ولإخواننا الذين سبقونا بالإيمان ولا تجعل في قلوبنا غلا للذين آمنوا ربنا إنك رءوف رحيم

translation: Have you not seen those who have befriended the people who have been condemned by God? They are the ones who say to their brethren who have rejected faith: 'We will go forth with you.' But they will not go forth with them. Indeed, they will go with you, but they will not fight except a little. Indeed, they are reluctant to fight and are afraid of you. They are the ones who are hypocrites, and God knows the hypocrites well.
interpretation: The verse addresses the issue of hypocrisy within the Muslim community. It refers to those who claim to be Muslims but do not truly believe in the faith. They are friendly with the disbelievers and pretend to be their allies, but they do not truly support them. When the time comes to fight, they are reluctant and afraid to engage in battle. They are more concerned with their own interests than with standing up for their faith. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of their hypocrisy and will not be fooled by their outward appearance of faith.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين نافقوا يقولون لإخوانهم الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب لئن أخرجتم لنخرجن معكم ولا نطيع فيكم أحدا أبدا وإن قوتلتم لننصرنكم والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And if they had gone out, they would not have been able to hold back the believers, and if they had fought, they would not have been aided, and if they had been aided, they would have been given a chance to escape.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a hypothetical situation in which the disbelievers were given the opportunity to fight the believers. The verse indicates that even if the disbelievers had gone out to fight, they would not have been able to defeat the believers. Furthermore, even if they had fought, they would not have received any help or support. And if they had received help, it would have been a temporary reprieve, allowing them to escape. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their ultimate victory is from God, and that they should not fear the disbelievers, for their fate is already sealed.
orig: لئن أخرجوا لا يخرجون معهم ولئن قوتلوا لا ينصرونهم ولئن نصروهم ليولن الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: Indeed, you are the most quarrelsome of people in speech, [even] more so than the polytheists.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the Muslim community, despite their belief in one God, are more contentious and argumentative than the polytheists. The verse highlights the irony of the Muslims' behavior, as they claim to worship one God, yet they are more divided and argumentative than those who worship multiple deities. The verse serves as a reminder to the Muslim community to unite and avoid unnecessary disputes, focusing on their shared beliefs rather than their differences.
orig: لأنتم أشد رهبة في صدورهم من الله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: They will not fight you altogether, except in fortified towns or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think they are united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of disbelievers who are reluctant to engage in open combat and instead resort to guerrilla warfare, using fortified towns or walls for protection. Their internal conflicts and lack of unity are also highlighted, indicating that their apparent strength is an illusion. The verse suggests that their ultimate defeat is due to their lack of understanding and inability to unite.
orig: لا يقاتلونكم جميعا إلا في قرى محصنة أو من وراء جدر بأسهم بينهم شديد تحسبهم جميعا وقلوبهم شتى ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: And indeed, those who came before them had also plotted, but the plan of Allah is superior to their plan, for Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that the disbelievers who came before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had also made plans to defeat him and his followers, but their plans were ultimately foiled by Allah's superior plan. The verse emphasizes Allah's power and control over events, and serves as a reminder to believers that Allah's plan is always superior to any human plan, and that they should trust in Allah's plan and not lose hope in the face of adversity.
orig: كمثل الذين من قبلهم قريبا ذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And (similarly) We have put forth the example of the devil when he said to man, 'Disbelieve, so I will take you as a friend (and guide).' And when man disbelieved, (the devil) said, 'Indeed, I am free from you, for I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse uses the example of the devil to illustrate the danger of temptation and the importance of faith. The devil, who was once a jinn named Iblis, was cast out of heaven for refusing to bow down to Adam, the first human. He then asked God for respite until the Day of Judgment, promising to mislead all but a few of Adam's descendants. In this verse, Iblis tempts Adam to disbelieve in God, promising to be his friend and guide. However, once Adam succumbs to temptation, Iblis immediately disowns him, stating that he fears God and is not responsible for Adam's actions. The verse warns against the dangers of following temptation and the importance of staying true to one's faith in God.
orig: كمثل الشيطان إذ قال للإنسان اكفر فلما كفر قال إني بريء منك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: And their punishment was that they were (cast) into the Fire, they remained in it (forever), and that was the reward of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who were unjust and wrongdoers. They were cast into the Fire, which symbolizes eternal suffering and punishment. The verse emphasizes that this punishment is a consequence of their own actions and is a just reward for their wrongdoing. It serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكان عاقبتهما أنهما في النار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be aware of a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul, and no ransom will be accepted from it, nor will any intercession benefit it, and nor will they be helped.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah and being mindful of the Day of Judgment, when every individual will be held accountable for their actions. The verse stresses that no one will be able to intercede or ransom another's soul, and no amount of wealth or status will be of any use on that day. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a righteous life and to be prepared for the Hereafter, as no one knows when their time will come.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. They are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse warns against forgetting Allah and becoming neglectful of one's relationship with Him. When people forget Allah, they become disconnected from their spiritual selves and may fall into disobedience and sin. The verse emphasizes the consequences of such forgetfulness, describing those who forget Allah as 'defiantly disobedient', indicating that their neglect of Allah leads to a state of rebellion against His commandments.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين نسوا الله فأنساهم أنفسهم أولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal; the companions of Paradise are the successful ones.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the difference between those who will end up in Hell (the companions of the Fire) and those who will end up in Paradise (the companions of Paradise). The verse implies that the latter group is successful, as they have lived a righteous life and will be rewarded with eternal happiness in Paradise. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal of human existence, which is to attain salvation and avoid damnation.
orig: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة أصحاب الجنة هم الفائزون

translation: Had We sent this Qur'an down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, rent asunder by the fear of Allah. We set forth these parables to people, that they may reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the immense power and authority of the Qur'an, suggesting that even a mountain would be humbled and rent asunder by the fear of Allah if the Qur'an were to be sent down upon it. The verse also highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation, as the Qur'an is full of parables and lessons that are meant to guide people towards a righteous life. The verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is not just a book of words, but a powerful and transformative force that can change individuals and societies for the better.
orig: لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس لعلهم يتفكرون

translation: And He is Allah, the One and Only; He is Allah, the Eternal, the Absolute; He begets not, nor is He begotten; And there is none like Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of God, emphasizing that He is the only deity worthy of worship and that He is not born nor does He give birth. The verse also highlights God's eternal nature and His being the source of all creation, emphasizing His power and majesty. The verse is a declaration of the greatness and majesty of God, and serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of recognizing and worshiping only one God.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب والشهادة هو الرحمن الرحيم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر سبحان الله عما يشركون

translation: And He is Allah, the Creator, the Inventor, the Flawless, the Bestower of forms. His are the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him. And He is the Exalted, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse describes Allah as the ultimate creator, who is capable of inventing and giving forms to His creation. He is also described as Flawless, indicating that His creations are perfect and free of defects. The verse highlights the beauty of Allah's names, indicating that His attributes and characteristics are worthy of praise. The verse also emphasizes that everything in the heavens and the earth, including all living things, glorifies Allah, indicating that all of creation is subservient to Him. Finally, the verse describes Allah as the Exalted, indicating His supremacy and greatness, and the Wise, indicating His infinite wisdom in creation and governance.
orig: هو الله الخالق البارئ المصور له الأسماء الحسنى يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, and have driven out the Prophet and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord, and I know what you have hidden and what you have declared. And he who does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: The verse warns believers against taking the disbelievers as allies and friends, and emphasizes that they have rejected the truth and driven out the Prophet and the believers. The verse highlights the danger of befriending those who reject God's message and reminds believers that their loyalty should only be to God and His Messenger. The verse also implies that those who do so have strayed from the right path and are in danger of falling into misguidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء تلقون إليهم بالمودة وقد كفروا بما جاءكم من الحق يخرجون الرسول وإياكم أن تؤمنوا بالله ربكم إن كنتم خرجتم جهادا في سبيلي وابتغاء مرضاتي تسرون إليهم بالمودة وأنا أعلم بما أخفيتم وما أعلنتم ومن يفعله منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: Indeed, they will hate you and expel you and say, 'May God's curse be upon you!' and they will wish evil upon you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers towards the believers. The disbelievers will not only reject the message of Islam but will also show hostility towards the believers, wishing evil upon them and expelling them from their homes. The verse highlights the intensity of their hatred and their desire to see the believers cursed and harmed. This verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to not be deterred by the hatred and rejection they may face from others.
orig: إن يثقفوكم يكونوا لكم أعداء ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء وودوا لو تكفرون

translation: Your wealth and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate you. Allah will see your actions.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that material wealth and children will not avail on Judgment Day. The verse warns believers not to rely on their worldly possessions or their descendants' successes, but to focus on their relationship with God and their adherence to His commandments. On Judgment Day, God will judge each person based on their deeds, regardless of their family connections or wealth.
orig: لن تنفعكم أرحامكم ولا أولادكم يوم القيامة يفصل بينكم والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And indeed, Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. [Allah] said, 'Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.' Abraham said, 'And of my offspring?' [Allah] said, 'My covenant will not include the wicked.'
interpretation: The verse speaks about the trial of Abraham by God, where he was commanded to sacrifice his son Ismail. Abraham fulfilled the command and was made a leader for the people. However, God excluded the wicked from His covenant, indicating that the blessings and leadership are not for those who disobey and reject God's commands.
orig: قد كانت لكم أسوة حسنة في إبراهيم والذين معه إذ قالوا لقومهم إنا برآء منكم ومما تعبدون من دون الله كفرنا بكم وبدا بيننا وبينكم العداوة والبغضاء أبدا حتى تؤمنوا بالله وحده إلا قول إبراهيم لأبيه لأستغفرن لك وما أملك لك من الله من شيء ربنا عليك توكلنا وإليك أنبنا وإليك المصير

translation: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might and the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to God, asking Him not to make the believers a test or a temptation for those who disbelieve. The verse also asks for God's forgiveness, acknowledging that He is the Most Exalted and Wise. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's power and wisdom are beyond human comprehension, and that He is capable of forgiving sins and guiding those who seek His guidance.
orig: ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للذين كفروا واغفر لنا ربنا إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And indeed, We will aid you with a manifest victory and victory. And indeed, We will aid you with a manifest victory.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. The first part of the verse emphasizes the clarity and manifest nature of the victory, indicating that it is a clear and decisive victory. The second part of the verse emphasizes the fact that God will continue to aid the believers and grant them victory. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers that their success and victory come from God's grace and support, and that they should always rely on Him for help and guidance.
orig: لقد كان لكم فيهم أسوة حسنة لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد

translation: And perhaps God will put, between you and those who have been angered by you, affection. And God is All-Powerful and God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the possibility of reconciliation and forgiveness between the believers and those who have been hostile towards them. The verse emphasizes God's power and mercy, suggesting that even in the face of adversity, God has the power to bring about peace and reconciliation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain hopeful and to seek forgiveness, knowing that God is forgiving and merciful.
orig: عسى الله أن يجعل بينكم وبين الذين عاديتم منهم مودة والله قدير والله غفور رحيم

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who are unjust, indeed Allah does not love him who is a habitual sinner and a mischief-maker.
interpretation: The verse warns against defending or speaking in favor of those who are unjust and wicked, as it is against God's will to support such individuals. The verse emphasizes that God does not love those who engage in sinful behavior and cause harm to others. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and not to align themselves with those who oppose God's teachings.
orig: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم وتقسطوا إليهم إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that Allah will help and support those who stand up for His cause and fight against injustice. The phrase 'And indeed, Allah will aid those who aid His cause' indicates that Allah's support is not limited to specific individuals or groups, but is available to anyone who works towards promoting justice and righteousness. The description of Allah as 'Powerful and Exalted in Might' serves to underscore His ability to help and protect those who seek His aid.
orig: إنما ينهاكم الله عن الذين قاتلوكم في الدين وأخرجوكم من دياركم وظاهروا على إخراجكم أن تولوهم ومن يتولهم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: O you who have believed, if you are approached by women who have believed, then test them. Allah knows their faith. And if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them. And give them what they have spent. And no blame will be upon you for what you have done in the past concerning their marriage. And do not hold onto the disbelievers' wealth and ask for what you have spent and do not ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah. He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: The verse addresses the situation where Muslim women who have been married to disbelievers are returned to them after embracing Islam. The verse instructs the Muslims not to return these women to their disbelieving husbands, as they are not lawful for them. Instead, the Muslims are commanded to give them their dowry, which they had spent on them before they embraced Islam. The verse emphasizes that the Muslims will not be blamed for what they did in the past regarding their marriage. The verse also prohibits the Muslims from holding onto the disbelievers' wealth and asking for what they had spent on them. The verse concludes by stating that this is Allah's judgment, and He is the All-Knowing and All-Wise.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا جاءكم المؤمنات مهاجرات فامتحنوهن الله أعلم بإيمانهن فإن علمتموهن مؤمنات فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن وآتوهم ما أنفقوا ولا جناح عليكم أن تنكحوهن إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن ولا تمسكوا بعصم الكوافر واسألوا ما أنفقتم وليسألوا ما أنفقوا ذلكم حكم الله يحكم بينكم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And indeed, you have been given a clear victory and a manifest triumph. And you will be tested with a little less than that which you were tested with before, and you will surely be victorious and have victory over them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the victory of the believers over their enemies, and how they have been given a clear and manifest triumph. The verse also warns the believers that they will be tested with a little less than what they were tested with before, but they will surely be victorious and have victory over their enemies. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in God's plan, even in the face of adversity.
orig: وإن فاتكم شيء من أزواجكم إلى الكفار فعاقبتم فآتوا الذين ذهبت أزواجهم مثل ما أنفقوا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: O Prophet! When the believing women come to you, swearing allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, and will not steal, and will not commit fornication, and will not kill their children, and will not bring forth a calumny they have devised between their hands and feet, and will not disobey you in what is right, then accept their allegiance and seek forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet accepting the oath of allegiance from the believing women, signifying their commitment to live according to the principles of Islam. The verse also highlights the women's pledge to refrain from various negative behaviors, such as associating partners with Allah, stealing, fornication, killing their children, and spreading false rumors. Additionally, the verse stresses the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah for the women, indicating that the Prophet should intercede on their behalf and seek God's mercy for them. The verse concludes by emphasizing God's attribute of being Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, highlighting His willingness to forgive those who turn to Him in repentance.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا ولا يسرقن ولا يزنين ولا يقتلن أولادهن ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن ولا يعصينك في معروف فبايعهن واستغفر لهن الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said, 'Surely Allah will not punish us, for they will not be punished.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the believers, urging them not to be like the disbelievers who were confident that they would not be punished by God. The disbelievers thought they were immune to God's punishment, but their arrogance and disbelief led to their downfall. The verse serves as a warning to the believers, reminding them of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتولوا قوما غضب الله عليهم قد يئسوا من الآخرة كما يئس الكفار من أصحاب القبور

translation: Glory be to Allah, in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Wise.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the greatness and majesty of Allah, who is worthy of all praise and glory. The phrase 'in the heavens and the earth' signifies that Allah's power and dominion extend over all of creation, both in the spiritual realm and the physical world. The description of Allah as 'the Most High' highlights His supremacy and transcendence, while 'the Most Wise' underscores His wisdom and justice in all His actions and decisions. The verse encourages believers to reflect on Allah's majesty and to glorify Him for His infinite greatness.
orig: سبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not say what you do not do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of truthfulness and sincerity in the believers' speech and actions. It warns against hypocrisy and encourages believers to be mindful of their words and deeds, ensuring that they align with their faith and values. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not just about belief, but also about action and conduct. The verse encourages believers to be truthful in their words and actions, and to strive for consistency between their beliefs and their behavior.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون

translation: And do not say about what your tongues describe, 'This is halal,' and 'This is haram.'
interpretation: The verse warns against making false statements or lies about what is lawful or unlawful, implying that such judgments should be left to God alone. It emphasizes that humans do not have the authority to make such judgments and should not speak about things they do not know. Instead, they should seek guidance from God and follow His commands. The verse underscores the importance of relying solely on God's revelation and not relying on personal opinions or desires when it comes to matters of faith and practice.
orig: كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون

translation: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they are a solid structure.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's love for those who fight in His cause, using the metaphor of a solid structure to describe their unity and cohesion. The image of soldiers standing in rows, shoulder to shoulder, convey's a sense of strength, determination, and discipline. The verse suggests that those who fight for God's cause are not just individual warriors, but a cohesive and formidable force, united in their quest to defend and promote justice and righteousness.
orig: إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص

translation: And Moses said to his people, 'O my people, you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [for worship]. You have turned away from the right path.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is addressing his people, who have committed a grave sin by worshipping the golden calf instead of Allah. Moses is reminding them that they have strayed from the right path and that their actions are a result of their own misguided choices. The verse highlights the importance of staying true to one's faith and the consequences of deviating from the righteous path.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم لم تؤذونني وقد تعلمون أني رسول الله إليكم فلما زاغوا أزاغ الله قلوبهم والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And when Isa, son of Maryam, said, 'O children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is between my hands of the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.' But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the Children of Israel when Prophet Isa (Jesus) presented himself as a Messenger of Allah and confirmed the Torah. Despite the clear evidences he presented, they rejected him and accused him of practicing magic. The verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of the People of the Book towards the prophets sent by Allah, and serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and submission to Allah's will.
orig: وإذ قال عيسى ابن مريم يا بني إسرائيل إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله الكذب وهو يدعى إلى الإسلام والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except that His light should be perfected, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the attempts of the disbelievers to suppress the truth and light of Allah. They try to extinguish it with their words and actions, but Allah's light will always prevail. The verse emphasizes the futility of their efforts and the ultimate success of Allah's light. It serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be discouraged by the attempts of those who seek to suppress the truth.
orig: يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم والله متم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and the universal message of Islam. The phrase 'guidance and the religion of truth' refers to the Qur'an and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad, which are considered the ultimate truth and guidance for all of humanity. The phrase 'manifest it over all religion' indicates that Islam is meant to be dominant and supreme over all other religions and beliefs. The verse also highlights the opposition and dislike of the polytheists towards Islam, but the verse reiterates that God's truth will ultimately prevail.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are truthful.
interpretation: The verse urges believers to have taqwa (fear of Allah) and to associate with people who are truthful in their words and deeds. The phrase 'those who are truthful' refers to those who are honest, sincere, and upright in their actions and speech. The verse emphasizes the importance of being in the company of such people, as their righteousness will have a positive influence on others and help them to remain on the path of truth. It is a reminder that the company one keeps has a significant impact on one's own character and conduct, and that believers should strive to surround themselves with people who will encourage and support them in their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم

translation: You have been believers in Allah and His Messenger and have struggled in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of faith in Allah and His Messenger, as well as the commitment to strive in the way of Allah, using one's wealth and life. The verse implies that this level of dedication is the best for believers, leading to ultimate success and happiness, though they may not immediately realize it.
orig: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And He will forgive your sins and admit you to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward for those who lead a righteous life and follow God's commandments. The verse describes a beautiful and peaceful afterlife, where believers will be admitted to gardens with rivers flowing beneath them and pleasant dwellings in perpetual gardens. The verse emphasizes the idea that this is a great triumph and a reward for those who have lived a life according to God's will. The verse serves as a reminder and encouragement for believers to live a righteous life and to strive for the ultimate goal of achieving God's forgiveness and reward in the afterlife.
orig: يغفر لكم ذنوبكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And another (favor) which He has bestowed upon you, (O Muhammad), that He has sent to you a helper (the Holy Spirit) and a plain victory and a manifest triumph (in the form of the Prophet's migration from Mecca to Medina).
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community. The 'helper' refers to the Holy Spirit, which was sent to guide and support the Prophet in his mission. The 'plain victory' and 'manifest triumph' refer to the Prophet's migration from Mecca to Medina, which was a turning point in his mission and a significant victory for the Muslim community. The verse emphasizes the favor and blessings of God upon the Prophet and the Muslim community, and serves as a reminder of the divine support and guidance that they received.
orig: وأخرى تحبونها نصر من الله وفتح قريب وبشر المؤمنين

translation: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are Allah's supporters.' And a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of supporting Allah's cause and being on the side of righteousness. The example of Jesus and his disciples is given as a model for believers to follow, where they stood up for their beliefs and supported Allah's cause, even in the face of opposition. The verse also highlights the reward for those who support Allah's cause, as they will be granted victory and dominance over their enemies.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا أنصار الله كما قال عيسى ابن مريم للحواريين من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله فآمنت طائفة من بني إسرائيل وكفرت طائفة فأيدنا الذين آمنوا على عدوهم فأصبحوا ظاهرين

translation: All praise to Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Holy One, the Most High, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse expresses the belief in the oneness of God and attributes qualities to Him, such as holiness, supremacy, and wisdom. It emphasizes God's sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, underscoring His power and dominion over all creation. It serves as a declaration of faith and a reminder of God's greatness and majesty.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم

translation: And He sent prophets from among them, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, and indeed they were previously in clear error.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the mercy of God, who sent prophets to guide and teach his people, who were previously living in error and ignorance. The verse highlights the role of the prophets in reciting God's verses, purifying their followers, and teaching them the book and wisdom. The verse emphasizes that the people were in a state of clear error before the prophets were sent to guide them. The verse serves as a reminder of God's grace and mercy in sending prophets to guide humanity and the importance of following their teachings.
orig: هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: And others have been left behind, who will be smitten by the Mighty and Wise.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who have been left behind and will be punished by God, the Most Powerful and Wise. The verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in meting out punishment to those who deserve it, indicating that the punishment is not only severe but also just and well-deserved. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you have received the Qur'an from the presence of One who is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and its connection to the wise and knowing God. The verse highlights the Qur'an's sacred nature and its role as a source of guidance, reminding believers of God's wisdom and knowledge.
orig: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And they are like the ones who carried the burden of the Torah, but they did not carry it as it should be carried, as an ass carries a heavy load of books, and they forgot the Message of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: The verse compares those who have been entrusted with the responsibility of carrying and upholding the teachings of the Qur'an, but have failed to do so, to a donkey carrying a heavy load of books. Just as the donkey carries the load without understanding or benefiting from the knowledge contained within the books, those who neglect their responsibility to uphold the teachings of the Qur'an are similarly not benefiting from the guidance and wisdom contained within its verses. The verse serves as a warning to those who have been entrusted with the responsibility of carrying and upholding the teachings of the Qur'an, reminding them of the importance of their role and the consequences of neglecting their duty.
orig: مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Say, O those who have been given knowledge, do you think that you are friends of Allah, while you are not?
interpretation: The verse addresses the arrogance of those who claim to be the friends of Allah, implying that they have a special relationship with God and are therefore immune to punishment. The verse challenges this notion, suggesting that their claim is baseless and that they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder that true friendship with God is not determined by claims or assertions, but by one's actions and adherence to His commandments.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will not cease to be in doubt about it until they witness the painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers will continue to reject the truth and refuse to believe in the punishment that awaits them until they actually experience it for themselves. The phrase 'they will not cease to be in doubt' implies a persistent state of denial and disbelief, while the phrase 'painful punishment' underscores the severity of the consequences they will face. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and instead choose to follow their own desires and doubts.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witness, and He will inform you about what you used to do.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the human tendency to avoid thinking about death and the afterlife. The verse tells the reader to confront the reality of death and the fact that it will eventually catch up with them. The second part of the verse mentions that after death, the souls will be returned to the 'Knower of the unseen and the witness', referring to God, who is all-knowing and all-seeing. The verse ends with the idea that God will inform us about our actions in this life, indicating that our deeds will be scrutinized and judged by God. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability and the inevitability of death and the afterlife, encouraging the reader to live a life that is pleasing to God.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when [the Muslims] are called to the Friday prayer, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing spiritual matters over worldly pursuits. On Fridays, Muslims are called to gather for congregational prayer, and they are encouraged to leave their businesses and commercial activities to focus on the remembrance of Allah. This verse highlights the benefits of setting aside time for spiritual reflection and communal worship, which can bring blessings and guidance to individuals and society as a whole.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, then remember Allah, standing, sitting, and [lying] down, and when you become secure, then perform the prostration, and remember Allah much that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah frequently and consistently, whether one is standing, sitting, or lying down. It also encourages Muslims to perform the prostration of gratitude (sajdah al-shukr) after finishing their daily prayers. The verse suggests that remembering Allah and being grateful to Him is a means of achieving success in this life and the hereafter. It also highlights the importance of humility and submission to Allah's will, as the act of prostration represents the ultimate expression of submission to God's greatness and dominion over all creation.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And when they saw a transaction or entertainment, they rushed to it and left you standing [while they went to their livestock]. And they forgot that We have provided for them the good things [in life]. Indeed, We have provided for you the good things in this world and the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the people's tendency to prioritize worldly pursuits and fleeting pleasures over their relationship with God. They are so consumed by their desire for material gain and entertainment that they neglect their spiritual well-being and their responsibility to worship and obey God. The verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God has provided for him and his followers in this life and the next, and that they should not be distracted by the allure of worldly things.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: And when the hypocrites came to you, they said, 'We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the hypocrites who pretended to be believers and acknowledged the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the Messenger of Allah. However, their words were insincere, and their actions proved that they were liars. The verse emphasizes that Allah is aware of the true status of the hypocrites and their false claims, and that their lies will be exposed. The verse serves as a warning to those who pretend to be something they are not and reminds believers to be sincere in their faith and actions.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: And they have been commanded no more than this: There is no god except Allah; indeed, they were, in that, too, disobedient.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the simplicity and clarity of the message of the prophets, which is the oneness of God. The verse suggests that despite this clear message, people have still chosen to disobey and reject the message, indicating a deliberate and persistent rejection of God's commandments. The verse serves as a reminder of the fundamental principle of the oneness of God and the importance of submitting to His will, and warns of the consequences of disobedience.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they were convinced and then they disbelieved, so a seal was placed upon their hearts, therefore they do not understand.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who initially believed in God's message but then rejected it, and as a result, a seal was placed upon their hearts, preventing them from understanding the truth. The verse suggests that once a person rejects faith, their heart becomes hardened, and they become unable to comprehend the truth. This serves as a warning to those who reject faith, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of remaining true to their beliefs.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when I saw them, I saw that their forms were like the forms of the people of Paradise, and they were talking and their voices were like the voices of the people of Paradise. It seemed as if they were the enemies of God, who had been defeated and were being punished.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet's vision of a group of people who appeared to be the inhabitants of Paradise, with their beautiful forms and peaceful voices. However, the verse also suggests that they were in fact the enemies of God, who had been defeated and were being punished. The vision serves as a reminder that appearances can be deceiving and that one's true nature and actions will ultimately be revealed. It also highlights the importance of living a righteous life and being mindful of one's relationship with God.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it was said to them, 'Bow down to the Messenger of Allah and beg for his forgiveness,' they turned arrogant and their heads were lowered, and they were not humble.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers when they were asked to submit to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and seek his forgiveness. Instead of humbling themselves and submitting, they became arrogant and refused to do so, indicating their lack of faith and unwillingness to accept the truth. The verse highlights the importance of humility and submission to the will of God, and serves as a warning to those who are too proud to submit to the commandments of God.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a generation before them, but they did not perceive the warning. And how can they perceive a warning when a messenger from among them came to them, but they denied him? Indeed, We destroyed the generations of old, but they did not believe in their messengers. And how can they believe in the One who is not yet sent to them? And thus We have made the wrongdoers lose their way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cycle of destruction and denial that has occurred throughout human history. God has sent many messengers to guide people, but they have consistently been rejected and denied. The verse emphasizes that the people of the past did not believe in their messengers, and as a result, they were destroyed. The verse then asks how the people of the present can believe in a messenger who has not yet been sent to them. The final sentence suggests that the wicked will continue to be misguided and lost.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: And those who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they desert him.' Indeed, the treasuries of the heavens and the earth belong to Allah, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who criticize the Prophet's companions for their financial support, suggesting that they should not spend on them until they desert the Prophet. The verse responds by emphasizing that the treasuries of the heavens and the earth belong to God, indicating that all wealth and resources ultimately belong to Him. The verse then highlights the ignorance of the hypocrites, who fail to understand that the Prophet's companions are not seeking material gain but are instead motivated by their faith and devotion to God. The verse serves as a reminder that true believers should not be deterred by the criticism of others but should continue to support the cause of God and His Messenger.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, 'If we return to Medina, the honor will be removed from us. They are dishonored. They will be humiliated.' Indeed, they will be defeated,
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reaction of the disbelievers when they were forced to leave Medina. They felt dishonored and humiliated, and they feared that returning to the city would mean losing their power and status. The verse indicates that their fears were well-founded, as they would indeed be defeated and lose their honor. The verse also highlights the contrast between the disbelievers, who are described as 'dishonored' and 'humiliated', and the believers, who are described as 'honored' and 'victorious'.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not let your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah and not allowing worldly possessions or children to distract from this remembrance. The verse warns that those who prioritize material wealth and family over their relationship with Allah will ultimately be the losers in the afterlife. The verse encourages believers to keep their priorities straight and not let worldly attachments get in the way of their devotion to God.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend [in charity] from what We have provided you before death reaches one of you and he says: 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so that I may give in charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of charity and encourages believers to give generously from what God has provided them before death comes. The verse describes a scenario where a person, realizing that death is near, regrets not having done enough good deeds and wishes for a brief reprieve to perform charitable acts and become among the righteous. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to prioritize charity and good deeds in their lives, as they will be held accountable for their actions in the afterlife.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And indeed, We will not delay the punishment until they have exhausted their term, for Allah is aware of what they do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of human actions and the fact that He will not delay punishment for those who deserve it. The phrase 'they have exhausted their term' implies that the punishment will come when their time is up, indicating a sense of inevitability and finality. The verse serves as a warning to those who are engaged in wrongdoing, reminding them that God is aware of their actions and will bring them to account.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Glory be to Allah, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, and praise be to Him. He has power over all things, and to Him all things are returnable.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness and power of Allah, the Creator of the universe. The phrase 'Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth' highlights His sovereignty and control over all creation. The phrase 'and to Him all things are returnable' suggests that everything in the universe, including all living things, will ultimately return to Allah, indicating a sense of accountability and responsibility for one's actions in this life. The verse encourages believers to acknowledge and praise Allah's glory and power, and serves as a reminder of the eventual return to Him.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a believer. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's role as the creator of all human beings, and how, despite this common origin, people have differing beliefs. The verse highlights the duality of human nature, with some individuals choosing disbelief and others choosing belief. The verse serves as a reminder that God is aware of all human actions and that our ultimate accountability is to Him. It encourages self-reflection and the pursuit of righteousness, as our choices have consequences in this life and the hereafter.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in truth, and We have made them well-proportioned.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the magnificence and harmony of God's creation, particularly in the way the heavens and the earth and everything in between are proportionate and balanced. The verse is a reminder of God's power and wisdom in creating the universe and all that exists within it, and serves as a call to reflect on and appreciate the beauty and complexity of creation.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: And He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare, and Allah is Knowing of the subtleties, the Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness. He is aware of everything in the heavens and the earth, including the hidden and the manifest, the subtle and the overt. The verse serves as a reminder that nothing can be hidden from God, and that He is fully aware of all human thoughts, actions, and intentions. It is a call to mindfulness and a reminder to live a life of integrity, as everything will be accounted for in the hereafter.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, We have sent to them prophets, but they denied them, and We destroyed them. Will they not then believe in the meeting with their Lord? Indeed, We have destroyed the states of the sinners.
interpretation: The verse highlights the pattern of denial and disbelief that has been consistent throughout human history. Despite the numerous prophets and signs sent by God, people have continued to reject the message and deny the truth. The verse serves as a reminder that the consequences of such denial and disbelief are severe, as seen in the destruction of entire communities. The verse also emphasizes the certainty of the meeting with God and the accountability that comes with it. The verse ends with the reminder that God is the ultimate authority and judge, and that He will not be mocked.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: And they think that they will not be resurrected (on the Day of Judgment). Say (O Muhammad SAW): "Yes, by my Lord, certainly, you will be resurrected, then you will be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah."
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' skepticism about the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. The verse tells the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to assure them that they will indeed be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds. The verse emphasizes that this is not only a possibility but a certainty, as it is easy for Allah to resurrect the dead and bring them to judgment. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, reminding them that their actions have consequences and that they will be held responsible for them in the afterlife.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: And believe in Allah and the Messenger and the Light that We have sent down, and Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of faith in God and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the revelation sent down to him. The phrase 'the Light that We have sent down' refers to the Qur'an, which is considered a light that guides people from darkness to light and provides guidance and wisdom. The verse also underscores God's knowledge and awareness of human actions and their consequences, serving as a reminder of the accountability of individuals for their deeds in this life and the hereafter.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: On a Day when they will be gathered together, (all) that they were wont to mock at!
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Judgment when all people will be gathered together and the things they used to mock at will be the very things that will be their undoing. It serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of the idea of the Day of Judgment and the idea of being held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the consequences of not taking it seriously.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally, and what an evil destination!
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject God's signs and deny the truth. They will be the companions of the Fire, indicating that they will be punished in Hell. The word "khaleed" which means "eternally" emphasizes that their punishment will never end.
