The phrase "wa bi's al-maseer" which means "and what an evil destination!" expresses the severity of their fate and the regret they will feel in the afterlife. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's existence and the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, but if you turn away, then Our messenger has already fulfilled his duty.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to God and His Messenger. The verse addresses the believers, reminding them that their obedience to God and His Messenger is a fundamental aspect of their faith. The verse also serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), stating that even if they refuse to listen, the Prophet has still fulfilled his duty of conveying the message. The verse highlights the responsibility of the Prophet as a messenger and the accountability of the believers in following his teachings.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: There is no god but Allah, and upon Allah the believers should rely.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the importance of relying on Him. It stresses that Allah is the only one worthy of worship and that believers should put their trust in Him alone. It serves as a reminder that true faith lies in recognizing and acknowledging the greatness and power of Allah, and that believers should seek guidance and support from Him in all aspects of their lives.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. And if you pardon them and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, warning them that their spouses and children can be their enemies, and they must be cautious of them. The verse emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and pardoning those who wrong us, even within our own families. It reminds us that by forgiving others, we are not only showing mercy, but also emulating Allah's forgiveness and mercy. The verse encourages us to overlook the faults of others and to forgive them, just as Allah forgives us.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah - with Him is a great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly possessions and children, and how they can lead to spiritual distractions and temptations. The true reward lies with God, and one should not be too attached to material things. Instead, one should focus on seeking spiritual growth and closeness to God, which will lead to a greater reward in the afterlife.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves into destruction, and do good. Indeed, Allah loves not the extravagant.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of spending in the way of God and doing good deeds, while also warning against extravagance and wastefulness. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid engaging in behavior that may lead to their own destruction. The phrase 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' suggests that one should not engage in acts that are harmful or destructive, whether physically, emotionally, or spiritually. Instead, believers are encouraged to focus on doing good deeds and spending in the way of God, which is seen as a form of worship and a means of purifying one's soul. The verse concludes by emphasizing that God does not love those who are extravagant or wasteful, suggesting that humility and moderation are important virtues in Islam.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you lend unto Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you, and Allah is Most Appreciative, All-Forbearing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the concept of 'qard hasan', or a goodly loan, which refers to any act of kindness, charity, or good deed that is done for the sake of God. The verse promises that if one lends unto God a goodly loan, He will multiply it and forgive the person's sins. The verse emphasizes God's appreciation and forbearance, indicating that He is always willing to forgive and reward those who do good deeds and act with kindness. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of doing good deeds and the rewards that come with them, as well as the mercy and forgiveness of God.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which encompasses all people, regardless of their backgrounds, and serves as a reminder that the Prophet's teachings are a source of guidance and compassion for all humanity, not just for a select few.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet! When you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for their [prescribed] waiting period and count the waiting period accurately, and fear Allah, your Lord, and do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave except in case they commit open immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allah, and whosoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged his own soul. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslim community, instructing them on the proper procedures for divorce. The verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the waiting period (iddah) for divorce, which is a period of time during which the wife remains in her husband's house, and the husband provides for her. The verse also emphasizes the importance of counting the waiting period accurately, indicating that the husband must provide for his wife during this time. Additionally, the verse prohibits the husband from forcing his wife to leave her home unless she has committed open immorality. The verse concludes by reminding the believers that these limits are set by Allah and that transgressing them will result in harm to one's own soul. The verse also suggests that there may be future consequences for those who disobey these limits, but the specifics of those consequences are left unclear.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: And when their term came, they were surprised, and they were in a state of panic. They were told, 'Enter the gate prostrate and say, "Repent!" that your Lord may have mercy upon you.'
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the destruction of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah. The people were taken by surprise when their time was up, and they were in a state of panic. They were given a chance to repent and were told to enter the gate of the city prostrate, acknowledging their sin and seeking mercy from God. The verse highlights the importance of repentance and the mercy of God, who is always willing to forgive those who turn to Him in sincere repentance.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And He provides for him from sources he never could imagine. And whosoever puts his trust in Allah, sufficient is Allah for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has set a measure for everything.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's provision and care for His servants, highlighting that He provides for them from sources they could never imagine. The verse also underscores the importance of trust in God, reminding believers that He is sufficient for them and will fulfill their needs. Finally, the verse affirms God's sovereignty and control over all things, stating that He has set a measure for everything, indicating that He is the One who determines what happens in the world and that everything is subject to His will.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse refers to those who pray to God for good fortune in both this life and the afterlife, while also seeking protection from the punishment of Hell. The verse highlights the importance of seeking God's guidance and protection, as well as the belief in the afterlife and the consequences of one's actions. It serves as a reminder that true happiness and success come from seeking God's pleasure and avoiding sin, and that one should strive for a life of righteousness in order to achieve ultimate success in the afterlife.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: That is the command of Allah which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah - He will remove his sins and increase his reward.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of following God's commandments, which are a source of guidance and wisdom for believers. The verse promises that those who fear God and follow His commandments will have their sins forgiven and their rewards increased. The verse also highlights the dual nature of obedience to God, where not only will the believer be rewarded in the Hereafter, but also in this life, they will be protected from the negative consequences of their sins. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to live a life in accordance with God's will, and to be mindful of their actions and their impact on their spiritual and moral well-being.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, and give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and the destruction of crops. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience during these trials, and assures the believers that they will receive good news if they remain patient and faithful. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and hardships faced in life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith, and that those who persevere will be rewarded.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: And God has punished them for their wrongdoing, (and it is said unto them): 'Taste the punishment of burning!',
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment that God has inflicted on those who have committed wrongdoing. The punishment is described as 'burning', indicating intense suffering and pain. The use of the word 'taste' emphasizes the idea that the punishment is a direct consequence of their actions, and that they must now endure the suffering that they have brought upon themselves. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's justice.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: Messenger! Proclaim what has been revealed to you from your Lord. If you do not do it, you will not have conveyed His message. God will protect you from the people. Indeed, God will not guide the disobedient people.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) conveying the message of God to the people. The verse warns the Prophet that if he does not convey the message, he will not have fulfilled his responsibility as a messenger of God. The verse also assures the Prophet of God's protection and support in his mission. The verse also warns that God will not guide those who are disobedient and reject the message of God.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: Allah is the one who created seven heavens and the like of the earth; the command descends among them, to know that Allah has power over everything, and that Allah has encompassed everything in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and knowledge, emphasizing that He is the creator of multiple heavens and earths. The phrase 'the command descends among them' refers to the angels who carry out Allah's commands in each heaven, demonstrating His power and control over all things. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, and encourages believers to trust in His plan and wisdom.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and questions him why he is prohibiting something that Allah has made lawful for him, just to please his wives. The verse highlights the importance of following Allah's commands and not giving in to personal desires or the desires of others when they go against Allah's will. The verse also emphasizes Allah's forgiving and merciful nature, indicating that even if one makes a mistake, Allah is always ready to forgive and show mercy to those who repent and turn back to Him.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory granted by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims, and serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers. The phrase 'a clear victory' signifies a decisive and evident triumph, while 'a manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is clear and obvious to all. The verse emphasizes God's role as the ultimate authority and guide, and serves as a reminder of the responsibility of the believers to live according to God's commandments and guidance.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And indeed, the Prophet has come to some of his wives with a Hadith (a narrative) which displeased them, so when he informed them of it, they became angry and disapproved of it, and Allah made it known to him. [The Prophet] said, "I have not brought it on myself, but it has been revealed to me."
interpretation: This verse describes an instance where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received a revelation from Allah through the angel Gabriel, which displeased some of his wives. They became angry and disapproved of it, but the Prophet clarified that he had not brought the revelation upon himself, but it was revealed to him by Allah. The verse highlights the Prophet's humility and submission to Allah's will, as well as the importance of accepting and following the guidance revealed by Allah, even if it may be difficult or challenging.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: Indeed, they have deviated from the truth, for their hearts have been sealed, and they have been deaf and blind to the remembrance of Allah, and they have been pretending to be righteous, but they are not. Indeed, Allah is the Guardian of the believers, and Gabriel and the righteous angels are their allies after that.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the state of those who have turned away from the truth and have become deaf and blind to the remembrance of Allah. Their hearts have been sealed, and they have been pretending to be righteous, but in reality, they are not. The verse highlights the contrast between those who have turned away from the truth and those who have remained faithful to Allah. The believers have been given the assurance that Allah is their Guardian, and they have the support of Gabriel and the righteous angels. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have strayed to return to the path of righteousness and to seek the protection and guidance of Allah.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human hearts, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and underscores the idea that human beings are never alone, and that God is always with them, aware of their thoughts, feelings, and actions.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, severe and powerful, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do as they are commanded.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting oneself and one's family from the Fire of Hell, which is fueled by people and stones. The verse describes the angels who are responsible for guarding Hell as 'severe and powerful', indicating their strength and authority. The verse also highlights the obedience of these angels to God's commands, emphasizing that they do not disobey Him in what He orders them to do. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their actions and to strive to live a righteous life in order to avoid the punishment of Hell.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who have disbelieved, do not prostrate to Allah, indeed you will not succeed.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who have disbelieved and warns them that they will not succeed in their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the futility of their actions and the certainty of their failure. The use of the word 'prostrate' specifically refers to the act of submitting to God in prayer, implying that the disbelievers will not be able to truly submit to God and will therefore not succeed in their disbelief. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of disbelief.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, turn to Allah in sincere repentance, perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed between their hands and their hearts, and they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us, indeed You are over all things capable.'
interpretation: This verse calls on believers to repent and turn to Allah, seeking His forgiveness and guidance. The verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance, using the Arabic word 'nasuh' to convey the idea of turning back to Allah with a genuine desire to change one's ways. The verse also highlights the promise of reward for those who repent and believe, describing a Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. The verse describes a scene of paradise, where the believers' light will proceed between their hands and their hearts, indicating a state of spiritual clarity and peace. The verse ends with the believers' supplication to Allah, asking Him to perfect their light and forgive their sins, acknowledging His power and ability to do so.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh upon them. Their ultimate abode is Hell, a hapless journey's end.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and commands him to struggle against the disbelievers and hypocrites. The Arabic word 'jaahada' means to strive or struggle, and in this context, it means to confront and challenge those who reject God's message. The verse also instructs the Prophet to be harsh upon them, indicating that he should not compromise or show leniency towards those who reject God's message. The ultimate destination of those who reject God's message is Hell, which is described as a 'hapless journey's end', indicating that it is a place of eternal punishment and regret.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: And God presents an example of those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were both under two righteous servants of Our servants, but they betrayed them and were not helped by their faith. And it was said: 'Enter the Fire with the entering.
interpretation: The verse presents an example of those who disbelieved and their fate. The wife of Noah and the wife of Lot were the wives of two righteous servants of God, but they themselves were not believers. Despite being in close proximity to righteous people, they were not influenced by their faith and instead rejected it. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and choose to disbelieve, reminding them of the consequences of their choice. The phrase 'Enter the Fire with the entering' is a reference to the punishment that awaits those who reject faith and live a life of disobedience to God's commands.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And Allah presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse presents an example of faith and righteousness, highlighting the wife of Pharaoh's belief in God and her desire to be close to Him. She recognizes God's power and authority and seeks refuge in Him from Pharaoh's tyranny and the injustices of her people. The verse emphasizes the importance of faith and the pursuit of righteousness, encouraging believers to seek a close relationship with God and to seek refuge in Him from the evils of the world.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into her from Our spirit and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was one of the devout ones.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the virtues of Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her devotion to God. The verse emphasizes Mary's chastity and her faith in God's words and scriptures. The phrase 'We blew into her from Our spirit' is interpreted as a reference to the Holy Spirit, indicating that Mary was chosen by God to bear His son, Jesus. The verse highlights the special relationship between Mary and God, and serves as an example of her righteousness and devotion.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He created death and life, that He may test you, which of you is the best in deed.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and wisdom in creating both death and life, and how He uses them to test humanity. The verse suggests that the purpose of this test is to determine who among humanity is the best in their actions and deeds. The verse highlights the idea that life and death are both part of God's plan and that they are both means by which God evaluates human behavior and rewards or punishes accordingly.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: It is He who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency, that you may be aware of the benevolence of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever watchful over His servants.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and wisdom of God in creating the seven heavens in layers, indicating the complexity and harmony of the universe. The verse also highlights God's attribute of being merciful and all-watchful, suggesting that God's creation is not haphazard but rather a deliberate act of mercy, and that God is always aware of His servants and their actions.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then he turned to their messenger and said, 'Return to your Lord and ask for forgiveness for your sins, for they have become insolent in their pride.',
interpretation: The verse describes a dialogue between the prophet Moses and the Pharaoh. The Pharaoh, who had been oppressing the Israelites, is being advised by Moses to seek forgiveness from God for his sins. The verse highlights the Pharaoh's arrogance and pride, which led him to refuse to listen to Moses' message and instead, he asked Moses to go back to his Lord and ask for forgiveness for his sins. The verse serves as a reminder of the dangers of pride and arrogance and the importance of humbling oneself before God.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles for the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: The verse describes how God has decorated the nearest heaven with lamps, which are actually missiles that will be used to punish the devils. The verse also mentions that God has prepared a severe punishment, described as the Blaze, for the devils. The verse suggests that the devils are trying to mislead humans and that God is warning them of the consequences of their actions. The use of the word 'nearest' heaven suggests that there are multiple heavens, and the fact that the lamps are missiles suggests that the punishment will be severe and swift.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: And for those who disbelieve, their Lord is Fire, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: The verse describes the fate of those who reject God's message and choose to disbelieve in Him. Their Lord, the one they reject, is described as 'Fire', symbolizing the punishment they will face in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the severity of their destination, describing it as 'wretched', indicating that their choice to disbelieve has led them to a state of eternal suffering. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's existence and reminds them of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with the true appraisal, for on the Day of Resurrection the earth will be destroyed, and the mountains will be blown away, and the mountains will be blown away.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mistake of the disbelievers in not giving Allah the respect and worship He deserves. The verse warns that on the Day of Resurrection, the earth and mountains will be destroyed, and the disbelievers will face the consequences of their denial of Allah's greatness. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of humanity for their actions and the importance of recognizing and worshiping Allah as the one and only God.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various trials, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and fruits. However, the verse also reassures the believers that they will be rewarded for their patience and perseverance in the face of these trials. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials and hardships of life are a means of purification and a test of one's faith, and that the patient ones will be rewarded with a better life in the Hereafter.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They said, 'We have been forbidden (from fighting) because of a promise made to a king, for we have been fed up with fighting.
interpretation: The verse describes the excuses made by the disbelievers of Mecca when they were called to fight against the Muslims. They claimed that they had made a promise to a king not to fight, and that they were tired of fighting. The verse suggests that this was just an excuse, as they were actually motivated by a desire to avoid the risk and hardship of battle. The verse serves as a reminder that those who reject the call to righteousness will come up with all sorts of excuses to justify their disobedience.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they say, 'If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: The verse describes the regret and remorse of those who have been condemned to Hell, lamenting their failure to listen to the truth and their inability to use their reason to comprehend the signs of God. They recognize that their fate could have been different if only they had been receptive to the message of the prophets and had used their intellect to understand the truth. The verse serves as a warning to those who are still alive, encouraging them to listen to the message of God and to use their reason to comprehend the signs of God, lest they suffer the same fate as those who have gone before them.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: And they recognize their sins, so they are despicable in the sight of their Lord, (and) they have fallen into disgrace.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have committed sins and are aware of their wrongdoing. They are ashamed of their actions and are humiliated in front of God. The verse suggests that their sin has caused them to lose their dignity and respect, both in their own eyes and in the eyes of others. The phrase 'so they are despicable in the sight of their Lord' implies that their sin has caused a rift between them and God, and they are no longer in a state of grace or favor with Him. The final phrase, 'and they have fallen into disgrace' suggests that their sin has led to a loss of status and reputation, both in this life and in the hereafter.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and great reward.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of having fear of God in one's heart, even when no one is watching. This kind of fear leads to forgiveness and a great reward in the afterlife. It emphasizes the idea that true faith is not just about outward appearances, but also about the inner state of the heart. The verse encourages believers to cultivate a deep sense of spirituality and to strive for righteousness in all aspects of their lives, knowing that God is always watching and aware of their thoughts and actions.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And they plotted and planned, but their plot was known to God, even before they had fully hatched their plan.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who were plotting and planning to do something, possibly to harm others or to commit an evil act. The verse suggests that their plan was known to God even before they had fully hatched it, implying that God is all-knowing and aware of everything that is happening and will happen. The verse serves as a reminder that our plans and actions are not hidden from God, and that we will be held accountable for our actions.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge and proximity to humanity. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whispers of human beings, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also underscores God's nearness to humanity, using the metaphor of the jugular vein to convey the idea that God is closer to us than our own blood flowing through our veins. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and should inspire a sense of accountability and humility in human beings.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: It is He who has made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its valleys and eat from His provision, and to Him is the return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and dominion over the earth and everything in it. The phrase 'He made the earth subservient to you' signifies that humans have been given dominion over the earth and all its resources. The verse encourages people to explore and benefit from the earth's resources, but also to remember that everything ultimately belongs to God and will return to Him. The phrase 'to Him is the return' is a reminder of the eventual return to God and the accountability for our actions in this life.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Have We not made the earth a cradle for you, and the sky a canopy, and We have held back the raging winds so that they do not blow except by Our leave, and We have sent the fertilizing winds, then We could make the earth a lifeless thing, how then would you be brought up again after destruction?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and control over the natural world. The verse describes the earth as a cradle and the sky as a canopy, indicating God's protection and care for humanity. The verse also mentions the raging winds that are held back by God's leave, and the fertilizing winds that are sent to bring life to the earth. The verse ends with a rhetorical question, asking how humanity would be brought up again after destruction, suggesting that God has the power to both create and destroy. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and humanity's dependence on Him.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Have you seen the one who has taken his desires as his god? Will you be satisfied with him as a judge?
interpretation: This verse speaks about people who have allowed their desires and passions to become their ultimate authority, rather than submitting to the will of God. The verse suggests that such individuals have effectively made their desires their 'god', and are relying on them for guidance and direction. The verse then asks the rhetorical question of whether such a person would be satisfied with their desires as a judge, implying that such a person would not be a reliable or trustworthy authority. The verse serves as a warning against allowing one's desires to become the primary source of guidance in life, and instead encourages submission to God and His revelation.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And indeed, those before them had lied, but how (awful) was their lying!
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers who rejected the prophets and their messages. The verse implies that the disbelievers' lies and denial of the truth will have severe consequences, and their actions will be met with God's wrath. The use of the word 'كذب' (kadhaba) meaning 'lied' emphasizes the gravity of their offense and suggests that their deception was deliberate and intentional. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and instead choose to follow their own desires and false beliefs.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with the true appraisal, for on the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will be in His grip, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Indeed, the Reckoning will be an easy affair for the Most Merciful.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the power and greatness of Allah, highlighting that on the Day of Judgment, the entire earth and heavens will be under His control, and He will be the sole authority. The verse also underscores the idea that the judgment will be straightforward and straightforward for Allah, who is the Most Merciful, indicating that He will be merciful to His creation while still upholding justice and accountability.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: And none can aid you against Allah, [for] indeed, Allah is a witness over what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the powerlessness of any opposition against God's will and plan. No one can protect or aid those who reject God's message and instead choose to oppose Him. The verse also highlights the all-knowing nature of God, who is a witness to everything that humans do, and nothing escapes His knowledge. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not fear persecution or opposition, as God is always watching and will ultimately bring justice.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'It is He who has produced you and has given you hearing and sight and hearts, little are you grateful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's role as the creator and sustainer of humanity. The verse highlights three specific senses that God has given humans - hearing, sight, and the ability to think and understand (represented by the heart). The verse ends with a statement that despite all these blessings, humans are often ungrateful for what they have been given. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and generosity and humanity's responsibility to be grateful for what they have been given.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be, and Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His knowledge of all human actions. It suggests that God is always with His creation, watching over them and aware of their deeds. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always present and aware of human actions, and that He sees and knows everything that people do, whether good or bad. It encourages people to be mindful of their actions and live a righteous life, as they are always being watched by God.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?
interpretation: The verse refers to the disbelievers' skepticism and mocking of the believers' belief in the promise of God's punishment. The disbelievers ask when this promised punishment will come to pass, suggesting that they do not believe in its imminence or authenticity. The verse serves as a reminder that God's timeline is not the same as humanity's and that His punishment will come at an unexpected time, as stated in the previous verse.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Indeed, the knowledge is with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by Allah to inform the people that knowledge and wisdom come only from Allah. The Prophet's role is to convey the message clearly, as a warning to those who are heedless of Allah's signs. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the limitation of human knowledge and the need to seek guidance from Allah, the only source of true wisdom.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: And when they saw Our punishment, they said: 'This is nothing but a spell of bewitchment!'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the disbelievers when they saw the punishment that came to them. They attributed the punishment to magic or bewitchment, rather than acknowledging it as a sign of God's power and wrath. The verse highlights the denial and arrogance of those who refuse to believe in God's message and His punishment, and serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and choose to disbelieve.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Have you seen that which your Lord has sent down to you of your Lord's punishment?"
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by Allah to ask his people if they have seen the punishment that Allah has sent down upon them. The verse suggests that the punishment is a consequence of their disbelief and rejection of Allah's signs and messengers. The verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers that Allah's punishment is imminent and that they should take heed of the warning signs that Allah has sent them. The verse also emphasizes the idea that Allah's punishment is not limited to this life, but will also extend to the Hereafter, where the disbelievers will face an even greater punishment.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful, we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. So, you will come to know who it is that is in clear error.'
interpretation: The verse is a response to the disbelievers who questioned the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) belief in Allah. The verse emphasizes the belief in Allah's mercy and the Prophet's reliance on Him. The verse also contains a warning to the disbelievers that they will come to know who is in clear error, implying that those who reject Allah's message will be punished. The verse highlights the importance of faith in Allah and His mercy, and serves as a reminder to the disbelievers of the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Have you seen that which your Lord has sent down to you of sustenance?"
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad, commanding him to ask his people if they have seen the provision that God has sent down to them. The verse is reminding the people of the blessings and provision that God has given them, and encouraging them to be grateful and appreciative of what they have been given. The use of the word "sustenance" (ma'wa) is significant, as it encompasses not only physical sustenance, but also spiritual and emotional nourishment. The verse serves as a reminder to the people to recognize and appreciate the blessings in their lives, and to acknowledge that everything they have is a gift from God.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: By the pen and what they write.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance of writing and the power of the written word. The pen is a symbol of knowledge, creativity, and expression, and the verse suggests that what is written has the power to shape reality and influence the world. In this context, the verse is often interpreted as a reference to the Qur'an itself, which is seen as a divine revelation that has the power to guide and transform human lives.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward that will not be denied.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the promise of a reward for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The reward is described as 'ghayr mamnun', which means 'not denied' or 'unfailing'. The verse emphasizes the certainty and abundance of the reward, suggesting that it is a promise from God that will surely be fulfilled. The verse serves as a source of encouragement and motivation for believers to continue their righteous deeds and strive for excellence in their faith.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are upon a great character.
interpretation: The verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's exceptional character, emphasizing his integrity, honesty, and compassion. It suggests that he was chosen by God for his excellent character, which made him worthy of receiving divine revelation. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to strive for similar moral excellence and to follow the Prophet's example in their personal and social lives.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind, and how many a generation, within this nation, do you not take heed?
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him of God's power and judgment. The verse warns the Prophet and his followers of the consequences of disobedience and encourages them to reflect on the past nations that were destroyed by God's punishment. The verse also emphasizes the importance of taking heed and learning from the lessons of history, in order to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past and inviting similar destruction.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Knowing of who strays from His way, and He is Knowing of the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's knowledge and awareness of all His creation, particularly in regards to those who stray from His path and those who are guided. The verse serves as a reminder that God is fully aware of the actions and intentions of all individuals and that He is aware of who is following His guidance and who is not. It also highlights the idea that God's knowledge is not limited to the present moment, but encompasses all of time, including the future. This verse encourages the reader to reflect on their own actions and intentions and to strive to be among the guided ones, as opposed to those who have strayed.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And do not approach the orphan's property except in the way of improving it until he reaches maturity.
interpretation: The verse prohibits people from approaching or touching the property of an orphan, unless it is to improve it for the orphan's benefit, until they reach adulthood. The verse emphasizes the importance of protecting the rights and property of the vulnerable, especially orphans, and ensuring that their well-being is prioritized. It is a reminder that the wealth and assets of orphans should not be exploited or misused, and that their interests should be safeguarded until they are old enough to manage their own affairs.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [while they were] unaware and defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of towns surrounding the Prophet's location, which were destroyed due to their ignorance and defiance of God's commands. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and his followers of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of heeding God's warnings.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of not worshiping any creature or object, including the sun and the moon, and instead, directing all worship to Allah, the Creator of all things. The verse highlights the fact that Allah is the sole source of guidance and the only one worthy of worship. It also serves as a warning against idolatry and the dangers of associating partners with Allah.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed many a prosperous town, and We have made it a lesson and a reminder for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and justice, emphasizing that He is capable of destroying even the most prosperous of towns, and that He does so as a lesson and reminder for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in prosperity and comfort, reminding them that their material success is not a guarantee of their salvation and that they too will be held accountable for their actions in the afterlife.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind, and there is no one who can protect them from Our punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's power and authority, highlighting the fact that no one can escape or protect themselves from His punishment. The use of the phrase 'your kind' suggests that the people being addressed are those who have been warned and have rejected the message of the prophets, and are now facing the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of God's justice and the need for people to heed the warnings of the prophets and turn to righteousness.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [which were] similar in [their] condition [to yours].
interpretation: The verse reminds the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that God has destroyed many towns in the past that were similar to Mecca, where the Prophet was living. These towns were destroyed because of their disobedience and rejection of God's messengers. The verse serves as a warning to the people of Mecca, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to accept Islam and follow the teachings of the Prophet.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the former peoples',
interpretation: The verse refers to a person who, when hearing the Qur'an, dismisses it as mere stories or legends of the past. The verse implies that such a person is not willing to accept the truth and is rejecting the message of the Qur'an without giving it due consideration. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of the Qur'an's message and encourages them to reflect on its teachings and to consider their own beliefs and actions in light of its guidance.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: Indeed, We have destroyed them as We destroyed the owners of the garden when they would not stop.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, who were punished for their wickedness and refusal to heed God's warnings. The verse emphasizes the certainty and finality of God's judgment, using the metaphor of a garden that was once beautiful but was destroyed for its owners' disobedience. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: And they will not be reprimanded
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the wicked will not be reprimanded or admonished on Judgment Day. Their punishment will be certain and severe, without the possibility of reprieve or forgiveness. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], but to all the people as a witness, and a bringer of good news and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of the Prophet's message, addressed to all people without exception. The Prophet is described as a witness, bearing witness to the truth of God's oneness and the accountability of human beings before their Creator. He is also described as a bringer of good news, as he announces the glad tidings of God's mercy and forgiveness to those who repent and believe. At the same time, he is a warner, warning those who reject God's message of the severe consequences they will face.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: And certainly We have tried you with adversity and prosperity, that you may be tried.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that God has tested the believers with both prosperity and adversity, in order to purify them and increase their faith. The verse suggests that the purpose of these trials is to assess the believers' patience, perseverance, and gratitude, and to distinguish them from those who are not truly committed to their faith. The verse serves as a reminder that the trials of life are a means of spiritual growth and that they should be embraced with patience and trust in God's plan.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: And they were followed by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. Evil is the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the consequences of the wicked and the sinners. They were cursed in this life and will be cursed on the Day of Judgment. Their ultimate destination is a wretched end, and they will suffer eternal punishment for their misdeeds.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: And indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good in deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's promise to reward those who do good deeds. The use of the word 'Miskin' (مسكين) meaning 'poor' or 'weak' suggests that the verse is specifically addressing those who may feel marginalized or oppressed. The verse reassures them that their good deeds will not go unrewarded, and that God is aware of their struggles and will provide them with a way out of their difficulties.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they have been prohibited from the tree and have been cursed.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of people who have been prohibited from a certain tree and have been cursed. The verse does not specify the reason for the prohibition or the nature of the curse, leaving it open to interpretation. However, it suggests that the people in question have been denied access to something valuable and beneficial, and are also suffering the consequences of their actions.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: And when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are lost!',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who were witnessing the destruction of their town. The phrase 'Indeed, we are lost!' expresses their shock, disbelief, and despair. It suggests that they were aware of their own sinfulness and the fact that they had brought the punishment upon themselves. The verse serves as a reminder that even in the face of calamity, people will be held accountable for their actions and that it is never too late to repent and turn to God.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [which were] similar in [corruption] to your town.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of communities similar to the one the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was addressing. The verse warns them that they will face a similar fate if they continue to reject God's message and live in disobedience to Him. The use of 'around you' emphasizes that these destroyed towns were nearby, making the warning more tangible and relevant to the listeners. The verse encourages the listeners to reflect on their own behavior and turn back to God before it's too late.
orig: بل نحن محرومون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. orig: قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون

translation: They said, 'Glory to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been destroyed by God's punishment. They acknowledge their wrongdoing and admit their sinfulness. The phrase 'Glory to our Lord' is a declaration of God's greatness and a recognition of His power and majesty. The verse highlights the idea that even in the face of destruction, the people still recognize and praise God's glory. The admission of wrongdoing is a sign of remorse and repentance, indicating that even in the face of punishment, there is still hope for redemption and forgiveness.
orig: قالوا سبحان ربنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And some of them (the towns) were made to suffer because of their sins, and some (of them) were destroyed completely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of sin and disobedience. The use of the word 'some' indicates that not all towns were destroyed, suggesting that some were spared due to their righteousness. The phrase 'made to suffer' implies a gradual punishment, while 'destroyed completely' indicates a sudden and total destruction. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather a consequence of one's actions. It also emphasizes the importance of living a righteous life to avoid such punishment.
orig: فأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتلاومون

translation: They said, 'Woe to us! We have indeed been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who have been destroyed by God's punishment. They acknowledge their wrongdoing and express remorse for their actions. The use of the word 'woe' emphasizes their regret and sorrow. The verse highlights the consequences of sin and the importance of recognizing and acknowledging one's mistakes.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا إنا كنا طاغين

interpretation: The verse speaks about the hope and optimism that believers should have in the face of adversity. The first part of the verse, 'And perhaps our Lord will substitute for us something better than it', suggests that even in the midst of hardship, God may replace it with something better. The second part of the verse, 'Indeed, we are directed towards our Lord', emphasizes the importance of focusing on one's relationship with God and striving to live a righteous life, regardless of the challenges that may come. The verse encourages believers to have faith in God's plan and to trust that He will guide them towards a better outcome.
orig: عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون

translation: And the punishment of this world is less than the punishment of the Hereafter, would that they knew!
interpretation: The verse highlights the difference between the punishment in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter. The punishment in this world is relatively less severe compared to the punishment that awaits those who are unjust and disbelieving in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them that the punishment they face in this world is only a fraction of what they will face in the Hereafter if they do not repent and change their ways. The verse also emphasizes the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the reality of the Hereafter, which is often ignored or denied by those who are living in sin.

The verse emphasizes the idea that the reward for good deeds is not limited to this life, but extends into the hereafter, where the righteous will enjoy unending pleasure and joy. orig: إن لكم فيه لما تخيرون

translation: Does man think that he will be left unquestioned, yet he will have a covenant that will be questioned on the Day of Recompense?
interpretation: The verse raises a rhetorical question, asking whether humanity thinks they will be exempt from judgment and accountability on the Day of Judgment. The verse emphasizes the idea that humans have a covenant with God that will be questioned and examined on the Day of Recompense, implying that individuals will be held responsible for their actions in this life. The verse serves as a reminder of the Hereafter and the importance of living a virtuous life in preparation for the Day of Judgment.

interpretation: The verse describes the Day of Judgment, when all hidden things will be revealed, and people will be called to prostrate themselves before God. However, those who have lived a life of sin and disobedience will be unable to prostrate, indicating their remorse and regret for their past actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience, reminding them of the Day of Judgment and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: يوم يكشف عن ساق ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون

interpretation: The verse describes the state of the people who were destroyed by God's punishment. Despite their state of security, they were called to prostration, a reminder that God's punishment can come at any time, even when one feels secure.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون

The verse warns that those who engage in such activities will be dragged away, indicating a sudden and forceful punishment. They lack understanding of the spiritual realm and are only guessing about what lies beyond this life. Their denial is based on their limited knowledge and lack of faith, rather than any concrete evidence. interpretation: The verse encourages believers to be patient and accept God's decree, just like the Prophet Ayyub, who remained patient during his suffering. interpretation: The verse expresses the idea that the speaker's life was spared only because of the mercy of God. The speaker acknowledges that they deserved to be punished for their wrongdoing, but instead, God showed them grace and kept them safe from destruction. This verse highlights the idea of God's mercy and grace, and how it can save individuals from the consequences of their actions. It also emphasizes the idea that one's life and well-being are a gift from God, and that one should be grateful for His blessings.

translation: And He it is Who has made me blessed, wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me prayer and poor-rate as long as I remain alive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings that God has bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the responsibility that comes with it. The verse emphasizes the importance of prayer and giving charity, which are fundamental aspects of a believer's life. The phrase 'as long as I remain alive' underscores the idea that these responsibilities continue throughout one's life, and serve as a reminder of the accountability to God. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their blessings and to use them for the greater good, and to always remember their responsibility towards God and their fellow human beings.
orig: فاجتباه ربه فجعله من الصالحين

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost cause you to lose your faith with their eyes when they hear the reminder, and they say, "Indeed, he is a madman."
interpretation: The verse describes how the disbelievers tried to make the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) doubt his own faith and mission by ridiculing him and calling him a madman. The verse highlights the psychological warfare that the disbelievers used to try to discredit the Prophet and undermine his message. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of the tactics of those who seek to mislead them and to remain steadfast in their faith.

interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophethood of Noah and his message to his people, calling them to worship only Allah and abandon polytheism. interpretation: The verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment when the righteous will be gathered around the throne of God, eager to see the King, their Lord. The verse highlights the close relationship between the righteous and God, as they are eager to be near Him and receive His blessings.
