translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of knowledge and its role in recognizing and accepting the truth. The phrase 'those who have been given knowledge' refers to those who possess a deep understanding of the Qur'an and its teachings. The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a guidance from Allah, and it leads to the path of the Exalted in Might and Praiseworthy, indicating that it is a source of guidance and enlightenment for those who seek to live a righteous life.
orig: والذين في أموالهم حق معلوم

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: للسائل والمحروم

translation: And those who are truthful in their promise to God
interpretation: The verse refers to those who are true to their covenant with God and fulfill their obligations towards Him. The phrase 'yusaddiqoon' (they confirm) emphasizes the importance of being truthful and sincere in one's commitment to God. The verse highlights the significance of keeping promises and living up to one's responsibilities, particularly in matters of faith and spirituality. It serves as a reminder that our relationship with God is built on trust and faithfulness, and that we must always strive to uphold our end of the covenant.
orig: والذين يصدقون بيوم الدين

translation: And those who are miserly with what Allah has given them of wealth, so they are not contributing to their Lord's cause.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who are stingy with the wealth that God has given them, and are not willing to spend it in the way of God. The verse implies that this behavior is a sign of their disbelief and lack of gratitude towards God's blessings. It also suggests that their reluctance to spend their wealth in the cause of God is a reflection of their lack of faith in God's promise of reward and their lack of concern for the well-being of others.
orig: والذين هم من عذاب ربهم مشفقون

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not averted from them, nor are they reprieved.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the punishment of God is inescapable for those who have earned it through their wrongdoing. The phrase 'not averted' suggests that the punishment is imminent and cannot be avoided, while 'nor are they reprieved' implies that there is no respite or postponement of the punishment. This verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God, reminding them of the certainty of His punishment and the need to repent before it is too late.
orig: إن عذاب ربهم غير مأمون

translation: And those who are patient, seeking their Lord's countenance.
interpretation: The verse highlights the quality of patience and its significance in seeking God's pleasure. The phrase 'li-furoojahum' (their Lord's countenance) implies a deep longing and yearning for God's approval and acceptance. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of adversity and challenges, and how it is a means to attain spiritual growth and closeness to God. The word 'hafizoon' (patient) is derived from the root 'hifz', which means to preserve or protect. Thus, the verse suggests that those who are patient are able to protect their faith and spiritual integrity, even in the face of hardship and temptation.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except those who repent, believe and do good deeds, for they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to the destruction of towns that were unjust. The exception is for those who repent, believe, and do good deeds. These individuals will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least, indicating that their faith and good deeds have earned them a place in Paradise, where they will be rewarded and protected from any harm.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: And those who have sought excellence after that will be the enemies (of the believers).
interpretation: The verse refers to those who seek to surpass the believers in righteousness and good deeds. The phrase 'wal-'ādūn' (the enemies) suggests that those who seek excellence in a way that opposes the believers will be considered enemies of the faith. This verse highlights the importance of humility and sincerity in one's pursuit of righteousness, as seeking to outdo others in good deeds without proper intention can lead to enmity and division within the Muslim community.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are maintained by Allâh, He takes care of them and their livelihood, and is watchful of them.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the righteous people who have placed their trust in God and are content with His decree. God, in turn, takes care of their livelihood and watches over them, ensuring their well-being in this life and the hereafter. The verse highlights the special relationship between God and the righteous, where He is their sole provider and protector. It serves as a reminder to those who trust in God and live according to His commandments, that He will always be there to support and guide them.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who are with their Lord are sustainers of the truth.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the righteous individuals who are steadfast in their faith and devotion to God. The phrase 'with their Lord' implies a close relationship between the believers and God, indicating that they are aligned with God's will and are following His commandments. The phrase 'sustainers of the truth' suggests that these individuals are not only believers but also actively uphold and support the truth of God's message. The verse emphasizes the importance of standing up for what is right and just, even in the face of adversity, and serves as a reminder that true strength lies in one's conviction and devotion to God.
orig: والذين هم بشهاداتهم قائمون

translation: And those who are maintaining their prayers, they are being kept away from their prayers.
interpretation: The verse refers to those who are consistent in their prayers and are diligent in their worship. The phrase 'they are being kept away from their prayers' suggests that despite their efforts to maintain their spiritual practice, they are facing obstacles and challenges that hinder them from fully devoting themselves to their prayers. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain committed to their faith and persevere in the face of adversity.
orig: والذين هم على صلاتهم يحافظون

translation: And those who are in the gardens of bliss.
interpretation: The verse describes the righteous individuals who are rewarded with gardens of bliss in the afterlife. The gardens are a symbol of spiritual and physical happiness, and the verse emphasizes that those who are worthy of this reward are in a state of joy and contentment. The verse also serves as a reminder to those who are living in sin and injustice, that there is a reward for good deeds and that they should strive to live a righteous life in order to achieve this reward.
orig: أولئك في جنات مكرمون

translation: And what is with those who disbelieved before, when they were commanded to prostrate themselves, they refused?
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who refused to prostrate themselves when they were commanded to do so. The verse highlights their arrogance and disobedience, and serves as a reminder that those who reject God's commands will face the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: فمال الذين كفروا قبلك مهطعين

translation: By the right hand of God, I swear, this is a noble Qur'an, in a guarded tablet
interpretation: The verse is an oath sworn by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which he invokes God's name to testify to the Qur'an's noble status and its protection from corruption or alteration. The phrase 'in a guarded tablet' suggests that the Qur'an is safely preserved and protected from human tampering or interpolation, ensuring its authenticity and reliability as a divine revelation.
orig: عن اليمين وعن الشمال عزين

translation: And every soul has a guardian over it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the idea that every individual has a guardian or a guide appointed by God to watch over them and guide them towards the right path. The guardian can be a parent, teacher, or any other person who has a positive influence on the individual's life. The verse serves as a reminder that every person has the potential to be guided towards goodness and righteousness, and that they are responsible for their own spiritual growth and development.
orig: أيطمع كل امرئ منهم أن يدخل جنة نعيم

translation: And indeed, We have created them, and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of human beings and their innermost thoughts. The use of the word 'selves' suggests that people have an innate understanding of right and wrong, and that God is aware of their thoughts and feelings. The phrase 'nearer to them than their own jugular vein' highlights God's proximity and intimate knowledge of human beings, implying that God's knowledge of them is even more profound than their own self-awareness. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and underscores the idea that humans will ultimately be held accountable for their actions.
orig: كلا إنا خلقناهم مما يعلمون

translation: And indeed, We have created the heavens and the earth and everything in between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and ability to create, as well as the ease with which He created the universe. The use of 'six days' may symbolize the idea of completion or perfection, as well as the idea that creation was a deliberate and deliberate process. The phrase 'and there touched Us no weariness' underscores God's infinite power and lack of limitations, as well as the idea that creation was effortless for Him. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and majesty, and encourages believers to reflect on the wonder and complexity of creation.
orig: فلا أقسم برب المشارق والمغارب إنا لقادرون

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy and guidance for all humanity. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form indicates that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse serves as a reminder that the purpose of prophethood is not to bring destruction or punishment, but rather to guide and support people towards a better life, spiritually and morally.
orig: على أن نبدل خيرا منهم وما نحن بمسبوقين

translation: And they will be engrossed in their games and their play, until they are confronted with their Day that they had been warned about.
interpretation: The verse describes the behavior of the disbelievers who are so engrossed in their worldly pursuits and pleasures that they neglect the warning signs of the approaching Day of Judgment. The verse suggests that they will be so absorbed in their games and play that they will be caught off guard when the Day of Judgment arrives, indicating that they will be unprepared for the reckoning and unable to defend themselves against the consequences of their actions.
orig: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

translation: They will come out of their graves as if they were bursting forth from their graves.
interpretation: The verse describes the scene of the resurrection, where people will emerge from their graves in a state of haste and urgency, as if they are bursting forth from their graves. The image conveyed is one of sudden and unexpected awakening, emphasizing the idea that the resurrection will be a dramatic and transformative event that will change the course of human history.
orig: يوم يخرجون من الأجداث سراعا كأنهم إلى نصب يوفضون

translation: And they will be exposed to the fire of Hell morning and evening, and on the day when the Hour will be established: 'Admit the groups of Gog and Magog, and take out from them the one who is weaker than the stick of wood.'
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment of those who will be thrown into Hell, where they will be exposed to fire both in the morning and evening, and on the Day of Judgment. The verse specifically mentions the 'groups of Gog and Magog', indicating that they will be among those punished. The phrase 'take out from them the one who is weaker than the stick of wood' suggests that even the weakest among them will be punished, emphasizing the severity of God's judgment. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة ذلك اليوم الذي كانوا يوعدون

translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], "Warn your people before the painful punishment comes to them."
interpretation: The verse speaks about the prophethood of Noah and his mission to warn his people of the impending punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of Noah's message and the urgency of the situation, as the punishment is described as 'painful' and imminent. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility of prophets to convey God's message and warn their people of the consequences of their actions, and the importance of heeding their warnings.
orig: إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه أن أنذر قومك من قبل أن يأتيهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, I am a clear warner.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is addressing his people, informing them that he is a clear warner, a prophet who has been sent by God to guide them to the right path. The verse emphasizes the significance of the Prophet's message and serves as a reminder to the people that they have been warned and that they must take heed of the warning and change their ways. The use of the word "clear" highlights the clarity and simplicity of the message, indicating that it is easy to understand and that there is no excuse for not following it. The verse is a reminder to believers to spread the message of Islam and to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: قال يا قوم إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: And worship Allah and fear Him and obey me
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping Allah and living a life that is pleasing to Him. The phrase 'fear Him' suggests a deep respect and awe of Allah's power and wisdom, and the word 'obey' implies a willingness to follow His commands and live according to His will. The verse serves as a reminder that true worship goes beyond mere rituals and requires a deep commitment to living a righteous life, as demonstrated by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
orig: أن اعبدوا الله واتقوه وأطيعون

translation: And He will forgive you of your sins and prolong your life, and that is a grace from Allah, for Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the mercy and forgiveness of God, who is willing to pardon the sins of those who seek His forgiveness and grant them a longer life. The verse emphasizes God's knowledge and wisdom in His decision to forgive and prolong life, indicating that His mercy is not arbitrary but rather a deliberate choice based on His infinite wisdom. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God's forgiveness is always available to those who seek it and that it is a manifestation of His grace and mercy.
orig: يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر لو كنتم تعلمون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قال رب إني دعوت قومي ليلا ونهارا

translation: And they did not appraise Allah with the true appraisal, for they said: 'Allah has not revealed anything to any human being.' Say, 'Who, then, revealed the Scripture that Moses brought as a light and guidance for the people? You [Muslims] were not present when the Scripture was revealed, nor did you witness its revelation, but We [Allah] have sent it down as a mercy.'
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who denied the revelation of the Qur'an and accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating it. The verse points out that the same people who deny the Qur'an's revelation also fail to recognize the truth of the Torah, which was revealed to Moses. The verse highlights the fact that the Qur'an is a mercy and guidance for the believers and that it is not something to be taken lightly or rejected without proper consideration. The verse serves as a reminder to those who reject the Qur'an to reflect on their own beliefs and to recognize the truth of God's revelation.
orig: فلم يزدهم دعائي إلا فرارا

translation: And indeed, I have called them to Your forgiveness, but they have put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments and become arrogant and were obstinate.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet's effort to invite people to God's forgiveness, but they refused to listen and instead, they became arrogant and obstinate. They plugged their ears and covered their ears, a metaphor for their unwillingness to hear and accept the message. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassion and mercy in calling them to forgiveness, while also emphasizing the people's stubbornness and refusal to listen.
orig: وإني كلما دعوتهم لتغفر لهم جعلوا أصابعهم في آذانهم واستغشوا ثيابهم وأصروا واستكبروا استكبارا

translation: Then I (Abraham) called upon them (the people) loudly.
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is calling out to the people, addressing them loudly and publicly, indicating a sense of urgency and importance. The use of the word 'جهارا' (jahara) emphasizes the loud and clear nature of Abraham's call, suggesting that he is not whispering or speaking softly, but rather proclaiming his message openly and boldly. This verse highlights Abraham's confidence and conviction in his message, as well as his desire to convey it to the people in a clear and unambiguous manner.
orig: ثم إني دعوتهم جهارا

translation: Then indeed, I have announced to them and I have hidden [My warning] from them.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the prophet has already warned the people of the impending punishment, but they have chosen to ignore and disregard the warning. The use of the word 'hidden' implies that the warning was not explicitly stated, but rather implied or hinted at. The verse highlights the idea that the people have been given every opportunity to repent and change their ways, but they have chosen to ignore the warning signs and continue in their sinful ways.
orig: ثم إني أعلنت لهم وأسررت لهم إسرارا

translation: And I (Abraham) said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord, indeed, He is ever forgiving.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is encouraging his people to seek forgiveness from God, emphasizing God's attribute of being ever-forgiving. The verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the possibility of God's mercy and pardon. It also underscores the idea that forgiveness is not limited to a specific time or occasion, but rather, it is always available to those who seek it.
orig: فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا

translation: The heaven is about to be rent asunder from above them, and the angels are about to cry out, 'This is your Lord's promise come true.'
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of the Day of Judgment, where the heavens are about to be torn apart and the angels are about to proclaim the fulfillment of God's promise. The verse emphasizes the imminent nature of the event and the power of God's wrath. The image of the torn heavens symbolizes the breaking of the barrier between the physical and spiritual realms, signaling the end of the world as we know it. The angels' proclamation serves as a reminder that God's promise of judgment is a certainty, and that all will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا

translation: And He will provide for you, [He] will be content with riches and sons, and He will make for you gardens and He will make for you rivers.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's provision and blessings upon His righteous servants. The verse emphasizes the abundance of God's provision, using the metaphor of riches and sons to convey the idea that God's blessings are not limited to material wealth, but also include spiritual and spiritual abundance. The mention of gardens and rivers further emphasizes the idea of abundance and prosperity. The verse serves as a reminder that God's blessings are not limited to this life, but also extend to the hereafter, and that those who live a righteous life will be rewarded with eternal happiness and peace.
orig: ويمددكم بأموال وبنين ويجعل لكم جنات ويجعل لكم أنهارا

translation: And what is with you that you do not implore Allah for victory, while you were asking for victory from your Lord?
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony of the believers' situation. Despite their belief in God's power and their request for victory, they are not imploring God for success. The verse serves as a reminder that true faith requires trust and reliance on God, and that believers should seek God's help in times of need. The verse also implies that the lack of reliance on God may indicate a weakness in faith.
orig: ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of humanity's innermost thoughts and feelings, suggesting a deep connection between the creator and the created. The verse also highlights God's proximity to humanity, indicating that He is always near and aware of their thoughts and actions. The use of the jugular vein as a metaphor for proximity underscores the idea that God's knowledge and presence are inescapable and integral to human existence.
orig: وقد خلقكم أطوارا

translation: Have you not considered how God has created the seven heavens, one above the other?
interpretation: The verse invites the reader to reflect on the majesty and grandeur of God's creation, specifically the seven heavens, which are arranged one above the other. The verse suggests that the creation of the heavens is a manifestation of God's power and wisdom, and that it is a reminder of the infinite distance between the Creator and His creation. The verse encourages the reader to contemplate the beauty and complexity of the universe and to recognize the greatness of God.
orig: ألم تروا كيف خلق الله سبع سماوات طباقا

translation: And He made the moon a light therein and made the sun a lamp.
interpretation: The verse describes God's creation of the moon and sun, emphasizing their roles as sources of light and guidance for humanity. The use of the word 'light' for the moon and 'lamp' for the sun highlights their respective functions as reflectors of divine light, with the moon providing a softer, more subtle illumination, while the sun offers a brighter, more intense light. This verse reminds us of God's power and wisdom in creating the universe and providing for humanity's needs.
orig: وجعل القمر فيهن نورا وجعل الشمس سراجا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kinds of old, the same way as We destroyed the people of the garden when they were unjust.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of communities that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the idea that God's punishment is not limited to any particular group of people, but rather, it is a warning to all communities, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا

translation: Then He will return you to it (the earth) and bring you out of it again, and bring you forth from it again.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the cycle of life and death, where God brings us forth from the earth, allows us to live our lives, and then returns us to it again. The verse emphasizes the idea that our ultimate return is to the earth, and that our time on this earth is limited and will come to an end. It serves as a reminder of our mortality and the temporary nature of our existence, and encourages us to make the most of our time and live our lives in accordance with God's will.
orig: ثم يعيدكم فيها ويخرجكم إخراجا

translation: And Allah has made the earth a habitat for you.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fact that Allah has provided humanity with the earth as a place to live and flourish. The word 'basata' (habitat) implies a sense of stability and permanence, indicating that the earth is a place where humans can settle and establish themselves. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's provision and blessings, and encourages humans to be grateful for the gift of life and the resources available to them.
orig: والله جعل لكم الأرض بساطا

translation: And indeed, We will test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient ones.
interpretation: The verse explains that God will test the believers through various means, including fear, hunger, loss of wealth and lives, and failure of crops. However, the verse also assures that those who are patient and persevering during these trials will receive good news and reward from God. The verse highlights the importance of patience and resilience in the face of adversity, and serves as a reminder that these trials are a means of purification and spiritual growth for the believers.
orig: لتسلكوا منها سبلا فجاجا

translation: And Noah said, 'My Lord, indeed they are my enemies, and they follow me because I am not wealthy, nor do they have sons, but only loss.'
interpretation: In this verse, Noah is expressing his frustration and sadness to God, explaining that his enemies are jealous of him because he is not wealthy and does not have sons to support him. Noah feels that he is being followed and oppressed by his enemies, who are motivated by envy and malice. The verse highlights the struggles that the righteous can face in a society that values material wealth and worldly success above spiritual values. It also emphasizes the importance of faith and trust in God, as Noah turns to God for support and guidance in the face of adversity.
orig: قال نوح رب إنهم عصوني واتبعوا من لم يزده ماله وولده إلا خسارا

translation: And they plotted and planned, but their plotting and planning was against themselves, and they perceived it not.
interpretation: The verse refers to the scheming and planning of the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. Despite their efforts to harm the Muslims, their plans ultimately backfired and resulted in their own downfall. The verse highlights the idea that those who seek to harm the righteous will ultimately be defeated and punished by God, and that their evil plans will ultimately turn against them.
orig: ومكروا مكرا كبارا

translation: And they say, 'Do not expose our gods and do not expose our daughters.'
interpretation: The verse refers to the reaction of the disbelievers towards the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They were asked to abandon their idols and their way of life, but they refused, saying that they did not want to give up their gods or their daughters. The verse highlights the deep-seated attachment of the disbelievers to their false deities and their reluctance to let go of their old beliefs and practices, even when faced with the truth of Islam. It also underscores the importance of the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the need for people to be willing to let go of their false beliefs and embrace the truth.
orig: وقالوا لا تذرن آلهتكم ولا تذرن ودا ولا سواعا ولا يغوث ويعوق ونسرا

translation: And indeed, they have strayed and cannot be guided aright, except a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of humanity's astrayal and their inability to find guidance on their own. The verse emphasizes that only a few individuals are guided, implying that the majority have strayed and are unable to find their way back to the right path. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance from God and adhering to His teachings in order to avoid being led astray by one's own desires and whims.
orig: وقد أضلوا كثيرا ولا تزد الظالمين إلا ضلالا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: مما خطيئاتهم أغرقوا فأدخلوا نارا فلم يجدوا لهم من دون الله أنصارا

translation: And Noah said, 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller.'
interpretation: In this verse, Noah is imploring God not to leave any disbelievers on earth, indicating that he wants God's mercy to encompass all of humanity. The verse highlights Noah's concern for the welfare of his fellow human beings and his desire for them to be guided towards the truth and avoid God's punishment. It also underscores the importance of faith in God's mercy and the belief that God's guidance is available to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs.
orig: وقال نوح رب لا تذر على الأرض من الكافرين ديارا

translation: Indeed, You will surely destroy those who are Your enemies, and they will not beget any children, or they will beget only wicked children.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's punishment on the wicked and their descendants. The verse implies that the wicked will not have children or their children will be wicked, indicating that their lineage will be cut off. The verse serves as a warning to those who oppose God and His prophets, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the powerlessness of their progeny.
orig: إنك إن تذرهم يضلوا عبادك ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفارا

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in which he seeks forgiveness from Allah for himself, his parents, and those who enter his house as believers. The verse also highlights the importance of forgiveness and the distinction between the righteous and the wicked. The phrase 'do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction' suggests that the punishment for evil deeds will be multiplied for those who refuse to repent and continue to commit injustices.
orig: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي ولمن دخل بيتي مؤمنا وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات ولا تزد الظالمين إلا تبارا

translation: Say, 'It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, "Indeed, we have heard a marvelous Qur'an."'
interpretation: The verse is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and commands him to say that he has received a revelation from God that a group of jinn have listened to the Qur'an and found it marvelous. The verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its ability to impress even the supernatural beings like jinn, who are known for their knowledge and wisdom. The verse serves as a testimony to the prophethood of Muhammad and the divine origin of the Qur'an.
orig: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا

translation: And indeed, [O Muhammad], you are guiding to a straight path. And indeed, those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. And indeed, [O Muhammad], you are not over them a controller.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a guide and a source of guidance for those who believe in Allah. The verse emphasizes that the Prophet's guidance is not limited to worldly matters, but rather it is a guidance towards righteousness and the straight path that leads to the pleasure of Allah. The verse also emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah and holding fast to Him, as it is the means by which one can truly be guided and receive the guidance of the Prophet. The verse also underscores the fact that the Prophet is not a controller over the believers, but rather a guide and a leader who shows them the way to righteousness.
orig: يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam
interpretation: This verse highlights the dignity and honor that God has bestowed upon human beings, specifically the descendants of Adam. It emphasizes the special status and responsibility that comes with being human, and serves as a reminder of the great potential and purpose that humans have in life. The verse also underscores the importance of recognizing and respecting the inherent worth and dignity of every human being, regardless of their race, gender, or background.
orig: وأنه تعالى جد ربنا ما اتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were unjust, and We gave them a punishment in the morning and at noon.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله شططا

translation: And indeed, We have believed that the humans and the jinn will say concerning Allah a lie.
interpretation: The verse suggests that humans and jinn will attribute lies to God, which is a warning to believers not to join them in their falsehood. It implies that people and jinn will accuse God of lying, which is a severe offense. The verse warns believers not to participate in such falsehood and encourages them to be truthful to God.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن تقول الإنس والجن على الله كذبا

translation: And indeed, there were men among mankind who took shelter with the jinn, but they increased them in wrongdoing.
interpretation: The verse speaks about a group of humans who sought refuge with the jinn, but instead of being helped, they were led astray and became more immersed in sin and wrongdoing. The verse highlights the negative influence of seeking refuge in other than God and the importance of relying solely on Him for guidance and protection.
orig: وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون برجال من الجن فزادوهم رهقا

translation: And they thought, as you thought, that Allah would never send a messenger.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the disbelievers underestimated the power of God and doubted the possibility of a prophet being sent to guide them. Their skepticism stemmed from their limited understanding of God's abilities and their belief that they were not accountable to a higher authority. The verse highlights the arrogance and ignorance of those who reject the idea of a divine messenger, which ultimately leads to their downfall.
orig: وأنهم ظنوا كما ظننتم أن لن يبعث الله أحدا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a source of mercy for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse underscores the Prophet's mission as one of compassion, forgiveness, and guidance, rather than one of vengeance or destruction. It serves as a reminder to Muslims that their faith should be centered on spreading love, kindness, and mercy to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs.
orig: وأنا لمسنا السماء فوجدناها ملئت حرسا شديدا وشهبا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all humanity. The verse also underscores the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, as he was sent to guide and enlighten people, rather than to condemn or punish them. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is relevant to all people, regardless of their time, place, or culture. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role as a source of guidance and mercy, and it highlights the importance of compassion and empathy in the spreading of his message.
orig: وأنا كنا نقعد منها مقاعد للسمع فمن يستمع الآن يجد له شهابا رصدا

translation: And I (Muhammad SAW) do not know but that perhaps my Lord may bring them back (to the right path) after this destruction.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses his hope that even though the towns were destroyed, their inhabitants may still have a chance to repent and turn back to God. The verse highlights the mercy and compassion of God, who may still show grace to those who have gone astray. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to always have hope in God's mercy and to never give up on those who have strayed, but to continue to pray for their guidance and forgiveness.
orig: وأنا لا ندري أشر أريد بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, as a source of mercy and guidance for all of humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their race, ethnicity, or religion. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's message and underscores the importance of spreading love, kindness, and forgiveness to all people.
orig: وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك كنا طرائق قددا

translation: And indeed, We have believed that Allah will not fail in the earth, and indeed, Allah will not fail in what He promises.
interpretation: The verse expresses the belief that God is all-powerful and will not fail in His promises. The use of the phrase 'and indeed' twice emphasizes the certainty of this belief. The first part of the verse refers to God's power and control over the earth, indicating that nothing can escape His authority. The second part of the verse emphasizes God's trustworthiness and ability to fulfill His promises. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that they should have faith in God's abilities and trust in His promises, and that they should not doubt His power and authority.
orig: وأنا ظننا أن لن نعجز الله في الأرض ولن نعجزه هربا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The verse highlights the scope of his message, which is not limited to a particular group or nation, but rather it is a universal message that encompasses all humanity. The verse also underscores the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to bring people closer to God and guide them to a righteous life. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to this world but also encompasses the hereafter, signifying the eternal nature of his teachings.
orig: وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى آمنا به فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا

translation: And We have destroyed the former generations, do you perceive them or are you unaware of them?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and justice by highlighting the destruction of past nations who were wicked and rejected God's messengers. The verse warns the current generation of the consequences of following in their footsteps and encourages them to reflect on the lessons of history. The use of the phrase 'do you perceive them' suggests that the speaker is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and asking him to ponder the fate of past nations. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to the past and that the present generation will also face consequences if they continue to reject God's message.
orig: وأنا منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون فمن أسلم فأولئك تحروا رشدا

translation: And as for the Qarun, they were destroyed by the earthquake.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the people of Qarun, who were consumed by the earthquake. The verse highlights the power of God and His ability to destroy those who are arrogant and wicked. The earthquake is seen as a manifestation of God's wrath, sent to punish those who have transgressed against Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who are proud and self-sufficient, reminding them of the fragility of their existence and the need to humble themselves before God.
orig: وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا

translation: And if they had walked on the path, We would have given them to drink of water in abundance.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the people of the town were not only unjust, but also disobedient and arrogant, refusing to follow the path that God had set for them. As a result, they were denied the blessing of abundant water, which is seen as a symbol of spiritual and material prosperity. The verse serves as a reminder that obedience to God's commandments is essential for receiving His blessings and that those who refuse to follow His path will be deprived of His favors.
orig: وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed nations before them, but they did not believe in their Messengers, so We seized them with a severe seizure.
interpretation: The verse mentions the destruction of previous nations who rejected their prophets and ignored the signs of God. The phrase 'We seized them with a severe seizure' emphasizes the sudden and intense nature of God's punishment, indicating that those who reject God's message will face severe consequences. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the fate of previous nations who met their demise for their disbelief.
orig: لنفتنهم فيه ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه يسلكه عذابا صعدا

translation: And that the mosques are Allah's, therefore do not call upon anyone with Allah.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the sanctity of mosques and prohibits the worship of anyone or anything else alongside Allah. It highlights the exclusivity of Allah's worship and warns against associating partners with Him. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the purity and sacredness of mosques and the belief in the oneness of Allah.
orig: وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا

translation: And indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger from among yourselves, who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the role he played in guiding his people. The verse highlights his ability to recite and interpret the verses of God, purify his people, and teach them the Book and wisdom. The verse also underscores the idea that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent by God to guide his people and that he was chosen from among them, indicating his close connection to his people and his understanding of their needs and struggles. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's role in guiding humanity towards righteousness and the significance of his message in the lives of believers.
orig: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only called me to worship Him, and not to associate anything with Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism, the central tenet of Islam. The verse stresses that the purpose of Prophethood is to worship God alone and to reject any form of polytheism. It highlights the belief that God is unique and peerless, and that no one should be associated with Him in worship. The verse also underscores the Prophet's role as a caller to the worship of one God, and serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and avoid any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I do not possess for you any harm or benefit, nor do I have any knowledge of the future.',
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to inform the people that he does not have the power to bring them harm or benefit. This is a reminder that the Prophet is only a messenger and does not have control over the fate of individuals. The verse also emphasizes that the Prophet does not possess knowledge of the future, indicating that he is not clairvoyant and cannot predict what will happen to people in the future. This verse serves to establish the limits of the Prophet's role and to emphasize the importance of relying on God for guidance and protection.
orig: قل إني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "I am not able to benefit or harm myself, except what Allah has willed for me. And if I had known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me. Indeed, I am not except a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is instructed by Allah to say that he has no control over his own fate, and that everything that happens to him is by the will of Allah. He also states that if he had knowledge of the unseen, he would have acquired much good and avoided harm. However, his role is limited to being a warner and a bringer of good tidings to those who believe in Allah and follow His commandments.
orig: قل إني لن يجيرني من الله أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: Except those who repent, believe and do good deeds, for them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the possibility of redemption for those who have committed wrongdoing. It emphasizes the importance of repentance, belief, and good deeds as a means of seeking forgiveness and replacing past mistakes with positive actions. The verse also underscores God's attribute of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that He is always willing to accept those who turn to Him in repentance and offer them a chance to redeem themselves.
orig: إلا بلاغا من الله ورسالاته ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا

translation: And indeed, they had seen the punishment that came to those who preceded them, and they will certainly know that the punishment is not less than what was promised.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of communities that disobeyed God and were punished as a result. The verse implies that people today should learn from the past and realize that God's punishment is not something to be taken lightly. The phrase "not less than what was promised" suggests that God's punishment is consistent and reliable, and that those who disobey will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون فسيعلمون من أضعف ناصرا وأقل عددا

translation: Say, Indeed, I know not whether what you are promised is near or if my Lord will prolong it.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded by God to inform the disbelievers that he is not aware of the exact timing of the promised punishment or when it will come to pass. The verse implies that the disbelievers were skeptical about the Day of Judgment and were questioning the Prophet about its certainty. The verse serves as a reminder that only God knows the exact timing of events and that it is not for human beings to know or question. The verse also highlights the importance of living a righteous life and being prepared for the Day of Judgment at all times.
orig: قل إن أدري أقريب ما توعدون أم يجعل له ربي أمدا

translation: And no soul perceives what has been hidden from it, so be content with your Lord's decree and be patient. Indeed, no soul will be given except what it can bear.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that humans are limited in their understanding and knowledge. The phrase 'عالم الغيب' (knowledge of the unseen) refers to the fact that there are things that are beyond human comprehension and perception. The verse encourages believers to be content with the decree of God and to be patient in the face of adversity, knowing that God will not burden a soul with more than it can bear. The verse serves as a reminder to trust in God's wisdom and justice, even when we cannot fully understand the mysteries of the universe.
orig: عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا

translation: Except for him who is granted a reprieve by the messenger, and his case is deferred to the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse speaks about the exception to the general rule of God's punishment. The verse implies that some sinners will be spared from punishment in this life and will be granted a reprieve until the Day of Judgment. The verse highlights the idea of individual accountability and the fact that everyone will eventually face judgment for their actions. It also underscores the idea that the messenger, who is divinely appointed, has the authority to grant such reprieves.
orig: إلا من ارتضى من رسول فإنه يسلك من بين يديه ومن خلفه رصدا

translation: And indeed, We have sent messages to the people of Mecca, but they have refused to believe in them, and instead, they have been confined to what they possess, and they have been obstinate in disbelief.
interpretation: The verse refers to the people of Mecca who rejected the messages of God despite the clear signs and warnings. Instead of accepting the truth, they chose to cling to their material possessions and worldly desires, and they became stubborn in their disbelief. The verse highlights the consequences of their actions, which led to their destruction and serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of rejecting God's messages.
orig: ليعلم أن قد أبلغوا رسالات ربهم وأحاط بما لديهم وأحصى كل شيء عددا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, and We have shown [them] the signs, that perhaps they might return [from their sins].
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the people of Mecca, who were familiar with the destroyed towns in their surroundings, that God's punishment is not far-fetched. The use of 'around you' emphasizes the proximity of the destroyed towns and serves as a warning to the people of Mecca that they too could face a similar fate if they do not mend their ways. The verse also highlights the purpose of the destruction, which is to encourage people to return from their sins and turn to God. The verse underscores God's mercy and desire for people to repent and change their ways, rather than face destruction.
orig: يا أيها المزمل

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قم الليل إلا قليلا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, then you are, O disbeliever, among the warned.
interpretation: The verse speaks to the disbelievers, reminding them that God has destroyed entire nations in the past for their sins and injustices. The verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers, informing them that they too will face the consequences of their actions if they do not repent and turn to God. The verse emphasizes the idea that the disbelievers are not superior to the nations that were destroyed before them and that they too will face the same fate if they continue to reject God's message.
orig: نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا

translation: Or add to creation (anew)? And (even) if We (so) will, We will reverts it to a (condition) as it were the first (time).
interpretation: The verse speaks about the power of God and His ability to create and recreate as He pleases. The verse suggests that even if God were to destroy and recreate the world, it would be as easy as the first creation. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the fact that He is the sole creator and sustainer of the universe.
orig: أو زد عليه ورتل القرآن ترتيلا

translation: Indeed, We will suffice you with a heavy word.
interpretation: The verse speaks about God's power and ability to punish those who reject His message. The 'heavy word' refers to the weight of God's punishment, which will befall those who disobey Him. The verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and refuse to submit to God's will, reminding them that God's punishment is severe and inevitable.
orig: إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا

translation: Indeed, the rising of the night is the severest and most potent and most eminent in order.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the darkness of night and how it is the most powerful and dominant force in the natural world. The verse uses the metaphor of the night to describe the power of God, indicating that just as the night envelops and overcomes everything in its path, so too does God's power encompass and overcome all things. The verse serves as a reminder of God's greatness and the insignificance of humanity in comparison.
orig: إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطئا وأقوم قيلا

translation: Indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Muslims. The verse emphasizes the clarity and manifest nature of this victory, indicating that it is a clear sign of God's favor and support for the believers. The verse serves as a reminder to the Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and to trust in God's help and support in times of difficulty.
orig: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا

translation: And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with devotion.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying God's name, and devoting oneself to Him with sincerity and dedication. It encourages the believers to cultivate a strong relationship with God and to focus their hearts and minds on Him. The verse also implies that this remembrance and devotion will lead to a deeper spiritual connection and a greater sense of peace and contentment.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك وتبتل إليه تبتيلا

translation: Lord of the east and the west; there is no god except Him, so take Him as a guardian.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over all creation, including the east and the west, indicating His omnipotence and dominion over all things. The phrase 'there is no god except Him' reinforces the idea of God's uniqueness and the fact that He is the only one worthy of worship. The verse concludes by advising believers to take God as their guardian, emphasizing the importance of seeking protection and guidance from Him alone.
orig: رب المشرق والمغرب لا إله إلا هو فاتخذه وكيلا

translation: And ignore what they say, and avoid them in a dignified manner.
interpretation: The verse advises believers to ignore the negative comments and mocking words of non-believers and to avoid engaging with them in a dignified manner, without stooping to their level or responding in kind. Instead, believers are encouraged to maintain their dignity and focus on their faith and righteous deeds, not letting the opinions of others distract them from their spiritual path.
orig: واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا

translation: And We have given you the clear victory and the manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' signifies a decisive and obvious triumph, while 'manifest triumph' implies a victory that is clear and evident to all. The verse is a reminder that God is always on the side of the believers and will grant them success and victory over their enemies, as long as they remain faithful and obedient to Him.
orig: وذرني والمكذبين أولي النعمة ومهلهم قليلا

translation: Indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity and His proximity to them. The verse emphasizes that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whisperings of human beings, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also underscores the idea that God is closer to human beings than their own vital organs, signifying His omnipresence and intimate connection with them. The verse serves as a reminder that God is always aware of human actions and thoughts, and that He is always near to guide and assist them.
orig: إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما

translation: On the day when the earth and the mountains will be in violent commotion, and the mountains will be like scattered dust.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of the end of the world, where the earth and mountains will be in chaos, and the mountains will be crushed and scattered like dust. The verse suggests a time of great upheaval and destruction, and serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the power of God.
orig: يوم ترجف الأرض والجبال وكانت الجبال كثيبا مهيلا

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) being sent as a witness over the believers, just as Prophet Moses was sent as a witness to Pharaoh. The verse highlights the importance of the Prophet's role as a witness, who is responsible for conveying the message of God and bearing witness to the truth. The verse also serves as a reminder that the Prophet is not the first to be sent by God, but rather part of a long line of prophets who were sent to guide humanity.
orig: إنا أرسلنا إليكم رسولا شاهدا عليكم كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا

translation: And the Pharaoh strayed, and We seized him with a seizure, a punishment.
interpretation: The verse refers to the Pharaoh's arrogance and disobedience, and how God punished him as a consequence. The word 'seizure' implies a sudden and forceful punishment, indicating that the Pharaoh was taken by surprise and had no time to repent or change his ways. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the power of God's justice.
orig: فعصى فرعون الرسول فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكيف تتقون إن كفرتم يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا

translation: The heaven and the earth were joined together, and We separated them, and We made the sky a roof, preventing the heaven from falling upon the earth, except that We poured down water in a measure.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of the universe by God, specifically the separation of the heaven and earth. The verse emphasizes God's power and control over the universe, as well as His mercifulness in providing a barrier between the heavens and the earth to prevent their collision. Additionally, the verse highlights the importance of water, which is essential for life on earth, and how it is a sign of God's mercy and provision for His creation.
orig: السماء منفطر به كان وعده مفعولا

translation: And indeed, this is a reminder to those who fear their Lord, that they will meet their Lord, and that He will indeed return to them what they used to do.
interpretation: The verse addresses those who fear their Lord and serves as a reminder that they will eventually meet their Lord and be held accountable for their actions. The verse emphasizes the idea of reciprocity, where every deed, good or bad, will be returned to the individual. It encourages the believers to live a righteous life, mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them in the hereafter.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows that you rise at night a little less than two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it, and the angels and the Spirit descend therein by the leave of their Lord, indeed, they are commanding beings. Indeed, this Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.

interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the wicked people will not be able to escape the punishment in the afterlife. The word 'Kalala' (كلا) is used to express negation, indicating that there is no doubt about the certainty of the punishment. The phrase 'bial-akhirati' (بالآخرة) means 'in the Hereafter', signifying that the punishment will befall them in the afterlife, not in this world. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment in the Hereafter.
orig: كلا بل لا يخافون الآخرة

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns that were older than you, so Our punishment came to them in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse highlights the destruction of towns that were older than the Prophet's (peace be upon him) time, emphasizing God's power and justice. The verse warns the disbelievers of the consequences of their actions and serves as a reminder to the believers of God's punishment and mercy. The use of 'older than you' suggests that the towns were well-established and had a long history, making their destruction even more significant. The verse also emphasizes the sudden nature of the punishment, which came without warning, reminding the reader of the certainty of God's justice.
orig: كلا إنه تذكرة

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) opponents, who were skeptical of his message and denied the possibility of resurrection. The verse informs them that God has destroyed entire nations in the past for their sins and injustices, but they did not learn from those examples. The verse serves as a warning and a reminder that God's punishment is real and inevitable for those who reject His message and continue to live in disobedience.
orig: فمن شاء ذكره

translation: And they are not remembered except that God wills it. He is the One worthy of praise and the One who forgives.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and control over all things. The phrase 'they are not remembered' refers to the fact that God is the only one who can remember and recall the deeds of human beings. The phrase 'except that God wills it' indicates that God's will is the sole determinant of what is remembered and what is forgotten. The second part of the verse highlights God's attributes of being worthy of praise and forgiveness, emphasizing His mercy and grace towards humanity.
orig: وما يذكرون إلا أن يشاء الله هو أهل التقوى وأهل المغفرة

translation: And certainly, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like carded wool.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message. The image of humans being like scattered moths and mountains being like carded wool emphasizes the powerlessness and fragility of humanity in the face of God's wrath. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical or dismissive of the idea of a Day of Judgment, reminding them that the day of reckoning is near and inevitable.
orig: لا أقسم بيوم القيامة

translation: And indeed, We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a mercy to all creation. The use of the word 'worlds' in the plural form indicates that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or nation, but rather it is a universal message that extends to all people, jinn, and other creatures. The verse highlights the Prophet's compassionate nature and his responsibility to guide humanity towards the right path. The verse also underscores the importance of the Prophet's role in bringing people closer to God and encouraging them to live a virtuous life.
orig: ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوامة

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity and His proximity to them. The phrase 'We know what their own selves whisper to them' suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and secrets of human beings, and that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also emphasizes God's nearness to humanity, using the metaphor of the jugular vein, which is the closest vessel to the heart. This nearness signifies God's omnipresence and His ability to hear and respond to human supplications. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and proximity, encouraging humans to be mindful of their actions and seek guidance from their Creator.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, and We have shown (their destruction) in various ways, that they might return (from their sins).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the destruction of towns near the Prophet's location, which serves as a reminder to those who witnessed it, of God's power and punishment. The verse highlights God's mercy in giving them the opportunity to repent and change their ways, rather than immediately destroying them. It also emphasizes the importance of learning from past mistakes and examples, and turning back to God.
orig: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه

translation: And indeed, mankind was created anxious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent anxious nature of human beings, indicating that humans are prone to worry and anxiety. This verse can be interpreted as a reminder that humans should recognize their natural disposition towards anxiety and take steps to manage it, such as seeking comfort and peace in their faith in God. It may also serve as a warning against excessive worry and anxiety, encouraging individuals to place their trust in God and cultivate a sense of inner peace.
orig: بل يريد الإنسان ليفجر أمامه

translation: The Day of Judgment will ask the sinner, 'Where are those you used to associate with?',
interpretation: The verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when each person's deeds will be judged, and those who associated with false deities will be asked where their associates are. The verse warns against the consequences of associating with false deities and serves as a reminder to focus on worshipping only Allah. It also highlights the accountability and judgment that will take place on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يسأل أيان يوم القيامة

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, then you are, O witness, a warner.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of past nations who were similar to the Quraysh, the tribe to whom the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent. The verse serves as a reminder to the Quraysh that they are not immune to God's punishment, just like the nations that came before them. The verse also emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a warner, whose duty is to remind his people of the consequences of their actions and to call them to righteousness.
orig: فإذا برق البصر

translation: And the moon has been cleft asunder
interpretation: The verse describes the miraculous event of the moon being split in two, which was a sign of God's power and a miracle for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The verse is often interpreted as a symbol of the power of faith and the ability of God to overcome seemingly impossible challenges. The image of the moon being split in two also represents the idea of something that was once whole and complete being divided, and the need for unity and wholeness to be restored.
orig: وخسف القمر

translation: And the sun and the moon are joined together.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the end of the world and the final judgment. The image of the sun and the moon being joined together symbolizes the unity of all things under God's power. The verse suggests that on the day of judgment, all things will be brought together and united under God's authority, and that there will be no escape from His wrath. The verse serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability of all human beings before God and the need to lead a virtuous life in preparation for the hereafter.
orig: وجمع الشمس والقمر

translation: And he says, 'Where is the path to the morning?'
interpretation: The verse speaks about a person who is seeking guidance and asking for the path to the morning, which symbolizes spiritual enlightenment and guidance. The question reflects the person's desire to seek a new beginning and to leave behind the darkness of ignorance and sin. The verse highlights the importance of seeking guidance and the willingness to change one's ways in order to live a righteous life.
orig: يقول الإنسان يومئذ أين المفر

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كلا لا وزر

translation: And to your Lord is the return on the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate accountability of all human beings to God on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'to your Lord' signifies the personal responsibility of each individual to their Creator, and the phrase 'on the Day of Reckoning' underscores the idea that every action, thought, and deed will be taken into account and judged by God. The verse serves as a reminder of the Hereafter and the need for self-reflection, repentance, and righteous living in preparation for the inevitable meeting with God.
orig: إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر

translation: Mankind will be destroyed on the Day of Resurrection by what they have sent ahead, and by what they have earned.
interpretation: The verse highlights the idea that human beings will be held accountable for their actions in this life, and that their ultimate destiny will be determined by their deeds. The phrase 'what they have sent ahead' refers to the good deeds and positive actions that people have done, while 'what they have earned' refers to the consequences of their negative actions. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and that we will ultimately face the consequences of our choices in the afterlife.
orig: ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر

translation: And indeed, mankind was created anxious.
interpretation: The verse highlights the inherent anxious nature of human beings, indicating that humans are prone to worry and anxiety. This verse serves as a reminder that humans should recognize this aspect of their nature and strive to overcome it by seeking guidance and peace in faith. The use of the word 'anxious' also implies a sense of restlessness and discontent, suggesting that humans are perpetually seeking something more, and that true contentment can only be found in seeking closeness to God.
orig: بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة

translation: And if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's mercy and patience in not destroying the sinners immediately. Instead, they are given a chance to repent and mend their ways. The verse also highlights the severity of the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message in the Hereafter. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.

orig: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به

translation: Indeed, We have gathered them and the Qur'an.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the gathering of all people and the Qur'an. The verse implies that the Qur'an is a gathering of all the previous revelations and that it is the final and complete word of God. The verse also suggests that all people will be gathered on the Day of Judgment, and that the Qur'an will serve as a witness against them, as it contains the truth and the final message from God. The verse emphasizes the importance of the Qur'an as the ultimate source of guidance and the final authority for all humanity.
orig: إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, then you are the descendants of those who were destroyed.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him that God has destroyed previous nations who were similar to the Quraysh, the tribe to which the Prophet belonged. The verse serves as a warning to the Quraysh, reminding them that they will face the same fate as the previous nations if they continue to reject God's message and continue their oppression and injustice.
orig: فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

translation: Then indeed, upon Us is the explanation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's role as the ultimate authority and interpreter of His revelation. The phrase 'upon Us is the explanation' suggests that the true meaning and interpretation of the Qur'an is known only to God, and that human understanding is limited. This verse serves as a reminder to believers to approach the Qur'an with humility and recognition of their own limitations, and to seek guidance from God in understanding His revelation.

interpretation: The verse emphasizes the idea that death and life are both part of God's plan to test humanity. The verse suggests that the purpose of life is not to avoid death, but to live a life that is pleasing to God and to fulfill one's duties and responsibilities to the best of one's ability. The verse also implies that the ultimate goal is to attain a good end in the afterlife, and that the test of life is not limited to the present life but extends beyond it.

translation: To your Lord is the return on that day.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the ultimate return of all creation to God on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the idea that everything will return to its source and be judged according to its deeds. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability and responsibility that comes with being a creation of God, and the need to live a life that is pleasing to Him in order to achieve a positive outcome on the Day of Judgment.
