interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that God has destroyed many towns in the past that were much stronger and more powerful than the town of Mecca, where the Prophet was living at the time. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of God, reminding them that they will face the same fate as those towns if they continue to disbelieve and oppose the will of God. The verse also highlights the power and authority of God, who is capable of destroying entire towns and nations if they disobey and disregard His commands.
orig: ولكن كذب وتولى

translation: And he went to his people, who were asleep.
interpretation: The verse describes Prophet Lot's actions after he was commanded by God to leave his wife and home in Sodom. The phrase 'he went to his people' implies that Lot's people were unaware of the impending punishment and were living in a state of spiritual ignorance. The word 'asleep' suggests that they were not only physically but also spiritually unaware of the danger they were in. The verse highlights Lot's sense of urgency and his desire to warn his people of the imminent destruction, which was about to befall them.

interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe by God. The phrase 'when it was smoke' suggests a state of chaos and disorder, which is in contrast to the ordered state of the universe as we know it today. The verse implies that God transformed the chaos into a well-ordered universe, demonstrating His power and wisdom in creating the heavens and the earth.
orig: ثم أولى لك فأولى

translation: And indeed, We have created man and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whispers of humans, indicating that nothing is hidden from Him. The verse also emphasizes God's nearness to humans, using the metaphor of the jugular vein, which is the closest vessel to the heart, signifying God's intimate connection with humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and encourages humans to be mindful of their thoughts and actions, as they are always under God's watchful eye.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own people in the past.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) people, the Quraysh, who were destroyed by the pagans. The verse serves as a reminder of God's power and judgment, and how He can punish those who reject His message and oppose His prophets. The verse also highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) grief and sadness at the loss of his people, despite their rejection of his message.
orig: ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى

translation: Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come willingly or unwillingly.' They both said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe by God. The verse suggests that the universe was initially in a state of chaos and disorder, represented by the image of smoke. God commanded the heavens and the earth to come into existence, and they both responded willingly, indicating their submission to God's will. The verse highlights the power and authority of God as the creator of the universe, and the obedience of the creation to His command.
orig: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى

translation: And He created from them (the children of Adam) pairs, male and female, and sent them forth (into the world) in order that they might enjoy (the good things of life)
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equal nature of men and women as they were created to enjoy the good things of life. It highlights the idea that both genders are complementary and interdependent, and that they are both responsible for enjoying and taking care of the world around them. The use of the word 'pairs' suggests that both men and women are equal in number and importance, and that they are meant to work together in harmony
orig: فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

orig: هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا

translation: Indeed, We have created mankind from a sperm-drop that is emitted, then We made him hearing and seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous creation of human beings by Allah, starting from a mere sperm-drop. The verse emphasizes the importance of hearing and sight, which are essential faculties for human beings to comprehend and appreciate the beauty and grandeur of Allah's creation. The verse also underscores the responsibility that comes with being endowed with these faculties, as human beings are expected to use them to recognize and worship Allah, and to live according to His commandments.
orig: إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

translation: Indeed, We have guided him to the path, whether he be grateful or ungrateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's role as the ultimate guide, who guides whomever He wills, regardless of their reaction to it. The phrase 'whether he be grateful or ungrateful' suggests that the guidance is not dependent on the individual's response, and that God's guidance is not limited by human attitudes or actions. This verse underscores the idea that God's guidance is a manifestation of His mercy and grace, and that it is not conditioned by human deservingness or worthiness.
orig: إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and fetters and a Blazing Fire.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and choose to disbelieve. The chains and fetters symbolize the constraints and limitations that will be placed upon them in the afterlife, while the Blazing Fire represents the intense suffering and torment that they will endure. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject God's message, reminding them of the severe consequences of their disbelief and encouraging them to turn towards God and adopt a righteous way of life.
orig: إنا أعتدنا للكافرين سلاسل وأغلالا وسعيرا

translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of ginger, a spring where the disbelievers will suffer.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the reward of the righteous in the afterlife. The 'cup of wine' symbolizes the spiritual joy and happiness that the righteous will experience in paradise. The 'ginger' in the cup represents the grace and beauty of paradise. The 'spring' where the disbelievers will suffer is a metaphor for the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message. The verse emphasizes the contrast between the bliss of the righteous and the suffering of the disbelievers, serving as a reminder of the consequences of one's actions in life.
orig: إن الأبرار يشربون من كأس كان مزاجها كافورا

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your own people in the past, when they were unjust, and We gave you a turn to flourish.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of the unjust communities in the past and how God gave their successors a chance to flourish. The verse serves as a reminder that God is just and will not allow injustice to persist, but also that He is merciful and gives opportunities for people to repent and do good deeds.
orig: عينا يشرب بها عباد الله يفجرونها تفجيرا

translation: And they (the people) mocked at the warning when they said, 'What! When we are (dead and) turned to bones, shall we really be raised up?',
interpretation: The verse describes the reaction of the people who were warned about the punishment of God. They mocked the idea of being raised from the dead and being held accountable for their actions. The verse highlights their disbelief and arrogance, questioning how they could possibly be resurrected after they had turned to bones. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the importance of heeding the warnings of God's messengers.
orig: يوفون بالنذر ويخافون يوما كان شره مستطيرا

translation: And they give food, despite their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive.
interpretation: The verse highlights the generosity and selflessness of the righteous, who are willing to give away their own food, despite their love for it, to those in need. The verse specifically mentions the poor, the orphan, and the captive, indicating that these groups are particularly deserving of charity and support. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be generous and selfless in their actions, and to prioritize the needs of others over their own desires.
orig: ويطعمون الطعام على حبه مسكينا ويتيما وأسيرا

translation: Indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: This verse refers to the victory and triumph that God has given to the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to a decisive and unambiguous victory, while 'manifest triumph' suggests a victory that is clear and evident to all. The verse emphasizes that this victory is a blessing from God and not something that the believers have earned or deserved. It serves as a reminder that all success and victory comes from God and should be attributed to Him alone.
orig: إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, on the day when the sky will be like murky oil, and the mountains will be like wool.
interpretation: The verse warns of an impending punishment from God, which is described as being near. The sky is compared to murky oil, indicating a sense of darkness and turmoil, while the mountains are likened to wool, suggesting a sense of chaos and disorder. The verse suggests that the punishment will be severe and widespread, affecting both the natural world and human societies. The verse serves as a reminder to those who have neglected God's commands and are living in disobedience, to repent and turn back to God before it's too late.
orig: إنا نخاف من ربنا يوما عبوسا قمطريرا

translation: And God's punishment came to them in the morning, and their hearts were hardened, so that they were not able to understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of ignoring God's signs and warnings. Despite the numerous warnings, the people's hearts were hardened, and they failed to understand and repent. As a result, God's punishment came to them in the morning, catching them by surprise and leaving them without the opportunity to change their ways. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding God's signs and warnings and turning towards Him in repentance.
orig: فوقاهم الله شر ذلك اليوم ولقاهم نضرة وسرورا

translation: And they were punished with a punishment that was not benevolent because they had been transgressing, being tyrants.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that was inflicted upon a group of people who had been oppressive and tyrannical. The verse suggests that their punishment was not a blessing or a favor, but rather a consequence of their own actions. The use of the word "جنة" (jannah) which means "garden" or "paradise" in Arabic, implies that the punishment was not a pleasant experience, but rather a form of retribution for their wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder that those who engage in oppressive behavior will face consequences for their actions, and that God is just in His punishment.
orig: وجزاهم بما صبروا جنة وحريرا

translation: And the moon has eclipsed, and the sun has been curtailed, and the stars have fallen, and the mountains have been blown away.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene of chaos and destruction, where the natural order of the universe has been disrupted. The moon and sun, which are symbols of light and guidance, have been eclipsed, and the stars, which represent hope and guidance, have fallen. The mountains, which are symbols of stability and endurance, have been blown away. The verse suggests that the world has been turned upside down, and that the usual markers of time and order have been disrupted. It could be interpreted as a description of the end of the world, or a time of great upheaval and change.
orig: متكئين فيها على الأرائك لا يرون فيها شمسا ولا زمهريرا

translation: And We have destroyed the like of them, (i.e., the towns).
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of similar towns and communities that were destroyed by God's punishment in the past. The use of the word 'like' indicates that these towns were similar in nature and action to the ones being addressed in the verse. The verse serves as a reminder that God's punishment is not limited to any particular community, but it is a warning to all those who reject God's message and continue to live in disobedience.
orig: ودانية عليهم ظلالها وذللت قطوفها تذليلا

translation: And We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, so that not a soul will be wronged in the least, and if there be but the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient is We to take account.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Day of Resurrection when all souls will be judged based on their deeds in this life. The 'scales of justice' represent the fairness and impartiality of God's judgment, and the verse emphasizes that even the smallest good or bad deed will be taken into account. The image of the mustard seed, which is tiny and almost weightless, underscores the idea that no one will be wronged, and that God's justice is perfect and all-encompassing.
orig: ويطاف عليهم بآنية من فضة وأكواب كانت قواريرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قوارير من فضة قدروها تقديرا

translation: And they will be given to drink boiling water, and it will be as if their bellies were bursting with fire.
interpretation: The verse describes the punishment that awaits those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience. The boiling water they will be forced to drink is a metaphor for the intense suffering they will endure, as if their insides are being burned by a fiery liquid. The image of bursting bellies suggests a violent and painful death, emphasizing the severity of God's punishment for those who reject His mercy and guidance.
orig: ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's knowledge of human nature and His proximity to human beings. The verse suggests that God is aware of the innermost thoughts and whispers of human beings, and is closer to them than their own vital organs. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and omnipresence, and highlights the intimate relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: عينا فيها تسمى سلسبيلا

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all humanity. The verse highlights the scope of his prophetic mission, which encompasses not only his contemporaries but also future generations and communities. The use of the plural form of "worlds" underscores the universal nature of his message and its relevance to all people, regardless of their cultural, linguistic, or geographical backgrounds. The verse serves as a reminder that the Prophet's teachings are not limited to a particular group or time period, but are indeed a mercy and guidance for all humanity, until the end of time.
orig: ويطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون إذا رأيتهم حسبتهم لؤلؤا منثورا

translation: And indeed, I saw the angel of death, and he was a noble and great king.
interpretation: The verse describes the Prophet's vision of the angel of death, who is described as a noble and great king. The verse suggests that the angel of death is a powerful and important figure, who is responsible for taking the souls of the deceased. The use of the word "king" emphasizes the angel's authority and majesty, and the adjectives "noble" and "great" suggest that he is worthy of respect and awe. The verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death and the power of the angel of death, who is responsible for carrying out God's will.
orig: وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت نعيما وملكا كبيرا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an is a sacred book, a reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the significance and sacredness of the Qur'an, highlighting its role as a source of guidance and inspiration for believers. The phrase 'a reward for those who believe and do righteous deeds' underscores the idea that the Qur'an is not just a book to be read, but a guide to be followed in daily life. The verse encourages readers to engage with the Qur'an actively and to allow its teachings to shape their beliefs and actions.
orig: إن هذا كان لكم جزاء وكان سعيكم مشكورا

translation: Indeed, We have sent the Qur'an down to you as a revelation.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a revelation sent down by God to humanity through the Prophet Muhammad. The use of the word 'indeed' suggests that the Qur'an is a confirmation of previous revelations and is a reminder to the people of their responsibility to follow its teachings. The verse also underscores the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and a reminder to humanity of God's existence and power.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا

translation: Therefore be patient with the command of your Lord and do not obey the disobedient among them, and do not follow the path of the ignorant.
interpretation: The verse commands the believers to be patient with the decree of God and not to follow the path of the disobedient and the ignorant. The verse emphasizes the importance of patience and obedience to God's command, and warns against the negative influence of those who disobey and reject God's teachings. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to stay on the path of righteousness and avoid the behavior of those who reject God's guidance.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا

translation: And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying God's name, both in the morning and evening, indicating a consistent and persistent mindset of worship and devotion. It serves as a reminder to believers to stay mindful of their relationship with God throughout the day, and to seek His guidance and protection in all aspects of their lives.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا

translation: And during the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him throughout the night, [also] in the late night.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of worshiping God during the night, specifically through prostration and glorification. It suggests that believers should dedicate a portion of their night to prayer and devotion, seeking guidance and forgiveness from God. The phrase 'late night' signifies the final moments of the night, just before dawn, implying that one should persevere in their worship until the end of the night, demonstrating their commitment to God. The verse serves as a reminder of the believer's responsibility to maintain a strong spiritual connection with God, particularly during the night, when one is most likely to be alone with their thoughts and able to focus on their faith.
orig: ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا

translation: Indeed, those who are apprehensive of the punishment of the Hereafter have been neglectful of their duty and have been turned away from the path of their Lord.
interpretation: The verse highlights the mindset of those who are concerned about the punishment of the Hereafter. Instead of being fearful of God's punishment, they have neglected their duty to worship and obey God and have turned away from the path of righteousness. This verse serves as a reminder that the fear of punishment should not be the primary motivator for worship, but rather the love and obedience to God should be the driving force behind one's actions.
orig: إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

translation: And We have created them, and We have strengthened their make, and if We had wished to destroy them, We would have punished them (in this life); but the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over the creation. By stating that God created and strengthened humanity, the verse highlights God's role as the creator and sustainer of all life. The verse also mentions that if God had wished to destroy humanity, He would have done so in this life, but the punishment of the Hereafter will be far more severe. This serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience, reminding them that they will face the consequences of their actions in the afterlife.
orig: نحن خلقناهم وشددنا أسرهم وإذا شئنا بدلنا أمثالهم تبديلا

The verse can be seen as a reminder that human beings are not in control of their own destiny, but rather, it is God who guides and directs the course of events. This understanding can bring about a sense of humility and submission to God's will, and encourage people to seek God's guidance and mercy in the face of conflict and strife.

interpretation: The verse emphasizes the accessibility and clarity of the Qur'an, indicating that it is a book that is meant to be understood and remembered by all people, regardless of their background or intelligence. It also serves as a warning to those who oppose the Prophet and the Muslims, that they will not be able to overcome the divine assistance and support that the believers enjoy.
orig: جزاء من ربك عطاء حسابا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful does not allow them to be possessed by anyone.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's sovereignty over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, and that no one can possess or own His dominion. It highlights God's unique attribute, ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful, indicating that His mercy encompasses all creation and that no one can escape His justice. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God's power and authority are absolute and that they must submit to His will.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما الرحمن لا يملكون منه خطابا

translation: On the Day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in row, they will not speak except for him whom the Most Merciful has given permission, and he will say what is right.
interpretation: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Judgment, when the Spirit (Gabriel) and the angels will be lined up in rows, and they will not speak except for the one whom the Most Merciful (God) has given permission to speak. The verse emphasizes the authority and power of God, who controls even the speech of the angels, and highlights the importance of His permission and approval. The verse also underscores the idea that on the Day of Judgment, only those who have been given permission by God will be able to speak, indicating that all will be judged according to their deeds and only those who have lived righteously will be able to defend themselves.
orig: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمن وقال صوابا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: ذلك اليوم الحق فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه مآبا

translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, on the day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth and the disbeliever will say, 'Oh, I wish I were dust!',
interpretation: The verse warns of an imminent punishment that will come suddenly and unexpectedly. The verse describes a scene on the Day of Judgment when people will see the consequences of their actions and the disbeliever will regret not having lived a righteous life. The phrase 'Oh, I wish I were dust!' expresses the deep regret and remorse that the disbeliever will feel when he realizes that he has wasted his life and missed the opportunity to live a righteous life. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disbelief, reminding them of the certainty of God's punishment and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه ويقول الكافر يا ليتني كنت ترابا

translation: By the angels who pull up the ruins.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: والنازعات غرقا

translation: By the soul and He who perfected it
interpretation: The verse praises God's creation of human souls and their perfected nature. The phrase 'He who perfected it' refers to God's power and wisdom in creating the soul and making it capable of distinguishing right from wrong. The verse highlights the importance of the soul's responsibility and accountability to God, emphasizing the idea that humans are not just physical beings but also possess a spiritual dimension that will be judged by God. It serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on their actions and strive to live a virtuous life.
orig: والناشطات نشطا

translation: By the morning hours, and by the night when it is still!
interpretation: The verse is an oath taken by God, swearing by the morning hours and the stillness of the night, emphasizing the importance and gravity of what is to follow. The verse serves as an introduction to the passage that describes the destruction of the wicked towns, and the impending punishment that awaits those who reject God's message.
orig: والسابحات سبحا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فالسابقات سبقا

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فالمدبرات أمرا

translation: And the sky is rent asunder, and the mountains are made to pass away.
interpretation: The verse describes the end of the world and the Day of Judgment, when the sky will be torn apart and the mountains will be made to disappear. The verse emphasizes the power and majesty of God, who is capable of destroying the heavens and the earth and bringing about a new creation. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Reckoning, when all humanity will be judged according to their deeds, and serves as a warning to those who reject God's message and choose to live in disobedience to His commandments.
orig: يوم ترجف الراجفة

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: تتبعها الرادفة

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: قلوب يومئذ واجفة

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of mercy for all creatures. The verse highlights the universality of Muhammad's message, indicating that his prophethood was not limited to a particular group or community, but rather it was a blessing for all humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the mercy of Muhammad (peace be upon him) encompasses both the spiritual and temporal realms, and that his teachings are relevant to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse serves as a reminder of the compassionate nature of Islam and the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a source of guidance and mercy for all.
orig: أبصارها خاشعة

translation: They say, 'We will not believe you until you break open for us from the earth a spring or you have a garden of date palms and grapes and make rivers flow in it.'
interpretation: The verse addresses the disbelievers' demand for a miracle as a condition for their belief in the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They are asking for something extraordinary, a spring or a garden of date palms and grapes, and rivers flowing in it, thinking that such a miracle would be a proof of the Prophet's authenticity. The verse highlights their skepticism and unwillingness to believe in the Prophet's message, and serves as a reminder that faith cannot be forced or coerced, it must be accepted willingly.
orig: يقولون أإنا لمردودون في الحافرة

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you did not pass by them.
interpretation: The verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and reminds him of God's power and justice. The verse speaks about the destruction of previous nations who were similar to the disbelievers of Mecca, who were rejecting the message of the Prophet. The verse warns them that they will face the same fate as those nations if they continue to reject God's message. The verse also serves as a reminder to the believers that God's justice is universal and that no one can escape it.
orig: أإذا كنا عظاما نخرة

translation: They said, 'This is a tough sorcery.' Indeed, this is a lying and losing people.
interpretation: The verse refers to the response of the disbelievers to the Qur'an and the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). They dismissed the Qur'an as a form of magic or sorcery, belittling its message and implying that it was nothing more than a clever trick. The verse emphasizes that this response is a result of their disbelief and unwillingness to accept the truth. The phrase 'lying and losing people' highlights the negative consequences of their disbelief and the ultimate defeat they will face in the Hereafter.
orig: قالوا تلك إذا كرة خاسرة

translation: And indeed, it is a single zajra.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the Qur'an being a single zajra, or a single, unified, and coherent revelation from God. The use of the word 'single' emphasizes the unity and consistency of the Qur'anic message, indicating that it is a single, unbroken chain of revelation that has been sent to guide humanity. The verse serves as a reminder of the Qur'an's unique status as a divine revelation, and underscores its role as a source of guidance and wisdom for believers.
orig: فإنما هي زجرة واحدة

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed towns around you, [as was specified] in the Book.
interpretation: This verse refers to the destruction of towns mentioned in the Qur'an, specifically in the context of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) era. The verse emphasizes that the destruction of these towns was already foretold in the Qur'an, and that the punishment was inevitable due to their disobedience and rejection of God's message. The verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet and his followers that God's word is true and that His punishment is certain for those who reject His message.
orig: فإذا هم بالساهرة

translation: And indeed, We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) over his opponents in Mecca, who had persecuted him and his followers for many years. The victory was a manifestation of God's support for the Prophet and his message, and a proof of the truth of Islam. The verse emphasizes the clarity and manifest nature of the victory, indicating that it was a clear and decisive victory, leaving no room for doubt or confusion. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that God is always with them and will support them in their struggles against injustice and oppression.
orig: هل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: And indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like carded wool.
interpretation: The verse warns of an impending punishment that will come suddenly and unexpectedly, just as a moth is suddenly scattered by the wind. The verse also compares the mountains to carded wool, indicating their utter destruction and powerlessness in the face of God's punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment and the need for preparedness and repentance.
orig: إذ ناداه ربه بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.
interpretation: The verse commands the Prophet Moses to go to Pharaoh and convey the message of God's wrath upon him for his transgression and oppression of the Israelites. The verse highlights the responsibility of prophets to confront oppressive rulers and hold them accountable for their actions, while also emphasizing the gravity of Pharaoh's sins and the consequences he will face if he does not repent.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى

translation: And inclining towards your Lord, so He may forgive you.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the importance of turning towards God and seeking His forgiveness. The Arabic word 'tawajjuh' used in the verse implies a sense of humility, submission and inclination towards God. The verse suggests that by turning towards God, one may receive His forgiveness and mercy. It emphasizes the idea that God's forgiveness is a result of His grace and mercy, rather than any personal effort or deed. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to cultivate a strong relationship with God and seek His forgiveness through humility and submission.
orig: وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you do not perceive.
interpretation: The verse refers to the destruction of nations before the Prophet Muhammad's time. The verse warns the Prophet's contemporaries of the consequences of their actions and encourages them to learn from the lessons of history. The verse emphasizes that even though the previous nations were destroyed, the current generation does not seem to understand or learn from their mistakes. It serves as a warning to the present generation, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and encouraging them to change their ways before it's too late.
orig: فأراه الآية الكبرى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فكذب وعصى

translation: Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke.
interpretation: The verse describes the creation of the universe by God. The phrase 'when it was smoke' suggests that the universe was initially in a state of chaos and disorder, with smoke representing the confusion and darkness that existed before God brought order and structure to it. The verse highlights the power and wisdom of God in creating the universe out of this state of chaos, and serves as a reminder of His greatness and majesty.
orig: ثم أدبر يسعى

translation: So We have put a barrier in front of them and a barrier behind them, blocking them off, and We have covered them up, so they cannot see.
interpretation: The verse describes the state of those who have been blinded by their own arrogance and disbelief. The 'barrier' mentioned in the verse symbolizes the spiritual blindness that prevents them from seeing the truth and accepting guidance. The verse also implies that such individuals are surrounded by barriers, both physically and spiritually, which prevent them from moving forward or backward, leaving them trapped in their state of disbelief. The phrase 'We have covered them up' suggests that God has placed a veil over their eyes, preventing them from seeing the truth and understanding the signs of God. The verse serves as a warning to those who are resistant to the message of God, reminding them that their arrogance and disbelief will only lead to their own downfall.
orig: فحشر فنادى

translation: And He is with you wherever you may be.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipresence and His ability to be with His creation at all times and in all places. It is a reminder that God is always watching and aware of everything that is happening, and that He is always close to those who seek Him. The verse also serves as a source of comfort and reassurance for believers, reminding them that they are never alone and that God is always with them, guiding and protecting them.
orig: فقال أنا ربكم الأعلى

translation: So, indeed, Allah will suffice you, [O Muhammad], against them as a Witness, and the believers, as a witness, [to the truth].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sufficiency as a witness for the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. It highlights God's role as a witness to the truth of the message brought by the Prophet and the belief of the believers. It underscores the idea that God is sufficient as a witness and that the believers need not seek any other witness or proof to confirm their faith. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omniscience and His ability to witness all that we do, say, and believe.
orig: فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى

translation: Indeed, in this is a sign for those who fear.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the destruction of the unjust towns serves as a sign or a lesson for those who fear God and are conscious of their actions. The verse implies that the punishment that was inflicted upon the towns is a reminder to those who are living in sin and injustice, and that they should take heed of the warning and change their ways before it is too late.
orig: إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى

translation: And indeed, We have created mankind and We know what their own selves whisper to them, and We are nearer to them than their own jugular vein.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's knowledge of humanity's innermost thoughts and His proximity to them. The use of the word 'selves' in the plural form suggests that humans have multiple layers of consciousness, and God is aware of each one of them. The verse also emphasizes God's nearness to humanity, indicating that He is always with them and aware of their thoughts, feelings, and actions. This verse serves as a reminder that God is all-knowing and ever-present, and that humans should be mindful of their thoughts and actions at all times.
orig: أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها

translation: And We have raised the highest point of the sky, the ceiling, and We have not created any cracks in it.
interpretation: The verse describes how God has raised the highest point of the sky, which serves as a metaphor for the infinite power and wisdom of God. The use of the word 'ceiling' emphasizes the idea that the sky is a solid structure that covers the earth, and the fact that there are no cracks in it highlights God's perfect creation. The verse is a reminder of God's greatness and the fragility of human existence, and it encourages believers to reflect on the majesty of God and their own place in the universe.
orig: رفع سمكها فسواها

translation: And He drew the night as a veil and brought the day out of it.
interpretation: The verse describes God's power and control over the cycles of day and night. The image of the night as a veil being drawn over the day suggests a sense of protection and concealment, emphasizing God's role as the guardian and caretaker of all creation. The phrase 'and brought the day out of it' implies a sense of emergence and renewal, signifying the cyclical nature of time and the constant opportunity for new beginnings.
orig: وأغطش ليلها وأخرج ضحاها

translation: And the earth, after that, was but a plain, empty (of vegetation).
interpretation: The verse describes the state of the earth after the destruction of the unjust towns. The earth was left barren and empty, devoid of any vegetation or life. The verse emphasizes the completeness of the destruction and the severity of God's punishment. The image of a barren earth serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the power of God's wrath.
orig: والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها

translation: And We have brought forth from it (the earth) springs of wealth and palm trees.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the abundance of resources and wealth that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. The 'springs of wealth' refer to the natural resources that are hidden beneath the earth, such as oil, gas, and minerals. The 'palm trees' symbolize the blessings and prosperity that come from these resources. The verse highlights Allah's generosity and provision for humanity, reminding us to be grateful for the abundance we enjoy.
orig: أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها

translation: And He has subjected to you, in the heaven and on earth, all that is in them, behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and control over all things in the heavens and the earth. The phrase 'subjected to you' indicates that God has given humanity dominion over the earth and all that is in it, but it also serves as a reminder that this dominion is a trust from God and that humans will be held accountable for their stewardship. The phrase 'behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect' suggests that the natural world and all that is in it contains signs and lessons for those who are willing to reflect and contemplate on the beauty and majesty of God's creation.
orig: والجبال أرساها

translation: And We have given you a clear victory and a manifest triumph.
interpretation: The verse refers to the victory and triumph given by God to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. The phrase 'clear victory' refers to the decisive victory given by God, while 'manifest triumph' indicates that the victory is clear and evident to all. The verse serves as a reminder of God's favor and support for the believers, and encourages them to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to God.
orig: متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم

translation: And when the great catastrophe came.
interpretation: The verse refers to a major disaster or calamity that befell a community. The word 'catastrophe' (ṭā'ima) implies a sudden and severe event that brings destruction and devastation. The verse does not specify the nature of the catastrophe, leaving it open to interpretation. It could refer to a natural disaster, such as an earthquake, flood, or storm, or a human-made disaster, such as a war or economic collapse. The verse serves as a reminder that such calamities are a part of life and can strike at any time, emphasizing the need for preparedness and resilience in the face of adversity.
orig: فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى

translation: And indeed, mankind will be aware of their effort on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: The verse highlights the fact that on the Day of Judgment, people will be fully aware of their deeds and the consequences of their actions. The word 'effort' refers not only to good deeds but also to bad deeds, indicating that everyone will be held accountable for their actions in this life. The verse serves as a reminder that our actions have consequences, and we will ultimately be held responsible for them in the afterlife.
orig: يوم يتذكر الإنسان ما سعى

translation: And the Hell-fire will be brought forth for him who sees,
interpretation: The verse describes the horrors of Hell and how it will be presented to those who have been wicked in their lives. The phrase 'for him who sees' suggests that the punishment will be tailored to the individual's crimes, and that they will be fully aware of their own guilt and the justice of their punishment.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: فأما من طغى

translation: And He has subjected to you, as from Him, all that is in the heavens and on earth: behold, in that are signs indeed for those who reflect.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes God's power and dominion over all things in the heavens and earth. The phrase 'subjected to you' signifies that all things have been placed under humanity's control, indicating their stewardship over creation. The verse also suggests that the natural world contains signs and messages for those who reflect and contemplate the wonders of creation. It is an invitation to appreciate and acknowledge God's majesty and wisdom as revealed in the natural world.
orig: وآثر الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, Hell is the Eternal Home.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that Hell is a place of eternal punishment and suffering, where those who have lived a life of disobedience and disbelief will reside forever. The use of the word 'mu'awwaj' (مأوى) to describe Hell as an 'eternal home' underscores the idea that once someone is cast into Hell, there is no escape or reprieve. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and disbelief, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the importance of turning towards God and living a righteous life.
orig: فإن الجحيم هي المأوى

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of his Lord's verses but turns away from them, and forgets the meeting of his Lord? We have prepared for him a shameful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of ignoring God's signs and verses, and the severe punishment that awaits those who do so. The verse emphasizes the idea that the individual's neglect of God's reminders is a personal choice, and that they will ultimately be held accountable for their actions. The phrase 'We have prepared for him a shameful punishment' underscores the idea that God's punishment is not only a consequence of their actions, but also a means of shaming them for their disobedience.
orig: وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever approaching.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of God's punishment, which is described as 'approaching' or 'drawing near'. The use of the word 'indeed' at the beginning of the verse suggests that what follows is a statement of great importance and significance. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in disobedience to God's commands, reminding them that the consequences of their actions are imminent and unavoidable.
orig: فإن الجنة هي المأوى

translation: They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to pass?
interpretation: The verse refers to the question posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the coming of the Hour, that is, the Day of Judgment. The verse indicates that the disbelievers were skeptical about the idea of the Hour and were asking the Prophet (peace be upon him) when it would occur. The verse serves as a reminder that only God knows the exact time of the Hour and that it will come unexpectedly, as a thief in the night. The verse also emphasizes the importance of being prepared for the Hour and living a righteous life, as the Hour will bring about a complete transformation of the present order and usher in a new era of justice and peace.
orig: يسألونك عن الساعة أيان مرساها

translation: And indeed, We have destroyed your kind in the past, but you, O human, are forgetful.
interpretation: The verse highlights God's power and justice, emphasizing that He has destroyed entire nations in the past for their wrongdoing. The phrase 'you, O human, are forgetful' suggests that humans have a tendency to forget God's lessons and warnings, and that they continue to repeat the same mistakes. The verse serves as a reminder to reflect on the past and learn from it, and to be mindful of God's wrath and the consequences of one's actions.
orig: فيم أنت من ذكراها

translation: And to your Lord is the return.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the ultimate return of all things to God, highlighting the idea that everything in existence belongs to Him and will eventually return to Him. It suggests that all things, including humans, will ultimately be judged by God based on their actions and deeds in life, and that the ultimate destination of all things is to return to God's presence. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability and responsibility that comes with being a creation of God, and the need to live a life that is pleasing to Him.
orig: إلى ربك منتهاها

translation: Indeed, you are a warner, and a reminder for those who fear My threat.
interpretation: In this verse, God is addressing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), acknowledging his role as a warner and a reminder to those who fear God's punishment. The verse highlights the Prophet's responsibility to convey the message of Islam and warn people of the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'those who fear My threat' refers to the believers who are mindful of God's power and authority, and are therefore more likely to heed the Prophet's warning and live according to God's commandments.
orig: إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so Our punishment came to it in the morning, or at noon.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the destruction of towns that were unjust and received their punishment from God. The verse emphasizes the sudden and unexpected nature of the 'punishment', which came either in the morning or at noon, indicating that the people were taken by surprise and had no time to prepare or repent. The verse serves as a warning to those who are living in sin and injustice, reminding them of the consequences of their actions and the certainty of God's punishment.
orig: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his role as a source of guidance and mercy for all of humanity. The use of the plural form of "worlds" suggests that the Prophet's message is not limited to a particular community or region, but is universal and applicable to all people, regardless of their background or beliefs. The verse highlights the compassionate nature of the Prophet's mission, which is to bring people closer to God and guide them towards a righteous and just life.
orig: عبس وتولى

translation: And he who is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter, and even more astray.
interpretation: The verse speaks about the spiritual blindness of those who reject God's signs and refuse to believe in the Hereafter. The verse indicates that their blindness in this life will be nothing compared to their blindness in the Hereafter, where they will be even more lost and astray. The verse serves as a warning to those who are skeptical of God's existence and the Hereafter, reminding them of the consequences of their disbelief and the importance of recognizing and submitting to God's truth.
orig: أن جاءه الأعمى

translation: And he (the man) knew not that the angel (Gabriel) was coming to him in the morning, or at noon.
